我将这本书献给所有督促我面对强加于我的一切的人，因为他们让我成为了一个更好的人。

I dedicate this book to all those who push me to face what is imposed upon me, because they make me a better person.

他们知道自己是谁，也知道我有多么感激他们。

They know who they are and how grateful I am to them.

 

 

感谢《卡洛斯，皇帝》系列剧本团队的同事们：何塞·路易斯·马丁、纳乔·佩雷斯·德拉巴斯、玛丽亚·何塞·莫查莱斯、克拉拉·佩雷斯·埃斯克里瓦、胡安·卡洛斯·布拉斯克斯和巴勃罗·泰巴尔。

To my colleagues on the script team of the series «Carlos, King Emperor»: José Luis Martín, Nacho Pérez de la Paz, María José Mochales, Clara Pérez Escrivá, Juan Carlos Blázquez and Pablo Tébar.

如果没有他们的才华和努力，这本书是不可能出版的。

Without their talent and work, this book would have been impossible.

 

 

尤其要感谢我在瑞典、塞维利亚和马德里的家人。

And especially to my family in Sweden, Seville and Madrid.

你是我最大的福气。

You are my greatest blessing.

1

1

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

船头划破了身后的迷雾。周围的景色渐渐清晰起来，变得清晰可见。根特的查理在甲板上走了几步，第一次看清了眼前这个地方，在此之前，它对他来说仅仅是一个概念。首席领航员刚刚为将皇家舰队改道至卡斯蒂利亚北部某个未知地点而道歉，那里肯定不是他们原定的目的地拉雷多。查理并不想改变登陆计划。对他来说，这个地方也挺好，尽管随着他们靠近，这个地方对于远征队的四十艘船来说显得越来越小，显得有些荒谬。之所以觉得好，是因为航程漫长，一路遭遇了可怕的风暴，船只被肆意地抛来抛去；而且，在此之前，他刚刚经历了一次长达一年半的煎熬，那次煎熬始于他的祖父费尔南多去世，而他希望以接管西班牙政权来结束。

The ship's advance pierced the mists in its wake. The surroundings were becoming defined, solid. Charles of Ghent took a few steps on deck and made out for the first time the place that, until that moment, had been merely an idea to him. The chief pilot had just apologized for having diverted the royal fleet to some unknown location in northern Castile, which was certainly not Laredo, their intended destination. Charles had not wanted to change the landing plan. This location was fine to him, even though, as they approached, it appeared increasingly ridiculously small for the landing of the expedition's forty ships. It was fine because the voyage had been long, accompanied by terrible storms that had tossed the ships about at will; and because before this journey he had endured another, lasting a year and a half, which began with the death of his grandfather Ferdinand and which he wanted to end by assuming the government of Spain.

卡洛斯挺直了肩膀，以示此刻的庄重。他身着丝绸西装，领口饰以弗拉芒蕾丝，尽显华贵，但他的脸上却透露出他只有十七岁的年纪。他的五官介于温柔与坚毅之间。金色的头发、苍白的肤色和好奇的眼神让他显得敏感；而棱角分明的下巴又赋予了他一位政治家应有的威严。

Carlos raised his shoulders to reflect the dignity of the moment. His silk suit and Flemish lace enveloped him in grandeur, but his face betrayed the fact that he was only seventeen. His features were a struggle between gentleness and determination. His blond hair, pale complexion, and curious gaze made him sensitive; his strong chin lent his face the sternness expected of a statesman.

卡洛斯沉浸在他特有的沉默中，仔细审视着眼前绵延的景色。他知道自己将永远铭记对这片土地的第一印象：高耸葱郁的山峦，狭长的海滩，以及几栋低矮房屋组成的村庄。自幼，他就试图了解这片土地，这里居住着他从未谋面的两个兄弟姐妹——费尔南多和卡塔琳娜；这片土地也是他父母费利佩和胡安娜的墓地，父亲已然离世，母亲也奄奄一息，隐居在托尔德西利亚斯宫中。卡洛斯希望自己能够爱上这里，希望自从离开弗利辛根港，甚至自从与姑姑玛格丽塔告别——这位如同母亲般被生活赋予他，却也模糊了他自身母亲身份的长辈——以来，一直萦绕在他心头的那份难以言喻的痛苦能够消散。他心中涌起一股怀旧和忧虑，但他不想向任何人承认，因为人们认为每个伟人都是勇敢而冷酷的，而他更是如此。他一岁时就成为了卢森堡公爵，六岁时继承了荷兰，从那时起，他就一直生活在西班牙终有一天会属于他的警告之下。

Enveloped in the silence so characteristic of him, Carlos scrutinized the landscape that stretched before him. He knew he would always remember that first impression of the kingdom: the high, verdant mountains, the narrow beach, the village of a few low houses. Since childhood, he had tried to form an idea of ​​this domain inhabited by two of his siblings, Fernando and Catalina, whom he had never seen; this kingdom that was also the tomb of his parents, Felipe and Juana, he already lifeless and she barely alive, cloistered in the palace of Tordesillas. Carlos hoped that he would come to love this place and that the sharp feeling that had been robbing him of his peace since he left the port of Flushing, even since he had said goodbye to his aunt Margarita, the mother that life had given him while simultaneously blurring his own, would dissipate. He felt a nostalgia and apprehension that he did not want to confess to anyone, because every great man is presumed to be bold and cold, and even more so him, who at the age of one had become Duke of Luxembourg, at six had inherited the Netherlands and, since then, had lived on the warning that Spain would one day be his.

 

 

 

 

一声巨响吓了他一跳，他循声望去。只见水手们正在把送随行人员上岸的小艇放入水中。

A loud noise startled him and forced him to look out. The sailors were lowering the boats that would take the entourage ashore into the water.

陛下，保重！

—Take care, Your Majesty!

一只有力的手扶他上了船；那是威廉·德·克罗伊的手，他毫不犹豫地也坐进了同一艘船。查理安全上岸后，这位自封的希耶夫尔领主看了他一眼，立刻察觉到他的紧张。对于大多数认识他的人来说，菲利普和琼的儿子是个难以捉摸的谜。他沉默寡言，表情矜持；可以说，他竭力隐藏着自己的内心。但希耶夫尔，这位从九岁起就一直是他的顾问、知己和形影不离的伙伴，却深谙查理的心思：即便他表面上装作镇定，查理此刻也比以往任何时候都更需要他。而如果说有什么能让希耶夫尔感到欣慰，那就是查理的这种需要，而这种需要，正是他近十年来一点一滴积累起来的。这位顾问，五官棱角分明，一头黑发已然斑白，他总是全身心投入工作，以至于查理根本不在乎他身上那些不好的名声。许多人谴责希耶夫尔野心勃勃、毫无底线，但查理却视他为坚定不移的支持者，以及通往荣耀的钥匙。多亏了希耶夫尔的建议，查理年仅十五岁便统治了尼德兰，因为希耶夫尔说服了查理的祖父——皇帝马克西米利安，让他相信年幼并非不可逾越的障碍。也正是多亏了希耶夫尔，查理才没有等到那次旅行才宣布自己为卡斯蒂利亚和阿拉贡国王；在希耶夫尔的建议下，查理在布鲁塞尔就宣布了这一消息。许多人认为这些幕后运作是这位顾问出于私利，像许多皇家顾问一样，渴望通过自己的门生来掌权。但查理却在思考，究竟是哪一个更自私：是那个为了攫取权力而不择手段的人，还是他自己，那个从希耶夫尔的阴谋诡计中获益却依然保持清白的人。

A firm hand helped him down into his boat; it was William de Croy's, who didn't hesitate to take his place in the same vessel. Once Charles was safely ashore, the self-styled Lord of Chièvres looked at him and immediately noticed his nervousness. For most of those who knew him, the son of Philip and Joan was an unfathomable mystery. He was quiet and reserved in his expression; one might say he was striving to conceal his soul. But Chièvres, who had been his advisor, his confidant, his constant shadow since the age of nine, knew how to read him perfectly: even if he feigned serenity, Charles needed him then more than ever. And if anything pleased Chièvres, it was precisely that need, which he had built brick by brick over almost a decade. The advisor, with his harsh features and black hair that was already turning gray, had always dedicated himself so completely to his work that the bad reputation he carried with him mattered little to Charles. Where many denounced Chièvres as having unbridled ambition and few scruples, Charles saw unwavering support and the master key that would lead him to glory. Thanks to his advice, he had come to govern the Netherlands at just fifteen years old, for Chièvres had convinced Emperor Maximilian, Charles's grandfather, that minority was not such an insurmountable obstacle. And thanks to him as well, he hadn't waited for that journey to proclaim himself King of Castile and Aragon; he had done so, at his suggestion, in Brussels. Many saw in these machinations the selfish interest of the advisor who, like so many royal advisors, aspired to govern through his protégé. But Charles wondered which of the two was more selfish: the one who, seeking a share of power, sullied himself to aggrandize him, or himself, who benefited from his machinations and retained his innocence.

 

 

 

 

船只抵达岸边，周围簇拥着护卫队的士兵。与此同时，在拉雷多，一支盛大的游行队伍徒劳地等待着皇室成员的登陆。

The boat reached the shore surrounded by a ring of troops acting as an escort. Meanwhile, in Laredo, a grand procession waited in vain for the royal landing.

“在这个世界的角落里，容不下你的伟大，哥哥，”莱昂诺尔在自己的船上，一边眺望着海岸线一边说道。

"In this corner of the world there is no room for your greatness, brother," said Leonor from her own boat, scanning the coast.

卡洛斯的妹妹莱昂诺尔比他大不了多少，是此行唯一陪伴他的亲人。她白皙的肌肤和铜色的头发，让她带着一种宫廷式的柔弱气质，但这与她内心的坚强形成鲜明对比。莱昂诺尔靠研读古籍和默默惩罚弟弟来熬过这段旅程。她的行为让所有人都感到困惑，只有卡洛斯不以为意，甚至没有表现出任何不满。他知道，因为他听人说过，世间确实存在爱情，而莱昂诺尔正为莱茵河畔的弗雷德里克伯爵而苦恼，因为这段旅程，她被迫与他分离。

Carlos's sister, barely two years older than him, was the only relative accompanying him on the journey. Her translucent skin and coppery hair gave her an air of courtly vulnerability that belied her inner strength. Leonor had endured the voyage by reading the ancients and imposing a silent punishment on her brother. Her behavior had puzzled everyone except Carlos, who hadn't even shown offense. He knew, because he had heard it said, that there was such a thing as love, and that Leonor was suffering from it for Count Frederick of the Rhine, from whom she had been forced to part because of the journey.

 

 

 

 

武装护卫队终于踏上了陆地。人数众多，而这片飞地却如此之小，很快，沙滩便消失在视野之外。查理看着士兵们沿着海岸线展开阵型，心中涌起一股强烈的感觉，这片王国即将属于他。然而，一阵撕心裂肺的惨叫声打破了他平静的思绪：从村庄边缘的海滩上，如圣经中诅咒般，无数石块如雨点般落下，砸向士兵们。猝不及防的士兵寥寥无几，只有少数人及时躲过了石块的袭击。其中几颗石块夺去了士兵的生命。

The armed escort finally set foot on land. It was so numerous and the enclave so small that soon there was hardly any sand left in sight. Charles watched his soldiers deploy along the shore and felt in his heart that this kingdom was beginning to belong to him. But a salvo of heart-rending screams shattered his solemn thoughts: from the edge of the beach bordering the village, a hail of stones began to rain down on the soldiers with the fury of a biblical curse. Caught off guard, few managed to take cover in time. Several of these projectiles proved fatal.

“他们攻击我们……他们攻击我们！”卡洛斯喊道。

"They're attacking us... They're attacking us!" Carlos shouted.

即使在最意想不到的情况下，希耶夫尔也毫不退缩，冲上前去掩护他。海滩的地平线上，袭击者开始出现。村子里房屋不多，但毫无疑问，人群中没有一个村民。当地人自发地拿起棍棒和农具，朝着新来的入侵者冲去，互相呐喊鼓励。

Chièvres, resolute even in the most unexpected of situations, rushed to cover him for protection. On the horizon of the beach, the attackers began to appear. There were few houses in the village, but undoubtedly none of its inhabitants were missing from the throng. Spontaneously armed with sticks and farming implements, the locals rushed toward the newly arrived invaders, encouraging each other with shouts.

“异教徒去死！”村民们高声喊道。

"Death to the infidel!" roared the villagers.

“他们把我们当成土耳其人了！”希耶夫尔总结道。“三列纵队去救国王！”

"They're taking us for Turks!" Chièvres concluded. "Three columns of men to save the king!"

当士兵们响应号召，查理在他们的身体和武器的保护下时，希耶夫尔从衣服上取下挂在脖子上的十字架，放在胸前，使其显眼。紧接着，这位议员跳入水中。查理试图阻止他，但徒劳无功。他认出了这个奋力跃入水中的人；他曾在办公室里见过他无数次，像现在这样固执己见、精力充沛。他知道希耶夫尔在谈判中无所畏惧；此刻，他确信希耶夫尔害怕的与其说是死亡，不如说是野心受挫。

When the soldiers answered the call and Charles was protected by their bodies and weapons, Chièvres took a cross from his clothing, which he wore around his neck, and placed it on his chest to make it visible. Immediately afterward, the councilor jumped from the boat. Charles tried to stop him, but his efforts were in vain. He recognized the man advancing against the water's resistance; he had seen him a thousand times obstinately in the offices with the same vigor he displayed now. He knew that he was impervious to fear in negotiations; at that moment, he was certain that Chièvres was less afraid of death than of seeing his ambitions thwarted.

“至少要保护好自己！”卡洛斯无奈地说。

"At least shield yourselves!" Carlos resignedly said.

她的声音带着颤抖：如果说她抵达西班牙后有什么事是她始料未及的，那就是她会担心自己的生命安全。

Her voice revealed a tremor: if there was one thing she didn't expect from her arrival in Spain, it was to fear for her life.

但希耶夫尔置若罔闻。查理从船上，即便被守卫的士兵团团围住，也看到他的顾问已经出现在沙滩上，正走向武装的村民。村民们顿时停下脚步，惊愕不已。希耶夫尔胸前的十字架成了进攻者的威慑，他们此刻完全不明白自己面对的是谁。妇女们抱着孩子，从房屋的窗户里低声祈祷，希望入侵者至少是法国人。

But Chièvres paid no heed. From his boat, even though surrounded by the men guarding it, Charles spotted his advisor already on the beach, walking out to meet the armed villagers. They stopped dead in their tracks, bewildered. The cross Chièvres wore on his chest became a deterrent for the attackers, who now didn't understand who they were facing. From the windows of the houses, the women, clutching their children, murmured prayers that the invaders might at least be French.

“以应有的方式迎接你们的国王！否则你们将被视为叛徒，”希耶夫尔敦促他们。

"Receive your king as he deserves! Or you will be considered traitors," Chièvres urged them.

村民们愣住了。国王竟然降临在塔佐内斯这样偏僻简陋的村庄，这简直难以置信。这就是查理，伟大的费迪南和更伟大的伊莎贝拉的孙子，注定悲剧的菲利普和可怜的胡安娜的儿子，这位迟迟未到的异乡人。手中的棍棒和锄头一件件掉落在沙地上。

The villagers froze. The idea that the king had landed in Tazones, so modest and remote, was hard to grasp. So this was Charles, the grandson of the great Ferdinand and the even greater Isabella, the son of the doomed Philip and poor Joanna, the foreigner who was taking so long to arrive. One by one, the sticks and hoes fell onto the sand.

村民们平静下来后，查理抛开了心中残存的恐惧，下了船。他只走了几步，便站在了臣民面前。他们彼此对视。他们从未见过如此华丽的服饰，如此佛兰德斯式的风范，也从未见过他身后地平线上那些船只的样式。查理也从未感受过如此难以理解的目光。仿佛国王和臣民是两个素不相识的人，在圣坛前初次相遇，注定要结合，相伴终生；两个陌生人，尽管知道彼此的结合已成定局，却依然彼此猜疑，忐忑不安地看着对方，不知未来会如何。

Once the villagers were pacified, Charles renounced the fear he still felt and disembarked. In just a few steps, he stood before his subjects. They looked at each other. They had never seen such finery, such Flemish bearing, nor the design of those ships that formed a horizon behind him. Nor had Charles ever felt gazes that understood him so little. It seemed as if king and subjects were two strangers meeting for the first time at the altar, destined to unite and live together until death did them part; two strangers who, despite knowing they were bound to this union, still regarded each other with suspicion, wondering what future awaited them together.

 

 

 

 

几个小时后，一位来自塔佐内斯的邻居，几乎掩饰不住内心的紧张，将一盘煎蛋和猪油放在查尔斯面前。不愿露面的莱昂诺尔也吃了一份。这间房子，和村里其他所有房子一样，简陋得如同孩童的画作：四面光秃秃的墙壁，以及最基本的生活用品。建造它的人恐怕做梦也想不到，一位国王竟会被迫在此过夜。查尔斯、莱昂诺尔和希耶夫尔华丽的服饰在这简陋的环境中显得格外醒目，如同黑夜中的明月。村民用陶杯为他们斟上兑了水的葡萄酒，查尔斯感激地看着他，心中却渴望在如此简陋的环境中也能感到自在。主人略作歉意，便离开了。莱昂诺尔看着食物，仿佛既不理解，也不想理解。

A few hours later, a neighbor from Tazones, his nervousness barely concealed, placed a plate of fried eggs and lard before Charles. Leonor, unwilling to be seen, was also served one. The house, like all the others in the village, possessed the simplicity of a child's drawing: four bare walls and the bare essentials. Whoever had built it could never have imagined that a king would be obliged to spend the night there. The elaborate clothing of Charles, Leonor, and Chièvres stood out in the place like the moon on a dark night. The villager served them watered-down wine in earthenware cups under the grateful gaze of Charles, who wished he felt more at ease in such humble surroundings. The host apologized with a gesture before leaving them alone. Leonor looked at the food as if she neither understood it nor wanted to.

“我们本应该在拉雷多降落，”他说。

"We should have landed at Laredo," he said.

“暂时把你的梅赫伦口味放在一边吧，”卡洛斯一边拿起餐具总结道。

"Put your Mechelen palate aside for a moment," Carlos concluded as he picked up his cutlery.

埃莉诺听到“马林斯”这个名字，胸口顿时涌起一阵灼热感，但这并非因为她怀念她和查尔斯度过一生的宫廷，怀念自幼便在宫廷中感受的精致礼仪和奢华盛宴。埃莉诺听到“马林斯”这个名字，便想起了伯爵，仅存的一点食欲也随之消失殆尽。她将盘子递给查尔斯，查尔斯虽然带着责备的神情，但还是接了过去。

Eleanor heard "Malines" and felt a burning sensation in her chest, but not because she longed for the court where she and Charles had spent their lives, with its exquisite etiquette and festive luxury that had nurtured her since childhood. Eleanor heard "Malines" and thought of her count, and what little appetite she had left vanished. She offered her plate to Charles, who, though with a reproachful look, accepted it.

“说实话，这点礼物不足以弥补你对他们的恩情，”希耶夫斯说道。

—The truth is that it is a poor offering to compensate for the kindness you have shown them —said Chièvres.

“相信我，被石头击退比你更让我恼火，”君主回答说。“但他们对眼前这个自以为是土耳其人的愤怒，却让我十分欣慰。我该如何惩罚他们呢？”

“Believe me, being repelled by stones has upset me more than it has upset you,” replied the sovereign. “But the fury they felt toward the Turk they thought they had before them is quite pleasing. How can I punish them?”

希耶夫尔点了点头。他比查理更容易心生怨恨，但他明白，如果他们对那些接待他们的可怜人冷酷无情，那么在卡斯蒂利亚和阿拉贡等待他们的困难只会更大。在他看来，慷慨是一种可以偶尔使用的武器，即使使用后会让人感到不满。“说到底，这愚蠢之举也有其积极的一面，”希耶夫尔心想，“相比之下，我们在这些土地上将要面临的猜疑简直就像是轻柔的抚摸。”这位顾问花了几个月的时间，竭力向查理淡化他确信他们将要面临的种种问题，以确保他们能够登上西班牙王位。但说实话，国王只是假装相信希耶夫尔那些令人安心的预言。他心里清楚，真正的征程才刚刚开始。

Chièvres nodded. He was more inclined to resentment than Charles, but he knew that the difficulties awaiting them in Castile and Aragon would be greater if they were ruthless with those poor fools who had received them. Generosity seemed to him a weapon to be used from time to time, even if its use left one unsatisfied. "Deep down, this folly has its silver lining," Chièvres thought. "The suspicions that await us in these lands will seem like caresses in comparison." The advisor had spent months working to downplay for Charles the problems he was sure they would face in order to secure the throne of Spain. But, to tell the truth, the king had only pretended to believe Chièvres's reassuring predictions. He knew full well that the real journey was just beginning.

 

 

 

 

当卡斯蒂利亚宫廷得知查理抵达的消息时，沉寂了一年半的不安情绪骤然苏醒。窃窃私语声愈发密集，眼神中也充满了意味深长的意味。一年前被查理派往卡斯蒂利亚的乌得勒支的阿德里安，如今感觉自己如同现代的阿特拉斯，孤身一人捍卫着国王的旗帜，抵御着各种威胁。对于一位年近六十的老人来说，这无疑是一项艰巨的任务。诚然，自阿拉贡的费尔南多去世后，在查理的默许下摄政的西斯内罗斯红衣主教，一直忠于遗嘱中的安排，并承认这位佛兰德人为继承人。然而，当他得知国王在塔佐内斯登陆的消息时，他的反应却远非热情。红衣主教瘦削的身躯因愤怒而颤抖。

When the Castilian court received news of Charles's arrival, the unease that had lain dormant for a year and a half was suddenly awoke. Murmurs intensified. Glances became heavy with meaning. Adrian of Utrecht, sent to the kingdom by Charles a year earlier, felt like a modern-day Atlas, single-handedly upholding the king's banner against threats. A daunting task for someone nearly sixty years old. It was true that Cardinal Cisneros, regent of Spain with Charles's approval since the death of Ferdinand of Aragon, had remained faithful to the mandate stipulated in his will and had accepted the Fleming as his heir. But as soon as he learned of the king's landing at Tazones, his reaction was anything but enthusiastic. The cardinal's gaunt frame writhed with indignation.

—他怎能轻视拉雷多对他的热烈欢迎呢？

—How could he have scorned the welcome that awaited him in Laredo?

为西斯内罗斯看病的医生假装没听见，只有哈德良对他的话有所反应。这位来自乌得勒支的男人坐了下来，积蓄力量准备交谈。

The doctor attending Cisneros pretended not to hear, leaving only Hadrian to react to his words. The man from Utrecht took a seat, gathering his strength for the conversation.

“我想应该是暴风雨吧。”他回答道。

"Storms, I suppose," he replied.

——或者他对礼仪的蔑视，这一点他在布鲁塞尔已经有所体现。而且，我还没提到更重要的……

—Or a disdain for protocol, which he already demonstrated in Brussels. And consider that I'm omitting what was more of a…

红衣主教的几声咳嗽打断了这句话。阿德里亚诺松了口气；他已经厌倦了听到查理发动政变的指控。

The sentence was interrupted by a few coughs from the cardinal. Adriano was grateful; he was tired of hearing that accusation that Charles had staged a coup.

“你和我一样清楚，如果公告被推迟发布，你的摄政生涯就会以兄弟之间的战争而告终。”哈德良说道。

—You know as well as I do that if the proclamation had been delayed, you would have ended your regency with a war between brothers— said Hadrian.

西斯内罗斯没有力气同意，于是他保持沉默，一口气喝下了医生递给他的药水。他相信这药能让他免于一死。令他惊讶的是，他竟然不想死。上帝的旨意早已非常明确：祂要他留在祂身边。可是，他怎能抛下王国独自漂泊呢？

Cisneros lacked the strength to agree, so he remained silent and downed the potion the doctor offered him in one gulp. He trusted that this treatment would grant him a reprieve. He was surprised that he didn't want to die. God's will had been quite clear for some time: He wanted him with Him. But how could he leave the kingdom adrift?

“他宣布什么时候会和我见面了吗？”西斯内罗斯问道。

"Has he announced when he will meet with me?" Cisneros asked.

——道路会说明一切，阁下。

—The roads will tell, Your Eminence.

“让他快点走吧，否则我活不了多久了。我对他的忠诚远超卡斯蒂利亚所鼓励的。我曾为他辩护，即便没有理由。若非有我，他哥哥的支持者早就壮大了，他恐怕不得不拔剑相向，争夺王位。”

"Let him walk swiftly, or I won't live long enough. I have been more loyal to him than Castile encouraged me to be. I have defended him when there was no reason to do so. Without me, his brother's supporters would have gained strength long ago, and he would have had to fight for the crown with the sword."

“国王陛下已经知道您的帮助，阁下，”哈德良说道，“他很快就会与您会合。”

"The king knows of your help, Your Eminence," said Hadrian. "He will soon join you."

这个承诺并没有缓解红衣主教的紧迫感。

The promise did not calm the cardinal's urgency.

“这不仅仅是把摄政权移交给他的问题，而是要把我这些年来对这些王国的了解传授给他。你根本无法想象他需要知道的比现在多得多。”

"It's not just a matter of handing over the regency to him, but of instructing him on what I've learned over time about these kingdoms. You have no idea how much more he'll need to know than he already does."

房间里一片寂静，红衣主教陷入了沉思。

A silence fell over the room, leaving the cardinal deep in thought.

“我有时怀疑自己是不是带来了厄运，”西斯内罗斯说道。“你无法想象伊莎贝拉女王召我到她身边时，这宫廷是多么的辉煌。”他划了个十字。“要摧毁这一切辉煌，需要多么大的厄运啊。而这一切，正一波又一波地在我眼前上演。”

“Sometimes I wonder if I bring misfortune,” Cisneros said. “You can’t imagine the grandeur of this court when Queen Isabella summoned me to her side.” He crossed himself. “It took a great deal of bad luck to bring down all that splendor. The kind that has been unfolding, blow by blow, before my very eyes.”

“运气转瞬即逝，好运和厄运都一样。”阿德里亚诺反驳道，“要有信心。查理谨慎稳重，野心也恰到好处。他读的是伊拉斯谟，而不是马基雅维利。他跟菲利普截然不同。儿子会抹去父亲留下的污点。”

“Luck is fleeting. Both good and bad,” Adriano countered. “Have faith. Charles is prudent and has just the right amount of ambition. He reads Erasmus, not Machiavelli. He’s nothing like Philip. The son will erase the bad memory of his father.”

—到目前为止，他在这里受到的指控全是过错：他发布的公告，任命那个来自希耶夫尔的人担任王国首席会计师……

—So far, all he's been accused of here are faults: his proclamation, appointing that Chièvres fellow as chief accountant of the kingdom…

“良好的治理是可以学习的，”哈德良赶紧说道，以免他把那些他知道还有很多不足之处一一列举出来。“陛下，您现在无需怀疑。”

"Good governance is learned," Hadrian hastened to say, preventing the list of faults, which he knew was longer, from being enumerated in full. "Do not doubt now, Your Eminence."

“王国才会怀疑，我不会，”他宣称。

"The kingdom doubts, not I," he declared.

——费尔南多呢？他有疑虑吗？

—And Fernando? Does he have doubts?

在乌得勒支人面前，西斯内罗斯将上次与胡安娜和菲利普之子——那个卡斯蒂利亚人——的会面记忆藏在心底。年轻人内心深处似乎在否定他对查理所说的每一句服从之言。他的目光中充满了对命运的反抗。“我愿做我兄弟的封臣，因为这是我祖父的遗愿。”他说道。然而，尽管他的话语听起来合情合理，他的眉宇间却写满了愤慨：不公！

Cisneros kept to himself the memory of his last encounter with the Castilian son of Juana and Philip, before the man from Utrecht. Something in the young man denied every word of obedience he uttered to Charles. His gaze rebelled against fate. "I will be a vassal of my brother, for that is what my grandfather wished," he said. But although his words seemed sensible, his brow cried out: Injustice!

 

 

 

 

奥地利的斐迪南的府邸客厅里，近几个月来西班牙的众多显贵都曾跪拜于此，仿佛随时都会形成一个弹坑。但当时，无人敢在那里露面，尤其是在摄政王西斯内罗斯惊恐万分，派出大批密探监视任何针对查理的阴谋之后。猜忌笼罩着斐迪南，使他陷入了孤独。那天早晨，像往常一样，他骑马穿过巴利亚多利德的田野。太阳躲在乌云后面。斐迪南凝视着乌云，顿时觉得自己难以理解。他应该感到轻松才对；难道这不正是他所渴望的吗？他希望阴谋诡计就此停止。希望他们不再考验他的忠诚。他希望卡拉特拉瓦大司令不再坚持认为他而非查理才是王位的继承人。他希望阿斯托尔加主教不再带着轻蔑的冷笑称他的兄弟为“外国篡位者”。 “史上最伟大的国王，唐·费尔南多，提拔你来统治。”阴谋者的话语如同毒药般侵蚀着他：并非猛烈袭来，却最终令他感到不适。他本该感到庆幸，因为他已经很久没听到这些话了。然而，在圣克里斯托瓦尔山脚下，寂静仿佛凝固，不安的情绪却挥之不去。该死的毒药。或许，它早已潜藏在他体内。

A crater could easily have formed in the drawing room of Ferdinand of Austria's residence, so many of Spain's grandees had knelt there in recent months. But at that time, no one dared to be seen there, especially since the regent Cisneros, filled with alarm, had sent out a flock of spies to report any conspiracy against Charles. Suspicion had condemned Ferdinand to solitude. That morning, like almost every other, he went riding through the fields of Valladolid. The sun was hiding behind storm clouds. Ferdinand gazed at them and immediately thought he was incomprehensible. He should feel relieved; wasn't that what he wanted? For the intrigues to cease. For them to stop testing his loyalty. For the Grand Commander of Calatrava to stop insisting that he, and not Charles, was the one who deserved the throne. For the Bishop of Astorga to stop calling his brother a "foreign usurper," with a sneer of contempt. "The greatest king there ever was, Don Fernando, raised you to rule." The conspirators' words, as they were spoken, had attacked him like poison: not violently, but ultimately making him ill. He should have felt relieved, yes, because he hadn't had to hear them for some time. But the silence seemed solid then, at the foot of San Cristóbal Hill, and the unease remained. That damned poison. Perhaps he already carried it within him.

 

 

 

 

费尔南多从乡间回来，浑身冰冷。他上午在乡间转了一圈，既没打猎，也没停下来生火取暖。他只是漫无目的地骑马兜圈，脸色冻僵，眼眶里噙满了泪水。走进书房，他发现有人在等他。那人衣着低调奢华，已然成熟稳重，身形如同他的原则一样坚定。费尔南多很了解他；所有人都认识法德里克·阿尔瓦雷斯·德·托莱多，西班牙的贵族，阿尔瓦公爵。过去几个月里，他频繁造访莫哈多斯，拜访王子的府邸。每次的场景都如出一辙：法德里克居高临下的语气；偶尔会提起费迪南国王，阿尔瓦公爵曾为他忠诚侍奉多年；那些看似无害但实则不然的问题，以及给出的建议，总是千篇一律：“忠诚是男人最大的价值”，“查尔斯需要我们的帮助”，“不要听那些要求你背叛的人的话，他们不是在为你服务，而是在为自己服务。”

Fernando returned chilled from his morning in the countryside. He had neither hunted nor stopped to build a fire to warm himself. His spirits had only allowed him to ride aimlessly in circles, his face freezing and his eyes welling with tears. When he entered the study, he saw that someone was waiting for him. It was a man dressed with understated luxury, already mature, with a figure as solid as his principles. Fernando knew him well; everyone knew Fadrique Álvarez de Toledo, Grandee of Spain, Duke of Alba, well. His visits to Mojados, to the Infante's residence, had been frequent over the last few months. They had all unfolded in the same way: Fadrique's paternalistic tone; here and there a remembrance of King Ferdinand, whom the Duke of Alba had served zealously for years; The questions that seemed innocuous but were not, and the advice, always the same: "Loyalty is a man's greatest value," "Charles needs our service," "Do not listen to those who ask you for betrayal, they do not serve you, only themselves."

你哥哥已经在卡斯蒂利亚了。

—Your brother is already in Castile.

费尔南多已经做好了听到这些话的准备很久了，以至于当他最终听到这些话时，他却没有任何感觉。

Fernando had been preparing himself to hear those words for so long that when he finally heard them he felt nothing.

——现在是时候证明你并非仅仅出身高贵了。殿下，请忠于你祖父的遗愿。

—The time has come for you to prove that you are not noble only by birth. Loyalty to your grandfather's wishes, Your Highness.

 

 

 

 

夜幕降临，费尔南多再次骑马出门。阿尔巴公爵的警告激起了他心中一股怒火，他自己也意识到这怒火幼稚得像个孩子，就像他祖父——那位国王——纠正他每一个错误时激起的怒火一样；那种明知自己错了却又痛恨被人提醒的无理怒火。费尔南多的马蹄声在他离开宫殿时显得格外刺耳。他想让西斯内罗斯的密探跟踪他，向红衣主教汇报，让整个王国都在紧张的窃窃私语中议论他的名字。

As night fell, Fernando rode out again. The Duke of Alba's warnings had stirred in him an anger he himself recognized as childish, like the anger his grandfather the king provoked when correcting his every mistake; that unjust anger of one who knows he is wrong but hates to be reminded of it. The hooves of Fernando's horse echoed indiscreetly as he left his palace behind. He wanted Cisneros's spies to follow him, to report to the cardinal, for the entire kingdom to whisper his name in nervous hushed conversations.

在杰尔玛娜·德·福瓦的府邸，夜总是漫长难眠。这位阿拉贡国王费尔南多的遗孀，长久以来都害怕入睡。噩梦总是如出一辙：一片无边无际的沙漠，她只在传说中见过它的模样；一个神圣的声音驱使着她穿越这片沙漠，走向一个她能感知却看不见的尽头。她第一次做这个梦，是在丈夫去世的那天。当时，西班牙正为如何处置这位麻烦的寡妇而苦恼，这位傲慢的女人，美丽却又过于精明，这位法国女人甚至没能为国王生下一个儿子，让他与这些王国联姻。再说，她还太年轻，没人会怜悯她。十八岁就已成家，二十八岁就成了寡妇。在位期间，杰尔玛娜从未试图讨好她的臣民，因为她知道自己的罪孽是原罪，无可挽回：她不是伊莎贝拉，却占据了她的床榻。那些年里，他几乎没能培养出任何感情，而那天晚上，他的爱人就出现在他家门口，嘴唇被凛冽的寒风吹得发紫，头发凌乱，刚刚下马：费尔南多。

At Germana de Foix's residence, the nights were long. The widow of Ferdinand of Aragon had long been afraid to sleep. The nightmare was always the same: an endless desert, the likes of which she only knew from tales, and a divine voice compelling her to traverse it to an end she sensed but could not see. She had first dreamt it the day her husband died, when Spain had wondered what to do with this troublesome widow, this haughty woman, beautiful but excessively shrewd, this Frenchwoman who hadn't even given the king a son to unite with these kingdoms. Besides, she was too young for them to take pity on her. Eighteen and a wife, twenty-eight and a widow. While she was consort, Germana never tried to charm her subjects, because she knew her sin was original, irreparable: she wasn't Isabella, but she occupied her bed. In those years he had barely been able to form a single affection, and that night that affection was at his door, with lips purple from the cutting wind and hair disheveled, having just dismounted: Fernando.

 

 

 

 

在杰尔马纳的客厅里，除了这位前王后之外，任何人都能坐得下，费尔南多和她各自落座了。

In Germana's living room, spacious enough for anyone except for the former queen, Fernando and she took their seats.

“我写了十封信才让你来看我，”杰尔马纳说。

—It took me ten letters to get you to visit me —Germana said.

别生气。你的留言我也没理会，其他人的留言我也一样。

—Don't be offended. I've ignored yours as well as everyone else's.

——而你后悔自己做了这件事。

—And you regret having done it.

费尔南多抿了一口白兰地，嘴唇火辣辣的疼。他注意到，杰尔马娜却毫不犹豫地喝了下去，仿佛那是甘露。“我真希望自己也有那样的力气，”他心想。杰尔马娜虽然只比他大九岁，却是他最亲近的人，如同母亲一般。住在托尔德西利亚斯的那个女人，对他来说不过是个令人羞愧的负担。费尔南多和杰尔马娜的童年虽然与国家有关，但他们从未缺少过关爱，那是他唯一感受到的温暖。

Fernando took a sip from a glass of brandy. It burned his lips. He noticed that Germana, on the other hand, drank it without flinching, as if it were nectar. "I wish I had that strength," he thought to himself. Although barely nine years older than him, she was the closest thing he had to a mother. The one who lived in Tordesillas was little more than a shameful burden to him. His childhood had been a state affair for Fernando and Germana, but there had been no lack of loving care, the only warmth he had ever received.

“我丈夫生前更偏爱你，”杰尔马纳说。“遗嘱的内容和现在不一样了。”

"My husband favored you," Germana said. "The will wasn't what it is now."

费尔南多不知道该说什么，也不知道该如何化解内心的挣扎：一方面是服从，另一方面是骄傲的愤怒。一年前，在他祖父修改遗嘱中的几个字之前，他原本要成为国王。

Fernando didn't know what to say, how to resolve the battle raging inside him between obedience and the proud rage of someone who, a year ago, before his grandfather changed just a few letters in his last will and testament, was going to be king.

“如果这些王国还没有保持沉默，那么它们在说什么呢？”费尔南多问道。

"What are the kingdoms saying, if they haven't already fallen silent?" asked Fernando.

他们都跪倒在你面前。红衣主教孤立你的伎俩收效甚微。查理在西班牙人民心中已遭谴责。一个未经母亲同意便自立为王、背叛母亲的人，还能指望他什么呢？哪个坏儿子能成为好国王？

—They kneel before you. The cardinal's maneuvers to isolate you have had little effect. Charles is condemned in the hearts of the Spanish people. What can be expected of one who has disloyal his own mother by proclaiming himself king without her consent? What bad son makes a good king?

—你在说我哥哥。

—You're talking about my brother.

“背叛查理反而是你对卡斯蒂利亚和阿拉贡最大的忠诚，”杰尔马纳回答道，“你生于此，你热爱这片土地，这片土地也爱你。”

—Disloyalty to Charles would be the greatest show of devotion to Castile and Aragon you could give—replied Germana. —You were born here, you love these lands and you are loved by them.

杰尔玛娜凝视着费尔南多的双眼，心想自己对他那份强烈的依恋是否是所有母亲的通病。但她并没有错：她知道自己是自私自利、务实的。她之所以希望费尔南多登上王位，主要是因为有了他掌权，她的未来就不会像一片茫茫沙漠般荒芜。相反，卡洛斯却是个未知数。这位来自根特的男人统治之后会如何处置她？让她在无人问津的宫殿里苟延残喘？或许给她一个微薄的收入，却只能得到一个爵位？又或许把她昔日的伴侣变成一个永远的拜金女？

Germana looked into Fernando's eyes and wondered if the demanding affection she felt for him was typical of mothers. But she wasn't mistaken: she knew she was self-serving, pragmatic. If she wanted Fernando on the throne, it was primarily because with him in charge, her future wouldn't resemble a vast desert to traverse. On the contrary, Carlos was an unknown quantity. What would the man from Ghent do with her when he ruled? Let her languish in a palace that received no one, offer her perhaps a title with a paltry income; turn her former consort into a perpetual gold digger.

杰尔玛娜一言不发地离开了房间。她回来时，握住费尔南多的手，小心翼翼地掰开，如同捧开一朵花。然后，她将一枚戒指放在他的掌心。他看着戒指，倒吸了一口气，因为他突然觉得好像少了点什么。

Without a word, Germana left the room. When she returned, she took Fernando's hand and opened it carefully, like a flower. Then she dropped a ring into his palm. He looked at it and gasped, because he suddenly felt something was missing.

“这是皇家印章，”费尔南多宣布道。

"The royal seal," Fernando announced.

—你爷爷一定会希望这件东西是给你的。

—Your grandfather would have wanted it to be for you.

费尔南多仔细端详着那枚戒指，觉得他从中看到了自己的倒影：他的脸被戒指的弧度扭曲，他金色的脸庞。

Fernando studied the ring and thought he saw himself reflected in it: his face deformed by the curvature, his golden face.

—亲爱的，如果你不采取行动，这将是你唯一能拥有的王者之物。

—If you don't act, my dear, it will be the only kingly thing you'll ever have.

 

 

 

 

一队马车、四轮马车和骑兵在目瞪口呆的男男女女的注视下缓缓前行。他们出来是为了核实那些传言是否属实。然而，就在他们眼前，卡斯蒂利亚的旗帜赫然出现，在狂风的吹拂下摇曳不定。在利亚内斯的道路上，从未有人见过如此景象。即使是陌生人、乞讨的官员或商人，走这条路也已是司空见惯；更何况是国王！这片土地仿佛对行者的尊严毫不在意，遍布的碎石和崎岖的地形令车队难以保持稳定。在皇家马车内，查理五世的脸色苍白，被层层叠叠的皮毛包裹着，随着马车的摇晃而滑落。希耶夫尔和埃莉诺虽然也裹得严严实实，却比查理五世更能抵御寒冷。

A line of carts, carriages, and cavalry advanced under the gaze of astonished men and women. They had come out to verify that the rumors were false. But there it was, before their eyes, the banner of Castile, barely staying still because of a ferocious wind. On the roads of Llanes, no one had ever seen anything like it. It was already unusual for a stranger, a begging official, or a merchant to travel them; but the king! The ground, indifferent to the dignity of the one who trod it, hampered the caravan's stability with stones and uneven terrain. Inside the royal carriage, Charles was a pale head under layers and layers of furs that slipped with the swaying of the vehicle. Chièvres and Eleanor, although also wrapped up, withstood the cold better.

“我想我还记得母亲的香水味，”卡洛斯喃喃道，“不是她的眼睛，也不是她的手。”

—I think I remember my mother's perfume— Carlos murmured. —Not her eyes, or her hands.

“我对她的脸印象很深；我八岁的时候就看到她离开前往卡斯蒂利亚了，”莱昂诺尔说。

—I do have a good memory of her face; I was already eight years old when I saw her leave for Castile—said Leonor.

—你很幸运能珍藏这份回忆。

—You are fortunate to treasure that memory.

-真的吗？

-Really?

有时，希耶夫尔的计划竟如此顺利，令他自己都感到惊讶。前往托尔德西利亚斯而非在巴利亚多利德会见西斯内罗斯红衣主教的政治原因，早已从查理的脑海中淡去。如今，一切都围绕着胡安娜以及与她的会面。正如顾问所预料的那样，国王毫不犹豫地追问，为何他们不先去会见那位垂死的摄政王，她渴望见到他，并将权力交还给他。查理一心想要解开母亲的谜团，以至于无暇顾及其他。顾问的一句话就足以让他信服：“只要我们获得胡安娜的支持，布鲁塞尔那些反对你宣言的声音就会消失。红衣主教可以等等。”“但愿上帝保佑，他会先被除掉，”希耶夫尔心想。他暗自希望这位一直忠心耿耿、勤勉尽责的红衣主教早点死去，这丝毫没有让他感到痛苦。事实上，如果不是因为查理阻碍了他最主要的目的——让查理完全在他的影响下掌控西班牙，而自己这个老者——不让查理从其权威和智慧的地位上，向这个年轻人灌输哪怕一丝他不希望查理拥有的想法，希耶夫尔本会祝愿他长寿。为了让天意有时间在红衣主教身上发挥作用，希耶夫尔特意选择了从阿斯图里亚斯到托尔德西利亚斯最长、最迂回的路线。

Sometimes Chièvres was surprised at how well his plans worked. The political reasons for heading to Tordesillas, and not to meet with Cardinal Cisneros in Valladolid, had faded from Charles's mind. Now everything revolved around Joanna and meeting her. Just as the advisor had predicted, the king hadn't asked twice why they weren't first meeting with a dying regent who was eager to see him and hand over the reins of power. Charles's desire to finally unravel the enigma that was his mother prevented him from thinking of anything else. A single sentence from the advisor had been enough to convince him: "The voices that have risen against your proclamation in Brussels will be silenced when we secure Joanna's support. The cardinal can wait." "But God willing, he'll be taken first," Chièvres thought. Wishing a swift death upon the cardinal, who had always been diligent and loyal to them, caused no distress whatsoever in Chièvres's heart. In truth, he would have wished him a long life had he not been an obstacle to his primary interest: that Charles assume command of Spain solely under his influence, without this old man, from his position of authority and wisdom, instilling in the young man even a single idea that the advisor did not wish him to have. To allow Providence time to work its magic on the cardinal, Chièvres had chosen the longest and most circuitous route to travel from Asturias to Tordesillas.

 

 

 

 

西斯内罗斯的间谍只用了几个小时就向摄政王通报了费迪南王子拜访日耳曼娜·德·福瓦的消息，不久之后，这位遗孀又接见了阴谋派的头目。红衣主教从未预料到费迪南国王的遗孀会做出什么事，但他一直觉得她最终会惹出麻烦。西斯内罗斯懊恼不已。他认为查理的缺席助长了阴谋者的气焰，而他的归来将终结一切针对他的阴谋。然而，即将亲眼目睹国王登上王位的焦虑，却也刺激着那些不希望他登基的人。

Cisneros's spies took only a few hours to inform the regent of Prince Ferdinand's visit to Germana de Foix, and that shortly afterward the widow received the ringleaders of the conspiratorial faction. The cardinal had never known what to expect from King Ferdinand's widow, but he had always sensed that she would eventually cause trouble. Cisneros cursed his calculation. He believed that Charles's absence had fueled the conspirators, and that his arrival would put an end to any maneuvers against him. But the anxiety of finally seeing the king on his way to the throne was spurring on those who did not want him there.

孩子会心生疑虑。

—The child will doubt.

西斯内罗斯低声向乌得勒支的阿德里安说了这不祥之兆，阿德里安只听了这五个字，便立刻冲到书桌前，用他能想到的最惊恐的语气起草了一封信。收信人：希耶夫尔。

Cisneros muttered his ill omen to Adrian of Utrecht, who needed only those five words to rush to his desk and draft a letter in the most alarming tone he could muster. The recipient: Chièvres.

 

 

 

 

卡洛斯已经好几个小时没看窗外的景色了，那是一望无际的群山和翠绿的山谷。旅途让他疲惫不堪，因为他没想到会这么漫长。他能忍受马车的摇晃和潮湿的寒冷，却无法忍受即将再次见到母亲时心中日益增长的不安。在他的一生中，胡安娜只不过是一个被低声细语提及的名字。人们提起她，本来就很少，而且随着她永远无法离开卡斯蒂利亚的禁锢，这些提及也渐渐消失了。提醒一个孩子，几百里之外还住着一个影子，又有什么意义呢？只有偶尔失言的家庭教师才会告诉他一些卡洛斯宁愿不知道的事情。所以，他相信，当他请求母亲将统治的重任交给他时，自己不会遭受太多的痛苦。他将向一个陌生人提出这样的要求，而这个人，无论是国王费迪南德，还是他的父亲菲利普，甚至是摄政王西斯内罗斯，都从未希望他登上王位。

Carlos hadn't looked out at the landscape for hours, a continuous expanse of mountains and verdant valleys. The journey was tiring him, for he hadn't imagined it would be so long. He could endure the swaying of the carriage and the damp cold, but not the growing unease he felt at the prospect of seeing his mother again. Throughout his life, Juana had been little more than a name whispered in hushed tones. The mentions of her, never many, had faded as the certainty grew that she would never leave her Castilian confinement. What would have been the point of reminding a child that a shadow dwelled hundreds of leagues away? Only the occasional indiscreet governess had told him things Carlos wished he didn't know. So he trusted he wouldn't suffer too much when he asked his mother to leave him the task of reigning. He would be demanding it of a stranger whom no one—not King Ferdinand, nor his father Philip, nor the regent Cisneros—had ever wanted on the throne.

车队上方天空裂开一道缝隙。片刻之后，倾盆大雨肆虐而来，将队伍彻底淹没。从无名的帮手到国王本人，所有人都争先恐后地寻找避雨之处。查理一边在路边寻找可以躲避的岩石，一边感谢上帝让他从沉思中解脱出来。

The sky cracked above the caravan. Moments later, a torrential downpour unleashed its fury upon the entourage. The scramble for shelter mobilized everyone, from the nameless helper to the king himself. As he searched the roadside for a rocky outcrop to take refuge under, Charles thanked God for having been pulled from his thoughts.

 

 

 

 

—独角兽擦伤了，殿下两天后就会康复。

—Unicorn scrapes and His Highness will recover in two days.

谢夫尔很高兴在这次被迫停留期间找到了一位能干的医生。卡洛斯坐在深红色的大扶手椅上，隔着皮草咳嗽着。他们现在住的房间比在塔佐内斯住的那间要体面得多。帕伦西亚似乎也没做好接待他们的准备，但自从他们抵达后，当地的贵族们就竭尽全力地营造出一种截然不同的假象。卡洛斯正在服药，这时一个身影怯生生地从门口走了出来。

Chièvres was pleased to have found a resourceful doctor during this forced stop. Carlos coughed through his furs, seated in a large maroon armchair. The room they were in was far more dignified than the one where they had stayed in Tazones. Palencia wasn't ready to receive them either, but since their arrival, the local gentry had gone to great lengths to make it seem otherwise. Carlos was taking his medicine when a figure timidly appeared from the doorway.

-威严？

-Majesty?

卡洛斯和希耶夫斯环顾四周，寻找声音的来源。那人一身大主教的法衣，足以吸引他们加入。

Carlos and Chièvres looked around, searching for the source of the voice. The newcomer's archbishop's vestments were enough to invite him to join them.

“请将布尔戈斯大主教视为您最忠诚的仆人，”来访者说着，便匍匐在查理面前。“我愿向您宣誓效忠。”

"Consider the Archbishop of Burgos as your most loyal servant," said the visitor, now prostrate before Charles. "I wish to swear to you due obedience."

查尔斯发烧了，他听完了大主教的誓词。誓词结束后，他仍然渴望独处，便请客人坐下。客人看着希耶夫尔，等着他离开，但这位议员却像钉子一样纹丝不动，仿佛双脚被钉在了地上。大主教别无选择，只能接受他的存在。

Charles, feverish, listened to the archbishop's oath. When it was finished, and still desiring solitude more than anything else, he offered his guest a seat. The latter looked at Chièvres, waiting for him to leave them alone, but the councilor remained rooted to the spot as if his feet were nailed to the ground. The archbishop had no choice but to accept his presence.

——我是众多即将向你宣誓效忠的人中的第一个。卡斯蒂利亚与你同在。不要理会那些持相反观点的人。

—I am the first of many who are on their way to swear allegiance to you. Castile is with you. Ignore those who say otherwise.

“他们现在还这么说吗？”希耶夫尔问道。

"Are they still saying that?" Chièvres asked.

大主教急于表明自己的忠诚，开始讲述各种谣言和闲话，贵族间的窃窃私语，以及那些夜晚费迪南王子的名字被反复提及的种种传闻。查尔斯凝视着这位顾问，顾问脸上带着微笑，仿佛他们正在聆听一首诗，而不是针对他们的阴谋诡计。大主教确信，他此行拜访托尔德西利亚斯的胡安娜王后，足以让费迪南派系像泥土溶于水般土崩瓦解。

The archbishop, eager to demonstrate his loyalty, launched into a tale of rumors and gossip, whispers among nobles, and evenings where the name of Prince Ferdinand was mentioned far too often. Charles gazed at the advisor, who smiled as if they were listening to poetry instead of intrigues against them. The archbishop was certain that his visit to Queen Joanna in Tordesillas would be enough to make the Ferdinand faction dissolve like dirt in water.

“费迪南的忠诚毋庸置疑，”希耶夫尔难以置信地说，“任何试图通过给他描绘一个荒谬的未来来威胁他的忠诚的人，都已经为此受到了惩罚。”

"Ferdinand's loyalty is beyond question," said Chièvres, incredulous. "And whoever tried to threaten it by painting an absurd future for him has already been punished for it."

大主教犹豫着是否该纠正希耶夫雷斯，解释人们对他们的不信任依然存在，卡斯蒂利亚授予弗拉芒人的官职激怒了许多人，西班牙接管的布鲁塞尔宫廷开支过高，以及他公告的合法性也受到了质疑。但他何必给国王蒙上阴影呢？那样一来，他岂不是会永远背负厄运的印记，就像一个无人怀念的预言家？因此，他只选择消除一个疑虑，而这却代表了许多人的心声。

The archbishop wondered whether he should correct Chièvres and explain that mistrust of them still existed, that the Castilian offices granted to Flemish people had outraged many, that the expenses of the Brussels court, which Spain had assumed, had been considered excessive, and that the legitimacy of his proclamation had been questioned. But what need did he have to cast a shadow over the king? He would thus be forever marked with an aura of misfortune, like the soothsayer whom no one remembers fondly. Therefore, he chose only to allow himself to dispel one doubt, and he spoke for many.

他们还说，你和法国的……友谊如此深厚，以至于纳瓦拉很快就会重回法国手中。这只是谣言，不是吗？

—They also say that your… friendship with France is such that Navarre will soon return to their hands. Rumors, aren't they?

 

 

 

 

——命运眷顾。

—Blessed be destiny.

这就是法国国王弗朗索瓦一世对查理抵达卡斯蒂利亚王国的全部表态。在昂布瓦兹城堡的议事厅里，人们早已习惯国王对国事漠不关心，但一向严谨的蒙莫朗西男爵却要求他详细解释此事。

That was all Francis I of France had to say about Charles's arrival in the kingdom of Castile. In the council chamber of the Château d'Amboise, they were accustomed to the king dismissing matters of state without much interest, but the Baron de Montmorency, always meticulous, demanded that he elaborate on the matter.

“什么问题？”弗朗西斯科问道。“他的父亲是法国的封臣，他现在是，将来也会是封臣。”

—What question? —Francisco asked—. His father was a vassal of France, and he is and will be a vassal.

尽管弗朗西斯登上王位并非出于他的出身，而是得益于他母亲萨伏依的路易丝的才能，但凡见过他的人都会说，他那副模样，除了挥舞权杖，别无所适从。他两米高的身高和宽阔的肩膀，让他绝不会屈服于任何人。他那高挺的鼻子，便是他坚定意志的化身。唯有他那纷繁复杂、恣意妄为的欲望，才能勉强约束着他。他生来就贪得无厌，一个奶妈根本无法满足他的胃口。而且，他的食欲并未随着时间的流逝而减弱，只是不再局限于温热的牛奶，而是转化为对土地、爱人和知识的渴求。他如此精力充沛，又怎会惧怕一个年轻的佛兰德斯人呢？这个佛兰德斯人在被拥立为西班牙国王后不久，就急忙提醒法国，他仍然是法国的附庸。此事并未让弗朗西斯感到困扰，他趁着枢密院会议之机，重读了两天前收到的那封信。此后，这封信便一直伴随着他。“你想要我做什么？”他读着，顿时激动起来。弗朗西斯卡·德·福瓦的字迹如同她本人一样优美流畅，有些字母还带有蜿蜒的笔画，国王将其解读为对感官享受的承诺。

Although it wasn't his birthright, but rather the skill of his mother, Louise of Savoy, that had brought Francis to the throne, anyone who saw him would have said that his appearance was suited for nothing other than wielding a scepter. His two meters of height and broad shoulders precluded any submission to another. His imposing nose was his determination made flesh. Only his desires, as varied as they were imperious, kept him in check. He had been born insatiable; a single wet nurse was not enough to feed him. And his appetite hadn't diminished with time; it had merely ceased to be confined to warm milk and transformed into a thirst for lands, lovers, and knowledge. How could he, with such boundless energy, feel threatened by a young Flemish man who, shortly after being proclaimed King of Spain, had hastened to remind France that he remained its vassal? The matter bothered Francis so little that he took advantage of the council to reread the letter he had received two days earlier, which had since accompanied him everywhere he went. "What do you want from me?" he read, and became excited. Francisca de Foix's handwriting was as fine and sharp as she was, with sinuous flourishes in some letters, which the king interpreted as a promise of sensuality.

“你与查理签订的《努瓦永条约》并非如此乐观的理由，”他的母亲总是乐于提供建议，她解释道，“不过，没有什么比你的自信更能指引法国前进，我的凯撒。”

"The Treaty of Noyon that you signed with Charles is no reason for such optimism," his mother clarified, always offering advice. "Although nothing guides France better than your confidence, my Caesar."

严苛与奉献之间难以平衡：这就是萨伏依的路易丝与弗朗索瓦之间的关系。自从弗朗索瓦在她出生时撕裂了她的子宫，国王的母亲便不再为自己而活。他们之间的第一眼便缔结了契约，而命运似乎也印证了这一点：弗朗索瓦的叔叔路易十二世膝下无嗣。然而，血缘并非一切；真正重要的是路易丝，她早年丧夫，将毕生精力都奉献给了她的女儿玛格丽特和弗朗索瓦，尤其对后者倾注了无限的爱与雄心。弗朗索瓦登基后，立刻起身奔赴他的第一场战役，仿佛他一直压抑着自己的力量，而王冠终于释放了他全部的潜能。凭借马里尼亚诺战役的胜利，他不仅征服了米兰，更实现了他最大的愿望：让欧洲知道，这位新任法国国王将以其胆识开创一个时代。路易莎珍视自己娇小的身躯所获得的世间一切关注，而这种贪婪在她儿子身上体现得淋漓尽致，那个身材魁梧的男人似乎印证了她的想法：她耗尽了自己的所有精力，只为让他变得高大。

The impossible balance between severity and devotion: such was Louise of Savoy with Francis. The king's mother had not lived for herself since he had torn her womb at birth. The first glance between them had sealed a pact, one that fate reinforced by leaving King Louis XII, Francis's uncle, without an heir. But blood ties were not everything; rather, it was Louise, whose early widowhood had left her entire life to dedicate to her children Margaret and Francis, with boundless devotion and ambition toward the latter. As soon as he had ascended the throne, he rose to depart for his first battle, as if he had been holding back his strength and the crown had finally unleashed it. With his victory at Marignano, he had not only conquered Milan, but also achieved what he most desired: for Europe to know that the new King of France was going to mark an era with his audacity. Luisa treasured all the attention in the world in her petite body, and that greed was personified in her son, in that man whose enormous stature seemed to prove her right: she had consumed herself to aggrandize him.

——别太自信。查理被认为是个软弱无能的年轻人，但卡斯蒂利亚人会利用他们对法国的仇恨来陷害他，他会利用这一点来觊觎勃艮第，谁知道呢，说不定还能得到我为你赢得的米兰公国。

—Don't be overconfident. Charles is considered a spineless young man, but the Castilians will rush to poison him with their hatred of France, and he will use this to his advantage to aspire to Burgundy and who knows, perhaps even the Duchy of Milan that I won for you.

说这番话的是波旁公爵。他的话语虽不全无道理，却总能激起弗朗索瓦一丝不悦。国王见到他时，看到的并非一位目光精明、举止高贵的绅士，而是奥弗涅和沙泰勒罗公爵；蒙庞西耶、吉安、马尔什、克莱蒙昂奥弗涅和弗雷兹伯爵领主；孔布赖耶、博若莱、罗阿奈、梯也尔和阿诺奈伯爵领主。这些头衔大多是他与法国安妮体弱多病的女儿苏珊娜·德·波旁结婚后获得的，但他的显赫地位令弗朗索瓦十分恼火，弗朗索瓦也并不在意这显赫地位是源于出身还是得益于这桩有利的婚姻。他是法国唯一一个被国王视为臣民的人。他任命他为法国军队总司令兼米兰总督，米兰是波旁王朝在战场上夺取的瑰宝。然而，弗朗西斯试图用这些特权来最终确立自己的优越地位（一个人真的能慷慨对待一个超越自己的人吗？），但这并没有缓和他对弗朗西斯的敌意。或许这源于这位法国君主对公爵所代表的家族根深蒂固的仇恨。不久之前，国王的家族——昂古莱姆家族——还因与邻近的波旁王朝相比地位低下而蒙羞。弗朗西斯利用王位使自己的家族富裕起来，以此弥补那段不光彩的过去，但再多的黄金也无法让国王相信，这位公爵的显赫地位足以与他匹敌。

The one who said this was the Duke of Bourbon. His words, though not always misguided, always provoked a spasm of displeasure in Francis. When the king laid eyes on him, he didn't see a refined man with a shrewd gaze and eternally dignified bearing, but rather the Duke of Auvergne and Chatellerault; the lord of the counties of Montpensier and Gien, Marche and Clermont-en-Auvergne, and Forez; the lord of Combrailles, Beaujolais, Roannais, Thiers, and Annonay. Most of these titles were bestowed upon him upon his marriage to Susanna of Bourbon, the ailing daughter of Anne of France, but his grandeur was such that it exasperated Francis, and he cared little whether its origin lay in birth or in such an advantageous marriage. He was the only man in France whom the monarch did not perceive as the subject he was meant to be. He had appointed him commander of the French armies and governor of Milan, a jewel the Bourbons had won on the battlefield. But the privileges, with which Francis had sought to finally assert his superiority (can a man truly afford to be generous to someone who surpasses him?), had not softened his animosity toward him. Perhaps it stemmed from the French monarch's enduring hatred for the lineage the duke represented. Not so long ago, the king's house, that of Angoulême, had lived in shame of its insignificance compared to its neighbors, the Bourbons. Francis had used the crown to enrich his family and thus compensate for that inglorious past, but no amount of gold could convince the king that the duke did not rival him in eminence.

“查理和我一样都是我的封臣，”国王说道，“他的地位越高，对我的影响力就越大。但我会听从你的建议，提防他，就像我提防你一样。”

“Charles is as much my vassal as you are,” said the monarch. “The higher his rank, the greater he will make me. But I will heed your advice and beware of him. As much as I beware of you.”

“殿下，不必如此，”公爵答道，“只有心怀嫉妒的人才会威胁。你的祖先曾甘愿做我祖先的侍从，我又怎会嫉妒你呢？”议事厅里一片寂静。“我对你并非嫉妒，而是敬爱，”公爵补充道，语气平静得非但没有缓和气氛，反而加深了彼此的隔阂。

“It won’t be necessary, Your Highness,” replied the duke. “Only those who are envious threaten. And how could I envy you, when your ancestors were happy serving as squires to mine?” A silence fell over the council chamber. “It is not envy I feel for you, but devotion and love,” added the duke with such serenity that rather than mending the offense, it only intensified it.

“我这群猎犬里最优秀的一只还能做什么呢？”国王说道。

"What else could the best greyhound in my pack do?" the king declared.

他接过弗朗西斯卡的信，宣布休会。离开房间时，他怒火中烧。他从不容忍公爵的傲慢无礼，但公爵竟然如此纵容，这让他怒不可遏。他内心深处确信，如果他们不是现在这样，恐怕早就血流成河了。

He then took Francisca's letter and adjourned the council. As he left the room, he felt his blood boil. He never let the duke's insolence go unanswered, but the mere fact that the duke allowed it infuriated him. Deep down, he was convinced that if they weren't who they were, blood would have been spilled long ago.

 

 

 

 

连接昂布瓦兹王宫和克洛吕斯城堡的走廊，在夜深人静之时，宛如一条漆黑的舌头。弗朗西斯手中的灯微弱地照亮着周围的一切。为了避免在黑暗中行走，弗朗索瓦丝·德·福瓦不得不紧跟在国王身后。她告诉自己，无论如何，弗朗西斯每次与她相遇，都让她离他更近一步。如今他走在她前面，她看不见他，于是她便允许自己用渴望的目光注视着他。自从得知自己是国王关注的对象后，她便努力装出一副生气、不感兴趣、厌倦他执着的样子，但她总会在拒绝中留下一丝裂痕，鼓励弗朗西斯继续追求她。这种伪装让她精疲力竭，但她的骄傲使她不愿成为国王众多情妇中的一员。她正是夏多布里昂伯爵夫人，而非宫廷里那些头衔可笑、蜂拥而至的贵妇人之一。她们被弗朗西斯一言不发地带进昏暗的房间，只被带去一次，便感到无比荣幸。对丈夫的爱是她唯一的束缚，但她与让的关系早已变得过于甜蜜。弗朗西斯充满欲望的目光助长了她的虚荣心，点燃了她内心的火焰，让她无法自拔；他那些言辞犀利、符合她受过良好教育的女性身份的谈话，对她而言也变得不可或缺。

The passageway that connected the royal residence of Amboise with the Château du Clos Lucé resembled a black tongue at that hour of the night. The lamp Francis carried barely illuminated his surroundings. To avoid taking steps in the dark, Françoise de Foix was forced to walk close behind the king. One way or another, she told herself, Francis was getting a little closer with each encounter. Now that he was walking in front of her and she couldn't see him, the woman allowed herself to look at him with desire. Ever since she had learned that she was the object of the monarch's attention, she had striven to feign offense, disinterest, and weariness of his persistence, but she always took care to leave a small crack in her rejections, to encourage Francis to continue courting her. The pretense exhausted her, but her pride prevented her from joining the endless list of the king's mistresses. She was none other than the Countess of Chateaubriand, not one of the many ladies with laughable titles who swarmed around the court and felt honored when Francis took them in a darkened room, without a word, and only once. Her love for her husband was another restraint, but her relationship with Jean had long since become too sweet. Francis's lustful glances fed her vanity and ignited her without her being able to stop it; his conversations, as sharp as those a woman of her education required, were beginning to be necessary to her.

他们走遍了所有通道后，克洛·吕斯城堡终于向他们敞开了大门。他们默默地穿过城堡里几条空荡荡的走廊和房间，来到一间房间的门口。弗朗西斯科转过身，看向那扇门。

Once they had exhausted the passageway, Clos Lucé finally opened up for them. After silently traversing several empty corridors and rooms of the castle, they arrived at the door of a chamber. Francisco turned to look at it.

他说：“没有人会给你我现在给你的东西。”

"No man will give you what I am giving you now," he said.

弗朗西斯卡假装对他的承诺不为所动，但当国王打开门，将她迎入屋内时，她的矜持瞬间消失。她转身，被深深吸引。蒙娜丽莎的画像也凝视着她。与她同在的，还有达·芬奇的众多其他杰作。他的《施洗者圣约翰》也用温柔的目光注视着这位伯爵夫人。

Francisca pretended not to be impressed by his promise, but when the king opened the door and ushered her inside, her restraint vanished. She spun around, captivated. The Mona Lisa gazed back at her. And with her, so many other masterpieces by Leonardo. His Saint John the Baptist fixed his gentle eyes upon the countess.

“如果主人发现我们未经允许擅自闯入，他会惩罚我的，”弗朗西斯科坦白道，“而我会让他惩罚我。我太敬仰他了，以至于我的王冠在他眼里对我来说毫无意义。”

“If the master found out we had entered without his permission, he would punish me,” Francisco confessed. “And I would let him. I admire him so much that my crown means nothing to me in his eyes.”

和所有法国人一样，伯爵夫人也知道达·芬奇已经在克洛·吕斯庄园住了整整一年，受国王的赏赐和庇护。但国王对这位天才的守护如此严密，以至于通常不允许任何人去他的工作室。弗朗西斯卡走到一张堆满了建筑图纸的工作台前，缓缓地、恭敬地拿起一张。弗朗西斯科站在她身后，深深地吸了一口她黑发的香气。她察觉到了。

The countess, like all of France, knew that Leonardo da Vinci had been living at Clos Lucé for a year, on the king's payroll and under his protection. But the sovereign guarded the genius with such zeal and affection that visits to his studio were usually denied. Francesca approached a worktable piled high with architectural plans. Slowly and respectfully, she picked one up. Francisco stood behind her and inhaled the scent of her black hair. She noticed.

“你难道要为了讨好我而冒着惹恼你如此在乎的人的风险吗？”弗朗西斯卡问道。

—Are you risking upsetting someone you care so much about just to please me? —Francisca asked.

“我若帮了你的忙，就等于得罪了上帝，”他回答说。

"I would offend God by doing your favor," he replied.

——您已经结婚了。我已经结婚了，陛下。

—You already do. I'm married, sire.

难道不是吗？

—Aren't I?

与此同时，在他们前往达芬奇住所的昂布瓦兹城堡的一间豪华卧室里，法国王后克劳迪娅像往常一样独自一人睡着了。

Meanwhile, in a luxurious bedroom of the castle of Amboise, from which they had departed to reach Leonardo's residence, the Queen of France, Claudia, slept alone, as she so often did.

“但我既不是男人，也不是国王，”伯爵夫人宣称。

—But I am neither a man nor a king—declared the countess.

“如果这是罪过，为什么上帝在我心中激起了对你如此强烈的渴望？”君主追问道。

"If it is a sin, why has God stirred up this feverish desire for you in my soul?" the sovereign insisted.

“不要因为你自己的过错而责怪他，”她回答说。“你没读过爱比克泰德的书吗？‘欲望和幸福无法共存。’”

"Don't blame Him for what is solely your own fault," she replied. "Don't you read Epictetus? 'Desire and happiness cannot coexist.'"

我非常清楚。只有拥有你，我才能感到满足。

—I know it well. Having you is the only thing that could fulfill me.

弗朗西斯卡没有回答。国王的身体离她很近，她能感觉到他身上散发的温暖。

Francisca did not answer. The king's body was so close to hers that she could feel him warming her.

“我得走了，”他转过身对弗朗西斯科说。

"I have to go," he said, turning to Francisco.

他们彼此凝视，沉默中充满了暧昧。国王握住她的手，顺从地领她走向出口。他感觉到伯爵夫人纤细手腕上急促的脉搏，嘴角露出一丝微笑。

They gazed at each other in a silence heavy with promise. The king took her hand and, obediently, led her to the exit. He felt the rapid pulse on the countess's slender wrist and smiled.

 

 

 

 

托尔德西利亚斯宫就在眼前。杜罗河静静地、几乎无声地流淌在宫殿脚下，仿佛不愿打扰多年来一直被困在河边的胡安娜。这是一个寒冷的早晨，云朵飘过。三辆马车停在与河岸平行的正门前。查尔斯迅速从第一辆马车里走了出来。宫殿的两层楼在他眼前耸立，对他而言，这威胁远大于他的身高。他花了几天时间准备这次会面，但此刻，他所有的思考，所有在旅途中试图让自己平静下来的方法，都消失了。他原本以为，父亲的葬礼——不久前在离他们不远的圣克拉拉修道院举行——会让他悲痛欲绝，从而分散他的注意力。但结果却恰恰相反：他一心想着与母亲的会面，以至于在父亲菲利普的墓前，他根本没有任何情绪波动。

The palace of Tordesillas awaited. Serenely, almost silently, the Duero flowed at its feet, as if unwilling to disturb Juana, who had been confined to its side for years. It was a cold morning, with passing clouds. Three carriages stopped at the main gate, parallel to the river. Charles quickly stepped out of the first. The two stories of the palace loomed before him, a threat far greater than his own height. He had spent days preparing for this encounter, but at that moment, all his reflections, all the ways of calming himself that he had sought during the journey, vanished. He had thought that the funeral for his father, recently held at the Santa Clara convent, a short distance from where they stood, would cause him such sadness that it would help distract him. But the opposite had occurred: his preoccupation with the meeting with his mother had robbed him of any emotion at the tomb of Philip, his father.

“你母亲的情绪很脆弱，她必须做好承受如此巨大情绪的准备。”希耶夫尔一边抚平旅途中皱巴巴的衣服，一边提醒她，“我会通知大家你的到来。”

—Your mother's spirits are fragile; she must be prepared for such a great emotion—Chièvres warned her as he smoothed his clothes, wrinkled from the journey. —I will announce your arrival.

莱昂诺尔挽着卡洛斯的胳膊。兄妹俩跟在希耶夫尔身后，走向宫门。穿过宫门前，他们彼此对视了一眼，选择保持沉默。

Leonor took Carlos by the arm. The siblings walked to the palace gate, following Chièvres. Before crossing it, they looked at each other and chose to remain silent.

 

 

 

 

希耶夫尔花了些时间才适应圣女贞德房间的黑暗。“女王不喜欢光亮，”她的侍从贝特朗·德·弗罗蒙曾警告过他。过了一会儿，希耶夫尔感觉到了贞德的存在，但他却看不见她。他闭上眼睛，让眼睛适应黑暗，当他再次睁开眼睛时，她由阴影交织而成的身影如同幽灵般出现在他眼前。

It took Chièvres a while to adjust to the darkness of Joan's chamber. "The queen doesn't want light," Bertrand de Fromont, her chamberlain, had warned him. After a few moments, Chièvres sensed Joan's presence, but he couldn't see her. He closed his eyes to let them adjust to the blackness, and when he opened them, her figure, woven from shadows, appeared to him like a specter.

-高度。

-Highness.

“那个声音……来自弗兰德斯，”胡安娜说道。

—That voice… It’s from Flanders —said Juana.

——我们上次见面就是在那里。那是十多年前的事了。

—That's where our last meeting took place. More than ten years ago.

—希耶夫尔领主。

—Lord of Chièvres.

希耶夫尔感觉自己仿佛置身梦境：两个来自过去的声音在那浓重的、炼狱般的黑暗中重逢。伊莎贝拉和费尔南多的女儿早已不再评判自己的存在。她的人生只有最初的三十年；在那三十年里，她爱过、恨过、反抗过，也承受过痛苦，其强度无人愿意理解。将近十年前，当她的父亲下令将她囚禁在托尔德西利亚斯，让她以他的名义统治卡斯蒂利亚时，乔安娜早已对生活失去了所有兴趣。事实上，菲利普最终还是个好丈夫：他死后带走了她。

Chièvres felt as if in a dream: two voices from the past reunited in that dense, purgatorial darkness. Isabella and Ferdinand's daughter had long since ceased to judge her existence. Her life had been her first thirty years; in them she had loved, hated, rebelled, and suffered with an intensity no one ever wanted to understand. When her father had ordered her imprisoned in Tordesillas to govern Castile in his name, almost a decade ago, Joanna had already lost all interest in the work of living. The truth was that Philip had ultimately been a good husband: he had taken her with him when he died.

“我的孩子们都长成什么样了？”胡安娜问道，从她的语气中可以明显看出，她能接受任何答案。

"How have my children grown?" Juana asked, and from her tone it was clear that she could handle any answer.

快乐。足智多谋。健康。

—Happy. Resourceful. Healthy.

太好了。

—How wonderful.

殿下，他们来拜访您了。

—Your Highness, they have come to visit you.

胡安娜的身影像风中的树枝一样摇曳。

Juana's silhouette swayed like a branch in the wind.

他问道：“为什么是现在而不是以前，或者从来都不做？”

"Why now and not before, or never?" he asked.

“因为你必须与你现在统治的对象进行交易和达成协议，”希耶夫斯解释道。

—Because you must have dealings and agreements with the one with whom you now reign —explained Chièvres.

女王的身影静止不动了。

The figure of the queen became still.

—我父亲去世了吗？

—Has my father died?

顾问感到惊讶，心想：“会议准备得再充分也不为过。”他万万没想到胡安娜竟然不知道费迪南国王的死讯，尽管他们已经从布鲁塞尔寄信告知了她。或许有人截获了这封信。又或许她读过，但她善良的本性驱使她将此事遗忘。

The advisor was surprised; "You can never prepare a meeting enough," he thought. He had never imagined that Juana would be unaware of King Ferdinand's death, which they had informed her of by letter from Brussels. Someone had intercepted it. Or perhaps she had read it and her demons, benevolent, had decided that the news should be forgotten.

——如今，政府将以您儿子卡洛斯的名义，在他的努力下，属于您。他渴望见到您，并得到您的祝福。

—The government will now be yours in the name of your son Carlos and in his efforts. He longs to see you and be blessed by you.

希耶夫尔侧耳倾听她的反应，却一片寂静。一时间，这位顾问心中涌起一股怜悯之情。他想象着王后的灵魂，多年来麻木不仁，如今却要一下子接受父亲已死的事实，接受无人告知她真相，接受隔壁房间里，那个与她疏远了十年的儿子正自称是她的王夫。终于，传来一阵回声：希耶夫尔听到一声压抑的啜泣，他转过身去，以示对她悲痛的尊重。

Chièvres strained his ears to hear her reaction, but there was nothing but silence. For a moment, the advisor was overcome with compassion. He imagined the queen's soul, numb for years, struggling to accept in one fell swoop that her father was dead, that no one had wanted to tell her, and that in the next room awaited the son from whom she had been estranged for a decade, now proclaiming himself her king consort. Finally, an echo: Chièvres heard a stifled sob and turned away to respect her grief.

——我有一个能给你带来最好安慰的办法。

—I have the best consolation for your soul.

 

 

 

 

在宫殿庭院对面一间空置的房间里，莱昂诺尔静静地坐在扶手椅上，心无旁骛。不远处，查理凝视着墙上的挂毯。宫殿里挂满了挂毯，但这一幅却格外引人注目。挂毯中央是圣母玛利亚，她神情悲恸。数十个人物簇拥在她周围，几乎不给她留下任何空间；所有人的目光都集中在她身上，既充满敬仰，又带着一丝恳求。圣母的斗篷下，躺着她赤身裸体的圣子，同样悲伤。查理明白圣母和圣子的感受：他们渴望做一对普通的母子，不求赞誉，也不背负命运的重担。

Across the palace courtyard, in an unused room, Leonor, unable to be distracted, sat in an armchair. Nearby, Charles contemplated the tapestry that covered the wall. The palace was decorated with many of them, but this one had caught his eye. In it, the Virgin Mary, who occupied the center of the design, displayed an expression of profound sorrow. Dozens of figures crowded around her, barely leaving her any space; all their gazes were directed toward her, admiring yet demanding. At the foot of the Madonna's mantle lay her Son, naked, also sorrowful. Charles understood what the Virgin and Child were feeling: the longing to be simply a mother and son, without accolades, without the burden of what fate had decreed for them.

“谁要去？”莱昂诺尔惊慌地问道。

"Who's going?" Leonor said alarmedly.

卡洛斯转身，正好看见隔壁房间里有人逃走。莱昂诺尔吓得从座位上跳起来，追了上去。卡洛斯也紧随其后。他们进入的房间同样挂满了挂毯，铅灰色的窗帘遮挡着阳光。从其中一面窗帘后面，传来一阵骚动。

Carlos turned just in time to spot a figure fleeing in the next room. Leonor jumped from her seat and ran after her. Carlos followed. The room they entered, also lined with tapestries, was shielded from the sun by leaden curtains. Behind one of them, a commotion could be heard.

“要么到你们的国王面前来，要么我就让我的士兵逮捕你们。”查理说道。

—Present yourselves before your king or I will have my soldiers arrest you—said Charles.

窗帘后面传来一声稚嫩的呜咽，听起来像个小女孩的声音。卡洛斯不再害怕，一把拉开了窗帘。女孩蜷缩在地上，惊恐万分。

A childish whimper came from behind the curtains. It sounded like a little girl's. No longer afraid, Carlos drew back the fabric. The girl cowered on the floor, terrified.

“她一定是位洗衣妇，”莱昂诺尔打量着她简陋的衣着，低声对卡洛斯说。

"She must be a laundress," Leonor whispered to Carlos, taking in her humble clothes.

女孩听到这番话，感到受到了冒犯，不由自主地站了起来。

The girl heard the comment and the offense forced her to stand up energetically.

“我是凯瑟琳公主，”她不耐烦地说，“你又是谁？你为什么假扮国王？”

—I am Princess Catherine—she said irritably. Who are you, and why do you pretend to be king?

卡洛斯和莱昂诺尔难以置信，眼前这个瘦弱颤抖、几乎透明的小家伙，竟然是他们的妹妹卡塔琳娜，胡安娜在费利佩死后生下的女儿，自两岁起就生活在这座宫殿里，对母亲来说却毫无慰藉。卡洛斯几乎不敢直视眼前的孩子，悲伤涌上心头。

Carlos and Leonor found it hard to believe that this trembling, thin, and almost translucent little creature, disguised as a servant, was their sister Catalina, the daughter Juana had had after Felipe's death, the one who had lived within the walls of that palace since she was two years old, a useless consolation to her mother. Carlos almost looked away from the child, overcome with sadness.

我们是你的兄弟。

—We are your brothers.

卡塔琳娜的嘴唇颤抖着。在此之前，她在托尔德西利亚斯的生活日复一日，毫无新意：午餐总是平淡无奇，和母亲待上几个小时，直到目光涣散，渴望独处，渴望回到没有窗户、寂静无声的房间。弟弟们的到来如此出乎意料，又如此令人兴奋，以至于她既害怕又想逃离；但她最终没有。

Catalina's lips trembled. Until then, her life in Tordesillas had unfolded like a cycle of identical days: lunches that never surprised, a few hours with her mother until her gaze faded and she longed for solitude, the darkness of her windowless room where no sound reached her. The arrival of her brothers was so unexpected and exciting that it terrified her and made her want to flee; but she didn't.

“我们的母亲一定跟你提起过我们，”莱昂诺尔说。

—Our mother must have told you about us —said Leonor.

“我妈妈很安静，”卡塔琳娜回答道。

"My mother is quiet," replied Catalina.

女孩注意到莱昂诺身上华丽的刺绣。她赞叹不已，伸手抚摸起来；然后又抚摸了她的耳环和头饰。这些对她来说都是全新的体验。莱昂诺强忍着泪水。

The girl noticed the rich embroidery Leonor was wearing. In admiration, she reached out and caressed it; then her earrings and her headdress. These were new sensations for her. Leonor choked back tears.

“这里的生活怎么样？”卡洛斯问卡塔琳娜，他想找个合适的措辞问她，她的生活是否如同地狱。“你们会接待访客吗？”

"What's life like here?" Carlos asked Catalina, searching for a way to ask if her existence resembled hell. "Do you receive visitors?"

卡塔琳娜沉默不语。

Catalina remained silent.

—有人在指导你吗？你听到音乐了吗？

—Are you being instructed? Do you hear music?

卡塔琳娜再次陷入沉默。

Catalina fell silent again.

——那条河，你会去那里散步吗？

—And the river, do you go for walks there?

“哪条河？”女孩回答道。

"Which river?" the girl replied.

卡洛斯急忙离开房间，独自一人待在隔壁房间。他一直羞于在别人面前崩溃。

Carlos hurried to leave the room to be alone in the next one. He had always been ashamed to break down in front of others.

“你母亲在等你呢。”希耶夫斯说道，片刻后他注意到查尔斯神情不安。“怎么了？”

—Your mother is waiting for you—announced Chièvres, who moments later noticed Charles's distress. —What's wrong?

 

 

 

 

就像希耶夫尔一样，查尔斯和埃莉诺也花了一段时间才适应卧室的昏暗光线。一道黄光划破黑暗：圣女贞德正在点燃一盏五枝烛台。

Just like Chièvres, Charles and Eleanor took some time to adjust to the dimness of the bedchamber. A yellow flash broke the darkness: Joan was lighting a five-branched candelabrum.

——前进，前进。

—Move forward, move forward.

兄妹俩顺从地倒在烛光下。片刻间，无人呼吸，无人说话。查尔斯和埃莉诺满怀渴望地凝视着母亲，弥补着多年来无法相见的遗憾。乔安娜的容貌诉说着她的过往：昔日的美貌褪色，被过往的情感刻画得斑驳陆离，双眼空洞无神；这美貌毫无意义，因为本该欣赏她的人——菲利普——已经不在人世了。

Both siblings obeyed and fell into the candlelight. For a moment, no one breathed or spoke a word. Charles and Eleanor gazed at their mother with longing, making up for the years they had been unable to do so. Joanna's appearance told her story: a faded beauty, etched with past emotions, her eyes lifeless; a beauty devoid of meaning, for the one who should have admired her, Philip, was no longer alive.

“但是……你们是我的孩子吗？”胡安娜问道，她被一个改变人生的时刻深深触动了。

—But… are you my children? —Juana asked, struck by a life-altering moment.

卡洛斯闻到了那股他记忆中熟悉的母亲的气息。这气息在他心中激起了一种强烈的情感：比喜悦更强烈，比悲伤更美好，而这种情感，他此刻才第一次体会到。

Carlos perceived that maternal perfume he still remembered. It stirred a violent emotion within him: something worse than joy and better than sadness, and which he felt for the first time at that moment.

-母亲。

-Mother.

儿子心中有很多问题，但他选择不问。他内心的政治家本能最终战胜了恐惧，他还是开口说话了。

The son had so many questions that he chose not to ask them. The statesman within him prevailed, and he ended up speaking.

—我想让你知道，我们一到村里，就举行了一场非常隆重的弥撒来纪念我们的父亲。

—I wanted you to know that, as soon as we arrived at the village, we honored our father with a very splendid mass.

——许多人为他流泪——莱昂诺尔撒谎了。

—Many tears have been shed for him —Leonor lied.

与此同时，希耶夫尔站在吊灯照射范围之外观看比赛。他感到不安，因为现场气氛过于激动。他担心这会动摇查尔斯的决心。

Meanwhile, Chièvres watched the match from beyond the area illuminated by the chandelier. He was uneasy about the excessive emotion. He feared it might shake Charles's resolve.

“你儿子有好消息要告诉你，”顾问打断道，“他愿意帮你卸下政务的重担，免得给你带来诸多痛苦……”

"Your son has great news for you," the advisor interrupted. "He offers to relieve you of the burden of government, which could cause you so much grief..."

胡安娜看着卡洛斯，仿佛希耶夫雷斯根本不存在。她握住儿子的手，发现他的手又湿又冷，全是神经。

Juana looked at Carlos, as if Chièvres didn't exist. She took her son's hands, which she noticed were damp and cold, pure nerves.

“如果说我失去了什么，那就是纯真，我的孩子。别假装你的野心是出于礼貌。你只是众多想从我这里得到同样东西的人中的最新一个。”

"If there's one thing I no longer possess, it's innocence, my son. Don't pretend your ambition is a courtesy. You're the latest of many to seek the same from me."

卡洛斯很尴尬。那个疯女人在哪儿呢？

Carlos was embarrassed. Where was the crazy woman?

——母亲，我愿与您共同治理国家。请不要剥夺您应得的一切。

—I wish to govern with you, mother. Do not deprive you of what is rightfully yours.

“跟我一起执政？”胡安娜的语气近乎嘲讽。“我能在你的朝廷里占有一席之地吗？我的决定能在议会里举足轻重吗？”

"Govern with me?" Juana's voice bordered on mockery. "Will I have a place at your court? Will my decision carry weight in the councils?"

卡洛斯想撒谎，但他害怕承担责任。不，他甚至都没考虑过这个选项；他的母亲只不过是文件顶端的一个头衔而已。他只能吞下苦果：对生他养他的女人自私自利，并将这份罪恶感背负终生。但西班牙又有谁会希望她统治呢？只有那些渴望权势薄弱、无需王冠就能统治的人才会如此。

Carlos wanted to lie, but he was afraid of committing himself. No, that option wasn't even considered; his mother was to be nothing more than a title at the top of the documents. He was left with the bitter pill of behaving selfishly toward the woman who had brought him into the world and bearing that guilt for the rest of his life. But who in Spain wanted her to rule? Only those who craved a weak throne so they could rule without a crown.

“如果上帝听从我的祈求，让我回到丈夫身边，”胡安娜继续说道，“祂就能让我们免受多少苦难。但祂从未善待过我。我依然是女王，只有我才有权放弃政权。”

“If God had heeded my plea and taken me to my husband,” Juana continued, “what sorrow He would have spared us all. But He has never been generous to me. I am still the queen, and only I have the power to relinquish the government.”

我知道，妈妈……

—I know, mother…

胡安娜用坚定的语气打断了他：

Juana interrupted him in a firm voice:

跪拜你的女王。

—Kneel before your queen.

查理转向希耶夫，就像每当他心神不宁、不知所措时那样。这位顾问只是回望了他一眼。于是，他转过身，跪倒在母亲面前，匍匐在地，不知接下来会发生什么。埃莉诺和希耶夫焦急地等待着；一切都取决于那个女人的意志。如果她选择不祝福查理，如果一股强烈的能量和骄傲攫住了她，如果她将自己拥有了此前被无数人夺走的东西，那么王位将完全属于她，正如法律所规定的那样。接下来会发生什么？争夺、派系、斗争：战争。查理不仅跪在她面前：他完全受制于她。琼低下头看着儿子，微微一笑，注意到他耳角的一颗小痣。她记得很清楚；他出生时就有了。在弗兰德斯。弗兰德斯。弗兰德斯……如果说乔安娜生活在半明半暗之中，那是因为她可以沉浸在一种错觉里，觉得自己仍然住在弗兰德斯的宫廷里。这样，她就能想象出那些她看不见的墙壁，就是她与菲利普相遇的地方。有时她觉得她能感受到他的存在，那种性爱前的低吟，那种多年前曾让她重获新生的香水味。但乔安娜知道，这不过是一场梦。现实并没有逃避她，也从未逃避过她：相反，是她自己，在痛苦的驱使下，明知故犯地逃离了现实。而且她还想继续逃避下去。她知道，如果没有黑暗，如果没有那种不负责任的孤独，就不会有记忆的庇护所，就不会有那种能给她带来平静幻象的幻想。乔安娜把手放在查尔斯的肩膀上；她看到他的手已经萎缩，磨损了。

Charles turned to Chièvres, as he did whenever something disconcerted him to the point of paralysis. The advisor merely returned his gaze. So he turned back to his mother and prostrated himself before her, unsure of what to expect. Eleanor and Chièvres waited anxiously; everything depended on that woman's will. If she chose to deny Charles her blessing, if a surge of energy and pride were to seize her, if she were to grant herself what so many had taken from her until now, the throne would be hers and hers alone, as the law dictated. What would follow? Claims, factions, struggles: war. Charles was not only kneeling before her: he was at her mercy. Joan lowered her gaze to her son and smiled, noticing a small mole on the corner of one of his ears. She remembered it well; it was there when he was born. In Flanders. Flanders. Flanders… If Joanna lived in semi-darkness, it was because she could indulge in the delusion that she still resided at the Flemish court. In this way, she could imagine that the walls she couldn't see were those within which she had met Philip. Sometimes she thought she felt his presence, that purr that preceded sex, the perfume that had breathed life into her years before. But Joanna knew it was nothing more than a dream. Reality didn't elude her, nor had it ever: rather, it was she who, knowingly, spurred on by pain, had fled from reality. And she wanted to continue doing so. She knew that, without darkness, without that irresponsible solitude, there would be no room for that constant refuge of memory, for that fantasy that provided her with a mirage of peace. Joanna placed her hand on Charles's shoulder; she saw it was withered, worn.

我愿由你为我执政。

—It is my will that you govern for me.

如果希耶夫斯能克制住自己，他一定会发出欣喜若狂的呐喊。卡洛斯站起来时，双腿都在颤抖。

If Chièvres hadn't been able to contain himself, he would have let out a shout of euphoria. Carlos's legs trembled when he stood up.

他是国王。

He was the king.

 

 

 

 

不久之后，希耶夫尔凝望着杜罗河，等待着查理和埃莉诺的离去。他们想在离开前向妹妹凯瑟琳告别。这位顾问沉浸在成功的喜悦中，憧憬着查理即将赐予他统治的王国。他心不在焉，没有注意到一个信使走近。当那人开口说话时，他吓了一跳。他立刻意识到，这是哈德良的来信。他正要打开信，却听到查理在他身后。

Shortly afterward, Chièvres gazed at the Douro River as he awaited the departure of Charles and Eleanor, who had wished to bid farewell to their sister Catherine before leaving. The advisor reveled in the peace of his success and the views of the kingdom over which Charles was about to grant him dominion. Lost in thought, he failed to notice a messenger approaching, and when the man spoke to him, he was startled. A letter from Hadrian, he realized at once. He was about to open it when he heard Charles behind him.

“公主必须陪我们一起去，”他自言自语道，也对在场的所有人说道。

—The Infanta must accompany us —he said to himself and to everyone present.

希耶夫斯转过身，注意到卡洛斯脸颊上的红晕：那是他情绪激动的标志。

Chièvres turned around and noticed the blush on Carlos's cheeks: that was the sign that he was overcome by emotion.

“如果我把灵魂留在这个地方，带着这样的生命离开，我的灵魂将无法安息，”他解释说。

"My soul will not rest if I leave it in this place, with this life," he explained.

一时间，希耶夫的战略直觉失灵了。查尔斯的想法如此出乎意料，而且他从查尔斯的语气中感受到了如此的紧迫感，以至于他不知道该反对还是顺从。

For a moment, Chièvres's strategic instincts failed him. Charles's idea was so unexpected, and he sensed such urgency in his voice, that he didn't know whether to oppose it or comply.

卡洛斯继续说道：“我的姑姑玛格丽塔告诉我，我的祖父母强迫我和母亲分开时，我母亲几乎没有感觉到儿子费尔南多的缺席。这些年来，她似乎也不介意没有收到我、莱昂诺尔或伊莎贝尔的消息。”

“My aunt Margarita,” Carlos continued, “told me that my mother barely felt the absence of her son Fernando when my grandparents forced the separation. Nor does she seem to have minded not hearing from me, Leonor, or Isabel all these years.”

希耶夫尔有二十个反对的理由，正要一一列举，但他心里有个声音告诉他，这一次查尔斯不会被说服。

Chièvres had twenty arguments against it and was about to list them, but something told him that on this occasion Charles would not be convinced.

 

 

 

 

几个小时后，凯瑟琳坐在查尔斯的马车窗台上。秋日的阳光慷慨地洒在她的脸上；毫无疑问，她已经享受了多年的阳光。当她哥哥的手下闯入她的房间，要从墙上一个极其隐蔽的小洞把她带走时，凯瑟琳吓得缩了回去，但当他们最终把她抱起来时，她甚至没有抗议，当他们没有通知乔安娜就离开宫殿时，她也一言不发。此刻，她坐在哥哥们身边，一言不发，但一股喜悦的兴奋从她身上散发出来。一切都让她着迷。马车里的每一个细节都成了她的游乐场；他们经过的每一处风景，都成了她的幻想；哥哥们的每一个举动，都成了她的一堂课。查尔斯骄傲地看着她。

A few hours later, Catherine perched on the windowsill of Charles's carriage. The autumn sun bathed her face generously; she had undoubtedly owed it its rays for years. When her brother's men entered her chamber to take her away through the most discreet hole they could find in the wall, Catherine had recoiled in fear, but there wasn't even a protest when they finally carried her in their arms, nor a word when they left the palace without informing Joanna. At that moment, as she sat beside her brothers, Catherine didn't speak, but a joyful excitement radiated from her. Everything interested her. Every detail inside the carriage was a playground for her; every landscape they passed, a fantasy; every gesture of her brothers, a lesson. Charles watched her with pride.

希耶夫尔全然不顾马车里弥漫的亲情，打开了阿德里亚诺的信。读完信，他顿时屏住了呼吸。他在杜罗河畔感受到的那份平静的胜利，仿佛只是一场幻觉。事实是，费迪南王子再次成为威胁，更糟糕的是，他们刚刚踏上了那场荒谬的营救凯瑟琳的冒险之旅，而且看不到尽头。希耶夫尔正要停车，却听到远处传来呼喊声，似乎一直跟着马车的行进。呼喊声被车轮碾过路面的哐当声淹没，过了一会儿才变得清晰起来。

Chièvres, oblivious to the familial feeling that filled the carriage, opened Adriano's letter. Reading it took his breath away. The placid victory he had felt on the banks of the Douro seemed like an illusion. The truth was that Prince Ferdinand was once again a threat, and to make matters worse, they had just embarked on that absurd adventure of freeing Catherine, with no end in sight. Chièvres was about to stop when he heard a distant call approaching; it seemed to be following the carriage's progress. The shouts were drowned out by the clatter of the wheels on the road and took some time to become clear.

—以胡安娜女王的名义，停止！

—Stop in the name of Queen Juana!

马车停了下来，一个骑马的人很快追了上来。他是贝尔特兰·德·弗罗蒙特，他没有下马就走向卡洛斯。

The carriage stopped, and a man on horseback soon caught up with it. It was Beltrán de Fromont, who didn't wait to dismount before approaching Carlos.

“你母亲注意到凯瑟琳公主不在了。她说她想死！”侍从长气喘吁吁地宣布道，他跑得筋疲力尽。

"Your mother has noticed the absence of Princess Catherine. She says she wants to die!" the chamberlain announced between gasps, exhausted from the run.

“没人指望我会让步，”卡洛斯回答说。“但你之前已经同意了。如果你后悔了，我不会。”

“Nobody expected me to give in,” Carlos replied. “But you were in agreement. If you regret it, I won’t.”

—他曾表示，他不会进食、饮水，也不会接受任何形式的照顾。

—He has said that he will not take food, water, or allow himself to be cared for in any way.

贝尔特兰·德·弗罗蒙特下了车，走到他跟前，直视着他的眼睛，尽管车子仍然隔在他们之间。

Beltrán de Fromont got out of the car to speak to him up close, looking him in the eyes, even though the car was still between them.

陛下，我的夫人并不惧怕死亡。

—Your Majesty, my lady is not afraid of death.

希耶夫尔心想，这神迹的干预要让他付出多少祈祷的代价，于是下了马车，把车门敞开着。

Chièvres, wondering how many prayers this divine intervention would cost him, got out of the carriage and left its door open.

“趴下，”顾问命令凯瑟琳。

"Get down," the advisor commanded Catherine.

“别理他，”卡洛斯说着，握住了妹妹的手。

"Ignore him," Carlos countered, as he took his sister's hand.

“那你下来吧。”希耶夫对国王说道。

—You come down, then —Chièvres told the king.

卡洛斯跟着他的顾问来到路边一个拐弯处，那里没人能听到他们的谈话。此时阳光微弱，寒风刺骨。田野的绿色都快要变成灰色了。

Carlos followed his advisor to a bend in the road where no one could hear them. At that time of day, the sunlight was weak and the cold was biting. The greens of the fields were turning almost gray.

“别像诗里的英雄那样行事，”希耶夫斯说，“你不会为了这件事而拿你取得的一切成就冒险的。”

—Stop behaving like the hero of a poem— said Chièvres. —You're not going to risk everything you've achieved over this.

——你和我一样清楚，我父亲每天都生活在那种威胁之下。我母亲不会自杀的！

—You know as well as I do that my father lived with those kinds of threats every day. My mother isn't going to kill herself!

“这才是你夜不能寐的原因！”对方回答道，“她还活着，却对你充满怨恨，很快就会背弃她赐予你以她名义统治的恩赐。殿下，请帮我一个忙，就一件，作为我多年来为您效力的回报。”

"That's what should keep you awake at night!" replied his interlocutor. "Alive and full of resentment toward you, she will soon renege on the blessing she bestowed upon you to govern in her name. Do me a favor, Your Highness, just one, as payment for the services I have rendered you for so long."

卡洛斯点了点头：如果说谁最应该得到他的让步，那就是谢夫雷斯。

Carlos nodded: if anyone deserved a concession from him, it was Chièvres.

“读读吧，”顾问说着，把哈德良的信递给他。“一切都可能岌岌可危。任何一个错误都可能致命。”

"Read it," said the advisor, handing him Hadrian's letter. "Everything may still hang by a thread. Every mistake will be fatal."

阿德里亚诺的话语果然对查理的灵魂产生了影响。费迪南的威胁令他感到无比沉重。这消息让他一时不知所措，片刻后，他注意到希耶夫尔正返回马车。查理多么想冲上前去阻止他，让他的愿望得以实现，阻止他的妹妹回到那如同地牢般的宫殿。但他的身体却不听使唤，这并非因为寒冷，也并非因为害怕希耶夫尔——他并不害怕；而是王冠的重担，是责任的召唤。

Adriano's words had the intended effect on Charles's soul. Ferdinand's threat weighed heavily upon him. The news paralyzed him for a few moments, and then he noticed Chièvres returning to the carriage. Charles longed to rush toward him and stop him, to make his heart's desire prevail, to prevent his sister from returning to that dungeon-like palace. But his body wouldn't respond, and it wasn't from the cold, nor from fear of Chièvres, for he felt no fear; it was the weight of the crown, it was duty.

就在几米之外，一切都发生得如此迅速：希耶夫尔的命令，凯瑟琳的哭泣，埃莉诺的抱怨，以及贝特朗·德·弗罗蒙的马咆哮着返回托尔德西利亚斯，他的妹妹在马鞍上挣扎，为即将再次失去的自由而放声痛哭。查理回到马车时，妹妹的哭声尚未完全停止。他坐在埃莉诺身边，她正在擦拭眼泪。马车启程时，国王闭上了眼睛。他精疲力竭。

Just a few meters away, everything happened quite quickly: Chièvres's order, Catherine's weeping, Eleanor's complaints, and Bertrand de Fromont's horse roaring back to Tordesillas, his sister thrashing in the saddle and crying loudly for the freedom she was about to lose again. When Charles returned to the carriage, his sister's wailing hadn't completely subsided. He sat down beside Eleanor, who was wiping away her tears. As they set off, the king closed his eyes. He was exhausted.

“我得去见费尔南多，”她低声说道。

"I have to meet with Fernando," she murmured.

希耶夫尔点点头，命令汽车驶向通往莫哈多斯的道路。

Chièvres nodded and gave the order for the car to take the road that led to Mojados.

 

 

 

 

当查理在西班牙努力克制自己的欲望时，在法国，国王的欲望却肆意蔓延。他对夏多布里昂伯爵夫人的追求并未停止，也未因他母亲的责备而止步。路易丝认为国王的任性背后隐藏着一个野心勃勃的女人，而她对国王欲望的抗拒，则纯粹是权谋。路易丝唯一的希望，就是她刚刚听到的传言，能立刻转告给弗朗西斯，让他断绝与伯爵夫人的关系。

While in Spain Charles was learning to control his desires, in France those of his king were running rampant. His courtship of the Countess of Chateaubriand had not ceased, nor had it been checked by his mother's censure. She saw in the king's whim a woman of hidden ambition, and in her resistance to the monarch's desires, pure maneuvering. Louise's only hope was that the rumor that had just reached her ears, promptly relayed to Francis, would poison him into repudiating the countess.

在一个晚上，十位乐师为昂布瓦兹宫廷演奏助兴，路易丝注意到她的儿子被旋律深深吸引，她认为这就是缘分：在激动的心灵中，节拍会更加响亮。

During an evening in which ten musicians entertained the court of Amboise, Louise noticed that her son was captivated by the melody and thought that it was the moment: in an excited soul the beats resonated more.

“波旁公爵曾吹嘘说，他早就满足了你现在追求的那个人，”路易莎低声对他说，“难道你们要用这种方式来彰显自己的与众不同吗？为了他早已鄙夷过的人，你们竟然如此费尽心思？”

—The Duke of Bourbon boasts of having long ago satisfied the one you are now courting— Luisa whispered to him. —Is this how you will distinguish yourselves, by going to great lengths for what he has already scorned?

弗朗西斯科再也听不到音乐了；愤怒震聋了他的耳朵。当他平静下来，开始思考时，他不禁思忖，究竟哪种情况更可怕：是谣言属实，还是波旁国王为了羞辱弗朗西斯卡和自己而散布的谎言？路易莎的沉默让她怀疑流言蜚语已经造成了毁灭性的打击，但如果她能窥见弗朗西斯科的内心，她绝不会喜欢看到那番景象，因为国王已被仇恨彻底吞噬，他决心要除掉——没错，但绝不会除掉伯爵夫人。

Francisco heard no more music; anger deafened him. When he calmed down enough to reflect, he wondered what would be more terrible: that the rumor was true or that it was a fabrication spread by the Bourbon king to humiliate not only Francisca, but also the king himself. Luisa's lack of response led her to suspect that the gossip had had a devastating effect, but if she had been able to glimpse Francisco's mind, she would not have enjoyed the sight, because the king had erupted in hatred and was determined to repudiate, yes, but not the countess.

 

 

 

 

——波旁公爵大人，从今天起，我的好朋友劳特雷克将接替您担任米兰总督一职。

—Lord Duke of Bourbon, from today my good friend Lautrec will occupy your position as governor of Milan.

波旁公爵和劳特雷克子爵茫然地听着。皇家大厅迎接了他们，也迎接了君主和那天早晨的灿烂阳光。要废黜米兰大公——国王的骄傲——而让一个既无荣耀也无才能的子爵来掌管米兰？这荒谬至极，劳特雷克感到羞愧，但又不至于拒绝这份殊荣。

The Duke of Bourbon and the Viscount of Lautrec listened without understanding. The royal hall welcomed them both, as well as the monarch and the many rays of sunshine on that bright morning. To depose the Grand Duke in command of Milan, the King's pride, in favor of a Viscount without glory or the talent to achieve it? The absurdity seemed such that Lautrec felt ashamed, though not enough to refuse such an honor.

“我究竟哪里辜负了你？”公爵一字一顿地问道。

"How have I failed you?" the duke wanted to know, chewing each word.

弗朗西斯科耸了耸肩。他从未像刚才那样，如此真切地感受到自己身居王位。这种只有国王才能容忍的不公，却因子爵是弗朗西斯卡的兄弟而显得更加残酷。他武断地羞辱了唯一敢于啄他的公鸡，并夺走了伯爵夫人的床单，因为国王刚刚给予他兄弟的那份慷慨恩惠，必然要得到偿还。弗朗西斯科唯一感到困惑的是，他为何没有更早地行使自己的暴政。
