Francisco shrugged. He had never felt more on the throne than when he gave in to this outburst he had just experienced. This injustice, which only a king could allow himself without being punished, was all the more cruel because the viscount was Francisca's brother. With an arbitrary decision, he had humiliated the only rooster that dared to peck at him and had drawn back the countess's sheets for himself, because the outrageously generous concession the king had just offered his brother would, without fail, have to be repaid. The only thing that puzzled Francisco was why he hadn't exercised his tyranny sooner.

当公爵冲进来质问理由时，弗朗西斯身穿在正午阳光下熠熠生辉的西装，解决了此事：

When the duke rushed in demanding reasons, Francis, his suit glowing in the midday sun, settled the matter:

—法国国王只对上帝负责！

—The King of France answers only to God!

 

 

 

 

“查理摧毁了可怜的疯女人的意志！”西班牙到处都在传颂着这句话。那些不希望他登上王位，而是希望费尔南多继承王位的人，拒绝相信胡安娜是在没有胁迫的情况下接受了他的意志。他们臆想着，这个残暴的佛兰德人是如何利用王后的疯狂来掌控政权的。他们自己捏造了这种暴行，却因此怒火中烧，前所未有地煽动费尔南多。“救救我们！统治吧！”在莫哈多斯，费尔南多跪倒在年轻人面前，面前堆满了数十封控诉托尔德西利亚斯惨剧的信件，杰尔马纳已经开始着手制定他的政府计划……说服他的理由最终简化为一个：为了王国，为了王国！阴谋者们意识到，费尔南多缺乏野心和私心，如果有什么能打动他，那就是为了卡斯蒂利亚和阿拉贡的利益而牺牲，这种责任感正是他从祖父那里学来的。

"Charles has broken the will of the poor madwoman!" No other phrase was heard in Spain. Those who didn't want him on the throne, but rather Ferdinand, refused to believe that Joanna had accepted his will without coercion. They imagined scenes in which the cruel Flemish exploited the queen's madness to gain control of the government. The rage they felt at this abuse, which they themselves had fabricated, led them to incite Ferdinand like never before. "Save us! Reign!" Back in Mojados, kneeling before the young man, dozens of letters complaining about what had happened in Tordesillas, Germana already drawing up plans for his government… The argument to convince him was reduced to a single one: it was for the kingdom, for the kingdom! The conspirators had realized that Fernando lacked ambition and selfishness, and that if anything would convince him, it was sacrifice for the good of Castile and Aragon, a sense of responsibility learned from his grandfather.

 

 

 

 

围绕王子的骚动如此肆无忌惮，以至于西斯内罗斯的密探非但没有向他汇报，反而高喊：“警报！”这位当时命悬一线的红衣主教，仿佛看到了王国即将爆发战争的阴影，他渴望痛哭一场，以释放内心的煎熬。自从阿拉贡的费尔南多去世后，他毕生致力于确保王位继承不会扰乱西班牙的和平，让那些持怀疑态度的人不再怀疑，让那些漠不关心的人也能像他一样尊重法律。但他没有料到查理会如此不服从命令。查理当时还没有来见他，而且在托尔德西利亚斯，查理本可以夺取王位，但这会进一步激怒费尔南多的派系。或许费尔南多是对的，查理确实不是一位合格的君主，但红衣主教知道，现在退缩已经太晚了。如果他必须用剩下的那点力气做点什么，那就是把它奉献给王国的和平。

The commotion surrounding the prince was so shameless that Cisneros's spies, rather than informing him, shouted: "Alarm!" The cardinal, whose life then hung by a thread, saw specters of war in the kingdom and longed to weep to release his anguish. Since Ferdinand of Aragon's death, his entire endeavor had been to ensure that the succession did not disrupt the peace in Spain, that the skeptics would tire of their skepticism, and that the indifferent would be as respectful of the law as he himself. But he had not reckoned on Charles's insubordination, who had not yet come to meet him, and who in Tordesillas might have secured the throne, but at the cost of further enraging Ferdinand's faction. Perhaps Ferdinand was right, and Charles was not a worthy monarch, but the cardinal knew it was too late to back down. If he had to do anything with the little strength he had left, it was to dedicate it to the peace of the kingdom.

 

 

 

 

年轻的费尔南多走进书房时，西斯内罗斯已在火炉旁落座。他威严的身影在火焰的映衬下显得格外醒目。费尔南多还没来得及开口，就打量起他那高大的侧脸，心中涌起一股十五岁少年的沉重感：他觉得自己像个孩子。

When the young Fernando entered his study, Cisneros had already taken his seat by the fire. The dignity of his figure was silhouetted against the flames. Before announcing his arrival, Fernando took in his imposing profile and felt the weight of his fifteen years: he felt like a child.

卓越。

-Eminence.

西斯内罗斯直视着他的眼睛，希望能从中找到答案。费尔南多察觉到了这一点，他多么希望自己也能清晰地感受到这一点，以便表达出来，或者反过来，努力掩饰。他吻了吻红衣主教的手，然后在他身旁坐下，等待着那不可避免的布道。

Cisneros looked him in the eyes, hoping to find an answer there. Fernando noticed this, and he wished he could feel it clearly enough to express it, or conversely, to try to hide it. After kissing the cardinal's hand, he sat down beside him and awaited the inevitable sermon.

“你我之间有共同之处，”西斯内罗斯说道，“我们的一切都归功于你们的祖父母。尤其是你，应该感谢费迪南国王。他像对待亲生儿子一样保护你。没有人有义务行善；善意源于人的灵魂。当死亡降临，唯有遵从他的遗愿才能报答这份慷慨。你愿意这样做吗？”

“We share something, you and I,” Cisneros said. “We both owe everything we are to your grandparents. Especially to King Ferdinand, in your case. He protected you like a son. No man is obligated to be kind; it is his soul that bestows it. When death intervenes, fulfilling his will is the only way to repay such generosity. Will you do so?”

“他想让我统治，”费尔南多回答道。

"He wanted me to reign," replied Fernando.

“他写的不是这个，”红衣主教回答说，“如果他当上了国王，那是因为他不是一个会任由他人左右自己决定的人。”

—That's not what he wrote—replied the cardinal. —And if he became king it was because he wasn't a man who would let others dictate his decisions.

年轻的王子沉默不语，因为他知道这是事实。他试图想象阿拉贡的费迪南德会屈从于他人的意志，但这根本不可能。他的祖父和他的命令是一体的。

The young prince remained silent because he knew it was true. He tried to imagine Ferdinand of Aragon bowing to the will of others, but it was impossible. His grandfather and his orders were one and the same.

“此外，”西斯内罗斯继续说道，“你忘记了，不仅他的意志重要，上帝的意志也重要，是上帝在你之前把查尔斯带到这个世界上。”

"Furthermore," Cisneros continued, "you forget that not only his will counts, but also God's, who brought Charles into the world before you."

——甚至在此之前，还有我的母亲。当有女王在位时，你诉诸法律，却不谴责查尔斯夺取她总督之位的行为？

—And even before that, my mother. You appeal to the law and don't condemn Charles for taking the governorship from her, when there is a queen?

“这里没有女人，怎么可能有女王呢？”摄政王宣称。

"There is no woman, so how can there be a queen?" the regent declared.

噼啪作响的火焰是对他话语的唯一回应。西斯内罗斯怜悯这个年轻人，但又为自己残忍到让他哑口无言而感到得意。

The crackling of the fire was the only answer to his words. Cisneros took pity on the young man, but was pleased to have been cruel enough to leave him speechless.

“我来到宫廷并无野心，”红衣主教说道，“我没有可以委托的世家。如果感情影响了我，那对你也有好处。我和查理没有任何关系。但我的使命是守护西班牙的未来，而我正在这样做。”

“I came to court without ambition,” the cardinal said. “I have no lineage to whom I can delegate. And if affection were to influence me, it would benefit you. I have no ties to Charles. But my mission is to safeguard the future of Spain, and that is what I am doing.”

——难道只有你对未来的看法才是正确的吗？

—And is your view of that future the only valid one?

至少比那些试图让你动摇的人要干净利落。一个为了讨好你而不尊重你合法权益的人，当你需要他服从时，他也不会尊重。

—At least cleaner than that of those who try to make you falter. He who does not respect what is rightfully yours in order to favor you, will not do so when you have to make him comply.

火势逐渐减弱，费尔南多城里盘踞的那只火也随之熄灭了。

The fire was dying down, and with it the one that was nesting in Fernando.

 

 

 

 

夜幕降临莫哈多斯后，一位以国王名义来的信使告知费尔南多，他的兄长希望次日与他会面。王子与西斯内罗斯交谈中获得的些许平静瞬间消失。他可以把即将与卡洛斯会面的消息告诉杰尔马娜，她或许会怂恿他反抗。他也可以去找阿尔瓦公爵，向他请教如何以命令的强制力来服从。但王子选择了独处。一年半以来，他听了太多人的议论，如今他渴望倾听自己的心声。他决定彻夜不眠。他拉过一把扶手椅，来到房间的窗边，凝望着漫天繁星。有的星光璀璨，有的则黯淡无光，微不足道，几乎只是一粒尘埃。费尔南多不禁纳闷，自己为何不经常仰望星空。能够每晚欣赏如此美景，是多么珍贵的恩赐，而错过又是多么可惜。沉思片刻，心中的焦虑烟消云散。他的祖父是不是在天上看着他呢？费尔南多注意到两颗平行的星星，他想象那是死去的国王的眼睛。

Once night had fallen on Mojados, a messenger, in the king's name, informed Fernando that his brother wished to meet with him the following day. The little peace the Infante had found in his conversation with Cisneros vanished. He could tell Germana of the imminent meeting with Carlos, and she might embolden him to rebel. He could also seek out the Duke of Alba and give his advice on obedience the force of orders. But the Infante chose solitude. After a year and a half of listening to so many, he longed to hear himself. He resigned himself to staying awake. He pulled an armchair up to the window of his chamber and gazed at the sea of ​​stars in the sky. Some shone brightly. Others were pale, insignificant, barely a speck. Fernando wondered why he didn't look at the heavens more often. What a privilege it was to be able to admire such beauty every night, and what a mistake not to. Contemplating it, no anxiety remained. Was his grandfather watching him from up there? Fernando noticed two parallel stars and imagined they were the eyes of the dead king.

“你们为什么不想让我登上王位？”他问道。

"Why didn't you want me on the throne?" he asked.

但那两颗星甚至连闪烁的光芒都没有，对他的困境漠不关心。费尔南多知道自己孤身一人，而这种确定性非但没有让他感到焦虑，反而让他感到平静。他自由了。他可以随心所欲地选择自己的灵魂所指引的。那些阴谋者的坚持，甚至那些并非阴谋者的声音，都无关紧要。除了他自己，没有人需要承担他选择的后果。年轻人微微一笑，仿佛被催眠般沉沉睡去。他向自己的灵魂发出了请求，而答案很快就揭晓了。

But the two stars didn't even twinkle, indifferent to his dilemma. Fernando knew he was alone, and suddenly that certainty, instead of distressing him, filled him with peace. He was free. He could choose whatever his soul asked of him. The insistence of the conspirators, and even that of those who weren't, was irrelevant. No one but him would have to live with the consequences of his decision. The young man smiled and, as if lulled to sleep, fell asleep. He had asked his soul, and it hadn't taken long to answer.

 

 

 

 

会面地点定在莫哈多斯附近的一片开阔地上。清晨寒风刺骨。草地上覆盖着一层冰，费尔南多的马蹄踩在冰面上发出嘎吱嘎吱的声响。当他到达约定地点时，才发现自己并非第一个到的。会面的消息早已传开，只见那些早已等候多时的人，个个裹得严严实实，神情严肃：阿斯托尔加大主教杰尔马纳、卡拉特拉瓦大公。当他们看到王子时，都比以往更加警惕地低下了头。

The rendezvous was set in an open field near Mojados. The morning was freezing. The grass, covered in a layer of ice, crunched under the hooves of Fernando's horse. When he arrived at the appointed place, he realized he wasn't the first. News of the meeting had spread, and there they were, bundled up and serious, some of those who had been waiting for this day for a long time: Germana, the Archbishop of Astorga, the Grand Duke of Calatrava. When they caught sight of the Infante, they lowered their heads with more awareness than ever before.

几十米开外，人群看不见，查理注视着他们，努力集中注意力，但距离太远，他看不清自己的兄弟。他和希耶夫尔都骑着马，有士兵护卫。查理本不想让他们陪同，但顾问坚持说这次会议什么事都有可能发生，甚至致命的，所以他们必须受到保护。

Dozens of meters away, unseen by the assembled crowd, Charles watched them, trying to focus his vision, but the distance prevented him from identifying his brother. Both he and Chièvres were on horseback, protected by an escort of soldiers. Charles would have preferred not to have them with him, but the advisor had insisted that anything was possible at this meeting, even the fatal, and they had to be protected.

“走吧，”希耶夫斯鼓励道，他再也无法忍受这种不确定性了。

"Let's go," encouraged Chièvres, who could no longer bear the uncertainty.

查理做了个手势，表示需要一些时间。他想起自己小时候，在敢于加入玩耍之前，总是先偷偷观察其他孩子。停下来观察，先理解，以免犯错。国王需要冷静一下，因为他还不知道该如何对待自己的弟弟。他应该专制吗？冷酷无情吗？他对凯瑟琳如此冷漠，以至于他的灵魂渴望温暖，渴望家庭的温暖。但他犹豫了。他知道，答案就在费迪南的眼神中。

With a gesture, Charles asked for time. He remembered himself as a child, spying on the other children before daring to play. To stop and observe, to understand first so as not to make a mistake. The king needed a pause because he didn't yet know how to deal with his brother. Should he be authoritarian? Cold, perhaps? He had been so cold with Catherine that his soul longed for warmth, for family. But he hesitated. He knew he would find the answer in Ferdinand's eyes.

“走吧，”卡洛斯重复道。

"Let's go," Carlos repeated.

当费尔南多和他的同伴们看到地平线上出现皇家队伍时，一种庄严肃穆的气氛笼罩了他们。众人思绪万千，谁也不敢打破这片寂静。王子下马迎接他的兄弟。阳光洒在晴朗的天空下，脚下的霜冻瞬间融化成水。卡洛斯仍然骑在马上，费尔南多已经下马步行，两人在走近之前第一次互相看了一眼。他们谁也没有想象过对方此刻的模样。费尔南多原本以为会看到一个傲慢、成熟、冷酷的身影。卡洛斯则预感到他的兄弟会做出一些反复无常的举动，但他却并未察觉。

When Fernando and his companions spotted the royal procession on the horizon, a solemn tension settled over them. So many thoughts raced through their minds that no one dared break the silence. The prince dismounted to greet his brother. Beneath his feet, the frost melted into water thanks to the sun, which was already shining in a clear sky. Before approaching, Carlos, still on horseback, and Fernando, already on foot, looked at each other for the first time. Neither had imagined the other as they appeared then. Fernando had expected a haughty, more mature, and implacable figure. Carlos had anticipated a capricious gesture from his brother, which he failed to detect.

最后，卡洛斯下了马。他们只走了几步，便面对面站着。周围的人仿佛都消失了。他们必须将所有的感官都集中在对方身上。

Finally, Carlos dismounted. A few steps were all it took for them to stand facing each other. Those around them became invisible. They needed all their senses focused solely on the other.

“哥哥，”卡洛斯说道。

—Brother —said Carlos.

费尔南多迟迟没有回复，这让希耶夫尔感到煎熬。他迫切想知道自己面对的究竟是叛徒还是忠诚的王子。如果注定要开战，他希望战争早点到来。

Fernando's reply was slow in coming, and Chièvres experienced it as torture. He longed to know what he was up against, whether a traitor or a loyal prince. If there was to be war, he hoped it would come soon.

但随着一个坚定的动作，婴儿的膝盖触到了地面，决定了王国的未来。

But with a firm movement, the infant's knee touched the ground and decided the future of the kingdom.

“陛下，”费尔南多说着，向他的兄弟低下了头，以示服从。

"Your Majesty," said Fernando as he bowed his head before his brother, in a sign of obedience.

费尔南多的忠诚如同雨水般降临在场的人身上。对于阴谋者而言，这雨水如同秋雨，让他们面色苍白、瑟瑟发抖；对于查理和希耶夫尔而言，这雨水如同夏雨，驱散了自他们踏上西班牙土地以来一直笼罩着他们的沉重气氛。

Fernando's loyalty fell upon those present like rain. An autumnal rain upon the conspirators, for it had left them bloodless and trembling, and a summer rain upon Charles and Chièvres, for it had swept away the heavy atmosphere that had clung to them since they had set foot in Spain.

 

 

 

 

一切始于一个动作，也终于一个动作：西斯内罗斯单膝跪地，眨了眨眼，向这个世界告别。他离世时并不知道和平终将到来，但他知道自己已为此献出了生命。他临终前的最后一个念头是给查尔斯的：“愿上帝赐予你力量，去完成你即将面对的使命。”

Everything begins and ends with a gesture: a knee on the ground and the blink with which Cisneros bid farewell to this world. He had died unaware that there would be peace, but knowing that he had given his life for it. His last thought was for Charles: "May God give you strength for the undertaking that awaits you."

2

2

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

1518年2月2日，圣巴勃罗教堂里人头攒动，盛装打扮，宛如一场盛大的游行。人们互相亲吻双手，互致问候，彼此间的怨恨也烟消云散，因为在这样的场合，容不得丝毫的琐碎。查理即将到来，这让他们感到团结一致：他们是卡斯蒂利亚人，而他不是。教堂的墙壁迎接了最杰出的贵族和教士。一个个姓氏反复出现：帕切科、门多萨、阿尔瓦雷斯·德·托莱多。西班牙的显贵和伟大的神职人员，阿门。在他们每个人的过去，都有一位恶人或一位圣人，这取决于他们在天主教君主统治下积累了多少财富。有些人视他们为不幸；有些人，仅仅一提起他们，就热泪盈眶。对于阿拉贡的费尔南多一世的统治，人们的看法也同样截然不同。然而，他们对查理的父亲菲利普一世却只有鄙夷之情。他统治时期唯一的可取之处就是短暂。至于这究竟是出于上帝的旨意，还是如许多人后来怀疑的那样，是天主教君主的干预，其实并不重要。但对于这个儿子，这个远在他乡长大的孩子，一个令人憎恶的统治者和一个可怜的疯女人的后代，又能指望他什么呢？“愿他以这王国应有的谦逊和智慧治理我们，”这是人们常说的话。他们的意思是，愿他能允许自己被治理。

On February 2, 1518, the Church of San Pablo was a parade of finery and polished habits. Hands were kissed, compliments exchanged, and grudges forgotten because the occasion brooked no pettiness, and because the imminent arrival of Charles made them feel united: they were Castilians, he was not. The walls of the church welcomed the most distinguished members of the nobility and clergy. Surnames were repeated: Pacheco, Mendoza, Álvarez de Toledo. The grandees of Spain and the great men of God, amen. In the past of each of them, there was a villain or a saint, depending on how much their wealth had grown under the Catholic Monarchs. Some considered them their misfortune; others, at the mere mention of them, had tears in their eyes. Regarding the sole reign of Ferdinand of Aragon, there was the same disparity of opinion. None of them, however, harbored anything but contempt for the memory of Philip I, Charles's father. The only redeeming quality of his reign had been its brevity. Whether this was due to God or the intervention of the Catholic Monarch, as so many came to suspect, mattered little. But what could be expected of the son, this child raised so far away, the offspring of a hated ruler and a poor madwoman? "May he govern us with the humility and wisdom this kingdom deserves," was the common refrain. May he allow himself to be governed, they meant.

当国王矮小的身影出现在教堂门口的阴影中时，窃窃私语声戛然而止。查理小心翼翼地迈着步子走了进去，他深知这是一个历史性的时刻。他的随从跟在他身后，他的弟弟费迪南德走在显眼的位置，以示忠诚；在他们身后，是希耶夫尔和阿德里安，他们骄傲得如同父亲一般。国王走进中央通道时，目光紧紧盯着祭坛，不愿与这些陌生人对视。在场的人认为他的这一举动纯粹是傲慢；他们做梦也想不到，像查理这样胆怯的人，竟然会在即将宣誓登基之际，如此谨慎，不愿冒险。他的目光只是短暂地游移了一下，他瞥见了一个女人的微笑，那女人皮肤白皙，神态活泼，五官比其他人更显异域风情，身披华丽的丝绸，宛如一份珍贵的礼物。当卡洛斯意识到她是他在莫哈多斯遇到的祖父的遗孀杰尔马娜·德·福伊克斯时，他露出了笑容，但感觉很奇怪。

The murmurs ceased when the king's small figure appeared in shadow on the church doorstep. Charles entered, measuring his steps carefully, aware that this was a historic moment. Behind him came his retinue, with his brother Ferdinand in a prominent position, displaying his loyalty; and behind them, Chièvres and Adrian, proud as fathers. As he entered the central aisle, the king fixed his gaze on the altar so as not to have to meet the eyes of any of these strangers. Those present considered this gesture pure arrogance; they would never have imagined that Charles, timid as he was, would have been the last person to want to risk his nerves just before being sworn in as monarch. His gaze only strayed for a moment, as he caught a glimpse of a woman's smile, a lady with snowy skin and a lively expression, her features more foreign than the rest, and draped in luxurious silks, like a gift. When Carlos realized that it was Germana de Foix, his grandfather's widow whom he had met in Mojados, he smiled back and felt strange.

查理来到圣坛前，落座，仪式开始：弥撒，他手按圣经，誓言为王国献出生命。在场的人看到的是查理平静，甚至有些冷漠的神情。有人认为这是他出身的缘故；大多数人则认为这是外国人对西班牙天生缺乏感情的表现。他的镇定令在场的人失望，查理内心却既感受到自己所作出的承诺带来的情感冲击，也涌起一股恐惧。此前，他一直沉迷于国王的头衔，无暇顾及其他。如今，障碍已然克服，眼前只剩下责任。教堂的灯光让他看不清在场众人的面容，但他能感受到他们的重要性。尽管他明白所有贵族家庭都难免会有纷争，但他却将他们视为一个拥有众多头衔、对王国有着他所缺乏的了解，以及对即将统治他们的人所肩负的重任的人。他也没能在普通民众中找到任何信任。前往教堂的路上，他穿过巴利亚多利德的民众，他们几乎没有装饰街道迎接他，也没有听到任何欢呼声，只有一片寂静，仿佛这段路程永无止境。希耶夫尔察觉到他的失望，便低声开了个玩笑，说卡斯蒂利亚人很克制，但国王并没有被蒙蔽：他心中充满怀疑。

Once at the altar, Charles took his seat and the ceremony began: the Mass, his hand upon the Holy Scriptures, the promise to give his life for the kingdom. Those present saw a serene, even cold, Charles. Some attributed this to the character of those of his birth; most, to the natural lack of affection a foreigner might feel for Spain. While his composure disappointed those present, Charles felt within himself the emotion of the commitment he was making, but also a surge of fear. The desire to hold the title of king had kept him too preoccupied until then. With the obstacles overcome, the horizon now showed only responsibility. The church light did not allow him to clearly distinguish the faces of those before him, but he could sense their importance, and although he was aware that conflicts were common in all noble families, he perceived them as a single man, laden with titles and overflowing with knowledge about the kingdom that he lacked, and above all, with demands on the one who was to govern them. He found no trust among the common people either. On his way to the church, he had walked among the people of Valladolid, who had barely decorated their streets to receive him, and he had heard no cheers, only a silence that made the walk seem endless. Chièvres, noticing his disappointment, whispered a joke about Castilian restraint, but the king was not fooled: there was suspicion.

宣誓效忠王国之后，贵族们依次走过祭坛宣誓。查理这才得以将他们一一辨认出来。在他们站在他面前的短短几秒钟里，他试图分辨出他们的本性：傲慢自大者、阿谀奉承者、目空一切者。但他们的誓言听起来发自肺腑，许多人起身时都对他露出微笑。查理心想，或许，恐惧是他们年轻的标志，这些人将来或许能成为优秀的封臣。

Once the oath to the kingdom had been sworn, the nobles filed past the altar to take their oaths. Charles thus put faces and names to each of them. In the few seconds they stood before him, he tried to discern their nature: the arrogant one, the flatterer, the proud one. But the oaths sounded heartfelt, and many smiled at him as they rose. Perhaps, Charles thought, fear was a sign of their youth, and these men could make good vassals.

 

 

 

 

接下来的几天里，国王的紧张情绪逐渐消散。狩猎成了他的良药，就像在弗兰德斯时一样。没有什么比乡村清新的空气和捕捉野兽的挑战更能让查理精神焕发。这是一种原始的仪式，因此也简单纯粹，没有他生活中其他种种的不确定性，没有他肩负的重任，也没有处理众多事务的复杂局面。

The king's nerves gradually dissipated over the following days. Hunting was his medicine, just as it had been in Flanders. Nothing invigorated Charles more than the fresh country air and the challenge of catching the beasts. It was a primitive ritual, and therefore simple, devoid of the uncertainties of the rest of his life, the weight of his destiny, and the complexities of dealing with so many.

他喜欢和费尔南多一起狩猎。他们最初几次狩猎时，几乎没说过几句话：两人都假装全神贯注于狩猎，以至于无法交谈。由于年龄相仿，也因为命运让他们争夺同一头衔，两人之间存在着某种竞争。猎物为此付出了代价：它们竭尽全力智取对方，以至于都变得致命。他们之间有猜忌和羞涩，但渐渐地，这种羞怯变得令人不安，狩猎也变得疲惫不堪，于是他们开始交谈，而且交谈的时间也越来越长。虽然是兄弟，他们却像陌生人一样，但有什么东西将他们联系在一起：那就是他们的青春。直到和费尔南多相处了一段时间，卡洛斯才意识到，身边总是围绕着一群至少五十岁的人作为顾问，这种感觉是多么不自然。他关心他们，但现在他意识到，他无法与他们分享他与兄弟之间分享的一切：那种豪情壮志，那种无缘无故的欢笑，以及他们之间对人生共同产生的种种困惑——而他们对人生的了解都还非常有限。除此之外，还有那份血脉相连的纽带。

He liked having Fernando with him. On their first hunts, they had barely exchanged a few words: both had pretended to be so engrossed in the hunt that it prevented them from talking. There was a certain rivalry, due to their age and because fate had made them both vie for the same crown. The beasts paid the price: they tried so hard to outwit each other that both were lethal. There was suspicion and shyness between them, but little by little, their timidity became uncomfortable, the hunt exhausting, and conversations began to emerge and lengthen. Although brothers, they were strangers, but something united them: their youth. Until he had spent time in Fernando's company, Carlos hadn't realized how artificial it felt to always be surrounded by men no less than fifty years old, as his advisors. He cared for them, but now he realized that he couldn't share with them what he shared with his brother: the bravado, the laughter for no reason, the doubts that arose between them about life, of which they both still knew so little. And besides all that, there was the bond, the blood.

“你觉得她像人们说的那样疯了吗？”一天晚上，狩猎结束后，卡洛斯问她。

"Do you think she's crazy, like they say?" Carlos asked her one evening, after the hunt was over.

费尔南多不喜欢谈论他的母亲。

Fernando didn't like to talk about his mother.

“你和任何人都清楚这一点，”他回答道。

—You know it as well as anyone —he replied.

——而没有人质疑的，是事实，是共识。我见到她时，发现她虽然情绪崩溃，但很懂事。为什么我们的祖父对她如此残忍？为什么要把她锁起来？

—And what no one disputes is true, or agreement? When I saw her, I noticed she was sensible, although overwhelmed. Why did our grandfather behave so cruelly toward her? Why did he lock her up?

“这都是为了王国的利益，”费尔南多补充道，这句话听起来像是一句听过无数遍、已经变成教条的话。“难道不是因为这个原因，当法律规定应该由她来统治时，你却要代劳吗？如果符合她的利益，国王就不应该手下留情。”

"It was for the good of the kingdom," Fernando added, and it sounded like a phrase heard a thousand times and turned into dogma. "Isn't that why you govern when by law it should be her? If it suits her cause, a king should show no mercy."

卡洛斯对费尔南多十五岁时的严厉感到惊讶。他确信这种感觉并非出自自己。

Carlos was surprised by Fernando's harshness at fifteen. He was certain that this feeling wasn't his own.

“我们的祖父一定是个铁石心肠的人，”卡洛斯说。

—Our grandfather must have been a man of stone— said Carlos.

伟人既不严厉也不宽容，而是视情况而定。他用严格的管教抚养我，但每天都拥抱我。

—Great men are neither stern nor lenient. They are both, depending on what is necessary. He raised me with rigor, but he hugged me every day.

“我只听到他对我的赞扬，”卡洛斯不悦地皱着眉头说。

"I only hear praise from him," said Carlos with a grimace of displeasure.

——难道你不感到自豪吗？他是你的祖父。

—Doesn't it fill you with pride? He's your grandfather.

——还有我的前任。如果他的名声无可挑剔，我又怎能让人们忘记他呢？

—And also the one who preceded me on the throne. How can I make people forget him, if his memory is beyond reproach?

夜鸟的鸣叫声开始在各处响起。伴随着它们的鸣叫，原本的谈话似乎也变得阴沉起来。

The cries of nocturnal birds began to sound here and there. The conversation seemed to grow more somber with their chirping.

“西班牙人不喜欢我，”卡洛斯说。“我觉得他们对我抱有最坏的预期。”

"The Spaniards don't like me," said Carlos. "I feel they expect the worst from me."

卡斯蒂利亚人也不喜欢我们的祖父。他们视他为陌生人，因为他是阿拉贡人。他必须赢得他们的认可。你也一样。

—The Castilians didn't like our grandfather either. They considered him a stranger because he was Aragonese. He had to win them over. You'll have to do the same.

 

 

 

 

查理每天下午外出狩猎时，希耶夫尔的猎物比他更多，但他的奖赏并非野兽，而是王国中尽可能多的贵族头衔和教会官职。没有奖赏的政府算什么？是沉重的负担，是制造敌人的机器，是任何一个头脑清醒的人都不会想要的东西。如果没有财富作为补偿，那就让别人来得及。虽然哈德良的野心似乎更为克制，因为他的性格更加理智和安于现状，但看到希耶夫尔的野心如此肆意释放，他不禁开始反思自己是否过于谦逊。渐渐地，他开始享受为自己攫取官职，并将其他官职分配给他的熟人——那些永远不会踏足西班牙的佛兰德人，但他们乐于见到自己得到奖赏。

While Charles hunted every afternoon, Chièvres bagged even more prey than he did, but his prizes weren't beasts, but rather as many noble titles and ecclesiastical offices as were available in the kingdom. What is government without rewards? A heavy burden, a machine for creating enemies, something no one in their right mind would want for themselves. If there are no riches to compensate, let someone else have it. Although Hadrian's ambition seemed more restrained, because his character was more sensible and content, seeing it unleashed in Chièvres made him wonder if he wasn't, perhaps, being a little too humble, and little by little he began to enjoy accumulating offices for himself and distributing others among his acquaintances, Flemish people who would never set foot in Spain but who would be grateful to see themselves rewarded.

空缺的职位都是因主教去世而留下的空缺。这类职位众多，包括主教和领主，遍布西班牙本土和大西洋彼岸的新大陆。但其中一个职位的重要性远超其他职位，令它们相形见绌。西斯内罗斯枢机主教的去世，使得西班牙教会的最高荣誉——主教——空缺出来。这个职位不仅收入丰厚，而且权力堪比国王。

The available positions were those of men whose deaths had left their titles vacant. There were many of these—bishoprics and lordships—both in Spain and in the new lands across the Atlantic. But the importance of one of them dwarfed the rest, making them seem like mere trifles in comparison. The death of Cardinal Cisneros had left open the highest honor in the Spanish Church, the position that brought with it not only the most substantial income but also a power rivaled only by that of the king.

“托莱多大主教区将会怎样？”阿德里亚诺问道，他的眼中闪过一丝希望。

"What will become of the archbishopric of Toledo?" Adriano asked, and a hint of hope appeared in his eyes.

“恐怕它已经有主人了：我的侄子吉列尔莫，”希耶夫雷斯说道。

—I'm afraid it already has an owner: my nephew Guillermo —Chièvres declared.

阿德里亚诺吓了一跳。他看着希耶夫尔，就像看着一个突然疯掉的亲戚一样。

Adriano jumped. He looked at Chièvres as if he were looking at a relative who had suddenly gone mad.

——看在上帝的份上，先生！有点常识好吗！他怎么了？才二十岁？

—For God's sake, sir! Have some common sense! What's wrong with him? Twenty years old?

希耶夫尔默默地点了点头。他的平静如此之深，以至于哈德良注意到自己的愤慨正在滋长，仿佛是为了弥补这种平静。

Chièvres nodded silently. His calmness was such that Hadrian noticed his indignation growing, as if to compensate for it.

托莱多大主教是西班牙教会的领袖！很少有人比他更有权力，而且不仅仅是作为神职人员。

—The Archbishop of Toledo is the head of the Church in Spain! Few have more power than he does, and not only as men of God.

——正因如此，它必须由一位永远不会动用它的人守护。威廉向我保证，他绝不会踏足这片土地。大主教的权力不会被行使，我们也不必与他为敌。难道你们宁愿将它授予一个卡斯蒂利亚人，赋予一个既不了解我们，也肯定不尊重我们的人如此重要的地位吗？

—And for that reason, it must be under the guardianship of someone who will never wield it. I have William's assurance that he will not set foot in this kingdom. The power conferred by the archbishopric will not be exercised, and we will not have to contend with him. Would you rather grant it to a Castilian, bestowing such importance upon someone who neither knows us nor, surely, esteems us?

阿德里亚诺点了点头。他感到无能为力。在希耶夫尔那些最具煽动性的计划背后，总有一些论点足以压制一切批评。但这位来自乌得勒支的男人心中涌起一股莫名的不安，这不安逐渐凝结成一个论点。

Adriano nodded. He felt powerless. Beneath Chièvres's most incendiary plans, there were always arguments that silenced all criticism. But the man from Utrecht then felt a vague unease that gradually solidified into a thesis.

“查理一世的第一次卡斯蒂利亚议会即将召开，”他说，“他们将授予王室维持统治所需的特权。在议会召开之前，我们不能激怒臣民。一旦我们赢得这些任命，就让我们来解释清楚。”

“The first Castilian Cortes of Charles will soon take place,” he said, “and they are to grant the crown the privileges that will sustain it. We cannot anger the subjects before they are held. Let us account for this and all other appointments once we have won them.”

“恐惧对统治者而言并非美德，”希耶夫尔回答道。“只要宫廷给我们足够的资金返回弗兰德斯就足够了。查理难道想留在这个乏味的地方吗？他在这里唯一的束缚仅仅是一个头衔。”

“Fear is no virtue in a ruler,” replied Chièvres. “It is enough that the Courts provide us with sufficient funds to return to Flanders. Does Charles wish to remain in this tedious place, to which he is bound only by a title?”

“如果真出了丑闻，他们连租船的钱都不会给我们。我们只能等了。”

"If there were a scandal, they wouldn't even grant us funds to charter a ship. We have to wait."

希耶夫尔思索片刻，点了点头。但他心中却涌起一丝恼怒。并非因为他不得不将自己的野心置于谨慎的摆布之下，而是因为他怀疑这是否是最佳策略。他想起有两种方法可以征服他人：一种是阴险的，只要对方不自知，这种方法就能得逞；另一种是暴虐的，不问缘由，先夺后给，其肆无忌惮反而赢得了被征服者的默默敬仰。他能忍受第一种方法吗？了解自己的他，他犹豫了。

Chièvres considered it and nodded. But he felt irritated. Not because he had to put his ambition at the mercy of prudence, but because he doubted that this was the best strategy. He remembered that there are two ways to subjugate others to one's own will: the insidious way, which triumphs as long as the other remains unaware of surrendering; or the tyrannical way, which doesn't ask, which takes before it's offered, and whose audacity is rewarded with the silent respect of the subjugated. Would he have the patience for the first? Knowing himself, he hesitated.

 

 

 

 

查理从未向他的顾问们提及他与费迪南的会面。他们以为他狩猎时只有狗和仆人陪伴。国王自己也不太清楚为何要对弟弟的行踪保密，但他乐在其中。自从近十年前希耶夫尔成为他的导师以来，无论多么微不足道的事情，他都毫不知情。多年来，希耶夫尔甚至就睡在离他几步之遥的同一间卧室里，仿佛也想守护他的梦境。当希耶夫尔察觉到查理对治理西班牙的责任日益焦虑时，他立即主动提出亲自处理大部分事务，并承诺运用自己的智慧帮助他尽快巩固权力。查理犹豫不决，但最终还是被不安感所支配，同意暂时将这项任务委托他人——只要他需要熟悉国情，并觉得自己能够胜任自己的职责。因此，他才会如此闲散，每日狩猎，以及他那副乐天派的模样——那种无需付出任何努力就能感受到权力的姿态。他原谅了自己：他知道自己还很年轻，哪个初出茅庐的国王没有一个可以信赖的顾问呢？众所周知，在英格兰，亨利多年来沉迷于运动和与名妓寻欢作乐，而沃尔西红衣主教则替他做决定；人们称他为“另一个国王”。他难道不能也这样做吗？查理不再被迫日夜待在希耶夫勒令人窒息的羽翼下，他觉得自己可以以一种不同的方式与他人相处。这位顾问疑心重重，总是警告他提防任何接近他的人，这种怀疑渗透到查理的每一段友谊、每一次人际交往中。然而现在，国王可以自己做出判断，有时他的判断中根本没有任何怀疑，就像对待费迪南德那样。或者像对待杰尔玛娜那样。

Charles never mentioned his meetings with Ferdinand to his advisors. They assumed he was accompanied only by dogs and servants on his hunting trips. The king wasn't entirely sure why he kept his brother's company a secret, but he enjoyed doing so. Since Chièvres had become his tutor almost ten years earlier, no matter how insignificant, had escaped his notice. For years, he even slept just a few feet away from him, in the same bedchamber, as if he wanted to watch over his dreams as well. When Chièvres noticed Charles's growing anxiety about the responsibility of governing Spain, he immediately offered to take on most of the affairs himself, promising to use his wisdom to help him consolidate his power as quickly as possible. Charles hesitated, but his insecurity won out, and he agreed to delegate the task for a time—as long as he needed to familiarize himself with the country and feel capable of fulfilling his duties. Hence his idleness, his daily hunts, and his cheerful disposition, the kind that comes from feeling powerful without having to earn it. He forgave himself: he knew he was very young, and what fledgling king didn't have an advisor to whom he entrusted himself? It was well known that in England, for years, Henry had dedicated himself to sports and impregnating courtesans while Cardinal Wolsey decided everything for him; "the other king," they called him. Couldn't he allow himself the same? No longer forced to remain day and night under Chièvres's suffocating wing, Charles felt he could allow himself to relate to others in a different way. The advisor, so suspicious, had always warned him against anyone who approached him, and that skepticism had infected every friendship of Charles's, every interaction. Now, however, the king could draw his own conclusions, and sometimes there was no suspicion in them at all, as was the case with Ferdinand. Or with Germana.

当天主教国王的遗孀意识到她的教子费迪南德无法继承西班牙王位时，她怒不可遏，整整两天下午都闷闷不乐。但第二天，她的失望便化作了精明：她的未来需要她这样做。她宣称自己效忠查理，如同皈依新的信仰，并拥护一位新的救世主——一位出生于根特的十七岁少年。她从国王与费迪南德的友谊中看到了实现自己野心的契机，有时她会以打招呼为由出现在国王的狩猎队伍中。她想趁着国王的私人生活还很有限，赶紧引起查理的注意，通过逐渐熟悉他来赢得他的信任。她心想，如果查理习惯了见到她，那么有一天，当她在宫中，或者日后出现在他的办公室里，要求一个与其身份相符的头衔时，就不会显得那么突兀了。但杰曼娜的计划出了问题：如果查理只是狩猎而不统治，那么赢得他的支持对她有什么好处呢？

When the widow of the Catholic King realized that her godson, Ferdinand, was not going to rule Spain, she was furious for two afternoons, but the next day her disappointment turned to shrewdness: her future demanded it. She proclaimed her loyalty to Charles as one embraces a new creed and, with it, a new savior, a seventeen-year-old born in Ghent. In the king's friendship with Ferdinand, she saw the gateway to her ambitions, and sometimes she would appear on his hunts under the pretext of simply saying hello. She wanted to be seen by Charles now, while the king's personal life was still so limited, and win him over little by little, through familiarity. If he grew accustomed to seeing her, she reasoned, it wouldn't seem strange to find her one day at the palace, or later in his office, demanding a title befitting her stature. But something was amiss in Germana's plan: what good would it do her to win over Charles if he hunted but didn't rule?

“殿下，王国里一切都好吗？”一天下午，杰玛娜骑在马上问道。

"How are things going in the kingdom, Your Highness?" Germana asked him one afternoon, from her horse.

卡洛斯做了个鬼脸，压低声音回答道。

Carlos made a face and deepened his voice to reply.

“跟他们一起散步太无聊了，没必要破坏你的行程。”他回答道。

—Too boring to spoil your walk with them—he replied.

“或者说，他们离你太远了？”杰尔马纳回答道，“他们说，你的顾问会提出方案，而你只需要签字就行了。”

—Or too far removed from you? —replied Germana—. They say your advisors make proposals and you just sign them.

卡洛斯感到羞愧。

Carlos felt ashamed.

——他们都是智者。

—They are wise men.

——但你是国王。

—But you are the king.

杰尔玛娜策马疾驰而去，以此强调自己的观点。她想让卡洛斯独自一人思考这个真相，使之在他心中生根发芽。

Germana emphasized her point by galloping off. She intended to leave Carlos alone with that truth so that it could take root within him.

费尔南多与卡洛斯一同狩猎的日子里，他总是默默地目睹杰尔玛娜的出现。起初，他只当是偶然相遇，但杰尔玛娜出现的频率越来越高，他这才意识到，这个不久前还怂恿他背叛哥哥的女人，如今却想方设法讨好他。杰尔玛娜的这番举动深深刺痛了费尔南多的自尊心。他并不希望杰尔玛娜反抗卡洛斯，但他至少希望她能怨恨一段时间，为她声称觊觎的、他拒绝的荣耀而哀悼一段时间。

On the days Fernando went hunting with Carlos, he was a silent witness to Germana's appearances. At first, he dismissed them as mere chance encounters, but they became more frequent, and he realized that the woman who had recently encouraged him to betray his brother was now trying to win him over. This surrender stung Fernando's pride. He hadn't wanted Germana to rebel against Carlos, but he had hoped for at least a period of resentment, a time of mourning for the glory she claimed to covete for Fernando, a glory he had rejected.

“你很快就对国王忠心耿耿了，”费尔南多在一次每周例行午餐时对杰尔马纳说，“你对他的疑虑消失得无影无踪，就像王冠戴在他头上一样快。”

—You have quickly become loyal to the king— Fernando told Germana during one of their weekly lunches. —Your reservations about him have taken about as long to disappear as the crown took to be placed on his head.

——而这一切的发生，是因为你接受了他的统治。你是在批评我遵守你的决定吗？

—And that happened because you accepted his rule. Are you criticizing me for abiding by your decision?

“我以为你对我的信任是真诚的。”费尔南多说道。

—I thought your faith in me was sincere— said Fernando.

——确实如此。但现在这对我有什么用呢？——杰尔马娜问道。

—And it was. But what good would it do me now? —asked Germana.

—毫无疑问，你受利益驱使。

—You are undoubtedly guided by profit.

“别想让我为此感到羞耻，你不会得逞的。”杰尔玛娜平静地回答道，“我知道自己是什么身份：一个被王国里许多人憎恨的寡妇。如果我得不到国王的恩宠，我该怎么办？你接近他，难道不也是为了得到同样的恩宠吗？”

"Don't try to make me ashamed of it, you won't succeed," Germana replied calmly. "I know what I am: a widow hated by many in this kingdom. What will become of me if I don't gain the king's favor? Aren't you seeking the same thing by befriending him?"

—我是他的兄弟，不是为了谋取职位而阿谀奉承的人。

—I am his brother, not a flatterer on the lookout for a position.

—嗯，你们两者都应该。因为现在，在他的指挥下，你们的未来和我一样充满不确定性。

—Well, you should be both. Because now, under his command, your future is as uncertain as mine.

费尔南多匆匆吃完饭，以便尽快退下独自思考。他原以为，身为王子，又以忠诚化解了纷争，便无所畏惧。然而，尽管他并不指望卡洛斯会报复，但事实是，他的兄弟不过是谋士们手中的傀儡，他们完全有可能将他彻底边缘化。他想象着自己未来沦为宴会上的摆设，过着无所事事、百无聊赖的生活，祖父灌输给他的所有才能，包括他卓越的治国天赋，都将因无用而被人遗忘。他渴望至少成为一名重要的顾问，能够就税收或战争的利弊提出自己的意见，并被人倾听；他渴望发挥自己的价值，而不是让它白白浪费，最终沦为那些沉溺于宴饮和游戏、对王国福祉毫无贡献的无用贵族。他接受自己无法成为国王，但绝不甘于平庸。

Fernando ate hastily so he could retire as quickly as possible to think in solitude. He had assumed that, as an infante, and having prevented conflict through his loyalty, he had nothing to fear. But although he didn't expect revenge from Carlos, the truth was that his brother was a puppet in the hands of his advisors, and they could well try to reduce him to nothing. He imagined himself in the future as a decorative figure at receptions, an unbearably idle life in which everything his grandfather had instilled in him, all that talent for governance, would be forgotten from lack of use. He wanted to be at least an important advisor, to offer his opinion on the advisability of a tax or a war and to be listened to; to use his worth and not let it languish until he became one of those useless nobles content with banquets and games, contributing nothing to the well-being of the kingdom. He accepted not being king, but never being nobody.

于是，在下次与杰尔马纳共进午餐时，费尔南多向她坦白了自己的想法，杰尔马纳骄傲地看着他。

So at the next lunch with Germana, Fernando confessed his thoughts to her and she looked at him with pride.

 

 

 

 

从国王的反应来看，杰尔玛娜在之后几次去狩猎时开始怀疑，费尔南多可能因为这件事而感到受伤，所以警告过他的弟弟要提防她。查理变得越来越沉默寡言，目光也总是避开她。但她很快意识到，这与其说是拒绝，不如说是羞涩，她明白这只能是一个原因：查理已经迷恋上她了。起初，这让她感到惊讶，然后觉得好笑，最终她才明白这究竟是什么：一种恩赐。

Judging by the king's reaction, Germana began to think, during subsequent visits to the hunts, that Fernando, hurt by the situation, had warned his brother against her. Charles became increasingly taciturn, and his gaze avoided hers. But she soon understood that it was more a growing shyness than rejection, and she realized that this could only be due to one cause: Charles was becoming infatuated with her. At first, this astonished her, then amused her, and finally revealed itself to her for what it was: a blessing.

尽管卡洛斯极力压抑，但他对杰尔玛娜的感情却与日俱增。他曾多次告诫自己绝不想起她，但他的思绪却总是不受控制地游荡。无论别人如何告诫他，爱上一个曾与祖父同床共枕的人是不道德的，事实是，压抑和谴责往往只会助长他的迷恋。他幻想她那红棕色的头发和丰润的嘴唇，费尔南多谈起她时对她智慧的赞叹也让他心潮澎湃。卡洛斯甚至不敢在人前提起她的名字，唯恐自己的声音泄露了他对她的爱慕之情。而这种将她藏于心底的做法，反而让杰尔玛娜的身影彻底侵蚀了他，如同毒药一般，若不加以清除，便会扩散到他身体的每一个器官。卡洛斯那天晚上似乎从杰尔玛娜的眼神中看到了邀请，为此他彻夜难眠。第二天，他精疲力竭，无力克制自己的冲动。夜幕降临，他便去拜访了她。

Carlos's feelings for Germana grew within him despite the guilt with which he tried to stifle them. There were days when he promised himself not to give her a single thought, but his mind seemed to wander on its own, beyond his control. No matter how often he was told it was indecent to desire someone who had shared his grandfather's bed, the truth was that repression and condemnation, as they often do, only fueled his infatuation. He fantasized about her reddish hair and luscious lips, and he was excited by the intelligence Fernando attributed to her when speaking of her. Carlos didn't even allow himself to mention her name in front of others, lest his voice betray the emotion he felt for her. And this keeping her to himself only served to allow the thought of Germana to completely contaminate him, like a poison that, if not expelled, spreads to every organ of the body. The day he thought he saw an invitation in Germana's gaze, Carlos spent a sleepless night, and the exhaustion of the following day left him too weak to censor himself. As night fell, he went to visit her.

见到他，杰尔玛娜感到紧张。她怎能指望这个腼腆的年轻人有勇气出现在她面前呢？当她察觉到国王对她感兴趣时，她原本只是想利用他，而不是想赢得他的心。她想，没必要那样；柏拉图式的爱比征服者更加慷慨。但眼前是查理，一个男人不会在夜里来访，除非他想在黎明前得到满足。

Upon receiving him, Germana felt nervous. How could she expect from this shy young man the courage it took to appear there? When she sensed the king's interest, she had only intended to use him to her advantage, not to win him over. It wasn't necessary, she thought; one who loves platonically is even more generous than one who conquers. But there was Charles before her, and a man doesn't visit at night unless he intends to be satisfied by dawn.

杰尔玛娜犹豫了一下，想找个借口推辞，但她注意到年轻人的紧张，想要鼓励他鼓起勇气前来。于是，她邀请他共进晚餐。

For a moment Germana considered making an excuse, but she noticed the young man's nervousness and wanted to reward the courage that had brought him there. She invited him to dinner.

一个小时后，卡斯蒂利亚葡萄酒让他们放松了下来。

After an hour, the Castilian wine had relaxed them.

“我开始喜欢上它了，”卡洛斯喝完杯中的酒说道，“但我还是更喜欢家乡的啤酒。”

"I'm starting to like it," said Carlos, finishing his drink. "But I still prefer the beer from my homeland."

——这也是你们的土地。

—This is your land too.

卡洛斯既没有点头也没有摇头。

Carlos neither nodded nor shook his head.

“你难道不是在等待王国爱你，然后你才能爱它吗？”杰尔马纳问道，“你是个外国人。西班牙人对任何外来事物都抱有戒心。”

"Aren't you waiting for the kingdom to love you so you can love it back?" Germana asked. "You're a foreigner. And the Spanish are wary of anything that comes from outside."

——他们的疑虑会持续多久？

—And how long will their misgivings last?

“这取决于你，”杰尔马纳答道。“去诱惑他们。你若不先臣服于他们，就无法征服他们。他们知道你把权力交给你的顾问。那些被你冷落的人，又怎会珍惜你呢？儿子爱的是父亲，而不是父亲派来照顾他的人。”

"It depends on you," Germana replied. "Seduce them. You can't conquer without first surrendering yourself. They know you delegate to your advisors. How can those who feel neglected by you possibly value you? A son loves his father, not the one he sends to care for him."

“也许吧。不过在我来之前不久，他们就已经很喜欢我了。在他们心里，我爷爷和费尔南多是第一位的。没有我的位置，”卡洛斯抱怨道。

"Maybe. But they already liked me shortly before I came. In their hearts there's my grandfather and then Fernando. There's no room for me," Carlos complained.

“不要为他们对你哥哥的爱而感到惋惜。好好利用这份爱吧。你也能从他对这些王国的了解中获益。费迪南德从小就被培养成统治者，虽然他忠于你，但他那为国效力的愿望依然未变。如果你让他失去利用价值，他会终生怨恨。他是个政治家，这是他的天性。”

"Do not lament the love they feel for your brother. Take advantage of it. You would also be benefiting from his knowledge of these kingdoms. Ferdinand was raised to rule, and although he is loyal to you, that desire to serve remains intact. He will live a life of resentment if you render him useless. He is a politician. It is in his nature."

让弟弟担任顾问的想法令卡洛斯感到惊讶。这合乎逻辑，他之前竟从未想到过。但如同他一贯的作风，每当需要深思熟虑时，国王便将答案留待日后，又喝完了一杯酒。这场充满政治意味的谈话几乎让他忘记了此行的目的。然而，杰尔玛娜纤细迷人的脖颈却重新点燃了他的欲望。她察觉到了，心中充满困惑。卡洛斯身上似乎有某种东西在诱惑着她。而这并非因为他的地位。她感到与他亲近。或许是因为他们都曾是这个王国的异乡人，而正是这种共同的无助将他们紧紧联系在一起。她的青春在她眼中也显得格外美丽，因为它并非张扬，而是甜美。他对她的渴望让她感到自己真正活着。自从丈夫去世后，杰尔玛娜便将爱的能力深藏于心；在这个充满敌意的地方，她需要爱才能生存下去。但现在，她再次有机会将自己交付于他人，她的身体也重新记起了被拥抱的愉悦、温暖和幸福。

The idea of ​​making his brother his advisor surprised Carlos. It was so logical, it had escaped him. But as was his custom when something required reflection, the king reserved his answer for another time and finished another glass of wine. The conversation, so political in nature, had almost made him forget the reason for his visit. But Germana's neck, delicate and alluring, rekindled his desire. She noticed and felt confused. There was something about Carlos that tempted her. And it wasn't his position. She felt close to him. Perhaps it was because they were both strangers in that kingdom, and that shared helplessness bound them together. Her youth also seemed beautiful to her, because it wasn't brazen, but sweet. And his desire for her made her feel alive. Since her husband's death, Germana had kept her capacity for love to herself; she needed it to survive in that hostile place. But now she had the chance again to give herself to another, and her body remembered the pleasure, the warmth, and the happiness of being embraced.

杰尔马纳注意到卡洛斯几乎什么都没吃。

Germana noticed that Carlos had barely eaten a thing.

——那只野鸡没能说服你。而且据说你胃口很好。

—The pheasant didn't convince you. And they say you have good appetites.

“我不是故意冒犯你的。我几乎没什么胃口，”卡洛斯说。

"I didn't mean to offend you. I barely have an appetite," said Carlos.

你是不是生病了？

—Are you ill, perhaps?

“不知怎么的，”卡洛斯心想。但他摇了摇头。

"Somehow," Carlos thought. But he shook his head.

“那你一定是恋爱了，”杰尔马纳说，“当爱情占据身体时，它会彻底侵蚀身体，让你没有空间进食。”

—Then you must be in love— said Germana. —When love takes hold of the body, it invades it so completely that it leaves no room for food.

卡洛斯注意到他的脸颊泛红。意识到这一点后，这种感觉更加强烈了。这时，杰尔马纳注意到国王的眼下有黑眼圈。

Carlos noticed his cheeks flushing. Realizing this only intensified the feeling. Germana then noticed that the king had dark circles under his eyes.

爱情也让我们彻夜难眠。当生活赐予我们梦想的一切，谁还想沉睡？我们仿佛乘风破浪，难以置信，如果没有那个如今成为我们生命意义的人，我们竟然还能活下去……

Love also keeps us awake. Who wants to sleep when life gives us what we dreamed of? We walk as if carried by the air, and we are amazed that we could have lived without the one who is now the reason for our being…

“我爱你们所有人。”卡洛斯打断道。

—I love you all —Carlos interrupted.

一片寂静。

Silence fell.

“不，你不爱我，”杰尔马纳回答道，并温柔地看着他。

"No, you don't love me," Germana replied, and looked at him tenderly.

卡洛斯随即站了起来，神情慌乱，头晕目眩，显然是喝了酒。

Carlos then stood up, flustered and dizzy from the wine.

—不好意思，酒让我胆子大了。

—Excuse me, the wine has emboldened me.

杰尔马纳抓住卡洛斯的手，阻止他。

Germana took Carlos's hand to restrain him.

你不必爱我才能留下。

—You don't have to love me to stay.

卡洛斯也看到她起身。两人沉默地面对面站着。他知道自己唯一的选择要么是逃走，要么是吻她，然后一直待到天亮才离开那栋房子，之后就得承担后果，更别提他们的婚外情曝光的恐惧了，谁知道会不会给他带来很多麻烦。然而，他还是吻了她。

Carlos saw her get up too. They stood there in silence, face to face. He knew his only options were to flee, or kiss her and not leave that house until dawn, and then have to face the consequences, not to mention the fear that their affair would get out, and who knows, maybe even cause him a lot of trouble. And yet, he kissed her.

 

 

 

 

第二天清晨，查理早早前来与希耶夫会面，后者面带满意的微笑迎接了他。如果说狩猎已经让国王分心，那么他的私事无疑会让王国更加牢牢地落入这位顾问的掌控之中。然而，当查理提出要参加当天的议会时，希耶夫的喜悦瞬间消失殆尽。他答应了，但却让国王难以应付。他连珠炮似地抛出一连串查理一无所知的棘手问题：尤卡坦半岛、宗教立法以及王国间的贸易细节。经过两个不眠之夜，国王终于在几个小时后屈服，但承诺第二天会再次主持议会。希耶夫这才意识到查理的爆发并非一时冲动，他下令监视查理的行踪。他怀疑有人在幕后操纵。当间谍报告查理与斐迪南和日耳曼娜的会面时，这位顾问勃然大怒。他真是太粗心了，如今国王竟然听信了那些不仅不受他控制，而且自身利益与他相悖的人的意见。他必须抓紧时间重夺地位，确保自己的计划在查理彻底脱离王位之前得以实现。

When Charles arrived early the next morning to meet with Chièvres, the latter greeted him with a satisfied smile. If hunting already distracted the king enough, his affair would leave the kingdom even more firmly in the advisor's hands. But his contentment soured when Charles asked to participate in the day's council. Chièvres complied, but made the meeting impossible for the king. He bombarded him with difficult questions about matters Charles knew nothing about: Yucatán, religious legislation, and details of trade between the kingdoms. After two sleepless nights, the monarch finally gave in after a couple of hours, but promised to preside over the council again the following day. Chièvres then understood that Charles's outburst had not been a passing whim, and he ordered that Charles's movements be followed. He suspected that someone was influencing him. When the spies reported Charles's meetings with Ferdinand and Germana, the advisor flew into a rage. How careless he had been, for now the king was listening to others who were not only beyond his influence but also had their own interests, contrary to his own. He had to hurry to regain his position and ensure his plans came to fruition before Charles finally broke away.

 

 

 

 

殿下，这些法令急需您的签字。

—Your Highness, your signature on these decrees is urgently needed.

顾问将文件放在查理坐的桌子上，笃定国王会像以往无数次那样：不经阅读就签字。但查理，这位日渐适应君主角色的国王，在希耶夫尔焦虑的注视下，逐一阅读了这些文件。

The advisor placed the documents on the table where Charles sat, trusting that the king would do what he had done so many times before: sign them without reading them first. But Charles, who with each passing day felt more at home in his role as ruler, read them one by one, under Chièvres's anxious gaze.

“这些职位有很多，”国王不以为然地说。

"These positions are numerous," said the king, unconvinced.

—学期伊始，需要做出许多决定。

—At the beginning of a term, many decisions must be made.

年轻人在阅读其中一份文件时，突然被吓了一跳。

Suddenly, the young man was startled as he read one of the files.

——你的侄子，托莱多大主教？

—Your nephew, the Archbishop of Toledo?

“这是西班牙的关键位置。我们必须控制住它。吉列尔莫会按照我们的意愿行事。”

"It's a key position in Spain. We have to keep it under control. Guillermo will do as we wish."

国王看着他的顾问，等待进一步的解释。

The king looked at his advisor, waiting for further explanation.

我曾向你承诺，我会巩固你的权力。

—I promised you that I would consolidate your power.

“这就是正确的道路吗？”火烈鸟带着真诚的怀疑问道。

"And this is the way?" asked the flamingo, with genuine doubt.

殿下，议会之行将是一项挑战。我们必须先展现出我们的权威才能抵达那里。

—Your Highness, the Cortes will be a challenge. We must arrive there having demonstrated our authority.

卡洛斯想了想。短暂的停顿后，顾问补充道：

Carlos thought about it. After a brief pause, the advisor added:

—如果我的一切都取决于你的荣耀，我又有什么理由不好好地为你服务呢？

—What interest would I have in serving you badly, if everything I am and have depends on your glory?

国王被这番论证说服，最终签署了那道法令，随后又签署了其余法令。另一个人松了口气，但又因险些失败而感到恼火，毕竟他习惯了不必如此详细地解释自己的决定。如今，希耶夫尔手握签署好的文件，准备继续执行他的策略。

The argument convinced the king enough to sign that decree, and then the rest. The other man felt relieved, but displeased at having come so close to failure, accustomed as he was to not having to justify his decisions in such detail. With the signed documents now in his possession, Chièvres prepared to continue with his strategy.

我注意到你经常和你的兄弟在一起。

—It has come to my attention that you spend time with your brother.

卡洛斯知道自己处于希耶夫斯的监视之下，感到很不自在，但他只是点了点头。

Carlos felt uncomfortable knowing he was under Chièvres' watch, but he simply nodded.

—在他前往弗兰德斯之前，你好好享受和他在一起的时光是对的。

—You are right to enjoy his company before he leaves for Flanders.

“弗兰德斯？费尔南多为什么要去那里？”卡洛斯问道。

"Flanders? Why would Fernando travel there?" asked Carlos.

希耶夫尔假装困惑。

Chièvres feigned bewilderment.

殿下，您应该明白他不能继续留在这些王国。他承载着那些尚未接受您统治者的希望。

—Your Highness, you will assume that he cannot remain in these kingdoms. He embodies the hope of those who have not yet accepted your authority.

“难道就因为有人想拥立他为王，我就应该把他流放吗？那样只会招致更多人的憎恨。”卡洛斯回答道。

"Should I exile him because some want to put him on the throne? That will only earn me more hatred," replied Carlos.

—因为费尔南多是西班牙人的软肋！

—Because Fernando is the weakness of the Spanish!

“我将以公正治理国家，我将成为公正的化身。”卡洛斯回答道。

—I will govern with judgment and I will become one —replied Carlos.

殿下，世上没有比只凭人们的想象统治更好的人了。把你的兄弟从这片土地上赶走，否则他的理想将永远无法从这片土地上消失。

—Your Highness, no one governs better than he who governs only in the imagination of men. Remove your brother from these lands, or his ideal will never be extinguished for those who live here.

看着希耶夫尔迈着他那标志性的坚定步伐匆匆走出办公室，查尔斯心中仿佛响起了一声孩童的哭喊，那是他妹妹卡塔琳娜的哭声，她被拖回了托尔德西利亚斯的囚禁之地。从那以后，那愤怒而无助的哭喊声多次出现在他的梦中，噩梦般的经历让他从噩梦中惊醒，浑身冷汗，愧疚不已。他怎能让自己良心背负着又一次针对自己亲生骨肉的不公呢？

As he watched Chièvres hurry out of the office, with his characteristic firm stride, Charles heard within him the cry of a child, that of his sister Catalina, dragged back into confinement in Tordesillas. That cry of rage and helplessness had appeared in his dreams several times since then, in nightmares that woke him drenched in sweat and guilt. How could he burden his conscience with yet another injustice against his own flesh and blood?

 

 

 

 

法国国王弗朗索瓦一世若能知晓查理五世的种种忧虑，定会欣喜不已。他将自己与这位饱受疑虑折磨的根特国王相提并论，该是多么自豪啊！因为他自己统治的王国鲜花盛开，无人质疑。然而，查理的自信并非完美无缺，而正是这唯一的一丝裂痕，令弗朗索瓦如痴如醉，如同身处寂静之中，却被某种声音所困扰。尽管弗朗索瓦剥夺了波旁公爵在米兰的统治权，但后者丝毫未受影响，反而更加桀骜不驯。弗朗索瓦最终明白了其中的缘由：他不再需要对公爵俯首称臣，也不再需要虚情假意地讨好他，因为他无需再为了保住自己在意大利公国的地位而取悦公爵。公爵只对他的岳母，法国的安妮——波旁家族的前摄政王和永恒的统治者——低头致敬。正是她祝福了女儿苏珊娜的婚事，也正是她将头衔、财富和放荡不羁的性情倾注于公爵。

Francis I of France would have relished knowing of the myriad anxieties plaguing Charles. How he would have swelled with pride comparing himself to this king of Ghent, plagued by doubts, for he himself wandered his kingdom amidst showers of flowers, his rule unquestioned. But his confidence had a crack, and since it was only one, it obsessed Francis, like someone surrounded by silence, kept awake by a single sound. Despite having stripped the Duke of Bourbon of the government of Milan, the latter had not been tamed in the slightest; quite the contrary. And Francis finally understood why: he no longer owed him obedience, nor false affection, for he no longer had to please him to maintain his position in the Italian duchy. The duke only bowed his head to his mother-in-law, Anne of France, former regent and eternal ruler of the House of Bourbon. It was she who blessed the marriage of her daughter Susanna, and thus who showered him with titles, wealth, and immodesty.

但公爵夫人体弱多病，她的母亲对她的未来忧心忡忡，因​​为尽管她年纪渐长，死神似乎却已近在咫尺。终于有一天，看似平常的一天，死神夺走了她的生命。

But the duke's wife was a sickly woman, and her mother was obsessed with her future, for although she was getting older, death seemed to be near. And one day, which seemed like any other, it took her.

苏珊娜的去世使公爵成了鳏夫；法国的安妮悲痛欲绝；而弗朗西斯的母亲萨伏依的路易丝则欣喜若狂。苏珊娜在没有兄弟的情况下，通过一项特殊的让步继承了爵位，但由于她无子嗣，波旁公国及其其他荣誉如今空置，等待着一位远房亲戚继承。而路易丝正是那位幸运儿。每当她的表妹苏珊娜流产，弗朗西斯的母亲都会露出愧疚的微笑。她们的血缘关系早已断绝，其中一个原因（如今已遥远）是，路易丝年轻时曾爱慕过这位如今的公爵，而他也同样爱慕着她；但这份爱恋只持续到苏珊娜向他献上诱人的嫁妆，将他带入婚姻的殿堂。

Susanna's death left the duke a widower; Anne of France inconsolable; and Louise of Savoy, Francis's mother, elated. Susanna had inherited her titles in the absence of a brother, through an unusual concession, but since she had died childless, the Duchy of Bourbon and its other honors now lay vacant, awaiting a distant relative to assume them. And Louise was the fortunate one. For each of her cousin Susanna's miscarriages, Francis's mother had offered a guilty smile. Their blood tie had long since been severed, and one of the reasons, now distant, was that Louise had loved the now-duke in her youth, and her feelings had been reciprocated; but that love lasted only until Susanna offered him that tempting dowry and led him to the altar.

路易莎神情沮丧地来到表兄的葬礼上。她发现这位鳏夫正在沙泰勒罗庄园的一个花园里喘息。

Luisa arrived at her cousin's funeral looking dejected. She found the widower taking a breath in a garden at Châtellerault.

—我很抱歉。替她，也替你。

—I'm so sorry. For her and for you.

——路易莎……殿下。

—Luisa… Your Highness.

女人紧紧地抓住公爵的手。

The woman clung tightly to the duke's hand.

“她一直比我更爱我。这件事一直让我耿耿于怀，而且永远都会如此。”他坦白道。

"She always loved me more than I loved her. That weighs on me and it always will," he confessed.

你是一位好丈夫。我们是否有选择爱人的自由？

—You were a good husband. Are we free to choose whom to love?

公爵摇了摇头，猜到了路易莎的意图，便允许她拥抱自己，但在此之前，他先确认周围无人。她喜欢他如此靠近自己。她几乎从孩提时代就成了寡妇，因此她不愿让自己怀念恋人的温暖，尤其是公爵的；所以她那颗向来冰冷的心，此刻也微微暖了起来。她自己也感到惊讶，竟然觉得等待着公爵的孤独，对她来说似乎也充满吸引力。

The duke shook his head, and, having guessed Luisa's intention, allowed her to embrace him, but not before checking that no one was watching. She liked having him so close. A widow since she was practically a child, she didn't allow herself to miss the warmth of lovers, least of all the duke's; so her heart, always cold, warmed a little. She surprised herself by thinking that the solitude that awaited the duke seemed promising to her.

“我很高兴你来了。我相信意志不会成为我们之间的障碍，”公爵真诚地说。

"I'm glad you've come. I trust the will won't come between us," the duke said sincerely.

路易莎拉开了与他们的距离。拥抱结束了。

Luisa put some distance between them. The hug was broken.

——什么会？

—What will?

公爵说：“苏珊娜非常慷慨，把她的全部遗产都遗赠给了我。”

—Susana was kind enough to bequeath her entire estate to me —said the duke.

弗朗西斯科母亲的脸先是变成了石头，然后变成了火焰。

The face of Francisco's mother turned to stone, and then to fire.

“你没有儿子！那份遗产是我的！”女人咆哮道。

"You haven't had any sons! That inheritance belongs to me!" roared the woman.

——你指望我违背妻子的意愿吗？不，夫人。我既不想，也不打算这样做。

—Do you expect me to deny my wife's wishes? No, my lady. I neither want to nor intend to do so.

 

 

 

 

尽管弗朗西斯一心只想羞辱波旁家族，但他母亲对他发起的继承权争夺战却令他心神不宁。法国的安妮在臣民和贵族中仍然拥有众多拥护者，在她心爱的女儿去世后违背她的意愿，显得粗暴无礼，有失国王的身份。此事如今已诉诸法庭，而国王又不愿屈从于母亲的意志，似乎永无止境地拖延下去。在等待判决的过程中，路易丝的健康状况每况愈下。她每晚祈祷，希望第二天早上一切都能对她有利。一年后，法国的安妮赶来与女儿团聚，她的离世给了路易丝一丝希望。然而，公爵在法官中似乎也拥有和她一样多的盟友，案件始终没有结果。一天晚上，躺在床上，弗朗西斯的母亲感到希望渺茫。她精疲力竭地躺在那里，脑海中浮现出一个画面：在弥留之际，她用尽最后一口气再次问道：“判决结果出来了吗？”痛苦如潮水般涌来，她不得不起身拉开窗帘，打开窗户，让冷风吹进来。一阵风吹得她皮肤发麻，一个主意立刻闪过她的脑海。

Although Francis desired nothing more than to humiliate the Bourbon, the inheritance battle his mother had waged against him was unsettling. Anne of France still had many devotees among the subjects and nobles, and going against her wishes after the death of her beloved daughter seemed crude, unworthy of a king. The matter, now a legal case, and with the king unwilling to bend his power to his mother's will, appeared to drag on endlessly. Awaiting the verdict, Louise's health deteriorated. She prayed every night that by morning everything would be resolved in her favor. The death of Anne of France, who had rushed to join her daughter a year after her death, gave her hope. But the duke seemed to have as many allies among the jurists as she did, and the resolution never came. And one night, in her bed, Francis's mother felt that it would never come. Lying there, exhausted, her imagination conjured up a scene where, on the verge of death, she used her last breath to ask again: "Is there a sentence?" The anguish overwhelmed her so much that she had to get up and draw back the curtains, open the windows, and let in the draft. The gust of wind made her skin tingle, and immediately an idea struck her.

 

 

 

 

“我们结婚吧，”第二天，路易莎对公爵说。

"Let's get married," Luisa told the duke the next day.

而他，因为审判而和路易莎一样筋疲力尽，突然放声大笑，并对弗朗西斯科的母亲破口大骂。

And he, who was as exhausted as Luisa because of the trial, burst into sincere laughter and poured a thousand insults on Francisco's mother.

你现在是在把贪婪伪装成爱吗？

—Are you now disguising greed as love?

她沉默不语。她感到脆弱，这对于她来说很不寻常，因为他的邀请无疑会解决遗产纠纷，届时他们便可共享；但最重要的是，在她内心深处，她渴望陪伴，渴望与这个男人重温早已逝去的时光。路易莎曾幻想与他相伴终老，拥有显赫的头衔和财富，在世人面前如同在卧室里般亲密无间。公爵的拒绝不容置疑，却将这些幻想化作滋生仇恨的沃土。当她回到如今平静的昂布瓦兹宫廷时，她散布了无数谎言，诋毁波旁家族的自负，并让她的儿子相信，只有当波旁家族彻底覆灭，他才能成为至高无上的国王。

She remained silent. She felt, and this was unusual for her, vulnerable, because his invitation would certainly provide a solution to the inheritance dispute, which they could then share; but above all, deep down, it was a certain longing for companionship and to relive with this man what had been lost long ago. Luisa had imagined growing old by his side, laden with titles and riches, as magnificent before the world as they were affectionate in the bedroom. The duke's rejection, which left no room for argument, turned these fantasies into fertile ground for a fierce hatred, and when she returned to the court of Amboise, now serene, she spread a thousand lies about the Bourbon's boasting and convinced her son that he would only be supreme king when nothing remained of the former.

弗朗西斯声称审判拖延已久，迟迟没有判决本身就是对诉讼双方的不公，于是以王室的名义决定剥夺波旁公爵的所有头衔和财产，这些财产在案件悬而未决期间全部归国王所有。这一决定令法国人困惑不已。他们认为这是滥用权力、自私自利、不公正的！但与西班牙的查理五世不同，弗朗西斯虽然也有缺点，却赢得了更多的敬佩而非愤怒。法国臣民深知自己处于臣服地位，他们享受国王展现权威的方式，国王越是专制，他们就越是乐于见到；因为他们越是觉得自己的统治者伟大，就越能为自己甘愿受其奴役的行为找到借口。

Claiming that the trial had dragged on long enough and that the lack of a verdict was itself an injustice to the litigants, Francis, in the name of the Crown, decided to strip the Duke of Bourbon of all his titles and possessions, which thus passed to the king while the case remained open. The decision bewildered the French. They considered it abusive, self-serving, unjust! But unlike Charles in Spain, Francis, with his own failings, provoked more admiration than anger. The French subjects knew they were subservient and enjoyed the king's displays of authority, the more despotic they were; for the greater they perceived their ruler to be, the more they excused themselves for allowing themselves to be subdued.

公爵竭尽全力阻止这场劫掠，但他预感到劫掠将永无止境，因为国王牵涉其中，审判必然以路易莎胜诉告终。他觉得自己已无计可施，但经过一番思索，他发现自己体内还残留着一丝力量，一丝微弱的希望。公爵知道这股力量会不断壮大，最终将他完全吞噬，赋予他复仇的全部力量。

The duke did everything he could to prevent the plunder, which he sensed would be endless, because with the king involved, the trial would inevitably end in Luisa's favor. He saw that he had nothing left, but after much thought, he discovered that something did remain within him, a small ray of strength. The duke knew that this ray would grow and that, when it completely engulfed him, it would grant him all the power for revenge.

 

 

 

 

希耶夫雷的侄子当选为托莱多大主教的消息首先激怒了阿德里安，他认为这位顾问承诺将此事留待以后处理的承诺已经违背；不久之后，更危险的是，西班牙人也对此感到愤怒，他们的这种大胆举动证实了他们对君主最糟糕的怀疑。

The news of the election of Chièvres' nephew as archbishop of Toledo first angered Adrian, who saw the advisor's promise to leave the matter for later as broken; and shortly afterwards, and with greater danger, the Spaniards, who with this audacity confirmed their worst suspicions about the monarch.

——简直不可容忍！竟然把托莱多大主教的职位交给一个年轻的外国人！

—It's intolerable! To give the archbishopric of Toledo to a young foreigner!

胡安·德·帕迪利亚怒不可遏。他从父亲那里继承的不仅是托莱多民兵队长的职位，还有王室独立于外来影响的观念。他的父亲曾公开表示效忠胡安娜女王，反对美男子菲利普架空妻子的统治手段。胡安从小就听着父亲的咒骂长大，认定所有外来者除了蔑视和掠夺西班牙之外，别无所图。当查理被拥立为王时，他预感到即将发生什么，但起初他还是抱有一丝希望。或许他父亲的偏见有些夸大其词；而他自己，却愚蠢地全盘接受。然而，随着新国王的一次次失误，他父亲的悲观情绪日益加深，而大主教的任命更是将这种不信任转化为愤怒。他父亲的预感是对的。

Juan de Padilla was beside himself. From his father, he had inherited not only the position of captain of the Toledo militia, but also a conception of the crown as independent of outsider influence. His father had declared his loyalty to Queen Joanna and his opposition to Philip the Handsome's maneuver of ruling by sidelining his wife. Juan grew up hearing his curses and assumed that anyone who came from outside had no other interest than to scorn and plunder Spain. When Charles was proclaimed king, he knew what was coming, but for a time he gave him the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps his father's prejudices were somewhat exaggerated; and he, foolish for accepting them without question. But with each misstep by the new king, his father's pessimism grew, and the appointment of the archbishop transformed that distrust into fury. His father had been right.

——这是最严重的问题，但并非唯一的问题：王国财政大臣谢夫尔，他们把多少个主教职位分给了自己人？

—That's the most serious thing, but not the only one: Chièvres, treasurer of the kingdom, and how many bishoprics have they distributed among their own?

真正激起胡安义愤的，是他的妻子玛丽亚·帕切科。她的姓氏彰显了她的身份：她出身于卡斯蒂利亚最显赫的家族之一，这个贵族世家权势滔天，以至于伊莎贝拉女王在世时都竭力想要削弱他们的地位。胡安出身卑微，仅仅是一个伊达尔戈（庄园主），但通过与玛丽亚的婚姻，他获得了贵族身份。正是这种缺乏特权的背景，使胡安对权贵的滥用职权有着格外敏感的感知。在玛丽亚身上，他总能找到支持他谴责权贵的动力；她是一位帕切科家族的成员：坚强、热情、不屈不挠。他是伊达尔戈，她是贵族；然而，一切又将他们紧紧联系在一起。他们的婚姻，如同许多其他婚姻一样，最初只是两个家族之间冷酷的契约，但爱情很快便在婚姻中萌芽。

The one who fueled Juan's indignation was his wife, María Pacheco. Her surname reflected her status: her family was one of the most illustrious in Castile, a line of nobles so powerful that, in her time, Queen Isabella struggled to diminish their rank. Through his marriage to her, Juan had been ennobled, for his origins were humble, that of a mere hidalgo. And this lack of a privileged background had given Juan a heightened sensitivity to the abuses of the powerful. In María, he always found support for his denunciations; she was a Pacheco: strong, fiery, and indomitable. He a hidalgo, she a noblewoman; yet everything united them. Their marriage, like so many others, was a cold agreement between two families, but love soon blossomed within it.

他提议：“让我们写封信向王室表达我们的不满吧！”

"Let's send a letter with our complaints to the Crown!" he proposed.

纸张易燃。我们要在议会中发出我们的声音。他们别无选择，只能为自己的暴行忏悔——玛丽亚插话道。

—Paper burns easily. We will make ourselves heard in the Cortes. They will have no other option but to repent of their excesses —María interjected.

对查理而言不幸的是，约翰和玛丽之间的对话只是众多类似对话中的一例。在集市、铁匠铺和客栈里，愤怒的情绪迅速蔓延，人们开始怀疑这位来自根特的君主并非为了西班牙的利益，而是为了西班牙的利益。有人指责他，也有人则将矛头指向他的顾问，认为他们利用了查理的幼稚、愚昧和不明智的弱点。

Unfortunately for Charles, the conversation between John and Mary was just one of many similar ones. In the markets, the blacksmiths' shops, and the inns, indignation spread uncontrollably, and suspicion began to grow that the man from Ghent was reigning against Spain, not for her. Some blamed him, while others preferred to demonize his advisors, who, in their view, were taking advantage of a naive, somewhat naive, and unwise Charles.

在宫廷里，希耶夫尔压制了这些抱怨，没有将它们转达给国王。谴责任命的信件被焚毁，请求觐见的信件也被置之不理。但真相总会找到缝隙渗入，这一次，它从费迪南德和杰尔马纳的口中溜了出来。他们只对费迪南德隐瞒了一个细节：愤怒重新激发了王子的忠实追随者，他们现在比以往任何时候都更加怂恿他背叛自己。但费迪南德对他们不屑一顾，镇定自若，认为没有必要告诉他的兄弟。他为自己的忠诚和将王国置于个人之上而感到自豪。为了不让背叛的痕迹在他心中留下丝毫印记，他将祖父曾拥有的皇家印章赠予了他的兄弟。费迪南德心中再无任何背叛的痕迹；无论是物品，还是思想。

At court, the echo of the complaints was silenced by Chièvres, who refrained from passing them on to the king. Letters denouncing the appointments were burned, and those requesting an audience were ignored. But the truth always finds cracks through which to seep, and in this case, it slipped through Ferdinand and Germana. They withheld only one detail from him: that anger had revived the prince's loyal followers, and that they were now urging him to betray him more than ever. But Ferdinand scorned them with such composure that he saw no reason to tell his brother. He was proud of his loyalty and of putting the kingdom before himself. And so that not even a symbolic trace of treachery could remain within him, he gifted his brother the royal seal that had once belonged to their grandfather. Nothing remained of a rival in Ferdinand; not an object, not a thought.

 

 

 

 

“为什么我没有被告知你的任命引起了如此大的不安？”卡洛斯打断了希耶夫雷斯的午餐，厉声质问道。

"Why haven't I been informed of the unease your appointments have caused?" Carlos snapped at Chièvres, interrupting his lunch.

“我不想因为自己造成的局面而打扰您，”顾问回答说。

"I didn't want to bother you with a situation that I alone created," the advisor replied.

“承担责任对我没什么好处。议会即将召开，我不认为你的决定会改善我的处境！”

"It does me little good to take the blame. The Cortes are imminent, and I don't see your decisions improving my position!"

——我会替你说话。错在我，担在我。

—I will speak for you in them. The fault was mine, the burden will be mine.

谈话虽短，却令两人心中都留下挥之不去的不安。查理不禁怀疑费迪南和杰尔玛娜所言是否属实；是否真如他们所言，希耶夫尔只顾自身利益，他多年来的效力不过是他如今地位的垫脚石：一个可以肆意掠夺王国而不计后果的人。这位君主并非对顾问的贪婪一无所知，但在此之前，他的忠诚从未动摇过。如果希耶夫尔聚敛财富后逃离王国，流亡他乡，留下他独自掌管西班牙，以及他一手造成的动乱呢？查理并不信任他，所以不敢断然排除这种可能性。事实上，他谁也不信任。查理始终感到不安，无法确定这个世界是否会善待他。他的母亲多年来对他漠不关心，而他的父亲也英年早逝。这种缺乏保护让他身心俱疲，变得内向多疑，稍有风吹草动便疑神疑鬼：为了避免受到伤害，他不惜一切代价。于是，他萌生了除掉希耶夫尔，让费尔南多成为自己顾问的想法。或许这是他在王国中保全自身的唯一途径：放弃那个如今人人憎恨的弗莱明，提拔他那位比自己更受爱戴的兄弟。

The conversation was brief, but it left both of them with a lingering unease. Charles wondered if Ferdinand and Germana were right; if, as they had assured him, Chièvres looked only after himself and the service he had rendered all those years had been merely a stepping stone to where he now stood: capable of plundering a kingdom without regard for the consequences. The monarch had never been unaware of his advisor's greed, but until then, it had not superseded his loyalty. What if Chièvres, having amassed wealth, fled the kingdom into an unknown exile, leaving him in charge of Spain and the unrest he had sown in those lands? He didn't trust him enough to dismiss the possibility. In truth, he trusted no one. Charles had always felt insecure in the world, with no certainty that it would be kind to him. His mother had ignored his existence for years, and his father had died young. This lack of protection had taken its toll, making him introverted and suspicious at the slightest suspicion: no effort was too great to prevent harm. The idea of ​​removing Chièvres from his side and making Fernando one of his advisors then took shape in his mind. Perhaps it was the only way to save himself in the eyes of the kingdom: to renounce that Fleming, now hated by all, and elevate his brother, whom everyone loved more than him.

 

 

 

 

查理得知任命丑闻后，希耶夫尔十分担忧。正如人们所担心的那样，国王现在愿意听取一些新意见，这威胁到他的影响力，并使其迅速衰落。这位顾问察觉到，查理与杰曼共度的夜晚不仅包含浪漫情调，还包含床笫之欢。尽管政治与爱情水火不容，但对于一位国王和一位另一位国王的遗孀来说，这似乎难以避免。希耶夫尔想象着查理在那些时刻的模样：性爱后的欢愉让他的灵魂变得脆弱，他将情人说的每一句话都奉为真理。他意识到，查理必须驱除心中的恶魔。

The fact that the scandal surrounding the appointments had reached Charles's ears was a source of great concern for Chièvres. The new voices the king was now willing to listen to, as had been feared, threatened his influence and caused it to dwindle rapidly. The advisor sensed that the nights Charles spent with Germaine involved not only romance but also conversations beneath the sheets, and although politics and romance were incompatible, between a king and the widow of another, it seemed inevitable. Chièvres imagined Charles in those moments, his soul vulnerable after the delights of sex, taking every word of his lover as truth, and he identified the demon he had to exorcise.

议员在午后抵达杰尔马纳的住所，浑身湿透，显然是刚下过一场暴雨。她正透过窗户看着雨，这时听到他进来了。

The councilor arrived at Germana's residence in the mid-afternoon, soaked from a storm. She was watching the rain through a window when she heard him enter.

——很抱歉让你失望了。我知道你以前遇到过更有希望的情况。

—I'm sorry to disappoint you. I know you're used to more promising encounters.

杰尔马纳给他安排了一个座位，但他拒绝了。

Germana offered him a seat, but he refused it.

“从来没有哪次不期而至的来访比你的来访更令人翘首以盼，”杰尔马纳说道，“我甚至可以说，你早就该来了。”

—There has never been an unannounced visit more eagerly awaited than yours—Germana remarked. —I would even say you were long overdue in coming.

——到那时你就会明白我要告诉你什么了。

—Then you will know what I am going to tell you.

—你想让囚禁国王的金笼保持关闭状态，让我无法进入。

—You want the golden cage in which you have kept the king to remain closed, and off-limits to me.

“如果你认为他被我欺骗了，那说明你对他评价不高，”希耶夫尔回答说，“我没有你那样的魅力。我不是在引诱他，而是在说服他。”

—You don't think much of him if you believe he's being deceived by me—replied Chièvres. —I don't have your charms. I don't seduce him: I convince him.

——即便现在，你们已经将王国赐予他了？

—Even now, when you have brought the kingdom upon him?

希耶夫尔没有回答，只是径直坐了下来，没有等杰尔马纳再次示意他坐下。

Chièvres did not reply. He simply took a seat without waiting for Germana to offer it to him again.

“你对他的影响源于激情。而我对他的影响力则源于他的生命本身。我了解他的每一个想法，预判他的意图，并引导他。查尔斯是由血肉、骨骼和希耶夫尔奶酪构成的。当你的魅力让他感到厌倦时——就像每个男人在不再恋爱时都会经历的那样——你认为他还会听谁的？”

"Your influence over him is born of passion. Mine is part of his very being. I know his every thought, anticipate them, and guide him. Charles is made of blood, flesh, bone, and Chièvres. When your arts bore him, as happens to every man when he no longer loves, whom do you think he will listen to?"

杰尔玛娜发现自己无言以对。顾问的话无疑有道理，但她宁愿沉默也不愿空洞地回应。她的目光落在地上，那是对方湿透的衣服在地上汇聚成的一滩水，而且这滩水势必会不断扩大。

Germana found herself without an answer. There was undoubtedly truth in what the advisor said, and she preferred silence to an empty reply. She fixed her gaze on the puddle of water that her interlocutor's wet clothes were forming on the ground, a puddle that was inevitably spreading.

“我不会因为你关注自己的未来而谴责你；那才是我最大的罪过，”希耶夫尔说。“但我才是你的救赎，不是他。远离他，你将一无所缺。”

“I will not be the one to condemn you for watching over your future; that crime is the greatest of mine,” said Chièvres. “But I am your salvation, not him. Turn away from him, and you will lack nothing.”

“如果我拒绝呢？”她大胆地问道。

"And what if I refuse?" she dared to say.

你会后悔的。

—You'll regret it.

议员离开后，杰尔玛娜披上斗篷，出门散步。雨还在下个不停，但她几乎没注意到。她往田野深处走去，想找点空气。雨水浸透了泥土，她的脚陷了进去。行走越来越困难。她只想呼吸，查尔斯就是她的空气；但现实是，希耶夫尔，就像这泥泞一样，不让她再往前走一步。

Once the councilor had left, Germana wrapped herself in a cloak and went for a walk. The rain was still falling heavily, but she barely noticed it. She ventured deeper into the fields, searching for air. The water had softened the ground, and her feet sank into the mud. It became increasingly difficult to walk. All she wanted was to breathe, and Charles was her air; but the truth was Chièvres, and he, like the mud, wasn't going to let her take another step.

 

 

 

 

几天后，查理拜访了杰尔玛娜，发现她的住所空无一人，家具上盖着破布，他曾经安享的床铺如今只铺着毯子，死气沉沉，布满灰尘。国王脸上浮现出一丝苦涩的微笑，这是他强忍着内心痛苦的姿态。仆人告诉他，他的爱人已经离开，永不归来，既没有留下字条，也没有透露去向。但查理不需要这些解释。杰尔玛娜在他心中激起的那种感觉已经足够了。离开住所时，他感到一片寂静和阴郁，一个疑虑在他年轻的君主心中生根发芽：多年以后，经历了这么多失望，她的不信任与日俱增，对别人的信任也彻底丧失，她的性格会变成什么样呢？他的想象让他感到无比悲伤。

When Charles visited Germana a few days later and found the residence empty, the furniture covered with rags, and the bed where he had been happy draped with blankets, lifeless and covered in dust, a bitter smile escaped the king, a restrained gesture for the pain he felt inside. The servants informed him that his lady had left the place never to return, without leaving a note or revealing her destination, but Charles didn't need so many explanations. The feeling Germana had evoked in him was enough. As he left the residence, enveloped in silence and gloom, a doubt took root in the young monarch: what would her character be like years later, after so many disappointments, with her distrust growing ever stronger and her faith in others lost forever? And what he imagined filled him with sadness.

 

 

 

 

除掉杰尔马纳后，希耶夫尔将注意力转向了费迪南，但要说服费迪南与国王保持距离并非易事。他意识到，围绕这些任命的丑闻可能唤醒了旧日的阴谋，尽管他并不知道任何试图用叛国罪诱惑费迪南的人最终都会一无所获，但仅仅是得知这些会面就足以让他向查理告发这位王子。

With Germana removed, Chièvres turned his attention to Ferdinand, whom it was not so easy to convince to distance himself from the king. It occurred to him that the scandal surrounding the appointments might have stirred up old conspiracies, and although he was unaware that anyone who tempted Ferdinand with treason always came away empty-handed, the mere knowledge of these visits was enough for him to denounce the prince to Charles.

“他或许跪下了，但似乎并非出于真心，”顾问警告国王。

"He may well have knelt down, but it seems not in spirit," the advisor warned the king.

换作以往，查理或许会相信希耶夫的指控，并对他的弟弟保持警惕。但近几周，两件事改变了这位君主的看法。围绕职位的丑闻动摇了他对这位顾问的信任，查理仍然认为他野心勃勃，但如今却被自私自利的念头所驱使。第二件事源于他与弟弟的关系，他们之间尚在萌芽的纽带，预示着一段美好的兄弟情谊和一段查理从未体验过的友谊。尽管他们身份迥异——国王与王子，一位是统治者，另一位是曾经的阴谋家棋子——费迪南和查理却能坦诚相待，如同年轻人之间一般。他们的关系平静祥和，因为他们都清楚自己的价值，也欣赏对方的善良。国王感到自己的灵魂正在慢慢敞开，以前所未有的方式向另一个人敞开心扉。他喜欢与他在一起：真诚、深情，如同家人一般。他让他觉得自己是一个真正的人，而不仅仅是一个头衔。

At another time, Charles would have believed Chièvres's accusation and would have been wary of his brother. But in recent weeks, two events had altered the monarch's perspective. The scandal surrounding the positions had shaken his faith in the advisor, whom Charles still considered just as ambitious but now driven excessively by self-serving whims. The second event stemmed from his relationship with his brother, that still-nascent bond they shared, which foreshadowed a beautiful brotherhood and a friendship unlike any Charles had ever known. Despite their differences—king and prince, one a ruler and the other a former conspirator's pawn—Ferdinand and Charles spoke to each other openly, young man to young man, and their relationship was characterized by tranquility, because both knew themselves to be good and liked that the other was. The king saw his soul slowly opening up, offering himself to another human being as he had never allowed himself to do before. He enjoyed being with him: honest, affectionate, and like family. He made him feel like a person, not just a title.

君主不愿仅仅因为一个恶意的谣言就断送这段新近缔结的珍贵情谊，但人的灵魂不可能在短时间内改变，查理生性多疑，即便那只是出于善意的微弱顾虑，也无法阻止他对费迪南的怀疑在他心中生根发芽。国王或许正在学习如何全心全意地付出，但永远无法做到完全的奉献。

The monarch refused to destroy this newly forged and precious bond simply because of a malicious rumor, but it is impossible for a soul to change in a short time, and Charles's ever-distrustful soul could not prevent suspicion of Ferdinand from taking root within him, even if it was a weak scruple masked by good feelings. The king might be learning to give himself fully, but never completely.

 

 

 

 

在巴利亚多利德议会第一次会议召开前夕，查理下定决心要由他本人，而不是希耶夫尔或其他任何人，来发表讲话。这将是他经受考验的试金石，他要确保任何未经他事先考虑的言论都被排除在外。他尚未下令让这位顾问离开宫廷，但他打算这样做，在西班牙面前让他噤声，会让他更有底气在日后与希耶夫尔决裂。

On the eve of the first session of the Cortes of Valladolid, Charles was determined that he, and not Chièvres or anyone else, would address them. This would be his baptism of fire, and he would prevent any word from being spoken that he had not first considered. He had not yet ordered the advisor to leave the court, but he intended to do so, and silencing him before Spain would embolden him to later break with him.

然而，第二天早上，当查理看到熙熙攘攘的官员和贵族，感受到他们之间弥漫的紧张和期待的气氛时，他瞥了一眼自己的双手，发现它们在颤抖。他感到羞愧。他试图让自己平静下来，感受头戴王冠的重量以求镇定。但这只会让他更加痛苦，因为他想象着自己坐在王位上，威风凛凛，却在那些面容坚毅的男人面前结结巴巴，他几乎能听到他们对一个傀儡国王的窃窃私语和嘲讽。权力越大，如果不能展现出来，受到的蔑视就越残酷。或许，他试图获得权力的努力，最终会让他失去一切。他以为自己能欺骗谁？他不知道该如何回应他们的要求，也不知道该如何充满信心地与他们交谈。

However, the next morning, when Charles saw the throng of procurators and nobles and sensed the atmosphere of tension and anticipation in which they were simmering, he glanced at his hands and saw them trembling. He was ashamed of himself. He tried to calm himself, to feel the weight of the crown he wore to gain composure. But this only distressed him more, for he imagined himself on the throne, magnificent, yet stammering before all those men with strong features, and he could almost hear their murmurs and mocking laughter at a puppet king. The greater the grandeur, the crueler the scorn if it is not seen to shine. Perhaps in his attempt to gain authority, he was going to lose it all. Whom did he think he was deceiving? He would not know how to respond to their demands, nor how to address them with conviction.

卡洛斯和希耶夫斯交换了一个眼神。这么多年相处下来，有时候一个眼神就足以让他们彼此了解。议员没有责备地点了点头，他要开口了。

Carlos exchanged a glance with Chièvres. After so many years together, sometimes that was enough for them to understand each other. The councilor nodded, without reproach; he would speak.

 

 

 

 

国王说，他深感荣幸能成为这个王国的新统治者。尽管他的领土众多，但这片土地却是他最珍视和最重视的。这里曾是一个辉煌的王国，拥有辉煌的功绩和令人敬畏的威望……

—The king says he feels deeply honored to be the new ruler of this kingdom. Even though his domains are numerous, this one is the center of his pride and his care. A magnificent kingdom in the past, of glorious deeds, of formidable prestige…

希耶夫尔讲话时，查理不时侧目扫视在场众人。检察官和贵族们沉默不语，在怀疑的氛围中默默聆听。

While Chièvres spoke, Charles glanced sideways at those present. Procurators and nobles listened in silence, behind a wall of skepticism.

——但骄傲必须得到回报，因为这片土地必须引以为傲，因为它的君主是国王之子，皇帝和君主之孙。决定他命运的并非偶然，而是上帝的旨意。服从君主，就是顺从神的旨意……

—But pride must be reciprocated, for this land must boast of having as its head a son of kings, grandson of emperors and monarchs. It was not chance that decided his destiny, but God himself. By obeying your sovereign, you submit to the divine will…

卡洛斯注意到这些话引起了不安。看来，西班牙人想要的是世俗的君主。

Carlos noticed that those words had caused unease. The Spaniards, it seemed, wanted earthly kings.

——鉴于您的主人想要保护您免受威胁我们边境的土耳其人的侵害，他请求您允许他支付两亿马拉维迪，三年内付清……

—And since your lord desires to protect you from the Turk who threatens our borders, he requests that you be pleased to grant him, to be paid in three years, two hundred million maravedis…

这请求如同狂风骤起，惊动了在场众人。寂静被呐喊声打破，严肃的脸庞瞬间涨得通红。几乎就在一瞬间，查尔斯将萦绕在他心头许久的恐惧化作现实：西班牙人不会支持他。他从未见过如此赤裸裸的怨恨，此刻他感到这怨恨即将爆发，如同被锁链束缚的野兽撕咬着空气。他从未如此渴望回到弗兰德斯。

The request, like a gust of wind, roused those present. Silence gave way to shouts, and serious faces to flushed red. In barely an instant, Charles gave a face and voice to that threatening thought that had haunted him for some time: that the Spaniards would not support him. He had never before witnessed such resentment in its rawest form, and now he felt it about to strike, like a chained beast snapping at the air. Never before had he longed more to be in Flanders.

其中一个声音格外突出。

One voice rose above the rest.

“你们打算在听我们说话之前就把我们的钱掏空吗？”胡安·德·帕迪利亚愤怒地站起身来，像许多其他人一样说道。

"Do you intend to empty our pockets before listening to us?" said Juan de Padilla furiously, standing, like many others.

希耶夫尔用一种平静而轻蔑的眼神看着他。帕迪利亚并未被吓倒。

Chièvres gave him a look of serene contempt. Padilla was not intimidated.

我们要求任何金银都不得离开卡斯蒂利亚！我们要求费尔南多王子留在王国，直到国王选出继承人！我们要求，我们坚持！所有授予外国人的任命都应被废除。

—We demand that no gold and silver leave Castile! We demand that Prince Ferdinand live in the kingdom until the king has a successor! And we demand, we insist!, that all appointments granted to foreigners be annulled.

帕迪利亚的发言正要得到议员的回应，议会听众却突然打断了他，他们点头、欢呼，并爆发出热烈的掌声。玛丽亚·帕切科挽着丈夫的胳膊，深情地凝视着他。他的话语似乎释放了几个月来积压的紧张情绪。现在，双方面对面站着：一方是王室，另一方是其他所有人。

Padilla's speech was about to be answered by the councilor when the Cortes audience interrupted, nodding, cheering, and erupting into applause. María Pacheco took her husband's arm and gazed at him, her expression adoring. His words seemed to have released a tension that had been building for months. Now there were two sides, and they stood face to face: the Crown and everyone else.

卡洛斯这才想起他的狩猎之旅，想起和杰尔玛娜共度的夜晚。他一直生活在自己的世界里，仿佛眼前这些对他大喊大叫的人从未存在过。他谈起他们，想起他们，但就像谈论一个与自己生活毫无交集的远房亲戚。面对他们的愤怒，他感到恐惧。一种理智的恐惧，一种突然意识到自己面临所有逆境，然后僵住不动的恐惧。

Carlos then remembered his hunting trips and his nights with Germana. He had lived in his own world, as if all those who now stood before him, shouting at him, had never existed. He spoke of them, thought of them, but as one speaks of a distant relative whose existence will never intersect with his own. And faced with their anger, he felt fear. A sane fear, the fear of someone who suddenly senses all the adversities he faces, and freezes.

 

 

 

 

会议拖延了很久。提出的要求近百条。希耶夫承诺会满足其中大部分，查尔斯点头表示同意，并表示支持，尽管他心里很清楚，这些人并非总是真心实意。他们会像一些人要求的那样，给乔安娜王后提供另一处住所吗？查尔斯会在一年内结婚吗？正如另一位顾问所要求的？他的顾问们会辞去所有职务吗？希耶夫的侄子威廉会搬到托莱多居住，管理大主教区吗？但这一次，顾问和查尔斯甚至无需对视，便心照不宣地达成共识：只有慷慨大方，才能成功摆脱困境，即便这意味着做出不可能的承诺，并给自己制造兑现承诺的难题。希耶夫一改最初的傲慢，语气变得温和谦逊，这是查尔斯从未听过的。这位君主欣赏他这种戏剧化的表演，而他自己却自认不具备这种能力。他知道何时该保持沉默，却不知道何时该撒谎。他不禁思忖，一位正直的国王将会面临怎样的未来。或许，他永远都需要一个愤世嫉俗的人在他身边，在他难以启齿真相的时候为他撑腰。

The session dragged on. The requests, nearly a hundred. Chièvres promised to fulfill most of them, and Charles nodded in agreement, offering his support, though he knew perfectly well they weren't always being sincere. Would they give Queen Joanna another accommodation, as some had requested? Would Charles marry within a year, as another had asked? Would his advisors resign all their posts? Would William, Chièvres' nephew, come to live in Toledo to govern the archbishopric? But this time, the advisor and Charles didn't even need to look at each other to agree that they would only emerge successfully from this predicament if they were generous, even if it meant promising the impossible and creating for themselves the problem of having to deliver. From his initial haughtiness, Chièvres had shifted to a conciliatory, almost humble tone, the likes of which Charles had never heard. The sovereign admired his theatricality, of which he felt incapable. He knew when to be silent, but not when to lie. He wondered what future awaited an honest king. Perhaps he would always need a cynic by his side to save him when the truth was not convenient to speak.
