议会批准了国王提出的贷款请求，这使他得以维持王位，并随时返回弗兰德斯。然而，国王及其盟友离开议会时，并未感到胜利的喜悦，因为他们看到了自己必须驯服的这头猛兽，却不知该如何驾驭。更糟糕的是，他们现在意识到自己终将背叛它，因为他们的许多承诺都将无法兑现，西班牙人民将会感到更加被背叛——如果这可能的话——然后他们会寻求推翻他们的统治。

The Cortes granted the king the requested loan, which would allow him to maintain the Crown and return to Flanders whenever he wished, but neither he nor his allies left those sessions feeling victorious, for they had seen the beast they had to tame, and they didn't know how. Moreover, they now knew they were going to betray it, because many of their promises would not be kept, so the Spanish people would feel even more betrayed, if that were possible, and then they would seek their downfall.

大约在那时，他们收到了一封来自德国的信，是查理的祖父，马克西米利安皇帝寄来的。信中，皇帝询问了西班牙政府的状况，并讲述了他自己的困境。他详细地谈到了一位宣扬异端教义的修士，这位修士吸引了民众的目光，并得到了一些贵族的支持。查理不理解祖父的担忧。异端分子一直存在，他所说的这位马丁·路德最终也会像其他异端一样，被世人遗忘，为了保命而放弃自己的思想，或者被送上火刑柱，他的异端邪说根本无法产生任何实际影响。但是，当他与阿德里安讨论此事时，后者却心存疑虑。

Around that time, they received a letter from Germany from Charles's grandfather, Emperor Maximilian, in which he inquired about the state of the Spanish government and recounted his own troubles. He spoke at length about a friar with heretical teachings who was captivating the people and enjoying the support of some noblemen. Charles didn't understand his grandfather's alarm. There had always been heretics, and this Martin Luther he spoke of would end up like all the others, forgotten, renouncing his ideas to save his life or losing it at the stake, without his heresies having made any real impact. But when he discussed the matter with Adrian, the latter had his doubts.

“你祖父的担忧和你的乐观一样有道理，”他说，“但谁又能预料未来呢？历史的进程总是出人意料。那个异端分子可能和其他异端分子没什么两样。一切都取决于有多少人听他的，以及他们有多渴望改变现状。一个人，无论地位如何，只要身边有追随者，他的地位就会提升。不管他愿不愿意。”

“It’s true that your grandfather’s fear is as valid as your optimism,” he said, “but who knows? History turns without warning. That heretic could be just like any other. It all depends on how many listen to him, and how much they want things to change. A man, no matter his stature, grows in stature when surrounded by followers. Whether he wants to or not.”

在查理看来，阿德里亚诺的警告以他哥哥的形象出现。他犹豫着是否应该与他交谈，尽管他知道这样做不会有什么收获，因为如果他是叛徒，他不会坦白，事实上，他会竭力表现得忠诚。难道这不正是他哥哥接近国王的原因吗？用温情打消国王的疑虑，让他忘记自己不久前还觊觎王位。费迪南德接受他的臣服真的如此轻易吗？费迪南德从小就被阿拉贡国王培养成掌权者，很难相信他的野心竟能如此轻易地隐藏。而且，杰尔马纳已经告诉过他：他的哥哥渴望成为某个重要人物。

Adriano's warning, in Charles's mind, took the form of his brother. He wondered if he should speak with him, though he knew he would gain little from it, because if he were a traitor, he wouldn't confess, and in fact, he would strive to appear loyal. Hadn't that been the reason for his brother's approach? To dispel the king's doubts with affection, to make him forget that until very recently he had coveted the throne. Had it been so easy for Ferdinand to accept his submission? Raised by the King of Aragon to wield power, it seemed difficult to believe that his ambition could be so easily concealed. And besides, Germana had already told him: his brother wanted to be someone.

 

 

 

 

卡洛斯连续几天心事重重，精疲力竭。不确定感让他心力交瘁。他疲惫不堪，卧床不起，无法解决关于费尔南多的难题，只能想起杰尔玛娜，思念之情如同瘾君子般挥之不去。一想到她，他就汗流浃背，有时甚至浑身颤抖，脑海中不断回放着她那些清晰而又无所畏惧的话语。他想知道是什么让她离他而去。还没等他想明白，答案就突然涌上心头。他责怪自己：失望蒙蔽了他的双眼，让他看不到希耶夫尔的援手，他那永恒的救星。明白这一点后，他笑了，擦了擦额头的汗，猛地从床上跳了起来。

Carlos spent several days lost in thought and drained of energy. Uncertainty was exhausting him. Lost in weariness, confined to his bed, and unable to resolve the dilemma concerning Fernando, he thought of Germana and missed her like an addict. He sweated at the thought of her, sometimes even trembled, and his mind replayed her words, always so lucid and shameless. He wondered what had made her flee from him. And before the question had even finished forming, the answer came to him suddenly. He blamed himself: his disappointment had blinded him to Chièvres's hand, his eternal deus ex machina . Understanding this, he laughed, wiped the sweat from his brow, and leaped out of bed.

她的使者在不远处的一座别墅里找到了日耳曼娜；她住在一座小宫殿里，这座宫殿隐藏在茂密的树林后面，与世隔绝。

Her messengers found Germana in a villa not far away; she occupied a small palace that was hidden from the world behind a vigorous grove of trees.

“拒绝服从希耶夫尔的命令很难，我们俩都知道这一点。”卡洛斯在他们的重聚中说道。

—It's difficult to refuse to follow Chièvres's dictates. We both know that —Carlos said at their reunion.

第一次约会重演：卡洛斯出乎意料地来了，杰尔马娜震惊不已，全世界都与她为敌。

The first date was repeated: Carlos unexpectedly, Germana stunned, and the world against her.

你的顾问是个很糟糕的人。

—Your advisor is a terrible man.

我知道。但他也是最能为我效力的人。他帮我赢得了议会选举。等到他不再对我有益的时候，我就会让他走。这就是我在这里的原因。因为没有人能替我做决定。

—I know. But he's also the one who serves me best. He won the Cortes for me. The day his service no longer benefits me, I'll let him go. That's why I'm here. Because nobody decides for me.

杰尔玛娜沉默不语。卡洛斯拉近了两人之间的距离。他们站得如此之近，甚至能感受到彼此的呼吸。

Germana remained silent. Carlos closed the distance between them. They stood so close they could feel each other's breath.

我知道他威胁过你。别理他。

—I understand he threatened you. Ignore him.

“我该相信她们俩中的哪一个呢？”杰尔马纳犹豫了一下。

"Which of the two should I believe?" Germana hesitated.

“如果你想让我指挥，就不要拒绝我。只要你待在我身边，就不会有事。我保证。”

"If you want me to take command, don't deny me. Nothing will happen to you if you stay by my side. I guarantee it."

杰尔玛娜凝视着卡洛斯，在年轻人的眼中发现了一种新的光芒——坚定。于是，她决定相信他。第二天清晨的第一缕阳光唤醒了彼此，他们紧紧相拥。

Germana looked at Carlos intently and found a new reflection in the young man's eyes, one of certainty. Then she decided to believe him. The first light of the next day woke them in each other's arms.

 

 

 

 

查理拒绝接受希耶夫尔关于他与日耳曼娜关系的命令，这让他既感到如释重负，又倍感压力。如今，他觉得自己有能力也有义务按照自己的判断做出决定，这促使他找到了解决费迪南难题的答案。他并不着急，而是连续数日深思熟虑。尽管他出席了各种会议，也接见了许多臣民，但这个问题始终萦绕在他的心头。即使他与他人交谈，他的思绪也始终在权衡，直到天平向一边倾斜，查理再也找不到任何办法来重新平衡。

The courage Charles discovered in himself, refusing to accept Chièvres's commands regarding his relationship with Germana, was both a relief and a burden. Now he felt capable and compelled to decide according to his own judgment, and this led him to find an answer to the dilemma concerning Ferdinand. He was in no hurry. He meditated for days on end. Although he attended councils and received many in audience, the question constantly hovered over him, and while he spoke with others, his mind continued to weigh it, until the scales tipped to one side and Charles found no way to rebalance them.

 

 

 

 

“哥哥，我能帮您什么忙吗？”费尔南多问道。

—Brother, how can I help you? —Fernando asked.

“我有个任务要交给你。”卡洛斯回答道。

—I have a mission for you —Carlos replied.

费尔南多笑了。终于，终于！他无比厌恶的那种被逼到墙角的孩子的命运，瞬间消失了。

Fernando smiled. At last, at last! His future as a cornered child, which he disliked so much, vanished in an instant.

——在佛兰德斯——国王补充道。

—In Flanders —added the king.

清晨鸟儿的鸣叫，以及其他房间里宫廷喧闹的低语，都无法阻止他们之间绝对的寂静。

Neither the songs of the early morning birds, nor the murmur of the court's bustle in the other rooms, prevented the silence that fell between them from being absolute.

——我需要你去那些地方。当然，你不会缺少任何东西，抵达后你将享有特权……

—I need you in those lands. Of course, you will lack nothing, and upon arrival you will be granted privileges…

“你要把我流放，”费尔南多打断道，仍然难以置信。“我到底哪里辜负了你？我所做的一切都是为了你好。你就是这样回报我的吗？”

"You're sending me into exile," Fernando interrupted, still in disbelief. "How have I failed you? Every step I've taken has been for your benefit. And this is how you repay me?"

查尔斯并非在做梦，但凯瑟琳的呻吟声在他耳边回荡，变得难以忍受。他多么希望自己能低头看向地板，不去看到哥哥眼中失望的神色，但他既然有胆量做出这样的决定，就必须承担相应的后果。

Charles wasn't dreaming, but Catherine's moans echoed back to him, becoming unbearable. He wished he could look down at the floor to avoid witnessing the disappointment in his brother's eyes, but if he was king enough to make such a decision, he would also have to bear the consequences.

“费尔南多，你无可指摘。正因如此，你才对我构成威胁。我没搞错，我的统治违背了许多人的意愿。他们会想方设法动摇你的忠诚，迫使你推翻我。我不能冒这个险。”

"You are beyond reproach, Fernando. And that is what makes you a threat to me. I am not mistaken; I reign against the will of many. They will do everything possible to break your loyalty and force you to overthrow me. I cannot take that risk."

—你躲在从未发生过的罪行背后背叛我！

—You are hiding behind a crime that never happened to betray me!

卡洛斯几乎崩溃了。他感到体内传来千百种剧烈的疼痛。

Carlos was about to break down. He felt a thousand sharp pains inside him.

—你说得对：如果符合他的利益，国王就没有怜悯的余地。

—You were right: if it suits his enterprise, a king has no place in pity.

 

 

 

 

那天下午，卡洛斯独自一人去打猎。他收获颇丰：猎物几乎是主动献身。但他猎获的猎物越多，胸口就越发紧绷。因为他知道，接下来的每一次狩猎，他都会做同样的事情：四处寻找费尔南多，要么是为了炫耀自己的枪法，要么是为了嘲笑自己糟糕的枪法。每一次狩猎，猎物本身都将是他最不关心的事情，因为他会错过最重要的那个人。

That afternoon Carlos went hunting, this time alone. He did well: the animals practically offered themselves up for the kill. But the more he bagged, the tighter his chest felt. Because he knew that in every hunt that followed, he would do the same thing: look around for Fernando, either to boast about his aim or to laugh at his own lack of it. In every hunt, the game would be the least of his concerns, because he would be missing the most important one.

3

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

杰尔玛娜的女仆将一壶滚烫的热水浇在女主人雪白的身体上。清晨寒气逼人，温暖的沐浴令人倍感舒适。杰尔玛娜赤身裸体，肌肤毫无遮掩，感到腹部一阵弥漫的压力。那不是疼痛，也不是愉悦，任何一种感觉都难以言喻。仿佛身体的某个部位在发出某种信号，提醒她注意，以免日后被人指责没有提前发出警告。那股压力悄然消失，却在当晚再次出现。那种难以名状的感觉又回来了。杰尔玛娜试图忽略它，因为一旦她不去理会，她那唯一的直觉就会让她感到不安。然而，随着时间的流逝，不仅是腹部，她的整个身体都开始感到异样。她的头部隐隐作痛；胸口一碰就疼；她的手脚仿佛不属于自己。当医生证实了她的怀疑后，杰尔玛娜请求独自一人待着。她不知该作何感想。这究竟是悲剧还是福气？她不知道卡洛斯知道后会作何感想。或许他什么反应都没有。也许他们会像往常一样，在疲惫时默默地对视，完全不会想到该如何谈论他们即将出生的孩子。

Germana's maid poured a steaming pitcher of water over her mistress's snow-white body. The morning was frigid, and the warmth of the bath a welcoming refuge. Naked, her skin unprotected, Germana felt a diffuse pressure in her abdomen. It wasn't pain, nor pleasure, nor anything for which there was a word. It was more as if that part of her body were demanding attention so as not to be accused in the future of not having warned her. The pressure disappeared unnoticed, but returned that night. Again, that nameless sensation. Germana tried to ignore it because, when she didn't, her intuition—of which there was only one—unsettled her. However, as the days passed, not only her abdomen but her entire body felt strange. Her head felt thumps; her chest ached at the slightest touch, and her hands and legs seemed to belong to someone else. When the doctor confirmed what she suspected, Germana asked to be left alone. She didn't know what to feel. Was it a tragedy or a blessing? She didn't know how Carlos would feel when he found out. Perhaps nothing. Maybe they would both just stare at each other in silence, as they liked to do when their bodies grew tired, and it wouldn't occur to them what to say about the child they were expecting.

 

 

 

 

“别担心。我什么都不想从你这里得到。我只想要我体内的东西。”杰尔马娜在告诉卡洛斯自己的情况后说道。

—Don't worry. I don't want anything from you. Only what I carry inside me—Germana told Carlos after informing him of her condition.

他凝视着她。那天早晨的她美极了，睡眼惺忪，肌肤泛着淡淡的金光。她身上散发着甜美的气息，几乎让他垂涎欲滴。前一天简直难以忍受，治理国家如同受刑一般：会议结束得比开始时更糟，贵族们怨声载道，令人沮丧的账目不断，而即将到来的阿拉贡之行更是雪上加霜，科尔特斯在那里等着他，据说比在卡斯蒂利亚还要严酷。黄昏时分，他与杰尔玛娜相会，她察觉到他的疲惫，以及卡洛斯身上那种偶尔流露出的气息，那种寻求庇护的感觉。他一言不发，她便读懂了他的心思。他们默默地待在一起，彼此凝视，亲吻，缠绵。对于这位视言语如禁忌的国王来说，此刻能找到一个可以做回自己的地方，他感到无比幸福。那种状态，那种坠入爱河前对好运的喜悦，就像一块柔软的垫子，让怀孕的消息得以安抚，不至于让他感到痛苦。卡洛斯向她保证他们之间不会有任何改变，她感激地吻了他，因为她知道那不是真的。

He gazed at her. She was beautiful that morning, her eyes still slanted with sleep and her skin a pale gold. Her sweet scent reached him, almost to his taste. The previous day had been unbearable, one of those days when governing is nothing but punishment: meetings that end worse than they begin, complaints from nobles and depressing accounts, all exacerbated by the imminent journey to Aragon, where Cortes awaited that promised to be even harsher than those in Castile. When he met with Germana at dusk, she noticed his weariness and that air Carlos sometimes carried, that sense of seeking refuge, and without him saying a word, she read his mind. They spent their time together in silence, gazing at each other, kissing, and making love. And the king, for whom words were like an evil to be avoided, felt blessed that there was a place in the world where he could be himself. That state, that celebration of good fortune that precedes falling in love, was like a cushion upon which the news of the pregnancy fell without causing harm. Carlos promised her that nothing would change between them, and she kissed him gratefully because she knew it wasn't true.

 

 

 

 

当这个秘密在卡斯蒂利亚的杰尔玛娜腹中悄然孕育时，在葡萄牙，曼努埃尔国王的女儿伊莎贝拉，如同往常一样，每天清晨的第一缕阳光照进她的房间，她便想起了查理。伊莎贝拉十五岁，拥有令诗人倾倒的绝世美貌。说实话，每一位女王或公主，仅仅因为她们的身份，都会受到史官的赞美；她们的嘴唇被形容为纤薄红润，即便那只是一条干裂的唇线；她们的眼睛被形容为两汪漆黑的潭水，而实际上，她们的眼睛往往黯淡无光，毫不起眼，甚至有些斜视。但伊莎贝拉却完美地诠释了所有赞美之词，在她面前，史官们感到愧疚：他们已经用尽了赞美之词来形容那些平庸之辈，如今又该如何赞美她呢？难道他们要创造新的词汇来描绘她吗？唯有如此，才能真正展现她的美。

While in Castile the secret grew tirelessly within Germana's womb, in Portugal, King Manuel's daughter, as soon as the first light of day pierced her chamber, thought of Charles, just as she had done for some time. Isabella was fifteen years old and possessed a beauty that inspires poets. Truth be told, every queen or princess, simply by virtue of being one, was praised by chroniclers; their lips were described as thin and red, even if they were little more than a cracked line, and their eyes as resembling two jet-black pools, when more often than not they were dull, unremarkable, even cross-eyed. But Isabella was the sincere embodiment of every compliment, and before her the chroniclers felt guilty: they had already exhausted their praise on the mediocre, what could they say now of her? Would they have to invent words to describe her? Only that would do her justice.

听过太多赞美她美貌的话语后，伊莎贝尔渐渐变得漠不关心。她对自己的成就感到厌倦，她认为炫耀上帝赐予她的、而非自己努力所得的美貌毫无意义。其他人或许会沉浸于自我陶醉，用目光贪婪地欣赏那注定凋零的青春之美。而她更喜欢闭上双眼，畅想未来。她博览群书，这些书激发了她的幻想，但她幻想的中心人物始终如一。她根据对查理的零星了解——“据说他面色苍白，腼腆内向”——勾勒出他的形象，并在此基础上添加自己的渴望，将他塑造成一个坚实的、能够与她共度一生的男人。在宫廷里，她的这种执念人尽皆知，也被认为是合理的。所有人都相信，葡萄牙和西班牙会通过这桩联姻维持和平，如果运气好的话，这桩联姻会诞下一位继承人，最终统一两国。他们之间的战争虽然过去不久，但怨恨却由来已久，谁也不怀念曾经有个竞争对手的邻居。如今，他们不再像过去那样激烈地争夺海洋和新近开放的陆地，而是以和平的方式展开竞争。这场竞争虽然对双方都至关重要，但由于距离遥远，最终演变成一场外交上的紧张关系。在半岛上，人们渴望和谐，而公主的愿望与王国的政策相悖，这无疑是件好事。

After hearing so many compliments about her beauty, Isabel had grown to ignore them. What she had achieved bored her, and she saw no merit in becoming vain about what God had given her, not her own effort. Others would have become engrossed in their reflections, consuming with their gaze that youthful bloom destined to fade. She preferred to close her eyes and dream of the future. Her fantasies were fueled by her reading, which was extensive, but the central figure in them was always the same. Her mind sketched Charles with the few details she knew about him—"they say he's pale, shy, somewhat withdrawn"—to which she added others, her own desires, to transform him into something solid, a man with whom to bind her destiny. At court, her obsession was known and considered valid. Everyone trusted that Portugal and Spain would maintain peace through a marriage that, with luck, would produce an heir who would finally unite the two kingdoms. The wars between them were not so long ago, but the resentment was, and no one missed having a rival neighbor. Now they vied, without fury, for control of the seas and the new lands to which they offered access; a competition that, although important to both, was dampened by the distance where it took place, remaining little more than diplomatic tensions. On the peninsula, harmony was longed for, and the fact that the Infanta desired what was preferable to the kingdom's policies was the best thing that could have happened.

但在这个年轻女子心中，与其说是策略，不如说是一种命运的安排。一切终将发生。夏日烈阳，母猫产仔，清泉解渴，根特的查理和葡萄牙的伊莎贝拉终将成婚。当求婚者出现时，伊莎贝拉毫不留情地婉拒了他，那种温柔只有笃定之人才能做到。

But in the young woman's mind there was less strategy than a sense of destiny. It had to happen. The sun beat down in summer, cats gave birth to kittens, water quenched thirst, and Charles of Ghent and Isabella of Portugal would marry. When a suitor appeared, Isabella dismissed him without malice, with the gentleness that only someone without doubt can afford.

在葡萄牙宫廷，如同在所有宫廷一样，欧洲地图有两种解读：它现在的样子以及它将如何变化。神圣罗马帝国，这个由查理曼大帝构想的宏伟概念，融合了古罗马的辉煌与基督教信仰的捍卫，它并非单一国家，而是一个由众多领土组成的联盟——从弗兰德斯到热那亚，从德国到西里西亚，从寒冷的奥地利到地中海沿岸的锡耶纳——如今掌握在马克西米利安一世手中。而就在他即将离世之际，他的双手已合十祈祷。由于痛风和肾结石，皇帝的健康状况早已岌岌可危，但自从心脏病发作后，病情更是急剧恶化。据说他出行时总是带着棺材，因为他深信自己时日无多。

In the Portuguese court, as in all courts, the map of Europe had two interpretations: what it was and how it could change. The Holy Roman Empire, that grandiose concept invented by Charlemagne, combining the memory of the might of Ancient Rome with the defense of the Christian faith, and which was not a single state but a kind of federation of domains—from Flanders to Genoa, from Germany to Silesia, from cold Austria to Mediterranean Siena—was in the hands of Maximilian I, and those same hands were already joined in prayer as death approached. The emperor's health had been hanging by a thread for some time, due to gout and kidney stones, but since suffering a heart attack, it had deteriorated even more, and it was said that he always traveled accompanied by his coffin, so certain was he that he had only a few days left in this world.

尽管皇帝的头衔并非世袭，但包括葡萄牙在内的许多人都认为皇帝的孙子是其天然继承人；而这位孙子正是查理。对于葡萄牙公主伊莎贝拉而言，这皇位继承至关重要。“要么成为凯撒，要么什么都不是，”她常常这样对自己说。伊莎贝拉并非出于对荣耀和财富的虚荣心而渴望成为女皇。她和所有人一样明白，帝国固然是一种荣耀，但也是一份沉重且并不丰厚的治理负担。其他君主的生活更加舒适安逸，也更少忧虑，几乎无需治理任何领土。她的抱负则更加浪漫而大胆：如果说有人能够承担起这样的重任，那非她莫属。

Although the title of emperor was not hereditary, many, including in Portugal, saw the emperor's grandson as its natural successor; and that grandson was none other than Charles. For the Portuguese infanta, this imperial future was indispensable. "Either Caesar or nothing," she would say, repeating it to herself. Isabella did not aspire to be empress out of a superfluous desire for homage and riches. She knew, as everyone did, that the Empire was an honor, but also a difficult and not particularly profitable burden of governance. The other monarchs lived more comfortably and with fewer worries, with barely a single territory to attend to. Her ambition was more romantic and audacious: if anyone was capable of assuming such a task, it was she.

伊莎贝尔的母亲阿拉贡的玛丽亚去世已经两年了。她依然在哀悼母亲，尽管总是独自躲在房间的黑暗中，因为如果说她最珍视的美德是什么，那就是宁静。玛丽亚温柔贤惠，作为母亲更是完美无瑕。但伊莎贝尔，即便深爱着她，也无法在她身上找到自己的影子，无法在她那由他人塑造的人生中找到自己的影子。如果说她的性格源于血脉，那么她必须追溯到她的祖母，她的名字和决心都来自祖母：天主教徒伊莎贝尔。从祖母的传奇故事中，这位年轻女子总能汲取教训：人生难免坎坷，而最终的胜利者也未必拥有战胜一切的勇气。

Two years had passed since Isabel had lost her mother, Maria of Aragon. She still mourned her, though always in the darkness of her chamber, for if there was one virtue she cherished above all others, it was serenity. Maria had been a sweet and obliging woman, and as a mother, flawless. But Isabel, even loving her dearly, did not recognize herself in her, in that life shaped by others. If the origin of her character lay in her blood, she had to go back to her grandmother, the one from whom she had taken her name and her resolve: Isabel the Catholic. From the tales of her grandmother's exploits, the young woman always gleaned a lesson: life does not avoid obstacles, nor does the triumphant have the courage to overcome them.

 

 

 

 

令查理自己都感到惊讶的是，他并没有对顾问们隐瞒杰尔马娜怀孕的消息。他以同样漫不经心的态度接受了这个消息，并同样漫不经心地忍受了希耶夫尔和阿德里亚诺的反应。两人一改往日的矜持，像两个蒙羞的母亲一样大声叫喊、手舞足蹈。“孩子！和你的祖父遗孀！丑闻！”几个月前，查理或许会跪地为自己的轻率道歉。但由于顾问们的过激行为让他在卡斯蒂利亚议会面前颜面尽失，他们的权威对他而言已不再是教条。鉴于他们的过错，查理觉得自己也有理由犯错；而他们的指责虽然有理，却也不足以让他质疑一切。

To his own surprise, Charles didn't keep the news of Germana's pregnancy from his advisors. With the same nonchalance with which he had accepted it, he made it known, and with the same nonchalance he endured the reaction of Chièvres and Adriano, who abandoned their measured tone to shout and gesticulate like disgraced mothers. "A child! With your grandfather's widow! Scandal!" Just a few months earlier, Charles would have knelt to apologize for his imprudence. But since his advisors' excesses had landed him in hot water before the Castilian Cortes, their authority was no longer dogma for him. Judging by their failings, Charles felt justified in making his own; and their reproaches, though valid, didn't make him question everything.

“你一定已经决定不再和她见面了。”希耶夫尔说道。

—You must have decided to stop seeing her —said Chièvres.

“我已经决定继续这样做了，”卡洛斯回答道，语气中丝毫没有羞耻之感。

—I have decided to keep doing it —Carlos replied, and there was no shamelessness in his tone.

这位议员义愤填膺。

The councilor was overcome with indignation.

“你们的行为简直像一群乡巴佬！”他咆哮道，“只有那些一无所有的人才会被激情蒙蔽双眼，最终失去一切。让我提醒你们，你们现在的身份是国王，而且一旦你们的祖父驾崩，你们就是皇帝的候选人。”

"You're acting like peasants!" he roared. "Only those who have nothing to lose allow themselves to be blinded by passions, which sweep everything away. Let me remind you who you are: king now, and a candidate for emperor as soon as your grandfather succumbs to fate."

卡洛斯几乎没有反应。他对杰尔玛娜的感情就像一道屏障，任何争论都无法撼动他。

Carlos barely reacted. His feelings for Germana were a shield against which any argument bounced.

“殿下，”阿德里亚诺用那种耐心导师的语气说道，仿佛在向愚钝的学生解释显而易见的事情，“我理解您的高贵身份，也明白您在这种情况下抛弃这位女士会令您痛苦。但是一份体面的养老金，或许再加上一个爵位就足够了。她一定会很满意，而您也能继续前行，不再背负这桩污点。”

“Your Highness,” said Adriano in that patient tutor’s voice that explains the obvious to a foolish student, “I understand your nobility and that it pains you to abandon the lady in this situation. But a decent pension and perhaps a title will suffice. She will undoubtedly be content, and you will be able to continue on without bearing that stain.”

“我继续见她并非出于礼貌，”国王回答说。

"It is not courtesy that compels me to continue seeing her," replied the king.

“你要谈爱情吗？”希耶夫尔嘲讽道，“你的命运就是娶个合你心意的人，跟个能悄悄溜出你卧室的人寻欢作乐。何须感情呢？”

"Are you going to talk about love?" Chièvres mocked. "Your destiny is to marry whomever suits you and frolic with whomever can slip quietly out of your bedchamber. What need is there for feelings?"

阿德里亚诺责备地看了希耶夫一眼。他知道，没有什么比愤世嫉俗者的不理解更能激起恋人的热情了。

Adriano shot a reproachful look at Chièvres. He knew that nothing inflamed a lover more than the incomprehension of a cynic.

“西班牙正翘首以盼你与伊莎贝尔公主的婚约，”阿德里亚诺插话道，“在我看来，在你统领如此众多领土的同时，维持与葡萄牙的和平是最明智的做法……”

“Spain awaits your engagement to the Infanta Isabel,” Adriano interjected. “And it seems to me the most sensible course of action to maintain peace with Portugal while you must attend to so many territories…”

卡洛斯镇定地打断了他。

Carlos interrupted him with composure.

—请允许我拒绝封臣们的联姻命令，也请允许我拒绝那些未能恪守正义之人的正义教诲。

—Allow me to refuse marriage orders from my vassals, nor lessons in righteousness from those who have failed to uphold it.

说完这些，国王平静地离开了议事厅，感觉希耶夫尔和哈德良的目光像鞭子一样抽打着他的后背。议员们呆立原地，被这个问题压得喘不过气来，他们的战略才能在这里几乎无济于事。

Having said this, the king calmly left the council chamber, feeling the glares of Chièvres and Hadrian lash down his back like whips. The councilors stood frozen, paralyzed by the weight of this problem, for which their strategic talents were of little use.

“难道爱情蒙蔽了他所有血脉的判断力吗？”希耶夫尔怒吼道。

"Does love cloud the judgment of all those of his blood?" Chièvres raged.

——他是个男人。他口中的“爱”，不过是一时兴起罢了。

—It's a man. Where it says love, it's just a whim.

“如果他是在自欺欺人，那么他真正的动机又有什么关系呢？我们怎么可能带着费迪南的遗孀，怀着他孙子的孩子，出现在阿拉贡议会面前呢？”希耶夫尔说着，感到一阵眩晕。“我的天哪，我感觉自己这么说简直就是亵渎神明。我们有什么办法阻止这场疯狂吗？”

"What does it matter what truly motivates him, if he's deluding himself? We can't possibly appear before the Aragonese Cortes with Ferdinand's widow pregnant by his grandson," Chièvres said, and felt faint. "My God, I feel I'm blaspheming just by saying it. Is there anything we can do to stop this madness?"

一阵漫长的沉默。他们找不到解决办法。

A long silence fell. They couldn't find a solution.

“我们早该预料到这一刻的到来，”哈德良总结道，“我们费尽心思培养统治者，却忘记了他作为一个人。如果他能从父母那里得到一些管教，并把他们的责备当作命令来听，他现在该会受益匪浅啊。”

“We should have known this moment would come,” Hadrian concluded. “We’ve gone to so much trouble to educate the ruler that we’ve forgotten the man. How much he would benefit now from parents whose rebukes he could take as commands.”

希耶夫尔忍不住露出了嘲讽的表情。

Chièvres couldn't help but make a sneering face.

—我们带他去托尔德西利亚斯，让胡安娜女王给他讲讲什么是明智的爱。

—Let's take him to Tordesillas and let Queen Juana enlighten him about sensible love.

“我们忘了他还有另一个母亲，”阿德里亚诺说道，并看着基耶夫雷斯，希望他能接受自己的想法，因为除此之外别无选择。

—We forgot that he has another mother— said Adriano, and looked at Chièvres hoping that he would accept his idea, because there was no other option.

 

 

 

 

奥地利的玛格丽特反复阅读哈德良的信，才相信信中的内容。她问信使，这封信是否真的来自巴利亚多利德宫廷，而不是某个喜剧剧院。确认信件真实性后，她立刻坐下来准备回信。然而，查理的愚蠢令她无比失望，她一手栽培教育的青年竟如此不负责任，这令她怒不可遏，以至于她笔尖颤抖，只能在纸上潦草地写下几笔，然后怒火中烧地将信撕碎。

Margaret of Austria had to read Hadrian's letter several times to believe what it said. She asked the messenger if the message had truly come from the court of Valladolid, and not from a comedy theater. Once she was certain of the letter's authenticity, she immediately sat down to write her reply, but so great was her disappointment at Charles's folly, so great was her anger that the man she had raised and educated should act so irresponsibly, that her hand faltered and she could only manage to smudge the paper before tearing it up in a fit of rage.

玛格丽特望着窗外，看到工人们正在扩建梅赫伦宫。这项工程已经持续多年，而且注定还要继续下去。他们从早到晚，每天都全身心投入工作，心中别无所求，只知道他们正在建造的这座宫殿将容纳那些权势滔天、地位高不可攀的人，以至于他们连嫉妒都不敢。玛格丽特想象着他们清晨起床，天色还未亮；她想象着他们在妻子们的注视下，吃着简朴的食物补充能量。妻子们怀抱着孩子，晚上他们又要和妻子们重聚。男人们劳作疲惫，女人们则忙于照顾孩子，但他们都心甘情愿，在睡前向上帝感恩，感谢自己所拥有的一切，无论他们自认为拥有的是什么。与此同时，查理却背弃了理智，这是他获得特权、享受凡人永远无法企及的荣耀所必须付出的唯一代价。

Margarita looked out the window and saw the men working on the expansion of the Mechelen palace, a project that had been going on for years and promised to continue for many more. There they were, from dawn till dusk, dedicated each day to their work, with no ambition but that, knowing that the building they were erecting would house people so powerful, so elevated above them, that they didn't even allow themselves to envy them. Margarita imagined them rising early, the world still dark; she pictured them gathering strength with humble fare under the watchful eyes of wives laden with children, whom they would meet again at night, the men exhausted from their labor and the women from raising their children, but both resigned and giving thanks to God before sleeping for their lot, whatever it was they imagined they had. And meanwhile, Charles turned his back on reason, the only price demanded of him for his privileges, for enjoying all the glory that the rest of mortals would never possess.

当她接管查理和他的姐妹们时，未来的国王只有四岁。玛格丽特当时还不到二十八岁，已经是第二次守寡了。第一次是在她丈夫阿拉贡的约翰去世之后，约翰是伊莎贝拉和费尔南多的儿子，婚后不久便去世了。这场悲剧在她心中留下了深深的烙印，尤其是紧接着她腹中的孩子也夭折了，她曾把守寡的希望寄托在这个孩子身上。不幸使她对命运充满怀疑，但也使她变得坚不可摧，因为她知道生命中最痛苦的事情已经过去。正是这两种特质的结合，使她在哥哥菲利普在卡斯蒂利亚去世后，不得不接管尼德兰的统治时，成为了一位无可挑剔的摄政王。照顾她的侄子侄女们减轻了她作为母亲的挫败感，但她也深知这个家族的未来，所以她不会过于溺爱他们，而是保持着严厉的管教。当她察觉到查尔斯的性格敏感而又有些沉默寡言时，便致力于培养他的坚强。她格外小心，不让哥哥费利佩的缺点在他身上生根发芽，尤其是那种既不征求同意也不听劝告的任性愚蠢。但那封信揭示了，如果激情闯入一个人的生活，所有的教育都将毫无意义。玛格丽特从信中不仅看到了眼前的困境，也看到了未来可能犯下的错误，这些错误必须立即制止。

When she took charge of Charles and his sisters, the future king was only four years old. Margaret, barely twenty-eight, had been widowed for the second time. The first time, when John of Aragon, son of Isabella and Ferdinand, died shortly after their marriage, had left its mark on her character, especially when that death was followed by that of the child she was expecting, in whom she had placed her hopes for solace in her widowhood. Misfortune had made her distrustful of fate but also indestructible, because she knew that the greatest pain of her life was behind her. These two traits combined made her an impeccable regent when the death of her brother Philip in Castile forced her to assume the government of the Netherlands. Taking responsibility for her nephews and nieces eased her frustration with motherhood, but she was too aware of the destiny that awaited that family to be overly affectionate without also being stern. When she sensed that Charles's character seemed sensitive and somewhat taciturn, she devoted herself to strengthening him. She took special care to prevent her brother Felipe's flaws from taking root in him, especially that capricious folly that neither sought permission nor listened to reason. But that letter revealed that all education was worthless if passion crossed a man's path, and Margarita glimpsed in those words not only the present problem but also a warning of future blunders that had to be stopped immediately.

玛格丽塔把信拿给费尔南多看。卡洛斯的哥哥只读了一遍就感到震惊不已。这件事对他来说充满了乱伦的黑暗诱惑。杰尔玛娜对他来说只是个空洞的母亲，想到她与卡洛斯在床上寻欢作乐，他就感到无比厌恶。他感觉自己第二次被放逐了。第一次，他被驱逐出自己的王国；而现在，他仅存的亲情纽带却交织在一起，对他毫不知情，反而为他的缺席而欢欣鼓舞。

Margarita showed the letter to Fernando. One reading was enough for Carlos's brother to feel scandalized. The matter held the dark allure of incest for him. Germana had been a mere shadow of a mother to him, and the thought of her pleasing Carlos in bed was abhorrent. He also felt exiled for the second time. First, he had been banished from his kingdom, and now the only bonds of affection he had left were intertwined, completely unaware of him, joyfully celebrating his absence.

尽管内心有些不安，费尔南多这才意识到，自从来到弗兰德斯，他几乎没怎么想起过他们俩。他没有强迫自己忘记他们，也没有在回忆涌上心头时刻意回避。他自然而然地失去了怀旧之情。他的现实不在西班牙，而是在那个夜幕降临得稍早一些，却比他预想中更善待他的地方。说实话，在梅赫伦，他需要刻意去让自己感到不自在，但他并不想这么做。这种改变对他来说就像一次洗礼，将他变成了一个他自己还无法命名，但却欣然接受的全新自我。就连镜子里的他，也仿佛是一个截然不同的人，一个更成熟、更没有怨恨的人。

Despite his unease, Fernando realized then that he had barely thought about the two of them since arriving in Flanders. He hadn't forced himself to forget them, nor did he reject their memory when it surfaced. His was a spontaneous lack of nostalgia. His reality wasn't in Spain, but in that place where night fell a little earlier but which had been kinder to him than he had expected. To tell the truth, he would have had to consciously try to feel uncomfortable in Mechelen, and he hadn't felt like making the effort. The change had been a baptism for him, transforming him into something he couldn't yet name, but which he accepted. Even the mirror reflected back at him a different person, more of a man, free of resentment.

“据阿德里亚诺说，如果这起丑闻公之于众，将会毁掉查尔斯在王国的声誉，”玛格丽塔说。

"According to Adriano, if this scandal were to become public, it would ruin Charles's reputation in the kingdom," said Margarita.

费尔南多摇了摇头。

Fernando shook his head.

——这件事或许会彻底毁了他的名声，但他的名声早已受损，而且受损严重。这一切都是因为希耶夫尔。

—This affair may bury his reputation, but it was already damaged, and badly so. Because of Chièvres.

费尔南多向玛格丽塔讲述了顾问的种种恶行，她一边听一边点头，毫不怀疑其真实性。希耶夫尔一直令她不悦，但当他在梅赫伦担任卡洛斯的家庭教师时，他的过错如此隐蔽，以至于她始终没有确凿的理由将他撤职。即便如此，她总能从他冷漠的眼神中感受到一种卑劣的智慧，那眼神中缺乏任何可能使他显得人性化的情感。顾问逐渐疏远了卡洛斯和玛格丽塔之间的关系。摄政工作如此繁重，某种程度上，她也庆幸自己对侄子的责任有所减轻；但她从未完全置身事外，因为她知道，如果卡洛斯只听从顾问的指示，他可能会迷失自我。

Fernando recounted the abuses of the advisor to Margarita, and she listened, nodding, without doubting their truth. Chièvres had always displeased her, but while he was Carlos's tutor in Mechelen, his transgressions had been so subtle that she had never had any compelling grounds to remove him. Even so, she always perceived in him a vile intelligence, reflected in his gaze, too impassive, devoid of any emotion that might humanize it. The advisor had gradually alienated Carlos from Margarita. Her regency was so demanding that, in a way, she was grateful that her responsibility for her nephew was diminishing; but she never completely disengaged, because she knew that Carlos, if heeded only his advisor, could lose his soul.

玛格丽塔很惊讶，费尔南多在弗兰德斯的几个月里，竟然没有举报这位议员的过激行为。

Margarita was surprised that Fernando, in the months he had been in Flanders, had not reported the councilor's excesses.

“我仍然不知道我在这间法庭上的角色是什么，”费尔南多回答道，语气中没有丝毫责备。

—I still don't know what my role is in this court—Fernando replied, without sounding reproachful.

玛格丽塔对他笑了笑。卡洛斯告诉她要去接费尔南多时，她觉得这会是个麻烦，而且必然会引发冲突。一个被亲兄弟流放的人，很难有什么美德可言。但费尔南多抵达梅赫伦宫时，举止绅士，心境平和，这与流放者的身份截然不同。他最近才提起卡洛斯，但每次提起，语气都十分温和，甚至还要求看看哥哥小时候读过的书，并认真地翻阅。从第一天起，他就以德报答别人的恩情，并对佛兰德斯的风俗表现出浓厚的兴趣：繁复的礼仪、不间断的庆典、美食、人民。他如此坦然地接受自己年少时就遭遇的命运，这不仅让玛格丽塔对他心生喜爱，更让她敬佩不已。

Margarita smiled at him. When Carlos told her he was going to receive Fernando, she saw it as a burden that would inevitably lead to conflict. Few virtues could be found in someone who had deserved to be exiled by his own brother. But Fernando arrived at the palace in Mechelen with the bearing of a gentleman and a peace of mind uncharacteristic of an exile. When he spoke of Carlos, which he did only recently, he never used a harsh tone, and even asked to see the books his brother had used as a child, which he reviewed attentively. From the first day, he repaid every favor with another and showed curiosity about Flemish customs: the meticulous protocol, the constant festivities, the food, the people. His stoic acceptance of the fate that had befallen him at such a young age made Margarita not only grow fond of him but also admire him.

“我相信你的判断，”玛格丽塔回答说。“从现在开始，别再藏着掖着了。跟我说说那个女人，杰曼娜·德·福瓦。你觉得她能让你哥哥爱上你，还是只会欺骗他？”

“I trust your opinion,” Margarita replied. “From now on, don’t keep it to yourselves. Tell me about that woman, Germana de Foix. Do you think she’s capable of making your brother fall in love with you, or merely of deceiving him?”

费尔南多在内心深处寻找着最不受情感影响的判断。

Fernando searched within himself for the judgment least clouded by his feelings.

—她心思缜密，但她有颗善良的心，她不会想要伤害别人的心。

—She is cunning, but she has a heart, and she doesn't seek to harm the hearts of others.

玛格丽塔点了点头，然后开始在心里斟酌该如何措辞，才能将此事告诉她认为唯一能够解决这个问题的人。

Margarita nodded and, to herself, began to search for the words she would address about this matter to the only person she believed capable of solving it.

 

 

 

 

—告诉我，我父亲的情况如何？

—Tell me, how is my father?

梅尔库里诺·加蒂纳拉向玛格丽塔鞠了一躬，脸上满是无奈的神情。

Mercurino Gattinara bowed to Margarita and responded with a look full of resignation.

——恐怕皇帝的判决已经签署完毕。我们唯一能指望的就是判决执行得晚些。

—I fear the emperor's sentence has been signed. All we can hope for is that it will be carried out late.

加蒂纳拉五十四年的人生中，有十八年是在玛格丽特王后侍奉的。和她一样，他拥有丰富的人文情怀和渊博的学识，但必要时既不天真也不冷酷，始终保持着优雅的举止和自认为无穷无尽的耐心。当他听到玛格丽特讲述查理的困境时，他的镇定自若显而易见。他非但没有感到震惊，反而默默地点了点头，仿佛早已习惯了意外怀孕和那些掠夺整个王国的谋臣——事实上，他对此并不了解。

Of his fifty-four years, Gattinara had spent the last eighteen in Margaret's service. Like her, he possessed a wealth of humanist sensitivity and erudition, but he was neither naive nor ruthless when necessary, never losing, however, his elegant manners or his patience, which he considered boundless. His composure was evident upon hearing Margaret's account of Charles's predicament. Instead of being scandalized, he nodded silently, as if he were accustomed to unwanted pregnancies and advisors who plundered an entire kingdom—which, in truth, he was not.

乌得勒支的阿德里安让我用寥寥数语劝服我的侄子，让他彻底放下对那个女人的迷恋。或许我能做到，但我希望他能两次放下心来，而这项任务我只能托付给我最得力的部下。在这个宫廷里，我最不愿失去的就是他。

—Adrian of Utrecht asks me to convince my nephew, in a few lines, to disenchant himself with that woman. Perhaps I could do it, but I want him to be disenchanted twice, and I can only entrust that task to the best of my men. The one I will be so saddened to lose in this court.

玛格丽塔和加蒂娜拉握手，这是她们多年来的第一次，她们用这个动作表达了对一切的感激之情。那天晚上，在她的顾问离开后，摄政王为她的父亲祈祷，祈求他不要过早离世，因为无论谁将来继承他的王位，似乎都还不够格。

Margarita and Gattinara shook hands, for the first time in so many years together, and with that gesture they expressed their gratitude for everything. That night, after her advisor's departure, the regent prayed for her father and asked that life not yet slip away from him, because whoever, should fortune grant, was to succeed him, did not yet seem worthy.

 

 

 

 

马克西米利安的健康状况让欧洲宫廷变成了悲观的医生诊室，因为人人都在谈论它，却无人相信它会好转。关于皇帝的讨论，即便没有开始，最终也总是围绕着谁将继承他的王位展开。这个人必须拥有足够的尊严来配得上这份荣耀，但更重要的是，他还要有能力为此挥霍无度。皇位之路被简化为一条通往查理曼大帝宝座的贿赂之路，被选中的人登上王位时，既光芒四射，又债台高筑。鉴于代价如此高昂，这位幸运儿需要拥有近乎不切实际的野心，渴望登上那至高无上的宝座——而实际上，它的代价远远大于它所带来的回报。

Maximilian's health had turned European courts into pessimistic doctors' offices, because everyone talked about it but no one believed it would improve. Conversations about the emperor ended, if they didn't begin, with bets on who would succeed him. It would have to be someone with enough dignity to deserve the honor, but also—and this was more crucial—capable of spending a fortune in the endeavor. The imperial career was reduced to a path of bribes that ended on the throne of Charlemagne, where the chosen one arrived as radiant as he was indebted. Given that the cost was so high, the fortunate one needed a rather unrealistic ambition, a desire to see himself on that pedestal whose price was, in practical terms, far greater than its reward.

如果说谁是威严、财富和对荣耀的无限渴望的化身，那非法国国王弗朗索瓦莫属。所有押注他的人都争相拥。他的王国富可敌国；他年轻有为；而他所拥有的“最虔诚的国王”这一象征性头衔更是激励着他，因为帝国正是由基督教信仰所定义和维护的。弗朗索瓦的母亲萨伏依的路易丝从小就称呼他为“我的凯撒”，以此来培养儿子的帝王梦。自幼年起，他便经常听到这个称呼，帝国与他的名字早已在他的意识中密不可分。事实上，王位的评选过程似乎更像是一种形式主义，而非必要之举。然而，随着马克西米利安的驾崩临近，弗朗索瓦开始听到传言，查理可能会挑战他的王位。

If anyone embodied grandeur, wealth, and an unbridled thirst for glory, it was Francis, the French king. Every bet placed on him was first in line. The riches of his kingdom were immense; his youth, promising; and the symbolic title of Most Christian King he held was an incentive, since the Empire was defined by and for that faith. Francis's mother, Louise of Savoy, had nurtured her son's imperial dreams by addressing him as "my Caesar." From responding to that name so often since his earliest childhood, the Empire and his name had become inextricably linked in his consciousness. The selection process, in fact, seemed more ritualistic than necessary. However, as Maximilian's death drew near, Francis began to hear rumors that Charles might challenge him for the title.

——你在开玩笑吧。

—You're joking.

“他是马克西米利安的继承人，接管西班牙让他获得了他所需要的荣耀，”他的顾问蒙莫朗西警告他。

"He is Maximilian's heir, and taking over Spain has given him the luster he needed," Montmorency, his advisor, warned him.

“他们说他还没能完全掌握这些领地的治理之道，尽管他统治着它们。哪个傻瓜会拥立一个连自己的领地都治理不好的人为帝呢？”弗朗西斯问道。

—They say he hasn't yet mastered them, even though he reigns over them. What fool would elevate to emperor someone who doesn't even know how to govern his own fiefdom? —Francis asked.

——我并不否认这一点，殿下。但获得确凿的支持并无坏处，这样就能将信任转化为确定性。

—I don't dispute that, Your Highness. But it wouldn't hurt to secure certain support, and thus turn trust into certainty.

弗朗西斯觉得宣传自己的候选资格是一种耻辱，仿佛自己有义务这样做一样。直到他收到沃尔西枢机主教要来拜访他的通知后，他才觉得可以利用这个机会讨论此事，而不会因为寻求他的支持而让自己蒙羞。

Francis felt humiliated by promoting his candidacy, as if he were obliged to do so, and only when he received the warning that Cardinal Wolsey was going to pay him a visit did he think he could take advantage of it to discuss the matter, without having dishonored himself by pursuing his support.

这位英国教士带着他温文尔雅的举止来到法国宫廷，但这温文尔雅的外表下却隐藏着锋芒。沃尔西说话声音低沉，或许是因为他从未需要提高音量来命令亨利八世服从。英国国王对他绝对信任，而整个欧洲都知道，要想赢得君主的青睐，首先要赢得红衣主教的青睐，而红衣主教只听命于利益。沃尔西的这种贪婪，是许多人的罪过，但在他身上却被归咎于他卑微的出身。一个屠夫的儿子能够成为英国最有影响力的人，必然要付出代价，而每个人都为此付出了代价。然而，尽管沃尔西精于自我提升，但他心中始终萦绕着一个执念：登上教皇之位，为了实现这个目标，他甚至愿意倾尽所有。

The English clergyman arrived at the French court with his gentle manner, the same manner that concealed a razor's edge. Wolsey spoke in a low voice, perhaps because he had never had to raise his voice to command Henry's obedience. The English king trusted him implicitly, and everyone in Europe knew that to win the monarch's favor, one first had to win the cardinal's, and that the cardinal answered only to profit. This avarice of Wolsey's, the sin of so many, was attributed in his case to the humbleness of his origins. That the son of a butcher had risen to become the most influential man in England had to come at a price, and everyone paid it. However, despite having made an art of self-improvement, the cardinal lived with the obsession of reaching the papacy, and he would gladly have parted with his wealth to achieve it.

“我以神仆的身份来到你们面前，”沃尔西说道，“我和罗马的意愿是促成基督教君主之间的协议，这将给我们的人民带来和平，如同给异教徒带来战争一样。英格兰已经为此做出了承诺，并希望得到你们的支持。”

“I come before you as a man of God,” Wolsey said. “It is my will, and Rome’s, to bring about an agreement between the Christian kings that will bring as much peace to our people as war to the infidel. England has already committed itself to this and hopes to have you on its side.”

“你的行动令人钦佩。”弗朗西斯回答道。

—Your undertaking is admirable —Francis replied.

—我听说你会和她一起去？

—I understand that you will join her?

弗朗西斯科做了个鬼脸，沃尔西试图解读，但没有成功。

Francisco made a face that Wolsey tried unsuccessfully to decipher.

我的党派会非常支持你的提议，你在罗马也会备受尊敬。你是欧洲和平的捍卫者！你的功绩足以实现你的抱负。你愿意帮我实现我的抱负吗？

—My party would greatly endorse your proposal, and you would be held in high regard in Rome. A champion of peace in Europe! Merit enough to fulfill your ambitions. Would you help me fulfill mine?

“帝国，”红衣主教猜测道。

"The Empire," guessed the cardinal.

与沃尔西这样的人打交道的好处在于，勒索对他们来说就像日落一样微不足道。枢机主教承诺会为弗朗西斯向教皇求情，教皇的意见在选择马克西米连的继任者时将举足轻重。他们心满意足地告别，并对促成和平的行动赞不绝口，尽管对他们两人而言，最终目标只不过是达成目的的手段而已。

The advantage of dealing with men like Wolsey lay in the fact that blackmail shocked them about as much as the sunset. The cardinal promised to intercede on Francis's behalf with the Pope, whose opinion would carry considerable weight in choosing Maximilian's successor. They parted satisfied and praising their peacemaking mission, although for neither of them was the end goal more than a means to an end.

 

 

 

 

沃尔西回到英格兰，向国王汇报外交上的成功时，小心翼翼地避免激起亨利天生的好胜心。他斟酌字句，力求解释为何在争夺帝国霸权的斗争开始时，他们应该支持弗朗西斯。他别无选择，只能竭尽全力，因为英法两国尚未从百年战争的创伤中恢复过来，所有英国人，包括国王在内，都把一切与法国有关的事物视为一种病毒——尽管他们现在对此免疫，但当年这种病毒几乎将他们灭亡。然而，沃尔西深知，最大的问题并非历史恩怨，而是亨利的性格。如果由他做主，他恐怕会不惜一切代价也要阻止任何人胜过他。要让他支持另一个人——而且这个人还是个法国人！——成为皇帝，绝非易事。但沃尔西向国王陈述了自己的理由，国王最终接受了。不过，他确实询问了关于他的侄子查理的情况。如果他竞选公职，支持他难道不是人之常情吗？

When Wolsey returned to England and told his king of his diplomatic successes, he was careful not to unleash Henry's natural competitiveness. He measured every word to explain why they should support Francis when the struggle for the Empire began. And he had no choice but to exert himself, for England and France had not yet healed from their Hundred Years' War, and every Englishman, including the king, viewed anything French as a virus to which they were now immune but which, in its day, had nearly killed them. Wolsey knew, however, that historical grudges were not the biggest problem, but rather Henry's character, who, had it been up to him, would have ordered the heavens to be torn down to avoid being outdone by anyone. To get him to lend his support to someone else—and that someone else, a Frenchman!—to become emperor was a complicated task. But Wolsey presented his arguments to the king, and he eventually accepted them. He did, however, ask about Charles, his nephew. Wouldn't it be natural to support him if he ran for office?

红衣主教回答说：“大人，必须与那些构成威胁的人结盟；而不是与那些因为是家人而永远不会构成威胁的人结盟。”

—My lord, alliances must be sought with those who threaten; not with those who, because they are family, will never do so—replied the cardinal.

“你是在推动签订永久和平条约，并警告我不要发动战争吗？”亨利问道。

—Are you promoting a treaty of perpetual peace and warning me against war? —Henry asked.

“如果我成功地让你们相信这份条约将永久有效，那么我的虚荣心在这座岛上就无处容身。只要武器能够闲置五年，我就心满意足了。我并不渴望改变人类的境况，更遑论改变君王的境况。”

"If I have managed to make you believe that this treaty will be perpetual, my vanity has no place on this island. I would be content if the weapons remained laid low for five years. I do not aspire to change the human condition, least of all that of kings."

英格兰国王对这个答复很满意，宣布休会。他像火花一样从座位上跳了起来。他很容易感到厌倦。他精力无限，如果不能通过运动或性爱来释放，他就会像一根燃烧的导火索，不停地从一件事跳到另一件事。他总觉得自己内心有一股驱动力，却没有明确的方向，而沃尔西在政治目标上的沉着冷静无疑是他作为统治者的救星。然而，他的精神比其他行动派要复杂得多。他受过良好的教育，既喜欢写诗，也喜欢和朋友们辩论。但是，尽管他热爱文字，却始终无法定义自己。他包罗万象，至少有时是这样。这种模糊性让他对自己的决定产生怀疑。每个决定似乎都正确，取决于当时的形势。正因如此，当他的妻子凯瑟琳得知他支持法国而勃然大怒时，国王犹豫了。

The King of England was satisfied with that reply and adjourned the meeting. He leapt from his seat like a spark. He was easily bored. He possessed boundless energy, and if he didn't release it through sports or sex, he became a burning fuse, leaping from one thing to another. He always felt within himself a driving force without a clear direction, and Wolsey's serenity in keeping political objectives in check was undoubtedly his salvation as a ruler. His spirit, however, was more complex than that of other men of action. He had been carefully educated and enjoyed writing poetry as much as sparring with his friends. But, despite his penchant for words, he would never have known how to define himself. He was everything, at least at times. This ambiguity led him to doubt his decisions. They all seemed valid depending on the moment. For this reason, when his wife Catherine was outraged to learn of his support for the French, the king hesitated.

“法定继承人是我侄子！”卡塔琳娜抱怨道。

"The natural heir is my nephew!" complained Catalina.

“一个缺乏经验的男孩，”恩里克回答道。

"An inexperienced boy," replied Enrique.

——你更希望看到帝国的全部权力掌握在非帝国之人手中吗？弗朗西斯积聚了如此强大的力量，他需要多久才会进攻英格兰？

—Do you prefer the full power of an Empire in the hands of someone who isn't one? How long will it take for Francis to attack England when he has amassed so much power?

“正因如此，我才需要你们的联盟！”国王说道。

"That's precisely why I want your alliance!" said the king.

帝国将在他们手中掌控数十年。你们的联盟能维持一年就算幸运了，其他联盟的联盟都难以长久。

—The Empire will be in their hands for decades. You're lucky if your alliance lasts a year, and not what all the others do.

凯瑟琳心烦意乱，这在她身上实属罕见。她一言一行都充满尊严，举止端庄而不谄媚，坚定而不失风度。只有独处时，她才会崩溃，诅咒那未能为亨利诞下继承人的子宫，只生下了玛丽——一个虽受人爱戴却对国王延续都铎王朝血脉毫无用处的孩子。她出身贵族，是天主教徒的女儿，但这无关紧要；她王后的身份也无济于事。一个没能为国王诞下儿子的妻子，甚至不如一个女招待，因为她没能做到国王真正要求她做的事。尽管人们敬佩她的智慧、品格和善良，但在所有人眼中，她终究只是一个可怜的、无用的女人，而正是因为她，英格兰王室的未来才如此岌岌可危。凯瑟琳继续相信上帝会赐给她一个孩子，她祈祷得如此虔诚，以至于亨利的背叛有时都没有被注意到，因为当亨利发泄怒气时，她跪在地上，在一位什么也没答应她的基督面前乞求了几个小时。

Catherine was agitated, something unusual for her. Everything she did or said was imbued with dignity. She was virtuous without being obsequious and firm without being offensive. Her spirit only broke when she was alone and cursed the womb that had not given Henry an heir, and that had only produced Mary, a child adored by all but who was of no use to the king's obsession with perpetuating his lineage, that of the Tudors. The nobility of her origins, daughter of Catholics, mattered little; nor did her rank, that of queen. The wife of a king who did not give him a son was worth less than a waitress, because she failed in the one thing that was truly demanded of her. And however much her intelligence, her character, and her kindness were admired, to everyone she was, in the end, a poor, useless woman, because of whom the Crown of England still faced an uncertain future. Catherine continued to trust that God would grant her a child, and she prayed so much that Henry's infidelities sometimes went unnoticed, because while he was letting off steam, she, kneeling, begged for hours before a Christ who promised her nothing.

关于弗朗西斯的谈话令两人陷入沉思，尽管原因各不相同。她回想起童年，想起法国对她父母伊莎贝拉和费迪南德宫廷构成的持续威胁。她记得自己曾惧怕战争，仿佛还能听到父亲对法国人新的背信弃义之举的咒骂声，他时不时就会如此。她辗转难眠，半夜起身给查理写信。

The discussion about Francis left them both pensive, though for different reasons. She relived her childhood and the constant threat that France posed to the court of her parents, Isabella and Ferdinand. She remembered fearing war and could almost hear her father's cries of curse, as he did every so often, at some new act of treachery by the French. Sleepless, she got up in the middle of the night and wrote to Charles.

 

 

 

 

自从那次争吵之后，查理和他的顾问们再也没有提起过杰玛娜怀孕的事。国王不再需要为她辩护，不再受她攻击，开始克制自己的感性，很快他就意识到自己的立场毫无意义。迟早，他都必须接受一桩对王国有利、能为他带来继承人的婚事。保持单身是不可能的，娶一个只有爱情维系的人也不行。然而，这种在他心中生根发芽的理性思考，在他与情人相处的那一刻便土崩瓦解，理智被肌肤的触碰或耳语所吞噬，令他脊背发凉。幽会归来后，查理既感到爱意满满，又怒火中烧。究竟是什么毒药，竟能摧毁一切正义？他感到自己被囚禁、被迷惑、被奴役。于是，他下定决心永不再见她，以捍卫自己的理智。接下来的几天，他的决心几乎没有动摇。但突然间，关于她的记忆会涌上心头，就在当晚，理智再次败下阵来。他懊恼不已，再次选择疏远，但这不过是重蹈覆辙的倒计时。

Since their argument, Charles and his advisors hadn't spoken of Germana's pregnancy again. No longer forced to defend her from her attacks, the king began to temper his sentimentality, and he soon realized his stance was utterly pointless. Sooner or later, he would have to accept a match that would benefit the kingdom and provide him with heirs. Remaining single was out of the question, as was marrying someone to whom he was bound only by love. But this judicious discourse that was taking root within him crumbled the moment he was with his lover, and logic was swallowed up by a touch of skin or a whisper that sent shivers down his spine. Returning from their trysts, Charles felt both in love and furious. What poison was this that obliterated what was right? He felt imprisoned, addicted, enslaved. And then he would resolve never to see her again, to protect his common sense. For days, his resolve barely wavered. But then, suddenly, a memory of her would assail him, and that very night, logic would once again lose the battle. Angry with himself, he imposed distance once again, but it was only a countdown to relapse.

她比往常更久地躲避她，这时一封来自葡萄牙的信寄到了，署名是曼努埃尔国王。国王知道皇帝的健康状况，希望伊莎贝拉和查理的婚事能尽快敲定。争夺帝国的斗争很快就会席卷查理，迟早会把他带到德国。他们应该利用彼此距离近的优势，尽快敲定婚事并举行婚礼。尽管葡萄牙国王的言辞中充满了美好的愿望和天文数字般的嫁妆，但他也不忘发出威胁：如果她拒绝这门婚事或拖延太久，他的王国将要求她偿还欠西班牙的债务。而宽恕这笔债务，不过是一位欣喜若狂的岳父的恩赐罢了。

She had been avoiding her for longer than usual when a letter arrived from Portugal, signed by King Manuel, who, aware of the Emperor's health, expressed his desire that the marriage between Isabella and Charles be negotiated without delay. The struggle for the Empire would soon engulf Charles and, sooner or later, lead him to Germany. They should take advantage of their proximity to finalize the agreement and celebrate the marriage. Although his words overflowed with good intentions and the promise of an astronomical dowry, the Portuguese king did not hold back a threat: if she refused the marriage or delayed it too long, his kingdom would demand repayment of its debt to Spain. Forgiving it would be merely the gift of an overjoyed father-in-law.

勒索奏效了，查理的朝廷陷入了焦虑之中。王室早已为他的帝王生涯积攒了不少开支，不惜一切代价，尤其是一些昂贵或可以避免的费用。葡萄牙国王并不知道，查理在压力之下很容易反抗。如果说他已经对所有人替他决定婚事感到恼火，那么被迫接受这桩婚事更是让他怒不可遏。

The blackmail worked, plunging Charles's court into anxiety. The Crown was already saving for the expense of his imperial career, and no money was being spared, especially not the costly or avoidable ones. What the Portuguese king didn't know was that Charles easily rebelled under pressure. If he was already annoyed that everyone had decided for him whom he should marry, he was even more annoyed that he was being coerced into it.

 

 

 

 

事实上，他的忧虑让他变得自私。在他眼里，其他人都像是他内心不安的舞台剧中的配角。直到一天早晨，一声哭喊才让卡洛斯终于从自怜中挣脱出来。哭声循着声音来到隔壁房间，他发现莱昂诺尔双手捂着脸，身体因悲伤而颤抖。

The truth was that his worries had made him selfish. Everyone else seemed like extras in a play about his own unease. It took a cry for Carlos to finally break free from his own self-pity one morning. The sound led him to a nearby room, where he found Leonor with her head buried in her hands and her body trembling with grief.

-姐姐。

-Sister.

莱昂诺抬起头。她沮丧的神情让她看起来比实际年龄要老。

Leonor raised her head. Her dejection made her look older than she was.

求求你，让我返回弗兰德斯吧。

—Let me return to Flanders. I beg you.

卡洛斯一直以为妹妹对费德里科伯爵的思念已经消退了。如果不是亲身体验过这种感情的奴役感，他永远也无法理解妹妹的悲伤。

Carlos had believed that his sister's longing for Count Federico had already subsided. And her grief would have been incomprehensible to him had he not discovered for himself how enslaving the feeling was.

“我不会让你独自旅行，”查尔斯说。“阿拉贡议会将是我在这片土地上的最后一个任务。一旦我完成这项任务，我们就会返回。”

"I will not let you travel alone," said Charles. "The Cortes of Aragon will be my last duty in these lands. As soon as I have fulfilled it, we will return."

—太迟了！如果我不马上回去，他会彻底忘记我的。

—It will be too late! If I don't return immediately, he will completely forget me.

“他不给你写信吗？”卡洛斯问道。

—Doesn't he write to you? —Carlos asked.

莱昂诺尔含着泪回答。她毫无防备，任人摆布。卡洛斯怒不可遏。他多么希望自己拥有魔法，能够解救被囚禁的妹妹。但他甚至连自己都做不到。

Leonor answered with tears in her eyes. She was defenseless, at the mercy of others. Carlos was furious. What he would have given to possess a magical power, the power to free his sister from this bondage. But he wasn't even capable of doing it for himself.

“什么样的爱情才能经受住距离的考验呢？”莱昂诺尔喃喃自语道。

"What love can withstand distance?" Leonor wondered aloud.

——你的就是这样。

—Yours does.

因为这本身就是一种折磨。而且这种折磨可能会持续一生。

—Because it's already torment. And this can last a lifetime.

莱昂诺尔的眼神里，更多的是谴责而非对未来的憧憬。她的哥哥想象着她长大后的样子，变成那种被怀旧掏空、内心总是哭泣的女人。卡洛斯意识到爱情是魔鬼，他曾经在被迫接受某种东西时所感受到的反抗，也必须被用来对付他。所以，如果妹妹无法挣脱束缚，他会替她挣脱。

Leonor's gaze was that of someone who sees more condemnation than a future. Her brother imagined her grown up, transformed into one of those women emptied by nostalgia, who are always weeping inside. Carlos realized that love was the devil, and that the same rebellion he felt when something was imposed upon him had to be used against him. So if his sister was incapable of freeing herself, he would do it for her.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，凯瑟琳的信在黄昏时分抵达宫廷。此时，宫殿里开始弥漫着烤肉的香气，仆人们正忙着点亮房间。查理吩咐人斟上啤酒，这可是他难得的享受，因为王国里唯一能喝到的啤酒——是他从佛兰德斯带来的——也快喝完了。他姑妈的话让他的酒更加苦涩。当希耶夫尔走进房间，看到查理的反应时，他接过信，国王欣然接受。

Meanwhile, Catherine's letter arrived at court at dusk, when the palace was beginning to fill with the aroma of roast meat and the servants were hurrying to illuminate the rooms. Charles had ordered beer to be served, a pleasure he rarely indulged in, as the only beer available in the kingdom, brought by him from Flanders, was almost gone. His aunt's words made his drinks even more bitter than they already were. When Chièvres entered the room and saw Charles's reaction, he took the letter, which the king readily accepted.

“我预料到弗朗西斯会觊觎皇帝之位，”国王说道，“但英格兰竟然会支持他？我的家人啊！”

"I expected Francis to aspire to be emperor," said the king. "But England to support him? My family!"

希耶夫尔做了个手势，不久后，一个仆人端来一大壶啤酒。议员品尝了一口啤酒后才开口说话。

Chièvres gestured, and shortly afterward a servant brought him a brimming jug of beer. The councilor savored it before speaking.

你为什么担心？

—Why are you worried?

“这是什么问题？”查尔斯说道，“法国人可能会从我手中夺走帝国！”

"What kind of question is that?" said Charles. "The French could take the Empire from me!"

——即使没有那份荣誉，你也会过得很开心。相信我，大多数男人都是如此。

—You would still be perfectly happy living without that honor. Believe me, most men do.

卡洛斯不理解他顾问的态度。

Carlos did not understand his advisor's attitude.

—你是鼓励我放弃吗？

—Do you encourage me to give it up?

“我绝不会做那种事，”希耶夫尔回答说，“但我看不出你有这种冲动。如果你有，你就会庆祝你和葡萄牙公主的婚礼，把她的嫁妆用来贿赂帝国的选帝侯，然后用剩下的钱确保杰尔玛娜在遥远的地方过上舒适的生活。”

“I would never do such a thing,” replied Chièvres. “But I don’t see in you the drive to do it. If you had it, you would be celebrating your marriage to the Portuguese princess, keeping her dowry to bribe the Electors of the Empire, and using whatever was left over to ensure Germana lived comfortably, and far away.”

—你说得对，成为皇帝的代价是极其高昂的：那就是事事服从你。

—You are right, the price of becoming emperor is exorbitant: obeying you in everything.

“你去问问任何人，他们都会给你和我一样的建议，”顾问继续说道，“对你最好的选择显而易见，除非你自尊心爆棚，否则根本不可能否认。不过，我怀疑你没那么愚蠢。如果你抗拒，那是因为你另有所图。而我只能接受，只要你满意，我就心满意足了。”

"Ask anyone, and they'll advise you as I do," the advisor continued. "What's best for you is so obvious that you'd have to summon all your pride to deny it. Though I doubt you're that foolish. If you resist, it's because you have other desires. And I'll have to accept it and be content with whatever pleases you."

议员喝完啤酒，回房休息了。卡洛斯留了下来，消化着心中的愤世嫉俗，尽管如此，他还是第一次开始怀疑，杰尔马纳会不会只是他逃避自己不想要的命运的借口。

The councilor finished his beer and retired to his room. Carlos remained, digesting his cynicism and, despite that, wondering, for the first time, if Germana wasn't just an excuse to escape a destiny he didn't want.

 

 

 

 

你想成为帝国的候选人吗？

—Do you want to be a candidate for the Empire?

沃尔西试图将自己的惊恐伪装成困惑。亨利点点头，笑容灿烂，如同开悟之人。凯瑟琳对弗朗西斯的警告深深触动了他，他违背一切理智，利用凯瑟琳的思想，妄图成为帝国的统治者。事实上，只有荒谬才能让他如此兴奋。

Wolsey tried to make his horror sound merely bewilderment. Henry nodded, his smile radiant, like that of an enlightened being. Catherine's warnings against Francis had taken hold of him, and in a defiance of all reason, he had used her ideas to see himself as master of the Empire. In truth, only absurdity filled him with enthusiasm.

“你应该感到羞愧，因为这个想法不是你提出的，”恩里克说。

"You should be ashamed that the idea didn't come from you," said Enrique.

-高度…

-Highness…

他该如何向他所效忠的人解释，他宁愿让对手而不是自己获得荣耀？他该如何既表现得忠诚，又同时维护与弗朗西斯的约定，而弗朗西斯又希望他成为教皇？

How could he explain to the one he served that he preferred glory for a rival and not for himself? How could he appear loyal while simultaneously protecting his pact with Francis, who wanted him to be Pope?

“这将给你们的资金造成巨大损失，”沃尔西继续说道。

"The cost would be immense for your coffers," Wolsey continued.

——如果不追求这个目标，我的精神将遭受沉重打击。

—Not aspiring to it would be a blow to my spirit.

沃尔西心想，正是这种孩子气的不安全感，让国王把世界看作一场球赛。亨利把所有问题都简化成一场拔河比赛，即便赢了就意味着他的垮台。如果说红衣主教从一开始就否定了国王成为帝国继承人的想法，那是因为他太了解亨利了，知道亨利太过务实，不会为了一个实际上与他格格不入、太过英国化以至于根本不会真正渴望的理想而背负债务。这位君主的野心仅限于北海和英吉利海峡，因为他真正关心的只有英格兰：在英格兰境内扩张势力，而不是境外。假装英格兰以外的世界对他有丝毫兴趣又有什么意义呢？

There it was, Wolsey thought, that childish insecurity that made the king perceive the world as a ball game. Henry reduced every issue to a tug-of-war, even if winning it meant his downfall. If the cardinal had dismissed the idea of ​​his king as a candidate for the Empire from the outset, it was because he knew him perfectly, and knew that Henry was too pragmatic to go into debt for an ideal that was, in reality, foreign to him, and too English to truly desire it. The monarch's ambitions were limited to the North Sea and the English Channel, for only England truly concerned him: to aggrandize himself within its borders, not beyond them. What was the point of pretending that what lay beyond England interested him in the slightest?

“那还不是唯一的障碍，”沃尔西继续说道，“一位英国皇帝……简直不可思议！”

"That's not the only obstacle," Wolsey continued. "An English emperor... It's inconceivable!"

——亲爱的沃尔西，如果世界想要无限地重复犯错，上帝为什么要把我带到这个世界上？

—Dear Wolsey, if the world had wanted to repeat its mistakes to infinity, why would God have brought me into it?

沃尔西察觉到亨利根本不可能被说服，于是同意了。他不得不违背对法国人的承诺，而罗马也将再次离他而去。愤怒让他独自一人待了一整天。在房间里用餐时，这位红衣主教不禁思忖，如果他效力的是一位明事理的国王，以他的谋略，又会是怎样一番景象。但他转念一想，这样的国王是否真的存在过呢？

Wolsey could sense when Henry was impossible to persuade, so he agreed. He would have to break the promise made to the Frenchman, and with that, Rome would slip away again. His anger compelled him to be alone for the rest of the day. As he dined in his chamber, the cardinal wondered what might have become of him, with his cunning, had he served a sensible king. But then he doubted that such a king had ever existed.

 

 

 

 

如果说加蒂纳拉在查理宫廷的第一天有什么让他感到愉悦的，那就是希耶夫尔见到他的反应。这位顾问久久说不出话来，好不容易开口假装同情，却也远不如往常犀利。加蒂纳拉的到来让他精疲力竭，尤其当他察觉到加蒂纳拉此行的目的时。宫廷容不下他们两人，而希耶夫尔对自己和对别人一样苛刻，他把加蒂纳拉的到来视为自己即将离去的征兆。当然，他们彼此认识已久。他们之间保持着一种客套，仿佛永远不会成为朋友，却又不得不接受。希耶夫尔认为这位意大利人的人文主义是一种虚伪的弱点。加蒂纳拉则认为查理的这位老师聪明却误入歧途，因为他缺乏原则。如果他们两人同时教导国王，他无疑会成为一位完美的君主，尽管他身上也难免存在一些矛盾之处。加蒂纳拉现在不得不逆流而上，弥补顾问对查尔斯造成的伤害。

If Gattinara enjoyed anything on his first day at Charles's court, it was Chièvres's reaction to seeing him. The advisor was speechless for a long time, and when he found his voice to feign sympathy, he wasn't as sharp as usual. The new presence drained his energy, especially when he sensed the reason for Gattinara's presence. There wasn't room for both of them at court, and being as harsh with himself as he was with others, Chièvres saw this arrival as a sign of his departure. Of course, they had known each other for some time. They treated each other with the politeness of those who will never be friends but accept it. Chièvres considered the Italian's humanism a pompous weakness. Gattinara saw Charles's tutor as a clever but misguided man, because he lacked principles. If they had both educated the king at the same time, he would undoubtedly have been the perfect ruler, albeit not without contradictions. Gattinara now had to swim against the current to repair what the advisor had done to Charles.

看到如此典型的姑母宫廷女子，国王仿佛置身其中，被她拥入怀中，回到了他熟悉的世界。一种愉悦的平静感笼罩着他，他再也无法将自己与加蒂娜拉分开。就这样，加蒂娜拉从一开始就轻而易举地赢得了查理的认可——一种感性的认可，而这种认可在所有形式的认可中最为持久。

Upon seeing someone so typical of his aunt's court, the king felt almost as if he were there, embraced by her and in the world he knew. A pleasant sense of peace enveloped him, and he could no longer separate himself from Gattinara. Thus, Gattinara effortlessly gained Charles's approval from the outset—a sentimental one, which of all forms of approval is the most enduring.

卡洛斯确信加蒂纳拉的出现是为了训斥他，于是带他骑马出去，希望独处能促使他完成任务。牲畜们允许骑乘，但它们躁动不安，因为天空阴云密布，暴风雨即将来临。

Since Carlos was convinced that Gattinara's presence there was to reprimand him, he took him for a horseback ride so that the solitude would encourage the other to carry out his mission. The animals allowed themselves to be mounted, but they were restless because the sky was charged with the electricity of a storm.

“殿下，这片土地真美啊！”加蒂纳拉一边说着，一边从马上眺望着被雨水滋润得绿意盎然的田野。

—Beautiful lands, Your Highness— said Gattinara, gazing from his horse at the fields greened by the rains.

“我爷爷怎么样了？”卡洛斯问道。

"How is my grandfather?" Carlos asked.

你必须做好准备。

—You must be prepared.

卡洛斯沉默不语，抬头望向天空。一只雄鹰的剪影掠过云层，正在捕猎。卡洛斯心想，这只动物似乎毫不费力。它别无选择，只能做它自己。没有丝毫怀疑，没有一丝愧疚。上帝多么残酷，竟以自由惩罚世人。

Carlos remained silent. He looked up at the sky. A silhouetted eagle flew against the clouds, hunting its prey. How little effort the animal seemed to make, Carlos thought. It had no choice but to be who it was. Not a doubt, not a pang of guilt. How cruel God is, punishing men with freedom.

——如果我不是呢？

—And what if I'm not?

“没有人是，”意大利人回答道。

"Nobody is," replied the Italian.

—如果我真的不想要呢？

—What if I really don't want it?

加蒂娜拉挑了挑眉。

Gattinara raised her eyebrows.

—如果你从来都不想要它，那就这样吧。如果只是在临近时刻时你才开始反感这个想法，那只是恐惧作祟。

—If you never wanted it, so be it. If it's only now, as the moment approaches, that you dislike the idea, it's just fear.

国王的马似乎替主人感到委屈，变得焦躁不安。查理安抚了它。他知道加蒂娜拉说得对。

The king's horse seemed offended on behalf of its master and became agitated. Charles calmed it down. He knew Gattinara was right.

懦夫不配享有这样的荣誉。

—A coward does not deserve such an honor.

“你管懦弱叫什么？”加蒂娜拉问道，“统治帝国就一定要懦弱吗？我敢肯定，查理曼大帝在战前也会战栗，在束手无策时也会失眠。”

"What do you call cowardice?" Gattinara asked. "Is it necessary to rule an empire? I'm sure Charlemagne trembled before battles, and lost sleep when he lacked solutions."

“我不相信你，”卡洛斯说。

"I don't believe you," said Carlos.

“陛下，世上没有英雄，只有偶尔做出英勇事迹的人。没有哪个种族天生就适合荣耀，沉着冷静，拥有永不磨灭的勇气。我们都属于同一个种族，不完美，胆怯，会怀疑，会犯错。奇妙之处在于，正是这充满缺陷的人类，能够克服自身的苦难，通过壮举将自己神化。”

"Your Majesty, there are no heroes, only men who sometimes perform heroic deeds. There is no race of human beings made for glory, unflappable and with undying courage. We all belong to the same race, the imperfect, the timid, those who doubt and err. The beautiful thing is that this paragon of flaws that is man is capable, with his miseries, of magnifying himself with feats that disguise him as a god."

查理没有回答。对方的话语中蕴含着美好和真理，国王想要接受它们，但他却不知该如何接受。

Charles did not reply. There was beauty and truth in the other man's words, and the king wanted to embrace them, but he didn't know how.

“永远要迎难而上，”加蒂纳拉继续说道，“这意味着它充满挑战。唯一不会让你感到恐惧的，是你已经掌握的事物；是你再也无法从中学习任何东西的事物。”

"Always go towards what unsettles you," Gattinara continued. "It means it holds a challenge. The only thing that doesn't frighten you is what you master; that from which you can no longer learn anything."

——我夜不能寐，担心我的命运，但更让我担忧的是，如果我犹豫不决，帝国将会面临怎样的命运。

—It keeps me awake at night what would become of me, but even more so what awaits the Empire if I hesitate to govern it.

“怀疑吧，怀疑吧！”加蒂纳拉高声说道，“只有傻瓜才会不怀疑。帝国不仅仅是一个头衔，它更是一种理念，一种旨在将人们团结在正义和真信仰之下的理念。它体现了人们对普世君主制的渴望，这种君主制能够将真正的信条和和谐带入人间。你能想象还有什么比这更美好、更忠于基督的教诲吗？而且，没有人能像你一样将它付诸实践。”

“Doubt, doubt!” Gattinara exclaimed. “Only fools don’t. The Empire is not just a title; it is an idea, one that seeks to unite men under justice and true faith. It embodies the desire for a universal monarchy that imposes the authentic creed and harmony among men. Can you imagine anything more beautiful and more faithful to the word of Christ? And no one can carry it out like you.”

“为什么？我有什么特别之处？”卡洛斯真诚地问道，并非寻求奉承。

"Why? What makes me stand out from the rest?" Carlos asked sincerely, not seeking flattery.

加蒂娜拉停下脚步，好让自己的目光与卡洛斯的目光相遇。

Gattinara stopped walking so that her eyes and Carlos's could meet.

“因为你生性善良，又如此年轻，可以从一切人和事中学习。你似乎并不渴望暴力，而且很明显，你的动力并非来自野心。此外，你的领地辽阔无垠，遍布欧洲乃至大洋彼岸。你拥有整个世界去完成这项使命。难道你想把它交给别人，交给那些毫无原则、只求胜利而别无他求的人吗？如果说有人能够实现查理曼大帝的梦想，那非你莫属。”

"Because your nature is human, and you are so young that you will learn from everything and everyone. You don't seem thirsty for violence, and ambition, it's clear, is not what drives you. Besides, your domains are immense, in Europe and across the ocean. You have an entire world in which to carry out this mission. Do you want to leave it in the hands of others, of men without principles, eager for triumph and nothing else? If anyone can embody Charlemagne's dream, it is you."

 

 

 

 

加蒂纳拉很有风度地没有提及日耳曼纳，也没有提及葡萄牙的婚礼。他知道，人天生反抗命令，只有当他认为自己是自由意志时才会做出决定，即便他可能受到了他人的影响。查理明白这个策略，但这并没有阻止他按照预想行事。他接受了帝国统帅权所带来的忧虑，这反而减轻了他的忧虑。在他的想象中，他甚至能看到查理曼颤抖的双手紧紧握成拳头，他觉得自己也能做到。他也在思考未来，以及他现在正在构建的未来。如果今天发生的事情继续下去，明天将不会多么辉煌。阿拉贡会因为前国王遗孀的婚事而拒绝他的恩宠；葡萄牙会因为没有举行婚礼而感到不满，撤回邀请并要求得到应有的回报；丑闻不仅会玷污查理在欧洲的声誉，还会让他破产，使他彻底无缘称帝。另一个选择虽然雄心勃勃，但代价高昂，而且必将蒙受损失；然而，这为他开启了新的前景，尽管他内心充满恐惧，却也不愿放弃。

Gattinara had the grace not to speak of Germana, nor of the Portuguese wedding. He knew that man, by nature, rebels against orders, and that he only decides when he believes he is doing so freely, even if he has been influenced by others. Charles understood the strategy, but that didn't stop him from acting as it predicted. Accepting the apprehension that the command of the Empire made him feel helped him to feel it less. In his imagination, he could even see Charlemagne's trembling hands clenching into a furious fist, and he saw himself capable of doing the same. He also thought about the future, and about his present building it. If what was happening today were to continue, tomorrow would not look very glorious. Aragon would deny him its favor because of the affair of the widow of its former king; Portugal, offended by the lack of a wedding, would withdraw its offer and demand what was owed to it; the scandal would tarnish Charles's reputation in Europe as well, and ruin would make it impossible for him to aspire to be emperor. The alternative was ambitious, costly in a thousand ways and would have to be paid for with losses; but it opened up a horizon for him that, however enormous his fear, he felt incapable of giving up.

 

 

 

 

自从上次和卡洛斯见面后，杰尔玛娜的肚子明显隆起了很多。现在它像一座苍白的山峰，她很喜欢凝视着它。她爱上了孕育新生命的感觉。没有什么感觉能比得上清晨醒来时涌上心头的那份平静的幸福。那时她忘记了怀孕的事，脸上洋溢着笑容，心中充满了使命感。她也感到自己被保护着，免受逆境的侵扰；无论发生什么，她都不会崩溃。所以，当卡洛斯在消失几周后宣布即将到来，而杰尔玛娜猜到这将是他最后一天时，她感到一阵悲伤，但她的悲伤就像肥皂泡一样，升起后便会破裂消失。

Germana's belly had swelled considerably since the last time she and Carlos had seen each other. Now it resembled a pale mountain that she loved to gaze at. She had fallen in love with the feeling of carrying a life. Nothing she had ever felt compared to that calm happiness that washed over her in the mornings, when upon waking she remembered nothing of her pregnancy and smiled, filled with a sense of purpose. She also felt protected from adversity; no matter what might happen, she wouldn't crumble. That's why, when Carlos announced his arrival after several weeks of absence, and Germana guessed that this day would be his last, she felt a pang of sadness, but her sorrow, like a soap bubble, rose only to burst and vanish.

卡洛斯在和她说话之前保持了一段距离。

Carlos kept his distance before speaking to her.

—如果你愿意，你可以嫁给勃兰登堡侯爵。

—You will marry the Marquis of Brandenburg, if you please.

如果几个月前有人告诉她这就是她的命运，她一定会欣喜若狂。自那时起，除了她腹中孕育着一个生命之外，唯一改变的就是她爱上了卡洛斯。她明白，这份感情，无论多么美好，都无法彻底改变她对人生的期待。她也无意成为国王的绊脚石。他肩负着一项使命，这段恋情无权危及。她无法承受为一段并非伟大的爱情——仅仅是一段足以让她沉醉其中，却又不足以改变两人未来的爱情——而扰乱卡洛斯命运的罪恶感。

If months ago someone had told her that this was her destiny, she would have celebrated. The only thing that had changed since then, besides the fact that she now carried a being within her, was that she had come to love Carlos. And she knew that this emotion, however beautiful, couldn't completely alter what she expected from life. Nor did she intend to become the king's downfall. He had a mission that this romance had no right to jeopardize. She wouldn't have been able to live with the guilt of disrupting Carlos's destiny for something that wasn't even a great love, but simply a love, good enough to have enjoyed more than she should have, but not so good as to warrant altering both their futures.

陛下，我喜欢那个地方。

—I like that destination, Your Majesty.

两人都点了点头。没什么可说的了。他们为自己的务实感到自豪，这并非毫无道理，因为即使分隔两地，他们依然彼此渴望，彼此思念。杰尔玛娜向他鞠了一躬：她接受了他们终将再次成为陌生人的事实。只有当他们彻底放弃了对爱情的希望时，才涌起一丝怀旧之情。他们彼此微笑，但眼中却闪烁着悲伤的光芒。

They both nodded. There was little more to say. They were proud of their pragmatism, which was not without merit, for they still desired each other and longed for each other even when they were apart. Germana bowed to him: she accepted that they would once again be strangers. Only then, when they had already given up hope of their love, did they feel nostalgia. They smiled at each other, but sadness shone through their eyes.

“跟我一起洗澡吧。摸摸我的肚子。让我们最后一次感受彼此的肌肤。”杰尔马纳说道。

—Bath with me. Touch my belly. Let's feel our skin one last time —Germana said.

于是，他们就这样做了。依旧是沉默，如同他们最美好的日子，海水将他们与现实隔绝开来，肌肤轻轻相触，卡洛斯的手抚摸着她的腹部，感受着那鲜活的生命——那是他第一次亲手创造，一件小小的神圣之作。在最后的几个小时里，只有幸福。

And so they did. Again in silence, as in their best days, the water isolating them from reality, their skin brushing against each other, Carlos's hand on her belly, feeling the life within, which was, for the first time, his own creation, a small divine work. There was only happiness in those last hours together.

离开杰尔马纳的住所时，卡洛斯像个孩子一样哭了起来。

When he left Germana's residence, Carlos cried like a child.

 

 

 

 

1519年1月12日，在帝国都城韦尔斯，马克西米利安一世的御医兼占星师坦斯特特博士发现皇帝并未前来赴约午餐，这让他感到十分意外。坦斯特特博士原本打算在午餐时就木星对路德教问题的影响以及皇帝的胆结石病情做出一些有利的预测。他来到皇帝的寝宫，多次宣告自己的到来。无人回应，他便走了进去。马克西米利安一世似乎正在沉睡。坦斯特特博士轻轻触碰他，试图唤醒他，但皇帝却猛然惊醒，立刻感受到了死亡的气息。坦斯特特博士划了个十字，在告知皇帝死讯之前，他沉思了一会儿。眼前这具冰冷的躯体，或许曾是他那个时代最有权势的人。这双如今已无法使用的双手，曾经挥舞过利剑——尽管有人说只是短暂的；这双眼睛曾如饥似渴地阅读书籍；这张嘴曾缔结过改变欧洲历史进程的联姻——例如他的儿子菲利普与阿拉贡的胡安娜的联姻；他精通六种语言，酷爱音乐；他的双臂曾饱经狩猎和战斗的摧残。而如今，他的内心却一片寂静，空无一物；一只害虫可以潜入他的寝宫，爬上床铺，将这位伟人吞噬殆尽，而他却毫无抵抗之力。坦斯特特离开了寝宫，径直走向议事厅，皇帝的侍从们都屏息凝神地侍奉着他。

On January 12, 1519, in the imperial city of Wels, Dr. Tannstetter, physician and astrologer to Maximilian I, was surprised when the emperor failed to appear for lunch, at which the doctor intended to offer favorable predictions regarding Jupiter's influence on the Lutheran question and the emperor's gallstones. He went to the imperial chamber and announced his arrival several times. Receiving no response, he entered. Maximilian I appeared to be asleep. Tannstetter touched him to awaken him, but the emperor startled, having immediately sensed the touch of death. The physician crossed himself and, before delivering the news, allowed himself a moment to philosophize. This block of cold flesh before him had perhaps been the most powerful man of his time. These hands, now useless, had wielded a sword—though only briefly, some said; these eyes had devoured books; That mouth had decreed marriages that had changed the course of Europe—like that of his son Philip and Joanna of Aragon; his mind had learned six languages ​​and delighted in music; his arms had been strained in hunts and battles. And now silence, nothingness, dwelt within him; a vermin could enter the bedchamber, climb onto the bed, and devour the great man without him offering any resistance. Tannstetter left the bedchamber and went straight to the council chamber, where the emperor's men fell silent to attend to him.

——让钟声响起吧。帝国已成孤儿。

—Let the bells ring. The Empire has been orphaned.

 

 

 

 

查理在阿拉贡待了几天后，才得知祖父去世的消息。议会将在巴塞罗那召开，不久之后便会举行。这位君主当时只统治卡斯蒂利亚，阿拉贡人对他的不信任甚至超过了卡斯蒂利亚人，但找到替代者似乎难上加难，尤其是在他的兄弟费尔南多无法指望他支持的情况下。接下来必然会是一场辩论和各种要求，国王在继承王位之前，无论真心与否，都不得不做出让步，但实际上，没有人怀疑最终的结果。真正充满不确定性的，是帝国的归属问题。

Charles had been in Aragon for several days when news of his grandfather's death reached him. The Cortes, to be held in Barcelona, ​​would begin shortly. The monarch still only ruled in Castile, and the Aragonese distrusted him more than the Castilians, but finding an alternative seemed too arduous, especially now that his brother Ferdinand could not be counted on for the cause. Debates and demands would follow, and the king would have to concede, sincerely or not, before assuming the crown of the kingdom, but deep down no one doubted that this would be the case. The uncertainty, and a colossal one at that, was reserved for the question of the Empire.

人们为马克西米利安的灵魂举行了弥撒。国王和他的随从祈祷上帝接纳皇帝，但这场庄严的仪式所带来的远不止于此。希耶夫尔反思着自己在宫廷中的衰落，加蒂娜拉已然成为掌权的宰相，查理的这一决定令这位顾问心碎，尽管他早有预料。哈德良和加蒂娜拉的地位并未受到威胁，他们思考着国王为赢得帝国必须克服的重重障碍——支付款项、外交斡旋、应对不择手段的竞争对手、确保西班牙的安全（西班牙当时仍不愿彻底投降）——而查理的目光凝视着祭坛上的基督像，感到一阵强烈的眩晕，但同时也第一次感受到了一种伟大的召唤，一种超越他自身的力量，将问题转化为考验，将恐惧转化为克服困难的动力。毫无疑问，这是一种与理性无关的状态；他接受了命运的安排，相信这会让他变得比现在更好。莱昂诺尔在他身边，卡洛斯注意到她含着泪在祈祷。

A mass was celebrated for the soul of Maximilian. The king and his entourage prayed that the emperor would be received by God, but the solemnity of the occasion yielded much more than that. Chièvres reflected on his decline at court, where Gattinara already held sway as chancellor, a decision by Charles that devastated the advisor, however much he had anticipated it. Hadrian and Gattinara, whose positions were not threatened, considered the obstacles the king would have to overcome to win the Empire—the payments, the diplomacy, the unscrupulous rivals, securing that Spain which still resisted surrendering completely—and Charles, his eyes fixed on the Christ on the altar, felt a fierce vertigo, but also, for the first time, the call of greatness, a kind of vigor that transcended him and transformed problems into trials and fears into energy to overcome them. Undoubtedly, it was a state of being that had little to do with rationality; The acceptance of a destiny that would make him better than he was now. Leonor was by his side, and Carlos noticed that she was praying through her tears.

 

 

 

 

弥撒结束后，举行了午宴。午宴后，国王想方设法与妹妹单独相处。埃莉诺很高兴，她确信自己终于能得到哥哥的许可，返回弗兰德斯。

After Mass, a luncheon was held, after which the king sought a way to be alone with his sister. Eleanor was pleased; she was certain that she would finally receive permission from her brother to return to Flanders.

—我将把你的手献给葡萄牙国王。

—I am going to offer your hand to the King of the Portuguese.

莱昂诺尔发现自己脸色苍白。空气变得令人窒息，仿佛突然凝固了一般。

Leonor noticed she was losing color. The air became unbreathable, as if it had suddenly turned solid.

——卡洛斯继续说道——这样的结合将免除我们对贵国的债务，并给予您应得的尊严；王位所带来的尊严。

—That union would forgive our debt to your kingdom —Carlos continued—, and would give you the dignity you deserve; the dignity that comes with the throne.

莱昂诺尔的胸膛剧烈起伏，越来越快，她睁大的眼睛直直地盯着脚下的地面，因为她感觉脚下的土地正在裂开。曼努埃尔国王究竟有多老？或许比她大三十岁。一个素未谋面的老人。统治着一个她毫无兴趣的王国。即便他年轻貌美，拥有无数美德，她所感受到的恐惧也丝毫不会改变，因为除了伯爵之外，其他人对她而言都毫无意义。

Leonor's chest rose and fell faster and faster, and her wide-open eyes remained fixed on the ground at her feet, for she felt the earth opening up beneath them. King Manuel was, how much older? Thirty years older than she was, perhaps. An unknown old man. Ruler of a kingdom that held no interest for her. And even if he had been young and possessed a thousand virtues, her horror would have been the same, for anyone other than the count had no meaning in her life.

“我爱上了另一个男人！你应该娶他的女儿！”

"I love another man! You're the one who should marry his daughter!"

但查理与杰玛娜分离后，心中充满悲伤，甚至无法忍受看到其他女人。他无法带着这种忧郁的心情结婚，因为这会让他对妻子产生怨恨，而妻子是他们共同生活的基石，这只会让他们永远痛苦。他知道这样的决定意味着让情感左右自己的选择，但他想相信这并非他拒绝迎娶伊莎贝尔的唯一原因。他告诉自己，在如此重要的事上屈从于臣民的决定有失身份，他必须以某种方式在他们面前展现自己的独立性。为了妹妹的未来，为了像他自己被迫那样强行让她摆脱痛苦，最终册封她为王后，这也足以成为他唯一的选择。

But Charles's heart, after parting from Germana, was in mourning, and the king couldn't bear even the sight of another woman. He couldn't marry with that melancholy within him, because it would turn into anger toward his wife, and since she was the cornerstone of their life together, it could only make them both unhappy, forever. He knew that such a decision meant letting his feelings dictate his choice, and he wanted to believe that wasn't the only reason for refusing to marry Isabel. He told himself that submitting to the decision of his subjects in a matter of such importance was unbecoming of his rank, and that he had to assert his independence in their eyes somehow. Settle his sister's future, forcibly removing her from heartbreak, as he himself had been compelled to do, and eventually bestowing upon her the title of queen, was also motivation enough for this to be the solution and no other.

“我恨你，”莱昂诺尔说，然后她就没再说话了。

—I hate you —said Leonor, and she said no more.

卡洛斯并没有预料到会有其他反应。他任由妹妹哭着走开，自己则一动不动，沉默不语，默默承受着这份新的愧疚，它与他之前背负的诸多愧疚交织在一起。

Carlos hadn't expected any other reaction. He let his sister walk away crying, and he remained motionless, silent, accepting this new guilt that added to so many others.

 

 

 

 

在葡萄牙宫廷，查理的提议引起了人们的惊讶和复杂的情绪。说实话，解除国王的丧偶之痛令所有人，包括查理本人，都感到高兴，但这桩婚事也带有某种安慰的意味，同时也意味着对伊莎贝拉的拒绝。然而，伊莎贝拉却鼓励父亲接受埃莉诺为妻。国王无需进一步劝说便欣然同意，但他难以理解女儿为何如此轻易地接受自己的抱负就这样破灭。

At the Portuguese court, Charles's offer was met with surprise and mixed feelings. To be honest, alleviating the king's widowhood pleased everyone, including Charles himself, but the proposed marriage held a sense of consolation and a rejection of Isabella. She, however, encouraged her father to accept Eleanor as his wife. The king needed no further convincing, but he struggled to understand how his daughter could so readily accept seeing her ambition thwarted in this way.

我知道你多么渴望嫁给查尔斯。

—I know how much you longed to marry Charles.

伊莎贝尔对父亲笑了笑，脸上没有一丝恼怒。

Isabel smiled at her father. There was no trace of annoyance in her.

那些愿望丝毫未变。我也不会接受它们无法实现的现实。只有当上帝带我到他身边，或者他带走他自己时，我才会放弃那份命运。我们还活着吗？如果还活着，那就只剩下等待了；因为该发生的，终究会发生。

—Those desires haven't changed one iota. Nor will I accept that they don't become reality. Only if God were to take me to his side, or if he were to take him, would I renounce that destiny. Are we still alive? Then all that remains is to wait; because what must be, will be.

 

 

 

 

杰尔玛娜生了个女儿。仿佛接受了在她与阿拉贡的费尔南多结婚期间乃至婚后一直萦绕在她心头的幽灵，她给女儿取名为伊莎贝拉。当她第一次将女儿抱在怀里，看到那双懵懂无知的眼睛、稚嫩的五官和无助的神情时，她感到前所未有的强大。她对查理的思念也渐渐消散，因为他能给予她的一切都无法与他已经给予她的相比。

Germana gave birth to a girl. As if accepting the ghost that had haunted her during her marriage to Ferdinand of Aragon and even afterward, she named her Isabella. The moment she held her in her arms for the first time and saw those eyes that didn't yet know how to see, those tiny features and that helplessness, she felt stronger than ever. And the longing she still harbored for Charles faded, because nothing he could give her would be worth more than what he had already given her.

或许没有人能理解她们为何相爱，但对杰尔玛娜来说，一切都已明了。她抱着伊莎贝尔沉沉睡去，这是她许久以来第一次睡得如此安稳，无需再跋涉沙漠。

Perhaps no one would ever understand why they had loved each other, but for Germana there was no longer any doubt. With Isabel in her arms, she fell asleep, and for the first time in a long time, her sleep was peaceful, and there was no desert to traverse.

4

4

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

数百颗宝石；八块金牌；镶嵌珍珠；两侧分别刻有耶稣基督和戴维王、所罗门王、希西家王的画像；正面是十字架。查理曾见过祖父马克西米利安头上的这顶皇冠，他记得那皇冠质朴而精美，仿佛此前从未有过皇冠，此后也绝无仅有。据说这顶皇冠是六个世纪前打造的，也就是查理曼大帝被拥立为第一位神圣罗马帝国皇帝两个世纪之后。

Hundreds of precious stones; eight gold plaques; set pearls; the image of Jesus Christ and those of Kings David, Solomon, and Hezekiah on its sides; a cross on the front. Charles had once seen the imperial crown on the head of his grandfather Maximilian and remembered it as beautifully rustic, as if no crowns had existed before it and none would ever exist again. They said it had been crafted six centuries earlier, two centuries after Charlemagne was proclaimed the first Holy Roman Emperor.

对查理而言，历史是真理的领域。十六世纪动荡不安，迷失方向，飞速向前发展，但究竟朝着何方？如同所有变革似乎迫在眉睫的时代一样，有些人义无反顾地投身未知，为革命感恩戴德；而另一些人则因眩晕而心生疑虑，对可能最终空洞无物的创新持怀疑态度，转而寻求回归一个理想化远胜于现实的过去。马克西米利安皇帝经常向他的孙子讲述那些始终以勇气、正义和信仰为指引的古人；他们正直不阿，既勇敢又谦逊，没有任何理由违背自己的原则：骑士。效仿他们是未来的唯一希望，因为他们所代表的理想蕴含着人类的本质和真理。唯有高贵、对基督的信仰和勇气，才能孕育出普世的和谐。孩提时代，查理将这些教义视为令人着迷的教条，他常常幻想自己身披中世纪盔甲，骑着骏马，置身于亚瑟王的传奇世界，双目闪亮，随时准备为自己的使命献身。然而，时间，以及希耶夫尔那卑鄙狡诈的手段，将他的憧憬扭曲成了一个与现实格格不入的乌托邦，一个需要策略、自私和猜忌的乌托邦。

For Charles, History was the realm of truth. The 16th century was restless and disoriented, advancing relentlessly; but toward what? And as in all eras where change seems imminent, while some men plunged into the unknown and gave thanks for the revolution, others, gripped by vertigo, skeptical of a novelty that could well prove empty, sought a return to a past that was more ideal than reality. Emperor Maximilian often spoke to his grandson of men of old who were always guided by courage, justice, and faith; incorruptible men, as bold as they were humble, and for whom there was no excuse for ignoring their principles: the knights. Emulating them was the only hope for the future, because in that ideal they represented resided the essence of man, his truth. Only from nobility, faith in Christ, and courage could universal harmony arise. As a child, Charles received these teachings as a fascinating dogma, and he liked to dream of himself on horseback, clad in medieval armor, in an Arthurian setting, his eyes shining, ready to sacrifice himself for what he was destined to be.
