在驶近弗兰德斯的船上，查尔斯感到潮湿的木板像沙滩上的沙子一样在他脚下陷下去。周围的景象似曾相识：狂风拍打着船身，鸟儿在水面上飞翔，远处是他一直视为家园的绿色土地。他几乎不易察觉地解开了衬衫的两颗纽扣，任由寒冷袭来，唤起了他童年的回忆。寒冷触碰到皮肤的那一刻，让他脊背一阵发凉。那是过去的寒冷，迎接着一个如今只属于未来的自己。他即将回归，但很快又要踏上征程，去夺取命运和雅各布·富格尔的财富为他预留的王位。然而，他心中却既没有喜悦，也没有温暖。他原本希望这次航行能让他感到轻松自在，离开卡斯蒂利亚也能让他远离那里的威胁，甚至不会再为英国、法国和罗马因他即将集结的强大力量而心生畏惧、结盟对抗他的传言所困扰。大海本应让他免受这些忧虑，但令他沮丧的是，大海反而加剧了他的焦虑，船身的摇晃似乎也反映了同样的焦虑：他对自身信心的怀疑。

On the deck of the ship approaching Flanders, Charles felt the damp wood sink beneath his feet like beach sand. Around him, the scene was familiar: the wind whipping against the ship's hull, birds descending on the water, and in the distance, the green land he had long considered home. With an almost imperceptible gesture, he unbuttoned two buttons of his shirt, surrendering to the cold that brought back memories of childhood. The touch of it on his skin sent a shiver down his spine. It was the cold of the past greeting one who was now only the future. He was returning, but soon to embark on the journey to claim the throne that fate and Jakob Fugger's wealth had reserved for him. Yet, he lacked both joy and warmth. He had hoped the voyage would instill in him a sense of ease, that by leaving Castile he would also distance himself from its threats, and that he wouldn't even be troubled by the rumor that England, France, and Rome, frightened by the power he was about to amass, would ally against him. Certainly, the sea should have shielded him from such anxieties, but to his dismay, it intensified them, and the ship's rolling seemed to reflect the same anxieties: those of his own confidence.

水手们在进行某种仪式时突然互相叫喊，喧闹和混乱遵循着某种既定的模式。他们正驶向港口。

The deckhands began shouting to each other in the middle of a ritual where noise and disorder followed a studied pattern. They were approaching the port.

查尔斯降落在弗兰德斯时，抬头仰望，寻找上帝的踪迹。然而，他看到的只有一片灰蒙蒙的天空。这再次提醒他，在他身后，卡斯蒂利亚正燃起熊熊烈火。

When he landed in Flanders, Charles looked up, searching for God. But all he saw above him was a gray, ashen sky. This reminded him once again that, behind him, Castile was burning.

 

 

 

 

查理返回家乡时，托莱多的街道上响起了震耳欲聋的呐喊声。起义始于数日前，当时民众阻止了前往拉科鲁尼亚参加国王召集的卡斯蒂利亚议会的队伍。当他们经过大教堂时，帕迪利亚和他的部下乘坐的马匹受惊，嘶鸣声令试图阻拦他们的民众噤若寒蝉。所有人都僵住了，被这紧张的气氛所震撼。帕迪利亚骄傲地看着挡在他面前的人们：他们拒绝让自己的代表向君主下跪。他心想，毫无疑问，这是一群值得他们为之奋斗的人民。他们如此勇敢，似乎注定要组成一支如此强大的军队。帕迪利亚下马，加入到人群中。他被形形色色的人们簇拥着，他们因共同的愤怒而团结在一起。王国并非仅仅是君主和他的臣民。每个地区都有自己的意志，即使它们都属于同一个王冠。这些是“社群”，是超越君主和臣民的灵魂集合体。他们是组成每个单位的成千上万的人，如今他们提高嗓门，却惊讶于自己声音的庄严。他们是平民百姓。

As Charles returned home, shouts filled the streets of Toledo. The insurrection had begun days earlier, when the people stopped those marching to the Castilian Cortes convened by the king in A Coruña. As they passed the cathedral, the horses carrying Padilla and his men spooked, and their neighing silenced the crowd trying to halt them. Everyone froze, gripped by the gravity of the moment. Padilla proudly observed those who blocked his path: they refused to allow their representatives to kneel before the monarch. Undoubtedly, this was a people worthy of their cause, he thought. A people so brave they seemed destined to form an army of such stature. Padilla dismounted and joined them. He surrounded himself with people of all stripes, united by their shared rage. The kingdom was not simply a sovereign and his subjects. Each region had its own will, even though they all belonged to the same crown. These were the Communities, a sum of souls beyond a governor and his subjects. They were the thousands of men who made up each one, and who, now that they raised their voices, were surprised by how grave they sounded. They were the commoners.

他们先是迫使城邦当局投降，然后帕迪利亚和他的部下抬起头来，因为君主权力的最后堡垒——阿尔卡萨宫——就在那里。没有它，这场起义的荣耀将是不完整的。门口的守卫抵抗比预想的要弱。他们被涌来的人群吓坏了，扔掉武器，服从了恐惧而非命令。他们很快就被人群淹没。有些人祝贺他们的决心，拥抱他们，亲吻他们的额头；另一些人则朝他们吐口水，撕扯他们的衣服，不愿接受流血的机会已经错失的事实。

First, they forced the city authorities to capitulate, and then Padilla and his men looked up, for the last bastion of the monarch's power remained: the Alcázar. Without it, the glory of the revolt would be incomplete. The guards at the entrance offered less resistance than expected. Frightened by the rushing crowd, they threw their weapons to the ground, obeying their fear rather than orders. They were soon swallowed up by the throng. Some congratulated them on their resolve, embracing them and kissing their foreheads; others spat on them and tore at their clothes, refusing to accept that the opportunity to shed blood had been lost.

殿内，法官也未作任何抵抗。帕迪利亚冲进大厅，高声斥责国王。他的部下欢呼雀跃，喊声不绝于耳。起义的攻势势不可挡。帕迪利亚回想起之前民众的消极被动，如今这种情绪已荡然无存。他再也没有时间去思考，那种曾经抑制住他怒火的思考。毫无疑问，是时候采取激烈的行动，鼓起勇气，挥舞利剑了。

Inside, the magistrate also offered no resistance. Padilla entered the hall and shouted against the king. His men cheered him, and the shouting continued. The advances of the revolt were relentless. Padilla recalled the frustration he had felt at the people's passivity, and how not a drop of it remained now. There was no longer room for reflection, the kind that had held back his anger. Undoubtedly, the moment for feverish action, for courage, for the sword, had arrived.

很快，叛乱蔓延至整个卡斯蒂利亚。总督们一个接一个地倒在了叛军手中。暴行毫不留情。有人被绞死，有人被斩首。在民众眼中，叛军就是国王的化身，迫使他们投降是国王走向衰落的开端。资产阶级和下层贵族逐渐掌控了政权。那些拿起武器的人交换着紧张的眼神。他们的眼神表明，这是他们应该做的，他们也深知自己是勇敢的。尽管民众很少反抗君主。这样做意味着推翻一条自古以来就被奉为神圣的律法。国王的顾问们说，上帝让查理成为王国的统治者并非偶然。但他们甚至不惧质疑上帝的旨意：他们自己的意志更加坚定。骄傲和对真理的笃信，让他们觉得自己成了英雄。

Soon, the revolt spread throughout Castile. Governors fell one by one to the rebels. No cruelty was spared. Some were hanged, others put to the sword. To the people, they were the personification of the king, and forcing them to capitulate was the starting point for his own downfall. The bourgeoisie and the lower nobility gradually seized control. Those who took up arms exchanged nervous glances. Their eyes declared it was the right thing to do, and they knew themselves to be brave. Although the people rarely rebelled against their monarchs. To do so meant overturning an almost divine law that had been obeyed since the beginning of time. Not for nothing, the king's advisors said, had Providence placed Charles at the head of the kingdom. But they were not even intimidated by questioning God's will: their own weighed more heavily. Pride and the certainty that truth was on their side were turning them, they told themselves, into heroes.

 

 

 

 

在卡斯蒂利亚，君主的未来还悬于几盏昏暗的灯光之下；而在梅赫伦，宫殿的脚手架上，所有人都驻足观看皇家队伍经过。查尔斯探出马车窗外，不禁将记忆中那座古老的宫殿与正在进行的翻修工程进行比较。他离开那里的时间并不长，如今却已截然不同。

While in Castile the monarch's future hung by a few dim lights, in Mechelen, from the palace scaffolding, everyone stopped to watch the royal procession pass by. Leaning out of the carriage window, Charles couldn't stop comparing the memory of the old building with the renovations that were taking place. It hadn't been that long since he had left that place, and already it was different.

奥地利的玛格丽特出来迎接他。她的眼神闪烁着光芒，如同妻子迎接一位从战争中幸存下来的丈夫一般。他不由自主地加快脚步迎上去。姑姑和侄子紧紧相拥，这是他们都渴望已久的。直到他闻到她身上的香气，感受到玛格丽特雪白的肌肤，查尔斯才真正感到自己回到了家。

Margaret of Austria came out to greet him. Her eyes shone like those of a wife welcoming a husband who has survived the war. He couldn't help but quicken his pace to meet her. Aunt and nephew embraced in the hug they had both longed for. It wasn't until he caught a whiff of her scent and felt the touch of Margaret's snow-white skin that Charles truly felt he was home.

“你必须把一切都告诉我。你的信我读过很多遍了，但我还是想亲耳听到你讲述所有的故事，”玛格丽塔对她说。

"You have to tell me everything. I've read your letters over and over, but I want to hear all the stories coming from your lips," Margarita told her.

卡洛斯抚摸着他姑妈的头发，想象着在自己背后，希耶夫斯还在咒骂那个女人对他的影响。

Carlos stroked his aunt's hair, imagining that, behind his back, Chièvres was still cursing the influence that woman had over him.

“在你帮我做准备工作的这段时间里，会有时间做这件事的。前提是，我不用再回卡斯蒂利亚了。”查尔斯回答道。

"There will be time for that while you help me with the preparations. That is, if I don't have to leave again for Castile," replied Charles.

玛格丽塔没有追问他为何提前离开梅赫伦。她自幼便认识这个年轻人，即便他如今即将以皇帝的身份归来，她也知道他内心深处那份看似永恒的平静正被某种东西所扰乱；这种不安远不止于她曾提议让弟弟统治帝国。说实话，她站在他这边。再次见到他的脸庞，就足以让她确信这一点。在他们身后，尘封于往事的迷雾之中，是数月艰苦卓绝的谈判、战略博弈、政治角力、以及众多重要人物和丰厚承诺。而摆在眼前的，唯有为查理加冕马克西米利安王冠，让他载入史册，继承祖父的遗志。

Margarita didn't ask about the reasons that might have taken him away from Mechelen prematurely. She had known the young man since childhood, and even though he was now returning as the soon-to-be emperor, she knew that something was disturbing the eternal calm in which he seemed to live; a disquiet that went beyond the fact that she herself had proposed her brother to rule the Empire. Truthfully, she was on his side. Seeing his face again had been enough to know that for certain. Behind them, buried in the mists of the past, lay the months of arduous negotiations, of strategy and politics, of important names and promises of riches. Ahead, all that remained was to invest Charles with the crown of Maximilian and let him pass into history, upholding his grandfather's legacy.

陛下，渡河之旅如何？

—How was the crossing, Your Majesty?

直到那一刻，费尔南多才被国王注意到，就像一只融入周围环境的动物，等待着攻击猎物的时机。

Fernando had gone unnoticed by the king until that moment, like an animal that blended into its surroundings waiting for the moment to attack its prey.

卡洛斯沉默了片刻才回答。他仔细端详着哥哥的脸：那张脸像戴着一副铁面具，掩藏着难以言喻的复杂情感。在船上，他想了很多事情，但很久没有认真思考过该如何应对这明显带有背叛意味的举动了。

Carlos took a while to answer. He studied his brother's face: it resembled an iron mask concealing who knew what feelings. He had thought about many things on board the ship, but it had been a while since he had reflected on how he was going to react to what he was certain had been a hint of betrayal.

“这很艰难，”卡洛斯回答说，“但能来到这里，一切都值得。我只希望你不要想念卡斯蒂利亚。”

"It's tough," Carlos replied, "but being here makes it all worthwhile. I just hope you don't miss Castile."

“我怀念的不过是掌控权力而已，兄弟，”费尔南多回答道。争论比预想的来得更快。“你是名正言顺的国王，”费尔南多继续说道，“但我从小接受的教育不是要待在这高墙之内，享受众人的瞩目。”

“I miss it no more than wielding some power, brother,” Fernando replied. The argument had started sooner than expected. “You are the rightful king,” Fernando continued, “but I wasn’t raised to stay within these walls, receiving attention.”

“我本人就是在那样的环境下长大的，也曾受到过这些人的照顾，”查尔斯说。“对国王有益的，对你也可能有益。”

—I myself grew up in that way and received care from these people— said Charles. —What was good for a king can be good for you.

一股怒火猛烈地抽向费尔南多。

A whiplash of fury lashed out at Fernando.

“你为什么要急着回卡斯蒂利亚？”他恶狠狠地问道。

"Why would you be rushing back to Castile?" he asked maliciously.

一片寂静。卡洛斯咬紧牙关。这时，希耶夫斯带着轻蔑的冷笑走上前去。

There was silence. Carlos gritted his teeth. Chièvres then stepped forward with a sneer of contempt.

西班牙人不服从命令。

—The Spanish are disobedient.

“他们要求什么？”玛格丽塔问道。

"What are they demanding?" Margarita asked.

“一切皆有可能，又仿佛什么都不是，”希耶夫尔继续说道。“我开始觉得，无缘无故地抱怨是那个王国固有的性格，一种幼稚的不忠……”

"Everything and nothing," Chièvres continued. "I'm beginning to think that complaining for its own sake is inherent in the character of that kingdom, a childish disloyalty..."

“荒谬！”费尔南多打断道，“他们已经无数次展现了忠诚。他们对待我们的祖辈就是如此。这就是他们回报祖辈良好治理的方式。”

"Absurd!" Fernando interrupted. "They have demonstrated loyalty on countless occasions. They did so with our grandparents. That's how they rewarded their good governance."

卡洛斯强烈地感受到了这番话的讽刺，打破了沉默。

Carlos felt the barb strongly enough to end his silence.

—如果你想冒犯我，我会原谅你。批评是缺乏权威者的习惯，更是那些渴望权威却未能如愿的人的习惯。

—If you seek to offend me, I forgive you. Criticism is the habit of those who lack authority, and even more so of those who aspire to it without achieving it.

费尔南多正要回答，却注意到玛格丽塔正气喘吁吁地看着这场决斗；于是他决定离开房间。片刻的沉默，反而加剧了气氛的尴尬。

Fernando was about to answer when he noticed Margarita, who was watching the duel with labored breathing; then he decided to leave the room. For a moment no one spoke, but the silence only heightened the discomfort.

“加蒂娜拉呢？她不是跟你一起来的吗？”玛格丽塔问道。

"And Gattinara? Didn't she come with you?" Margarita asked.

 

 

 

 

梅尔库里诺·加蒂纳拉亲吻了渔夫戒指，这枚戒指曾被用来签署一些可能引发欧洲信仰分裂的决定。利奥十世脸上带着从清晨就已显露的疲惫，他邀请这位皮埃蒙特人坐下休息，以缓解房间里的闷热。

Mercurino Gattinara kissed the Fisherman's Ring, the same one used to sign decisions that could then provoke a schism in the faith of Europe. Leo X, his face showing the fatigue that had marked him since early morning, invited the Piedmontese to sit down and rest from the heat that filled the room.

查理的使者抵达罗马，其使命是寻求教皇的支持，以对抗法英两国之间正在酝酿的威胁性联盟；很可能，有人已经将这一意图告知了教皇。他们刚一落座，利奥十世便擦了擦额头的汗，刻意拖延着顾问此行的目的。他先是谈起了圣彼得大教堂的工程以及负责监督的建筑师。他着重强调了这座宏伟的建筑，它将成为捍卫上帝圣言的最坚固堡垒。他疲惫地重复道，它的墙壁必须像罗马教会本身一样坚固。然后，他停下来擦了擦额头上滴落的汗珠，开始逐一列举他为教皇寓所委托创作的绘画和挂毯。他念出了每一位曾在此创作的大师的名字，从拉斐尔到那位给他留下深刻印象的年轻画家切利尼。加蒂纳拉开始对教皇的态度感到绝望。利奥十世，一个体态臃肿却举止温文尔雅的庞然大物，深知无人敢打断他，于是便尽情展现自己夸张的姿态，故意让对方显得不耐烦，以此削弱对方的信心。直到他注意到查理的顾问脸上开始显露出紧张的神色，他才拖着脚步走到桌前，找到一把小钥匙，转动钥匙打开一个抽屉，抽屉的木门无声地滑开。他从抽屉里取出一份文件。

Charles's envoy had arrived in Rome with the mission of seeking the Pope's support against the threatening alliances brewing between France and England; an intention that, in all likelihood, someone had already made known to him. As soon as they were seated, Leo X wiped the sweat from his brow and painstakingly delayed the conversation the advisor had come seeking. First, he spoke of the works at St. Peter's and the architect overseeing them. He emphasized the impressive structure, which would stand as the most formidable bastion conceived to defend the Word of God. Its walls, he repeated wearily, had to be as solid as the Church of Rome itself. Then he paused to wipe the sweat trickling from the folds of his forehead and proceeded to list, one by one, the paintings and tapestries he continued to commission for the papal apartments. He recited the names of each and every master who had passed through there, from Raphael to that young Cellini who had impressed him so much. Gattinara was beginning to despair at the Pope's attitude. Leo X, a mountain of fat and gentle manners, knew that no one would dare interrupt him and reveled in his theatrical demeanor, letting impatience overwhelm his interlocutor in order to weaken him. Only when he noticed that nerves were beginning to show on the face of Charles's advisor did he drag his feet to the desk and, after obtaining a tiny key, turned it to a drawer whose wood slid silently open. From it he took out a file.

儿子，你对印刷机有什么看法？你不认为所有的印刷机，毫无例外，都应该由罗马控制吗？

—What is your opinion on printing presses, son? Don't you agree that all of them, without exception, should be controlled by Rome?

“尊者的目光能延伸到那么远吗？”加蒂纳拉回答道，她不确定谈话会走向何方。

"Can His Holiness's eyes reach that far?" Gattinara replied, unsure where the conversation might be headed.

——它们必须覆盖上帝事业的每一个角落。如果落入坏人之手，这些机器就会成为邪恶的工具，用来传播亵渎神明的言论。

—They must reach every corner of God's work. In the wrong hands, these machines become tools of evil to spread his blasphemies.

教皇清了清嗓子，然后才开始读纸上的内容。当他看到上面的文字时，感到一阵恶心。

The Pope cleared his throat before reading what was written on the paper. When he looked at the text, he felt nauseous.

 

 

基督教世界的最高统治者过着如此奢靡的生活，任何君王都无法与之匹敌，这令人震惊。他自诩至圣，却比世人更加世俗。如果上帝像过去毁灭索多玛和蛾摩拉那样，降下硫磺和地狱之火，将罗马投入深渊，也并不奇怪。既然教皇的一切都与基督所建立的教义背道而驰，那么他难道不是敌基督吗？

It is appalling to see the supreme lord of Christendom living in such luxury that no king can match it. He calls himself most holy, yet he is more worldly than the world itself. It would not be surprising if God were to rain down sulfur and infernal fire and plunge Rome into the abyss, as He did with Sodom and Gomorrah in times past. Since his entire being, work, and activity are directed against what Christ established, might the Pope not be the Antichrist?

 

 

朗读结束后，一片寂静，亵渎之语在房间里回荡。加蒂纳拉熟知路德的文本，但亲耳听到教皇的声音，就在梵蒂冈，还是让他脊背发凉。他划了个十字。

The silence that followed the reading made the blasphemies echo through the room. Gattinara knew Luther's text, but hearing it from the Pope's voice, right there in the Vatican, sent shivers down his spine. He crossed himself.

教皇说：“你们所侍奉之人的子民。”

"A subject of the one you serve," said the Pope.

—大人听到这些话也和您一样感到恶心。

—My lord gets sick from those words as much as you do.

“我们该怎么办？毒死自己，让那个异端把我们埋葬吗？你必须逼他公开忏悔这些污秽之言。上帝对被邪灵附身的人是无限的怜悯，因此我给了他六十天时间忏悔。如果他不服从我的命令，我希望查理国王逮捕他，并确保他永远无法再玷污任何人的思想。”

"What shall we do? Poison ourselves and let that heretic bury us? You must force him to publicly recant this filth. God's mercy is infinite for the possessed, and for this reason I have given him sixty days to repent. If he fails to comply with my command, it is my wish that King Charles arrest him and ensure that he never again contaminates any mind."

加蒂纳拉点头表示同意。鉴于路德的话，在他看来，教宗的要求只是最低限度。

Gattinara nodded in agreement. Given Luther's words, the Holy Father's request seemed to him the bare minimum.

国王忠于圣王，必将毫不犹豫地服从。如果他尽心尽力地执行您的命令，您会谴责任何针对他的联盟吗？

—The king is loyal to His Holiness. He will obey without hesitation. Will you condemn any alliances formed against him if he zealously follows your orders?

汗珠顺着教皇的额头滑落，刺得他睁不开眼。他用前臂拂去汗珠，就在这个动作中，他的长袍失去了应有的尊严。

Beads of sweat trickled down the Pope's forehead, blinding him. He brushed them away with his forearm, and with that gesture, his robes lost their dignity.

“我不喜欢一个人积聚如此大的权力，”他回答说，“但如果你的主人履行了他对罗马的义务，罗马也会履行对他的义务。”

"It is not to my liking that a man should accumulate so much power," he replied, "but if your lord fulfills his obligations to Rome, Rome will fulfill them to him."

利奥十世向加蒂娜拉伸出手，加蒂娜拉再次亲吻了那枚被汗水浸湿的戒指。查理的使者匆匆离开房间，对走廊里经过的艺术品视而不见。他满脑子想的都是如何让那位修士放弃那些让他成为德国人英雄的经文。

Leo X offered his hand to Gattinara, who kissed the ring again, slippery with sweat. Charles's envoy hurried out of the room, paying no attention to the works of art he passed in the corridors. He could only think of how to get the friar to renounce the texts that had made him a hero to the Germans.

 

 

 

 

你哥哥没有毛遂自荐参选。如果你因此心怀怨恨，那就把怨恨指向我吧。

—Your brother did not put himself forward as a candidate. If you harbor any resentment because of that, let it be directed at me.

卡洛斯不想谈这件事，但他又不好意思让玛格丽塔阿姨闭嘴。他们一起享用的晚餐注定要失去味道了。

Carlos didn't want to talk about it, but he couldn't tell his Aunt Margarita to be quiet. The dinner they were sharing was doomed to lose its flavor.

“你背叛了我，”国王指责道。

"You were disloyal to me," accused the king.

“必须采取措施防止帝国落入外国之手！如果你输了选举，难道你不希望看到费迪南德而不是弗朗西斯登上皇位吗？” 无人应答。“天哪，查尔斯，他是你哥哥！” 玛格丽特脸红了。

"Something had to be done to prevent the Empire from falling into foreign hands! Had you lost the election, wouldn't you have been pleased to see Ferdinand on the imperial throne instead of Francis?" There was no reply. "For heaven's sake, Charles, he's your brother!" Margaret blushed.

——而且你已经看到他并没有那样对待我。我为什么要那样对待他呢？

—And you've already seen that he doesn't treat me as such. Why should I?

卡洛斯把一块肉放进嘴里，几乎没怎么咀嚼就狼吞虎咽地咽了下去。

Carlos put a piece of meat in his mouth. He swallowed it almost without chewing, eagerly.

“我知道你，”玛格丽特说，“如果他的话伤害了你，那是因为你自己也怀疑卡斯蒂利亚发生的事情。”

—I know you —Margarita said—. If his words have hurt you, it is because you yourself doubt what was done in Castile.

那块肉像路上的木头一样卡在皇帝的喉咙里。他咕咚咕咚灌了一大口啤酒，才把它咽了下去，同时思考着该如何回应这个事实。

The meat stuck in the emperor's throat like a log in the road. He swallowed it down with a long swig of beer, while he pondered how to respond to that truth.

 

 

 

 

卡洛斯将一排齿轮整齐地摆放在桌上，仔细地擦拭着。这些齿轮来自一座钟，这座钟从他记事起就让他魂牵梦萦。一位英国贵族将它赠予了他的曾祖父，勃艮第的查理一世。在弗兰德斯生活的整个时期，每当他需要静心思考时，他都会坐在钟前，滴答作响的声音始终陪伴着他。钟壳内，每个部件都自成一体，构成了一个独立的世界。钟内的一切都与他的忧虑截然相反。每当他寻求平静时，这件艺术品总能带给他安宁。

Carlos lined up the row of gears on the table and cleaned them meticulously. They were part of a clock that had obsessed him for as long as he could remember. An English nobleman had given it to his great-grandfather, Charles I of Burgundy. Throughout his life in Flanders, he had sat before it for hours, its ticking a constant companion, whenever he needed to think in peace. Inside that case, the pieces coexisted in a world where each had its own order and function. Everything within it was the antithesis of his worries. That work of art had always brought him peace whenever he sought it.

他的目光飘向其中一个钟摆，凝视着自己的倒影。他想起加冕那天，一股恐惧的寒意涌遍全身。他试图将注意力重新集中到钟的各个部件上，却做不到。或许，耗费了这么多心血和金钱，这一切不过是他失败的前奏：他可能会在西班牙遭受失败，也可能在英法两国可能对他发动的战争中遭受失败。全世界都在与他作对，这种想法令他备受煎熬。每当他试图驱散这种念头时，他就会想起卡斯蒂利亚正处于叛乱之中，一心想让他永远成为一段不堪回首的记忆。这时，有人敲门。

His gaze drifted to one of the pendulums, staring at his own reflection. He thought of the day of his coronation and felt the chill of fear coursing through his body. He tried to refocus on the clock's components, but he couldn't. Perhaps, after all the effort and money spent, this was nothing more than the prelude to his defeat: the one he might suffer in Spain and in the war that the English and French might declare against him. It tormented him that the world was conspiring against him. And every time he tried to banish that thought, he remembered that Castile, gripped by insurrection, wanted to consign him to a bad memory. Someone knocked at the door.

加蒂纳拉带着来自罗马的消息进来。希耶夫尔紧随其后，急于参与其中。教皇的条件非但没有加重君主的忧虑，反而缓解了国王的焦虑。他知道获得利奥十世要求的、以换取他支持的条件的唯一途径。路德撤回其著作的最后期限尚未到来，但人人都怀疑，除非罗马以外的势力要求，否则他不会撤回，因为这位叛逆者自视为反抗教会贪婪的解放者。解决之道在于维滕贝格大学，也就是萨克森的腓特烈。

Gattinara entered with news from Rome. Chièvres followed, eager not to be left out of the proceedings. Far from adding to the monarch's troubles, the Pope's condition served to relieve the king's anxiety. He knew the only way to obtain what Leo X demanded in exchange for his support. The deadline for Luther to recant his writings had not yet passed, but everyone suspected he would not recant unless a force other than Rome demanded it, for the rebel saw himself as a liberator against ecclesiastical rapacity. The solution lay with the University of Wittenberg, that is, with Frederick of Saxony.

“如果萨克森来的那个人不履行他的义务怎么办？”加蒂纳拉问道，这让查尔斯和希耶夫尔感到惊讶。

"And what if the one from Saxony doesn't fulfill his obligation?" Gattinara asked, to the astonishment of Charles and Chièvres.

“你的意思是说，皇帝的权力还不足以让他的命令得到服从吗？”希耶夫尔说道。

—Are you suggesting that the emperor's power is not such that his orders should be obeyed? —said Chièvres.

“我并不质疑皇权，而是质疑那些将这位修士视为远不止挑衅者的人的服从。如果路德的思想得逞，罗马的资金就会流向德国诸侯，其中就包括腓特烈。”

"I don't question imperial authority, but rather the obedience of those who see in the friar something more than a provocateur. If Luther's ideas were to triumph, money from Rome would flow to the German princes, Frederick among them."

卡洛斯盯着桌子，努力寻找解决问题的办法，但他看到的只是一排齿轮。

Carlos stared at the table, searching for a solution to the problem, but all he could see was a row of gears.

“在这件事上，你绝不能动摇。在罗马和诸侯面前，你绝不能犹豫。萨克森的腓特烈会遵从你的命令。如果那个邪恶的奥古斯丁教徒执迷不悟，他会第一个逮捕他，并把他当作异端示众。不要怀疑上帝将赐予你的权力。”

"You cannot waver on this matter. Not before Rome and the Princes. Frederick of Saxony will follow your orders. And if that devilish Augustinian does not come to his senses, he will be the first to arrest him and display him as a heretic. Do not doubt the power that God is going to grant you."

国王随后请求独处。说实话，自从来到弗兰德斯，开始回忆童年往事以来，这正是他最渴望的。于是他试图专注于曾祖父的怀表，推迟任何决定，但他感到脖子沉重，手腕持续刺痛，仿佛身体的这些部位背负着这片领土的重担。查理告诉自己，他必须彻底平息这种躁动，因为它不过是他内心滋生的一棵恶树，其种子源于与卡斯蒂利亚人的误会。他想起得知自己当选皇帝时那种震撼人心的感觉，那种让他觉得自己无所不能的力量。这，也只有这，才是他全新的自我。他要向世人证明这一点。第二天，他将命令萨克森的腓特烈处理马丁·路德的问题。

The king then asked to be alone. Truth be told, this was what he had longed for most since arriving in Flanders and beginning to reminisce about his childhood. So he tried to concentrate on his great-grandfather's watch and postpone any decision, but he felt a heavy weight in his neck and an incessant tingling in his wrists, as if these parts of his body carried the burdens of the territories. Charles told himself that, once and for all, he had to subdue this agitation, for it was nothing more than a malignant tree sprouting within him, its seed planted by the misunderstandings with the Castilians. He remembered the feeling that had overwhelmed him when he learned he had been elected emperor, that strength that made him feel capable of anything. This, and nothing else, was his new self. He would prove it to the world. The next day he would order Frederick of Saxony to deal with Martin Luther.

他终于能够像小时候那样，全神贯注地研究钟表机械装置了。

He was finally able to concentrate on the clock mechanism like he did when he was a child.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，平民百姓分散在树下，躲避倾盆大雨。这里是事先约定的集合地点，尽管至今无人出现告知他们消息。一道闪电划破夜空。短短几秒钟，隐藏在夜色中的武装人员清晰可见，他们的武器在雨水浸透的树梢下闪闪发光。巴利亚多利德仍然是卡斯蒂利亚最忠于查理王室的城市，但帕迪利亚及其部下已成功渗透到其附近，他们的目标足以推翻国王。

Meanwhile, the commoners spread out under the trees, sheltering from the heavy downpour. This was the agreed-upon meeting place, although no one had yet appeared to give them news. A flash of lightning illuminated the sky. For a few seconds, the line of armed men, hidden in the night, could be clearly seen, their weapons gleaming beneath the rain-soaked treetops. Valladolid was still the Castilian city most loyal to Charles's crown, but Padilla and his men had managed to penetrate its vicinity with an objective that could, on its own, overthrow the king.

“他几个小时前就应该到了。他肯定已经被发现了。”玛丽亚·帕切科说道，她的脸上满是水。

"He should have been here hours ago. He must have been discovered," said María Pacheco, her face covered in water.

“暴风雨可能耽误了他。我们耐心点，女士，”帕迪拉回答道，全然不顾自己的紧张情绪。

"The storm may have delayed him. Let's be patient, woman," Padilla replied, ignoring his own nerves.

玛丽亚深知，仅仅动员民众并不足以确保胜利。因此，她劝说追随者们，最佳策略是向远处雨幕下隐约可见的城市——托尔德西利亚斯进军。胡安娜女王将成为这场起义的催化剂。她将成为团结所有卡斯蒂利亚人对抗她儿子的完美象征。只要提起她的名字，人们就会想起父母和祖父母的故事，并会不由自主地憧憬一个不再惧怕外族势力的卡斯蒂利亚。

Maria knew that simply rallying crowds wasn't enough to secure her victory. That's why she had convinced her followers that the best course of action was to march on the city visible in the distance through a curtain of rain: Tordesillas. Queen Juana would be the catalyst for the revolt. She would be the perfect symbol around which to unite all Castilians against her son. Just mentioning her name would evoke the stories of their parents and grandparents, and the people would be compelled to envision a Castile that did not fear the power of foreigners.

帕迪利亚看到一个黑影靠近。听到有人喊“谁在那里？”，他便命令黑影停下。原来是几天前被派到村里的那个间谍。

Padilla saw a shadow approaching. At the cry of "Who goes there?" he ordered it to stop. It was the spy who had been sent to the village days before.

“先生，我们的人数是蒙特罗人的两倍。”那人咬牙切齿地说，牙齿冻得咯咯作响；他浑身湿透了。

—We outnumber the Monteros twice, sir—the man said through gritted teeth, which chattered from the cold; he was soaked.

“那么我们就从两个侧翼进攻，”帕迪利亚赶紧说道，然后转身向他的部下解释路线。

"Then we'll enter from two flanks," Padilla hastened to say, turning back to explain the routes to his men.

平民们出发了，包围了托尔德西利亚斯，毫不迟疑地向前推进，他们被暴风雨中即将到来的荣耀所激励。两小时后，长矛和火把的碰撞声响彻笼罩着整座城市的黑暗。王室派驻在那里的蒙特罗斯·德·埃斯皮诺萨小分队，几乎只是象征性的，似乎根本不是起义者的对手；他们轻易地遭到伏击，或惊慌失措地逃窜。如果卡塔琳娜公主此刻看到了她渴望看到的那条河，她看到的将是一条被鲜血染红的杜罗河。

The commoners set out, surrounding Tordesillas and advancing without delay, spurred on by the glory that awaited them in the midst of the storm. Two hours later, the clash of lances and torches filled the darkness engulfing the city. The small detachment of Monteros de Espinosa, which the Crown had stationed there almost as a mere token, seemed no match for the insurgents; they were easily ambushed or fled in panic. Had the Infanta Catalina discovered the river she longed to see at that moment, she would have found a Duero bathed in red.

从后方望去，玛丽亚·帕切科没有看到血迹，只有远处传来的战斗呐喊声。呐喊声与雷声和暴雨声交织在一起。

From the rear, María Pacheco saw no blood, only the distant shouts that bore witness to the battle. Shouts mingled with thunder and the pounding of rain.

胜利的消息比预想的来得更快。玛丽亚和护卫她的士兵们向城里进发。午夜时分，数百双眼睛透过窗户注视着他们进入街道，恐惧着那些几个小时前曾用皇家卫队成员的死亡玷污了这片土地的身影。

The news of the victory arrived sooner than expected. Maria and the men protecting her headed toward the city. In the middle of the night, hundreds of eyes behind windows watched their entry into the streets, fearful of those figures who, for a few hours, had stained the place with the death of the members of the Royal Guard.

 

 

 

 

——战争，殿下，战争！

—War, Your Highness, war!

托尔德西利亚斯宫的仆人们惊恐的呼喊声响彻黑暗。他们用锁和祈祷寻求庇护。胡安娜对警报的反应和她对其他一切事物的反应一样，仿佛有一堵冷漠的墙将她与世界隔绝开来，让她除了自己之外感受不到任何其他情绪。多年来，她的生活如同漫无目的的惯性，任何威胁对她来说都显得不够可怕，因为她已经没有什么幸福可失去了。直到女仆们表达了对土耳其人占领城市的恐惧，胡安娜才找到女儿，命令她用刀自卫。

The servants of the Tordesillas palace filled the darkness with panicked cries. They sought protection with locks and prayers. Juana reacted to the alarm in the same way she reacted to everything else, as if a wall of indifference separated her from the world, preventing her from feeling anything but herself. Life had been a aimless inertia for her for years, and no threat seemed terrible enough, for she had no happiness left to lose. Only when the maids expressed their fear that the Turks had taken the city did Juana seek out her daughter and order her to defend herself with a knife.

卡塔琳娜既害怕又兴奋，她看到托尔德西利亚斯宫殿所在的陵墓竟然重获新生。

Catalina trembled with fear, but also because of a pleasant excitement: that of seeing that the tomb that was the palace of Tordesillas showed life for once.

城门向帕迪利亚夫妇率领的暴徒敞开。仆人们听到袭击者说着卡斯蒂利亚语，松了口气，但即便被告知不必担心，他们仍然心存恐惧。他们没有阻止平民百姓进入王后的寝宫；如果这伙人并非要杀死王后，而是要杀死疯女人，那就随他们便吧。

The gates gave way to the horde led by Padilla and his wife. The servants were relieved to hear the attackers speaking Castilian, but they still feared for their lives, even when told they had no reason to. They did nothing to prevent the commoners from reaching the queen's chamber; if it wasn't her death but the Madwoman's that this band sought, so be it.

当他们与女王面对面时，袭击者们齐齐鞠躬。乔安娜完全不知所措。

Upon finding themselves face to face with the queen, the assailants joined in a bow. Joanna was utterly bewildered.

“我之前听说你们是进攻这座城市的土耳其人，”他说。

"I had been told that you were Turks attacking the city," he said.

——我们是您的子民，殿下。

—We are your subjects, Your Highness.

“什么样的卡斯蒂利亚人会占领女王的宫殿？”胡安娜问道。

—What kind of Castilians take over their queen's palace? —Juana inquired.

——那些对卡斯蒂利亚最忠诚的人。那些哀叹他们的国王日复一日地掠夺国家、玩忽职守的人。

—Those most loyal to Castile. Those who lament that their king plunders it and neglects his duties day after day.

卡塔琳娜躲在壁炉旁拉开的帘子后面，注视着眼前的景象，这些男人仿佛是从小说里走出来似的，她看得入了迷。她把刀藏进袖子里，却发现自己握刀的手松了。

Hidden behind the curtain that opened by the fireplace, Catalina watched the scene, fascinated by these men who seemed straight out of a novel. She concealed the knife up her sleeve, but noticed that her hand was now gripping it less tightly.

“我们来是为了解放你，让你能够统治那些理应属于你的土地。”玛丽亚·帕切科庄严地说，急切地想听到胡安娜的回应。

—We have come to free you so that you may govern the lands that are rightfully yours—said Maria Pacheco solemnly, eager to hear a response from Juana.

但女王开口只是为了让女儿走出避难所。

But the queen only spoke to ask her daughter to come out of her refuge.

“我明天会听你的。女王通常不会在清晨讨论王室事务。既然你已经占领了宫殿，你可以用它来休息并安置你的伤员。”

"I will listen to you tomorrow. A queen does not usually discuss matters of the Crown in the early hours of the morning. Since you have taken the palace, you may use it to rest and shelter your wounded."

“我们没有伤员。”玛丽亚骄傲地回答道。

—We have no wounded —María answered proudly.

但王后早已对他不屑一顾。只有公主仍将目光投向平民百姓。那晚，胡安·德·帕迪利亚炯炯有神的双眼成了她梦境的焦点。

But the queen had already turned her back on him. Only the infanta kept her gaze fixed on the commoners. That night, Juan de Padilla's vigorous eyes were the focus of her dreams.

 

 

 

 

1520年10月23日，亚琛的号角声响起，这一天注定载入史册。好奇的旁观者三五成群地聚集在宫廷礼拜堂，当参加加冕典礼的人员名单和头衔被宣布时，他们鼓掌欢呼。家人、盟友和敌人在为仪式铺设的地毯上交叠，亲吻、鞠躬，这套礼仪似乎注定要持续数小时之久。国王、王子和整个王室家族都借此机会商讨国事，并展示子女的美貌，以此作为政治博弈的手段。整个上午，这张地毯所承载的权力，比历史上大多数王国加起来还要多。

On October 23, 1520, the trumpets of Aachen sounded on a day destined for history. Curious onlookers formed groups, applauding as the names and titles of those attending the coronation were announced in the Palatine Chapel. Family members, allies, and enemies mingled on the carpet laid out for the ceremony, kissing and bowing in a protocol that seemed destined to last for hours. Kings, princes, and entire royal families took advantage of the occasion to discuss matters of state and display the beauty of their children as a form of political bargaining. Over the course of the morning, that carpet accumulated more power than most kingdoms that have ever existed.

幸运的是，查理前一晚睡得很好，与其说是因为对仪式漠不关心，不如说是因为连续几天不眠不休而筋疲力尽。在走出马车，踏上查理曼的土地之前，这位君主将最后的思绪献给了他，祈祷他能赐予自己力量，将自己的遗产延续到整个帝国。

Fortunately, Charles had slept well the night before, more from exhaustion after several days of ignoring the call of sleep than from any lack of concern about the ceremony. Before stepping out of the carriage and onto Charlemagne's soil, the monarch dedicated his last thought to him, praying that he would grant him strength to extend his legacy over the Empire.

查理一出现在阳光下，围观者便纷纷低下了头。他们人数众多，有些人甚至从几天路程之外的城市赶来，但即便如此，与他们所代表的数百万臣民相比，他们也只是微不足道的一小部分。

The onlookers lowered their heads as soon as Charles appeared in the sunlight. There were many of them, some having come from cities days away, but even so, they were an insignificant number compared to the millions of subjects they represented.

查理进入大教堂，立刻被金碧辉煌的大理石建筑所震撼。他拾级而上，走了七十八级台阶，来到主祭坛前。这七十八级台阶，所有人的目光都聚焦在他身上。在所有宾客的注视下，他俯身在祭坛前，张开双臂，向上帝俯首称臣。这位至高无上的人物如此宣告，在上帝面前，他永远只是个仆人。当他起身时，他看到了巨大的基督像，金色的背景衬托着它，在教堂的最高处熠熠生辉。他与基督的目光相遇，刚才的焦虑如同缕缕轻烟般消散了。大主教打开圣经，他刚开口，在场的所有人都起立致敬。

Charles entered the cathedral, which immediately enveloped him in its beauty of gold and marble. He advanced seventy-eight steps to the high altar. Seventy-eight steps during which all eyes were upon him. In full view of all the guests, he lay down before the altar, extending his arms in a gesture of submission to God. The most honored man thus acknowledged that before Him he would always be a mere servant. As he rose, he saw the immense Pantocrator with its golden background, resplendent from the highest point of the chapel. He met Christ's gaze, and his recent anxieties vanished like faint smoke. The archbishop opened his Bible, and as soon as the first words left his lips, those present rose in a show of respect.

弥撒结束后，那一刻终于到来。主教用两根手指蘸了蘸圣油，为君主涂抹圣油，并册封他为查理曼大帝的继承人。查理默默祈祷，王冠被戴在了他的头上。王冠完美地贴合在他的太阳穴上，他几乎感觉不到头顶上旧约诸王和上帝之子的形象所带来的重量。新皇帝感到眼眶湿润，便闭上了双眼。他细细品味着自己付出巨大代价——金钱和内心的平静——所换来的成果，而这些牺牲与他此刻的感受相比，似乎微不足道。

After the Mass, the moment arrived. The prelate dipped the tips of two fingers into the holy oil, anointed the monarch, and designated him as the heir of Emperor Charlemagne. Charles prayed to himself as the crown was placed upon his head. It fit so perfectly on his temples that he barely noticed the weight of bearing the images of the kings of the Old Testament and the Son of God. The new emperor felt his eyes well up with tears and closed them. He savored the fruit of an effort that had cost him so much gold and peace of mind, and that sacrifice seemed small compared to what he was feeling.

他意识到自己就是凯撒，再次睁开双眼，拾级而上，踏上通往查理曼宝座的六级台阶。宝座粗糙简朴，由石头砌成，没有任何装饰，却蕴含着超越时间的纯粹之美。查理曼坐上宝座，眺望前方，却什么也看不见，因为阳光透过教堂的窗户照射进来，刺得他睁不开眼。他感到自己被一种光芒四射的孤独所包围，这六级台阶将他高高举起，凌驾于世间万物之上。亚琛大教堂顿时爆发出雷鸣般的欢呼声和钟声，教堂外也响起了鸣放礼炮的声响。

Knowing himself to be Caesar, he opened his eyes again and ascended the six steps that led to Charlemagne's throne. It was rough, made of stone, and unadorned. It possessed the simplicity of that which transcends time. As he sat upon it, Charles looked ahead, but could see nothing, for the rays of the sun filtering through the cathedral's windows blinded him. He found himself enveloped in a luminous solitude, lifted above the rest of the world by those six steps. The Aachen Cathedral then erupted in cheers and the pealing of bells. Outside, salutes began to be fired.

在万众瞩目的荣耀之中，卡洛斯想起自己当时只有二十岁。

Amidst all the glory, Carlos remembered that he was only twenty years old.

 

 

 

 

信使们花了数日才从卡斯蒂利亚抵达帝国，这宽容的喘息之机令查理十分欣慰。然而，当他得知托尔德西利亚斯发生的事情后，痛苦再次袭来，如同一个久别重逢、忠贞不渝的爱人，始终无法放手。

The messengers took several days to reach the Empire from Castile, a generous reprieve that pleased Charles. When he was informed of what had happened in Tordesillas, anguish returned to haunt him, like an old and faithful lover unable to let him go.

“不要灰心，很少有背叛会来自自己的母亲，”加蒂纳拉告诉他。

"Don't lose hope, few betrayals come from one's own mother," Gattinara told him.

卡洛斯心想，这在任何家庭都是意料之中的事。但在这个儿子决定囚禁母亲以独揽大权的家庭里，却并非如此。他怎能不预料到母亲的怨恨？他内心充满深深的愧疚，仿佛愿意为此付出灵魂，而灵魂深处却不会发出丝毫声响。他知道胡安娜只是为了自己的利益。如果她最终同意继承卡斯蒂利亚王位，那更多的是因为他作为儿子的失职，而非叛军的胜利。但忏悔并不能赢得这场战斗。他将自己托付于上帝的旨意，并下令授予阿德里亚诺全权镇压叛乱。

This was to be expected in any family, Carlos thought. But not in one where the son had decided to keep his mother imprisoned to wield power alone. How could he not expect resentment from her? He was overcome with such profound guilt that he could have shed his soul for it without a sound being heard in the depths. He knew that Juana had only sought her own gain. If she finally agreed to the request to claim the crown of Castile, it would be more because of his failure as a son than because of the success of the rebels. But repentance wasn't going to win the battle. He entrusted himself to the will of the Lord and gave orders to grant full powers to Adriano to quell the revolt.

她再次感到恐惧。恐惧总是像一块巨石压在她胸口，挥之不去。这种折磨何时才能结束？

She felt fear again. The fear always returned like a weight on her chest. Would this torment ever end?

 

 

 

 

与此同时，凯瑟琳走出托尔德西利亚斯宫，脸上带着一种仿佛突然拥有了水上行走能力的茫然。自从查尔斯试图带她一起走后，她就一直没让自己沐浴在阳光下。她的眼睛还不习惯如此广阔的视野，十步之外的一切都显得模糊不清，但她仍然好奇地凝视着。远处，为他们打开宫门的帕迪利亚正带着解放者的骄傲注视着她。

Meanwhile, Catherine stepped outside the Tordesillas palace with the bewilderment of someone who suddenly finds herself able to walk on water. Since Charles had tried to take her with him, she hadn't allowed herself to be bathed in sunlight. Her eyes weren't used to such a vast horizon, and anything beyond ten paces appeared blurry, but she still gazed at it with curiosity. At a distance, Padilla, who had opened the palace gates for them, watched her with the pride of a liberator.

妈妈，我可以跑吗？

—Can I run, Mom?

胡安娜点了点头。公主加快脚步，拉开与她的距离，两人随即奔跑起来，欢声笑语不断。女王看到她如此开心，心中也涌起一丝暖意。那一刻，她忘记了身处宫墙之外的不安。

Juana nodded. The Infanta moved away from her, quickening her pace until they broke into a run filled with laughter. The queen was touched to see her happy. For a moment, she forgot the unease she felt at being outside the palace walls.

外出活动仍在继续。平民们相信，这些外出活动给乔安娜带来的快乐最终会促使王后签署反对国王的条约——她此前一直拖延着此事，甚至连个借口都没有。但乔安娜心中的疑虑太过复杂，凯瑟琳的笑声无法消除。叛军详细地讲述了查理及其部下的暴政，他们渴望赋予她绝对的权力。然而，王后对这些自以为有权审判国王、对她毫无敬畏之心的人几乎一无所知，这些人对王位的尊重甚至不如对王座钥匙的尊重。

The outings continued. The commoners believed that the joy these outings brought to the girl would finally encourage the queen to sign against the king, something she had been postponing day after day without even offering an excuse. But Joanna's doubts were too complex to be silenced by Catherine's laughter. The rebels had recounted in detail the misrule of Charles and his men, and they were eager to grant her absolute power. However, the queen knew almost nothing about these men who believed they had the right to judge kings and who held her in no more respect than one might show for the key to the throne room.

 

 

 

 

卡斯蒂利亚的紧张气氛与昂布瓦兹城堡弥漫的和谐氛围形成了鲜明的对比。弗朗西斯醒来时兴奋不已，因为他即将在金缕原野与诸侯会面，他的仆人们正忙着准备。这场会面的奢华安排，正是他向世人宣告：失去帝国并未削弱他的伟大。战败的忧郁持续了数周，最终将他击垮。他对查理的仇恨转化为复仇的渴望，这如同查理曼大帝当年争夺王​​位一样，令他精神振奋。如今，他所有的精力都集中在让对手的帝国统治成为永无止境的噩梦。而拉拢英格兰加入这场战争，正是实现这一目标的最佳途径。一旦各大王国联合起来对抗哈布斯堡王朝，他曾经赢得的王冠，将成为对他的惩罚。

The tension in Castile contrasted sharply with the atmosphere of harmony that permeated the Château d'Amboise. Francis had awakened with excitement for his upcoming meeting at the Field of Cloth of Gold, which his servants were busily preparing. The lavishness surrounding the encounter was his way of telling the world that losing the Empire had not diminished his greatness. The melancholy of his defeat lingered for weeks, but eventually wore him down. His hatred for Charles transformed into a desire for revenge, a mission as invigorating as Charlemagne's quest for the throne had been. Now, all his energy was focused on making his rival's imperial rule a constant nightmare. And seducing England to the cause was the best way to achieve this. With the great kingdoms united against the Habsburg, the Crown he had won would become his punishment.

午后，法国国王收到消息，亨利八世的随从距离他们的会面地点还有四个小时的路程。会面地点位于一个山谷，弗朗西斯下令在那里建造了用金线装饰的亭台楼阁。亭台楼阁内部的奢华同样令人叹为观止：喷泉汩汩流淌着美酒，大理石长椅错落有致。毗邻的草坪上，还修建了用于比武和其他适合国王参与的游戏的场地。考虑到此次会面的目的是为了达成一项友好条约，如此铺张的奢华在许多人看来似乎毫无意义。但弗朗西斯除了顾及查理的不幸遭遇之外，还想给这位据说与他一样豪放不羁的英国人留下深刻印象。他希望法国的辉煌能够如此触手可及。自从沃尔西主教来访，最终促成两位国王的会面后，弗朗西斯就将这次会面视为抚慰他受伤自尊的良机。

In the mid-afternoon, the French monarch received news that Henry VIII's entourage was four hours away from their meeting place, a valley where Francis had ordered the construction of pavilions draped in gold thread. Inside, the luxury was no less impressive. There were fountains flowing with wine and marble benches. On the adjacent lawns, fields had been built for jousting and other games fit for kings. Such extravagance would seem senseless to many, considering that the intention was to hold a friendly meeting that would lead to a treaty. But Francis, in addition to Charles's misfortune, sought to impress the Englishman, whose bravado was said to be similar to his own. He wished for the splendor of France to be so palpable that it could be touched. Ever since Cardinal Wolsey had visited him to finalize the meeting between the two kings, Francis had understood this encounter as a salvation for his wounded pride.

远远地，阿拉贡的凯瑟琳注视着他们正接近的华丽营地。眼前的景象只会让她更加确信，这次旅程是对她侄子查理和她亲生骨肉的背叛。她无法相信自己的名字竟被用来促成这桩旨在削弱她家族成员的联姻，她发誓，总有一天，沃伊切赫会为这种只顾自身利益的阴谋付出代价。她曾试图劝说亨利拒绝法国人的邀请，但当国王宣布这次会面可能会为他们的女儿带来一笔有利可图的婚事时，凯瑟琳虽然仍然反对这桩联姻，但她的态度有所软化。或许这样一来，亨利的私生子就会被人遗忘，而年轻的玛丽也能确保她应得的继承权。

From a distance, Catherine of Aragon watched the ornate encampment they were approaching. The sight only served to remind her that she considered this journey a betrayal of her nephew Charles and her own flesh and blood. She couldn't believe that her name was being used in this alliance to weaken a member of her own family, and she vowed that one day Wojciech would pay for such a maneuver, one that considered nothing but his own self-interest. She had tried to convince Henry to reject the Frenchman's invitation, but when the king announced that this meeting could lead to a profitable engagement for their daughter, Catherine, though still opposed to the alliance, softened her stance. Perhaps in this way Henry's bastard son would be forgotten, and young Mary would secure the succession that was rightfully hers.

女王深吸一口气，努力将目光集中到对面，那里田野一直延伸到地平线尽头。亨利握住了她的手。

The queen took a deep breath and tried to focus her gaze on the opposite side, where the fields stretched beyond the horizon. Henry took her hand.

“你会玩得很开心的。”她丈夫笑着说，他察觉到她内心思绪万千。

"You'll end up having fun." Her husband laughed, aware of the whirlwind of thoughts that was unleashed within her.

“最让我不担心的就是无聊。唯一让我担心的就是那个法国人可能会向你许诺什么。”凯瑟琳回答道。

—Nothing worries me less than being bored. Only the distrust of what that Frenchman might promise you —replied Catherine.

亨利吻了吻妻子的手，妻子非但没有平静下来，反而继续凝视着田野，但很快，一阵号角声和马蹄声吸引了她的注意力，法国随从来了。

Henry kissed his wife's hand, who, far from calming down, continued with her gaze lost in the fields, but, soon, a rumble of trumpets and horses' hooves drew her attention to the arrival of the French entourage.

弗朗西斯在英国人面前下马时，他那华丽的丝绸长袍在阳光下熠熠生辉。亨利下马走近他时，弗朗西斯立刻注意到，英国人的装束同样令人印象深刻。法国人身姿挺拔，无人能及他的身高。两人拥抱良久，笑容满面。他们说，这是在庆祝彼此的友谊。尽管两人都明白，他们唯一的共同目标就是削弱查理的势力，但这种兄弟情谊的展现让他们感到自己更有人情味。

When Francis dismounted before the English, his fine silk robes gleamed in the sun, and he noticed, as soon as Henry dismounted and approached him, that the Englishman's attire was equally impressive. The Frenchman stood tall; no one could outdo him in height. The embrace was long, and many smiles followed. They were celebrating their friendship, they said. And although both knew that their only common ground was to diminish Charles's power, this display of brotherhood made them feel more human.

谈判开始时，双方都对彼此的默契感到惊讶。没有分歧，只有和谐与共同的目标。亨利对查理远没有法国人那样充满敌意——尽管查理小心翼翼地掩藏在言辞之中——但自从得知查理当选皇帝后，亨利便认为削弱这个已经掌控半个欧洲的人的权力是理所当然的。然而，弗朗西斯感到形势紧迫，因为他发现自己已被新皇帝的领地所包围：北方是佛兰德斯和帝国；南方是西班牙；而他心中，则怀着难以消除的怨恨。

When the negotiations began, both were surprised by their rapport. There were no disagreements, only harmony and shared objectives. Henry was far from harboring the animosity toward Charles that the Frenchman displayed and which he carefully concealed in every word, but since learning of his election as emperor, he understood it as natural to diminish the power of the man who, in that way, already possessed half of Europe. Urgency, however, pressed on Francis, for he now found himself surrounded by the domains of the new emperor. To the north, Flanders and the Empire; to the south, Spain, and in his heart, an incurable resentment.

但当法英两国兄弟情谊的演讲结束，一夜酒酣耳热之后，法国人一把搂住亨利的肩膀，坦白了自己的真实意图：尽快进攻哈布斯堡王朝。他所表达的动机远比政治考量更为直接。他用尽一切语言，将查理五世的种种冤屈一指地倾泻而出，语气凶狠无比。英国人默默地听着这番充满仇恨的告白，他想相信这只是醉酒的表现。但转念一想，他自己也只有在失去清醒的时候才会流露出内心的真实渴望。

But once the speeches of fraternal union between France and England had run their course, and after a night in which wine had reigned supreme, the Frenchman threw his giant arms around Henry's shoulders and confessed his true intentions: to attack the Habsburg as soon as possible. The motives he offered were far more visceral than political. He heaped upon Charles every grievance that language could, and he did so with ferocity. The Englishman listened in silence to this confession of hatred and wanted to believe it was due to drunkenness. But then he thought of himself, of how only when he lost his sobriety did he reveal his true desires.

 

 

 

 

萨克森的腓特烈一听到召见查理的命令，便立即前来觐见。他对皇帝的敬意略显冷淡，但查理认为这是因为来访者年事已高。

Frederick of Saxony appeared before Charles as soon as he heard of his summons. His deference to the emperor was lackluster, but Charles attributed it to his visitor's advanced age.

能够觐见新凯撒，真是莫大的荣幸。

—What an honor to be granted the first audience with the new Caesar.

“答应我的请求，就当回报我的恩惠，”查尔斯说，“你知道路德还没有放弃他的异端邪说。”

—Repay the privilege by serving me in what I ask of you— said Charles. —You know that Luther has not yet recanted his heresies.

费德里科笑了。他早就料到自己会出现在这里会有其他原因。

Federico smiled. He hadn't expected the reason for his presence there to be anything else.

—截止日期尚未过去。

—The deadline has not yet passed.

他的沉默表明他拒绝服从罗马的命令。他是你的门生。说服他收回他的话——查理命令道。

—His silence indicates that he refuses to obey Rome's order. He is your protégé. Convince him to retract his statement—Charles ordered.

“他任教的大学是我的，但不是他的灵魂，”费德里科谦卑地辩解道。

"The university where he teaches is mine, not his soul," Federico argued in a humble tone.

“我毫不怀疑他会服从您的命令，因为只有您的命令才能保护他。难道您看不出他正在危害德国的和平吗？”

"I have no doubt that he will answer to your authority, since it is the only one that protects him. Don't you see that he is jeopardizing peace in Germany?"

撒克逊人心知肚明，但他惊讶地发现皇帝竟然也如此清楚。他原以为查理会过于沉迷于王位，以至于看不到其中的危险。

The Saxon knew it, but he was surprised to find that the emperor was so aware of it. He had expected Charles to be too vain with his crown to perceive the dangers.

——陛下，没有什么比帝国的命运更令我担忧的了——弗雷德里克回答道。

—Nothing worries me more than the fate of the Empire, Your Majesty —replied Frederick.

 

 

 

 

路德的房间只有四面墙、一张简易床和一张简陋的木桌，他的监护人来访时，他就坐在桌旁。地板上堆放着这位修士的著作，那是他深信自己所从事的事业后，思想的结晶。但自从教皇命令他放弃教义，否则将面临后果后，每当他拿起笔，都感到力不从心。他相信自己的信念胜过对死亡的恐惧，但焚尸炉的景象却开始每晚萦绕在他的噩梦中。

Luther's room was confined to its four walls, a cot, and a simple wooden table, at which he sat when his protector visited. Piled on the floor were the friar's writings, the product of his mind, convinced of the cause he had undertaken. But since the Pope had ordered him to renounce his doctrines or face the consequences, the friar's hand felt weaker when he took up his pen. He believed his convictions were stronger than his fear of death, but the pyre had begun to haunt his nightmares each night.

弗雷德里克说：“皇帝命令我让你闭嘴。”

—The emperor has ordered me to silence you—said Frederick.

路德转过身。这位撒克逊人感觉到，这个身材魁梧、面容冷峻的男人内心深处隐藏着恐惧。

Luther turned around. The Saxon sensed that this burly man with the implacable face harbored fear.

“想都别想，”他继续说道。

"Don't even think about doing it," he continued.

修士注意到他的保护者身穿丝绸西装，双手镶满珠宝，脚穿饰有金饰的天鹅绒鞋。

The friar noticed his protector's silk suit, his bejeweled hands, and his velvet shoes with gold embellishments.

你不可拿自己的生命冒险。让我的灵魂来决定吧。

—You must not risk your life. Let my soul decide.

“我会竭尽全力保护你！”弗雷德里克说。“你的风险就是我的风险。我向你保证。”

"I will do everything in my power to protect you!" Frederick said. "Your risk will be my risk. I give you my word."

路德知道弗雷德里克并不相信他的言论。他甚至懒得假装相信。他们的友谊，如果真有其事的话，也只不过是两人达成各自截然不同目的的手段而已。

Luther knew that Frederick didn't believe his pronouncements. He didn't even bother to pretend he did. Their friendship, if it existed, was merely a means to two very different ends.

“我的十字军东征是为了实现你的政治抱负，”修士明白了。

"My crusade is in service of your political aspirations," the friar understood.

——而这些都将为你们的圣战效力！两股力量合力将势不可挡。德国的命运掌握在我们手中，谁知道呢，或许整个基督教世界的命运也掌握在我们手中。

—And these are at the service of your crusade! Both forces together will be unstoppable. The fate of Germany is in our hands, and who knows, perhaps that of all Christendom.

路德小桌上的蜡烛光芒摇曳，在光秃秃的墙上投下长长的影子。修士看着这些影子，欣喜地发现，自己的倒影比实际看起来要大得多。

The light from the candle resting on Luther's small table flickered, and their shadows lengthened on the bare wall. The friar observed them and was pleased to see that his reflection could be larger than he actually was.

 

 

 

 

几天后，路德当着一群追随者的面，将罗马教皇诏书投入火中，他的勇气令追随者们欢欣鼓舞。查理一世得知此事后，怒不可遏，痛斥路德的顽固不化和萨克森的腓特烈二世的背信弃义。两人都应受到最严厉的惩罚，但他若下令，德国很可能像卡斯蒂利亚一样起义。最终，理智战胜了愤怒和正义感。他决定不再煽动臣民，除非迫不得已。

A few days later, Luther threw the papal bull from Rome into the fire before a crowd of followers thrilled by his bravery. When Charles learned of this, he furiously cursed the heretic's obstinacy and Frederick of Saxony's treachery. Both deserved the most severe and exemplary punishment, but if he ordered it, Germany could rise up as Castile had, and prudence prevailed over anger or a sense of justice. He would not incite his subjects again if he could avoid it. At least, not until he was forced to.

 

 

 

 

在平民百姓面前避免发表任何声明，这种博弈耗尽了胡安娜仅存的一点力气，最终她同意主持在宫殿最宽敞的房间里举行的一次会议。帕迪利亚一踏进门，便站起身来，享受着胜利的喜悦；女王的出现似乎预示着她的祝福。

The game of avoiding making a statement before the commoners was consuming what little strength Juana had left, and finally she agreed to preside over one of the meetings they held in the palace's most spacious room. Once he had crossed the threshold, Padilla stood up, savoring his victory; the queen's presence seemed to foreshadow her blessing.

时机再好不过了。哈德良从国王那里获得了更大的权力，并利用这种权力来拉拢贵族。贵族们对叛乱的走向感到恐惧——叛乱如今已演变成对所有掌权者的愤怒，而不仅仅是针对查理——他们开始支持王室对抗共产主义者。在此之前，贵族们对哈德良请求他们出面干预国王的请求一直保持着谨慎的态度。他们对查理的尊重微乎其微，并将暴乱视为削弱王权的手段。但如今，当他们自身的特权也受到威胁时，国王似乎成了两害相权取其轻的选择，因此，他们不得不支持他。

The timing could not have been more opportune. Hadrian had obtained greater authority from the king, and he was using it to win over the nobility. The nobility, frightened by the direction the revolt was taking—which had now become a fury against all who wielded power, not just Charles—had begun to lend support to the crown against the Comuneros. Until then, the lords had been careful to remain sufficiently ambiguous in their response to Hadrian's pleas for them to intervene on the king's behalf. Their esteem for Charles was negligible, and they saw the riots as a way to weaken royal authority. But now that their own privileges were also threatened, the king seemed the lesser evil, and as such, they had to back him.

玛丽亚·帕切科赶紧把椅子搬到胡安娜要坐的地方。女王刚坐下，帕迪利亚就递给她一份文件。

María Pacheco hurried to place the chair where Juana was to sit. As soon as the queen was settled, Padilla handed her a document.

“殿下，这是我们请您审阅的文件，”他解释道，“它表明我们是您忠诚的封臣，除了您头戴的王冠之外，任何其他王冠都无权统治卡斯蒂利亚。”

—Your Highness, this is the document we ask you to consider— he explained. —It states that we are your loyal vassals and that no crown other than the one you wear will rule over Castile.

女王看了看文件，但没有读。

The queen looked at the document, but did not read it.

“我为什么要积攒这么多权力？”他问道，“我身体不好，最不想做的就是每天处理办公室事务。”

"Why should I accumulate such authority?" he inquired. "I am not in good health, and the last thing I want is to have to deal with office matters on a daily basis."

“我们任何人都可以帮您处理这些事情，”玛丽亚愉快地回答道，“治理国家不会成为您的负担。”

—Any of us can help you with those tasks—María replied cheerfully. —Governing will not be a burden for you.

胡安娜用锐利的目光打量着那个身材健美的年轻女子。

Juana observed that young woman with a penetrating gaze and sinewy body.

—我看得出来，没有什么比在我身边行使无人赋予你的权力更能让你高兴的了。

—I see that nothing would please you more than to wield power by my side that no one has granted you.

一阵低语在会场中荡漾开来。坐在房间后排的卡塔琳娜公主简直不敢相信母亲刚才说的话。若非帕迪利亚镇定自若，玛丽亚·帕切科也未曾对这番侮辱做出回应；她们必须尽快化解这场风波，以免紧张气氛危及文件获得皇家印章的机会。

A murmur rippled through the assembly. Seated at the back of the room, Infanta Catalina could scarcely believe what her mother had just said. Only Padilla's composed expression restrained María Pacheco from responding to the insult; they needed to defuse the situation before the tension jeopardized any chance of obtaining a royal seal on the document.

“殿下，如果您这样看待我们，那就大错特错了。我们代表着所有留在城墙之外的人们的意愿，并将之传达给您。我们将卡斯蒂利亚的未来，它应有的未来，而不是查理正将我们引向的深渊，交到了您手中。”

"You are mistaken if you think such a thing of us, Your Highness. We represent the will of all those who remain outside these walls, and we convey it to you. We place in your hands the future of Castile, the future it deserves, and not the abyss to which Charles is leading us."

—你在说我的儿子。

—You're talking about my son.

“王国的利益高于一切，血缘关系才是最重要的！”玛丽亚大声说道。

"The good of the kingdom is above blood!" Maria burst out.

胡安娜怀疑这一切是否属实。但她不明白这种家庭感从何而来。她从未像一个母亲那样爱过自己的孩子，她既意识到这一点，又觉得自己无力改变。她对费利佩的爱已经占据了她的全部，让她无法感受到其他任何东西。

Juana doubted that it was true. But she didn't understand where this sense of family came from. She had never loved her children as a mother should, and she both recognized this and felt incapable of changing it. Her love for Felipe had consumed her, preventing her from feeling anything else.

她接过文件，低声念诵着上面的文字，声音低得几乎听不见，从房间后排的人都难以分辨这声音究竟是女王的，还是昆虫的嗡嗡声。在场的人渐渐不耐烦起来，玛丽亚·帕切科也一样，递给她一支羽毛笔。卡塔琳娜看到母亲接过笔，顿时感到一阵刺痛。那一签名意味着她的自由，意味着她终于能重获被剥夺的尊严，也意味着她能为几乎从出生起就遭受的不公惩罚讨回公道。仅仅一个签名，此前被禁锢在宫殿里的世界，就将向她敞开。然而，仿佛灵魂被撕裂一般，卡塔琳娜看到母亲把笔放在桌上，文件也面朝下放了下去。女王抬起头，目光却没有落在任何人身上。

She took the document and read it, repeating those words in a voice so low that from the back of the room it was difficult to tell if they belonged to the queen or the buzzing of an insect. Those present grew impatient, as did María Pacheco, who handed her a quill pen. When Catalina saw her mother take it, she felt her skin prickle. That signature would mean her freedom, finally gaining the dignity that had been denied them and avenging the unjust punishment to which she had been subjected almost since birth. Just a single signature and the world, which until then had been confined to that palace, would open up to be experienced. But, as if her soul were being ripped away, the girl saw her mother place the pen on the table and put the document face down. The queen raised her gaze without fixing it on anyone.

“他们说我的理智随着丈夫在绳索之屋的死亡而消亡。的确如此，所以我每晚都向上帝祈祷，求他带走我，让我免受这人生的苦难。但如果​​说我作为这片土地的女王学到了什么，那就是无论理智与否，无论生死，我都能轻易认出眼前的狼群。我恳求你离开这座宫殿，因为它就像卡斯蒂利亚本身一样，不属于你。”

"They say my sanity died with my husband in the House of the Cord. That's true, and that's why every night I pray to God to take me and spare me this suffering that is life. But if there's one thing I've learned as queen of these lands, it's that sane or not, alive or dead, I can easily recognize a pack of wolves when it's right in front of me. I beg you to leave this palace, for, like Castile itself, it is not yours."

女王站起身来。经历了多日的忐忑不安，她疲惫不堪，鼓起勇气走向门口。很快，她又将回到那高墙之内，继续她日复一日的日常生活，而她也将永远无法再次走出这堵墙。她听到身后传来帕迪拉妻子的声音。

The queen stood up. Weary after so many days of uncertainty, she steeled herself to reach the door. Soon she would return to the routine within those walls from which she would never again emerge. Behind her, she heard Padilla's wife.

我们建立了一个王国，把它置于你的统治之下，我们解放了你，你竟然还在怀疑？他们说你疯了，一点没错。

—We built a kingdom, we put it under your rule, we freed you, and you still doubt? They rightly call you crazy.

胡安娜转过身，给了他一个居高临下的微笑。女王难得享受了一次掌控一切的感觉。

Juana turned and gave him a condescending smile. For once, the queen was enjoying being in charge.

 

 

 

 

那天下午，仿佛是受到胡安娜的召唤，卡斯蒂利亚贵族的军队夺回了托尔德西利亚斯，归还王室。平民们像攻占宫殿一样迅速地放弃了它，带走的只有失望和对未来的迷茫。凯瑟琳出去送别他们，恳求他们取得一场永远无法实现的胜利。她太年轻了，无法轻易放弃希望。直到宫殿恢复了往日的平静，公主才意识到一切都不会改变。当她问母亲为何要将她囚禁于此时，得到的只有母亲的恳求和原谅，没有其他的回答。此后数日，宫殿恢复的宁静只被孩子的哭泣打破。

That afternoon, as if summoned by Juana's will, the Castilian lords' forces recaptured Tordesillas for the Crown. The commoners abandoned the palace as quickly as they had taken it, carrying away nothing but disappointment and uncertainty about the future. Catherine went out to see them off and begged them to achieve a victory that never came. She was too young to lose her hope in a single blow. Only when the palace returned to its routine did the Infanta realize that nothing would change. When she asked her mother why she had condemned her to remain in that prison, she received no answer but a plea for forgiveness. The tranquility restored to the palace was broken, for days, only by the child's weeping.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在法国乡村腹地一座金碧辉煌的亭台楼阁中，经过一上午的比武和盛大宴会后，弗朗西斯和亨利签署了盟约。盟约宣告了永恒的友谊，并以他们子女弗朗西斯和玛丽的婚约作为象征。在金缕原野的几天里，两位国王在每项游戏、每一次谈话、每一件华服上都展开了较量，但维系他们的盟约足以弥补兄弟间的竞争，最终所有较量都以平局告终。亨利勉强接受了这一牺牲。事实上，尽管弗朗西斯是一位有用的盟友，但他却觉得弗朗西斯虚荣得令人难以忍受。他不习惯与如此骄傲自大的人共处一室，因此，当听到关于这位法国人在米兰取得胜利的种种描述时，他强颜欢笑。这些描述很快就变成了对达芬奇博学演讲的详细描述，最终以一种微妙的方式赞美了所有高卢的事物。事实上，如今他们在皇帝面前发出的声音已然统一。这一成就当然值得庆祝。

Meanwhile, in one of the gilded pavilions erected in the heart of the French countryside, after a morning of jousts and colossal banquets, Francis and Henry signed their alliance. The agreement spoke of eternal friendship, symbolized by the betrothal of their children, Francis and Mary. Throughout the days at the Field of Cloth of Gold, the two kings had competed in every game, every conversation, and with every finery, but the pact that bound them was well worth a fraternal rivalry, and all the competitions had ended in a draw. Henry accepted this sacrifice grudgingly. In truth, although Francis was a useful ally, he found him unbearably vain. He wasn't used to sharing the space with someone as swollen with pride as him, so he forced himself to smile at the numerous accounts of the Frenchman's victory in Milan, which quickly devolved into detailed descriptions of Leonardo's erudite lectures and ended up glorifying, albeit subtly, everything Gallic. The truth was, now they sounded like a unified voice before the emperor. And that achievement certainly deserved to be celebrated.

弗朗西斯出人意料地提议与英国人摔跤，以此来活跃宴会气氛。法国葡萄酒喷泉几乎滴水不多，只剩下涓涓细流，因为人们为了庆祝协议的达成而豪饮了太多。亨利醉醺醺的，像个水手一样厚颜无耻地为摔跤手们欢呼。

Francis surprised the Englishman by offering him a wrestling match to liven up his last banquet. The fountains of French wine were barely dripping, a trickle of reddish wine, so much had they drunk it to toast the agreement. His drunkenness led Henry to cheer the wrestlers with the shamelessness of a sailor.

“你给了我我最爱的运动！”亨利喊道。

—You have granted me my most beloved sport! —cried Henry.

喝了那么多酒之后，弗朗西斯的缺点似乎没那么让他感到恼火了。

Francis's flaws seemed less irritating to him after being washed down with so much drink.

“我不知道，”法国人镇定地回答道，“说实话，我把它们带到这里来是为了自己开心。没有什么比这更让我高兴的了！”

“I didn’t know that,” replied the Frenchman, more composed. “To be honest, I brought them here for my own enjoyment. Nothing amuses me more!”

你练习过吗？

—Do you practice it?

——尽我所能……你呢？

—As much as I can… And you?

恩里克点了点头。他们交换了一个充满挑战的眼神，由于酒精的作用，这个眼神在英语中显得转瞬即逝。

Enrique nodded. They exchanged a challenging glance, which in English was fleeting due to the alcohol.

“为什么不行呢？”恩里克自言自语道。

"Why not?" Enrique wondered aloud.

两个法庭的官员悉数到场，他们困惑地看着两位国王脱下外套，代替战士们上场。

The two courts, present in full, watched in bewilderment as the two kings took off their jackets and took the place of the fighters.

“就体型而言，我赌弗朗西斯科赢，”沃尔西说。“但喝醉的英国人是不可战胜的。幸亏有外交手段，才能让他们再次打成平手。”

"In terms of size, I'd bet on Francisco," Wolsey said. "But a drunken Englishman is unbeatable. Thank goodness for diplomacy, which will bring them to a draw again."

凯瑟琳微笑着，她清楚一旦开战会发生什么。在法国随从中，只有一位名叫安妮·博林的宫廷贵妇注意到了这位英国女王的举动。

Catherine smiled, aware of what might happen once the battle began. In the French entourage, one of the ladies of the court, named Anne Boleyn, was the only one to notice the English queen's gesture.

这场搏斗只持续了几秒钟。弗朗西斯科一记果断的重拳，将恩里克击倒在地，脸部着地。

The fight lasted seconds. A decisive move by Francisco sent Enrique crashing face-first to the ground.

以亨利和凯瑟琳为首的英国随从匆匆离开了营地。战败后的羞辱让这位英国人瞬间从醉意中清醒过来，他对弗朗西斯的厌恶之情也无需再掩饰。

The English entourage, with Henry and Catherine at their head, hastily left the camp. The humiliation had instantly sobered the Englishman from his drunkenness after losing the battle, and his dislike for Francis no longer needed to be disguised.

几个小时后，当这位法国人看着数百名工人拆除精美的金色亭台楼阁时，萨伏依的路易莎向他走来。

Hours later, the Frenchman was watching hundreds of men dismantle the elaborate golden pavilions when Luisa of Savoy approached him.

“省省吧！”国王警告道，“再说，我也没冒什么风险。协议已经签了。”

"Spare me the trouble!" warned the king. "Besides, I haven't risked anything. The agreement is signed."

但现在亨利急于打破它。

—But now Henry is eager to break it.

凉亭的黄色板条纷纷掉落在草地上。弗朗西斯科希望自己的希望不会以同样的方式破灭，因为他不知道该如何应对这会激起他内心的愤怒。

The yellow panels of the pavilions were falling onto the grass. Francisco wanted to believe that his hopes wouldn't collapse in the same way, because he didn't know what he could do with the anger that this might provoke in him.

凯瑟琳临行前给侄子写了一封简短的信，敦促他访问英国宫廷。虽然弗朗西斯已从她丈夫那里得到了签名，但由于这位法国人傲慢的性情（如同百年老柏树般），签名已经褪色。查理必须利用亨利的不安，否则，一旦他的决心动摇，亨利就可能结成联盟对抗皇帝。

Before departing for England, Catherine wrote a brief letter addressed to her nephew. In it, she urged him to visit the English court. Although Francis had obtained a signature from her husband, it had faded due to the Frenchman's temperament, as haughty as a hundred-year-old cypress tree. Charles had to take advantage of Henry's unease, or else, once his resolve cooled, Henry could forge the alliance against the emperor.

 

 

 

 

卡洛斯对这次旅行感激不尽。托尔德西利亚斯已被收复，卡斯蒂利亚叛乱几乎刚开始就逐渐平息的消息，让他从最焦虑的情绪中解脱出来。险些失去卡斯蒂利亚的经历让他陷入了深深的反思，而专注于赢得亨利的青睐似乎是一个切实可行的目标，可以让他暂时放下诸多思绪。有时，他的思绪就像一个漩涡，一旦陷入其中便会不断滑落，直到无法自拔，除非有新的挑战出现，迫使他集中精力。

Carlos was grateful for the trip. The news that Tordesillas had been recaptured and that the Castilian revolt was waning almost as soon as it began had freed him from his worst anxieties. Having come so close to losing Castile had plunged him into deep reflection, and focusing on winning Henry's favor seemed a concrete goal that would allow him to put aside so much contemplation. At times, his thoughts resembled a spiral he could easily enter and slide down until he was unable to escape unless a challenge presented itself that required his attention.

皇帝准备服从姑母的命令，在那个英国人面前表现得谦卑。在亨利面前，他毫不费力地就能压抑住自己的虚荣心。每次与叔叔见面，他都会被叔叔强势外向的举止所震慑，这与他自身的胆怯截然不同。他的声音与英国人的洪亮嗓音相比，如同受伤的鸟儿般凄厉，他们的身形仿佛出自不同的神祇之手。英国人的身躯如同巨人，而查理的身躯则如同诗人般柔美。

The emperor was prepared to obey his aunt's orders and display humility before the Englishman. It would take no effort for him to suppress his vanity in Henry's presence. Whenever they had been together, he had felt intimidated by his uncle's forceful and extroverted manner, so different from his own timidity. His voice sounded like that of a wounded bird next to the Briton's bellows, and their bodies seemed sculpted by different gods. The Englishman's was that of a titan; Charles's, that of a poet.

亨利说：“您的来访真是个惊喜。我们很荣幸能接待新加冕的皇帝。”

—Your visit is a pleasant surprise. We are honored to receive the newly crowned emperor— said Henry as he welcomed him.

—那么我很遗憾没能让你如愿以偿，因为独自出现在你面前的是你的侄子卡洛斯。

—I regret then not to give you such satisfaction, for the one who appears before you alone is Carlos, your nephew.

英国人微笑着看向哈布斯堡家族，然后与凯瑟琳拥抱在一起。

The Englishman smiled at the Habsburg as he melted into an embrace with Catherine.

“我们几乎没有时间准备配得上您的敬意，”这位西班牙女子道歉道。

—We've barely had time to prepare tributes worthy of you —the Spanish woman apologized.

——你真是帮了大忙。皇室的荣耀不过是一种笨重的伪装，而炫耀它也只是一场令人精疲力竭的闹剧。

—You're a relief. Imperial glory is a cumbersome disguise. And flaunting it is an exhausting charade.

查尔斯和凯瑟琳先行一步，以便王后能引领皇帝前往他的寝宫，他将在那里休息，然后再享用午餐。亨利走向沃尔西，沃尔西对招待会毫无热情。

Charles and Catherine went ahead so that the queen could show the emperor to his apartments, where he would rest before lunch. Henry approached Wolsey, who had followed the reception without any enthusiasm.

亨利宣称：“弗朗西斯应该羡慕查理的不是他的帝国，而是他的品格。”

—What Francis should envy about Charles is not his Empire, but his character —Henry declared.

红衣主教只能怜悯他主人的无辜。

The cardinal could only take pity on his lord's innocence.

—令人惊讶的是，那些鄙视荣耀的人，为了获得荣耀而毁了自己。

—It is striking that he who disdains glory has ruined himself to obtain it.

但亨利对他的话置若罔闻。脸部撞击法国土地的疼痛依然存在，相比之下，查理五世就像一剂抚慰剂，抚慰着他痛苦的回忆。

But Henry ignored his words. The impact of his face against the French soil still hurt, and Charles, compared to such a painful memory, was a balm.

皇帝旅途劳顿，休息之时，英国国王走进了妻子的寝宫。他躺在床上，就像他以前还渴望她时那样。

While the emperor rested from his journey, the English king entered his wife's chamber. He lay down on the bed, as he used to do when he still desired her.

“你侄子没有孩子，真是太可惜了。我宁愿把我们的小女儿嫁给他的儿子，而不是那个法国人的儿子。”

"It's a shame your nephew has no children. I would gladly marry our little girl to one of his sons, and not to the Frenchman's."

卡塔琳娜笑了。有时，她会感到害怕，因为她的丈夫在不知不觉中，正引导她走上她希望他走的路。

Catalina smiled. Sometimes it frightened her to what extent her husband, without realizing it, was leading her down the path she wanted him to follow.

—你看到的是挫折，但同时也有盈利的空间。

—You see a setback where there is room for profit.

 

 

 

 

午餐时分，宾客们畅饮了大量的佛兰德斯啤酒。亨利克制住自己不喝醉的冲动，以免再次遭到挑战。但他还是喝了些酒，以便能礼貌地微笑回应皇帝的每一句话。查理看到肉质鲜嫩，可以切开了。

Lunch was accompanied by plenty of Flemish beer. Henry refrained from getting drunk, lest he be challenged to another battle. But he did drink enough to greet each of the emperor's words with a polite smile. Charles saw that the meat was tender and ready to be carved.

拒绝法国人向你提出的结盟提议。

—Reject the alliance that the Frenchman proposes to you.

英国人做出了无助的表情。

The Briton made a gesture of helplessness.

我很乐意这么做。但我会失去女儿的婚约，我会为此深感遗憾。我只会用她未来的婚姻换取一段同样或更美好的姻缘。

—I would gladly do it. But I would lose my daughter's engagement, and I would deeply regret that. I would only exchange her future marriage for one that is equally or more worthy.

卡洛斯感到束手无策。

Carlos felt disarmed.

—你很清楚，我无法给你提供一个儿子来娶她。

—You know very well that I cannot offer you a son to marry her off to.

“你没有男人，但你却像个男人。”凯瑟琳说道。

—You have no man, yet you are a man —said Catherine.

哈布斯堡家族的这位成员不得不反复确认自己是否听懂了姑妈的话。他发现亨利丝毫没有惊讶之色。这是他们共同制定的计划。

The Habsburg had to repeat his aunt's words to himself to make sure he had understood correctly. He saw that Henry showed no surprise whatsoever. It was a plan they had both devised.

——跟玛丽亚订婚？你女儿才四岁！我得等一辈子才能娶她。

—Get engaged to Maria? Your daughter is barely four years old! I would have to wait a lifetime to marry her.

——弗朗西斯科计划攻击你。

—Francisco plans to attack you.

凯瑟琳的话如同利箭般击中了查尔斯。

Catherine's words struck Charles like a blazing arrow.

他一心只想赢你。他不再是法国国王，他是你的敌人。

—He is obsessed with your victory. He is no longer King of France. He is King against you.

皇帝听从叔父们的转述，得知了弗朗西斯对他发出的每一条威胁。他知道亨利会欺骗他，但凯瑟琳不会。卡斯蒂利亚刚刚平息，法国就可能向他宣战；而另一边，帝国正因路德的宣言而陷入狂热——这一切令他难以忍受。

The emperor listened to every threat Francis had made against him, as told by his uncles. He could expect deception from Henry, but not from Catherine. The prospect of France declaring war on him while Castile had only just barely been quelled, and on the other flank, the Empire was feverish with Luther's proclamations, was too intolerable for him to bear.

—但如果弗朗西斯攻击我，你的军队将与我的军队一起保卫我。

—But if Francis were to attack me, your troops would join mine to defend me.

恩里克没有预料到这种情况，他陷入了怀疑之中。

Enrique did not expect conditions, and he was plunged into doubt.

“家庭是纽带，政治是代价。”卡洛斯说道。

—Family is the bond. Politics, the price— said Carlos.

 

 

 

 

在启程前往弗兰德斯之前，查理见到了他的未婚妻。这位年轻的姑娘向他行屈膝礼，并宣布十年后她将成为一位幸福的皇后。凯瑟琳和亨利作为见证人，温柔地笑着。查理也模仿他们的笑容，但他知道，迟早有一天，他注定要违背这个承诺。

Before departing for Flanders, Charles met his betrothed. The young girl curtsied to him and announced that in ten years she would be a happy empress. Catherine and Henry, witnesses, smiled tenderly. Charles imitated them, but he knew that he was doomed, sooner or later, to break that promise.

 

 

 

 

回到梅赫伦后，皇帝再次陷入了困境的漩涡。卡斯蒂利亚一直按兵不动，而他自己也违背了法英之间的盟约。但如果他不从自己的轻率中吸取教训，庆祝好运就毫无意义。在西班牙，只有当哈德良拥有足够的权力时，冲突才能得到控制；信任他人的能力是维持其领土的唯一途径。他的领土如此众多，假装所有决定都由他一人做出，这看似矛盾，实则反而会让他失去控制。而信任只能源于公正。他害怕被母亲背叛，是因为他知道自己对待母亲的方式有失体统。任何对他表现出的忠诚，都将源于他自身的慷慨。

Upon returning to Mechelen, the emperor once again succumbed to the spiral of his tribulations. Castile had held back, and he himself had broken the pact between the French and the English. But there was no point in celebrating his good fortune if he did not learn from his imprudence. In Spain, the conflict had only been contained when Hadrian possessed the powers to do so; trust in the abilities of others was the only way to maintain his domains. With so many of them, pretending that every decision depended solely on him seemed, paradoxically, to be a recipe for losing control. And trust could only spring from justice. The fear he had felt of being betrayed by his mother stemmed from knowing that his treatment of her had been undignified. Any loyalty shown to him would be a product of his own generosity.

 

 

 

 

—我向你们介绍新任奥地利大公：我的兄弟。

—I present to you the new Archduke of Austria: my brother.

弗兰德斯宫殿的皇家大厅里挤满了人，其他任何头衔的授予仪式也一样。公爵、伯爵和高级教士们都应查理的要求聚集于此。费迪南听到任命的宣布，随后是众人的掌声。之后，他仍然有些恍惚，但还是接受了所有人的祝贺。这个头衔立刻为他赢得了尊重，政治也成了他参与的每一次谈话的焦点。他的观点不再是一位流亡王子的观点。

The royal hall of the palace in Flanders was packed to capacity, as was any other title. Dukes, counts, and high-ranking members of the clergy had gathered at Charles's behest. Ferdinand heard the announcement of his appointment and then the applause of those assembled. Afterward, still somewhat dazed, he allowed himself to be congratulated by everyone. The title earned him immediate respect, and politics became the focus of every conversation in which he participated. His opinion was no longer that of an exiled prince.

费尔南多知道现在不是和哥哥说话的时候，但在一次三三两两的谈话中，他无意间瞥见了哥哥一眼。那一瞬间，房间仿佛消失了，房间里的所有人也随之消失，取而代之的是巴利亚多利德的乡村景色，野兽们在追逐它们的兄弟俩的笑声中四处逃窜。不知为何，他知道卡洛斯也正身处同样的梦境之中。

Fernando knew it wasn't the time to talk to his brother, but, in the middle of one of those small groups, he caught a glance from him. For a moment the room vanished, and with it everyone in it, and all around him stretched a countryside of Valladolid where beasts fled from the two brothers, who laughed as they chased them. Somehow, he knew that Carlos was living the same dream.

你将会成为一位伟大的皇帝，因为你有能力战胜恐惧。

—You will be a great emperor. For you are capable of acting against your fears.

卡洛斯很感激姑妈的话。慷慨是他一直在努力塑造的品格中缺失的一环，而找到它让他确信，无论未来会面临多少磨难，无论有多少叛乱、异端和敌对的君王横亘在他面前，他都不再恐惧。未来充满未知，但他的精神正变得坚如磐​​石，足以抵御一切。

Carlos appreciated his aunt's words. Generosity was the missing piece in the character he had been building, and having found it convinced him that no matter how many obstacles he faced, no matter how many revolts, heretics, and rival kings crossed his path, he would no longer be afraid. The future was uncertain, but his spirit was becoming a rock capable of withstanding anything.

6

6

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

马丁·路德听到屋外传来马蹄声。他划了个十字，走到门口，临走前，最后看了一眼这间多年来见证了他所有思绪和恐惧的房间。他觉得房间里几乎空无一物；或许，空无一物是他自己体内的？确认自己带着皇帝赐予他的通行证，可以安心前往沃尔姆斯参加会议后，他轻轻地关上了身后的门；多日的饥饿让他身体虚弱。

Martin Luther heard the sound of horses' hooves outside his house. He crossed himself, went to the door, and just before leaving, took one last look at the room that for years had witnessed his thoughts and fears. It seemed to him that there was hardly any air left in it; or was it in him? After making sure he had the safe-conduct pass the emperor had granted him to attend their meeting in Worms without fear, he gently closed the door behind him; the many days without appetite had left him weak.

停在外面的马车简朴却宽敞。车厢里，三个好友探出头来，他们决定陪同路德同行。他们的脸上既流露出此刻的庄严，也流露出对这位修士勇气的钦佩。车夫忧心忡忡地看了路德一眼；他要载着一个异端分子从维滕贝格到沃尔姆斯，行程四百公里；这十四天的路程，任何一个正统基督徒都可能随时袭击他们，终结这场撼动德国乃至他们自身的宗教革命。

The carriage waiting outside was humble but spacious. From inside, the heads of three good friends, who had decided to accompany him on the journey, peered out. Their faces reflected the gravity of the moment, but also the admiration they felt for the friar's courage. The driver cast an apprehensive glance at Luther; he was going to have to drive a heretic for four hundred kilometers, from Wittenberg to Worms; fourteen days' journey during which any orthodox Christian could attack them and put an end to the theological revolution that was shaking Germany, and to them as well.

“你确定自己在做什么吗？”他斗胆问修士。

"Are you sure about what you're doing?" he dared to ask the friar.

路德的反应很简单，就是猛地跳上车，要求出发。

Luther's response was simply to jump vigorously onto the vehicle and demand that the journey begin.

 

 

 

 

旅程的最初几个小时，车厢里一片寂静。四月阳光灿烂，但马车篷布上却笼罩着一层阴影：那是扬·胡斯的阴影。一百年前，这位波西米亚神学家的人生轨迹与路德颇为相似；他因谴责罗马的腐败而被逐出教会，随后又被皇帝召见，要求他觐见皇帝，解释自己的教义，并收回那些使他被视为异端的言论。胡斯前往觐见皇帝时，随身携带了皇帝的通行证；但那张通行证与他一同被烧毁在火刑柱上。

During the first hours of the journey, silence reigned. It was a bright April, but a shadow hung over the canvas covering the carriage: that of Jan Hus. A hundred years earlier, the Bohemian theologian had lived a life similar to Luther's; his proclamations against the corruption of Rome had been followed by excommunication, and this, in turn, by a summons from the emperor to appear before him, explain his doctrines, and recant those that made him a heretic. When he set out to meet the emperor, Hus had also carried with him an imperial safe-conduct; but the paper was burned with him at the stake.

得知查理的传唤后，许多人试图劝阻路德，因为他们确信这是个逮捕他的陷阱。“记住胡斯！记住胡斯！”他们反复念叨着。这位修士本人也犹豫了数日。他辗转难眠，脑海中浮现出熊熊烈火的景象。但最终，一道光芒，而非火焰，照亮了他的内心：他的使命是摧毁教会这座腐朽的大厦，而这样的使命无疑充满风险。现在是时候以英雄般的沉着面对这一切了。他的话语已经在德国人中引起了强烈的共鸣。如果他能活下来，他就能继续宣讲这些话语；如果死亡在等待着他，他的殉道将激励他的追随者走向胜利。他放弃了彻底摆脱恐惧的不可能任务：他会努力不让恐惧影响他的决定，但恐惧会像以往一样伴随他左右。令他惊讶的是，他的追随者们对他的敬仰之情，仿佛他已经彻底摆脱了恐惧。只有路德自己才知道，他自幼便承受着多么深重的痛苦。幼年时，他每日饱受父母的责打，骨骼颤抖。他的童年如同漫漫长夜，永无黎明，这让他终生心怀恐惧和不安。二十二岁那年，一场暴风雨席卷乡间，一道闪电击中了他附近，这痛苦瞬间爆发。路德目睹了这电光火石般的灾难，他知道自己的末日已至。他只来得及向上帝许愿，如果上帝能救他，他将完全臣服于祂。他很快便履行了誓言，但教会生活并未平息他内心深处不断滋生的恐惧。后来，他已成为一名修士，前往罗马，却发现他信仰的中心竟如同巴比伦一般，而那些最权威的宗教人物也不过是沉溺于奢靡享乐的放荡之徒，这令他感到无比厌恶。那份将他与上帝紧紧相连的纯粹敬畏，与如此轻浮放荡的生活方式格格不入。人类灵魂与造物主关系的真相何在？如果教皇容忍如此腐败，甚至乐在其中，他又怎能作为人与神之间的中介？自此以后，清洗教会的执念便一直萦绕着他。面对火刑柱令他不寒而栗，但对于一个在恐惧中长大的人来说，走向火刑柱不过是继续活下去的必要手段。

Upon learning of Charles's summons, many had tried to dissuade Luther from what they were convinced was a trap to arrest him. "Remember Hus! Remember Hus!" they repeated. The friar himself had hesitated for days. His sleepless nights had been filled with visions of flames. But finally, a light, not of fire, had broken through in his mind: his destiny was to destroy the rotten edifice of the Church, and such a mission would undoubtedly entail risks. The time had come to face them with the serenity of a hero. His words had already resonated deeply among the Germans. If he lived, he could continue preaching them; if death awaited him, his martyrdom would spur his followers on to victory. He renounced the impossible task of completely ridding himself of fear: he would try not to let it influence his decisions, but it would accompany him, as it always had. He was astonished that his followers regarded him with the admiration reserved for someone who has shed all fear. Only Luther knew the depth of anguish he had carried within him since childhood. During his early years, his bones had trembled daily under the blows of his parents. His childhood had been a long night that never dawned, leaving him with a nervous distrust. At twenty-two, this anguish erupted during a storm in the countryside when lightning struck near him. Luther saw this electrical scourge before him and knew his time had come. He only had time to promise God that he would surrender himself to Him if He saved him. He soon fulfilled his vow, but church life did not quell the fears that festered within him. When, some time later, already a friar, he traveled to Rome and saw that the seat of his faith resembled a Babylon and that the most authoritative religious figures were nothing more than unrestrained hedonists surrounded by luxury, he felt revulsion. The purity of the fear that had bound him to God was utterly incompatible with such frivolous debauchery. Where was the truth of the human soul in its relationship with the Creator? How could the Pope stand as intermediary between man and divinity if he tolerated such corruption and wallowed in it with gusto? The obsession with purging the Church had haunted him ever since. Facing the stake chilled his blood, but for one who had grown up in fear, walking toward it was simply a matter of continuing to live.

当他们经过一个村庄附近时，人群突然围住了马车，静默的冥想和扬·胡斯的幽灵也随之消失。透过遮盖他们的帆布，路德和他的朋友们隐约看到人群中传来一阵激动的呼喊声。帆布掩盖了他们的喊叫，以至于听不清楚。直到修士终于鼓起勇气走到车外，他才听清他们在说什么。

The silent meditations and the ghost of Jan Hus vanished abruptly when, as they passed near a village, a crowd surrounded the carriage. Through the canvas covering them, Luther and his friends could make out a stirring mass. The fabric muffled their shouts until they were incomprehensible. Only when the friar finally dared to step outside was he able to understand what they were saying.

感谢上帝救了我们！勇敢！勇敢吧，亲爱的路德！

—God bless you for saving us! Courage! Courage, beloved Luther!

人群拥抱了他。他们给他面包和鲜花，拥抱他，像慈父一样微笑着看着他。

The crowd embraced him. They offered him bread and flowers, hugged him, and smiled at him like a good father.

第二天、第三天、第四天，同样的场景再次上演。人们视路德为德国灵魂的救赎者，相信在他的帮助下，德国人会转向神，并在此过程中将帝国从罗马的枷锁中解放出来。

The scene was repeated the next day, and the next, and the next. People saw in Luther the redeemer of German souls who, with his help, would turn towards God, and in the process would free the Empire from the Roman yoke.

如果他是英雄，那么反派就一定是卡洛斯。

And if he was the hero, the villain had to be Carlos.

 

 

 

 

自从查理决定无视梵蒂冈的命令，给路德一个解释的机会后，无数张面孔便出现在他周围，如同戴着戏剧面具般冷峻。在希耶夫尔看来，查理的宽宏大量无异于自杀。邀请这位修士在整个帝国议会面前发言，意味着为他的异端邪说提供了一个平台，无论会面结果如何，这只会让这些异端邪说传播得更广。这个异端已经用尽了最后的机会；除了逮捕他、判他死刑，并确保他的骨灰沉入最卑微的河流深处之外，别无他法。加蒂纳拉虽然没有那么激烈，但也怀疑查理的骑士精神是否掩盖着某种天真。皇帝唯一能找到的支持，只有他的兄弟。

Ever since he decided to disregard the Vatican's order and give Luther the opportunity to explain himself, countless faces, as stern as theatrical masks, had appeared around the emperor. For Chièvres, Charles's magnanimity was nothing short of suicidal. Inviting the friar to speak before an entire Imperial Diet meant giving his heterodoxies a platform that would only further spread them, regardless of the outcome of the encounter. The heretic had already used up his last chance; there was no other solution but to arrest him, condemn him, and ensure that his ashes sank to the depths of the least worthy of rivers. Gattinara, though less vehement, wondered if Charles's chivalric ideals weren't masking a certain naiveté. The only support the emperor found was that of his brother.

自从被授予奥地利大公头衔后，斐迪南从昔日慵懒地躺在天鹅绒沙发上，一跃成为帝国议会的重要成员。随着两人交往的频繁，他和查理意识到他们都渴望修复彼此的关系。狩猎之旅重拾，关于女士们的秘密也开始流传。他们之间产生了只有彼此才能理解的玩笑，为了增进彼此的默契，他们也会在众人面前分享这些玩笑。

Since being granted the title of Austrian archduke, Ferdinand had gone from languishing on velvet sofas to serving on imperial councils. With the frequency of their interactions, he and Charles realized they were eager to mend their bond. Hunting trips resumed. Confidences about ladies began. Inside jokes arose, jokes only they understood, which they shared in front of others to feel a sense of complicity.

费尔南多心思敏锐，他的兄弟也注意到了这一点。由于年轻，他不像希耶夫尔和加蒂纳拉那样博闻强识，但他天生具有一种未经世事磨砺的洞察力，这种洞察力赋予了他的视野一种纯真而精准的力量。在路德事件上，他认为采取专制手段是危险的。德国人民会认为这位修士是为他们而死的，而复仇很快就会到来，要么以起义的形式，要么以对这位殉道者的崇敬的形式。

Fernando was astute, and his brother noticed it. His youth had prevented him from having had time to accumulate the thousands of facts that men like Chièvres and Gattinara possessed, but he had an innate perspicacity, untouched by experience, which gave his vision an innocent and unerring force. Regarding the Luther affair, opting for an authoritarian solution seemed to him a dangerous measure. The people of Germany would judge that the friar had died for them, and revenge would not be long in coming, either in the form of an uprising or devotion to the martyr.

——那么，大公爵，你有什么提议？任由异端邪说像油污一样蔓延吗？

—And what do you propose, Archduke? To let heresy spread like an oil slick?

希耶夫尔总是用一种仿佛神明被迫与最卑微的造物共存的语气与他交谈。

Chièvres always addressed him with the tone of a god forced to share space with the lowest of creation.

“罗马有责任确保这场运动失去力量，”卡洛斯插话道，“因为正是罗马煽动了这场运动，所以它难辞其咎。”

—It is Rome's responsibility to ensure that the movement loses strength—Carlos interjected. —For it bears the blame for having instigated it.

“你同意路德的观点吗？”加蒂纳拉问道。

"Do you agree with Luther?" Gattinara asked.

“没有人像我一样对他的亵渎之言感到如此厌恶，”皇帝回答说，“但即使是最顺从的信徒，也无法忽视教会的腐败。教皇最好听取批评，改正自己的错误，这样那些谴责他的人就会停止谴责，也不会逃离他的怀抱。”

“No one finds his blasphemies as repugnant as I do,” replied the emperor, “but the corruption of the Church is not lost on even the most submissive of the faithful.
