The Pope would do well to listen to the criticisms and correct his faults, so that those who censure him will cease doing so and not flee from his bosom.”

议员们仍然心存疑虑。教会腐败堕落、背弃自身教义几乎是公开的秘密。但指望它改变，就好比指望石头能被塑造一样不切实际。

The councilors remained skeptical. That the Church was corrupt and treacherous to its own precepts was hardly a secret. But expecting it to change was like wishing stones could be molded.

——扬·胡斯。——希耶夫尔念出这个名字，就像念咒语一样；仿佛只要提起这个名字，就能改变皇帝的想法。

—Jan Hus. —Chièvres uttered the name like someone uttering a spell; as if simply mentioning it would be enough to change the emperor's opinion.

“他的死引发了血腥骚乱，”卡洛斯说。

"His death sparked bloody riots," said Carlos.

——随着岁月流逝，他们逐渐销声匿迹。叛乱者最终回归罗马的统治。我们的修士也将如此。

—They faded away over the years. The rebels eventually returned to obedience to Rome. The same will happen with our friar.

“如果胡斯没有被烧死在火刑柱上，谁知道会发生什么呢？”凯撒问道，“或许那些叛乱就能避免了。”

"Who knows what would have happened if Hus hadn't burned at the stake?" asked Caesar. "Perhaps those revolts would have been avoided."

——或者，你今天可能就是一个异端帝国的统治者。

—Or perhaps you would be the ruler of a heretical empire today.

查理脑海中浮现出一幅基督教世界如同摩西划过河面般分裂的未来景象，他的胃像受惊的孩子一样揪了起来。他甚至想过一见到路德就逮捕他，即便这意味着背叛这位修士，也背叛自己。然而就在那天早上，来自卡斯蒂利亚的消息让他意识到，在旧火尚未熄灭之际，他不该再添新火。

For a moment, Charles imagined a future in which Christendom was divided like the waters of Moses, and his stomach clenched like a frightened child's. He considered arresting Luther as soon as he saw him, even if it meant betraying the friar and himself. But that very morning, news arrived from Castile that convinced him he shouldn't light a fire while another was still burning.

 

 

 

 

在写给查理的信中，乌得勒支的阿德里安试图掩饰自己的焦虑。他深知国王对挫折的敏感。他直截了当地陈述了卡斯蒂利亚的现实，言辞平淡：“收复托尔德西利亚斯之后，并未取得任何其他胜利。领主们担心他们的封地会被叛军夺走，作为报复，而他们又不愿与叛军正面交锋。他们只愿意出兵，前提是王室要给予他们财富和比他们目前拥有的更多的头衔作为补偿。您很清楚，我们的国库已经捉襟见肘，我斗胆劝您不要用荣誉来支付这种勒索。如果以如此高昂的代价换取他们的忠诚，那无异于屈服。我们唯一的希望寄托在共产主义者之间的不和上，据说这种不和每天都在加剧……”

In the letter Adrian of Utrecht sent to Charles, he had tried to conceal his anxiety. He was well aware of the king's sensitivity to frustration. He bluntly stated the reality of Castile, without dramatic words: “The recapture of Tordesillas was not followed by any other victories. The lords fear that their fiefdoms will be seized as an act of revenge by the rebels, whom they prefer not to confront. They would only be willing to lend their armies if the Crown compensated them with wealth and more titles than they currently possess. You know full well that the depths of our coffers are already showing, and I dare to advise you not to pay such blackmail with honors. Their loyalty would be submission if obtained at such a high price. Our only hope is the discord among the Comuneros, which, they say, grows with each dawn…”

 

 

 

 

胡安·德·帕迪利亚离开托莱多的那晚，繁星满天。他把这当作吉兆。随行的士兵们神情肃穆地跟在他身旁。帕迪利亚回头望去：在遥远的距离，他的家乡就像他们即将离开的那些闪耀的石头之一。玛丽亚会在其中一块石头里哭泣。她原本希望与他同行，但这座城市需要一位领袖来领导这场运动，她不希望他们的儿子成为孤儿。帕迪利亚的口袋里装着妻子的一封信。“你是燃烧大地、使其重生的火焰。我是守护这火焰的人。”

The night Juan de Padilla left Toledo, the sky was overflowing with stars. He took it as a good omen. The men who accompanied him rode beside him with the seriousness of good soldiers. Padilla looked back: at that distance, his home was one of those illuminated stones they were now leaving behind. Inside one of them, María would be weeping. Her wish would have been to accompany him, but the city needed a leader for the movement, and she didn't want their son to feel orphaned. Padilla carried a letter from his wife in his pocket. "You are the fire that burns the earth to make it reborn. I am the one who guards the flame."

托尔德西利亚斯战役失败后，市民运动不再是一支统一的力量。对最终失败的恐惧使他们都变成了精于谋略的战略家，很快便形成了两个派系：一派主张起义应该转向反对领主，这样才能彻底、永久地解放被压迫者；另一派则担心，反对贵族会迫使他们倒向王室，从而助其取得胜利。争论没完没了，同样的论点从同样的人口中重复出来。帕迪利亚深知特权阶层的想法：他们唯一的利益在于维护自身的特权地位。他们绝不会支持像他这样的起义；至多，他们会利用起义为自己谋利，但这种利用不会长久。

After the failure at Tordesillas, the Comuneros had ceased to be a unified force. The fear of ultimate defeat transformed them all into expert strategists, and two factions soon emerged: one argued that the revolt should turn against the lords, so that the liberation of the oppressed would be complete and permanent; the other feared that turning against the nobles would drive them into the arms of the Crown, thus propelling it to victory. The discussions became endless. The same arguments came from the same mouths. Padilla knew well how the privileged thought: their sole interest lay in maintaining their privileged status. They would never support a revolt like his; at most, they would use it to their advantage, though not for long.

帕迪利亚对平民百姓说：“迟早有一天，贵族们会向国王俯首称臣。他们从我们这里得不到任何好处，从国王那里，他们只能保住或提升自己的荣誉。”

"Sooner or later, the lords will bow before the king," Padilla said, addressing the commoners. "They can gain nothing from us. From him, they can only preserve or increase their honors."

“既然你们掌握了这么多证据，那就给我们解释一下，为什么他们没有继续向王室提供援助？”出身名门的战士佩德罗·吉隆插话道。

—If you see it with so much evidence, explain to us, why haven't they continued to provide aid to the Crown? —intervened Pedro Girón, a fighter of good lineage.

——因为他们等着她受苦到需要他们的时候。他们怀念曾经享有的地位和特权，那些都被伊丽莎白女王夺走了。

—Because they are waiting for her to suffer enough to need them. They miss the importance and privileges they once enjoyed, those that Queen Elizabeth took away from them.

——这就是他们全部的动机吗？难道他们就没有对正义的渴望吗？

—Is that all that motivates them? Don't they also yearn for justice?

—它的独特之处在于正义并不存在。

—Its distinction comes from the fact that justice does not exist.

吉隆和帕迪利亚交换了一个充满敌意的眼神。议会最终决定支持吉隆。他的理由并非人人都能接受，但托莱多王室因拥立胡安娜女王失败而声名受损。他们不再信任他；换个人就行了。

Girón and Padilla exchanged a rival glance. The council decided in favor of the former. His reasons didn't convince everyone, but the Toledan's prestige had been tarnished by the failed attempt to place Queen Juana on the throne. They no longer believed in him; any other would do.

帕迪利亚和玛丽亚随后撤退到托莱多，虽然失望，但并不认为自己失败了：他们坚信没有比他们更优秀的领导者。时间证明了他们的判断：吉隆和他那脆弱的原则最终叛逃，加入了敌军。叛军很快召回了他们这位昔日的队长，他顾不上受伤的自尊心：他渴望重返战场。

Padilla and María then retreated to Toledo, disappointed but not considering themselves failures: they were certain there were no better leaders than themselves. Time proved them right: Girón and his fragile principles one day deserted to join the enemy. The rebels soon summoned their former captain, who ignored his wounded pride: he was eager to return to the fight.

离开托莱多几天后，帕迪利亚再次站在他的军队面前。他察觉到士兵们在他这位被背叛的领袖面前投来羞愧的目光，他们的面容比那些送别他的士兵更加憔悴。他用沉重的声音敦促他们忘记过去——托尔德西利亚斯、吉隆，以及他的缺席。他们必须相信他，鼓起勇气。很快，他们就要发起进攻了。

Days after leaving Toledo, Padilla stood before his army once more. He sensed furtive glances of shame before the betrayed leader and faces more gaunt than those that had bid him farewell. In a grave voice, he urged them to forget the past—Tordesillas, Girón, his absence. They had to trust him and summon their courage. Soon they would launch an attack.

 

 

 

 

阿德里亚诺预感到叛军会利用贵族们的懒惰，便致信葡萄牙宫廷，请求提供火药和兵力。起义初期，曼努埃尔国王曾向卡斯蒂利亚王室运送过物资。但阿德里亚诺的这次请求，得到的却只是象征性的物资，以及一封解释信，信中说葡萄牙国王已病入膏肓，无法亲自处理此事。

Adriano, sensing that the rebels would exploit the nobles' indolence, wrote to the Portuguese court requesting gunpowder and men. In the early stages of the uprising, King Manuel had sent supplies to the Crown of Castile. But this new request from Adriano was met with a shipment that was little more than symbolic and a letter explaining that the Portuguese monarch could not address the matter as he would have liked, as he was on the verge of death.

 

 

 

 

曼努埃尔的痛苦持续了数日。他的女儿伊莎贝尔寸步不离地守在他身边，凭借着坚强的意志，她强忍着泪水；她希望父亲能够安详地离去，因为她知道父亲一直教导她节制自律。与此同时，她的弟弟胡安日夜为父亲的灵魂祈祷，泪水盈眶。这位未来的继承人年方十九，终日忧郁。他总觉得生活中缺少了什么，或许是有些事情让他不堪重负。莱昂诺尔成为他的继母，更加剧了他的忧郁，因为他第一眼见到她就爱上了她。

Manuel's agony lasted several days. His daughter Isabel never left his side, and thanks to her courage, she managed not to cry; she wished her father could depart peacefully, knowing he had raised her with temperance. Meanwhile, her brother Juan's eyes welled with tears as he prayed day and night for their father's soul. The future heir was nineteen years old and perpetually sad. He always felt something was missing, or perhaps something was too much. Leonor becoming his stepmother only intensified his melancholy, for he had fallen in love with her the moment he met her.

查理的妹妹抵达葡萄牙宫廷时毫无热情；面对这场包办婚姻，她唯一剩下的自由便是装出一副逆来顺受的样子。这种坦诚深深吸引了约翰，他早已习惯了父亲和妹妹的情感伪装。他和埃莉诺年龄相仿，难得的几次交谈中，他们总能彼此微笑。她对丈夫，也就是国王，只有一种超然的爱慕之情，而这位王位继承人立刻察觉到了这一点。他知道父亲和她之间不过是一场协议，这让他幻想亲吻她时，不至于觉得自己像个叛徒。

Charles's sister had arrived at the Portuguese court without any enthusiasm; feigning complacency was the only remaining margin of freedom she had in the face of this forced marriage. Such honesty captivated John, who was accustomed to the emotional armor of his father and sister. He and Eleanor were close in age, and on the rare occasions they spoke, they made each other smile. She felt nothing more than dispassionate affection for her husband, the king, and the heir noticed this immediately. Knowing that there was nothing more than an agreement between his father and her allowed him to feel less like a traitor when he fantasized about kissing her.

国王去世后，在数百场悼念活动和弥撒之后，已经坐在葡萄牙王位上的约翰听取了他妹妹伊莎贝尔的请求。

After the king's death, and after the hundreds of condolences and masses, John, already seated on the throne of Portugal, listened to the pleas of his sister Isabel.

西班牙和葡萄牙之间的联盟已经破裂，必须恢复。立即致信皇帝。我与他的会面刻不容缓。

—The union between Spain and Portugal, which has been broken, must be restored. Write to the Emperor without delay. My meeting with him cannot wait any longer.

胡安答应了她，但每次他强迫自己坐下来写下妹妹的愿望时，他的手都会僵硬，大脑一片空白。那些他一直想不起来的话语，在莱昂诺尔意识到自己必须前往帝国时，却自然而然地涌上心头。

Juan promised her he would, but each time he forced himself to sit down to write down his sister's wish, his hand went stiff and his mind blank. The words, which had eluded the paper, readily came to him when Leonor realized she had to leave for the Empire.

夫人，请不要离开宫廷。

—Do not abandon the court, my lady.

—殿下，您太客气了，但是一旦失去了王冠，我在这里的存在就毫无意义了。

—You are very kind, Your Highness, but once stripped of the crown, my presence here is meaningless.

“你错了！”胡安为自己刚才的失言感到脸红，压低了声音。“除非你想离开。”

"You're wrong!" Juan blushed at his own outburst and lowered his tone. "Unless your wish is to leave."

莱昂诺尔否认了这一点。尽管她与曼努埃尔国王的婚姻并非出于任何魔法，但在葡萄牙，她生平第一次不再仅仅是随从的一员。她成为了王后，但更重要的是，她成为了一个独立的人。回到哥哥身边，履行她的职责，意味着她将再次失去自由意志。她将再次受制于查理的意志。

Leonor denied it. Although no spell had been cast upon her marriage to King Manuel, there in Portugal, for the first time in her life, she had ceased to be merely part of a retinue. She had become queen, but above all, someone. Returning to her brother's side, as was her duty, would mean losing her free will once again. She would find herself once more at the mercy of Charles's will.

“你这话好像我能逃脱命运似的，”莱昂诺尔回答道，“我的寡居对皇帝来说就像一份礼物。他可以利用这一点，把我嫁给任何符合他政治目的的人。”

“You speak as if I could escape my fate,” Leonor replied. “My widowhood is like a gift to the emperor. He can use it to unite me with whomever suits his political agenda.”

胡安想象着她依偎在另一个男人怀里，嫉妒得浑身紧绷。

Juan imagined her in another man's arms and tensed with jealousy.

“有些人能避免这种命运。”他的声音听起来像是在恳求。

"There are those who avoid that fate." His voice sounded like a plea.

殿下，我对修道院也没什么兴趣。

—Your Highness, the convent doesn't appeal to me either.

“写信给你的兄弟，”国王建议道，“告诉他，在我父亲去世后，你必须振作起来。”

"Write to your brother," the king suggested. "Tell him that you must recover your spirits after the death of my father."

但我为什么要推迟不可避免的事情呢？

—But why would I postpone the inevitable?

胡安听到这话，真想跑过去抱住她的腿，热情地亲吻她的手，但他只敢说：

In response, Juan wanted to run to her, hug her legs, and kiss her hands fervently, but he only dared to say:

—因为贵公司令我感到满意。

—Because your company is pleasing to me.

房间里一片静谧，却又透着一丝活力。莱昂诺尔感到一阵颤栗，迅速蔓延至全身，无一幸免。她不明白为什么自己和胡安会突然如此对视，仿佛有无数根丝线牵引着他们走向拥抱。她感到一阵眩晕，便请求去休息。躺在床上，目光凝视着天花板蜿蜒的图案，莱昂诺尔觉得现在离开还为时过早。

The room was enveloped in a vibrant silence. Leonor felt a shiver run through her, spreading across her entire body, leaving not a single inch undisturbed. She couldn't quite understand why she and Juan were suddenly gazing at each other as if countless threads were pulling them toward an embrace. She felt faint and asked to go and rest. Once lying on the bed, her eyes fixed on the sinuous patterns of the ceiling, Leonor decided it was still too soon to leave.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在法国，英格兰国王亨利在金缕会晤中怒火的余波仍未消散。许多人斥责他们的国王愚蠢——当然，这些斥责总是以几乎听不见的耳语进行——因为他在最不利于国家利益的时候展现出了好胜心。

Meanwhile, in France, the echoes of Henry of England's anger at the meeting at the Field of Cloth of Gold had not yet faded. There were many who called their king stupid—always, of course, in almost inaudible whispers—for having displayed his competitiveness when it was least in the kingdom's best interest.

然而，弗朗西斯科已不再为那件事烦恼。事实上，与所有人的看法相反，他为自己即使在摔跤比赛中也需要胜利而感到自豪。正是在这种自我满足的状态下，他得知亨利违背了之前与他签订的子女未来联姻的协议。英国君主的女儿如今已许配给了皇帝。

Francisco, however, was no longer bothered by that incident. In fact, contrary to everyone else's opinion, he was proud that he had needed victory even in a wrestling match. And it was in this state of self-satisfaction that he received the news that Henry had spurned the agreement signed with him for their children to marry in the future. The English monarch's daughter was now betrothed to the emperor.

根特的查理。永远是根特的查理。帝国？都归他。与英格兰的联盟？全都归他。接下来会发生什么？什么？什么？！

Charles of Ghent. Always Charles of Ghent. The Empire? For him. The alliance with England? All his. What would come next? What? What?!

亨利对皇帝的背叛——那份荒谬的承诺竟然要花数年才能兑现！——在弗朗西斯看来如此残酷，他只能从自己的认知出发来解读：上帝在考验他。自从他在马里尼亚诺战役中获胜，夺取米兰以来，已经过去了六年。那次胜利让他心满意足，直到帝国岌岌可危，他才感到需要再次征服。就在那时，根特的查理出现在他的视野中。据了解他的人说，他身材矮小，毫不起眼，此前只是法国的一个附庸，偶然间被安排在了西班牙的统治之下——其他继承人的死亡和疯狂为他扫清了道路。法国国王明白，哈布斯堡家族不断羞辱他，是全能的上帝在激励他重返初次征服时的辉煌。还有什么比让一个平庸之辈成为他野心的绊脚石更能激起他的斗志呢？弗朗西斯科认为卡洛斯就像一只找到了进入他身体的昆虫：相对于他来说微不足道，但却能让他的生活变得痛苦不堪。

Henry's disloyalty to the emperor—with that absurd commitment that would take years to materialize!—struck Francis as so cruel that he could only interpret it in the way his senses allowed: God was testing him. Six years had passed since his victory at Marignano, with which he won Milan. That success had satiated him enough that he hadn't felt the need to seek another until the Empire was at stake. And it was then that the figure of Charles of Ghent appeared on his horizon, small and unremarkable, according to those who knew him, until then a mere vassal of France whom chance had placed in the government of Spain—the death and madness of the other heirs clearing the way for him. The French king understood that, through the repeated humiliations the Habsburg was inflicting upon him, the Almighty was spurring him on to return to the grandeur of that first conquest. What better way to provoke him than by turning a mediocre man into a constant obstacle to his ambitions? Francisco thought of Carlos as an insect that had found a way into his body: minuscule in relation to him, but capable of making his life miserable.

 

 

 

 

西班牙方面有什么最新消息吗？帝国方面呢？

—Are there any updates from Spain? And from the Empire?

蒙莫朗西感到困惑的是，近来法国的枢密院会议总是以讨论外国局势开场。而且这种习惯似乎越来越根深蒂固，因为弗朗西斯越来越渴望了解所有与皇帝有关的事情。与这种权力斗争相比，法国的事务在君主看来就像是繁琐的文书工作。

Montmorency was puzzled by the fact that, lately, the French councils always opened with a question about the situation in foreign territories. And the habit seemed to be taking hold, for Francis was increasingly anxious to be informed of everything related to the emperor. French affairs, compared to this rivalry, seemed to the monarch like tedious paperwork.

显然，叛军尚未被摄政王哈德良的命令镇压。

—Apparently, the rebels have not yet been subdued by the command of the regent Hadrian.

弗朗西斯眼中闪烁着喜悦的光芒，说道：

Francis's eyes shone with joy as he said:

——于是，他害怕极了，躲藏在帝国境内，逃避面对挑战……

—And, frightened, he hides in the Empire to avoid facing that challenge…

—我并不认为你很勇敢，但今天从德国传出的消息似乎证明了你留在那里是值得的。

—I don't presume you're brave, but the news that has come out of Germany today seems to justify your stay there.

国王走向蒙莫朗西，仿佛要从他胸口掏出情报一般。

The king advanced towards Montmorency as if he were about to extract the information from his chest.

你面临什么？

—What are you facing?

——对一位修士说。

—To a friar.

弗朗西斯对此感到失望。他原本希望查理的遭遇如同圣经中的惩罚：战争、瘟疫或君主的背叛。

Francis reacted with disappointment. He had hoped that Charles's troubles were like biblical punishments: wars, epidemics, or betrayals by princes.

——难道仅仅是一个修士就把他关在那里吗？

—Is a mere friar keeping him there?

罗马已将他逐出教会。

—Rome has excommunicated him.

——就像其他许多人一样。

—Like so many others.

——萨克森的腓特烈也支持他。成千上万的德国人也支持他。

— …And Frederick of Saxony supports him. As do thousands of Germans.

这件事突然引起了君主的兴趣。

The matter suddenly became interesting to the monarch.

他已召他前往沃尔姆斯议会。许多人认为，这次会议对皇帝来说绝无可能……

—He has summoned him to the Diet of Worms. According to many, there is no way that meeting will end in success for the emperor…

国王听完顾问的话，细细品味着每一个字：

The king finished his advisor's sentence, savoring each word:

——因为如果他判他死刑，就会激起民众的愤怒；如果他释放他，就会加剧帝国的分裂。

— …for if he condemns him, it will inflame the people. And if he lets him go free, it will fuel the division of the Empire.

蒙莫朗西点了点头。弗朗西斯科默默地在房间里踱步，脚步声如同钟表滴答作响。这位顾问注意到国王的背脊渐渐挺直，仿佛每一秒都在增长。他万万没想到，国王正在与上帝对话，感谢祂的安排。上帝多么睿智，派来一个敌人，迫使他重新燃起对伟大的渴望！上帝又多么慷慨，用无数的磨难削弱他，无论是在西班牙还是在帝国境内。神的旨意清晰明了。

Montmorency nodded. Silently, Francisco paced the room. His footsteps sounded like the ticking of a clock. The advisor noticed that the king's back was gradually straightening; he seemed to be growing taller with each passing second. What he couldn't guess was that the monarch was speaking with God, thanking Him for the move. How wise He had been to send him an enemy who would force him to rediscover his desire for greatness! And how generous to weaken him with countless hardships, both in Spain and in the Empire. The divine message was clear.

弗朗西斯转向那位顾问。他的身高已经达到了超人的程度，五官宁静而光彩照人，如同偶像一般。

Francis turned to the advisor. His height had already reached superhuman levels, and his features were serene and luminous, like those of an idol.

——蒙莫朗西先生，法国刚刚与根特的查理开战了。

—Dear Montmorency, France has just gone to war with Charles of Ghent.

 

 

 

 

1521年4月16日清晨，皇帝在黎明时分起身，前往沃尔姆斯大教堂祈祷。进入教堂前，他驻足凝视着教堂的塔楼，在晨曦的映衬下，塔楼显得格外醒目。教堂的坚固令人感到平静，但清晨时分，塔楼的红色阴影却赋予它一种令人不安的气息。查理祈祷了很久，以至于身体都麻木了。他为路德祈祷：愿理性指引他以及那些赞扬他的人。尽管他意识到罗马的种种弊端，但他明白亵渎神明无法弥补这些缺陷。教会就像一个被辱骂的顽劣孩子，会对任何不和平的批评都怒不可遏。皇帝抬起头，看到一个十字架；两根横梁交叉，象征着酷刑。卡斯蒂利亚和德意志。他当时还很年轻，经验尚浅，却不得不独自承受重担，那些早已刺穿他皮肤的伤口让他痛苦不堪，甚至连一天好运都享受不到。诚然，他身边有顾问和家人，但他领地的命运却完全掌握在他自己手中。托尔德西拉斯摆脱了共产主义者的控制后，他相信战火会在几天之内熄灭。正是这份希望让他乐观地面对路德教的问题，也因此他对那位修士宽容有加。但如今，两种困境交织在一起，能否化解这一切已近乎一种信仰。只有一件事让他感到安心：真理站在他这边。他的理想是神圣的：正义、和平、荣誉。天意无法惩罚他。

On the morning of April 16, 1521, the emperor rose at dawn and went to pray at Worms Cathedral. Before entering the church, he paused to contemplate its towers, which stood out sharply against the sunrise. The building's solidity was calming, but its reddish hue, shadowed at that early hour, gave it a menacing air. Charles spent so long in prayer that his body grew numb. He prayed for Luther: that reason might guide him and those who praised him. Although he was aware of Rome's failings, he knew they could not be corrected with blasphemies. Like a wayward child reprimanded with insults, the Church would react with anger to any criticism that was not peaceful. The emperor raised his eyes and saw a cross; two beams crossed for torture. Castile and Germany. And he, still so inexperienced, had to bear, alone, the weight of his troubles, the wounds that already pierced his skin and caused him constant suffering that had prevented him from enjoying his good fortune for even a single day. It was true that he was surrounded by advisors and family, but the responsibility for the fate of his domains belonged to him alone. When Tordesillas was freed from the control of the Comuneros, he believed that fire would be extinguished in a matter of days. That hope had encouraged him to face the Lutheran problem with optimism; hence his leniency toward the friar. But now both predicaments overlapped, and believing that this would be resolved was beginning to be a matter of faith. Only one thought reassured him: the truth was on his side. His ideals were sacred: justice, peace, honor. Providence could not punish him.

离开教堂前，卡洛斯想起圣保罗的话：“信仰是为义人预备的。”这句话给了他力量去面对这意义非凡的一天。但他并不知道，路德正是用这句话开启了他的十字军东征。

Before leaving the church, Carlos recalled the words of Saint Paul: "Faith is for the righteous." The statement gave him strength to face this momentous day. What he didn't know was that Luther had used that very same phrase to launch his crusade.

 

 

 

 

几个小时后，当他走进即将召开他首次德国议会的会场时，在场的众位——王子、国家元首和帝国显贵——都起立致敬。当他走向等候着他的宝座时，查理注意到萨克森的腓特烈和其他人一样站着，假装顺从，但他知道那至少是怯懦的姿态。他冷冷地瞥了腓特烈一眼，转身走向自己的座位。落座后，他观察着陪同他上台的人：希耶夫尔，他的姿态似乎在指责他无端挑起这场考验；还有斐迪南，他的言辞似乎恰恰相反。

When, hours later, he entered the hall where his first German Diet was to be held, those gathered there—princes, heads of state, and illustrious men of the Empire—rose in respect. As he made his way to the throne that awaited him, Charles noticed Frederick of Saxony, standing like everyone else, feigning an obedience that he knew to be, at the very least, timid. He exchanged a cold glance with him and turned his back to reach his seat. Once settled, he observed those who escorted him on the dais: Chièvres, whose gesture seemed to accuse him of having unnecessarily provoked this ordeal; and Ferdinand, whose message seemed to convey quite the opposite.

所有人的目光都集中在皇帝身上，直到一个身穿深色长袍的魁梧男子走进房间。路德的相貌正如查理想象中那般粗犷，因此他对这人犹豫的步伐感到惊讶。事实上，从他踏进门槛的那一刻起，这庄严的场合就已令这位修士疲惫不堪。前往沃尔姆斯的漫长旅程让他眼花缭乱。每个村庄都以欢呼声迎接他，如同英雄凯旋归来。这种民众的热情如同毒品般让他沉迷：他感觉自己已经胜利，而事实上，战斗甚至还没有开始。到了议会，就连皇帝的身影都令他感到畏惧：尽管哈布斯堡王朝的皇帝面容并不凶狠，但路德却能感受到他权势滔天，如同被某种令人窒息的力量所笼罩。皇帝的一句话就能判他死刑。他立刻想起多年前在田野里那道闪电，如今他意识到，那道闪电已化作血肉之躯。

All eyes were fixed on the emperor until a burly man in dark robes entered the room. Luther had the rugged appearance Charles had imagined, which is why he was surprised by the man's hesitant steps. The truth was, from the moment he crossed the threshold, the solemnity of the occasion had taken its toll on the friar. The long journey to Worms had blinded him. Every single village had greeted him with cheers, like a hero returning from war in triumph. This popular enthusiasm had acted like a drug on him: it had made him feel victorious when, in fact, the fight hadn't even begun. Once at the Diet, even the sight of the emperor intimidated him: although the Habsburg's appearance wasn't fierce, Luther could feel, like a paralyzing energy, the power of his office. The man's words could pronounce his death sentence. He immediately remembered that lightning bolt in the field years ago, which he now recognized as made flesh.

修士站在查理面前，等待皇帝的训诫，但开口说话的却是希耶夫尔。这位顾问态度傲慢，令在场的议员们都露出了不满的表情。

The friar stood before Charles, awaiting an imperial address, but it was Chièvres who spoke to him. The advisor approached him with such an arrogant manner that grimaces of displeasure spread among those attending the Diet.

—你认得这些文字吗？

—Do you recognize these writings?

路德看着几本印刷好的书籍随意地落入他手中。他仔细地翻阅着。房间里只有纸张沙沙作响的声音。

Luther watched as some printed texts fell carelessly into his hands. He leafed through them carefully. The rustling of the papers was the only sound in the room.

“的确，它们出自我的手笔，”修士说道。

"Indeed, they came from my own hand," said the friar.

“这些文件充满了对教宗和教会的亵渎之词。它们还企图煽动头脑简单的人发动异端邪说。它们威胁着帝国的和平，也威胁着那些受骗者的灵魂。”顾问用极其严肃的语气问神职人员：“你是否愿意收回你在这些文件中表达的观点？”

"They are filled with blasphemies against the Holy Father and the Church. They also seek to incite simple minds in a heretical crusade. They threaten the peace of the Empire and the fate of the souls of those who have been deceived." The advisor, adopting his most serious tone, asked the clergyman, "Do you retract what you have expressed in them?"

在场众人屏住了呼吸。王座上的查理感到双手因焦虑而微微出汗。与此同时，萨克森的腓特烈正焦急地寻找着修士的目光：他想鼓励他，让他不要轻易放弃。但路德的目光却茫然地落在茫然的空气中。当问题被提出时，童年时期遭受毒打的恐惧如潮水般涌遍全身，他的内心再次剧烈颤抖，几乎要哭出来。他为自己感到羞愧，但他意识到，自己比以往任何时候都更加诚实。

The breaths of those present caught in their throats. On the throne, Charles felt his hands grow damp with anxiety. Meanwhile, Frederick of Saxony searched intently for the friar's eyes: he wanted to instill courage in him, to encourage him not to give up right then. But Luther's gaze was lost in the void. When the question was posed, he felt waves of terror from the beatings of his childhood surge through his body, and once again his insides trembled so intensely that he wanted to weep. He was ashamed of himself, but he recognized that he was more honest than ever.

“你收回你的话吗？”希耶夫斯厉声问道。

"Do you retract?" Chièvres repeated fiercely.

我需要时间回答你。

—I need time to answer you.

房间里响起一阵惊讶的低语。

A murmur of surprise filled the room.

“时间？”顾问问道，“你如此擅长言辞，难道连‘是’或‘否’都回答不了吗？”

"Time?" asked the advisor. "You, who are so skilled with words, are you incapable of answering 'yes' or 'no'?"

修士选择保持沉默。希耶夫尔感到沮丧，便转向查理，恳求他出面干预。皇帝感到无数双眼睛像刺猬的刺一样刺痛着他。他寻找路德的目光，而那些目光并没有躲闪。一阵漫长的沉默后，他开口说道：

The friar chose to remain silent. Frustrated, Chièvres turned to Charles, urging him to intervene. The emperor felt dozens of eyes piercing him like goads. He sought Luther's gaze, and they did not shy away. After a long silence, he addressed him:

——我只允许你反思一天。仅此而已。

—I grant you one day of reflection. Not one more.

 

 

 

 

路德要求的日期一到，他出现在国会大厅后，皇帝便试图从他的举止中揣测他的回应，因为他再也无法忍受这种不确定性。两次会面之间的几个小时对他来说仿佛无比漫长，对所有在场的人来说也是如此。每一分钟都足以让人反复想象各种答案可能带来的后果。然而，这位修士缓缓走向皇帝，他的意图却如同他身上的法衣一样神秘莫测。他伫立在大厅中央，宛如一座凝固在石像中的斯芬克斯，拒绝揭开谜底。

Once the day requested by Luther had passed and he appeared in the Diet hall, the emperor tried to discern from his manner what his response would be, for he could no longer bear the uncertainty. The hours that had separated the two sessions seemed endless to him, as they did to everyone involved. Every minute had been enough time to imagine a thousand times what one answer or the other might entail. But the intentions of the friar, who advanced slowly toward the emperor, remained as obscure as his vestments. His presence in the middle of the hall was like that of a sphinx, frozen in stone, refusing to reveal an enigma.

勤奋的卡洛斯预料到了谢夫雷：

Carlos, ever diligent, anticipated Chièvres:

—你是否撤回你已承认是自己创作的作品？

—Do you retract the writings that you have acknowledged as your own?

房间里所有人都屏住了呼吸，等待的气氛凝固了。寂静无声，仿佛一幅历史画卷，而事实上，它正是如此。最后，路德胸膛起伏，开口说道：

The anticipation froze everyone in the room. The stillness and silence were so profound that the scene could have been a painting of a historical moment, which, in fact, it was. Finally, Luther's chest swelled as he answered:

—除非圣经或显而易见的理由驳斥我的观点，而不是驳斥我不相信的教皇或宗教会议的所谓权威，否则我既不想也不能收回我的观点，因为那将违背我的良心和上帝的旨意。

—Until I am refuted by the Holy Scriptures or by evident reasons, and not by the supposed authority of popes or councils in which I do not believe, I neither want to nor can retract, for it would be an offense against my conscience and against the word of God.

修士的话语融入了房间里的空气，如同闪电般传遍在场的每一个人。它像邪灵般刺穿了查尔斯，无情地撕扯着他的内心。

The friar's speech mingled with the air of the room and, carrying it with them, flew like lightning toward each of those gathered there. It pierced Charles like an evil spirit, wounding him mercilessly in his very core.

“愿主帮助我，”路德总结道。

"May the Lord help me," Luther concluded.

那位牧师悄无声息地溜到门口，宛如一缕轻烟。突然间，他消失了。人群中的萨克森的腓特烈强忍着喜悦，而希耶夫尔则被眼前的形势所迫，冲向了皇帝。

The clergyman slipped to the door with such stealth he seemed like smoke. Suddenly, he had vanished. While Frederick of Saxony, among the crowd, suppressed his urge to express his jubilation, Chièvres, seized by the urgency of the moment, rushed toward the emperor.

逮捕他！

—Arrest him!

卡洛斯的目光始终盯着大厅的入口，仿佛在等待修士再次出现，好让他改变主意。

Carlos kept his gaze fixed on the entrance to the hall, as if he were waiting for the friar to reappear so he could change his mind.

“我向他保证，他可以出席这次国会，并且能够安心离开，不必担心被逮捕。”皇帝说这话时，仿佛不是在履行自己的承诺，而是在宣读别人的诏令。

"I gave him my word that he could appear at this Diet and leave without fear of being arrested." The emperor spoke as if, instead of recalling his promise, he were reading from someone else's decree.

“你这话！”议员愤怒地反驳道，“荣誉只会奴役你，让你的帝国永远陷入动荡！”

"Your word!" the councilor retorted furiously. "Honor enslaves you, and condemns your Empire to perpetual unrest!"

“他一离开这座城市，我就会下令逮捕他。我的良心与你的一样受到谴责。”

"I will order his arrest as soon as he leaves the city. My conscience is no less demanding than yours."

 

 

 

 

离开听众席后，路德受到人群的热烈欢迎，他向他们宣布自己没有退缩。他的勇气赢得了掌声和赞扬，但这丝毫无法减轻这位修士当天余下时间里所承受的痛苦。他为自己没有屈服于恐惧而感到自豪，但他也清楚自己已经自取灭亡。即便他能平安离开沃尔姆斯，那道帝国法令的魔爪迟早也会将他吞噬，最终将他一步步引向火海，让他生不如死。在那难以忍受的痛苦之中，他或许会怀疑，自己的勇气是否值得。

Upon leaving the audience, Luther was greeted by a crowd to whom he announced that he had not backed down. His courage was acknowledged with applause and praise, which did little to soothe the anguish the friar suffered for the rest of the day. He was proud that fear had not forced him to yield, but he was aware that he had condemned himself. Even if he could leave Worms safely, the jaws of the imperial edict would catch him sooner or later and lead him to a fire that would burn him alive, inch by inch. And in the midst of that unbearable pain, he might well have wondered if his courage had been worth it.

当天下午，马车开始返回维滕贝格。车厢里再次陷入一片寂静，持续了数小时。扬·胡斯的身影再次萦绕在他们身边，仿佛与他们所坐的木椅融为一体。和去程一样，马匹出乎意料地停了下来，因为它们看到了几个陌生人。路德和他的朋友们以为他们是仰慕者。但遮挡他们的帆布后面的影子却像一把利刃。

That same afternoon the carriage began its return to Wittenberg. Once again, silence enveloped the carriage for hours. Jan Hus again haunted them, becoming as present as the wooden seat on which they sat. And, as on the outward journey, unexpectedly, the horses stopped at the sight of some strangers. Luther and his friends assumed they were admirers. But the shadows behind the canvas covering them resembled a knife.

绑架只持续了几秒钟。还没等他反应过来，修士就被一个麻袋蒙住了双眼，骑上一匹飞驰而去的马。路德知道他的朋友们已经走了，因为呼喊他的声音很快就消失在远方。

The abduction lasted only a few seconds. Before he knew it, the friar found himself blindfolded by a burlap sack and mounted on a horse that sped away. Luther knew his friends were gone because the shouts calling for him soon faded into the distance.

你是谁？！你要对我做什么？！

—Who are you?! What are you going to do to me?!

但他从绑匪那里只听到粗重的喘息声。他的命运未卜，但无疑是致命的。

But all he heard from the kidnappers were ragged breathing. His fate was uncertain, but undoubtedly fatal.

 

 

 

 

路德被绑架的消息最初令皇室感到困惑，但随着时间推移，杳无音讯，他们反而松了一口气。这位异端的追随者虽有数百人，但正统信徒的数量更多，毫无疑问，他们中的一些人抢先一步，阻止了皇帝的谴责，除掉了这位德国乃至整个基督教世界的煽动者。查理二世并不乐见他人在他的领地内替他伸张正义，但事实上，他更希望避免亲手处死这位修士，以免被冠以暴君之名，因为他扼杀了一位象征性人物的生命。

The news of Luther's abduction was initially met with bewilderment at the imperial court, but later, as the days passed and nothing was heard of the friar, with relief. The heretic's followers numbered in the hundreds, but the number of orthodox believers was even greater, and undoubtedly some of them had preempted the emperor's condemnation, eliminating the agitator of Germany and, potentially, of all Christendom. Charles was not thrilled about others dispensing justice for him in his domains, but the truth was that he preferred to avoid ordering the friar's martyrdom and being branded as the tyrant who had ended the life of a man who was also a symbol.

数日来，宫廷风平浪静，一片祥和。舞会和宴会陆续举行，音乐声不绝于耳，直到黎明才渐渐平息。在一次并无特别意义的庆祝活动中，查理注意到一位有着红褐色头发和精致五官的年轻女子。他一有机会，便莫名其妙地冒出一股轻佻的诱惑欲，邀请她共舞。

For a few days, the lack of incidents made the court a calm place to enjoy. Dances and banquets were organized, enlivened by music that only fell silent at dawn. At one of these celebrations that held no particular meaning, Charles noticed a young woman with auburn hair and delicate features. As soon as he could, and with a seducer's boldness that he didn't know where it had come from, he asked her to dance.

当皇帝问她叫什么名字时，她回答说：“约翰娜·范德盖斯特。”

—Johanna van der Gheyst —she replied when the emperor asked her name.

听到她的声音，卡洛斯几乎要叫停音乐。他从未听过如此悦耳动听的嗓音。虽然这位年轻女子容貌姣好，举止妩媚，但她那宛如天籁的歌声，却瞬间让他无法抗拒。他不停地问她问题，只为继续沉醉于她的魅力之中。

Upon hearing her, Carlos almost ordered the music to stop. He had never heard a more melodious tone. Although the young woman was beautiful and had a sensual manner, that voice, which was pure song, instantly made her irresistible to him. He kept asking her questions so he could continue to be charmed by her.

—你从哪里学来的如此优雅的身姿？

—Where did you learn to move so gracefully?

乔安娜笑了，同时脸红了。

Johanna smiled and blushed at the same time.

陛下，请不要取笑我。我非常清楚，跳舞并非我的强项。

—Don't make fun of me, Your Majesty. I know very well that dancing is not among my virtues.

——什么是……？

—What are…?

——恩赐一旦被宣扬，便会消逝。因为虚空会使一切完美失效。

—As soon as a gift is preached, it vanishes. For vanity nullifies all perfection.

舞会还没结束，卡洛斯就已经想吻她了。

Before the dance had even ended, Carlos already wanted to kiss her.

 

 

 

 

远在葡萄牙宫廷的伊莎贝拉每天都问哥哥，皇帝是否已回复她要求立即正式订婚的请求。事实上，葡萄牙国王羞于对妹妹撒谎：那封信根本没有离开里斯本，他迟早要承认这一点。然而，葡萄牙驻英国大使的一封简短的信，却无意中为约翰解开了向妹妹隐瞒真相的谜团。

Far away, at the Portuguese court, Isabella asked her brother every day if he had received a reply from the emperor to her request that their engagement be finalized immediately and without delay. Truthfully, the Portuguese monarch was ashamed to lie to his sister: the letter had not left Lisbon, and at some point, he would have to admit it. But the Portuguese ambassador in England, through a brief message, unwittingly absolved John of his lack of explanation to his sister.

“皇帝已经和英国国王的女儿订婚了。这事早就定下来了，但我们却毫不知情。我想，这大概是为了避免我们感到不快吧。”

"The emperor is engaged to the daughter of the English king. The agreement was made some time ago, but we weren't informed. I suppose that was to spare us our displeasure."

突然间，伊莎贝尔觉得自己置身于一个荒诞的世界，一个疯子的想象，因为只有这样才能理解，她命中注定要嫁的那个男人，竟然决定将自己的命运与一个五岁女孩的命运结合在一起。

Suddenly, Isabel felt immersed in an absurd version of the world, the product of a madman's mind, because only in that way could one understand that the man she was destined to marry had decided to unite his fate with that of a five-year-old girl.

“一定是协议里那条毫无道理的条款。凯撒不可能等十年才结婚，也不可能等十年才找继承人！”

"It must be the senseless clause in an agreement. Caesar isn't going to wait ten years to marry, or to find an heir!"

“我也觉得这很荒谬，”君主说，“但是，在他悔改之前，如果他恢复理智的话，你的思想将无处容身。”

—I find it as grotesque as you do —said the monarch—, but until the day he repents of that commitment, if sanity ever returns to his mind, yours will have no place.

——让我看看她的答案。她的决心中肯定会有裂痕。让我去发现它们！

—Show me her answer. There will undoubtedly be cracks in her resolve. Let me discover them!

胡安临时想出了一个摆脱困境的办法。

Juan improvised a way to get out of that predicament.

—至今连回应都没有。

—There hasn't even been a response.

起初，公主感到前所未有的愤慨。沉默？这就是她向查尔斯投降后应得的回应吗？然而，她注意到哥哥身上有些异样，这让她的愤怒转为怀疑：他说话不够坚定，而且还带着一丝恼怒。为什么他对皇帝如此轻蔑地拒绝葡萄牙的提议没有感到愤怒呢？

At first, the princess felt more offended than ever before. Silence? Was that the response she deserved from Charles after surrendering herself to him? However, she noticed something in her brother that transformed her anger into suspicion: a lack of firmness in his words, and also annoyance. Why wasn't he furious that the emperor had so dismissively rejected the Portuguese offer?

她过了好几天才明白过来，但一切都明了了。伊莎贝尔在宫廷花园漫步时，瞥见两个身影，便悄悄走近，只见他们正欢快地跳舞，宛如两个仙女的剪影。公主绕了个弯，以便不被发现地观察。当她看到莱昂诺尔和胡安紧紧相拥，情意绵绵时，她的眼眶瞬间干涩。他们像传说中的恋人那样热吻：奔放不羁，无所畏惧，忘却一切。伊莎贝尔几乎悄无声息地退了出去，身体僵硬，胸口一阵剧痛。她多年来的渴望和期盼，终将化为泡影，因为她确信，她的哥哥已经决定，莱昂诺尔的再婚将修复西班牙和葡萄牙之间的联盟。

The explanation took days to reach her, but it was crystal clear. While strolling through the palace gardens, Isabel caught sight of two shadows and, stealthily, approached them and saw them dancing happily, like the silhouettes of two fairies. The princess took a detour so she could observe without being discovered. Her eyes went dry as she beheld Leonor and Juan's bodies intertwined in an embrace brimming with desire. They kissed like the lovers of legends: unrestrained, fearless, oblivious to everything. Isabel withdrew almost silently, her body rigid and her chest tight with pain. Her longing, the aspiration that had defined her days for years, was going to come to nothing, because, she was certain, her brother had decided that the union between Spain and Portugal would be mended with Leonor's second marriage.

公主生平第一次感到如此脆弱。她意识到，自己一直以来的沉着冷静，竟源于对未来的笃信。如今，未来正在消逝，她也随之黯然失色。然而，忧郁与伊莎贝尔注定无法共存。

The princess felt vulnerable for the first time in her entire life. She realized the extent to which her composure stemmed from taking her future for granted. Now that it was fading, so was she. But melancholy and Isabel were not meant to coexist.

王国必将憎恶你们的结合。上帝作证，你就是它的继母。

—The kingdom will abhor your union. You are its stepmother, by God.

在葡萄牙宫廷的这些年里，莱昂诺尔从未听过伊莎贝尔公主如此坦率直言。在她看来，伊莎贝尔生活在一个与世隔绝的世界里，那里讲究礼貌，谈吐犀利，但她从未被邀请进入她的世界，一窥她的本质。

In all her time at the Portuguese court, Leonor had never heard such a frank and unvarnished tone from the princess. To her, Isabel lived in her own world, where polite manners and sharp conversations were practiced, but she had never been invited to enter her atmosphere, to glimpse her essence.

卡洛斯的妹妹突然哭了起来；她的哭声平息了公主的怒火。

Carlos's sister burst into tears; her crying froze the princess's rage.

我曾以为自己再也无法爱上任何人。你的哥哥抚平了我灵魂深处那些我以为会随我而去的伤痕。理智告诉我应该拒绝他，但我的心却像港湾般紧紧地将我与他相连。如今，我感恩每一个日出，而过去那些年，我唯一的愿望就是不要醒来。

—I thought I could never love again. Your brother has swept away wounds from my soul that I thought would die with me. Sanity tells me to reject him. But my heart binds me to him like a harbor. Now I bless every sunrise, when for years all I longed for was not to wake up.

公主内心正经历着一场激烈的斗争。莱昂诺尔的痛苦是她见过的最真切的。对于她这样冷漠的人来说，目睹如此脆弱的灵魂，令她心碎不已。即便如此，她也无法放弃自己的命运。

A battle raged within the princess. Leonor's pain was the most genuine she had ever witnessed. And for someone as hardened as she was, it was heartbreaking to witness such an exposed soul. But even so, she felt unable to renounce her destiny.

你们的结合会破坏我与皇帝的结合。

—Your union will ruin my union with the emperor.

“绝不能这样，”继母连忙回答道，“我向你保证，我会从中斡旋，确保你们的婚事顺利进行。我不能容忍我的幸福成为别人痛苦的根源。”

"It must not be so," her stepmother hastened to reply. "I give you my word that I will intervene to ensure your marriage takes place. I could not bear for my happiness to be the source of other people's unhappiness."

过了一会儿，伊莎贝尔在她身边坐下，擦干了眼泪。她不相信埃莉诺的意愿在皇帝的计划中会有任何影响；如果皇帝反对这门婚事，无论是因为他希望这个英国女孩长大成人，还是因为与葡萄牙结盟对他更有利，她也无能为力。但她实在没有勇气继续违抗这个深爱着他的女人。

After a few moments, Isabel sat down beside her and dried her tears. She didn't believe Eleanor's wishes counted for anything in the emperor's plans; she could do little to help her if he resisted the marriage, whether because he preferred the English girl to become a woman, or because an alliance with Portugal seemed more advantageous to him. But she couldn't find the strength within herself to continue defying this woman in love.

 

 

 

 

当那些地区弥漫着情绪的氛围时，卡斯蒂利亚则以行动为主导。帕迪利亚的科穆内罗军队仅用了四天就攻占了巴利亚多利德的托雷洛巴顿镇，这是他们不依靠任何人夺取这座大城市——宫廷所在地——的第一步。然而，这场胜利来之不易。镇上的居民进行了顽强的抵抗。科穆内罗军队的劫掠——除了教堂之外，几乎没留下任何遗迹——使得这些所谓的解放者在村民眼中变成了暴徒。叛军辩解说：他们需要补给和资金来继续战争。但如果第二天连饭都吃不上，受害者们对科穆内罗的“十字军东征”又有什么兴趣呢？

While emotion reigned in those latitudes, action ruled in Castile. Padilla's Comunero army, in four days, had taken the Valladolid town of Torrelobatón, as a first step towards seizing, without relying on anyone, the great city, seat of the court. The victory, however, had not been easy. The town's inhabitants had resisted fiercely. The pillaging by the Comunero troops, who had left little of the town untouched except the church, turned the supposed liberators into abusers in the eyes of the villagers. The rebels excused themselves: they needed provisions and funds to continue their war. But the victims cared little for the Comunero crusade if they weren't going to have anything to eat the next day.

从托雷洛巴顿城堡，帕迪利亚眺望着地平线。黎明破晓，卡斯蒂利亚平原在红紫交织的晨曦中苏醒，如平静的海面般轻柔起伏，田野绵延，宛如一幅巨大的马赛克画。这位来自托莱多的男子深深吸了一口清晨纯净的空气。自从他重新领导这场运动以来，一种弥赛亚般的信仰便深深地扎根于他心中。在他的脑海中，无需任何刻意的努力，英雄事迹便已浮现。

From Torrelobatón Castle, Padilla scanned the horizon. Dawn was breaking, and the Castilian plain awoke enveloped in reds and purples, gently undulating like a calm sea, and divided into fields that gave it the appearance of a vast mosaic. The man from Toledo breathed in the innocent air of those early hours. A messianic faith had taken hold of him since he had resumed leading the movement. In his mind, without any conscious effort, only heroic deeds took shape.

弗朗西斯科·马尔多纳多和帕迪利亚一起登上了塔楼。这位贵族，萨拉曼卡平民的首领，曾参与了托雷洛巴顿的攻占。他们彼此对视了一眼：周围的景色太美了，让他们无法将目光从他身上移开。

Francisco Maldonado joined Padilla in the tower. The aristocrat, leader of the Salamanca commoners, had collaborated in the capture of Torrelobatón. They glanced at each other: the landscape was too beautiful to distract their gaze from him.

萨拉曼卡人说：“布拉沃征服了西曼卡斯和扎拉坦。”

—Bravo has conquered Simancas and Zaratán —said the man from Salamanca.

帕迪利亚几乎没有露出笑容。他对最终胜利的信心早已根深蒂固，成功对他来说并不意外：一切似乎早已注定。

Padilla barely smiled. His confidence in the final victory had settled so deeply within him that success didn't surprise him: it was written in the stars.

—今天，我第一次相信了。

—Today I believe, for the first time.

——你以前不是做过吗？你的声音总是比其他任何人的声音都更有说服力。

—Didn't you do it before? Your voice has always sounded more convincing than any other.

“我曾全心全意地渴望相信，”来自托莱多的男子回答道，“但我内心充满失败感。这就是我离开托尔德西利亚斯时没有得到女王签字的原因：因为我觉得自己没有能力得到它。我仍然是一个假装不是的附庸。”

“I longed to believe, with all my heart,” the man from Toledo replied. “But I carried defeat within me. That is why I left Tordesillas without the queen’s signature: because I did not feel capable of obtaining it. I was still a vassal pretending not to be one.”

——那么今天呢？

—And today?

“今天我是一个自由人，我可以毫不含糊地说，我们所有人都是自由人。这片田野……”帕迪利亚指向远处的平原，旭日东升，田野的色彩在阳光下闪烁，泥土和青草交织成一幅变幻莫测的画卷。“这片田野属于我们，就像属于我们的双手和肌肤一样。暴政迫使我们把真正属于我们的东西拱手让给他人。这种欺骗终有一天会被揭穿。”

“Today I am a free man, and I can state unequivocally that we all are. This field…” Padilla gestured across the plain, its colors shimmering as the sun rose; a shifting display of earth and grass. “This field belongs to us as much as our hands or our skin. Tyranny forces us to surrender to others what we truly possess. It is such a deception that one day it was bound to be exposed.”

太阳迅速升起，阳光刺得他们睁不开眼。但他们谁也不想打破这片刻的宁静。直到一阵寒风毫无预兆地袭来，马尔多纳多才回过神来。

The sun was rising quickly; it was beginning to blind them. But neither of them wanted to break that moment. Only when a cold wind rose without warning did Maldonado come to his senses.

接下来我们将去哪里？

—Where will we go from here?

——朝着托罗镇的方向。再往前走，就是萨莫拉。

—Towards the town of Toro. And beyond it, Zamora.

 

 

 

 

在巴利亚多利德的宫廷里，摄政王阿德里安得知公社叛乱的动向后，召见了法德里克·德·阿尔瓦。法德里克是贵族中唯一一位始终公开效忠王室的人。事实上，从叛乱伊始，这位公爵就对贵族们的态度感到羞愧难当。他的地位让他自以为在贵族中拥有权威，但他协助摄政王的命令——实际上已变成了恳求——却遭到了蔑视。法德里克越来越感到尴尬，因为他觉得贵族们的不作为越来越不可饶恕。但在下次会面的前夜，他得知了一件事，这让他下定决心，迈着坚定的步伐走进了王宫。

At the court of Valladolid, when Regent Adrian learned of the advances of the Comuneros, he summoned Fadrique de Alba to an audience. Fadrique was the only one of the Grandees who had always openly declared his loyalty to the Crown. In fact, from the very beginning of the revolt, the duke could feel nothing but shame at the nobles' attitude. His preeminence had led him to assume he held authority among them, but his orders to aid the regent, which had become pleas, had been scorned. Fadrique attended his meetings with Adrian with growing embarrassment, because the inaction of the lords was becoming increasingly inexcusable. But on the eve of their next meeting, he learned of an event that made him enter the royal hall with a resolute step.

——杜埃尼亚斯。这座城镇高举平民旗帜，反抗其领主。这并非一场骚乱，而是一场革命。

—Dueñas. The town, raising the flag of the commoners, has rebelled against its lord. It has not been a mere disturbance, but a revolution.

阿德里亚诺听到这些话，就像从地狱中解脱出来后呼吸到了一口新鲜空气。

Adriano received his words as if a breath of fresh air had reached him after a season in hell.

“而且，这件事也传到了其他贵族的耳中，”摄政王察觉到。

—And it has reached the ears of the other nobles—the regent sensed.

公爵点了点头。他们四目相对，彼此的目光已经等待了数月之久。

The duke nodded. They met the gaze they had been waiting months to exchange.

—他们宣称效忠王室。

—They proclaim their loyalty to the Crown.

——既然他们的特权受到了威胁……——阿德里亚诺的语气中带着轻蔑，尽管他早就预料到，只有当贵族们能从中获利时，他们才会帮助他。

—Now that their privileges are threatened… —There was a tone of contempt in Adriano's voice, although he had long expected that he would only be helped by the lords if they gained something from it.

——难道你们不能把审查制度置于他们的自私之上，而放弃恢复王国和平的可能性吗？

—Will you not be able to put censorship before their selfishness, rather than the possibility of restoring peace to the kingdom?

摄政王在大厅里走了几步，仿佛要用他的举动驱散与这类自私自利之徒打交道时心中的厌恶。然后，他转向那位情绪低落的公爵。

The regent took a few steps across the hall, as if to leave behind, with his advance, the distaste he felt at having to deal with this breed of self-serving individuals. He then turned to the duke, whose spirits had been cast aside.

你以为我这么愚蠢吗？我召集他们为我效力！让他们立即将军队置于我的指挥之下！否则，即使有他们的帮助，也可能为时已晚。

—Do you think me so foolish? I call them to my service! Let them place their armies under my command, without delay! Or even with their help, it may be too late.

 

 

 

 

查理反复研读哈德良的信，直到将其背诵下来。长久以来，来自卡斯蒂利亚的消息都是接连不断的挫折，因此他觉得这封新信并非来自那个麻烦的源头——因为卡斯蒂利亚王国本身就是一个麻烦的化身。贵族们的合作不仅极有可能扭转战局，而且也代表着他们对王室的臣服，是国王与贵族之间妥协的开端。从查理抵达西班牙的那一刻起，直到此刻，贵族们几乎从未掩饰过他们的行为，那不过是虚伪的服从罢了。那些希望新国王能像他父亲“美男子”腓力二世那样，重施贵族特权的人——腓力二世与天主教徒斐迪南二世的敌对关系，使他不得不依靠贵族势力来制衡后者——很快就失望了：真正享受到王室恩宠的，是国王的弗拉芒随从。但随着科穆内罗起义的展开，似乎即将平息贵族们的不满。因此，查理认为，尽管这场危机给他带来了无数的焦虑，但从长远来看，它很可能成为王国稳定的种子。

Charles eagerly read Hadrian's letter, over and over, until he had memorized it. For so long, the news arriving from Castile had been a succession of setbacks that he felt this new letter came from somewhere else, not from that wellspring of trouble—for that was how the kingdom could be described. The nobility's cooperation would not only, in all likelihood, reverse the course of the conflict; it would also represent a capitulation to the Crown, the beginning of a compromise between the king and the Grandees. From the moment Charles had arrived in Spain until that very moment, the aristocrats had barely concealed their behavior, which amounted to little more than a facade of obedience. Those who hoped that the new king would repeat the privileges his father, Philip the Handsome, had granted to the nobility—his rivalry with Ferdinand the Catholic having led him to rely on the aristocratic faction to counter the latter's power—were soon disappointed: it was the monarch's Flemish retinue that benefited lavishly from royal favors. But the Comunero Revolt, as it was unfolding, seemed poised to finally quell the discontent of the Grandees. Thus, Charles reasoned that, despite the countless anxieties this crisis had caused him, it might well be, in the long run, the seed of the kingdom's stability.

受哈德良的话语影响，皇帝心中多了一份淡然，他几乎欣喜若狂。路德仍然下落不明，德国人对他的担忧也渐渐消退：几乎所有人都确信他已遇害。接下来的几天，查理一心只陪伴着约翰娜，他对她没有丝毫爱意，只有强烈的欲望。在他们同床共枕时，他们没有像与杰尔玛娜那样谈笑风生；维系他们的只有激情，而两人似乎都对此感到满足。

Imbued with the relative nonchalance that Hadrian's words had instilled in him, the emperor succumbed to something very close to joy. Luther was still missing, and the anxiety about his whereabouts was fading among the Germans: few doubted then that he had been murdered. For several days, Charles devoted himself solely to Johanna, for whom he felt nothing akin to love, but certainly desire. In the bed they shared, they did not engage in the witty conversations he had enjoyed with Germana; passion was the only thing that bound them, and both seemed content with that.

一天早晨，两人还在睡梦中，就听到皇家寝宫门外传来低沉的说话声。查理等着声音渐渐消失，但声音似乎越来越大，语气也变得阴沉而令人不安。他起身，急切地想知道发生了什么事，便穿着睡衣，赤着脚穿过走廊，脚踩在冰冷的石板上。他刚走了几步，加蒂纳拉就出现在走廊的另一端。他匆匆走过，目光紧盯着地板，紧张地低声念叨着什么，查理听不太清。皇帝知道大臣正朝他的寝宫走来：那条路通往的只有这一个房间。意大利人终于抬起头，看到来自根特的男人，顿时停住了脚步。他眼神中流露出一种查理从未见过的深邃。

One morning, while they were both still asleep, deep voices were heard on the other side of the door to the royal bedchamber. Charles waited for them to fade, but they seemed to grow louder, and their tone held a dark, unsettling note. He rose and, anxious to know what was happening, crossed the corridor still in his nightclothes and barefoot, his feet freezing on the stone. He had barely taken a few steps when Gattinara appeared at the other end of the corridor. He walked hurriedly, his eyes fixed on the floor, nervously muttering a litany that Charles couldn't quite make out. The emperor knew the chancellor was heading for his chamber: that path led to no other room. The Italian finally raised his head and, seeing the man from Ghent, stopped dead in his tracks. There was a depth in his gaze that Charles had never perceived before.

—发生了什么事？

—What's happening?

—法国入侵了你们在纳瓦拉和意大利的领土。

—France has invaded your territories in Navarre and Italy.

皇帝注意到自己脸上的血色渐渐褪去。

The emperor noticed the blood draining from his face.

 

 

 

 

纳瓦拉是法军的首要目标。其借口是为亨利二世收复十年前被阿拉贡的费迪南征服的王国。指挥法军营的是国王情妇弗朗西斯卡·德·福瓦的兄弟，此人军事才能平庸，根本不适合如此关键的战役。国王无视母亲萨伏依的路易丝的警告——路易丝认为这一选择是出于浪漫主义而非君主应有的务实精神——最终，他的鲁莽之举招致了惨败。

Navarre was the first target of the French troops. The pretext was to recover for Henry II the kingdom that Ferdinand of Aragon had conquered a decade earlier. Commanding the French battalion was a brother of the king's mistress, Francisca de Foix, a man of mediocre military talent ill-suited for such a crucial campaign. The monarch, ignoring the warnings of his mother, Louise of Savoy, who considered the choice a concession born of romanticism rather than the pragmatism that should guide a ruler, saw his audacity punished with defeat.

但与此同时，其他高卢军队正在越过荷兰边境。

But at the same time, other Gallic forces were crossing the border of the Netherlands.

 

 

 

 

通过一系列紧急外交努力，皇帝终于获得了他未来的岳父——英格兰国王亨利八世和教皇的支持。教皇急于支持这位在帝国境内打击异端邪说的皇帝，尽管在他看来，查理五世的决心还不够坚定。之后，查理五世才派遣军队向法国东北部进军。进军比预想的要顺利得多，他的意图也很明确：只有当弗朗西斯一世从占领区撤军时，他才会撤出自己的军队。

Through frantic diplomatic efforts, the emperor secured the support of his future father-in-law, Henry of England, and the Pope, who was eager to back the man who was fighting—albeit, in his opinion, without sufficient resolve—against heresy within the Empire. Only then did Charles send his armies toward northeastern France. The advance was easier than expected, and his intention was clear: he would only withdraw his troops if Francis did the same with his in the occupied territories.

凯撒密切关注着战争的进展，起初这种紧张感几乎令他难以忍受，但他不仅逐渐习惯了，最终甚至乐在其中。这是一种令人振奋的刺激：不确定性、战争的敌意、恐惧、精心策划的战役，以及自战争爆发以来宫廷一直沉浸其中的那场生死游戏。然而，随着时间的推移，他开始渴望更多的刺激，更大的风险！当他得知法国国王决定率军进攻弗拉芒边境时，他明白，他自己的第一场战争即将到来。

The Caesar followed the events of the war with a nervousness that at first he found almost unbearable, but to which he not only grew accustomed, but which he ultimately came to enjoy. It was an invigorating excitement: the uncertainty, the warlike enmity, the fear, the meticulous planning of the battles, that deadly game in which the court had been immersed since the conflict began. However, as the days passed, he began to crave more thrills, more risk! And when he learned that the French monarch had decided to lead his armies in their offensive on the Flemish border, he understood that the time had come for him to experience his first war.

 

 

 

 

查理身着帝王铠甲，率领军队巡视着敌军驻扎的山谷。敌军人数之多，即使只是粗略一看，也明显远超己方。突然，铠甲的金属重量压得他喘不过气来。铠甲之下，他瘦削的身躯汗流浃背，气喘吁吁。他决定参战的决定遭到了大多数顾问的反对。君主必须亲自率军作战的时代正在远去，如今，在位期间凭借智慧做出正确的军事决策并有效运用外交手段赢得战争，已不再被视为不光彩之举。然而，查理的骑士精神——正是这种精神将他推上了帝国的王位，也正是这种精神让他对路德展现了如此高尚的品格——却不允许他回避这场冲突。

Beneath his imperial armor, Charles, at the head of his troops, surveyed the valley where the enemy soldiers were encamped. Their numbers, even at first glance, were clearly far greater than those of his own army. Suddenly, the metal of his armor began to weigh heavily on him. Beneath it, a gaunt body, drenched in sweat, gasped for air. His decision to take part in the fight had been censured by most of his advisors. The days when monarchs were obligated to lead their armies were fading, and it was no longer considered dishonorable to win a war from the office, using intelligence as the weapon to make the right military decisions and to wield diplomacy effectively. However, Charles's chivalrous spirit, the very thing that had placed him on the throne of the Empire and that had led him to act so honorably toward Luther, would not allow him to avoid the conflict.

“你才二十一岁，”希耶夫提醒他，“你从未上过战场，当然，你也没有继承人。你的想法简直是自杀！一时冲动！”

"You are twenty-one years old," Chièvres reminded him, "you have never fought on a battlefield, and of course, you have not yet had an heir. Your intention is simply suicidal! A senseless whim!"

“我绝不允许法国军队以他们的国王为旗手，而我的军队却像孤儿一样！”

"I refuse to let the troops of France have their king as their standard-bearer, while mine appear orphaned!"

顾问准确地指出了皇帝语气中那种没有丝毫改变主意的意味。

That register in the emperor's voice that gave no reason to change his mind was perfectly identified by the advisor.

至少要保证你不会冒不必要的风险。你肩负着守护众多王国和帝国的重任，这份责任必须凌驾于其他一切之上。

—At least promise that you will not take unnecessary risks. You are the one who watches over many kingdoms and an Empire. That responsibility must outweigh any other.

查理的目光紧紧锁定在法军身上，他丝毫不后悔自己的决定，但双方兵力悬殊，胜利几乎不可能，甚至如同奇迹一般，他明白这次进攻无异于自杀。他那骑士般的心驱使他策马扬鞭，高举利剑，在一声呐喊的鼓舞下，迎战敌人。但这位明智的君主最终还是没有策马出击。

With his gaze fixed on the French troops, Charles was far from regretting his decision, but the numerical disparity between the two sides was so vast, victory so impossible or miraculous, that he understood the attack would be suicidal. His knightly heart urged him to ride, sword raised, and, buoyed by a feverish cry, confront his enemies. But the sensible ruler preferred not to spur his horse.

 

 

 

 

几公里外，在法军一侧，国王凝视着阴沉的天空，又望向地平线，最后看向他的士兵，人数众多，他的眼睛都无法全部看清。一名士兵骑马来到他身边。这名士兵奉命侦察敌情，任务完成后凯旋而归，脸上难掩喜悦之情。

A few kilometers away, on the French side, the monarch gazed at the overcast sky, then at the horizon, and finally at his men, so numerous that his eyes couldn't take them all in. A soldier rode up to his side. He had been sent to spy on the enemy, and having done so, he was returning, unable to hide his joy.

殿下，敌军兵力不过我军的一半，胜利在望！我们恭候您的命令。

—Your Highness, the imperial army is barely half the size of ours. Victory is assured! We await your orders.

弗朗西斯点了点头，但没有再补充任何指示。“胜利已成定局。”这句话在他脑海中回荡，就像在几个月的皇位争夺战中，他已经听过无数遍一样。他记得那段时间里一直伴随着他的那种绝对的自信，也记得在他看来，皇帝在竞选过程中多次濒临失败。选举结果带来的苦涩滋味，如今仍像消化不良一样萦绕在他的心头。

Francis nodded, but added no further instructions. “Victory is assured.” The phrase echoed in his mind, just as he had heard it before, a thousand times, during the months of the imperial race. He remembered the feeling of absolute certainty that had accompanied him throughout that time, and how it seemed to him that the emperor was on the verge of defeat at so many points in the contest. The caustic taste left by the election result now lingered in his mind like indigestion.

突然，远处传来一个警报声：

Suddenly, an alarm voice from a distant post said:

——他们撤退了！帝国军队正在撤退！

—They're retreating! The imperial troops are retreating!

随后，法国君主做出了反应。他急忙且近乎绝望地组织军队追击查理的军队。法军骑兵以迅雷不及掩耳之势猛烈冲锋，从远处看，他们就像战场上随意挥洒的一笔。他们策马疾驰，却始终未能看到猎物的身影，猎物早已像落日般消失在地平线尽头。正当战马开始疲惫，一个黑影——敌人！——终于出现在法军面前时，天空骤然倾盆而下，暴雨如注，短短几分钟，战场便变成了一片泥沼，牲畜们跌跌撞撞地陷了进去。士兵们停了下来，茫然不知所措，眼前只有一片浑浊的水幕。就在这时，尽管暴雨震耳欲聋，人们还是听到了一声愤怒的怒吼。那是弗朗西斯的声音。

Then the French monarch reacted. Urgently and somewhat desperately, he organized his men to pursue Charles's forces. The French cavalry charged with such speed and ferocity after the imperial army that, from a distance, they resembled a careless brushstroke in the landscape of the battle. They rode and rode without catching a glimpse of their prey, which had vanished over the horizon like the setting sun. And then, when the horses' strength began to wane but a dark shape—the enemy!—finally appeared before the French, the sky began to unleash such torrential rain that in minutes the field became a quagmire in which the animals stumbled. The soldiers stopped, disoriented, unable to see anything before them but an opaque curtain of water. And, despite the deafening storm, a cry of fury was heard. It was Francis.

 

 

 

 

-下雨了。

-It's raining.

帕迪利亚抬头望向天空，只见乌云密布。他立刻想起托雷洛巴顿城堡清晨的晴朗景象，那紫橙色的天空与眼前的景象形成了鲜明的对比。如今，他周围只有灰色和赭色。他转身看向部下，催促他们加快步伐，向托罗进发。正当队伍加快步伐时，大地开始震动。科穆内罗斯人的马匹本能地停了下来。随着地面震动加剧，一声轰鸣也随之响起，如同雷鸣与闪电交织。帕迪利亚和他的部下回头望去。

Padilla looked up at the sky, where the clouds appeared murky. He immediately thought of the contrast with that clear dawn at Torrelobatón Castle, the mauve and orange hues. Now he was surrounded only by grays and ochres. He turned to look at his men and urged them to advance with more vigor toward Toro. Just as the march was picking up a brisk pace, the ground began to tremble. The Comuneros' horses, responding to instinct, stopped. The vibration of the ground intensified as a roar joined it, like thunder to lightning. Padilla and his men looked behind them.

有成千上万个。

There were thousands.

 

 

 

 

叛军没能赶到托罗。途中，在维拉拉尔，王室军队——其中不乏领主及其士兵——追上了他们。帕迪利亚亲眼目睹了数百人死亡，而死者无一例外都是他自己的部下。城里的街道上尸横遍野，房屋的石头和墙壁上溅满了鲜血。每一声痛苦的呻吟之后都是死一般的寂静；每一个受伤的人都倒在地上，被无情地杀死。

The rebels didn't have time to reach Toro. Halfway there, in Villalar, the Crown's troops, swelled by lords and their soldiers, caught up with them. Padilla witnessed hundreds of deaths, all of them his own men. The town's streets were littered with corpses. The stones and walls of the houses were spattered with blood. Each cry of pain was followed by a brutal silence; each wounded man was finished off on the ground.

尽管这场运动历经数年才发展起来并投入战斗，期间经历了辩论、骚乱、招募、谈判、煽动叛乱、优柔寡断的女王以及一些胜利，但最终却在短短几个小时内就永远地解决了。

Although the movement had taken years to develop and launch into the fight, with debates, riots, recruitment, negotiations, seditions, an indecisive queen and some victories, it had just been settled in just a few hours and forever.

在战斗中，王室军队没有杀害叛军首领。直到战斗结束，少数幸存的平民投降后，帕迪利亚才被郑重逮捕。他的手腕被粗绳捆绑，押往广场。马尔多纳多和布拉沃也和他一样，被制服在那里等候着他。几米开外，一名刽子手姿态放松地站在那里。平民们曾以悲观的想象和噩梦来设想这一天的到来，但令他们三人惊讶的是，阳光穿透了云层，一头驴滑稽的嘶鸣声传到了广场，附近一户人家飘来了炖菜的香味：这个世界对他们的悲剧漠不关心。

The Crown's troops refrained from killing the rebel leaders during the battle. Only when it was over and the few remaining commoners had surrendered was Padilla solemnly arrested. His wrists were bound with rough rope, and he was led to a plaza where Maldonado and Bravo, like him, awaited him, subdued. A few meters away, in a relaxed posture, stood an executioner. The commoners had imagined that day in pessimistic thoughts and nightmares, but all three were surprised to find the sun breaking through the clouds, the comical braying of a donkey reaching the plaza, and the aroma of stew wafting from a nearby house: the world was indifferent to their tragedy.

 

 

 

 

众位领袖听着判决。他们震惊于背叛王国的指控。不久之后，马尔多纳多跪在木桩前，低下头，以便与帕迪利亚的目光相接。刽子手挥斧砍下他的脖子时，他的头上仍带着一丝骄傲。下一个是布拉沃。刽子手显然经验丰富：伤口同样干净利落。帕迪利亚眼睁睁地看着一个人化作一股鲜血喷涌而出。轮到他了。他感到后背被人推了一下。在旁观处决的总督和军官中，他寻找着最仁慈的面孔，走近了他。

The leaders listened to the sentence. They recoiled at the accusation that they had betrayed the kingdom. Soon after, Maldonado knelt before the wooden stump, resting his head so that he could meet Padilla's gaze. When the executioner brought the axe down on his neck, his head still held a hint of pride. Bravo was next. The executioner was clearly experienced: the cut was clean as well. Padilla watched as a man became a fountain of blood. It was his turn. He felt a push against his back. From among the governors and military officers witnessing the executions, he searched for the most merciful face and approached it.

我胸口有一封写给我妻子的信。请您发发慈悲，把它交给她。

—I have a letter for my wife in my chest. Please have mercy and deliver it to her.

那张仁慈的脸紧紧抿着嘴唇，努力压抑着情绪；帕迪利亚知道自己选对了信使。当他把头靠在树桩上时，这位来自托莱多的男人感到同伴们温热的鲜血沾在了他的脸颊上。他闭上眼睛，努力寻找最后一个念头。各种画面涌入他的脑海，他的意志无法将它们驱散。然而，当他听到斧头举起的呼啸声时，他脑海中只浮现出一个画面：从托雷洛巴顿城堡顶端俯瞰的卡斯蒂利亚风光。塔顶上有人陪伴着他。那不是马尔多纳多，而是一位目光炯炯、黑色卷发中蕴藏着力量的女子。就在他生命即将终结的那一刻，他再次感受到自己是一个自由的人。

The merciful face pressed its lips together to contain the emotion; Padilla knew he had chosen his messenger well. When he laid his head against the tree stump, the man from Toledo felt the warm blood of his companions on his cheek. He closed his eyes and searched for one last thought. Images crowded his mind, none of which his will could dismiss. However, the moment he heard the whistle of the axe being raised, he glimpsed only one within himself: the Castilian landscape from the top of Torrelobatón Castle. Someone was with him at the top of the tower. It wasn't Maldonado, but a woman with an energetic gaze, strength incarnate in her black curls. And in the instant before his life left him, he felt once more that he was a free man.

斧头落下。

The axe fell.

 

 

夫人，若您的悲伤不比我的离世更令我难过，我便心满意足了。我多么希望有更多时间，能写些话安慰您。夫人，您像个正常人一样，为自己的不幸而哭泣，而非为我的离世。我已一无所有，只留下我的灵魂，请您像对待最爱您的人那样对待它。

Lady, if your sorrow did not grieve me more than my death, I would consider myself blessed. I wish I had more time to write you some things for your comfort. You, lady, like a sane person, weep for your misfortune and not for my death. My soul, since I have nothing else, I leave in your hands. Do with it as you would with the thing that loved you most.

 

 

 

 

当查理五世正埋头研究对抗法国的大量地图和战略时，他才得知保皇党军队在维拉拉尔战役中取得胜利的消息。这场战争注定旷日持久，两位君主之间的敌意也使谈判毫无余地。尽管皇帝远未以同样的仇恨回应弗朗索瓦一世，但他认为法国君主在基督教世界和西班牙如此危急的时刻攻击自己，实在卑鄙无耻。他绝不会做出如此卑劣的事情。从这个意义上讲，他们的敌对是必要的。

The news of the royalist troops' victory at Villalar reached Charles while he was lost in a sea of ​​maps and strategies against the French. The war promised to be long, and the hostility between the two monarchs left no room for negotiation. Although the emperor was far from reciprocating Francis's hatred with a similar kind, he considered it vile enough that the French monarch would attack him at such a delicate moment for Christendom and for Spain. He would never have acted in such an ignoble manner. In that sense, their rivalry was necessary.

科穆内罗起义结束后，查理五世欣喜若狂，而与此同时，路德教的动乱也逐渐平息。查理五世每日祈祷，感谢上帝出人意料地出手相助，使他摆脱了困境。若是这场动乱持续下去，恐怕会给他的帝国带来致命的动乱。如今，他可以全力投入对法战争，因为其他一切障碍都已消失。

The joy at the end of the Comunero Revolt was compounded by another similar sentiment: Lutheran unrest continued to wane after the friar's disappearance. Charles prayed daily to thank God for intervening so unexpectedly to deliver him from a predicament that, had it persisted, could have fatally destabilized his Empire. He could now dedicate all his efforts to the war against France, because all other obstacles had vanished.

 

 

 

 

瓦特堡傲然屹立于艾森纳赫城附近的一处悬崖边。它的雄伟壮丽，可谓优雅：既如宫殿般华丽，又如堡垒般坚固。城堡内房间众多，不胜枚举，因此很容易迷失其中，不知不觉间便会俯瞰到城堡所依附的那条长达半公里的峡谷。然而，近来，所有房间中，只有一间日夜灯火通明。萨克森的腓特烈喜欢从自己的房间里瞥见这间客厅，那永不熄灭的光芒，仿佛城堡里有一座灯塔。他时不时会走到这间客厅前，恭敬地敲响房门。每次得到允许进入后，他看到的总是同样的景象：一张堆满文件的桌子，马丁·路德正埋头于此，认真地处理着文件。这时，这位萨克森人便会露出骄傲的微笑。多亏了他策划的绑架事件，德国才有可能爆发并永远改变，而罗马或皇帝本人却无力阻止。

Wartburg Castle stood perched on the edge of a precipice near the city of Eisenach. Its robustness was, one might say, elegant: beautiful as a palace and as sturdy as a fortress. The number of rooms was countless, and it was therefore easy to get lost within its walls and end up, unwittingly, peering down the half-kilometer-long gorge upon which it was built. But lately, of all its chambers, only one remained illuminated day and night. Frederick of Saxony liked to glimpse this living room from his own chamber, this glow that never faded, as if the castle possessed a lighthouse. From time to time, he would approach this room and knock respectfully on the door. Upon receiving permission to enter, the scene he encountered was always the same: a table laden with documents and Martin Luther working diligently on them. Then the Saxon would offer a proud smile. Thanks to the kidnapping he had orchestrated, Germany could still erupt and change forever, without Rome or the emperor himself being able to do anything to prevent it.

7

7

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

查理缓缓走向灵柩台。当他走到躺在那里的尸体旁时，首先映入眼帘的是那双紧握在腹部的大理石手，僵硬而青筋暴起，却连一根羽毛都抓不住。一只苍蝇落在其中一根食指上，无辜地掠过那僵硬的手指。皇帝拂去苍蝇，不经意间轻轻触碰到了死者的皮肤。他感到一阵寒意袭来，嘴唇干裂。随后，他抬起头，看向尸体的脸。“亲爱的希耶夫，即使现在你也不得安宁，”他心想；因为即使双眼紧闭，尸体脸上的表情也透着一丝紧张的警觉，仿佛在等待着什么紧急的皇家指示：一种怀疑。或许，即使在死后，他也像所有人一样，对自己不幸遭遇的原因心存疑虑，这或许就是他既无法安息，也无法获得生命的意义。尽管医生们断定死因是自然死亡，但死得如此突然，以至于有人怀疑路德教徒可能为了永远封住那张在沃尔姆斯议会上对修士出言不逊的嘴，而毒死了他。查理拒绝相信这种说法。从得知噩耗的那一刻起，失去恩师就成了他唯一的牵挂。就连仍在进行的法法战争，在短短几天内也失去了意义。顾问的离世，让皇帝感到孤单：这个人的缺席比他的在世更令他难以承受。现在他明白了，躺在灵柩上的这个人，多年来一直像他的父亲一样：一位严厉、有时专横的父亲，犯下的罪行一旦被发现，便令他痛苦不堪；他不知疲倦，狡猾如饥饿的野兽，言辞犀利，时而自我牺牲，时而自私自利，全凭风向使然。这绝非理想的父亲形象，但正因如此，他才显得更加真实，像大多数父母一样，既全心全意地爱着儿子，又对自己的错误视而不见。尽管皇帝已坚定决心许久，有时也展现出成熟稳重的风度，但失去希耶夫尔却让他感到支离破碎，仿佛失去了抵御世间一切的盾牌。他意识到自己一直理所当然地认为，他的保护圈将永世长存，仿佛没有什么能够将其打破。他真是个孩子，竟然如此轻视死亡。

Charles approached the catafalque slowly. When he reached the corpse lying there, he first studied the marble hands clasped over the belly, so rigid and with such powerful veins, and yet so incapable of grasping even a feather. A fly landed on one of the index fingers and flitted across the inert fingers with innocent shamelessness. The emperor brushed it away and, in doing so, lightly touched the dead man's skin. He felt a chill that dried his mouth. He then raised his gaze to the corpse's face. "Not even now do you rest, dear Chièvres," he thought; for the grimace of his expression, even with his eyes closed, reflected a tense alertness, a sense of urgent royal counsel: of suspicion. Perhaps he, even in the afterlife, harbored, like everyone, doubts about the reason for his misfortune, and that was why he lacked both life and rest. Although the physicians concluded that the cause of death was natural, it happened so suddenly that it was suspected the Lutherans might have poisoned him to silence forever the mouth that had uttered such arrogance toward the friar at the Diet of Worms. Charles refused to give credence to this theory. The loss of his mentor was his sole focus from the moment he learned the news. Even the war with France, which was still ongoing, lost its importance for a few days. With his advisor gone, the emperor felt orphaned: the absence of this man would mark him more deeply than his presence. Now he understood that the man lying on the catafalque had served as his father for years: a stern, sometimes despotic father, with sins that had been painful once discovered, tireless, as cunning as a hungry animal, with a forked tongue, self-sacrificing or selfish depending on which way the wind blew. Nothing like an ideal of fatherhood, but precisely for that reason all the more real, as devoted and blind to his mistakes as most parents are. And although the emperor had been strengthening his resolve for some time and at times possessed the poise of unblemished maturity, losing Chièvres made him feel dismembered, with one less shield against the world. He realized that he had taken it for granted that his circle would be eternal, as if nothing could break it. What a child he had been to ignore death.

 

 

 

 

在顾问下葬几天后启程返回西班牙的途中，查理始终怀着即将与哈德良重逢的憧憬，相信在哈德良的陪伴下，以及在加蒂娜拉的陪伴下，他的孤寂感会减轻一些。加蒂娜拉为人坦率果断而不失风度，才智过人，而且忠诚如传教士。在航行途中，皇帝很享受与她的交谈，但他意识到自己与这位宰相相处的时间还不够长，彼此之间的关系并不亲密，至少不像与希耶夫尔那样亲密——那种亲密有时令人窒息，最后甚至灼热难耐，但终究是温暖。说实话，他觉得自己年纪大了，无法再自欺欺人地在加蒂娜拉身上寻找另一个父亲般的角色。他们会是合作者、朋友，仅此而已。总有一天，他会走到他的遗体前，默默祈祷，感谢他曾经的付出、建议和玩笑。但他的离世不会让他难以承受，也不会让他留下挥之不去的被抛弃的痛苦。随着希耶夫的去世，他几乎没有任何情感上的牵绊，而他仅存的那些——他的玛格丽塔姑妈，还有费尔南多？——也随着他远航的船被抛在了身后。查尔斯感到周围弥漫着空虚、孤独和冷漠的气息。他害怕自己永远无法与任何人建立起足够深厚的感情，以至于仅仅想到失去他们就会让他颤抖。

During the return voyage to Spain, which began a few days after the advisor's burial, Charles clung to the idea of ​​his imminent reunion with Hadrian, trusting that his sense of abandonment would lessen in his presence, and also to the company of Gattinara. Gattinara knew how to be direct and resolute without being offensive, possessed abundant intelligence, and, moreover, was as faithful as an evangelist. Throughout the crossing, the emperor enjoyed their conversation, but realized that he and the chancellor had not spent enough time together for their bond to be truly warm, at least not as intimate and endearing as it had been with Chièvres—a warmth that was sometimes stifling, scorching in its final stages, but warmth nonetheless. To tell the truth, he felt too old to delude himself into seeking another father figure in Gattinara. They would be collaborators, friends, and little more, and one day he would approach his body and thank him with a prayer for the services rendered, the advice, and a few jokes, but his passing would not be unbearable, and no, it would not leave him with that lingering taste of abandonment. With Chièvres dead, he had hardly any sentimental ties left, and those he possessed—his Aunt Margarita, Fernando?—were left behind as the ship sailed on. Charles sensed around him an aura of emptiness, of loneliness and indifference. He was afraid he would never bond with anyone enough for the mere thought of their loss to make him tremble.

 

 

 

 

桑坦德人迎接他的方式与多年前他在塔佐内斯遭遇的石块雨截然不同。皇帝一踏上这片土地，便从每一位迎接他的西班牙人身上感受到的远不止礼貌；他们对他表现出的尊重，是他第一次感受到如此真挚的敬意。科穆内罗起义，尤其是法国宣战，极大地提升了西班牙人对国王的敬重：没有什么比外部威胁更能团结他们，让他们忘却恩怨，渴望一位他们甘愿臣服的强权领袖。查理正享受着臣民们的盛情款待时，加蒂纳拉召见了他。

Santander welcomed him in a manner quite different from the hail of stones that had greeted him in Tazones years before. The moment he set foot on land, the emperor perceived in each of the Spaniards who awaited him something more than mere courtesy; they treated him with a respect that, for the first time, seemed genuine. The Comunero Revolt and, above all, the war declared by France, had elevated the Spaniards' esteem for their king: nothing like an external threat to unite them, make them forget grievances, and yearn for a strong leader to whom they would gladly submit. Charles was allowing himself to be feted by his subjects when Gattinara summoned him to his side.

“陛下，阿德里亚诺……！”那位意大利人激动得热泪盈眶。“阿德里亚诺当选教皇了！”

"Your Majesty, Adriano…!" The Italian was overcome with nervous joy. "Adriano has been elected Pope!"

“我们的哈德良？”国王脸上满是惊讶。随即，自豪之情涌上心头。“我真为他……也为我们感到高兴。”

"Our Hadrian?" The king was the very picture of surprise. Then, without delay, pride overwhelmed him. "How happy I am for him... and for us."

——你说得对。法国明智的做法是退出这场冲突。现在，罗马军队将以更加饱满的斗志向他们的军队发起猛攻！我们将守住米兰，高卢人如果想夺回它，就只能被迫撤退。

—You speak well. France would be wise to withdraw from the conflict. Now, the armies of Rome will descend upon their troops with renewed vigor! We will hold Milan, and the Gauls will be forced to retreat if they wish to recapture it.

查理听到“米兰”这个名字，想起了自己得知军队攻占米兰时那种扭曲的喜悦——他骑士般的举止确实有所停顿；但是，从弗朗西斯手中夺走他伟大的征服成果，让他心生一丝恶意也是值得的。

Charles heard "Milan" and remembered the perverse joy with which he had received the news that his armies had taken it—a pause in his chivalrous demeanor, yes; but snatching away from Francis what had been his great conquest was well worth allowing himself a certain malice.

“上帝希望我们取得胜利，大法官，”查尔斯说。“我渴望与阿德里安会面，并希望基督教世界的两位领袖能够开始齐心协力。”

"God wants us to be victorious, Chancellor," said Charles. "I long to meet with Adrian, and for the two heads of Christendom to begin thinking as one."

七月的烈日无情地炙烤着港口。皇帝白皙的脸颊开始泛红，但他却可以花上几个小时凝视着那平静的大海，以及山坡上闪耀着翡翠般光泽的景色。西班牙人对他的仇恨正在消退，一位忠诚的朋友如今已登上罗马的王位，而路德依然沉默不语。那一刻，希望让他忘记了内心的空虚。命运如此眷顾他，让他感觉不到任何人的缺席。

The July sun beat down relentlessly on the port. The emperor's milky complexion was beginning to flush, but he could have spent hours gazing at the calm sea that stretched across the sky, as well as the emerald-hued landscape that shone on the hillsides. The Spanish were letting their hatred for him fade, a loyal friend now occupied the throne of Rome, and Luther still hadn't made a sound. For a moment, hope made him forget his own emptiness. Fortune smiled upon him so brightly that he missed no one.

我做梦也想不到，当他沿着人们为他庆祝的道路深入王国腹地时，乌得勒支的阿德里安已经逃往梵蒂冈，躲避他。

I would never have imagined that, while he was going deeper into the kingdom along roads where he was being celebrated, Adrian of Utrecht was already traveling to the Vatican, fleeing from him.

 

 

 

 

“什么？他已经走了？”卡洛斯愤愤不平地问道，“他不是一直等着见我吗？他不是知道我马上就要到了吗？”

"What do you mean he's already left?" Carlos spat the words out indignantly. "Didn't he wait to meet me, knowing my arrival was imminent?"

在巴利亚多利德的法庭中央，法德里克·德·阿尔巴强忍住一声无奈的叹息。他早就料到皇帝会是这般反应，别无其他。正因如此，他坚持让阿德里安留在卡斯蒂利亚，直到查理五世祝福他启程前往罗马——这样才能巩固他们新的关系，使两人都站在权力的巅峰。然而，这位来自乌得勒支的教皇在被任命后却变得固执而焦躁，这对他来说实属罕见。教皇之位是他未经请求便被授予的，这对他来说无疑是难以接受的：他突然变得紧张而难以捉摸。事实上，他并不渴望这份荣耀，但他又怎能拒绝呢？

In the middle of the Valladolid courtroom, Fadrique de Alba stifled a sigh of resignation. He had guessed that this, and nothing else, would be the emperor's reaction. For this reason, he had insisted that Adrian remain in Castile until Charles could bless his departure for Rome—and thus solidify their new relationship, with both of them at the pinnacle of power. But the man from Utrecht, after the appointment, had been stubborn and agitated, something unusual for him. The papacy had been granted to him without him even having asked for it, and it had been a bitter pill to swallow: suddenly he had become nervous and elusive. The truth was, he hadn't longed for this honor, but how could he refuse it?

“正如他告诉我的，”公爵回答皇帝说，“他的目的是避免被指控与您过度勾结。他说，他的身份要求他保持公正，任何举动都可能使这种公正受到质疑。”

“As he informed me,” the duke replied to the emperor, “his intention is to avoid being accused of excessive collusion with you. His position, he said, demands an impartiality that any gesture could call into question.”

“我们刚到这里时，他就充分利用了我缺乏中立立场这一点！他会回报我，无视我们之间的共同点吗？即使是在对法战争中？”

"He took full advantage of my lack of neutrality when we arrived here! And will he repay me by ignoring what unites us? Even in the war against France?"

从法德里克的举动中，卡洛斯明白事情会是这样。

From Fadrique's gesture, Carlos understood that this would be the case.

“叛国！”皇帝说道，他感到一股孤独的气息在他周围蔓延，直到他与世隔绝。

"Treason," said the emperor, and he felt the aura of loneliness growing around him until it isolated him from the world.

随后，一个新的声音响起：

A new voice was then heard:

陛下，如果您允许我提些建议，请不要因为他的缺席而表现出恼怒。那样会让他意识到自己的权力。而且，他迟早还是需要您的。

—If you'll allow me to offer some advice, Your Majesty, don't show irritation at his absence. That would make him aware of his power. And it's not so much that he won't need you sooner or later.

“谁说的？”卡洛斯问道，他指的是那个长脸、眼神深邃如井的年轻人，他竟然主动和他搭话。虽然他是和法德里克一起来的，但对头衔不熟悉的人会以为是公爵陪同他来的，而不是反过来。他那张稚气未脱的脸庞，无需任何言语或举动，便散发出一种独特的魅力，给人的感觉是前途光明，而且完全符合他的心意。

"Who says so?" Carlos asked, referring to the young man with the long face and deep, well-like eyes who had dared to speak to him unprompted. Although he had arrived with Fadrique, someone unfamiliar with titles would have assumed it was the duke accompanying him, not the other way around. With that boyish face, he exuded magnetism without needing to do or say anything, and gave the impression of having a future not only promising but perfectly suited to his desires.

法德里克解释说：“我向你们介绍我的孙子费尔南多·德·阿尔巴，我的儿子（愿上帝保佑他）把他赐予我，作为我的头衔继承人。”

—I present to you my grandson, Fernando de Alba, whom my son, may God have him in his glory, gave to me as heir to my titles —explained Fadrique.

年轻人向国王鞠躬。

The young man bowed to his king.

“如你所知，我幼年时也失去了父亲，”凯撒说道，“我很遗憾我们遭遇了同样的命运。”

—As you well know, I too lost my father when I was just a child—said the Caesar. —I regret that we have suffered the same fate.

命运磨砺性格，孤独雕琢性格。大人，没有哪个伟人不是从不幸中崛起的。

—Fate hardens the character and solitude chisels it. There is no great man who does not arise from misfortune, my lord.

皇帝凝视着费尔南多·德·阿尔瓦。随着谢夫尔的离世，世间所有的活力都消逝了，甚至可以说，自古以来所有逝者的活力，似乎都凝聚在这个年轻人身上。查理意识到，法德里克的孙子拥有成为巨人的潜质，他的伟大并非源于头衔，而是源于一种超越常人的精神追求。拥有这种品格的人不宜过多，否则，世界将会毁灭。

The emperor gazed at Fernando de Alba. All the vitality that had left the world with Chièvres' departure, and one might almost say all the vitality of those who had died since the beginning of time, seemed concentrated in this young man. Charles sensed that Fadrique's grandson possessed the seed to become a titan, one of those men whose greatness stems not from the title they hold but from a spiritual drive that elevates them above the rest. There couldn't be too many men with such character because, if they were the norm, the world would explode.

“我会重视你的意见。”卡洛斯瞥了法德里克一眼；他不想太快让这个年轻人得意忘形。“告诉我科穆内罗起义的消息。”

"I will value your opinion." Carlos glanced at Fadrique; he didn't want to make the young man proud too soon. "Give me news about the Comunero uprising."

“只有少数村庄仍然动荡不安，”公爵骄傲地回答道。

"Only a few villages remain agitated," the duke replied proudly.

“是时候伸张正义了，这些火苗必须熄灭，”皇帝宣布道。“所有首领都被逮捕了吗？”

"It is time to do justice, and those embers will be extinguished," the emperor declared. "Have all the leaders been arrested?"

——其中最臭名昭著的几人已在维拉拉尔被处决。但许多罪魁祸首仍然在世，尽管现在身陷囹圄。至于那些响应这些煽动者的号召加入战斗的人……人数成千上万，男女老少，来自各行各业。各城市的市长们正在努力统计他们的名字。

—The most prominent ones were executed in Villalar. But many of those responsible are still alive, though now in prison. As for those who answered the call of these agitators and joined the fight… there are thousands, men and even women of all walks of life. The governors of each city are working hard to compile their names.

“不必如此，”来自根特的男子说道，“我将赦免王国所有公民。但所有领导人都必须处决，一个不留。”

"That won't be necessary," the man from Ghent declared. "I will grant a general pardon to the kingdom. But the leaders must be executed. Every single one of them."

仅仅几个小时后，查理就用同一只手签署了赦免令和谴责令。他如释重负，因为他找到了解决问题的理想方案：赦免民众似乎合情合理，也有助于他赢得民众的支持；而处决首领则可以起到震慑作用，防止他们日后再次发动暴力叛乱。他懊恼自己没有办法与阿德里安交涉；他意识到，在这件事上，唯一的希望就是这位前卡斯蒂利亚摄政王能够明白，任何统治者，即使是教皇，都不能选择中立，因为即便不作为，也总会有一方比另一方更有利。

Just a few hours later, Charles was signing indulgences and condemnations with the same hand. He was relieved to have found an ideal solution to resolve the matter: pardoning the people seemed just, and it would also help him gain their favor, while executing the ringleaders would serve as a warning against future temptations to violent rebellion. He lamented not having a way to address the issue with Adrian; he sensed that in this matter, the only hope was that the former Castilian regent would understand that no ruler, not even the Pope, could choose neutrality, because even inaction always benefited one side more than the other.

 

 

 

 

那天晚上，查理一踏进自己多年未曾踏足的寝宫，就想起了杰尔玛娜。几个月来，他一直没有想起她。他和约翰娜共度的那段田园牧歌般的时光——快乐、肉欲、却又转瞬即逝——让他免于思念。他深情地向这位佛兰德斯女子告别，却毫无遗憾，以皇帝的身份向她承诺，他会确保她腹中的孩子永远衣食无忧——那会是个女孩，又一个他的私生子。然而，自从他回到巴利亚多利德的宫廷后，无数的细节如同幽灵般将这位天主教寡妇的身影拼凑起来。他们曾无数次共枕的床，贴着他的肌肤，仿佛又回到了她的身边，仿佛在召唤着他。然后，当他终于入睡时，他梦见了战争，梦中他孤身一人面对着成千上万的法国士兵，统帅弗朗西斯的脸庞酷似阿德里安。战场上尸横遍野，死者们目光冰冷地望着天空，身上爬满了苍蝇，其中就包括日耳曼娜。

That night, as soon as he entered his chamber, which he hadn't set foot in for years, Charles remembered Germana. His memory of her hadn't brought him back for months. The idyll he'd shared with Johanna—joyful, carnal, forgettable—had spared him nostalgia. He had bid the Flemish woman farewell with affection but without regret, giving her his word as emperor that he would see to it that the baby she carried would always have its every need met—it would be a girl, another little bastard of his blood. However, since his return to the court in Valladolid, countless details had been piecing together the ghost of the Catholic's widow. The bed they had shared so many times felt like hers against his skin, as if it were calling to him. Then, when he finally fell asleep, he had dreams of war in which, alone, he faced thousands of French soldiers, led by a Francis who wore the face of Adrian. Among the dead carpeting the battlefield, with their icy gaze fixed on the sky and covered in flies, was Germana.

他醒来时感到一阵眩晕，这种不安的感觉持续了两天，直到在一次皇家会议上，他才鼓起勇气询问她的下落。法德里克的脸色阴沉了下来。

He woke up dizzy, and that feeling of unease lasted two days, until he dared, during a royal council, to ask about her. Fadrique's expression darkened.

据说她饱受丈夫虐待……

—It is said that she suffers at the hands of her husband…

卡洛斯挺直身子，保持警觉。

Carlos stood up straight, alert.

——你如何称呼苦难？

—What do you call suffering?

贪婪、蔑视……令人作呕。

—Rapacities, contempt… blows.

皇帝感觉胃里像被人用长矛刺穿了一样。他真想取消这次会面，花剩下的时间骑马赶到杰曼娜和她丈夫所在的地方，把她安全救出来后，把勃兰登堡公爵按倒在地，打断他的指关节，让他为自己的卑鄙行径付出代价。

The emperor's stomach felt like it had been speared. He would have liked to cancel the meeting and spend the rest of the day riding to wherever Germana and her husband were, and after bringing her to safety, pin the Duke of Brandenburg to the ground and break his knuckles making him pay for his vileness.

你必须尽快到我面前来。

—You must appear before me as soon as possible.

“你丈夫？”法德里克问道。

"Your husband?" Fadrique asked.

不，是她。

—No; she.

公爵点了点头，注意到国王因天主教寡妇的不幸遭遇而情绪激动，便开始谈论王国的其他事务来安抚他，把最棘手的事情留到最后。

The duke nodded and, noticing the king's agitated mood due to the misfortunes of the Catholic's widow, proceeded to calm him with other matters of the kingdom, leaving one of the most adverse for last.

——遵照你的命令，平民领袖们已被逮捕。但是，他们当中那位举足轻重的人物却下落不明。

—As you ordered, the commoners' leaders are being arrested. But there is no trace of the one who was so important among them.

你指的是谁？

—Who are you referring to?

 

 

 

 

玛丽亚·帕切科身着当年逃离托莱多时穿的那件衣服出现在葡萄牙宫廷——她几乎不记得那次逃亡了，当时城里弥漫着泪水和恐怖的气氛；每个人都害怕王室的报复，许多人逃离或脱离了市民民兵组织，混入平民之中，仿佛那几个月的战斗只是一场梦，现在是时候醒来了。令她惊讶的是，她受到了国王约翰的接见。在表明身份后，她解释了自己此行的目的：
