María Pacheco appeared at the Portuguese court in the same dress she had worn when she fled Toledo—she barely remembered the escape, which had been amidst tears and the climate of terror that reigned in the city; everyone there feared the Crown's vengeance, and many were fleeing or deserting the Comunero militias to blend in with the civilians, as if those months of fighting had been a dream and the time had come to wake up. To her surprise, she was received by King John. After stating who she was, she explained what had brought her there:

——我恳求您允许我将这片祖先的土地作为我的新家。我可以藏身于您王国的某个角落而不引起怀疑，但我问心无愧，没有什么需要隐瞒的：我宁愿将这一切告知您，殿下。

—I beg you to allow me to make this the land of my ancestors my new home. I could hide in a corner of your kingdom without arousing suspicion, but my conscience is clear and I have nothing to hide: I prefer to make this known to you, Your Highness.

—如果你来到我们面前，那是因为你不仅寻求一个席位，而且寻求保护——葡萄牙的伊莎贝尔插话道。

—If you come before us it is because you seek not only a seat, but protection—intervened Isabel of Portugal.

“我唯一的罪过就是渴望卡斯蒂利亚走向更美好的未来。除了失去我的丈夫——他被王室以正义之名斩首——之外，我既不配得到任何荣誉，也不配受到任何惩罚。”

"My only crime has been to yearn for the best for Castile. I deserve neither honors nor punishment, beyond the loss of my husband, whom the Crown beheaded in the name of justice."

胡安得知此事后震惊不已。他想象着失去挚爱之人竟是如此惨烈的痛苦；在他脑海中，莱昂诺尔浑身浴血，他几乎要怒吼出声。他心生怜悯，仔细端详着玛丽亚：她蓬乱的头发，脸上刻满了并非岁月痕迹而是苦难印记，眼神中满是黯淡的自尊。她骨瘦如柴，憔悴不堪，国王怀疑这并非长途跋涉或卡斯蒂利亚叛乱所致；而是亲眼目睹爱情破碎、对未来彻底绝望的折磨。

Juan was shocked to learn this. He imagined the pain of losing a loved one in such a brutal way; in his mind's eye, Leonor appeared stained with blood, and he felt like screaming with rage. Moved with compassion, he studied María: her unkempt hair, her face etched with marks not from age but from suffering, her gaze a shadow of diminished pride. She was gaunt, wasted away, and the king suspected it wasn't because of the long journey or the Castilian revolts; it was the effect of having seen her love shattered and of having lost any hope for the future.

我准许你。

—I grant it to you.

平民君主恭敬地亲吻了君主的手。君主离开后，伊莎贝尔质问了她的哥哥。

The commoner kissed the monarch's hands, albeit with dignity. Once he had left, Isabel confronted her brother.

——你们竟然欢迎一个几乎以武力夺取卡斯蒂利亚政权的人？

—Are you welcoming someone who almost seized power in Castile by force?

“一个孤身一人的女人能对我构成什么威胁？你见过她，她就像个幽灵，早已成为过去。再说，任何有名望的人，无论是天使还是魔鬼，都是很好的筹码。”

"What threat does a lone woman pose to me? You've seen her, she's a ghost, she's nothing but a past. Besides, anyone illustrious, angel or demon, is good currency."

她问道：“你打算勒索皇帝吗？”

"Do you plan to blackmail the emperor?" she asked.

——但我相信我应该不必这么做……

—I trust I won't have to, however…

伊莎贝尔胸口剧烈起伏：积压已久的怒火在她体内翻腾，几乎让她喘不过气来。胡安见她这般模样，便没再说完话，起身离开王座，匆匆赶在暴风雨来临前离开王宫，留下妹妹独自一人。这时，远处传来钟声。对公主而言，这钟声如同丧钟。每一次钟声响起，她的怒火便化作绝望。此刻，她觉得嫁给卡洛斯的想法至少是天真的。日复一日，事事发生，他们的命运如同肌肤般分离：两个原本注定要相伴一生的人，却因残酷的干​​预而永远分离。唯一能给她带来希望的，是他坚持要促成这桩婚事的决心。但她的信心却如同枯萎的花朵般开始凋零；她的白日梦里早已充斥着对未来的沮丧、孤独和忧郁——岁月都浪费在幻想那些很可能永远不会实现的事情上。她最终会嫁给任何一个国王，或许甚至连国王都算不上，可能是一个拥有庞大军队、傲慢自大的贵族，她不得不为他生儿育女，然后与他一起在寂静的夜晚，在炉火旁慢慢老去，强忍着泪水，回忆着那个从未实现的帝王之梦。

Isabel's chest heaved: so much pent-up anger surged within her that there was barely room for air. Seeing her in such a state, Juan didn't finish his sentence: he rose from the throne and hurried to leave the royal hall before the storm, leaving his sister alone. It was then that the tolling of bells reached the room from afar. To the princess, they sounded like a death knell. With each peal, her anger turned to desolation. By now, the possibility of her ever marrying Carlos seemed, at the very least, a naive thought. Day by day, event by event, their destinies were separating like the skin of a body: two elements that seemed condemned to live together but that, if cruelty interfered as much as it was, would be forever torn apart. And the only thing that could give her hope was his determination that this union would take place. But her confidence was beginning to wither like a parched flower; her daydreams were already filled with visions of a future of frustration, loneliness, and melancholy—years wasted fantasizing about something that might very well never come to pass. She would end up marrying just any king, or perhaps not even that, maybe an aristocrat with vast armies and a haughty air, whom she would have to bear children and with whom she would grow old in silent evenings by the fire, holding back tears as she remembered that imperial dream that never materialized.

与此同时，胡安为了躲避妹妹的怒火，拥抱了莱昂诺尔隆起的腹部，那里正孕育着一个生命。但真正需要安慰的却是卡洛斯的妹妹。

Meanwhile, Juan sought refuge from his sister's storm by embracing Leonor's belly, where a child was growing. But it was Carlos's sister who needed comfort.

我出去散步，竟然有臣民胆敢朝我吐口水。王国上下都知道：他们也知道我们的恋情。

—I went out for a walk and some subjects dared to spit on me. The kingdom knows: it's aware of our romance.

莱昂诺尔很沮丧，脸上写满了屈辱。

Leonor was upset; the humiliation was etched on her face.

“当我们结婚时，你将再次成为女王，”君主说，“任何冒犯你的人都将面临死刑。”

"When we marry, you will be queen again," said the monarch, "and whoever offends you will face death."

“你总是谈论我们的婚礼，但那都只是说说而已，”她抱怨道。

"You always talk about our wedding, but it's all just talk," she complained.

—我说的话就是誓言。

—If it's my word, it's an oath.

但当胡安吻别心爱的女子后离开房间时，他脑海中却挥之不去臣民们向埃莉诺吐口水的画面，这意味着他们对国王的选择嗤之以鼻。尽管他的爱意本应驱散这种态度在他心中激起的疑虑，但他第一次开始怀疑，仅仅遵从自己的情感是否正确。

But when Juan, after kissing his beloved, left the room, he was haunted by the image of his subjects spitting at Eleanor, which meant they scornfully disapproved of their king's choice. And although his love was meant to dispel the doubts that this attitude aroused in him, for the first time he wondered if he was doing the right thing by obeying only his feelings.

 

 

 

 

莱昂诺尔为什么还没回来？她的丈夫很久以前就去世了。

—Why hasn't Leonor returned yet? Her husband died a long time ago.

卡洛斯天真地问道，这种天真正是加蒂娜拉在精心编造答案时所缺乏的。

Carlos asked innocently, the kind of innocence that Gattinara lacked when she cooked up her answer.

—你的妹妹怀了曼努埃尔国王的孩子。他的儿子，也就是现在的国王，恳求她在里斯本生下孩子，以免在前往卡斯蒂利亚的途中出现任何问题。

—Your sister became pregnant by King Manuel. His son, who now sits on the throne, has begged her to give birth in Lisbon to avoid any problems that might arise from the journey to Castile.

皇帝点了点头，并未太在意，但他注意到宰相虽然一直保持沉默，有所保留，但已经张开了嘴，似乎想要继续说话。

The emperor nodded without giving it much importance, but he noticed that his chancellor had opened his mouth with the intention of continuing to speak, although he had remained silent, holding back.

——告诉他——卡洛斯鼓励他。

—Tell him —Carlos encouraged him.

—陛下，关于您在葡萄牙宫廷的处境，有很多非常恶毒的谣言。

—There are… really poisonous rumors about your situation at the court of Portugal, Your Majesty.

到底是哪一个？

-Which is it?

—有传言说她和她的继子约翰国王之间有一段恋情。

—There is talk of a romance between her and her stepson, King John.

皇帝花了片刻时间，从意大利人的举动中判断事情的真伪：他的表情如此严肃——并且表现出对背负如此屈辱的指控的羞愧——这只能是真的。

The emperor allowed himself a moment to gauge the veracity of the matter in the Italian's gesture: his expression was so grave —and showed such shame at being the bearer of such a degrading accusation— that it could only be true.

“能传遍王国的谣言，想必在王国内部蔓延得如同瘟疫一般，”查尔斯担忧地说，“等她生产之后，我立刻命令她回到我身边，我一定会想办法弥补这桩耻辱。”

"A rumor that has managed to cross the borders of a kingdom must have spread like a plague within it," said Charles, worried. "I will order her to return to my side as soon as she has given birth, and I will find a way to repair the dishonor."

她刚离开办公室，杰尔马纳的身影就再次占据了皇帝的心神。埃莉诺卷入的丑闻让她想起了自己当年爱上祖父遗孀而引发的丑闻。这一次，轮到她扮演“希耶夫尔”的角色了：为了维护自己的颜面，她必须拆散这段无疑是真挚的爱情——她认为埃莉诺无法毫无感情地付出真心；不幸的是，她是个浪漫的人。她的血统在激情面前显得软弱无力；不过，考虑到她是乔安娜的后裔，又能指望什么呢？

No sooner had she left the office than Germana once again occupied the emperor's thoughts. The scandal in which Eleanor was embroiled reminded her of the one he had caused by falling in love with his grandfather's widow. This time, it was her turn to play the role of Chièvres: to save face by breaking up what was surely a sincere love—she saw Eleanor as incapable of surrendering herself without feeling; she was a romantic soul, unfortunately for her. Her lineage showed weakness in the face of passion; although what could be expected, given that she was descended from Joanna?

那天早晨，卡洛斯虽然努力想入睡却徒劳无功，整日都在想着杰尔玛娜。他的失眠与以往那种因对她的爱慕而辗转难眠的痛苦截然不同。如今，他感受到的不再是欲望，而是无尽的悲伤。躺在床上，被寂静和黑暗笼罩，他的孤独感愈发强烈。他仿佛掉进了一口无人愿意救他上来的井里，甚至连死亡也无法解脱：他只能苟活，却没有牵绊，没有情感，没有温暖可以驱散他的痛苦。无数的头衔和荣誉反而加剧了这种感觉；他想，宫殿越是宏伟，独自居住的空虚感就越发强烈。

That morning, though he tried in vain to sleep, Carlos spent the hours thinking of Germana. His insomnia was hardly like the kind that used to plague him when his passion for her consumed him. Now he felt not desire, but an infinite sadness. In bed, shrouded in silence and darkness, his feeling of loneliness grew. He seemed to have fallen into a well from which no one was willing to rescue him, and where not even death would come to relieve him: he would have to live, but without ties, without emotions, without warmth in which to burn away his anguish. So many titles and honors only intensified the feeling; the grander the palace, he thought, the more intense the emptiness of inhabiting it alone.

与法国的战争是他唯一牵挂的事，让他忘却了其他一切。来自各条战线的消息都令人沮丧。法国人攻陷米兰后，再次入侵，而战争的开支已经达到了天文数字，进一步掏空了本就因帝国征战而捉襟见肘的国库。查理担心，终有一天他会因为无力支付军饷而被迫下令撤军；这无疑将意味着一场耻辱性的失败，不仅会让他作为凯撒的形象蒙羞，更重要的是，还会刺激弗朗索瓦等人进攻他的其他领地。

The war with France was the only concern that made him forget everything else. The news arriving from the various fronts was not very encouraging. The French had responded to the capture of Milan by invading it again, and the expenses of the conflict, which were increasing to an astronomical sum, were depleting coffers still weakened after the expenditure on the imperial campaign. Charles feared that the day would come when he would be forced to order the withdrawal of his troops because he lacked the funds to pay them; this would undoubtedly mean a humiliating defeat, one that would ridicule him as Caesar and, above all, encourage Francis and perhaps others to attack his other domains.

“告诉哈德良，战争的矛头指向你们。向他请求增援！”加蒂纳拉恳求道。

"Tell Hadrian that the war is against you. Ask him for troops!" Gattinara urged.

“教皇不会帮我们的，”卡洛斯断言，“我不会向那个帮我做我本该自己做的事的人下跪。别指望他了。”

"The Pope won't help us," Carlos asserted. "And I won't kneel before the one who helped me do what I should already be doing. Let's not count on him."

—既然如此，或许是时候请求休战了，陛下。

—In that case, perhaps it is time to ask for a truce, Your Majesty.

皇帝沉思了片刻。

The emperor pondered it for a few moments.

“现在还太早了。”她说这话的时候，明知自己在撒谎，明知现在连挽回名誉都太迟了，但她不想这么快就放弃。

"It's still too soon." As she said it, she knew she was lying, that it was even too late to save her honor, but she didn't want to give up so soon.

法德里克·德·阿尔巴一直旁观着这场对话，没有插手，他向前走了几步。他的孙子费尔南多站在他身旁，沉默不语，仔细聆听着对方的每一个建议。

Fadrique de Alba, who had witnessed the conversation without intervening, moved a few steps forward. Beside him, his grandson Fernando remained silent, absorbing every detail of the advice.

“在围绕法国国王的链条中，存在一个薄弱环节。这个环节能够召集三万大军加入他的领地。如果这个环节对我们有利，就能改变这场战争的走向，陛下。”

"In the chain surrounding the King of France, there is a weak link. A link capable of rallying thirty thousand men to his domains. If it were to work in our favor, it could change the course of this war, Your Majesty."

卡洛斯困惑地看着公爵。

Carlos looked at the duke in bewilderment.

 

 

 

 

波旁公爵骑着一匹骏马，在约定的地点驻足良久。他来得早，心中忐忑不安。此刻，在这片春意盎然的法国乡村腹地，他不时地整理丝绒外套的纽扣，以缓解紧张。终于，他看到了一位绅士。这一定是他的联络人。他催马靠近那位绅士。待距离合适，波旁公爵和阿尔巴公爵微微一礼，互相致意。他们彼此都感受到了只有伟人才具备的独特气质。

The Duke of Bourbon, mounted on a magnificent horse, lingered at the appointed place. He had arrived early, his nerves on edge. Now, in the heart of the French countryside, the landscape adorned with spring blossoms, he released his tension by repeatedly adjusting the buttons of his silk and velvet jacket. At last, he caught sight of a gentleman. This had to be his contact. He urged his horse to approach the approaching gentleman. When the distance was right, the Duke of Bourbon and the Duke of Alba greeted each other with a slight gesture. They recognized in one another the distinction that only great men possess.

“我们别下马，”法德里克说，“这主要是为了你的安全，而不是我的。”

"Let's not dismount," said Fadrique. "More for your safety than mine."

波旁酒鬼点了点头。他感到胃部一阵阵抽痛，浑身冒汗却并不觉得热；他已经等待这一刻多年，如今它终于到来，他感到无比激动。

The Bourbon man nodded. He felt twinges in his stomach and was sweating without feeling hot; he had been waiting for this moment for years and, now that it had arrived, he was overwhelmed.

“你这是在提议背叛。”他回复了几天前阿尔巴发来的信息，正是这条信息把他带到了这里。

—You are proposing a betrayal —he replied to the message he had received from Alba days before, which had brought him there.

“即使领主待封臣不公，剥夺其一切，封臣也不会背叛领主，”卡斯蒂利亚人答道，“你们要听命于皇帝，必将得到奖赏。”

"A vassal does not betray his lord if the latter treats him unjustly and deprives him of everything that is his," replied the Castilian. "Place yourselves at the emperor's disposal and you will be rewarded for it."

-如何？

-How?

“最长久的，”阿尔芭回答说。“凯撒的妹妹埃莉诺嫁给了葡萄牙国王，成了寡妇。你的婚姻将是巩固这一联盟的最佳方式。”

"The most lasting," Alba replied. "Eleanor, Caesar's sister, has been widowed by the King of Portugal. Your marriage would be the best seal for this alliance."

这位法国人没想到会收到如此慷慨的提议，但他掩饰住了内心的喜悦。自从弗朗西斯剥夺了他大部分财产和头衔后，他就对所有人都心存戒备。说实话，他最忠诚的部下并没有离他而去，但对许多其他人来说，他却因国王的憎恨而蒙上了污名。每当他出现在宴会上，都会引发一片沉默和紧张，因为他的存在——曾经至少是一种荣耀——如今却成了一种污点。这位贵族知道，这样的场景注定会一直重复，直到他生命的尽头，因为弗朗西斯丝毫没有悔改之意。波旁公爵看着阿尔巴公爵，心想他是否敢这么做。这在某种程度上类似于中年改嫁：放弃所有过去的羁绊，放弃那些一直陪伴着他的风景、面孔，更不用说名誉，以及几乎全部的回忆。

The Frenchman hadn't expected such a generous offer, but he concealed his pleasure. Ever since Francis had stripped him of most of his possessions and titles, he distrusted everyone. To tell the truth, his most loyal men hadn't abandoned him, but for many others, he had been stigmatized by the king's hatred, and when he entered a party, he provoked silence and tension, because his presence, which had once been at least an honor, now constituted a stain. The nobleman knew that this scene was destined to repeat itself until the end of his days, because Francis showed no sign of repenting for his abuse. The Duke of Bourbon looked at the Duke of Alba and wondered if he would dare to do it. It was, in a way, akin to changing families mid-life: renouncing all previous ties, the landscapes that had always been his companions, faces, not to mention reputations, and almost memories.

—我需要考虑一下。

—I need to think about it.

 

 

 

 

查理等待着法国人的回信，努力将注意力集中在战争上，这时他的妹妹凯瑟琳从托尔德西拉斯寄来一封信。信中，她颤抖着笔迹，描述了她和母亲在现任总督德尼亚侯爵手中遭受的虐待。皇帝感到一股复仇的怒火再次涌上心头，就像当初得知杰尔马娜婚姻不幸时一样。但他的顾问警告他，公主可能因为厌倦了被囚禁，试图通过捏造不幸来逃避他的控制。尽管如此，查理还是没有忽视妹妹的控诉，下令调查真相。托尔德西拉斯宫廷的仆人们被询问后，都不愿多言——他们总是低着头，声音哽咽，焦虑不安——但足以让人明白，侯爵是个阴险狡诈之人，能够做出凯瑟琳所描述的那些暴行：残酷的侮辱和惩罚，甚至会在受害者身上留下伤痕。

Charles awaited the Frenchman's reply and tried to keep his mind focused on the war when a letter arrived from Tordesillas from his sister Catherine. In her trembling handwriting, she described the mistreatment she and her mother were suffering at the hands of the current governor, the Marquis of Denia. The emperor sensed a return to the same thirst for violent revenge he had felt upon learning of Germana's marital misfortunes, but his advisors warned him that the Infanta, weary of her confinement, might be trying to escape him by fabricating misfortunes. Nevertheless, Charles refused to ignore his sister's complaints and ordered an investigation to determine the truth behind them. The servants at the Tordesillas palace who were consulted confessed little—always with their eyes on the ground and their voices choked with anxiety—but enough to understand that the marquis was a dark man capable of the atrocities that Catalina described: brutal insults and punishments that left marks on the skin.

卡洛斯在王座上坐好，迎接这位贵族，并暗自发誓要像被某种胶水粘在木头上一样纹丝不动，因为他担心这位来自德尼亚的人站在他面前，可能会让他做出疯狂的愤怒之举。

Carlos settled himself on the throne to receive the nobleman, and promised himself to remain seated as if some kind of glue bonded him to the wood, for he feared that having the man from Denia before him might lead him to commit a mad act of anger.

“大人，您怎能相信这种卑劣之事？”侯爵带着和蔼的微笑说道，那笑容对于一个天真无邪的人来说未免太过和蔼。

"My lord, how can you give credence to such infamies?" The marquis said it with a kind smile, too kind for an innocent.

“我应该相信你而不是我姐姐吗？她有什么理由捏造出如此残暴的事件？”

"Should I believe you rather than my sister? What reason would she have to fabricate such brutality?"

“为了掩盖其他罪行，举报一件罪行是惯例，陛下，”来自德尼亚的男子得意洋洋地回答道。

"It is customary to report one crime to cover up others, Your Majesty," replied the man from Denia with a smug air.

一个小女孩能犯什么错呢？

—And what wrong could a little girl have committed?

侯爵随后向国王详细地、添油加醋地讲述了平民百姓在托尔德西拉斯宫度过的日子，以及凯瑟琳如何倒向叛军，表现出极大的不忠。据这位贵族所说，革命被挫败后，这位年轻女子责备她的母亲懦弱，选择维护法律：她渴望王后的忠诚动摇。他继续说道：

The marquis then recounted to his king, in great detail and with countless exaggerations, the days the commoners had spent in the palace of Tordesillas, and how Catherine had sided with the rebels, displaying the greatest disloyalty. Once the revolution had been thwarted, the young woman, according to the nobleman, had reproached her mother for her cowardice in choosing to uphold the law: she longed for the queen's loyalty to waver. And he continued:

“如果再次爆发起义，你妹妹支持叛军，我一点也不会感到惊讶。她知道我知道她的恶行，所以才诬陷我，想让我蒙羞，让她的秘密在我面前永远消失。”

"I wouldn't be surprised at all if, should another uprising break out, your sister were to support the rebels. Knowing that I'm aware of her misdeeds, she's accusing me so that I'll be disgraced and her secret will be silenced around me."

那时，查理不知该作何感想。侯爵浑身散发着恶意，但并非只有他一人向他告发了公主那几天的可疑行径。皇帝遣走了那位贵族——看到他带着阴森的气息离开，他如释重负——之后，便下令当天下午就准备一辆马车，送他前往托尔德西利亚斯。

By then, Charles didn't know what to think. The Marquis exuded malice, but he wasn't the only one who had informed him of the Infanta's questionable behavior during those days. The Emperor, after dismissing the nobleman—and what a relief he felt seeing him depart with his sinister aura—ordered that a carriage be prepared for him that very afternoon, with Tordesillas as his destination.

 

 

 

 

当胡安娜王后看到儿子走进寝宫时，她仿佛看到了前世的幻影；仿佛距离他们上次相遇已经过去了一百年。

When she saw her son enter the bedchamber, Queen Juana regarded him as if he were an apparition from a past life; as if a hundred years had passed since their previous encounter.

你变了。

—You've changed.

卡洛斯意识到母亲说得对：他不再是上次母亲来访时那个懵懂无知、容易受影响的年轻人了。这些年究竟发生了什么？一个帝国的建立，一场被镇压的叛乱，一场与另一个王国的战争，爱情纠葛，女儿的出生，异端邪说，失望，喜悦，以及死亡。短短五年，他便从迷茫无助走向成熟。二十二岁的他依然饱受无数疑虑和恐惧的折磨，但肩负的责任让他变得更加宽厚，似乎能够承受一切。如今，在这间昏暗的房间里，面对着那位神秘莫测的母亲，他几乎感觉不到一丝脆弱。

Carlos realized his mother was right: he was no longer the same impressionable and confused young man from her last visit. What had happened during all that time? An empire, a suppressed insurrection, a war with another kingdom, love affairs, daughters, heretics, disappointments, joys, and deaths. In barely five years, he had traveled the path from constant uncertainty to maturity. At twenty-two, he was still assailed by countless doubts and fears, but his shoulders had broadened from bearing responsibilities, and he seemed capable of withstanding whatever might come. Now, in that shadowy room and before that enigmatic woman who was his mother, he barely felt vulnerable.

“你是来减轻内心的愧疚感的吗？”凯瑟琳走进房间时问道。

"Have you come to ease your conscience?" asked Catherine as she entered the place.

卡洛斯转过身。他愣了一会儿才认出自己的妹妹；那个曾经胆怯的女孩如今已长成一位表情坚毅的年轻女子。她眼底深处满是苦涩，一副绝望的模样。虽然她的皮肤光滑，身材也像个少女，但她的精神却已老态龙钟，以至于卡洛斯感觉自己仿佛在看着同一个人的两个几乎一模一样的版本：十五岁的卡塔琳娜，已经活出了胡安娜的模样。

Carlos turned around. It took him a moment to recognize his sister; that timid creature of years past had become a young woman with a hardened expression. Bitterness lingered in the depths of her eyes, and she wore the demeanor of a desperate woman. Although her skin was smooth and her figure that of a young girl, her spirit had aged so much that he felt as if he were looking at two almost identical versions of the same person: Catalina, at fifteen, already reflected Juana.

“我仔细读了你的信。”他说。

—I read your letter carefully —he said.

——你难道要允许那个残暴的男人继续统治这个地方吗？

—And are you going to allow that ferocious man to continue ruling this place?

查理看向王后，想确认这些指控是否属实，但他的母亲已经不再说话，眼神中也毫无表情。皇帝无奈地转过身，看向凯瑟琳。

Charles looked to the queen for confirmation that these accusations were true, but his mother had withdrawn from the conversation, and her eyes revealed nothing. Resigned, the emperor turned back to Catherine.

——你怎么能站在那些起来反对我的人一边呢？

—How could you side with those who rose up against me?

—为了离开这里，我甚至愿意和魔鬼联手。

—I would have teamed up with the devil himself to get out of here.

“那当机会来临时，你会这么做吗？”卡洛斯担忧地问道。

"And will you do that when the opportunity arises?" Carlos asked, alarmed.

公主看向哥哥的眼神，是其他人从未有过的：轻蔑。

The princess looked at her brother in a way no one else ever did: with contempt.

“我有什么理由站在奴役我的人一边呢？”她问道。“因为奴隶无法掌控自己的自由，他们的命运完全取决于一个对他们毫无感情的主人的意志。”

—What reasons would I have to side with the one who enslaves me? —she asked—. Because a slave is someone who does not have control over their freedom and whose fate depends on the will of an owner who feels nothing for them.

一阵漫长的沉默笼罩着一切。卡洛斯的目光和胡安娜一样茫然，因为面对一个只说真话的人，他什么也说不出来。

A long silence fell. Carlos's gaze was as lost as Juana's, because nothing could be said in response to someone who was only telling the truth.

 

 

 

 

片刻之后，皇家马车在细雨中驶离了托尔德西利亚斯。车内，皇帝想起了希耶夫尔，不仅因为这位顾问曾陪同他走过这条路，更因为他得出了一个令他毛骨悚然的结论：多年来，他一直对希耶夫尔的恶言恶语感到震惊，如今却发现自己已经将这些恶言恶语内化，甚至成为了自身的一部分。“我所做的，不过是许多孩子对待父母的方式，”他想，“我愤慨的，恰恰是我最终也染上的这些恶习。”说实话，将母亲囚禁起来已经够卑鄙了，而以同样的方式对待自己的妹妹，则是一个冷酷无情之人的表现。乔安娜希望女儿陪伴在身边，但这并不足以成为将公主囚禁的理由。十五岁的凯瑟琳对宫殿之外的世界一无所知，而以谨慎为名，她甚至连在宫殿里走一走都不被允许。她的生活如同一个衣着光鲜、吃得饱的囚犯，但终究还是个囚犯。同样，查理也为杰曼娜的悲惨命运自责不已。他为了拆散他们，将她许配给了勃兰登堡公爵，但一旦做出决定，他就从未考虑过这会对她造成怎样的后果。他自诩为有荣誉感的人，却将他本应深爱的人视作棋子，只顾自己一己私利，哪怕这意味着使用卑鄙的手段。

Moments later, the royal carriage left Tordesillas behind in a light drizzle. Inside, the emperor remembered Chièvres, not only because the advisor had accompanied him on the previous occasion when he had made this journey, but because he reached a conclusion that chilled him to the bone: after having spent years being scandalized by the man's vile outbursts, it turned out that he had assimilated them to the point of making them part of himself. "I am doing no more than what so many children do with their parents," he thought, "I am indignant precisely at the faults I have ended up making my own." To tell the truth, keeping his mother cloistered was already vile, but to act in the same way with his sister was the mark of a soulless man. That Joanna wanted her daughter by her side was not sufficient reason to condemn the infanta to such imprisonment. At fifteen, Catherine had known no world beyond the cold walls of that palace, and, under the guise of prudence, she wasn't even allowed to walk its grounds. Her life resembled that of a well-dressed and well-fed prisoner, but a prisoner nonetheless. Similarly, Charles blamed himself for Germana's tragic fate. He had betrothed her to the Duke of Brandenburg to separate them, but, once the decision was made, he had never inquired about the consequences this circumstance had for her. He boasted of being a man of honor, and yet he treated those he should have loved as if they were pieces in a chess game where winning mattered only to him, even if it meant resorting to dirty tricks.

 

 

 

 

然而，回到宫廷后，皇帝得知杰尔玛娜正在等候他。似乎是愧疚驱使她前来，给了他一个请求她原谅的机会。查理需要独自待一会儿，才能与这位昔日情人见面。尽管他对她的迷恋早已消逝，但再次见到她仍然令他心神不宁，尤其是在他意识到自己曾将她带入怎样的境地之后。

However, upon returning to court, the emperor was informed that Germana awaited him. His guilty conscience seemed to have summoned her, thus offering him the opportunity to ask forgiveness for his mistakes. Charles needed to be alone for a few moments before meeting with his former lover. Although his infatuation was long gone, the prospect of seeing her again was unsettling, especially knowing the life he had led her into.

他走进房间时，日耳曼娜背对着他。皇帝停下脚步，凝视着眼前的身影。多年前，他曾用唇一点一点地描摹过她的轮廓，而如今，她却静静地站在那里，双肩耷拉着，等待着他的到来。即便还没看清她的脸，他也能感受到她的悲伤。

When he entered the room, Germana had her back to him. The emperor paused to contemplate this figure whom, years before, he had traced with his lips, inch by inch, and who now stood motionless, awaiting his encounter, her shoulders slumped. Even without having yet glimpsed her face, he sensed her sadness.

——夫人。

—My lady.

她转过身。两人沉默地对视着。杰尔玛娜惊讶地发现眼前这位男子面容成熟；而他则震惊于短短几年间，她竟变成了一个相貌平平、甚至有些臃肿的女人；她昔日的性感魅力也被一层无奈的外表所掩盖。卡洛斯怒火中烧，快步走近她。

She turned around. They looked at each other in silence. Germana was surprised to see a man with a mature face before her; he was astonished that in so few years she had become a rather unremarkable-looking woman, even heavier; her former sensuality had been obscured by a veneer of resignation. With quick steps, Carlos closed the distance between them, consumed by anger.

—你为什么忍受了这么多痛苦却不来找我？！

—Why have you suffered so much without coming to me?!

“陛下，您所面临的纷争数不胜数，”她回答说，“我为什么要用我的烦恼来打扰您呢？”

—Your Majesty, the conflicts that beset you are countless —she replied—, why should I bother you with my worries?

因为我关心你！还需要我提醒你吗？

—Because I care about you! Do I have to remind you?

“恐怕是这样。”杰尔马纳的语气中没有责备，只有一种不再习惯被温柔对待的淡淡忧伤。

—I'm afraid so. —There was no reproach in Germana's tone, only the melancholy of someone who was no longer used to receiving tenderness.

—侯爵是否挥霍了我命令发给你和我们女儿的津贴？

—Has the marquis squandered the allowance I ordered to be given to you and our daughter?

她的沉默证明了她的信仰。

Her silence was a testament to her faith.

—他竟敢打你？

—And has he dared to strike you?

依然没有任何回应。杰尔玛娜的眼眶里噙满了泪水，她紧紧抿着嘴，努力抑制住呜咽。卡洛斯想不起来自己曾有过如此义愤填膺的时刻。如果说得知事情的真相已经让他怒不可遏，那么看到曾经如此活力四射、坚强独立的女子如今沦为受害者，则让他对侯爵充满了仇恨。

Again there was no response. Germana's eyes welled up with tears, and her mouth pressed tightly together to hold back her sobs. Carlos couldn't recall ever feeling such righteous anger. If learning what had happened had enraged him, seeing the woman who had once been so vibrant and strong now a victim filled him with hatred for the marquis.

“我很抱歉我判了你死刑，”他说。

"I am sorry I have condemned you," he said.

你以为你在帮我。你的愧疚毫无根据。

—You thought you were doing me a favor. Your guilt is unfounded.

皇帝知道这段婚姻无法解除，但他渴望找到一种方法，让杰玛娜的未来比现在更好。

The emperor was aware that this marriage could not be dissolved, but he longed to find a way to make Germana's future better than her present.

经过数日的商议，查理下令召见他的前情人及其丈夫。勃兰登堡藩侯并不知道皇帝已知晓他的种种劣行，故而表现得自信沉着，直到看到对方毫不妥协的眉头紧锁，他的好心情才荡然无存。

After several days of deliberation, Charles ordered his former lover and her husband to appear before him. The Margrave of Brandenburg, unaware that the emperor knew of his abuses, appeared confident and calm, and only when he saw the other's implacable frown did his good spirits vanish.

—侯爵大人，我已决定任命您的夫人为瓦伦西亚总督夫人。

—My lord marquis, I have decided to appoint your wife vicereine of Valencia.

杰尔玛娜惊讶地接受了这份荣誉。在她丈夫身上，她感受到了被视为妾室的屈辱。

Germana accepted the honor with surprise. In her husband, she felt the humiliation of being seen as a consort.

你将成为那个王国的总司令，但实际治理权归她所有。记住，你的一切都归功于她。我相信从此刻起，你会努力不辜负她的期望，因为我会一直关注着你。

—You will be captain general of that kingdom, but the governance will be her prerogative. As in this matter, know that everything you are you owe to her. I trust that from this moment on you will strive to deserve her, for I will be watching to see that you do so.

查理的目光如同闪电般锁定在侯爵身上，锐利而有力。这位贵族知道自己被选中了，顺从而又不安地低下了头。然而，他并没有看到妻子与那位女王交换的眼神，她的眼中充满了感激和感动；而他的眼中则充满了释然和怀念。

Charles's eyes locked onto the Marquis's like lightning, blinding and powerful. The nobleman knew he had been singled out and lowered his head in obedience and distress. He did not, however, witness the glance exchanged between his wife and the one who occupied the throne, her eyes brimming with gratitude and emotion; his, with relief and nostalgia.

与日耳曼娜的重逢令皇帝心跳加速。他意识到自己无比怀念他们曾经拥有的一切：默契、激情，以及两人灵魂交融，共筑起属于他们自己的世界。爱情曾为他筑起一座慰藉之岛，让他得以在政务纷扰、心力交瘁之时，找到一处避风港。而自从与她分离后，他再也没有找到过那份纯粹情感的庇护；一切都变得空虚——政治、冲突、战争——或是平庸的情感，如同他与约翰娜相处时那炽热的激情，仅此而已。或许，这种始终萦绕在他心头的空虚感，随着希耶夫尔的失踪和哈德良的失望而愈发强烈，唯有爱情才能治愈。

The reunion with Germana left the emperor's heart pounding. He realized he missed what they had shared: the complicity, the passion, the fact that their two souls formed a world of their own. Love, when he had it, created for him an island of comfort where he could take refuge when the affairs of state tormented him, which happened often. Since his separation from her, he had not found the shelter of those pure emotions; everything had been barren—politics, conflict, war—or mediocre feelings, like the fiery passion and nothing more he had experienced with Johanna. Perhaps this feeling of emptiness that always accompanied him, and which had intensified with the disappearance of Chièvres and the disappointment of Hadrian, could only be cured by love.

 

 

 

 

远在梵蒂冈，那位来自乌得勒支的男子，如今的阿德里安六世，正饱受教宗之苦。正如他接受这份荣耀时所预感的那样，这不过是一杯毒酒。罗马教廷的高级神职人员对他毕恭毕敬；但当这位前卡斯蒂利亚摄政王以坚定的语气宣布他希望教会提升尊严、成为信徒的榜样时，反对的低语便如烈火前的缕缕青烟般响起。人人都明白这看似无害的雄心壮志意味着什么：从轻松享乐的习俗转向一种严厉的教规，这种教规无疑是基督教的，但却令他们感到难以接受。教廷逐渐孤立了这位新教宗，而他却开始怀念卡斯蒂利亚摄政时期的紧张氛围；对他而言，任何地方都比那座金碧辉煌、人人互不信任的牢笼要好。

Far away, in the Vatican, the man from Utrecht, now Adrian VI, was suffering through his papacy. As he had sensed upon receiving the honor, it was a poisoned chalice. The high-ranking Roman clergy received him with impeccable respect; but when the former regent of Castile announced, in a firm voice, his intentions for the Church to gain in dignity and serve as an example for the faithful, the first murmurs of disapproval were heard, like the wisps of smoke that precede a great conflagration. Everyone knew what this seemingly innocuous ambition meant: a shift from relaxed and hedonistic customs to a severity that was undoubtedly Christian but utterly unappealing to them. Little by little, the Curia isolated the new Pontiff, who came to miss the tensions of the Castilian regency; any place seemed better than that gilded cage where no one trusted anyone.

在这片阴霾之中，他得知了土耳其占领罗德岛的消息。这个帝国野心勃勃，信仰迥异，对基督教世界构成了威胁。随着奥斯曼帝国的祸患蔓延，另一种祸患——瘟疫，欧洲周期性的灾难——也侵入了罗马。由于没有有效的治疗方法，逃离似乎成了避免传染的唯一途径。当地居民纷纷逃离，梵蒂冈几乎所有的神职人员也随之而去。直到疫情平息，永恒之城的街道都将空无一人，只有疾病的阴霾笼罩着这座城市。阿德里安，与其说是凡人，不如说是教皇，决定留在教会的中心。在那里，在身心俱疲的孤独中，他坐下来写了一封信：

In the midst of this bleak feeling, news reached him of the Turkish capture of Rhodes, that empire which threatened Christendom with its ambition and its different faith. And as the Ottoman stain spread, another, that of the plague, Europe's periodic scourge, made its way into Rome. With no remedies to combat it, flight seemed the only way to avoid contagion, and so the local people did, and with them almost all the clergy of the Vatican. Until the epidemic subsided, the streets of the Eternal City would remain deserted, inhabited only by the heavy air of disease. Adrian, more Pope than man, decided to remain at the seat of the Church, and from there, in solitude of both spirit and body, he sat down to write a letter:

 

 

陛下：

Your Majesty:

罗德岛已落入土耳其人之手。整个基督教世界都岌岌可危。罗马城荒芜一片，瘟疫肆虐。我当初接受彼得的王位是个错误。我不该离开卡斯蒂利亚。在这里，我举目无亲，更谈不上朋友。我的离去给您带来了诸多不便，敬请谅解。在这危难之际，我前来恳求您的帮助。作为回报，我将罗马城置于帝国的庇护之下。永远爱您的，

Rhodes has fallen to the Turks. All of Christendom is threatened. Rome lies deserted, ravaged by plague. I was wrong to accept the throne of Peter. I should never have left Castile. Here I have no allies, much less friends. Please forgive any hardship my departure may have caused you. I come to you in this terrible hour, begging for your help. In return, I place Rome at the service of the Empire. Yours always,

 

 

致阿德里亚诺

To Adriano

 

 

查理读到教皇的讲话后，不禁露出了胜利的笑容。教皇的支持或许能扭转战局，使他在对法战争中取得胜利。然而，法德里克·德·阿尔巴从战场上带来的令人不安的消息，却让他的乐观情绪有所降温。

When Charles read the Pope's words, he couldn't help but let out a triumphant grin. His support could tip the scales in his favor in the war against France. But his optimism was tempered when Fadrique de Alba delivered disturbing news from the battlefields.

英格兰无视了与你们的协议：他们奉命从西北方向发起的进攻并没有发生。

—England has ignored its agreement with you: the attack from the northwest that they were ordered to carry out has not been made.

“他们退出冲突了吗？”加蒂纳拉插话道，“当年他们武力攻占了布列塔尼和皮卡第，现在为什么要撕毁协议呢？”

"Have they withdrawn from the conflict?" Gattinara interjected. "They stormed Brittany and Picardy with force back then. Why would they break their agreement now?"

“人人都知道，对英国国王来说，每一笔开支都是一种负担，”阿尔巴公爵辩解道，“我怀疑除此之外，还能有什么其他原因。”

"Everyone knows that for the English king every expense is a hardship," argued the Duke of Alba. "I doubt any other reason could have prevailed."

“我才不在乎我叔叔的任性妄为！”皇帝咆哮道；在他眼里，亨利国王瞬间从忠诚的朋友变成了卑鄙的叛徒。“他签了字，承诺在任何冲突中都支持我，就像我承诺娶他的女儿一样。没有英格兰的帮助，我们就得加倍努力，而我们根本没有足够的资金！”

"I couldn't care less about my uncle's whims!" roared the emperor; in an instant, King Henry had gone, in his mind, from loyal friend to vile deserter. "With his signature, he pledged to support me in any conflict, just as I pledged mine to marry his daughter. Without England's help, we will have to double our efforts, and we don't have the funds for it!"

“希望我们能够退出是因为我们已经赢了，而不是因为破产迫使我们退出，”这位意大利人说道，语气中丝毫没有希望。

—Let's hope we can withdraw because we've won, not because bankruptcy forces us to— said the Italian, in a tone that failed to sound hopeful.

“波旁公爵难道还没有发表声明吗？”卡洛斯问道。

—And has the Duke of Bourbon not yet made a statement? —Carlos inquired.

法德里克否认了此事；自从在法军一侧的战场上那次短暂而紧张的遭遇之后，就再也没有这位贵族的消息了。皇帝再次被因资金短缺而无法参战所带来的耻辱所困扰。如果他缺乏维持其统治所需的财富，那么他的伟大又有何意义？他把希望寄托在罗马的干预上。如果教皇阿德里安站在他这边，或许这位英国人的缺席就不会那么令人感到如此强烈。

Fadrique denied it; since that brief, tense encounter on the French side of the battlefield, nothing more had been heard of the aristocrat. The emperor was once again gripped by the fear of the potential dishonor of being unable to fight due to a lack of funds. What good was his greatness if he lacked the riches to sustain it? His hopes rested on the intervention of Rome. With Pope Adrian on his side, perhaps the Englishman's absence would not be so keenly felt.

几天后，查理收到梵蒂冈寄来的另一封密封信件，他急忙打开，以为里面会宣布罗马将对意大利的法军发动进攻。然而，当他读完信的内容时，信却像一片枯叶般从他手中滑落到脚边。哈德良死了。

When, days later, he received another sealed letter from the Vatican, Charles rushed to open it, expecting to find in it the announcement of Roman offensives against the French troops in Italy. But when he read the contents of the letter, it fell from his hands at his feet like a dead leaf from a tree. Hadrian was dead.

对乌得勒支教皇来说，这真是莫大的讽刺：他功成名就，荣登罗马之巅，却英年早逝，据说死于瘟疫。然而，历任教皇的死都会引起关注，人们怀疑其中有阴谋和谋杀。这位挚友兼顾问的离世，对皇帝的打击远超预期。事实上，命运似乎注定要让他失去所有依靠：他的孤立无援如今已成定局。如果说希耶夫尔死后，他并没有感到需要与他人建立新的联系，那么哈德良死后，他意识到，既然自己的世界已经崩塌，就必须重建一个全新的世界。

What an irony for the Pope of Utrecht: to reach the glory of Rome only to die so soon, a victim of the plague, it was said, although no Pope's death went unnoticed, raising suspicions of conspiracy and murder. The passing of his friend and advisor affected the emperor more than he had anticipated. The truth was that fate seemed determined to leave him without any anchors: his isolation was now, without a doubt, a reality. But if after Chièvres' death he had felt no impulse to replace those ties with others, after Hadrian's he concluded that if his world had crumbled, a new one would have to be built.

多年来，每周皇家会议上都会有人提出这样一个想法：如果查理同意迎娶葡萄牙的伊莎贝拉，她带来的嫁妆就能弥补帝国国库的赤贫。这个建议迟早都会被所有顾问采纳，但早已被反复提及，令人厌倦。皇帝每次听到这个提议都嗤之以鼻。事实上，近几年他唯一的任务就是巩固自己在西班牙和帝国的权力，他那如同黏土般易于塑形的性格直到最近才变得坚定。他对婚姻的理想，如同他所有的理想一样，既傲慢又不切实际，他对完美的渴望——对失望、对平庸的恐惧——使他不敢迈出这一步。与英国国王女儿的婚约既是一个障碍，也是一个推迟婚期的借口。他一直都知道这份协议永远不会得到遵守，因为他的领地不可能像玛丽·都铎的年龄那样一直没有继承人。如今，亨利在对法战争中临阵脱逃，他更觉得自己没有义务履行这份约定。死亡摧毁了他的世界，他心中充满了对爱情的渴望，而务实的考量也起了很大的作用：为对法战争筹集资金迫在眉睫。因此，经过深思熟虑，这位皇帝找不到任何反对这桩婚事的理由，于是，带着一种只有一条路可走的平静，他决定是时候结婚了。

Every week, as had been the case for years, the idea was floated in royal councils that the ruin of the imperial coffers could be repaired with the dowry Isabella of Portugal would bring if Charles agreed to marry her. The suggestion, which all the councilors adopted sooner or later, was already worn out from overuse. The emperor had scorned this possibility every time it had been suggested to him. In truth, his sole occupation during the last few years had been consolidating his power, both in Spain and in the Empire, and his clay-like, ever-malleable personality had not hardened until very recently. His ideals regarding marriage were, like all of his, as arrogant as they were utopian, and his yearning for perfection—that fear of disappointment, of mediocrity—had prevented him from daring to take the step. The engagement to the daughter of the English king had been an obstacle, but also an excuse to postpone the marriage. He had always known that this agreement would never be honored, for his domains could not remain without heirs for as long as required by Mary Tudor's age. Now, with Henry's desertion in the war against France, he felt no obligation to uphold his part of the bargain. His world had been shattered by death and steeped in the longing for love, and pragmatism also played a significant role: the need for revenue to finance the war with France was more than urgent. So, after careful consideration, the emperor found no grounds against the marriage and, with the serenity of one who has only one option for the future, decided that the time had come to marry.

 

 

 

 

—推，女士，推！

—Push, my lady, push!

莱昂诺尔使出浑身解数，像过去几个小时那样用力。终于，在汗水和哭喊声中，床单被染成红色，卧室里弥漫着痛苦和紧张的气氛，卡洛斯的妹妹听到一声尖锐的呻吟。她气喘吁吁，几乎昏厥过去，但她没有失去意识，因为她渴望看到孩子的脸。

And Leonor pushed with all her might, as she had been doing for the past few hours. Finally, amidst sweat and cries, the bed stained red and the air in the bedroom heavy with suffering and nerves, Carlos's sister heard a sharp moan. She was breathless and nearly fainted, but she didn't lose consciousness because she longed to see her child's face.

——是个女孩。一个健康的女孩，而且和你一样漂亮。

—It's a girl. A healthy girl, and as beautiful as you.

莱昂诺尔把她放在腿上，闭上了眼睛。她感受到女儿幼小的心跳与自己的心跳交相辉映，不禁露出微笑。当初离开卡斯蒂利亚前往葡萄牙时，她是多么的懵懂无知——那时她怒不可遏，有时甚至会在马车里怒吼——而如今，在那个王国里，等待着她的却是她从未体验过的深刻情感：胡安的爱，她对胡安的爱，以及此刻她对这个孩子瞬间涌起的挚爱。

Leonor laid her on her lap and closed her eyes. She felt her daughter's tiny heart pounding against her own and smiled. How little she knew when she left Castile for Portugal—so angry that sometimes, inside her carriage, she would shout with rage—that in that kingdom emotions awaited her that were as profound as any she had ever experienced before: Juan's love, her love for him, and now the instant devotion she felt for this child.

“请把国王带来，”她恳求女管家。

"Bring the king here, I beg you," she asked the matron.

胡安出现在卧室时，空气中已弥漫着宁静的气息，空气中弥漫着新生、柔嫩肌肤和脆弱的气息。莱昂诺尔仍然抱着小女孩，仔细端详着她如同洋娃娃般的五官。

When Juan appeared in the bedroom, a sense of tranquility already filled the air, and the scent of new life, of soft skin, of fragility, was palpable. Leonor still held the little girl in her arms, studying each of her doll-like features.

“恭喜！”国王说道。

—Congratulations—said the monarch.

事实上，他是认真的，但他试图掩饰。莱昂诺尔一向观察敏锐，在那种紧张的时刻更是如此，她察觉到他有所隐瞒。

The truth was that he was serious, but he was trying to hide it. Leonor, usually very perceptive but even more so in that intense moment, noticed that he was hiding something.

-你这人怎么回事？

—What's wrong with you?

国王矢口否认，并找了各种各样的借口，直到他意识到，如果不坦白，她是不会让他离开卧室的。

The king denied it and offered all sorts of excuses, until he realized that she would not let him leave the bedroom without having confessed.

——你哥哥从卡斯蒂利亚写信来。

—Your brother has written from Castile.

弗拉明戈舞者额头上的汗珠凝固了。卡洛斯是她喜怒无常的神明，可以毫不留情地玩弄她的命运。

The sweat froze on the flamenco dancer's forehead. Carlos was her capricious deity, the one who could play with her destiny without any mercy.

—你命令我做什么？

—What are you ordering me to do?

—他已将你许配给波旁公爵。

—He has betrothed you to the Duke of Bourbon.

莱昂诺尔的愤怒几乎被困惑所取代。波旁公爵？这究竟是为什么？难道她连君主的资格都没有了吗？或者至少，她连一个渴望成为君主的人的资格都没有了吗？

Bewilderment nearly overcame anger in Leonor. The Duke of Bourbon? What reasons could there be for that? Wasn't she even worthy of a monarch anymore, or at least of someone who aspired to be one?

“他配不上我。我拒绝接受这场比赛，这样我就不会让我们的关系陷入危险。”

"He is not worthy of me. I will refuse to accept this match, and thus I will not jeopardize ours."

恐怕你别无选择。这是我与王国之间一项更大协议的一部分。

—I'm afraid you have no choice. It's part of a larger agreement with my kingdom.

“什么协议？”莱昂诺尔问道，她知道这个问题注定会令人失望。

"What agreement?" said Leonor, knowing that the question was bound to lead to disappointment.

—他最终决定娶我的妹妹，也希望我能娶卡塔琳娜公主。

—He has finally decided to marry my sister, and that I should do the same with the Infanta Catalina.

莱昂诺尔勉强笑了笑。卡塔琳娜？那个被囚禁在托尔德西利亚斯的野孩子竟然要嫁给她心爱的男人？卡洛斯明明有很多方法可以给公主她应得的生活，为什么偏偏选择了彻底毁掉她幸福的那条路？

Leonor let out a strained laugh. Catalina? The wild child locked away in Tordesillas was going to marry the man she loved? Of all the ways Carlos could give the Infanta the life she deserved, did he have to choose the one that completely ruined her happiness?

“我不能让伊莎贝尔的婚姻冒险，”他说。“一切都必须按照你哥哥的指示去做。他在信中说，他得知我支持叛军。只有服从他的决定，我才能使我的王国免于战乱。”

“I cannot risk Isabel’s marriage,” he said. “Everything must be done as your brother has stipulated. In his letter, he states that he was informed that I supported the rebel. Only by abiding by his decisions can I spare my kingdom from conflict.”

她心想，站在她面前的这个男人是谁？她不认识他的声音，不认识他的手势，更不明白他的意图。

Who was this man standing before her? she wondered. She didn't recognize his voice, his gestures, or much less his intentions.

“谈判！别像我一样接受他们的要求。看在上帝的份上，反抗吧，否则你会让我们永远分离！” 小女孩在她怀里哭了起来。

"Negotiate! Don't accept their demands like I did. Rebel, for God's sake, or you'll be condemning us to be separated forever!" The little girl began to cry in her lap.

你的提议很明智。葡萄牙绝不会承认你为女王。

—Your proposal is sensible. Portugal would never accept you as queen.

你的承诺都白费了吗？

—Were your promises in vain?

这时，小女孩的哭声变成了尖叫。生活并没有像她应该的那样以喜悦迎接她，而是以一对恋人痛苦的分离来迎接她，她似乎也意识到了这一点。她的呜咽声激怒了莱昂诺尔。胡安把孩子抱在怀里，但她仍然不停地哭闹。

By then, the little girl's crying had turned into a scream. Life wasn't welcoming her with joy, as it should, but with a painful separation between two lovers, and she seemed to realize it. The whimpering infuriated Leonor. Juan took the baby in his arms, but she continued to protest.

国王问道：“你想给她取什么名字？”

"What do you wish to name her?" asked the king.

玛丽亚。

-Maria.

胡安点点头，看着那个女孩，她牙龈发白，动作颤抖。

Juan nodded and looked at the girl, with her white gums and trembling gestures.

“你们随时都可以去看望她，”国王继续说道。

"You may visit her whenever you please," the monarch continued.

卡洛斯的妹妹突然忘记了分娩带来的痛苦，只感到心碎。

Carlos's sister suddenly forgot the pain the birth had caused her and only noticed her heart breaking.

你做不到。

—You won't be able to.

——她是曼努埃尔国王的女儿，属于我的王国。毫无疑问，你和波旁公爵会生儿育女，你的悲伤也会随之减轻。

—She is King Manuel's daughter. She belongs to my kingdom. Undoubtedly, you and the Duke of Bourbon will have children, and this sorrow will be eased.

胡安抱着孩子离开了卧室。他沿着走廊走着，虽然表面上镇定，但内心却因自己造成的痛苦以及被迫与此生挚爱之人分离而痛哭流涕。但他没有回头；责任驱使他毫不犹豫地离开莱昂诺尔躺着的卧室。卡洛斯的妹妹从床上起身，想要追上去，但她的身体却几乎毫无反应，她感到鲜血顺着大腿缓缓流淌。她动弹不得。她脸色苍白，鲜血汩汩流淌，灵魂仿佛被撕裂，她意识到自己刚刚经历了一场生不如死的折磨。

Juan left the bedroom with the baby in his arms. As he walked down the hall, though composed, he wept for the pain he was causing and for being forced to part from the only woman he had ever loved. But he did not turn back; duty compelled him to leave the bedroom where Leonor lay without hesitation. There, Carlos's sister rose from her bed, intending to pursue him, but her body barely responded, and she felt drops of blood trickling down her thighs. She could not move. Pale, bleeding profusely, and with her soul crushed, she realized she had just died a living death.

与此同时，在宫殿的另一间房间里，伊莎贝拉祈祷感谢上帝扭转了她的命运。她知道，促成这封信的并非天意，而是她自身的坚持。这封信她至少读过十四遍，信中查尔斯绅士而庄重地提出与她共度余生。公主祈祷完毕，突然间，睡意袭来。她感到无比疲惫，仿佛多年未眠。尽管才刚过中午，她便回到寝宫，躺在床上。她睡了几个小时，醒来时神清气爽，发现那封信还在手中，信的内容也并非梦境，她意识到自己刚刚开启了一段崭新的人生。如同宫殿另一间房间里的新生儿一样，她喜极而泣。

Meanwhile, in another room of the palace, Isabella prayed to thank God for the turn of her fortunes. She knew that her perseverance, not Providence, had made it possible for that letter to be written, the same one she had reread at least fourteen times, in which Charles, gallant and grave, offered to share what remained of their lives with her. The princess had not finished praying when, suddenly, sleep overtook her. She felt so tired that it seemed as if she had not slept for years. Although it was barely midday, she went to her chamber and lay down on the bed. She slept for hours, and when she awoke, refreshed, and saw that the letter was still there, in her hands, and that she had not dreamed what it said, she knew that she had just dawned on a new existence and, like the newborn in the other chamber of the palace, she burst into tears.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，笼罩在铅灰色云层中的伦巴第城市帕维亚正等待着一场大战的到来。攻占该城的帝国军队总司令安东尼奥·德·莱瓦，尽管兵力悬殊（仅有六千人对三万法军），却顽强抵抗了法军的进攻。敌人的围攻开始显现成效，莱瓦预感到败局已定。当一支意想不到的部队出现在地平线上时，这位上尉担心最后的打击即将到来。然而，令他惊讶的是，这支部队开始与围困帕维亚的敌军展开激战，敌军如同灵魂之墙般坚不可摧。帝国援军终于来了！然而，由于距离遥远，他未能察觉到，这支前来救援的军队竟然是由一位法国人率领的：波旁公爵。

Meanwhile, the Lombard city of Pavia, shrouded in leaden clouds, awaited the great battle. Antonio de Leyva, captain-general of the imperial armies that had captured the town, had long resisted French attacks despite his troops being ridiculously outnumbered: barely six thousand men against thirty thousand French soldiers. The enemy siege was beginning to take its toll, and Leyva sensed defeat and death were near. When an unexpected battalion appeared on the horizon, the captain feared the final blow. However, to his surprise, these forces began to fight fiercely against their rivals, who surrounded Pavia like a wall of souls. Imperial reinforcements, at last! What the distance prevented him from discerning was that the army that was saving him was led by a Frenchman: the Duke of Bourbon.

弗朗西斯科几乎没来得及咒骂他昔日的警官的背叛，那个他曾羞辱过的人，却没想到，在这样的日子里，他会展开可怕的报复。法国国王的怒火被生存的挣扎所掩盖：莱瓦的部下，在波旁军队的鼓舞下，离开了城镇，向法军发起进攻，法军突然发现自己被敌军包围。弗朗西斯科落马后，像个普通士兵一样奋力求生。他的剑挡住了数十次攻击，刺穿了敌人的尸体；那一刻，法国国王感觉自己刀枪不入：即使在如此绝境中，他也能避免失败。但突然，他感到脖子一阵刺痛：那是一把剑的尖端。弗朗西斯科意识到，持剑者身穿的制服并非他的。与这名士兵同行的还有其他人，他们都不是法国人。在他们身后，他的部下一个接一个地倒在了帝王的利剑之下。那个挥舞着威胁他的钢铁武器的人，用炯炯有神的双眼凝视着他。

Francisco barely had time to curse the betrayal of his former constable, the man he had humiliated without imagining that, on a day like this, he would exact a terrible revenge. The French monarch's fury was overshadowed by the struggle for survival: Leyva's men, emboldened by the presence of the Bourbon forces, left the town to attack the French, who suddenly found themselves surrounded by enemy troops. Francisco, unhorsed, found himself fighting like a common soldier to save his life. His sword blocked dozens of attacks and pierced bodies in defense; for a moment, the French king felt invulnerable: even in this desperate situation, he was avoiding defeat. But suddenly he felt a prick in his neck: it was the end of a blade. Francisco realized that the one wielding it wore a uniform that was not his own. There were others with this soldier, and none of them were French. Behind the group, his men fell, one after another, without exception, beneath the imperial swords. The one wielding the steel that threatened him gazed at him with radiant eyes.

—奉皇帝之名，殿下：你已被逮捕。

—In the name of the emperor, Your Highness: you are under arrest.

 

 

 

 

法国国王被俘的消息一传到，皇家议会顿时鸦雀无声。震惊之深，令在场的所有人都哑口无言。直到查理脸上绽放出灿烂的笑容，压抑已久的喜悦才终于爆发。

As soon as news of the capture of the King of France arrived, silence fell over the royal council. The astonishment was so profound that it left everyone present speechless. Only when a broad smile spread across Charles's face did the pent-up joy finally erupt.

“战争结束了，大人！”欣喜若狂的加蒂娜拉说道。

"The war is over, my lord!" said an ecstatic Gattinara.

“这是神的旨意，”皇帝补充道。他从未见过如此巨大的胜利；当他加冕时感受到的荣耀，与他现在所看到的相比，已然黯然失色：这是一场或许永远无法复制的胜利。“我下令将他押到我面前。卡斯蒂利亚将成为他长久的牢笼。”

"God has so willed it," added the emperor, who had never before witnessed a triumph of this magnitude; the feeling of glory he had felt when the imperial crown was placed upon his head paled before what he now perceived: a success such as might never be repeated. "I order that he be brought before me. Castile will be his prison for a long time."

 

 

 

 

当弗朗西斯被查理俘虏的消息如野火般传遍欧洲，震惊不已之时，一辆马车从葡萄牙出发。前往巴利亚多利德宫廷的旅程对埃莉诺来说如同梦境一般。她的身体仍残留着分娩的痕迹，精神也沉浸在一片阴郁的情绪之中。马车窗外的景色只是一片绿褐色交错的斑驳，时间仿佛静止：每一秒都与上一秒如出一辙，令人难以忍受的不安绵延不绝。一个幽灵萦绕在她心头：那是她女儿的心跳声。

While news of Francis's capture by Charles spread across Europe with wildfire, filling it with astonishment, a carriage departed from Portugal. The journey to the court in Valladolid held a certain dreamlike quality for Eleanor. Her body still felt the effects of childbirth, and her spirit was immersed in a sea of ​​dark emotions. The landscape beyond the carriage window was merely a patchwork of green and brown, and time seemed to stand still: each second was the same as the last, a continuous stream of unbearable unease. A phantom rested in her chest: the phantom of her daughter's heartbeat.

抵达目的地后，莱昂诺尔的悲伤与周围一片欢腾形成鲜明对比，整个王国都洋溢着喜悦。弗朗西斯科被捕，宫廷上下都为此欢欣鼓舞。似乎只有她内心深处藏着其他人身上明显缺失的那份忧郁。

Upon arriving at her destination, Leonor's sadness intensified by comparison, for the kingdom was overflowing with joy. Everyone at court was exultant because of Francisco's arrest. It seemed as if she harbored the melancholy that was conspicuously absent in the others.

-我的姐妹。

—My sister.

卡洛斯拥抱了她，她却没有回应。两人分开后，他做好了挨骂的准备；他知道莱昂诺尔作为他的傀儡，对他有多么痛苦。但他惊讶地发现，她的眼神中没有愤怒或反抗，而是阴沉的。

Carlos greeted her with a hug, which she did not return. When their bodies separated, he braced himself for a scolding; he knew how much Leonor suffered at being nothing more than a puppet at his beck and call. But he was surprised to find that her gaze was not one of fury or rebellion, but rather of darkness.

“我非常清楚我的命令不合你的心意。但你应该明白，你的自由和我一样都是有限的。亲爱的莱昂诺尔，我们并非普通人，而是上帝赋予我们的使命的仆人。”

"I know full well that my commands do not please you. But you should accept that your freedom is as limited as mine. We are not people, dear Leonor, but servants of the design that the Lord has imposed upon us."

她朝他吐了口唾沫，然后消失在宫殿里。查理擦了擦脸颊，感到十分难受，但他知道自己别无选择。尽管他痛苦地以暴君的方式统治着妹妹的生活，但他却看不到其他出路。诚然，是他将凯瑟琳从囚禁中解救出来，但归根结底，这份慷慨是为了他的利益，巩固了与葡萄牙的联盟。难道他没有为了他的统治而牺牲自己的幸福吗？他对即将迎娶的这个女人又了解多少呢？他渴望婚姻美满，但爱情能否开花结果，他需要极大的运气。尽管他渴望摆脱孤独，但他被迫结婚的原因却极其务实：为了获得她的嫁妆来充实国库，也为了将来能有一个继承人。他需要幸福就像需要空气一样，但没有任何保证能从这段婚姻中找到幸福。

She responded by spitting at him, then disappeared into the palace. Charles wiped his cheek and felt miserable, but he knew he was forced to be. As much as it pained him to rule his sister's life tyrannically, he saw no other option. It was true that he had freed Catherine from her confinement, but ultimately, that generosity had served his interests, strengthening the alliance with Portugal. Did he not sacrifice his own happiness for the sake of his government? What did he know of this woman he was about to marry? He hoped for a harmonious marriage, but he would need a great deal of luck for love to blossom. Although he longed to escape his loneliness, he had been compelled to marry for the most pragmatic reasons: to obtain her dowry to replenish his coffers and also to provide his possessions, one day, with an heir. He needed happiness like air, but nothing guaranteed that he would find it in this union.

那天晚上，当他辗转难眠时，他意识到，在短短的时间里，天意夺走了他生命中不可或缺的一部分，但他同时也知道，他很快就会遇到那些将塑造他未来命运的人：强大的敌人，他很快就会将敌人带到他面前，囚禁起来，被迫谈判；还有伊莎贝拉，他想起她时，心中既充满渴望又充满恐惧。彻夜难眠的查尔斯跪下，向上帝祈求，愿祂赐予他在战场上所拥有的福泽也能降临到他的妻子身上，并赐予他爱她的恩典。

That night, as he sought sleep, he realized that, in a short time, Providence had deprived him of some who had been a part of his very being, but he also knew that he would soon meet those who would shape his future: the great enemy, who would soon be brought before him, imprisoned, and forced to negotiate; and Isabella, whom he thought of with a mixture of desire and fear. Sleepless, Charles knelt and begged his God that the fortune He had bestowed upon him in battle would be repeated with his wife, and that He would grant him the grace to love her.
