聚集在马德里迎接法国国王的民众，看到宽阔街道的尽头停着一辆敞篷马车，车内站着一个巍峨的身影，一动不动。从远处看，他宛如一尊古代神像。人群熙熙攘攘，急切地想要庆祝战胜宿敌法国的胜利；但随着俘虏的靠近，他威严的身姿令人肃然起敬，许多人都克制住了羞辱他的冲动。然而，对于这位法国人来说，无论是游行队伍，还是被捕后的每一秒，都如同煎熬。这不仅是因为他引以为傲的尊严受到了伤害，更因为他的未来一片黯淡。“只剩下我的荣誉和生命，”他在被捕后不久写信给母亲；但他不知道自己还能拥有多久。事实上，他并不了解这位皇帝；他只知道，自从皇帝夺取皇位以来，他就决心与他对抗。他又怎能指望得到自己曾如此费尽心力折磨过的人的怜悯呢？从逻辑上讲，他会抓住机会复仇，要么通过屈辱的停战协定，要么直接处决。随着战车缓缓驶近，被人群团团围住，弗朗西斯科的恐惧也愈发强烈。他能感受到人们眼中的仇恨，即使是那些在他经过时保持镇定的人也不例外。他发现自己不仅身处敌对之地，而且内心也充满了苦涩，被两国之间数十年的纷争所毒害。他强忍着不让自己显露出来，不禁打了个寒颤。他确信，如果查理屈服于西班牙人的意志，那么他的日子就屈指可数了。

The people of Madrid who had gathered to welcome the King of France saw at the end of the wide street an open carriage in which a colossal figure stood motionless. From a distance, it resembled the statue of an ancient deity. They had a large crowd, eager to celebrate the victory over their perpetual enemy, France; but as the captive drew closer, his imposing presence commanding respect, many refrained from humiliating him. For the Frenchman, however, both the procession and every second since his arrest were proving to be an ordeal, not only because his pride, his defining characteristic, was wounded, but also because his future looked bleak. "Only my honor and my life remain," he had written to his mother shortly after his capture; but he didn't know how long he would have either. The truth was, he didn't know the emperor; he only knew that he had been determined to oppose him ever since he had seized the imperial crown. How could he expect compassion from the one he had so painstakingly tormented? Logically, he would seize the opportunity to exact his revenge, either through a humiliating armistice or through execution. As the chariot advanced until it was surrounded by the crowd, Francisco's fear intensified. He sensed hatred in the eyes of the people, even those who maintained their composure as he passed. He found himself not only in hostile territory but also embittered, poisoned by decades of disputes between the two kingdoms. With a shiver he didn't allow himself to show, he was certain that if Charles yielded to the will of the Spaniards, his days were numbered.

 

 

 

 

事实上，皇帝对高卢君主被捕的喜悦早已消退，一个问题逐渐浮现：如何处置他？逮捕行动结束了战争，但如何处置他却成了新的战场，如今已演变成一场外交博弈。

In reality, the emperor's jubilation at the capture of the Gallic monarch had been waning as a question took shape: what to do with him? The arrest had ended the war, but managing it represented a new battleground, now a diplomatic one.

“你必须彻底解决他，”加蒂纳拉说道。

"You must finish him off," Gattinara declared.

——结束一位国王的生命？——卡洛斯甚至难以用语言表达如此卑劣的行径。

—To end the life of a king? —Carlos even struggled to verbalize such a vile act.

——胜利属于你；弗朗西斯，奖赏属于你。天意让你处置他的人身和领地，如同它们属于你一般，因为事实上，它们本来就属于你。

—The victory is yours; and Francis, the prize. Providence has willed that you dispose of his person and his domains as if they belonged to you because, in fact, they do.

卡洛斯既不否认也不承认。说实话，他似乎沉浸在加蒂纳拉非常熟悉的那种冥想状态中，而这种状态会让他因思绪纷乱而感到恐惧。

Carlos neither denied nor agreed. To tell the truth, he seemed immersed in that meditative state that Gattinara knew well and that left him petrified due to the frenetic activity of his mind.

陛下，您被授予皇权是为了完成普世君主制的使命。请记住，为实现您的目标而征服法国并非出于自私的野心，而是履行您职责的必然途径。

—Your Majesty, the imperial scepter was bestowed upon you to carry out the mission of the Universal Monarchy. Consider that taking France for your cause is not synonymous with selfish ambition, but an unavoidable way of fulfilling your duty.

意大利人的意见得到了查理所有忠臣的认同；就连他的姑姑玛格丽特和弟弟费迪南也给他捎去了同样的话：“加快你的胜利，一个法国人都别放过！”玛格丽特一向行事谨慎，而非冲动，她同意要求俘虏完全臣服。然而，皇帝仍心存疑虑，而且当时并不着急，他宁愿等到确信无疑后再做决定。这时，法德里克·德·阿尔巴出现在了办公室门口。

The Italian's opinion was shared by all those whom Charles considered loyal; even his aunt Margaret and his brother Ferdinand had sent him a message expressing the same sentiment: "Hasten your triumph, leave nothing of the Frenchman!" She, generally more strategic than impulsive, agreed in demanding the captive's complete submission. The emperor, however, was not yet convinced and, as there was no urgency, preferred to wait until he was certain. Fadrique de Alba then appeared at the door of the office.

——波旁公爵恭候您的光临，陛下。

—The Duke of Bourbon awaits you, Your Majesty.

 

 

 

 

如果他能随心所欲地安排自己的命运，波旁亲王恐怕也难以承受命运的安排。即便在他最恶毒的幻想中，他也从未想到弗朗西斯会成为皇帝的人质。事实上，长久以来，他的生活都难以忍受，但现在他确信，上帝正在从天上纠正那些卑鄙之人所造成的破坏。自从得知昔日君主被俘后，他的呼吸和步伐都焕然一新；他再次为活着而欢欣鼓舞。此外，弗朗西斯的不幸遭遇本身就令他欣喜，因为这也意味着他自身的重生；正如查理承诺的那样，他的财产将会归还给他，而他与埃莉诺的婚姻至少会永远庇护他，即便不能像他所希望的那样，从长远来看，也会给他带来更大的好处。

Had he been able to design his own destiny as he pleased, the Bourbon prince would have fallen short of what fate had in store for him. Not even in his most spiteful fantasies had he imagined Francis as the emperor's hostage. The truth was that, for a long time, his existence had been unbearable, but now he was convinced that, from on high, God was setting right what vile men had disrupted. Since learning of the capture of his former lord, he breathed and walked differently; he once again celebrated being alive. Moreover, Francis's misfortune, which in itself filled him with joy, entailed his own rebirth; his possessions would be returned to him, as Charles had promised, and his marriage to Eleanor would at least protect him forever, if not bring him, in the long run, even greater benefits, as he hoped.

“我亲爱的朋友，”皇帝接见他时说道。

"My dear friend," said the emperor as he received him in audience.

这位法国人身着华丽的盛装，其华丽程度甚至超过了查理的装束，向他现在称之为主人的那个人做出了臣服的姿态。

The Frenchman, in his finest attire, so splendid that it dwarfed that of Charles, made a gesture of submission to the one he now called his lord.

—即使奖杯价值较低，对你来说也很有用，但请相信我：你获得的这个奖杯让我终生忠于你。

—It would have been useful to you even if the trophy had been of lesser value, but believe me: the one you have achieved makes me loyal to you for life.

他们相视一笑，尽管这位贵族察觉到皇帝对弗朗西斯的厌恶远不及自己；他的眼中没有那种心满意足的仇恨之光。

They smiled at each other, although the nobleman perceived that the emperor's dislike for Francis was much less than his own; he lacked the gleam of satisfied hatred in his eyes.

陛下，我非常渴望见到您的妹妹。

—I am eager to meet your sister, Your Majesty.

“你不用再等了，”门口传来一个女声。

"You won't have to wait any longer," replied a female voice from the doorway.

莱昂诺尔神情愉悦地走进觐见厅，这让卡洛斯感到惊讶。自从他从葡萄牙回来后，妹妹就一直刻意回避他。即便在宫廷走廊里不可避免地与他相遇，她也总是径直走过，甚至连看都不看他一眼，仿佛皇帝是个只有她才能看见的幽灵。然而，此刻，这份怨恨似乎烟消云散。波旁国王吻了吻这位年轻女子的手。

Leonor entered the audience chamber with a cheerful demeanor that surprised Carlos. Since his return from Portugal, his sister had deliberately avoided him, and when, inevitably, she crossed paths with him in the court corridors, she passed by without stopping or even glancing at him, as if the emperor were a ghost everyone could see but her. But that resentment seemed to have evaporated at the opportune moment. The Bourbon king kissed the young woman's hand.

—如果说我已经庆祝过我们的订婚，那么现在我亲眼见证了你的美貌，我再也找不到任何能在财富上与我匹敌的人了。

—If I already celebrated our engagement, now that I am a witness to your beauty, I cannot find anyone who can rival me in fortune.

莱昂诺尔满意地笑了。

Leonor smiled with satisfaction.

你战功赫赫，英勇无畏，现在我还知道你相貌英俊。那么，你的缺点是什么呢？

—You win battles, you enjoy gallantry, and now I also know that you are a handsome man. What is your flaw?

“我不配得到你的爱，”贵族笑着回答。

"Not being worthy of your love," the nobleman replied with a smile.

查尔斯的妹妹用充满期待的眼神望着公爵，但眼神突然凝固了。皇帝注意到了这一点，但他来不及压抑住即将涌上心头的预感。

Charles's sister gazed at the duke with a promising look that suddenly froze. The emperor noticed, but didn't have time to suppress what he sensed was coming.

“你说得对，因为你不过是个叛徒。”她宣称。

—You speak well, for you are nothing but a traitor —she declared.

随后，气氛变得令人难以忍受。

Immediately afterwards, the atmosphere became unbearable.

“今天我们不需要你再待在这里了。走吧，妹妹。”卡洛斯简短地命令道。

"We require no more of your presence today. Go, sister," Carlos ordered curtly.

“我生来就是女王。”莱昂诺尔冷冷地看了公爵一眼，然后离开了房间。

—I was born to be queen— Leonor said, looking coldly at the duke, before leaving the room.

一时间，无论是皇帝还是贵族，都不知道该如何打破年轻女子留下的沉默。

For a few moments, neither the emperor nor the nobleman knew how to break the silence that the young woman had left behind.

“别担心，”卡洛斯最终安慰他道，“我会像你一样。”

"Don't worry," Carlos finally reassured him. "Just like you did, I will."

公爵点了点头，但实际上他极力掩饰内心的愤慨。莱昂诺尔的态度让他认出了过去几年里他一直忍受的那种轻蔑，而如今他已将这种轻蔑视为过去。仅仅是想到弗朗西斯科的囚禁，就让他平静下来，并让他带着一种近乎自信的感觉结束了这次会面。

The duke nodded, but the truth was he was trying hard to hide how offended he felt. In Leonor's attitude, he recognized the same contempt he had lived with for the past few years, a contempt he now considered a thing of the past. Just thinking about Francisco's captivity calmed him and allowed him to end the meeting with a feeling akin to confidence.

 

 

 

 

在英国宫廷，如同在欧洲其他地区一样，弗朗西斯被捕的消息令人震惊。消息是通过受害者的母亲萨伏依的路易丝传达的，她一得知儿子的悲惨遭遇，便急忙将此事告知整个欧洲大陆，并以她带有偏见的视角歪曲了事实。她巧妙地将查理描绘成一个暴君，仿佛每个人都必须奋起反抗。

In the English court, as in the rest of Europe, the capture of Francis was met with astonishment. The news arrived through the self-serving voice of the victim's mother, Louise of Savoy, who, as soon as she learned of her son's tragic fate, hastened to inform the entire continent, slanting the event with her own biased perspective. Subtly, her account portrayed Charles as a tyrant against whom everyone had to defend themselves.

尽管亨利八世在不久前结束的冲突中站在帝国一方作战，但他仍将这消息视为威胁。保护他的侄子免受法国人的欺凌是一回事，接受这个年轻人如今又拥有另一个王国——而且并非普通的王国——则是另一回事。这个年轻人，尽管权势滔天，却一直显得有些软弱温顺，如今却越过了界限，这激起了这位英国人与生俱来的竞争和生存本能。因此，当西班牙使节告知他，皇帝与他女儿玛丽的婚约已被取消，转而迎娶葡萄牙公主时，亨利的不安转为了愤怒。

Despite having fought on the imperial side in the recently ended conflict, Henry VIII received the news as a threat. Defending his nephew from French abuses was one thing; accepting that the young man now held yet another kingdom—and not just any kingdom—was quite another. This young man, who despite his power had always seemed somewhat weak and docile, was now overstepping his bounds, and this stirred the Englishman's instinct for competition and survival. So when a Spanish embassy informed him that the betrothal between the emperor and his daughter Mary had been spurned in favor of the Portuguese princess, Henry's unease turned to anger.

他以为他是谁，你侄子吗？！

—Who does he think he is, your nephew?!

“大人，这条条款很难遵守，”凯瑟琳平静地回答道；令她惊讶的是，在场的沃尔西枢机主教点头表示同意她的判断。

"My lord, it was a clause that was difficult to comply with," Catherine replied calmly; and, to her surprise, Cardinal Wolsey, who was present, agreed with her judgment with a nod.

“要说有什么不忠的话，那就是背叛，”亨利说。“如果他已经失去了我的信任，那么现在他掌握着法国的命脉，我只能对他心存畏惧。”

"Disloyalty, if anything," said Henry. "If he has lost my trust, now that he holds the key to France, I can only fear him."

沃尔西发出了一声猫一样的低吼；他表示反对。

Wolsey let out a cat-like growl; he disagreed.

殿下，您评估形势过于仓促。俘虏弗朗西斯能给您带来与皇帝一样的荣耀，而且不会让您有任何损及自身名誉。

—Your Highness, you are assessing the situation hastily. The capture of Francis can bring you as much glory as it did the emperor, without you having tarnished your honor in any way.

凯瑟琳对红衣主教的态度感到惊讶，他一向对那位法国人很友好，直到她意识到他只是在按本性行事：冷酷地适应形势，带着掠夺性的本能。他把自己置于胜利者的一方，因此，他毫不犹豫地抛弃了与那位法国人的友谊，仿佛那污点玷污了他深红色的主教服，一切都显得那么自然，他渴望展现出耀眼的光彩。

Catherine was surprised by the cardinal's attitude, who had always been so favorable to the Frenchman, until she realized he was simply behaving according to his nature: coldly adapting to the situation, with predatory reflexes. He was positioning himself on the victorious side and, therefore, discarding his friendship with the Frenchman as if it were a stain on his crimson habit, with a naturalness and a desire to appear radiant.

“你拥有的头衔中，就包括法国国王，”沃尔西提醒他，“这原本不过是一个空洞的荣誉，就像一个过时的绰号，如今却以某种方式变成了现实。”

—Among the titles you hold is that of King of France— Wolsey reminded him. —What until now was nothing more than an empty honor, similar to a nickname from another time, has now found a way to become a reality.

“没错，”凯瑟琳下意识地插话道，“向皇帝索回你应得的一切。如果他能与你团结一致，即便他背信弃义，即便他俘虏了弗朗西斯，使自己在欧洲面前陷入尴尬境地，对他来说也只是微不足道的牺牲。”

"That's right," Catherine interjected reflexively. "Claim from the emperor what is rightfully yours. It will be a small sacrifice for him if he remains united with you, despite his disloyalties and the awkward position he has put him in before Europe by taking Francis captive."

从凯瑟琳坚定的语气中，谁也想不到她内心的煎熬。她不禁担忧，如果亨利疏远查理，她的命运将会如何。她的丈夫对她日益冷漠，不再与她同寝，仿佛已经放弃了诞下继承人的希望。王后无法预料这场危机将如何收场。他会立他的私生子为继承人，将玛丽逐出王位吗？或者，他甚至会不惜犯罪，除掉她和她那被诅咒的子宫？她难以相信，那双曾经充满爱意的清澈双眸，如今竟隐藏着杀意。但凯瑟琳了解她的丈夫，她知道他内心翻涌着各种冲动，这些冲动或许会在某一天以最可怕的方式爆发。唯有查理的支持才能让她免受亨利的伤害：如果伤害她会让他成为帝国的敌人，查理绝不敢这么做。否则，如果叔侄之间的联盟破裂，英国人会毫不犹豫地除掉它。

Judging by the firmness in Catherine's voice, no one would have guessed the turmoil within her. She wondered what her fate would be if Henry distanced himself from Charles. Her husband treated her with growing indifference and no longer visited her bed, as if he had given up hope of producing an heir. The queen couldn't foresee how such a crisis would end. Would he make his bastard son his successor, removing Mary from the throne? Or would he even be capable of getting rid of her and her cursed womb by committing a crime? She found it hard to believe that those clear eyes, which had once overflowed with love, now concealed murderous thoughts, but Catherine knew her husband and knew that a chaos of impulses swirled within him, impulses that might one day be unleashed in the worst possible way. Only Charles's support shielded her from Henry: he would never dare to harm her if doing so would make him an enemy of an empire. Otherwise, if the alliance between uncle and nephew were to break down, the Englishman would not hesitate to get rid of it.

沃尔西和王后的一致建议让亨利意识到摆在他面前的是一种平衡：一方面是查理一世对他的蔑视，查理一世是他低估的那个权势滔天的小个子；另一方面是收复英国在法国的欧洲大陆领土，以及随之而来的所有商业和声望利益。

The unanimous advice of Wolsey and the queen led Henry to imagine a balance before him: on one side was the disdain inflicted upon him by Charles, that all-powerful little man whom he had underestimated; on the other, the recovery of England's continental domains in France, with all the commercial and prestige benefits that would come with it.

“我会为你求情，”凯瑟琳说，“我的侄子无法拒绝你的请求。”

—I will intercede for you— said Catherine. —My nephew will not be able to deny you that.

“你说话像西班牙女人还是像英国女王？”国王严肃地问道。

"Do you speak like a Spanish woman or like an English queen?" the king inquired seriously.

“你冒犯了我。我只效忠于赐予我王位的王位，也只效忠于它。”她回答道。

"You offend me. I owe my allegiance to the throne that gives me my seat, and to it alone," she replied.

恩里克和他的妻子交换了一个意味深长的眼神，其中既包含了他们共同经历的一切，也包含了他们关系如今的黯淡境地。

Enrique and his wife exchanged an intense look that contained, at once, everything they had experienced together and the bleak place their relationship had reached.

—让他明白，如果他不肯取悦我，他将为后果付出沉重的代价。

—Make it clear to him that if he refuses to please me, he will pay dearly for the consequences.

 

 

 

 

弗朗西斯的住处远比牢房体面，他所享有的自由也更像贵族而非囚犯。他可以自由行走、狩猎，还能吃到自己喜欢的食物。尽管如此，这位法国人却始终郁郁寡欢，压抑着怒火。他从未忘记自己身为囚犯。自由的记忆折磨着他，虽然他像往常一样吃喝运动，却感觉自己如同行尸走肉，被困在炼狱之中，或许会一直煎熬到生命的尽头。更糟糕的是，令他蒙羞的是，查理拒绝与他会面，仿佛乐于将他囚禁，不愿就他的自由进行谈判。正因如此，这位高卢人的悲伤如此深重，以至于他无法思考；他终日无精打采，甚至连一丝灵感都无法闪现。他花了些时间才意识到，即便他的生活条件并非完全残酷，那也是皇帝的命令。而从皇帝的言行来看，他似乎并非一个卑鄙之人。正是这种认识让他想起了路德。尽管这位修士在帝国掀起了一场异端革命，查理二世却对他宽宏大量，信守承诺，无论这位宗教人士在沃尔姆斯议会上的立场如何，都放他离开。皇帝展现了一种无与伦比、近乎殉道者般的高贵品格。再加上这两点——不卑鄙和荣誉——弗朗西斯的视野终于开始出现一丝曙光。

Francis's quarters were far more dignified than a cell, and the liberties of his captivity more befitting a nobleman than a prisoner. He was allowed to walk and hunt, and was fed to his liking. Despite this, the Frenchman was all melancholy and suppressed rage. He never forgot that he was a prisoner. Memories of freedom tormented him, and although he ate, drank, and exercised as usual, he felt dead, trapped in a purgatory that might last until the end of his days. To make matters worse, to his disgrace, Charles refused to meet with him, as if content to keep him captive and unwilling to negotiate his freedom. Because of all this, the Gaul's sadness was so profound that it prevented him from thinking; he spent his days listless, without even a glimmer of wit. It took him some time to realize that if his living conditions weren't entirely cruel, it was due to some order from the emperor, who, judging by his behavior, didn't seem like a vile man. From this realization arose the memory of Luther. Although the friar had caused a heretical revolution in the Empire, Charles had behaved magnanimously toward him, having kept his word to let him go regardless of the religious figure's stance at the Diet of Worms. The emperor had demonstrated an inimitable, almost martyr-like, nobility. Adding these two traits—the lack of vileness and the honor—Francis's horizon finally began to receive faint rays of light.

 

 

 

 

当法国人满脑子都是查理，试图根据自己掌握的关于他的零星信息来猜测他的性格时，皇帝也在做着同样的事。他毫不怀疑查理性格专横跋扈，也知道他反复研读过愤世嫉俗的马基雅维利——只有这样才能解释为何在西班牙和德国都经历革命动荡之际，皇帝会对他发起攻击——西班牙的动荡源于共产主义者运动，德国的动荡源于路德教运动。但要由此推断查理是个奸诈狡猾、只能被彻底摧毁的人，在他看来未免有些牵强。唯一可以确定的是，查理已经落入自己的掌控之中，他会按照自己的意愿行事；问题是，皇帝会如何操控查理？来自英国和梵蒂冈的消息令他感到不安；据他的姑姑凯瑟琳说，英国方面希望分裂或制造冲突，而新任教皇克莱门特则对皇帝权力的不断扩张感到担忧。

While the Frenchman thought of nothing but Charles and tried to guess, from the few details he had about him, what his personality might be like, the emperor was doing the same with the Frenchman. He had no doubt that his character was domineering, nor that he had read and reread that cynic Machiavelli—only that could explain why he had launched an attack on him while Spain and Germany were suffering revolutionary upheavals, one with the Comuneros and the other with the Lutherans. But to infer from this that he was a treacherous man who could only be crushed seemed to him a stretch. The only certainty was that he was in his hands and that he would dance to whatever tune he wished to play; the question was, what should that tune be? Disturbing echoes reached him from England and the Vatican; the former, according to his aunt Catherine, wanted either division or conflict, and the new Pope, Clement, was alarmed by the emperor's accumulation of power.

——你建议我除掉他，却没预料到后果。在其他君主中，他将一个朋友都没有。

—When you recommend I finish him off, you don't foresee the consequences. Among the other monarchs, he wouldn't have a single friend left.

如果你满足恩里克的要求，他就会像父亲一样忠于你。

—Enrique would be loyal to you like a father if you would grant him what he asks for.

“我不会那么做，”卡洛斯宣称。

"I won't do it," Carlos declared.

加蒂纳拉向后靠去，仿佛想要逃避这个在他看来荒谬的决定。

Gattinara leaned back, as if trying to avoid that decision which seemed absurd to him.

——英国人会从这场掠夺中获益，这场掠夺会损害我的荣誉，却不会损害他们的荣誉。如果我同意瓜分法国，那么用不了多久，其他人就会炫耀他们从古代继承的法国领地，或是他们远祖在那里定居的头衔。争端将永无止境，冲突也将不可避免。

—The English would benefit from a plunder that would diminish my honor but not theirs. And if I were to agree to the partition of France, how long would it be before others brandished Gallic possessions from bygone eras, or titles of distant ancestors who were settled there? The disputes would be endless, and conflict inevitable.

这位意大利人因为反复重复同样的论点而舌头都磨破了，于是尝试了一个新论点。

The Italian, whose tongue was worn out from repeating the same arguments, tried a new one.

陛下，请超越政治考量。如果您将法国纳入版图，路德教必然会衰落：当异端分子发现自己身处一个完全属于您的世界，孤立无援时，他们终将放弃信仰。

—Your Majesty, look beyond politics. Lutheranism would inevitably subside if you added France to your possessions: the heretics would give up when they found themselves isolated in a world that is yours.

“我不想独占世界，我想要的是和平。难道你不知道如果我占领了那个王国会发生什么吗？臣民们会反抗，而且并非没有道理。我不想重温我不久前所遭受的苦难。”

"I don't want the world for myself: I want it at peace. Are you unaware of what would happen if I took possession of that kingdom? The subjects would rebel, and not without reason. I have no desire to relive what I suffered so recently."

加蒂纳拉说：“如果你的经验还有什么用的话，记住，卡斯蒂利亚叛乱只是靠严厉镇压才被平息的，而路德则是因为你们的宽宏大量才得以逃脱。”

—If your experience counts for anything —Gattinara said—, remember that the Castilian revolt was only crushed with rigor, and that Luther escaped thanks to your magnanimity.

德国传来消息，说那位修士仍然在世，并且正在撰写新的著作以推进他的运动。查理正苦思冥想该如何回复他的宰相，这时一位信使出现了。信中送来一封方济各的信。皇帝急忙接过信。信上的字迹有些颤抖，这让查理感到一丝怜悯：这位法国巨人似乎有些害怕。

Rumors had arrived from Germany that the friar was still alive and producing new writings to further his movement. Charles was searching for the words to reply to his chancellor when a messenger appeared. He carried a letter from Francis. The emperor eagerly grasped it. It was written in shaky handwriting, which aroused a certain pity in him: the French colossus seemed frightened.

“我别无慰藉，只能寄希望于您的仁慈，”皇帝大声念道，“您定能以此赢得胜利。像您这样的君主所下达的命令，必然是宽宏大量且高尚的。请怜悯法兰西国王，给予他应有的尊重，您定能让他成为您无条件的奴隶。”

—“I have no other consolation than to trust in your goodness,” the emperor read aloud, “which you will use in your victory. The orders of a prince like yourself can only be magnanimous and honorable. Have pity on the King of France, show him the respect he deserves, and you will make him your unconditional slave.”

加蒂纳拉发出了一声嘲讽的哼声。

Gattinara let out a mocking snort.

陛下，您的仁慈之心已广为人知。

—Your humanity has gained fame, Your Majesty.

但查理没有理会他的话，而是认真地重读了一遍法国人的话语，然后凝视远方。虽然他什么也没看见，但眼前却浮现出一片领地：他拥有领地的头衔，却无权统治，因为他的祖先已将它割让给了法国；如果他能收复这片领地，就象征着在法国面前重振家族的荣耀。

But Charles, ignoring his comment, seriously reread the Frenchman's words and then gazed into the distance. Though he saw nothing, a domain appeared before his eyes: the one he held the title of but did not rule, because his ancestors had lost it to France; the one which, if he were to recover it, would symbolize restoring his lineage's honor in the face of that kingdom.

勃艮第。

-Burgundy.

总理猜到了接下来会听到什么，也知道那不会是什么令人愉快的事情。

The chancellor guessed what he would hear next and knew it would not be pleasant.

—我将向弗朗西斯提议，让他通过谈判获得自由，以换取永久的友好联盟，并修复他征服的意大利领土……以及勃艮第。

—I will propose to Francis that he negotiate his freedom in exchange for a perpetual alliance of friendship, and that he repair the Italian territories he has conquered… and Burgundy.

皇帝宣布意图后，一片死寂，宫廷里的低语声甚至传到了办公室。意大利人的脸上露出了从未在皇帝面前流露过的不满表情。他仿佛变了一个人，一个普通人。

The silence that followed the emperor's declaration of intent was so profound that the murmur of the court reached the office. The Italian's face contorted into a grimace of displeasure he had never before displayed before his lord. He seemed like a different man, just an ordinary one.

——然后让你的俘虏重新掌控法国？

—And let your hostage take back command of France?

——但未来，它将作为盟友。

—But, in the future, as an ally.

你理所当然地认为他是个言而有信的人。陛下，恕我直言，您太天真了。

—You take it for granted that he is a man of his word. Your Majesty, allow me to be bold, but you are naive.

“你是在不尊重我吗？”卡洛斯问道，对这种居高临下的语气感到不满。

"Are you disrespecting me?" Carlos asked, offended by such condescension.

“我只是在警告你。君主也是人，而君主的品行也千差万别。有些君主像你一样正直，但有些则卑鄙无耻，甚至连你身上那种骑士精神都丝毫没有。任何一心只想夺回王位的人，都会毫不犹豫地伪装成值得信赖的人，即便他们根本不值得信任。”

"I'm simply warning you. Monarchs are human, and there's as much variety of the former as there is of the latter. Some are honorable, like yourself, but others are wretched, lacking even a trace of the chivalry that guides your actions. And anyone whose only goal is to reclaim a throne won't hesitate to feign trustworthiness, even if they're anything but."

“是你，但我听到的却是希耶夫尔，”来自根特的男人愤怒地回答道，“你怂恿我夺取一个王国，而不是遵循一个明智的计划。”

—It's you, but I hear Chièvres —replied the man from Ghent angrily—. You encourage me to take a kingdom rather than follow a sensible plan.

——这简直是个可怕的计划！它预示着你未来与法国的关系将与现在如出一辙：敌意、斗争、开支……！

—A fearful plan, rather! And a guarantee that your future with regard to France will be a carbon copy of what it has been until now: enmity, struggles, expenses…!

宰相气急败坏，皇帝恼怒地命令他安静下来。如果建立普世君主制会迫使他背离正义、仁慈和追求和平的原则，那么对他来说，这毫无意义。这位意大利人似乎只看到了攫取领土的机会，而没有看到安抚欧洲的契机——这正是欧洲迫切需要的。他又该如何从他人那里得到他想要的东西呢？“慷慨大方，”皇帝自言自语道，“别无他法。”

The chancellor was beside himself, and the emperor, irritated, ordered him to be quiet. The establishment of a Universal Monarchy held no meaning for him if it forced him to stray from justice, compassion, and the pursuit of peace. The Italian seemed to see in the situation only an opportunity for territorial gain and not the chance to pacify Europe, something so desperately needed. And how could he obtain from others what he desired? "With generosity," the emperor answered himself, "and in no other way."

这是我的决定，你必须遵守。

—It is my decision, and as such you will have to abide by it.

加蒂纳拉挣扎着低下头，表示顺从。他和卡洛斯沉默地对视着，意识到他们之间突然间永远地破裂了。

Gattinara struggled to lower his head in obedience. He and Carlos looked at each other in silence and realized that, suddenly and forever, something had broken between them.

 

 

 

 

勃艮第？绝不可能！

—Burgundy? Never!

弗朗西斯傲慢地挥手打发了帝国使者，转而看向他从黎明起就一直在狩猎的那片广袤田野。然而，眼前的地平线此刻却显得波涛汹涌、摇摇欲坠，他感到自己已无力继续猎捕害虫。查理的提议彻底击垮了他的意志。如有必要，他宁愿战死沙场，也不愿让王国的财富有所减少。毕竟，这是他仅存的自由：忠于法国，并且不再以任何方式玷污法国的名誉——他已经沦为皇帝的人质。如果他带着被剥夺的公国回到故土，他将不再是君主的尊严，而是叛徒的背信弃义。

Francis dismissed the imperial emissary with a haughty gesture and turned his attention to the vast field where he had been hunting since dawn. However, the horizon before him now seemed watery and unstable, and he felt incapable of continuing his search for vermin. Charles's proposal had broken his spirit. If necessary, he would die a prisoner rather than diminish the possessions of his kingdom. After all, this was the only freedom he had left: to be loyal to France and not to further dishonor her beyond what he had already done by becoming the emperor's hostage. If he returned home stripped of that duchy, he would not do so with the dignity of a monarch, but with the treachery of a traitor.

法国人轻蔑地拒绝了狩猎，牵着他唯一的伙伴——一匹马——踏上了返回住处的旅程。陪伴他的，除了那些日夜守护着他的众多西班牙卫兵之外，其他人都保持着礼貌的距离，但都紧握着武器，随时准备阻止他逃跑。途中，马儿停下来，好奇地看着一株结满果实的植物，国王摘下几个果实献给它。

Having scorned the hunt, the Frenchman began his journey back to his quarters, leading the horse that was his only companion, not counting the numerous Spanish guards who had watched over him morning and night and who now kept a respectful distance but held their weapons tight, ready to prevent any attempt at escape. The animal stopped to inquire at a plant laden with fruit, from which the king picked several to offer it.

-停止。

—Stop.

弗朗西斯科转过身，看到警告他的是一位衣着华丽、容貌姣好的年轻女子。多日未曾享受过女性的陪伴，此刻的她令他心醉神迷。他无比怀念她光滑的肌肤、温柔的声音、纤细的腰肢、纤细的双手和羞涩的笑声。他这才意识到，牢狱之灾让他与自己最珍视的一切隔绝了多久。

Francisco turned and saw that the one who had warned him was a young woman with dazzling clothes and harmonious features. After the many days he had been deprived of the delight of female presence, this woman was captivating. He missed her smooth skin and soft voice, her slender waist, her delicate hands, and her shy laughter. He realized the extent to which prison had separated him from what he enjoyed most.

“那种果实有毒。它或许不会要了你马的命，但肯定会让它痛苦不堪，我怀疑一位王室神灵会希望一个无辜的生命遭受这样的命运。”

"That fruit is poisonous. It might not kill your horse, but it would certainly cause him suffering, and I doubt a royal spirit would wish such a fate for an innocent creature."

“你是谁？”弗朗西斯科问道，同时把食物扔到了地上。

"Who are you?" Francisco inquired, as he dropped the food to the ground.

——哈布斯堡的埃莉诺。

—Eleanor of Habsburg.

法国人毫不掩饰自己的惊讶。

The Frenchman did not hide his surprise.

——你哥哥拒绝见我，却愿意见你。如果我说这其中没有夹杂着如此美妙的甜言蜜语的轻蔑，那我就是在撒谎。

—Your brother refuses to meet with me, but not you. I would be lying if I said there wasn't contempt sweetened with such an exquisite balm.

这句赞美让她露出了笑容。和其他人一样，她也曾在脑海中想象过卡洛斯的竞争对手，在她想象中，那个法国人令人厌恶，仿佛只有像她这样卑劣的人才能容纳邪恶。但现实却让她看到一个风度翩翩的男人，或许称不上英俊，但绝对魅力十足，他的笑容极具欺骗性，危险至极。

The compliment made her smile. Like everyone else, she had pictured Carlos's rival in her mind, and in that image, the Frenchman appeared unpleasant, as if vileness could only be contained in a vessel as low as her. But reality revealed to her a gallant man, perhaps not handsome but certainly magnetic, and with a smile so deceptive it was dangerous.

“只要你满足他的要求，他就会像对待兄弟一样接纳你，”她说。

"Please him in his requests and he will receive you as a brother," she said.

——那样我会被迫以兄弟般的眼光看待你，而我无法做出这样的承诺。

—That would force me to look upon you fraternally, and I cannot promise such a thing.

莱昂诺尔背过身去，不想让他看到自己脸红的样子，但弗朗西斯科无需看到她的脸颊就知道自己对她产生了怎样的影响。查尔斯的妹妹走后，这位法国人瞥了一眼他掉在她脚边的一小堆水果，趁着卫兵不注意，悄悄地把它们塞进了自己的口袋。

Leonor turned her back on him, hoping to spare him the satisfaction of seeing her blush, but Francisco didn't need to see her cheeks to know the effect he had had on her. Once Charles's sister had walked away, the Frenchman glanced at the small pile of fruit he had dropped at her feet and, without his guards noticing, slipped it into one of his pockets.

 

 

 

 

在葡萄牙宫廷，查理俘虏法国国王的消息几乎没有引起任何反响，因为有两个对王国来说意义重大的事件掩盖了这一消息：葡萄牙国王与一位西班牙公主的婚姻，以及伊莎贝拉公主即将成为神圣罗马帝国皇后。

At the court of Portugal, the news that Charles had taken the King of France captive had barely stirred a lukewarm echo, as it had been overshadowed by two events that were far more significant for the kingdom: the marriage of its monarch to a Spanish princess and the imminent conversion of Princess Isabella into Empress of the Holy Roman Empire.

自从得知自己将成为葡萄牙女王以来，凯瑟琳一直沉浸在一种复杂而矛盾的情绪之中。尽管她多年来一直向上帝祈祷，希望托尔德西利亚斯不会成为她的坟墓，但一想到要从隐居之地前往异国宫廷，她就感到一阵眩晕。事实上，她不习惯与陌生人打交道，她的心也早已习惯了隐居生活的死寂宁静。她能否在一夜之间摆脱自我封闭和独居的习惯，去履行女王的职责？她能否学会出于礼貌而微笑，能否像没有过往经历一样与丈夫交谈，能否摒弃她那饱经苦难之人特有的疑心重重的性格？

Ever since receiving the news that she was to become Queen of the Portuguese, Catherine had been immersed in a constant and ambiguous emotion. Despite having spent years praying to God that Tordesillas would not become her tomb, the idea of ​​going from seclusion to a foreign court filled her with vertigo. Truthfully, she was unaccustomed to dealing with strangers, and her heart had grown accustomed to the lifeless tranquility of seclusion. Would she be able, overnight, to shed her self-absorption and solitary habits to fulfill the demands placed upon a queen? Would she know how to smile out of obligation, converse with her husband as if she didn't carry an empty past, and leave behind her suspicious nature, typical of someone who had only suffered?

然而，她的疑虑很快就烟消云散了。她的未婚夫约翰国王深知这位年轻女子漫长而艰辛的人生，因此用温柔的言语和举止迎接她，小心翼翼地不让她感到害怕。他还送给她许多礼物，凯瑟琳欣然接受，感激之情深深打动了国王：她不像个公主，而像个出身卑微的年轻女子，对任何善意都视若珍宝。查理的妹妹欣喜地抚摸着新衣华丽的面料，婚礼后，约翰带她去看大海，她被那美丽无垠的地平线所震撼，不禁潸然泪下，这与她长期以来只能看到的石墙截然不同。她的恐惧消失了：她可以成为王后，她可以幸福。

Her doubts, however, were soon dispelled. Her betrothed, King John, aware of the young woman's long and difficult life, greeted her with gentle words and gestures, careful not to frighten her. He also showered her with gifts, which Catherine received with such gratitude that it moved the monarch deeply: instead of an infanta, she behaved like a young woman from a humble family for whom any kindness was a gift. Charles's sister touched the rich fabrics of her new dresses with delight, and when, after their wedding, John took her to see the sea, she wept at the sight of a beautiful and endless horizon, so different from the stone walls that had been her only view for so long. Her fears vanished: she could be queen, and she could be happy.

加冕之后，她不得不与即将成为她弟媳的女子告别。在她离开的那天，伊莎贝尔如同阳光下的钻石般闪耀。她一向美艳动人，而那天更是光彩夺目。公主早已为这一刻做好了充分的心理准备。尽管即将离开家乡、家人，以及那些塑造了她感官的景象和声音，她却丝毫没有感到悲伤。她明白自己或许再也无法踏足这片土地，这一天标志着一段人生的结束和另一段人生的开始——一段她如此渴望却又充满未知的人生。但她心中那份坚定的信念——她决心嫁给皇帝——给了她面对未来的勇气：她的未来将会幸福美满，充满着喜悦的憧憬，她满怀喜悦地告别了家乡。

Now crowned, she had to bid farewell to the woman who would soon be her sister-in-law. On the day of her departure, Isabel shone like a diamond in the sun. Her beauty, always breathtaking, shone brighter that day than ever before. The princess had carefully prepared her heart for this moment. She felt no sadness, even though she was leaving her home, her family, and the sights and sounds that had shaped her senses. She was aware that she might never set foot in her kingdom again, and that this day marked the end of one life and the beginning of another, one that, though so longed for, seemed uncertain. But her hope, upon which she had built her determination to marry the emperor, gave her courage for what lay ahead: her future would be happy, and filled with the promise of joy, she felt elated as she said goodbye to her home.

“我哥哥一见到你就会爱上你，”卡塔琳娜告诉他。

"My brother will be smitten with you as soon as he sees you," Catalina told him.

——就像你丈夫对你做的那样？

—As much as your husband did to you?

他们相视一笑。伊莎贝尔知道胡安仍在为莱昂诺尔哀悼，但她确信他的新婚妻子很快就会抹去这些记忆。突然，一个令人不安的画面闪过未来皇后的脑海，她犹豫不决，不知该纠结于此还是让它消散。凯瑟琳早已学会了从千百种角度解读母亲的情绪，她注意到了这一点。

They smiled at each other. Isabel knew that Juan still grieved for Leonor, but she was certain that his new wife would soon erase those memories. Suddenly, an unsettling image crossed the mind of the future empress, and she hesitated, unsure whether to dwell on it or let it fade away. Catherine, who had learned to read her mother's moods in a thousand different ways, noticed.

你担心什么？

—What worries you?

伊莎贝尔犹豫了一下才回答。

Isabel hesitated before answering.

——听说你哥哥已经当爸爸了，这是真的吗？我听说了这个传闻，但我从来不想知道这传闻有多少真实性。

—Is it true that your brother has already become a father? The rumor has reached me, but I never wanted to know how much truth there was to it.

女王对这个问题感到惊讶，来不及想出一个令人满意的答案，只好保持沉默，这足以让伊莎贝尔感到不安。

The queen, surprised by the question, did not have time to invent a pleasing answer, and preferred to remain silent, which was enough to unsettle Isabel.

“果然是个男孩，”卡塔琳娜最终回答道。

"It's a boy, after all," Catalina finally replied.

对我来说，这始终是一个梦想，而梦想是完美无瑕的。

—For me it has always been a dream, and dreams are without flaws.

葡萄牙女人的脸上浮现出一丝忧郁的微笑；幻想如今已成为过去：它们终将变成现实，因此也难免不完美。

A melancholic smile appeared on the Portuguese woman's face; fantasies now belonged to the past: the time had come for them to become real and, therefore, imperfect.

伊莎贝尔一行人按约定时间出发。离开故土的那一刻，这位年轻女子开始摆脱证实了关于她未来丈夫的传闻后留下的苦涩。他的过去与她无关，但她告诉自己，他的未来也只能属于她。

Isabel's entourage set off at the appointed hour. As she left her homeland behind, the young woman began to shake off the bitterness left by having confirmed the rumor about her future husband. His past did not belong to her, but his future, she told herself, would have no other owner.

 

 

 

 

当未婚妻前来与他会面时，查理一心只想解决与弗朗西斯之间的问题。每天，都有使者出现在这位法国人面前，重申皇帝的提议，而他的回答始终如一：“绝不。”时间对这位来自根特的君主极为不利：欧洲对这位法国君主持续被囚禁感到不安，并将此归咎于其对手的野心。在各个宫廷中，普遍流传着一种担忧：查理决心将这位法国人逼入绝境，直至将其彻底剥夺。难道他拥有的还不够吗？一个帝国，西印度群岛，西班牙，以及他在意大利和佛兰德斯的领土？他对权力的贪婪难道没有止境吗？

While his betrothed traveled to meet him, Charles had no other concern than to resolve his situation with Francis. Every day, an emissary appeared before the Frenchman to repeat the emperor's offer, and the answer was always the same: "Never." Time was working against the man from Ghent: Europe was growing uneasy about the French monarch's continued imprisonment and attributed it to his rival's ambition. In every court, there was a widespread fear that Charles was determined to drive the Frenchman to despair until he stripped him of everything. Didn't he already have enough with an empire, the Indies, Spain, and his territories in Italy and Flanders? Did his voracious appetite for power know no bounds?

 

 

 

 

陛下，昂古莱姆的玛格丽特已抵达宫廷。

—Your Majesty, Margaret of Angoulême has arrived at court.

皇帝惊讶地眨了眨眼。

The emperor blinked in amazement.

弗朗西斯科的妹妹在这里吗？她有何意图？

—Is Francisco's sister here? What are her intentions?

疑虑很快便得到了解答。玛格丽特长途跋涉后丝毫没有疲惫之感。她仪态端庄，举止优雅；她深知自己代表着法兰西王国，这让她倍感自豪，昂首挺胸。

The doubt was soon answered. Margaret did not appear tired after the long journey. Her bearing was full of dignity; she was aware that she represented the kingdom of France, and that made her stand tall with pride.

“我哥哥的处境不能再继续下去了，”卡洛斯邀请她坐在他对面后，她说道。

"My brother's situation cannot be prolonged any longer," she declared once Carlos had invited her to sit down in front of him.

“你不需要说服我，而是要说服弗朗西斯科。如果他同意我的条件，日落之前他就能获得自由。”

"It's not me you need to convince, but Francisco. His freedom would come before sunset if he agreed to my conditions."

“他永远不会，”玛格丽塔说，她的话听起来很有说服力。

"He never will," Margarita said, and she sounded credible.

“我的固执为何要比他少？你忘了他是我的人质。无限期地延长他的监禁对我没有任何损失。”

"Why should my stubbornness be any less than his? You forget that he is my hostage. I lose nothing by prolonging his confinement indefinitely."

——失去你们的宽宏大量，以及与你们并不拥有的王国之间的友谊，难道不是一种损失吗？罗马正在谴责你们的顽固不化。

—Is it not a loss, perhaps, to lose your magnanimity, and the friendship of kingdoms you do not possess? Rome cries out against your obstinacy.

查理知道这是真的。继阿德里安之后的教皇克莱门特七世在信件中越来越不加掩饰地表达了对皇帝的敌意，而皇帝也未能幸免于这种不满；这不仅是因为他必须服从罗马，还因为他意大利领地的稳定取决于与梵蒂冈的良好关系。如果他与梵蒂冈交恶，梵蒂冈就会煽动这些领土上的叛乱，甚至鼓励竞争对手征服它们。

Charles knew it was true. The Pope who had succeeded Adrian, Clement VII, was increasingly less careful in his letters to conceal his hostility toward the emperor, and the emperor was not immune to this disaffection; not only because of his obligatory obedience to Rome, but also because the stability of his Italian domains depended on good relations with the Vatican, for if he were to antagonize it, the Vatican would incite rebellion in those territories, if it did not encourage a rival to conquer them.

“你忘了我对你哥哥一直很仁慈，”查尔斯补充道。“许多人劝我征服他。但我并不觊觎他的领地，我只追求公正和长久的友谊。”

“You forget that I have been merciful to your brother,” added Charles. “Many have urged me to subdue him. But I do not covet his fiefdom, only justice and lasting friendship.”

“大人，如果您继续把勃艮第作为条件，您就找不到她了。她被绑架已经过去几个月了。难道您看不出来，她宁愿死在人质位置上，也不愿蒙羞获释吗？”

"You will not find her if you continue to make Burgundy a condition, my lord. Months have passed since her abduction. Do you not see that she would rather die a hostage than be released in dishonor?"

查理接见玛格丽特时，深信弗朗西斯的顽固不化源于他受伤的自尊心，任何其他法国人都会理解，对于一个可能失去一切的人来说，勃艮第是一个合理的代价。然而，无论是在初次会面还是之后的几次会面中，这位法国君主的妹妹都没有表现出任何妥协的意愿。起初，皇帝不明白她此行西班牙的目的，以为她只是在重复她哥哥的观点。但随着时间的推移，日益增长的挫败感让他意识到，玛格丽特试图让他陷入绝望，让他相信整个法国都在拒绝他的条件，无论他如何坚持，他们都不会同意勃艮第条款。厌倦了如此多毫无成效的觐见，皇帝宣布他必须前往边境与他的未婚妻会面，他们将在塞维利亚举行婚礼。或许几周后他回来时，会发现弗朗西斯不再那么傲慢了。

Charles had received Margaret convinced that Francis's intransigence stemmed from his wounded pride, and that any other French interlocutor would understand that Burgundy was a reasonable price to pay for someone who could have lost everything. However, neither in that first meeting nor in their subsequent encounters did the French monarch's sister show any willingness to compromise. At first, the emperor didn't understand the reason for her visit to Spain, if she was merely echoing her brother's opinion. But, as the days passed, the growing frustration made him realize that Margaret was trying to drive him to despair, to make him believe that all of France was rejecting his terms and that, no matter how much he insisted, they would never grant him the Burgundy clause. Tired of so many unproductive audiences, the emperor announced that he had to travel to the border to meet his betrothed, whom he would marry in the city of Seville. Perhaps upon his return, which would take weeks to occur, he would find a less haughty Francis.

但就在他们启程的前一天，当伊莎贝拉在另一边已经能远远望见西班牙时，宫廷里响起了警钟。不久之后，法德里克·德·阿尔巴激动地冲进了房间。

But the day before their departure, when Isabella, on the other side, could already glimpse Spain in the distance, alarm bells rang at court. Soon after, Fadrique de Alba burst into the room, agitated.

他快死了！

—He's dying!

这种担忧只能是指方济各。

Such concern could only refer to Francis.

 

 

 

 

查理匆匆赶到牢房，发现法国人的妹妹正躺在他身边失声痛哭。他意识到，即将发生的灾难远非最大的灾难：人质的死亡。全世界都会指责他是凶手，法国人也会要求复仇。更糟糕的是，他提出的任何要求都将无法实现，因为两位君主尚未签署任何协议。漫长的囚禁将让他一无所有，并背负弑君者的污名。

As he hurried to the cell, where he found the Frenchman's sister sobbing uncontrollably beside him, Charles realized that there could be no greater catastrophe than the one about to unfold: the death of his hostage. The whole world would point the finger at him as a murderer, and the French would demand vengeance. Moreover, he would be unable to claim any of his demands, since the two monarchs had not yet signed any agreement. The long captivity would leave him empty-handed and branded a regicide.

查理走进房间，发现一个高大的男人蜷缩在床上，像个生病的孩子一样瑟瑟发抖，丝毫没有敬畏之心。他长长的头发被热气浸透，原本就白皙的脸色也黯淡无光。弗朗西斯立刻将他那双呆滞的眼睛转向皇帝。两位宿敌的第一次对视持续了很久，随后陷入了沉默。最后，查理走到床边，将手放在法国人的手上，法国人握住他的手，仿佛握着一位挚友的手。

Upon entering the room, Charles found a tall man who exuded no awe, for he was twisted on the bed, shivering like a sick child. His long hair dripped with fever, and his already fair complexion resembled a dimmed light. Immediately, Francis turned his glassy eyes toward those of the emperor. The first glance between the great rivals was prolonged and followed by silence. Finally, Charles approached the bed and placed his hand upon that of the Frenchman, who grasped it as if it were the hand of a good friend.

“我是你的奴隶和囚犯。”俘虏的声音充满痛苦。

"I am your slave and prisoner." The captive's voice was agonized.

“不，你是我的兄弟，而且是自由的，”皇帝仁慈地说。

"No, you are my brother, and free," said the emperor mercifully.

无需多言。即便弗朗西斯并非濒临死亡，这次相遇也必定会令人动容，但弗朗西斯的临终更增添了这份情感的浓烈，两人都感到难以承受在此时此刻相遇，而此时此刻，他们更应该道别。

No more words were needed. The encounter would have been intense even if Francis hadn't been dying, but that fact charged it with heightened emotion, and both felt overwhelmed to meet at a time when it would have made more sense to say goodbye.

幸运的是，法国人慢慢恢复了健康。他曾一度担心自己的性命，为此他反复划十字，因为他知道自己是导致他生病的原因，如果害死了他，那将是不可饶恕的罪孽。但埃莉诺说得对：那些水果并没有致命的毒性。这一切的伤害都是值得的：他身体虚弱，胃部仍然隐隐作痛，仿佛在承受普罗米修斯的惩罚，但他成功地吓到了皇帝，拉近了两人之间的距离；正如他所愿。

Fortunately, the Frenchman slowly recovered. There was a moment when he feared for his life, and he crossed himself a hundred times because, being the cause of his illness, if he had caused his death, his sin would have been unforgivable. But Eleanor was right: those fruits were not lethal. The harm had been worth it: he was weak and his stomach still ached as if he were suffering Prometheus's punishment, but he had managed to frighten the emperor and break the distance between them; just as he had wanted.

他的病也带来了皇帝妹妹的到来。她开始探望这位病人，表面上是为了询问他的健康状况，并送他一些圣徒画像，以此弥补玛格丽特的离去——玛格丽特是她的哥哥恳求她离开的。尽管弗朗西斯病重，面容憔悴，埃莉诺仍然被他那猫一般的眼神和缓慢而沉稳地讲述的关于著名画家和诗人的轶事所深深吸引。弗朗西斯则对这位年轻女子的博学感到惊讶，也对她谈及自己人生时所展现出的悲喜剧气质感到意外。尽管疲惫不堪，她仍然努力对他微笑，每次见面都流露出她的魅力。

His illness had also brought with it the approach of the emperor's sister, who took to visiting the sick man, ostensibly to inquire about his health and give him images of saints, and to compensate for the departure of Margaret, whom her brother had begged to leave. Even with the sickly appearance his condition gave him, Eleanor was captivated by the convalescent's feline gaze and by his slow, deliberate recounting of anecdotes about important painters and poets. For his part, Francis was surprised by the young woman's erudition, and also by the tragicomic streak she displayed when speaking of her life. Despite her exhaustion, she made an effort to smile at him, her charm evident in each of their encounters.

 

 

 

 

勃艮第……它将是你的。

—Burgundy… It will be yours.

卡洛斯细细品味着弗朗西斯科的话语，却无法判断这些话是甜言蜜语还是毒药。

Carlos savored Francisco's words and couldn't decide whether they were sweet or poisonous.

是什么让你改变了主意？

—What made you change your mind?

——当死亡临近，并慷慨地允许我们继续活下去时，良心便会变得清明。我一直与上帝亲近，他赐予我的平安使我不再执着于一时兴起。

—Conscience becomes clear when death has hovered near us and, generously, allows us to continue living. I have been close to God, and the peace He has given me has diminished the value of my whims.

皇帝努力不被法国人的坦白所感动，但他脸上的表情如此真实地反映了他的感受，以至于很难不相信他说的是真的。

The emperor tried not to be moved by the Frenchman's confession, but his face so accurately reflected those feelings that it was hard not to believe them to be true.

“陛下，您战胜我是无可争议的，”弗朗西斯继续说道，“释放我吧。一旦回到法国，我将说服议会接受我们的协议。这是他们批准条约的必要前提，因为他们必须相信最终决定权在他们手中，即便并非如此，因为只有自认为自由的人才会服从。”

—Your victory over me has been indisputable, Your Majesty—Francis continued. —Free me, and once in France, I will convince Parliament to accept our agreement, a necessary precaution for them to approve the treaty, for they must believe that the final decision is theirs even if it is not, because only he who considers himself free submits.

卡洛斯犹豫了一下。

Carlos hesitated.

“陛下，我实话实说，”高卢人坚持道，“拒绝奖赏您的胜利几乎让我丢了性命。我的骄傲害了我。我接受您所有的条件，只加一条。”

“Your Majesty, I am being honest with you,” the Gaul insisted. “Refusing to reward your victory may have been what nearly cost me my life. My pride has poisoned me. I accept all your conditions, and I add only one.”

-告诉我。

—Tell me.

让我们以牢不可破的盟约巩固我们的友谊。请将你妹妹嫁给我。

—Let us seal our friendship with an unbreakable bond. Grant me your sister's hand in marriage.

 

 

 

 

“莱昂诺尔夫人已经和波旁公爵订婚了！”加蒂娜拉愤愤不平。

"Doña Leonor is firmly engaged to the Duke of Bourbon!" Gattinara was indignant.

皇帝在走廊里来回踱步，把鞋子都磨破了。

The emperor wore out his shoes pacing back and forth along the corridor.

“她会因此被逐出家门，”他回答说，“因为她认为这有损她的尊严。如果她接受这个提议，我将让她登上法国王位，大臣。有了这桩姻缘，我们两国之间的敌对关系就变得不自然了。”

"And she would be disowned for it," he replied, "for she considers it beneath her dignity. If she were to accept the proposal, I would place her on the throne of France, Chancellor. With that bond, the enmity between our two kingdoms would become unnatural."

“陛下，这并非我最关心的事。”意大利人仔细打量着陛下的目光。“您能相信弗朗西斯这突如其来的慷慨吗？他突然说他想方设法取悦您！”

“That’s not the matter that concerns me most, Your Majesty.” The Italian scrutinized his lord’s gaze. “Can you believe this sudden burst of generosity from Francis? He suddenly says he wants to please you in every way!”

总理再次称他天真。

Once again the chancellor called him naive.

你怀疑我会要求保证吗？但这件事必须解决，因为我害怕他会再次生病，甚至危及生命。

—Do you doubt that I will ask for guarantees? But something has to be resolved, because I am terrified that he will fall ill again, and fatally.

“他起初病得很重，而且来得也很突然，但最终却没什么大碍。这很不寻常，你不觉得吗？”意大利人说道。

"His illness was sudden and severe at first, but in the end it amounted to nothing. Quite unusual, don't you think?" the Italian remarked.

卡洛斯开始厌倦了如此多的猜疑，这破坏了他彻底解决问题的愿望，而且，也让他觉得自己很天真。

Carlos was beginning to get fed up with so much suspicion, which sabotaged his desire to settle the situation once and for all and, moreover, made him feel naive.

“难道你只会怀疑他吗？我的确怀疑他，但他毕竟是个落魄之人，一个受辱的国王。难道他现在的骄傲就不能比他刚来时少一些吗？”

"Is it that all you know how to do is suspect him? I'm suspicious, but he's a fallen man, a humiliated king. Isn't it possible that his pride is less now than when he arrived?"

加蒂纳拉只是面无表情地保持沉默。皇帝迈着轻快的步伐离开了房间，急于摆脱这个无能的顾问。

Gattinara's only response was to maintain his impassive expression and remain silent. The emperor left the room with a brisk step, eager to be rid of the company of this hopeless advisor.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，塞维利亚以欢呼和鲜花迎接葡萄牙的伊莎贝拉。这座富饶繁华的城市为这位未来的女皇向臣民亮相提供了完美的场所。然而，这位年轻女子对华丽的建筑、人们的微笑和奉承却漠不关心。“请原谅，旅途劳顿，”她在离开每个朝拜地点前都会这样说道。她只想倒在床上，咒骂查理五世。

Meanwhile, Seville welcomed Isabella of Portugal with cheers and flowers. The rich and bustling city provided the perfect setting for the future empress's presentation to her subjects. The young woman, however, paid little attention to the exuberant architecture, nor to the smiles and flattery bestowed upon her. "Forgive me, the journey has sapped my strength," she would say before leaving each tribute. She longed nothing more than to collapse onto her bed and curse Charles.

皇帝的使者告知她，他正忙于一件至关重要的事，无法像现在在塞维利亚那样在边境与她会面。他的迟到与他想见她毫无关系，而他想见她的愿望——使者在此故作激动——是无比强烈。一旦眼前的事情解决，查理就会立刻赶到她身边，弥补他因缺席而让她感到的每分每秒的不快。然而，皇帝的信丝毫没有平息伊莎贝拉的怒火。她的整个人生都围绕着这桩婚姻，尽管她知道他肩负着政治责任，但令她感到无比痛苦的是，这件事对他来说竟然如此次要，而且他甚至在见到她之前就觉得自己有权冒犯她。这种轻蔑预示着她的未来会怎样？冷漠和遗弃。

The emperor's envoy had informed her that he was engrossed in a matter of vital importance and had been unable to meet her at the border, as was the case now in Seville. His delay had nothing to do with his desire to meet her, which—and here the emissary feigned emotion—was boundless. As soon as the matter at hand was resolved, Charles would rush to her side and more than compensate her for every hour of absence with which he had offended her. However, the imperial message did nothing to lessen Isabella's anger. Her entire existence had revolved around this marriage, and although she knew of his political responsibilities, it devastated her that the matter was so secondary to him, and that he felt entitled to offend her even before having met her. What did this disdain foretell regarding her future? Coldness and abandonment.

这位葡萄牙女子躲避着人群，在塞维利亚的教堂里祈祷到深夜，以此来排解心中的忧郁。她祈求上帝赐予她力量，让她能够忍受这磨难，并阻止她内心深处的躁动——她的骄傲——战胜她。因为一旦骄傲占据上风，她就会头也不回地离开塞维利亚，而那场皇室联姻也就永远不会发生了。

The Portuguese woman hid from the crowds and eased her melancholy by praying in Seville's churches until late into the night. She begged God to give her strength to endure this ordeal and to prevent that stirring within her—her pride—from overcoming her, for if it were to win, she would leave Seville without looking back, and the imperial marriage would never take place.

 

 

 

 

“你的孩子将是我们协议的保证。下令将他们交由我监护。如果你返回法国后未能遵守协议，我将毫不犹豫地将他们据为己有。”

"Your children will be the guarantee of our agreement. Give orders that they be placed in my custody. If you return to France and fail to uphold the agreement, I will not hesitate to keep them for myself."

弗朗西斯在路中央停了下来。这是两位君主第一次一起散步，这位外国人在经历了疾病的折磨后，再次感受到阳光洒在脸上的惬意。他一如既往地保持着健壮的身姿：体格匀称，身形修长，仿佛造物主在创造他时，用了比创造查理时多一倍的肌肉和骨骼。

Francis stopped in the middle of the path. It was the first time the two monarchs had gone for a walk together, and the foreigner was enjoying feeling the sun on his face again after the debilitating effects of illness. He had his usual bearing: athletic, slender, as if Providence, in creating him, had used twice as much muscle and bone as when crafting Charles.

那就这样吧。但是……

—So be it. But…

我向你保证，我会像对待自己的孩子一样照顾他们。朋友，我恪守荣誉。

—I promise you I will take care of them as if they were my own children. I have honor, my friend.

高卢人点了点头。皇帝唤起了他内心某种柔情；他聪明睿智，心思细腻，却又拥有一颗纯洁的灵魂。只需看一眼他的眼睛，就能看透一切。他并非天真，而是卓尔不群，弗朗西斯一时竟为此羡慕不已，但同时又视他为自己最大的竞争对手。

The Gaul nodded. The emperor stirred a certain tenderness in him; he was intelligent and thoughtful, yet possessed a pure soul. One could see everything just by looking into his eyes. More than naive, he was exceptional, and for a moment Francis envied him for it, while still considering him his worst rival.

尽管法国人承诺以子女作抵押几乎让查理相信了他的诚意，但在条约签署当天，他却手持一本《圣经》出现在房间里。他首先命令一位公证人宣读协议条款。弗朗西斯不得不一遍又一遍地听到那句诅咒般的词语：放弃，放弃，放弃。放弃米兰、热那亚、勃艮第、那不勒斯、阿图瓦、图尔奈……还要放弃对纳瓦拉脱离西班牙王室独立的任何支持。唯一的收获：埃莉诺。

Although the promise to offer his children as collateral almost convinced Charles of the Frenchman's honesty, on the day of the treaty's signing, he appeared in the room with a Bible in his hand. First, he ordered a notary to read the terms of the agreement. Francis had to hear the cursed word over and over again: renounce, renounce, renounce. Renounce Milan, Genoa, Burgundy, Naples, Artois, Tournai… Renounce also any support for Navarre's independence from the Spanish Crown. Only one gain: Eleanor.

——还有我们永恒的联盟——卡洛斯补充道，他的话语比他的举动更体现出乐观。

—And our eternal alliance—added Carlos, whose words reflected more optimism than his gesture.

两份华丽的签名正式确立了协议。皇帝亲切地挽起对方的胳膊。

Two florid signatures sealed the agreement. The emperor fraternally took the other's arm.

—你现在是自由人了。

—You are a free man.

一滴泪水顺着弗朗西斯科的脸颊滑落，但他确保没人注意到。然后他整理了一下西装，深吸一口气，笑了。

A tear slid down Francisco's cheek, but he made sure no one noticed. Then he straightened his suit, took a deep breath, and smiled.

——如果我没记错的话，我现在应该结婚了。

—If I remember correctly, I should get married now.

“你得先为我做一件事。”卡洛斯指着《圣经》，“发誓你会履行你今天在这里签署的一切。”

"There's just one thing you must do for me first." Carlos pointed to the Bible. "Swear that you will fulfill what you have signed here today."

法国人毫不犹豫地走到圣书前，将手紧紧按在上面，发了誓。皇帝松了一口气。

The Frenchman, without hesitation, approached the holy book, firmly placed his hand upon it, and swore. The emperor breathed a sigh of relief.

 

 

 

 

说实话，当查理讲述他疑虑如何消除时，波旁公爵脸上露出了一丝不悦的表情。他们当时正在一个绿树成荫的庭院里享用午餐。仆人们在地上铺满了东方地毯，宴会也比往常更加丰盛，以示盛大庆典的隆重。查理之所以如此款待这位贵族，是为了平息他的怒火，因为他为了迎娶自己的敌人而取消了与埃莉诺的婚约。公爵虽然感到愤慨，却别无选择，只能保持忠诚。作为法国的叛徒，西班牙将是他长久的避难所，而能否恢复他的家产则掌握在皇帝手中。然而，弗朗西斯破坏了他的婚姻，这件事非但没有激怒他，反而给他蒙上了一层阴影；他觉得自己注定要失去一切，他渴望的一切最终都会被夺走。

To tell the truth, the Duke of Bourbon let slip a grimace of displeasure when Charles recounted how his doubts had been resolved. They were having lunch in a shaded courtyard. The servants had covered the floor with oriental carpets, and the banquet was more lavish than usual, befitting a grand celebration, for Charles sought to lavish the nobleman to soothe his anger, since he had canceled his wedding to Eleanor in favor of his enemy. The Duke, though offended, had no choice but to remain loyal, since, as a traitor to France, Spain would be his refuge for a long time, and it was in the Emperor's hands to restore his patrimony. But the fact that Francis had ruined his marriage, rather than infuriating him, cast a shadow over him; he felt condemned to have whatever he desired ultimately snatched away.

“你认为他不可能无端咒骂吗？”贵族厉声质问卡洛斯。

—Do you believe him incapable of swearing in vain? —the nobleman snapped at Carlos.

不仅是他，任何男人都是如此。这正是我们与害虫的区别：我们拥有灵魂，并且会为之恐惧。

—Not only him, but any man. That's what distinguishes us from vermin: to possess a soul and to fear for it.

“陛下，我比您更了解他。他为人肆无忌惮，虽然虔诚，但他的信仰和行为却截然不同，甚至可以说是背道而驰。我并非想让您灰心丧气，我只是提醒您：您无法想象如此邪恶之事，这说明您心智高尚，而非他如此。”

"I know him better than you do, Your Majesty. He is unscrupulous, and although devout, his faith and his actions follow different, if not opposing, paths. I do not seek to discourage you. I merely warn you: that you cannot imagine such wickedness speaks well of you, not of him."

针对法国君主的种种警告充斥着查理的脑海，筑起了一道疑虑之墙。然而，他别无选择，只能继续前行，选择信任。弗朗西斯为了表明自己的诚意，甚至以子女和灵魂为担保；皇帝所要求的任何其他保证都无法比这更能约束他。延长逮捕也毫无意义，这不仅会危及法国人的性命，还会让逮捕者在众人眼中沦为一个冷酷无情——实际上，也是不切实际——的人。即便如此，皇帝还是决定让埃莉诺不要随未婚夫前往法国，而是等到他回到自己的王国履行完放弃誓言之后，再与他圆房。查理可以放心地拿自己的信任冒险，但绝不能拿妹妹的名誉冒险。尽管婚礼在法国人返回之前举行——仪式冷清，旁观者也疑心重重——但皇帝不允许他们有任何身体接触，只允许他们轻轻地吻了一下。只有当这位高卢人证明自己言而有信时，他才配得上他的妹妹。

Warnings against the French monarch crowded Charles's mind, forming a wall of suspicion. Yet he had no choice but to proceed and trust. Francis had pledged his children and even his very soul to demonstrate his goodwill; nothing else the emperor demanded as a guarantee would bind him more. Nor did the alternative of prolonging the arrest make sense, risking the Frenchman's death and his captor being branded a cruel—and, in truth, impractical—man in the eyes of all. Even so, the emperor decided that Eleanor should not depart for France with her betrothed, but rather wait until he, back in his kingdom, fulfilled his renunciations before consummating the marriage. Charles felt free to gamble with his trust, but not with his sister's honor, and although the wedding took place before the Frenchman returned home—in a lackluster ceremony with suspicious witnesses—the emperor did not allow their bodies to touch beyond a chaste kiss. When the Gaul had shown himself to be a man of his word, he would deserve his sister.

尽管她与弗朗西斯的关系十分奇特，埃莉诺却感到无比幸福。她从一个叛军的战利品，一跃成为法国王位，而且还是拜她至少倾慕的男人所赐。葡萄牙的往事依然萦绕在她心头，每日数次，而且毫无预兆地袭来，令她备受煎熬。然而，她日渐成熟的心智决定将对约翰的单恋转化为对弗朗西斯的希望。最初的不安过后，查理对她而言不再是遥不可及的幻影，因为尽管她的命运仍掌握在皇帝手中，但最终，皇帝做出了正确的决定。

Despite the strange circumstances surrounding her relationship with Francis, Eleanor felt blissful. She had gone from being the prize of a rebel to, no less, the throne of France, and at the hand of a man she was, at the very least, infatuated with. Her memories of Portugal still lingered, haunting her several times a day, and, to top it all off, without warning, but her heart, growing wiser, had decided to transform the energy of her unrequited love for John into hope for Francis. Once the initial unease had passed, Charles ceased to be a phantom for her because, although her fate remained in the hands of the emperor, those hands, at last, had made the right decision.

 

 

 

 

当英国大使觐见亨利，告知他弗朗西斯和查理签署的《马德里条约》时，凯瑟琳不在。那天下午，当地天气宜人，一向阴冷，王后决定带女儿玛丽到乡间享受几个小时的时光。十岁的玛丽抱怨不得不离开父亲。她对父亲无比忠诚，而在此之前，父亲也一直对她忠贞不渝。凯瑟琳却需要暂时离开他。过去几周，由于一直杳无西班牙方面的消息，国王变得异常谨慎，整个宫廷的气氛也因此变得阴沉。他那双蓝眼睛还在，但却不再像以前那样明亮动人。他的声音也变了：再也听不到他爽朗的笑声，也听不到他热情或愤怒的呐喊。如今，他常常沉默不语，沉思冥想。有人窃窃私语，说他已经迷恋上了托马斯·博林——宫廷政治中的重要人物——的幼女。但这并不能解释太多。“不过是又一个情妇罢了，”凯瑟琳心想，她早已对君主的背叛习以为常。事实上，这对夫妇几乎见不到面，只有在觐见或庄严的庆典等正式场合才会见面。随着时间的推移，凯瑟琳开始察觉到丈夫性情的变化，但她却不知该如何形容这种转变。亨利总是避免与她交谈，即便不得不开口，他也总是冷漠地回避任何关于他精神状态的问题。西班牙王后最后一次见到他，完全是出于意外。她发现他端坐在王座上，仿佛在等人，尽管当天并没有安排觐见。王后站在皇家大厅入口处，凝视着他，而他却浑然不觉。她所感受到的，令她震惊不已：她的丈夫周身笼罩着一股阴暗的力量，仿佛他的灵魂已被撕裂。

When the English ambassador appeared before Henry to inform him of the Treaty of Madrid, signed by Francis and Charles, Catherine was away. The weather, almost never mild there, was pleasant that afternoon, and the queen decided to enjoy a few hours in the countryside with her daughter, Mary. The girl, now ten years old, complained about having to leave her father. Her devotion to him was boundless and, until then, had been reciprocated. Catherine, on the other hand, needed to get away from him. During the last few weeks, the lack of news from Spain had plunged the king into such a state of circumspection that it had soured the mood of the entire court. His blue eyes were still there, but they didn't look as they once had. His voice wasn't the same either: no longer were his boisterous laughs heard, nor his shouts of enthusiasm or anger. Now he remained silent for hours, meditating. It was whispered that he had become infatuated with the young daughter of Thomas Boleyn, an important figure in court politics. But that didn't explain much. “Just another mistress,” thought Catherine, who had long since resigned herself to the monarch’s infidelities. The truth was, the couple barely saw each other, only meeting for official events such as audiences or solemn celebrations. On each of these occasions, as time went on, Catherine began to perceive a change in her husband’s temperament, though she didn’t know what to call the nature of this transformation. Henry avoided speaking to her, and when it was unavoidable, he curtly dodged any questions about his state of mind. The last time the Spanish queen had encountered him, it had been by surprise, when she found him seated on the throne as if waiting for someone, even though no audience had been scheduled for that day. The queen stared at him from the entrance to the royal hall, without him noticing her presence, and what she perceived shocked her: her husband was surrounded by an aura of dark power. It was as if his soul had been ripped out.

与玛丽亚的散步让凯瑟琳暂时忘却了不知丈夫究竟是谁的不安。乡村的芬芳清新怡人，与她日复一日的生活截然不同。然而，刚刚露面的太阳又躲进了云层，不久，天空中响起了隆隆的雷声，预示着暴风雨即将到来。王后和女儿不得不返回宫廷，回到宫廷后，王后被召去觐见她的丈夫。

The walk with Maria allowed Catherine to forget for a few hours the unease caused by not knowing who she was married to anymore. The fragrance of the countryside was sweet and invigorating, the complete opposite of her daily life. But the sun, which had dared to appear, hid again behind the clouds, and soon thunderclaps were heard in the sky, heralding a storm. The queen and her daughter had to return to court, and once there, the queen was summoned to meet with her husband.

亨利端坐在王座上迎接她，仿佛自从上次她发现他处于这种状态以来，他就从未从王座上起身过。凯瑟琳紧张地寻找着他那双蓝色的眼睛，却只看到一片深渊。

Henry received her on the throne, as if he hadn't risen from it since the last time she'd found him in that state. Nervous, Catherine searched for his blue eyes and found only an abyss.

—你侄子已经和弗朗西斯科达成协议。协议条款中没有提到我的名字。

—Your nephew has reached an agreement with Francisco. My name is not mentioned in any of the clauses.

恩里克的声音低沉空洞，仿佛来自最深的井里。

Enrique's tone sounded deep and hollow, as if it came from the deepest of wells.

—我原谅了皇帝，因为你答应过要从他那里得到很多好处。

—I forgave the emperor because you promised to get a lot from him.

“我谴责你的决定，”她真诚地说。“我从未想过你会以这种方式解决问题。”

"I condemn your decision," she said sincerely. "I never thought you would be capable of resolving the situation in such a way."

“你答应过我会从他那里得到很多好处，”亨利重复道，目光紧紧盯着王后，王后畏惧不已，沉默不语。“从今以后，法国将蒙受我的恩宠。查理又一次藐视了我，但这将是最后一次。”

"You promised me you would get much from him," Henry repeated, fixing his gaze on the queen, who, intimidated, remained silent. "France will enjoy my favor from now on. Charles has scorned me once again, but it will be the last time."

——我不能因此批评你，尽管我非常担心弗朗西斯不仅会轻蔑地对待你，还会背信弃义……

—I cannot criticize you for that, although I greatly fear that Francis will not behave disdainfully towards you, but treacherously…

“我将与他结盟，为英格兰保驾护航，”他补充道。“现在我知道我不能将王国的命运托付给他人。从今天起，我将只服从自己的意志，上帝知道，我将成为他的奴隶。”

“I will secure an alliance for England from him,” he added. “Now I know I cannot delegate the fate of my kingdom to others. From this day forward, I will obey only my own will, and God knows I will be his slave.”

国王从王座上起身，走到妻子面前。他走到她面前，冷冷地抚摸着她的脸颊。

The king rose from his throne and went to his wife. Once in front of her, he coldly caressed her face.

你给了我什么？告诉我。

—What have you given me? Tell me.

卡塔琳娜想哭，但她忍住了。

Catalina wanted to cry, but she held it back.

——我尽我所能，我的爱人。

—As much as I could, my love.

恩里克目不转睛地盯着她，一眨不眨。

Enrique stared at her without blinking.

“你剥夺了我王国应有的继承人，你强迫我与一个从未尊重过我的人结盟。你因你的血脉而判我效忠于他。但我已经厌倦了这一切。”

"You have denied my kingdom the heir it needs, and you have forced me to ally myself with one who has never respected me. You condemn me to be bound to him because of your blood. But my will has grown weary of it."

—请您自行决定最适合英格兰的联盟，我将遵从您的意见。

—Choose at your own discretion the alliance that suits England, and I will abide by your opinion.

“我不相信你，”他说，“但这也不能弥补你未能履行给我生个儿子的义务。”

"I don't believe you," he said, "nor does that compensate for your failure to fulfill your duty to give me a son."

-仍然…

-Still…

“不，”亨利说着，手顺着她的脖子滑下，感受着她跳动的脉搏，“我会请求罗马教廷批准我和你离婚。”

—No—Henry declared, running his hand down her neck and feeling her throbbing pulse. —I will ask Rome to grant me a divorce from you.

君主立刻与妻子分开，离开了王宫。凯瑟琳没有跟上去；她呆立在那里，不知自己是否已经死去，就这么站在那里，成了他话语的牺牲品。直到泪水涌上眼眶，胸口仿佛被一根无形的木桩刺穿，她才知道自己还活着。她的未来消失了，一股黑暗的力量攫住了她，直到她发出尖叫。

Immediately, the monarch separated from his wife and left the royal hall. Catherine did not follow him; she was paralyzed, wondering if she had died there, standing, a victim of his words. She only knew she was still alive when tears welled in her eyes and her chest felt pierced by an invisible stake. Her future vanished, and the aura of dark power gripped her until she screamed.

 

 

 

 

当皇帝得知弗朗西斯的子女已抵达西班牙，并由亲信照料后，便释放了被他囚禁数月的那个人质。查理选择在伊列斯卡斯与他告别。在他们最后的谈话中，双方随从都保持着礼貌的距离。

When the emperor learned that Francis's children had arrived in Spain and were under the care of trusted men, he granted freedom to the man who had been his hostage for months. Illescas was the place chosen by Charles to bid him farewell. Their respective entourages respectfully maintained their distance during their final conversation.

“让我们像兄弟一样道别吧。”法国人说道。

"Let's say goodbye like brothers," said the Frenchman.

他们拥抱在一起。皇帝能感觉到周围人的目光，他确信许多人都在谴责他这兄弟般的举动。幸好，与他几乎不再交谈的加蒂娜拉决定留在宫廷，让他免于遭受众人异样的目光。在松开拥抱之前，查理凑近她的耳边低语。

They embraced. The emperor could feel the stares of those around them, and he was certain that many were censuring him for this fraternal gesture. Fortunately, Gattinara, with whom he barely spoke anymore, had decided to remain at court, sparing him a path fraught with disapproving looks. Before breaking the embrace, Charles leaned close to her ear.

—如果你要欺骗我，无论是部分还是全部，都不要涉及我的妹妹，因为我永远无法原谅这种罪行。

—If you were to deceive me in part or in whole, let it not be in regard to my sister, for I could never forgive that offense.

法国人看着他，好像不明白似的。

The Frenchman looked at him as if he didn't understand.

你不信任我吗？那为什么放我走？

—Do you distrust me? Why let me go, then?

皇帝心想，但他没有说出来，他有很​​多理由这样做，尽管他也说不出任何具体的理由。

The emperor thought, but did not say, that he had plenty of reasons, although he could not argue any specific one to do so either.

“现在我们是盟友了，”方济各继续说道。“团结起来，我们完全可以扩大我们的势力范围。面对我们的联盟，教皇的领土必然会缩小……”

“Now we are allies,” Francis continued. “United, we could very well expand our domains. Faced with our alliance, the Pope’s territories would inevitably diminish…”

—你难道还没明白，我不想要不属于我的东西吗？

—Haven't you understood yet that I don't want what isn't mine?

法国人笑了。某种程度上，他会怀念卡洛斯清澈的眼神。他一生中从未见过这样的眼神。

The Frenchman smiled. In a way, he would miss Carlos's clear-eyed gaze. He had never known anyone like it in his life.

——陛下，您真是个奇怪的人。

—You are a strange man, Emperor.

根特人默默地看着弗朗西斯转身，翻身上马，头也不回地任由押送他前往边境的士兵们引领着他。他不禁思忖，自己是否还能再见到他，也琢磨着，除了自身那份因众人灌输的不信任而加深的怀疑之外，自己对弗朗西斯究竟还有什么感觉。他们如此不同，如果能成为朋友，他一定会很开心，因为那永远不会让他感到厌倦。他羡慕法国人的魅力和直率的机智。然而，他们的分离最终还是让一切回归了原状，从某种意义上说，这给他带来了一丝平静。

The man from Ghent watched in silence as Francis turned, mounted his horse, and, without looking back, allowed himself to be led by the retinue of soldiers whose mission was to escort him to the border. He wondered if he would ever see him again, and also what he felt toward him, apart from his own distrust, compounded by the distrust so many had instilled in him. They were so different that their friendship would have pleased him, for it would never have led to boredom, and he envied the Frenchman's charisma and brash wit. However, their separation finally restored the natural order of things, and in that sense, it brought him some peace.

在他们启程返回宫廷不久后，一名使者以极快的速度，甚至有些疲惫地，出去迎接皇室随从。

Shortly after beginning their journey back to the court, an emissary, swift to the point of exhaustion, went out to meet the imperial entourage.

——陛下，您的未婚妻！

—Your fiancée, Your Majesty!

伊莎贝尔。与弗朗西斯科的谈判让他全神贯注，以至于他几乎没想起在塞维利亚等着他、想要献身于他的女人。这件事立刻吸引了他的注意力，仿佛他从一个世界进入了另一个世界，法语在这里变得无关紧要。

Isabel. The negotiations with Francisco had absorbed him so completely that he had barely thought of the woman waiting for him in Seville to give herself to him. The matter immediately captured his attention, as if he had passed from one world to another where French mattered little.

—你有什么关于她的消息吗？

—What news do you have of her?

—她已经放弃再等你了。

—The fact that she has given up waiting for you any longer.

 

 

 

 

当她再次看到西班牙和葡萄牙边界上的十字架时——几周前她曾满怀希望地瞥见过它——伊莎贝尔努力克制住泪水。没有什么比在众人面前崩溃更不像她了，因为如果她在陪同她返回葡萄牙的士兵和贵妇们的注视下失态，那将是莫大的耻辱。但如果说她一生中有什么时刻让她几乎丧失了镇定和自尊，那就是此刻，没有之一。她不知道未来会怎样，但她确信，无论未来如何，她都将承受这份失望的痛苦，直到生命的尽头。她的世界观如同纸牌屋般轰然倒塌：她一直相信意志力可以塑造命运，但她渴望与皇帝在一起的强烈愿望却毫无用处。她那时才明白，如果一个灵魂朝着另一个相反的方向前进，那么另一个灵魂的结合就毫无意义。毫无疑问，查尔斯的灵魂与她的灵魂并不和谐。她本可以永远在塞维利亚等他，但她意识到，她渴望的不仅是这段婚姻，更是他能让她感到幸福、非凡和被爱。如果她是通过羞辱自己而获得的皇后头衔，那么这个头衔又有什么意义呢？

Upon seeing the cross that marked the border between Spain and Portugal, which she had glimpsed with such hope weeks before, Isabel fought to hold back her tears. Nothing could have been more unlike her than to break down in front of others, for if she had succumbed under the gaze of the soldiers and ladies who accompanied her on her return to Portugal, she would have been humiliated. But if there could be a moment in her life when she had been on the verge of abandoning her composure and self-respect, it was this one and no other. She did not know what the future held for her, although she was certain that, whatever it might be, she would bear the pain of this disappointment, and so it would be until the end of her days. Her worldview had just crumbled like a house of cards: she had always believed that willpower shaped destinies, but her burning desire to be with the emperor had been of little use. She understood then that one soul achieves nothing if another moves in the opposite direction, and Charles's soul, without a doubt, was not in harmony with her own. She could have waited for him in Seville forever, but she had realized that she not only longed for this marriage, but also for him to make her feel happy, extraordinary, loved. It was worthless to hold the title of empress if she had attained it by disgracing herself.

当一行人即将抵达边境口岸时，一个声音命令他们停下。伊莎贝尔停了下来，却犹豫不决，不知是否该回头。一个突如其来的幻象浮现，卡洛斯在她身后气喘吁吁，他曾拼命阻止她离开。这景象美得令人难以置信，仿佛是她渴望抛弃的那个伊莎贝尔的倒影，那个渴望着不可能之物的伊莎贝尔。

As the group was about to reach the border cross, a voice ordered them to halt. Isabel stopped, but hesitated, unsure whether to turn around. A sudden fantasy conjured up a vision of Carlos behind her, gasping for breath after a desperate attempt to prevent her from leaving him. The image was too beautiful to be true, a reflection of the Isabel she longed to leave behind, the one who yearned for what was impossible.

夫人，虽然夜已深，但我仍冒昧前来觐见。

—My lady. Although it is late, I dare to present myself before you.

葡萄牙女子不禁打了个寒颤。这不可能是真的。她转过身，想确认这究竟是玩笑，还是自己悲痛欲绝的幻觉。她转过身，正好看见一个有着孩子般眼神、皮肤白皙（因旅途劳顿而略显红润）的男子下了马。他的衣着华丽，堪比帝王，随行的武士也同样英姿飒爽。但这不可能是真的。还没等她反应过来，那人便奔到她身边。

The Portuguese woman shuddered. It couldn't be true. She turned to make sure it was a joke or a figment of her grief-stricken mind. She turned just in time to see a man with childlike eyes and white skin, reddened by a hurried journey, dismount. His clothes were exquisite, fit for an emperor, as was the martial retinue he brought with him. But it couldn't be true. Before she could react, he ran to her side.

——一切都还没有结束。事实上，一切都还有可能获得。但如果你决定不嫁给我，我会尊重你的决定，因为我辜负了我唯一应尽的义务——尊重，我理应受到同样的惩罚。

—Nothing is lost yet. In fact, everything is yet to be gained. But if you decide not to marry me, I will respect your decision, for I deserve no less punishment for having neglected the one I owe only to honor.

狂风呼啸着掠过边境平原，趁着众人寂静之际肆意肆虐。伊莎贝尔和卡洛斯第一次四目相对。他，此前只是出于责任感才来到这里，此刻却瞬间忘却了所有的承诺、政治、义务和外交礼仪。眼前的女子是他见过的最美的，她不仅美貌绝伦，更拥有令人倾倒的魅力。难道是上天赐予了他如此巨大的福气？他立刻后悔给了她离开的选择：他想要她留在自己身边，而失去她将令他痛苦万分。伊莎贝尔仔细观察着皇帝的表情，惊讶地发现他的爱慕之情竟如此真挚。她强压傲气，心中的怨恨却随着呼啸的狂风迅速消散。她曾为这个男人怀揣的所有梦想再次鲜活起来。边境仿佛瞬间化作一道钢铁之墙，她绝不会轻易跨越。

The wind howled across the border plain, taking advantage of the silence of all those present. Isabel and Carlos looked into each other's eyes for the first time. He, whom only duty had spurred on to this point, instantly forgot about commitments and politics, obligations and diplomacy. The woman before him was the most beautiful he had ever seen, and she also possessed the charm of a character. Had Providence bestowed upon him such immense fortune? He immediately regretted having given her the option of letting her go: he wanted her in his life, and the opposite would devastate him. Isabel, for her part, scrutinized the emperor's expression and was astonished to find that his desire seemed genuine. With a swiftness that belied her pride, resentment blew away on the wind that whipped around them. All the dreams she had harbored for this man came alive again. The border, suddenly, had transformed into a wall of steel that she had no intention of crossing.

塞维利亚从未像1526年3月那样屏息凝神。当地最年长的居民仍记得卡斯蒂利亚女王伊莎贝拉一世的到访，那次访问可谓喜忧参半，因为她给这座城市带来了一种以严苛手段维系的秩序。那是在半个世纪前，那时世界边界泾渭分明，与自1492年克里斯托弗·哥伦布离开帕洛斯港以来不断扩张的地图截然不同。短短几十年间，塞维利亚从一个由反复无常的贵族统治的繁荣商业中心，摇身一变，成为西班牙通往印度的门户，随之而来的是繁荣与变幻莫测。它是最早见证大西洋彼岸新世界奇迹的城市。因此，这座城市早已习惯了非凡之事，但即便如此，当得知皇帝选择这里作为他与葡萄牙女王伊莎贝拉的婚礼举办地时，它依然感到无比自豪。因此，为了报答皇室的恩惠，人们举行了一场前所未有的盛大仪式：街道上挂满了布料和挂毯，一百名乐师排练着迎接皇帝和他未来的妻子时将要演奏的曲调。

Seville hadn't held its breath as much as it did that March of 1526. The oldest locals remembered the visit of Isabella I of Castile, a bittersweet one, for she had brought to the city an order achieved through excessive rigor. It had taken place half a century earlier, when the world had rigid borders and bore no resemblance to the map that had been expanding ceaselessly since Christopher Columbus had left the port of Palos in 1492. In just a few decades, Seville had gone from being a vibrant commercial center dominated by a capricious nobility to becoming the gateway to and from the Indies in Spain, with all the exuberance and unpredictability that entailed. It was the first witness to the wonders arriving from that new world across the Atlantic. The city was thus accustomed to the extraordinary, but even so, it swelled with pride upon learning that the emperor had chosen it as the setting for his marriage to Isabella of Portugal. The royal favor was therefore returned with an unprecedented display: the streets were adorned with cloths and tapestries, and one hundred musicians rehearsed the melodies with which the emperor and his future wife would be received.

虽然花费巨大，但塞维利亚的民众一看到查理五世从皇家大街（Calle Real）入城，便将一切牺牲抛诸脑后。他身后簇拥着一大批贵族、教士，以及代表城市各个阶层的众多队伍——律师、医生和其他各行各业的人士。游行队伍一路奏乐，几乎没有片刻的寂静，仿佛这些显赫人物的行进本身就散发着音乐的气息。每当皇帝及其随从穿过沿途建造的七座凯旋门之一时，庄严的气氛便愈发浓烈。每座凯旋门上都镌刻着皇帝的功绩，因为塞维利亚迎接的并非西班牙国王，也非流经瓜达尔基维尔河的印度领主；它首先迎接的是一位皇帝。因此，在那场庆典的每一个细节中，查理的威严都得以彰显，仿佛是对罗马昔日辉煌的回响，那面镜子正是文艺复兴时期人们极力想要映照自身的地方。人群的情绪自然高涨，不仅因为来访者的身份显赫，更因为他们迎接的正是俘虏法国君主的人。这一事件深深触动了民众——他们感到终于在多年遭受北方邻国的压迫之后得到了复仇——即使在弗朗索瓦获释之后，它仍然被视为一项英雄壮举。在游行队伍中，皇帝听到了反对法国人的呼喊声，也听到了赞扬他俘虏自己时所展现的力量和勇气的赞颂声。听到这些，他骄傲地站在马背上，心满意足，仿佛刚刚赢得了百场战役的胜利。

The expense was high, but the people of Seville forgot the sacrifice as soon as they saw Charles enter through the Calle Real, accompanied by a considerable retinue of nobles, clergymen, and, behind them, numerous squadrons representing each sector of the city—lawyers, doctors, and other professions. Music accompanied the procession, so much so that there was hardly a moment of silence, as if the illustrious figures exuded music as they passed. The concert grew more solemn each time the emperor and his followers passed through one of the seven triumphal arches that the city had erected along the route. On each arch, one could read an inscription about some virtue of the emperor, because Seville was not receiving the King of Spain, nor the lord and master of the Indies, which flowed into the city through the veins of the Guadalquivir; it was welcoming, above all, an emperor. Therefore, in every detail of that celebration, the grandeur of Charles was revealed, an echo of the grandeur once invented by Rome, that mirror in which the Renaissance so loved to see itself reflected. The spirits of the crowd rose inevitably, not only because of the importance of the visitor, but also because the one they were receiving was the captor of the French monarch. The event had resonated deeply with the people—who felt finally avenged after years of grievances from their northern neighbor—and it endured as a heroic feat even after Francis had been freed. In the midst of his procession, the emperor heard shouts against the Frenchman and also others that extolled the power and bravery he had shown in capturing him. Upon hearing them, he stood proudly on his horse, as satisfied as if he had emerged victorious from a hundred battles.

不久之后，伊莎贝尔登场了。查尔斯的未婚妻注意到成千上万双眼睛正注视着她，那贪婪的目光几乎要将她吞噬。她有​​些紧张，但正如她一贯的作风，无人能察觉，因为她的面容宛如一位慈祥的斯芬克斯。那些此刻正仔细打量她的人——他们知道，这肯定是他们唯一一次见到她——很快将成为她的臣民。虽然此刻，她骑着马，由随从簇拥着，身姿高大，气势逼人，但事实上，从此刻起，为他们服务的将是伊莎贝尔，即使是最盛大的仪式也无法让她忘记即将肩负的责任。尽管查理五世拥有遍布全球的领土，但未来的女皇伊莎贝拉深知，这桩婚姻的目的之一是为了给西班牙提供一位贤能稳定的摄政，以免皇帝不在时，政府落入不可靠的人手中，也不会让西班牙人民再次感受到他们早已饱受煎熬的被遗弃感。伊莎贝拉将拥有神圣罗马帝国女皇的头衔，但她首先也是永远是这个王国的统治者。

Shortly after, Isabel made her entrance. Charles's betrothed noticed thousands of eyes fixed upon her, almost draining her with such avidity. She was nervous, but, as was her nature, no one could have guessed, for her countenance resembled that of a benevolent sphinx. Those who now scrutinized her—knowing that, surely, it would be the first and last time they would see her—were soon to be her subjects, and although at that precise moment, mounted on horseback and escorted by her retinue, her figure seemed to tower over them with an insurmountable superiority, the truth was that from then on it would be Isabel who was at their service, and not even the greatest pomp could make her forget the responsibility she was about to assume. Although Charles possessed dominions across the globe, the future empress was aware that one of the reasons for this marriage was to provide Spain with a worthy and stable regent so that the emperor's absences would not force the government into unreliable hands, nor provoke in the Spanish people the sense of abandonment they so poorly endured. Isabella would hold the title of Empress of the Holy Roman Empire, but she would be, above all and forever, the administrator of that kingdom.

然而，当她准备穿过第七道拱门时，她注意到拱门上刻着献给她的铭文，与献给查理的铭文并列，上面写着“要么凯撒，要么一无所有”（ Aut Caesar aut nihil）。起初的紧张感瞬间转化为一种前所未有的满足感。这句格言提醒她，为了实现这个命运，她付出了多少努力，而这道拱门也象征着她毕生目标的最终达成。塞维利亚人欢呼雀跃，他们很快就爱上了他们的皇后，这更加激发了她的热情。她迫不及待地想要与查理结合，因为她已经爱上了他。仅仅一次邂逅，就足以让她在他身上看到自己渴望的化身。尽管她心中仍保留着一丝理性的谨慎，但她的心已经彻底沦陷，抛开了理智，渴望更深入地了解他。自从见到他以来，伊莎贝拉就一直非常仔细地观察着他的每一个举动，从中她都能感受到他们结合的恰当性。

However, when, preparing to pass through the seventh arch, the young woman noticed the inscription dedicated to her, which, alongside the one addressed to Charles, adorned the archway, and read Aut Caesar aut nihil— "Either Caesar or nothing"—what had initially been nervousness transformed into a satisfaction unlike anything she had ever experienced. The motto reminded her how much she had striven to reach this destiny, and the archway served as a symbol of her life's goal finally achieved. The cheers of the Sevillians, who quickly fell in love with their empress, heightened her emotion, and the young woman felt she could hardly wait to be joined to Charles, whom she already felt she loved. One encounter had been enough for her to recognize in him the personification of her desires, and although she harbored a certain rational prudence, her heart had surrendered completely, disregarding logic and waiting to know him better. In each of his gestures, which Isabella had observed with the utmost attention since she had seen him, she had sensed the propriety of their union.

他们最终在宽恕之门相遇，塞维利亚大主教在那里迎接了他们。这对新人以应有的庄重神情彼此凝视，但两人脸上都带着一丝羞涩的微笑。

They finally met at the Gate of Forgiveness, where the Archbishop of Seville received them. The couple gazed at each other with the seriousness the occasion demanded, but on both their faces, however shy, a smile of enchantment appeared.

带着同样的紧张感——既庄重又冲动——他们走进了皇家阿尔卡萨宫。伊莎贝拉被这里的美景深深震撼，异域风情的建筑让她怀疑自己是在梦中还是在现实中。一切都完美无瑕，如同梦境般令人心碎：皇帝在她身旁；四周尽是美轮美奂的装饰；他那只温暖而柔软的手，绅士地引领她进入宫殿；庭院中弥漫着令人陶醉的花香。

With the same conflict between solemnity and the spontaneity of their infatuation, they entered the Royal Alcázar. Isabella was overwhelmed by the beauty of the place, for its exotic architecture made her doubt whether she was awake or dreaming. Everything seemed perfect, like in a dream that brings sadness when it ends: at her side, the emperor; all around, a decoration of impossible beauty; his hand, which chivalrously guided her inside, was warm and soft; the intoxicating perfume of the flowers in the building's courtyards filled the air.

“我没想到大家会这么喜欢我，”入学仪式结束后，他告诉卡洛斯。

"I didn't expect so much favor from people towards me," he told Carlos when the entrance ceremony had concluded.

“你不需要囚禁国王才能赢得爱戴。我理解他们。”

"You don't need to imprison a king to be loved. And I understand them."

她的双颊努力不让自己泛红。

Her cheeks struggled to keep from turning red.

我需要休息。

—I need to rest.

查理目送她消失在宫殿深处。与他怦怦的心跳相比，她裙摆的摆动显得轻柔无比。皇帝低声感谢上帝赐予他的好运。这桩最初出于外交和经济考量的婚约，为何最终却占据了他内心最深处、最渴望的情感？从见到她的那一刻起，查理就感到无比幸运。尽管他未来的妻子美貌绝伦，但事实上，这份吸引力早已超越了外表。在他们的第一眼中，未婚妻的灵魂仿佛被揭示出来，她的双眼仿佛开启了他通往她内心世界的大门。那一刻，查理感到自己完全沉浸其中；那是一个充满高贵、温暖和活力的世界，令他惊叹不已。伊莎贝尔是这样的人，而不是别人，他该是多么幸运啊！卡洛斯一生中认识许多品德高尚的女子，但她们无一例外都有缺点，因为她们是人，难免有瑕疵：美貌往往与冷漠相悖，智慧与卑劣并存，品格高尚却容貌平庸，难以触动人心。他原本只希望妻子少有缺点，因此，每当遇到一个似乎完美无瑕的女子时，他总是感到无比惊讶。

Charles watched her disappear into the palace. The sway of her dress was gentle compared to the beating of his heart. In a murmur, the emperor thanked God for his good fortune. How had this engagement, initially motivated by nothing more than diplomacy and finances, come to fill his deepest and most ambitious emotions? From the moment he saw her, Charles felt blessed, and although his future wife's beauty was unparalleled, the truth was that the attraction had transcended mere appearance. The soul of his betrothed had been revealed to him in their first glance, as if her eyes had granted him entry into her inner world, where for a moment Charles felt immersed; a world that surprised him with its nobility, warmth, and energy. How fortunate must he be for Isabel to be this way and not someone else? Throughout his life, Carlos had known many virtuous women, but none were without flaws, for they were human and, as such, imperfect: beauty was often counterbalanced by coldness, intelligence by vileness, or good character by an appearance that failed to stir the soul. He would have been content with a wife of few faults, which is why he was always astonished to have found one who seemed to be completely without them.

-威严。

-Majesty.

如果说阿尔巴公爵的声音勉强将卡洛斯从失恋的遐想中拉了出来，那么这位贵族的严肃表情则瞬间将他拉回了现实。

If the Duke of Alba's voice had barely managed to pull Carlos out of his lovelorn reverie, the nobleman's somber expression brought him back down to earth in a flash.

——我谨致以最深切的慰问。从弗兰德斯传来消息，您的妹妹伊莎贝尔已经去世了。

—I offer you my deepest condolences. News has arrived from Flanders that your sister Isabel has passed away.

皇帝反应迟钝。他的心在短短几秒钟内，就从喜悦转为绝望。

The emperor was slow to react. His heart had to travel, in mere seconds, from joy to desolation.

“据你姑姑玛格丽塔说，她已经受苦一段时间了。据说她去世时如释重负。”

"According to your aunt Margarita, she had been suffering for some time. They say she passed away with relief."

厄运开始侵蚀查理的灵魂，随之而来的是一段回忆：十四岁的妹妹伊莎贝拉在前往丹麦嫁给克里斯蒂安国王之前，向他告别。那是他们最后一次见面。她美丽动人，外表柔弱，但内心却无比坚强。她对这桩婚姻感到满意，告别时既有悲伤，也有对未来的期盼。然而，她的乐观并未实现：几年后，她被拥立为瑞典女王，却发动叛乱，推翻了丈夫的统治，将他们二人逐出王位。在丹麦，由于克里斯蒂安的叔叔的背叛，他们也遭遇了同样的命运。伊莎贝拉和查理，如今已是无冕之王，不得不逃往尼德兰避难，他们为重夺王位所做的不懈努力也以失败告终。卡洛斯一直沉浸在自己的麻烦中，忽略了她的求助信息，现在，除了她去世的悲剧之外，他还背负着忽视她的罪恶感。

The misfortune began to take hold in Charles's soul, bringing with it a memory: that of his sister Isabella, at fourteen years old, bidding him farewell before leaving for Denmark, where she was to become the wife of King Christian. That had been the last time they had seen each other.
