She, beautiful and with an appearance more fragile than her character, was content with the marriage that had befallen her, and in her goodbye there was sadness but also hope for what was to come. But her optimism was not borne out: a few years later, after having also been proclaimed Queen of Sweden, they rebelled against her husband and expelled them both from the throne. In Denmark, they met the same fate, due to a betrayal by Christian's uncle. Isabella and he, now kings of nothing, had to take refuge in the Netherlands, and their tireless attempts to regain their lost power met with no success. Carlos, engrossed as he had been in his own troubles, had ignored her messages for help, and now to the tragedy of her death was added the guilt of having neglected her.

“如果他感激死亡，那不是因为痛苦，而是因为他的人生黯淡无光，”国王喃喃自语，目光沉浸在宫殿的阿拉伯式花纹中，这些花纹似乎在模仿人类命运的复杂性。

"If he was grateful for death, it was not because of the pain, but because his life was bleak," murmured the king, his gaze lost in the arabesques of the palace, which seemed to imitate the complexity of men's destinies.

阿尔巴公爵尊重皇帝的悲痛片刻，直到他觉得有必要打断他。

The Duke of Alba respected the emperor's grief for a few moments, until he felt compelled to interrupt him.

“陛下，您是否意识到这场悲剧的后果？必须尊重您妹妹的哀悼。皇家婚礼的庆祝活动与持续数周的哀悼期格格不入。”

"Your Majesty, are you aware of the consequences of this tragedy? Mourning for your sister must be respected. The festivities of the imperial wedding are incompatible with mourning, which will last for weeks."

卡洛斯感到一股强烈的痛苦涌上心头，这痛苦与他妹妹去世的悲伤交织在一起，让他难以承受。上帝似乎在权衡命运的天平，收回祂通过选择他未来的妻子而赐予他的过剩财富。

Carlos felt a current of anguish coursing through him, one that mingled with the grief of his sister's death, creating an unbearable sensation. God was balancing the scales of fortune, taking away the excess He had bestowed upon him with the choice of his future wife.

“我先是迟到惹她生气，现在又不得不推迟婚礼。我该如何避免未婚妻后悔答应我的求婚呢？”

"First I offended her with my lateness, and now I have to postpone our wedding. How can I prevent my fiancée from regretting having agreed to my marriage proposal?"

 

 

 

 

葡萄牙的伊莎贝尔正在阿尔卡萨宫的庭院里享受花香，这时查尔斯神情严肃地告诉她发生了什么事，这是她从未见过的。

Isabel of Portugal was enjoying the perfume of the flowers in the courtyard of the Alcázar when Charles, as serious as she had never seen him, told her what had happened.

“你看，我不能只尊重一个伊莎贝尔而不冒犯另一个，”他说。“她活着的时候我就冷落了她，现在她死了，我怎么能继续这样下去呢？”

"As you can see, I cannot honor one Isabel without offending the other," he said. "I already neglected her while she was alive. How can I continue to do so now, after her death?"

那位葡萄牙女子默默地点了点头。上天究竟为她安排了什么？为何迟迟不让她幸福？

The Portuguese woman nodded silently. What did Providence intend for her? Why did it hesitate so long to make her happy?

——我没有什么可责怪你的。让我感到不满的是命运，而不是你。看来上帝并不想让我们在一起，陛下。

—I have nothing to reproach you for. It is fate that offends me, not you. It would seem that God does not want us together, Your Majesty.

她的声音宛如一首哀婉的鲁特琴。查理垂下眼帘。命运啊。看来欲望或权宜之计束缚了他们的手脚；最终，他们不过是命运的傀儡。皇帝悲伤地再次抬眼看向伊莎贝拉，她的悲伤深深刺痛了他。他心中涌起一股怒火，随后一个念头闪过他的脑海——或许有些异想天开，甚至可能冒犯了他的未婚妻——但这不失为一个好机会，可以看看这个女人是否真如他想象的那般非凡。

Her voice sounded like a mournful lute. Charles lowered his gaze. Fate. It seemed that desire or expediency had their hands tied; in the end, they were puppets of fortune. Sorrowfully, the emperor raised his eyes again to Isabella, whose sadness pierced him. He felt anger, and then an idea occurred to him—perhaps far-fetched, and maybe, he thought, even offensive to his betrothed—but it was a good opportunity to see if this woman was as extraordinary as he thought.

我会替你保守妹妹的秘密几个小时，就够你结婚的。不会有庆祝活动，不会有舞会，也不会有西班牙的贵妇或贵族亲吻我们的手。

—I will keep my sister's news a secret for a few hours. Just long enough for you to get married. There will be no festivities, no dances, no ladies or grandees of Spain kissing our hands.

伊莎贝尔被这提议惊得目瞪口呆，呼吸都急促起来。卡洛斯心想，如果她如此热切期盼的时刻就这样被破坏，失去了它应有的庄严，她该有多么失望啊。哪个女人听到这样的提议不会觉得受到了侮辱呢？

Isabel, astonished by the proposal, felt her breathing quicken. Carlos imagined how disappointing it must be for her if the moment she had been so eagerly anticipating were marred in this way, stripped of the grandeur it deserved. What woman wouldn't feel insulted by such a suggestion?

“那就这样吧。”她回答道。

—So be it —she replied.

就这样，年轻女子不仅答应了这门婚事，还赢得了皇帝的心，仿佛这颗心从未属于过他一样。

And with that word, the young woman not only agreed to the marriage, but she won the emperor's heart as if it had never belonged to him.

当晚，在塞维利亚皇家阿尔卡萨宫大使厅，在宏伟穹顶的映衬下，订婚仪式举行。随后，由专程前往塞维利亚的托莱多大主教主持弥撒。最后，在西班牙教会领袖的见证下，举行了披纱仪式。伊莎贝尔和卡洛斯跪下后，他们的头被一块薄纱遮盖。在那轻盈洁白的纱幔下，他们聆听着彼此的呼吸，第一次感受到了婚姻的真谛。尽管夜已深，他们的眼中依然闪烁着对未来的憧憬。大主教握住他们紧紧相拥的双手，用拉丁语诵读祷文。这对新人沉浸在彼此的亲密之中，远远地聆听着祷文。

That evening, in the Hall of Ambassadors of the Royal Alcázar, with its magnificent dome as one of the few witnesses, the betrothal took place, followed by a Mass officiated by the Archbishop of Toledo, who had traveled to Seville for this purpose. Finally, with the head of the Spanish Church also present, the veiling ceremony took place. Once Isabel and Carlos knelt, their heads were covered by a single veil. Under that light, white mantle, listening to each other's breathing, they felt married for the first time, and despite the late hour, their eyes shone with a joy that spoke of a future. The archbishop joined their hands, which clasped with deep feeling, and recited a prayer in Latin, which the newlyweds heard from afar, so electrified were they by the intimacy they shared.

从仪式结束到他们在寝宫幽会的这段时间，对两人来说都充满了喜悦和激动。当仆人为卡洛斯穿戴晚礼服时，他已故妹妹的身影偶尔会掠过他的脑海，如同一只垂死挣扎的黑鸟；但仿佛推迟葬礼仪式也延缓了他独自哀悼的心情，他的妻子已经占据了他的心神。与此同时，伊莎贝尔默默地接受着侍女们的服侍，进行着某种仪式。这位年轻女子深知自己在面对这一刻时远不如他成熟，但这丝毫没有让她感到恐惧，因为她知道自己会用渴望来弥补任何恐惧。

The time between the ceremony and their private encounter in the bedchamber was filled with joyful excitement for both of them. As his servants dressed him in his evening attire, the memory of his deceased sister occasionally crossed Carlos's mind, like a dark bird in its final flight; but as if by postponing the funeral rites he had also delayed his private mourning, his wife had taken hold of his spirit. Meanwhile, Isabel allowed herself to be prepared by her ladies-in-waiting in a silent ritual. The young woman knew she came to this moment with less experience than he, but this ignorance did not frighten her, for she knew that she would compensate for any fear with desire.

当卡洛斯走进即将圆房的卧室时，他感觉仿佛黎明已过，白昼已至。站在床边的伊莎贝尔，尽管睡衣朴素，却散发着耀眼的光芒。他走向她，目光始终交汇，他开始轻柔地为她脱去衣物，如同展开一只娇嫩鸟儿的翅膀。伊莎贝尔被他的静谧弄得有些不安，决定帮他脱衣服，但令她惊讶的是，紧张使她笨手笨脚。

When Carlos entered the bedroom where the wedding night was about to be consummated, it seemed to him that dawn had passed and day had already broken, such was the light radiating from Isabel, standing beside the bed, resplendent despite the simplicity of her nightgown. Their gaze remained fixed as he moved toward her, and also as he began to undress her with the care of one who spreads the wings of a delicate bird. Isabel, unsettled by his stillness, decided to help him undress, but, to her surprise, her nerves made her clumsy.

“我的自制力哪去了？”他暗自叹息道。

"Where is my temperance?" he lamented to himself.

查尔斯握住她的手，轻轻地吻了一下。他的唇仍有些犹豫，缓缓向上移到妻子的颈项，直到触及她的唇瓣，才释放出凯撒压抑已久的激情。然而，衣衫仍将他们隔开；查尔斯还无法平静下来，轻易地解开它们。两人都有些尴尬，不禁笑了起来。笑声渐渐消失，他们凝视着彼此，仿佛世间再无其他。

Charles then took her hands and kissed them gently. His lips, still hesitant, then moved up to his wife's neck, and only when they reached her lips did they unleash the Caesar's pent-up passion. Their garments, however, still separated them; Charles was not yet calm enough to handle them with ease. Their shared embarrassment made them laugh. The laughter faded as they gazed at each other as if there were no other world but them.

“你对我做了什么？”他喃喃自语，目光完全被葡萄牙女人的眼神吸引住了。

"What are you doing to me?" he said, lost in the Portuguese woman's eyes.

在亲吻和迷醉的凝视中，他们的衣衫终于褪去。几个小时后，黎明到来，但沉浸在爱河中的他​​们几乎毫无察觉，他们的目光中只有彼此，只为探寻这般幸福的真谛。

Their clothes finally fell away, amidst kisses and spellbound glances. Dawn greeted them hours later, but they, lost in their love, barely noticed, for their eyes had no other purpose than to ask each other how such bliss was possible.

 

 

 

 

法国国王弗朗索瓦二世进入昂布瓦兹城堡的皇家大厅，其庄严程度堪比查理和伊莎贝拉进入塞维利亚时的情景。然而，在场者的热情远不及瓜达尔基维尔河畔塞维利亚城内民众的热情。数十位被召集的贵族对国王报以冷淡的掌声。自从马德里条约的条款泄露以来，整个王国就陷入了混乱，尽管当时还只是传言。这位法国人向皇帝低头，法国也随之沦陷！国王被俘后，失去意大利领土已成定局，但勃艮第！许多人宁愿接受弗朗索瓦二世的终身监禁，也不愿放弃这个公国。

Francis of France entered the royal hall of the Château d'Amboise with a solemnity akin to that displayed by Charles and Isabella upon their entry into Seville. But the enthusiasm of those present was nowhere near that of the crowd in the city on the Guadalquivir River. The monarch was greeted by lukewarm applause from the dozens of nobles who had been summoned. Disarray had spread throughout the kingdom since the clauses of the Treaty of Madrid had leaked, still only as a rumor. The Frenchman had humbled himself before the emperor, and with him, France! The loss of the Italian territories had been considered a foregone conclusion after the king's capture, but Burgundy! There were many who would have preferred to accept Francis's eternal imprisonment rather than surrender the duchy.

尽管气氛紧张，君主仍端坐于王位之上，神态凯旋。他的母亲萨伏依的路易莎站在他身旁，姿态如雄鹰般挺拔。在场众人惊愕不已，不禁怀疑他们的君主是否因卡斯蒂利亚的孤立而精神失常。弗朗西斯的一番讲话打断了他们的思绪。

Despite the tense atmosphere, the monarch took his seat on the throne, appearing triumphant. Standing beside him, his mother, Luisa of Savoy, stood poised like an eagle. Those present were bewildered, wondering if their sovereign had lost his mind due to Castilian isolation. Francis interrupted their thoughts with a speech.

——我的家乡，我的人民。能够再次见到你们，并且保持着我的尊严，我感到无比欣慰。

—My home. My people. What joy I feel to see myself before you, and with my pride intact.

贵族们交换着怀疑的眼神。国王的声音铿锵有力，仿佛他的囚禁经历只是一场噩梦。国王察觉到在场者的疑虑，脸上露出了笑容。

The aristocrats subtly exchanged skeptical glances. The king's voice sounded forceful, as if his captivity had been nothing but a nightmare. The king noticed the doubts of those present and a smile spread across his face.

“你以为我会为了自由出卖法国吗？你会为了重见天日而屈服于皇帝的贪婪吗？对我来说，死亡都比这甜蜜！”

"Do you think I would sell out France in exchange for my freedom? That I would submit to the emperor's greed just to see the light of day again? Death would have seemed sweeter to me!"

就像有人藏着一张王牌，急切地等待着出牌后的效果一样，弗朗西斯停下来观察他的观察对象。他知道，仅仅几秒钟后，那些疑虑的表情就会变成截然不同的样子。

Like someone holding back their best card, eagerly anticipating the effect of playing it, Francis paused to observe his subjects. He knew that in mere seconds those suspicious expressions would change to something quite different.

——法国贵族们，我在此对我在马德里签署的条约提出质疑！

—Nobles of France, the treaty I signed in Madrid is hereby challenged!

在场的人几乎都忍不住发出赞叹的“哦！”

Few among those present could stifle an admiring "Oh!"

“没错，我的确签了字，”君主继续说道，“但我是在胁迫下签的，因为皇帝强迫我要么签字，要么就接受永世监禁。而未经自由意志的决定，根本毫无约束力！”

“I did sign it, yes,” the monarch continued, “but I did so under duress, for the emperor forced me to choose between signing it or condemning myself to eternal imprisonment. And what is not decided freely, binds nothing!”

贵族们的钦佩之情化作一阵狂热的掌声。他们为能侍奉这样一位即便损害王国利益也毫不畏惧法律的人而感到自豪。

The aristocrats' admiration erupted in a frenzy of applause. They were proud to serve a man so admirably disdainful of legality if it harmed the kingdom.

国王万岁！

—Long live the king!

那声呐喊，出自一位深受感动的贵族之口，反复回荡，热情似火，深深触动了弗朗西斯。自从从西班牙归来，这位君主的精神似乎比以往更加脆弱。他在卡斯蒂利亚阴暗寂静的牢房中忍受的孤独，似乎使他的灵魂变得异常敏感。如同长期失明之人重见光明，这充满喧嚣与情感的世界对他而言已变得过于强烈。在马德里被囚禁期间，他曾设想过截然相反的情景：如果能够重返故土，他将以双倍的勇气和活力行事，并以比以往更加炽热的热情热爱生活，因为已经经历了最艰难的处境，他将不再恐惧。然而，当他踏入家门的那一刻，喜悦之后，随之而来的是想要远离尘嚣的渴望，想要回到自己的牢房——如今，这已不再是真正的牢房，而是精神上的牢笼——就像家畜在乡间漫步之后，为了躲避自由的危险而回到主人身边一样。

The cry, born of a deeply moved nobleman, was repeated so often and with such fervor that it stirred Francis. Since his return from Spain, the sovereign's spirit seemed more vulnerable than usual. The solitude he had endured in the shadowy and silent Castilian cell appeared to have sensitized his soul. Like blindness to one who has been deprived of it for a long time, the world, with its orgy of events and emotions, had become too intense for him. During his confinement in Madrid, he had imagined the exact opposite: that upon his return, if it came to pass, he would behave with twice the courage and energy, and that he would love life with even greater fervor than before, free from all fear thanks to having already suffered the worst of circumstances. But when he stepped back into his home, the joy was followed by a need to shelter from the rest, to return to his cell, now spiritually—like the domesticated animal that, after a walk in the countryside, returns to its master to avoid the dangers of freedom.

“但是……”国王庆幸自己不得不打断欢呼声继续讲话；如果他继续听下去，恐怕会泪流满面。“基督教导我们要宽恕，因为和平是我们的宗旨。出于对囚禁我、如今又囚禁我孩子的那个人的宽容，”他说道，在场众人为幼小的婴儿祈祷，划了个十字，“我同意履行协议中的部分条款，我已经将这些条款告知了基督教世界以及其他相关人士……”

“But…” The king was grateful to have to cut short the cheers to continue his speech; had he continued listening to them, he would have burst into tears. “Christ taught us to forgive, for peace is our purpose. Out of generosity toward the one who imprisoned me and now holds my children captive,” he said, and those present crossed themselves for the health of the little infants, “I agree to fulfill some of the clauses of the agreement, which I have already reported to Christendom, and to whomever else may be concerned…”

 

 

 

 

如果说有人真正关心弗朗西斯为自己设想的未来，那非埃莉诺莫属。查理的妹妹在卡斯蒂利亚北部等待法国大使馆接她前往新家时，收到了丈夫的来信。如今，王位理应属于她。然而，这位法国君主在信中重申了婚约，却对皇帝充满了怨恨，并表达了反抗条约大部分条款的意愿，尤其强烈反对割让勃艮第。埃莉诺意识到，她当初拒绝嫁给叛徒波旁公爵，却最终嫁给了罪大恶极之人。事实上，她已经很久没有哭过了，所以只是苦涩地笑了笑：在爱情方面，她似乎总是被诅咒。这时，她胸口一阵悸动，令她猝不及防：那感觉，如同离开里斯本时一样，再次涌上心头，那是她女儿的心跳，是她分娩时感受到的那份渴望被呵护的小生命跳动，也是她生命中最美好的体验。过去几个月里，埃莉诺努力麻木自己，不去想失去女儿的痛苦。法国问题对她来说反而是一份礼物，因为无论弗朗西斯是否信守诺言，埃莉诺的生命注定要经历革命，这足以让她思绪万千。然而，当失去女儿的痛苦最终袭来时——这种痛苦总是毫无预兆地袭来，如同突如其来的悲伤将她彻底淹没——查尔斯的妹妹会将注意力转移到任何事上，无论多么荒谬，她都会努力去关注，仿佛那是生死攸关的大事；仿佛它比与独生女分离更重要。她如此无力——她怎能否认葡萄牙王室对小玛丽亚的权利？——以至于抗争似乎毫无意义。唯一能让她不至于悲痛欲绝的办法，就是假装自己从未为人母。很久以前，她偶尔才会梦见自己握着一个幼小孩子的手。

And if anyone cared about the future Francis envisioned for himself, it was Eleanor. Charles's sister received her husband's letter while waiting in northern Castile to be picked up by a French embassy that would take her to her new home, whose throne was now rightfully hers. But the French monarch's words, while reaffirming the marriage agreement, poured venom against the emperor and a desire for rebellion against most of the treaty's points, with particular vehemence, of course, regarding the cession of Burgundy. Eleanor realized that she had refused to marry a traitor, the Duke of Bourbon, only to marry the greatest of felons. The truth was, she hadn't cried in a long time, so she simply smiled melancholically: she was cursed when it came to love. Then she felt something in her chest that startled her: it was, once again, as when she had left Lisbon, the memory of her daughter's heartbeat, that needy little animal's throb she had felt the moment she gave birth, and which had been the most beautiful experience of her life. During the last few months, Eleanor had worked hard to numb herself to the memory of her little girl. The French question had been a gift, for whether Francis kept his word or not, the fact remained that Eleanor's existence was destined for revolution, and that provided her with plenty to occupy her thoughts. When, despite everything, the pain of loss reached her—and it always came unannounced, in the form of a sudden attack of sadness that overwhelmed her with despair—Charles's sister would redirect her thoughts to any matter, however ridiculous, striving to attend to it as if it were a question of life or death; as if it were more important than having been separated from her only daughter. Such was her powerlessness—how could she deny the Portuguese Crown its right to little Maria?—that fighting seemed pointless. The only thing that could keep her from going mad with grief was pretending she had never been a mother. Only occasionally, long ago, had she dreamed of clasping the hand of a tiny child.

想到女儿的安危，莱昂诺尔心灰意冷，甚至没有征求皇帝的意见，就决定不再等待法国使节——她非常担心使节永远不会到来。她语气急切地向府邸的官员喊话。

Her spirits crushed by the thought of her daughter, and without even consulting the emperor, Leonor decided to stop waiting for the French embassy, ​​which, she greatly feared, would never arrive. She addressed the officer at her residence with an urgent tone.

——我们要去皇帝所在的地方。

—We are leaving for wherever the emperor is.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，查理正前往格拉纳达。他决定弥补婚礼的冷清，带妻子去看看据说是整个王国最美丽的城市。如果运气好的话，他的蜜月之旅或许能回报伊莎贝拉带给他的所有幸福。他几乎无法忍受与她分离，国事突然变得枯燥乏味得令人难以忍受；他在开会时努力克制自己不打哈欠，更努力克制自己不去想妻子，因为妻子的身影让他更加渴望她，以至于他无法专注于其他任何事情。阿尔瓦公爵记不清自己是否曾如此痴迷于她，最终对查理的需求越来越少，因为国王在这种情况下几乎无能为力。这使得查理可以日夜沉浸在爱人的怀抱中，给予她应得的爱，因此，仅仅几天后，他就决定将宫廷“无限期”迁往格拉纳达。

Meanwhile, Charles was on his way to Granada. He had decided to make up for the lackluster wedding ceremony by showing his wife what was said to be the most beautiful city in the entire kingdom. With luck, his honeymoon might repay Isabella for all the happiness she was bringing him. He could scarcely bear to be apart from her, and affairs of state had suddenly become unbearably dull for him; he struggled to keep from yawning during councils, and even more so to keep his mind from picturing his wife, which inflamed his desire to the point of preventing him from attending to any other matter. The Duke of Alba, who could not remember ever being so enamored, ended up requiring less and less attention from him, because the king was of little use in that state. This allowed Charles to be consumed day and night by his beloved and the devotion she deserved, and thus he decided to move the court to Granada "indefinitely" after only a few days.

“我的祖父母真有福气，他们为西班牙赢得了这个奇迹。”卡洛斯一边说着，一边走进了阿尔罕布拉宫。

—Blessed are my grandparents, who won this miracle for Spain— said Carlos as he entered the Alhambra.

狮子庭院以舒缓的声音迎接皇帝和他的妻子——喷泉的潺潺流水声、春风的轻拂、小鸟的婉转鸣唱。伊莎贝拉曾以为世上再也找不到像皇家阿尔卡萨宫那样令人叹为观止的地方，如今却被眼前的美景惊得说不出话来。仿佛他们刚一靠近，她就被眼前的景色深深震撼。当她从马车上看到阿尔罕布拉宫时，萨比卡山的夜幕已经降临。疲惫的夕阳缓缓落下，余晖洒在石头上，使这座建筑宛如一颗从山坡植被中生长出来的巨大红宝石。查理看到妻子沉醉的目光，不禁微笑起来，拥抱她，一同欣赏这安达卢西亚的奇观。他被眼前的景象深深震撼，屏住了呼吸。在她漫长的旅途中，她见过无数令人心旷神怡的宏伟建筑和风景，但这是她第一次感受到如此神奇的景象，仿佛置身于梦幻世界，而非现实。多日之后，她的目光不再被伊莎贝尔所吸引，而是转向了其他事物。

The Court of the Lions welcomed the emperor and his wife with soothing sounds—the murmur of its fountains and the spring breeze, the gentle trilling of tiny birds. Isabella, who had thought it impossible to ever find a place as sublime as the Royal Alcázar, was speechless before the beauty that surrounded her. It seemed as if they had barely approached the place before it had dazzled her. When she caught sight of the Alhambra from her carriage, evening was falling over the Sabika hill. The weary sun bid farewell, its light tinging the stone until the structure resembled an enormous ruby ​​born from the hill's vegetation. Charles, who smiled upon recognizing his wife's rapt gaze, embraced her to contemplate the Andalusian marvel and, as he did so, he was left breathless. In her many travels, she had seen imposing buildings and landscapes that calmed the soul, but this was the first time a building had struck her as so magical, like a scene from a fantasy, never a reality. After many days, her eyes delighted in something other than Isabel.

进入阿尔罕布拉宫后，他们手牵手漫步于各个房间，心中充满了惊奇。在科马雷斯大厅，皇后抬头仰望穹顶及其上雕刻的宇宙图景。就在那一刻，她突然泪流满面。查理大为震惊，也由此领悟到爱情之泪的力量。

Once inside the Alhambra, they wandered hand in hand through its rooms, their sense of wonder growing. In the Hall of Comares, the Empress raised her gaze to the dome and the representation of the universe carved upon it. It was then that she burst into tears. Charles was alarmed, and thus he understood the power of the tears of one who loves.

-你这人怎么回事？

—What's wrong with you?

—我明白了。我现在懂了。

—I understand. Now I get it.

皇帝困惑不解，疑惑地看着她。

The emperor, bewildered, looked at her questioningly.

——我哥哥对莱昂诺尔的感情。不真实的幸福。以及失去她后的巨大痛苦。我从未拥有过如此珍贵的东西，以至于害怕失去。告诉我，我亲爱的，我现在拥有它了吗？

—What my brother felt for Leonor. Unreal happiness. And the profound pain of having lost her. I have never possessed anything so precious as to fear its loss. Tell me, my beloved, do I possess it now?

伊莎贝尔等待着答案。卡洛斯凝视着她清澈的双眸，泪水也无法玷污那双眼睛。那一刻，仿佛那并非他自己的记忆，那种一直萦绕着他的永恒孤独感再次袭来，伴随着缺乏温暖情感的痛苦，那种无法被任何情绪淹没的煎熬。尽管与伊莎贝尔相处的短短几天，他周身的空虚感却已消散，是的，他终于开始害怕失去像她一样的人。

Isabel waited for the answer. Carlos gazed into her clear eyes, which not even tears could mar. At that moment, as if the memory weren't his own, that feeling of perpetual loneliness that had always haunted him came back to him, along with the anguish of being devoid of warm connections, of emotions that could overwhelm him. Despite the few days he had spent with Isabel, that aura of emptiness around him had vanished, and yes, at last, he was terrified at the prospect of losing someone like himself; her.

“我一直渴望嫁给你，”她继续说道，“我希望我们的结合会幸福美满，充满理解和爱意。仅此而已。”皇帝在妻子的感受中看到了自己的影子。他们是两个陌生人，却彼此融为一体。“与你在一起的幸福真的如此美好吗？还是这不过是一场幻觉？”

“I always longed to marry you,” she continued. “I hoped our union would be happy, filled with understanding and affection. Nothing more.” The emperor saw himself reflected in his wife’s feelings. They were two strangers experiencing each other as one. “Is the happiness that awaits me with you so great? Or is this nothing more than an illusion?”

“我一直在问自己同样的问题，”他回答说。

"I ask myself the same thing all the time," he replied.

他们彼此对视。两人似乎都被一种既着迷又焦虑的复杂情绪所淹没，如同死而复生之人一般，既为命运的恩赐而欣喜若狂，又怀疑如此非凡之事是否真的存在。直到阿尔巴公爵到来，告知他们有随从跟随，才将他们从那只有彼此和彼此感受的私密世界拉了出来。

They looked at each other. Both seemed overwhelmed by fascination and anxiety, the same feeling a resurrected person might have, exultant at the gift bestowed by fate yet doubtful that something so extraordinary was possible. Only the arrival of the Duke of Alba, informing them that a retinue had followed them, pulled them from that intimate world where only they and their feelings mattered.

“是你姐姐的随从，”公爵说道，这让皇帝感到困惑不解。

"Your sister's entourage," said the duke, to the emperor's bewilderment.

 

 

 

 

读完弗朗西斯科的信——正是这封信将莱昂诺尔带到了格拉纳达——卡洛斯沉默不语。他召集了议会，在前往会议的途中，他穿过阿尔罕布拉宫的各个房间，不再留意那些曾经令他着迷的装饰，这些装饰如今却成了他痛苦的背景。他心中的愤慨太过强烈，难以言表，只能借助时间的沉淀来压抑，直到他走进阿尔巴公爵、他的孙子费尔南多和波旁公爵等候他的房间，才能最终爆发出来。

After reading Francisco's letter, which had brought Leonor to Granada, Carlos remained silent. He summoned the council and, on his way to the meeting, crossed the rooms of the Alhambra, no longer paying any attention to the decoration, which had once fascinated him but had become a mere backdrop to his anguish. The indignation he felt was too intense to be expressed, and it had to be tempered by that lapse of time so that, once in the room where the Duke of Alba, his grandson Fernando, and the Duke of Bourbon awaited him, it could finally erupt.

弗朗西斯科是最卑鄙的人！

—Francisco is the most vile of men!

“他把自己的背叛包装成仁慈，向你提出新的交易，”法德里克轻蔑地插话道。

—And he sells his betrayal as benevolence by offering you a new deal—Fadrique interjected contemptuously.

——又侮辱我！你以为只要你交出孩子的赎金我就满意了吗？还是只要你信守和莱昂诺尔的婚约我就满意了？

—Another insult! Do you think I'll be satisfied with a ransom for your children? Or with you keeping your engagement to Leonor?

“他很清楚你不会答应他的要求，”波旁家族的人宣称，“他只是在等你拒绝，好把责任推卸给你，好让他的复仇显得合情合理。”

"He knows full well that you will not comply with his wishes," the Bourbon declared. "He is only waiting for your refusal so that he can blame you, and so that his revenge will appear legitimate."

法国人说话时语气笃定，令在场的人不寒而栗。

The Frenchman spoke with a certainty that chilled the blood of those present.

“你认为他有能力把最近签署的和平协议变成战争吗？”阿尔巴公爵震惊地问道。

"Do you think he is capable of turning a recently signed peace into war?" asked the Duke of Alba, scandalized.

对付他最好的办法就是做好最坏的打算。

—The best defense against him is to expect the worst.

这次背叛深深震撼了查尔斯，他知道自己不能再拖延回应这种侮辱。如果说他之前对弗朗西斯过于信任，那么现在悲观情绪和强硬的回应将成为他最有力的武器。

The betrayal had shaken Charles to his core, and he knew he could not delay responding to this affront. If he had been too trusting of Francis, now pessimism and a forceful response would serve as his allies.

“再次启程前往意大利，”皇帝命令波旁王子。“让我们的军队保持警惕。如果那个叛徒把这套歪理邪说告诉了整个欧洲，那是因为他想寻求支持，发动进攻。”

"Leave for Italy again," the emperor ordered the Bourbon prince. "Let our troops be on alert. If that traitor has told all of Europe this putrid version of events, it is because he seeks support for an attack."

出乎所有人意料的是，这位法国贵族发出了一声抱怨声，这对于一个臣民来说太过不合时宜，无论他的上级多么伟大。

To everyone's surprise, the French aristocrat made a complaining sound, unbecoming of a subject under the command of a superior, however great the former might be.

“服从您是我的义务，”他解释道，“但是您会履行您的义务，支付我将要带领的士兵们工资吗？他们被拖欠工资的时间太长了。”

“It is my duty to obey you,” he explained. “But will you fulfill your duty to pay the men I will lead? They have been denied their wages for far too long.”

“我们没有资金，”卡洛斯回答道，难掩心中的不安。

"We don't have the funds," Carlos replied, unable to hide his unease.

陛下，没有比为毫无意义之战的士兵更糟糕的士兵了。

—There is no worse soldier than one who fights for nothing, Your Majesty.

皇帝对法国人挑衅的语气感到不安，但更令他不安的是，法国人是对的。

The emperor was disturbed by the Frenchman's defiant tone, but even more so by the fact that he was right.

“我们会尽快给予他们补偿。我言出必行，杜克。”

"They will be compensated as soon as possible. And my word is my bond, Duke."

贵族无奈地点了点头，请求允许离开。他走出大厅的拱门时，正好与皇后相遇。皇后被阿尔罕布拉宫突然弥漫的紧张气氛所惊扰，想知道原因。这么多压抑的对话、这么多愤怒的举动、这么多僵硬的笑容，究竟是为了什么？

Resigned, the aristocrat nodded and asked for permission to leave. As he stepped out through the archway of the hall, he crossed paths with the Empress, who, alarmed by the sudden tension that had settled over the Alhambra, wanted to know the reason. What was the purpose of so many stifled conversations, so many angry gestures, so many frozen smiles?

“别担心。”这是她丈夫唯一的回答，同时还做了个手势，示意她让委员会来处理。

"Don't worry." That was her husband's only response, accompanying his words with a gesture that suggested she let the council do its work.

如果皇帝试图平息伊莎贝尔的怒火，结果却适得其反。

If he sought to calm Isabel's temper, the emperor achieved just the opposite.

 

 

 

 

后来，查尔斯在圣母无染原罪庭院找到了埃莉诺。当时已是夜幕降临，泳池里的水让原本就寒冷的气温更加刺骨。但她似乎丝毫感觉不到寒冷，因为她被水中倒映的塔楼的影像冻住了。

Later, Charles found Eleanor in the Court of the Immaculate Conception. It was already night, and the water in the pool made the already chilly temperature even cooler. But she didn't seem to feel the cold at all, for she was frozen by the reflection of the tower in the water's surface.

——人生就像这幅画。表面美丽，但……

—Life is like this picture. Beautiful on the surface, but…

莱昂诺尔跪下，将手伸进水池里。塔楼的倒影变得模糊不清。

Leonor knelt to dip her hand into the pool. The reflection of the tower blurred.

你与法国国王的婚事无法进行。很抱歉，但他的条件我无法接受。

—Your marriage to the King of France cannot go ahead. I'm sorry, but his conditions are unacceptable.

她点了点头；她不指望会有别的结果。她伫立凝视着水面，水面正缓缓地重构着塔楼的轮廓，那自然的韵律与人类的焦虑如此格格不入。

She nodded; she expected no other outcome. She stood gazing at the water, which was slowly reconstructing the image of the tower, with the rhythm of nature, so alien to human anxiety.

你有没有想起过梅赫伦？

—Do you ever think about Mechelen?

——当然。——卡洛斯做了一个富有感染力的手势，这与他平时的心情相符，这手势突然把他带回了童年的宫廷；他也想起了可怜的伊莎贝尔，上帝这么快就把她召到了他身边。

—Of course. —And Carlos adopted an evocative gesture, in keeping with his spirit, which suddenly transported him to the court of his childhood; he also remembered poor Isabel, whom God had called to his side so soon.

我多希望能够回到过去。那时我们的姐妹还活着。我们所有人都还拥有美好的未来，还没有经历过任何伤害。我已经不再记得希望了。

—I wish I could go back to then. That our sister were still alive. That we all still had our lives ahead of us, without anything having hurt us yet. I no longer remember hope.

池水再次平静下来，就在这时，莱昂诺尔颤抖了一下，仿佛池水的波涛抓住了她的身体。

The surface of the pool became still again, and just then Leonor trembled, as if the agitation of the water had taken hold of her body.

“未来只会带来更多悲伤，卡洛斯，”她虚弱地说，“我没有力量去面对。”

"The future will only bring more sorrow, Carlos," she said in a fragile voice. "I don't have the strength to face it."

你吓到我了。你不会是想冒犯上帝吧？

—You frighten me. You're not thinking of offending God, are you?

——更确切地说，是将自己交付于他。

—Rather, in surrendering myself to him.

皇帝走近妹妹，拥抱了她，这是他很久以来都没有做过的事。事实上，他们之间的矛盾与日俱增。埃莉诺或许太过敏感敏锐，不愿成为棋子，即便那是她的命运。但查尔斯比他自己承认的更了解她，他对她有一种超越其他任何家人的羁绊。他意识到，维系他们之间的纽带比他现在与伊莎贝拉之间的纽带更加复杂、更加不安，但也因此更加珍贵。

The emperor approached his sister and embraced her as he hadn't done in a long time. Truthfully, the conflicts between them were only multiplying. Eleanor was perhaps too sensitive and perceptive to be a pawn in the game, even if that was her destiny. But Charles, who understood her better than he had ever admitted, felt a bond to her like no other member of his family. He realized that the tie that bound them was more complex and uneasy than the one that now tied him to Isabella, but no less precious for that.

不，莱昂诺尔。不是因为弗朗西斯科。他的堕落无法束缚你。我为那份承诺感到愧疚。让我来弥补。我保证你会拥有美好的未来，以及一位好丈夫。

—No, Leonor. Not because of Francisco. His depravity cannot confine you. I blame myself for that commitment. Let me rectify it. I promise you a good future, and a good husband.

皇帝听到妹妹粗重的呼吸声和撕心裂肺的哭泣，心中不禁一阵震颤。他知道，虽然妹妹从未提及，但她留在葡萄牙的女儿带给他的痛苦远胜过法国人的任何轻蔑，但他还是没有提起这件事，因为他甚至不确定自己能否平静地处理它。

The emperor was then shaken to hear his sister's ragged breathing, the sound of her most heartfelt weeping. He knew that, though it wasn't mentioned, the daughter she had left behind in Portugal caused him even more suffering than any disdain from the Frenchman, but he refrained from bringing it up, because he wasn't even sure he could handle the matter with composure.

“我厌倦了伤害自己的人民，”卡洛斯说。

—I'm tired of hurting my own people— said Carlos.

莱昂诺尔松开拥抱，看着哥哥的眼睛。

Leonor broke the hug to look her brother in the eyes.

—所以他们说的是真的：你恋爱了。你比以前更好了。

—So it's true what they say: you've fallen in love. You're a better man than you were before.

虽然这句话让卡洛斯脸上露出了笑容，但自从认识妻子以来，卡洛斯第一次感到一丝不自在，因为他想到了自己的妻子。

Although the comment brought a smile to his face, for the first time since he had known her, Carlos felt uncomfortable thinking about his wife.

——别告诉他弗朗西斯的事。求你了。

—Don't tell him what happened with Francis. I beg you.

 

 

 

 

当晚，皇帝离开了他们的婚床。第二天，他以政务繁忙为由——这说法只说对了一半——避开了伊莎贝拉。查理突然与他们疏远，令皇后痛苦万分。她最害怕的事情似乎正在发生：他们初婚时的幸福不过是幻象：正如她经常从不幸的妻子口中听到的那样，丈夫为了赢得妻子的爱而做出的妥协。一旦他们确信妻子忠贞不渝，便会重拾自己的事业和抱负，而渴望得到他们关注的妻子们，只要得到一点好意便心满意足，放弃了她们最初以为能在婚姻中获得的完全幸福。伊莎贝拉在葡萄牙宫廷听到这些故事时，对这种女性的顺从和轻易满足感到震惊。她绝不会用爱换取冷漠！如今，她害怕自己正在步那些女人的后尘。但她的尊严告诉她，她还有时间避免陷入平庸的日常生活中。因此，一天晚上，她神情坚定地走向查理，令他不敢忽视她。当皇帝坦白了疏远她的原因后，伊莎贝尔既感到如释重负，又感到义愤填膺。

That night, the emperor left their marital bed. The next day, he avoided Isabella with the excuse—only partly true—that he was occupied with numerous matters of state. The sudden distance Charles placed between them caused the empress terrible distress. Her greatest fear seemed to be coming true: the happiness she had shared with him during their early days had been nothing but an illusion: that concession which, as she had so often heard from unhappily married women, husbands made to win their wives' love. As soon as they were certain of their wives' devotion, they returned to their world of tasks and ambitions, and the women, eager for their attention, were then content with any kind gesture, renouncing the complete happiness they had initially believed possible in their marriage. When Isabella heard these stories at the Portuguese court, she was astonished by this feminine docility, so easily satisfied. She would never give love in exchange for indifference! Now she feared she was following in the footsteps of those women. But her dignity told her she still had time to avoid falling into mediocre routines, and for that reason, one night she approached Charles with such a determined expression that he dared not ignore her. When the emperor confessed the cause of his estrangement, Isabel experienced both great relief and indignation.

—你怎么会认为我会因为那个法国人的卑鄙而责备你呢？

—How could you have thought that I would reproach you for the meanness of the Frenchman?

很明显，卡洛斯对整件事感到很尴尬。他的目光在地板的两侧来回游移，竭力避开她的目光。

It was clear that Carlos was embarrassed by the whole thing. His gaze darted from one side of the floor to the other, as he did his best to avoid hers.

“若非我的纯真，他的卑劣行径毫无价值。许多人都警告过我提防他，但我拒绝相信。而如今，全世界都在嘲笑我的天真。”

"His vileness would have been worthless without my innocence. Many warned me against him, but I refused to believe them. And today the whole world laughs at my tenderness."

“你是不是也怕我嘲笑你？”她问道。“从这件事来看，我只得出一个结论：你是个好人。”

—And were you afraid that I would make fun of you too? —she said—. From what happened I only conclude one thing: that you are a good man.

伊莎贝尔，你难道看不出来，在这个什么都可能发生的世界里，这让我显得很软弱吗？

—Isabel, don't you see that makes me a weak man in this world where anything goes?

那一刻，她意识到，正是丈夫的这份善良，让她从一开始就感受到，并最终爱上了他。或许是那双清澈明亮、充满好奇与温柔的眼睛让她发现了这一点；或许是他言谈举止的尊重和简洁，与许多男人的傲慢和滔滔不绝截然相反；或许是卡洛斯带给她的那种平静，一种卑劣的男人无法传递给身边人的感受。她的丈夫拥有至高无上的荣耀，但真正让他与众不同的，是他的品德，这让她既感到无比幸运，又害怕失去他。

At that moment, she realized that it was precisely this—her husband's kindness—that she had sensed from the very beginning and that had led her to love him. Perhaps it had been those clear eyes that gazed at the world with curiosity and gentleness that had revealed it to her; or perhaps she had discovered it in the way he spoke, respectful and laconic, the opposite of the arrogant verbosity of so many men; or perhaps it had been revealed to her in the feeling of peace that Carlos evoked in her, an effect that vile men were incapable of transmitting to those around them. Her husband possessed an imperial crown, but it was his virtue that distinguished him from the rest, and that made her feel so fortunate and so afraid of losing him.

——没有什么能阻止你既保持美德，又从错误中吸取教训。不要把你的高尚品格拱手让给叛徒。要守护好它！这世上不需要更多卑鄙小人，我也不想嫁给这样的人。

—Nothing prevents you from being virtuous and at the same time learning from your mistakes. Do not give your nobility to the traitor. Preserve it! The world does not need more petty men, nor do I want one for a husband.

从她的语气中，卡洛斯知道她没有撒谎。如果他变成另一个人，或许她再也不会像以前那样看待他了，而他需要那种欣喜若狂的感觉，就像需要空气一样。

From her tone, Carlos knew she wasn't lying. If he became someone else, perhaps she would never look at him the same way again, and he needed that rapture as much as he needed air.

——以后别再让我免受你的烦恼了。你越是回避我的痛苦，就越会让我更加痛苦。

—And don't ever spare me from your troubles again. By avoiding my discomfort, you cause me greater pain.

皇帝点了点头。

The emperor nodded.

“我并不擅长言辞。但是，预料到你会生气，我想到了一个不用开口就能获得你原谅的办法。”

"I'm not a man skilled with words. But, anticipating your anger, I thought of a way to gain your forgiveness without even speaking."

“哪一个？”她带着真切的好奇问道。

"Which one?" she asked with genuine curiosity.

卡洛斯牵起伊莎贝尔的手，领她来到阿尔罕布拉宫的一个庭院。庭院角落里摆放着几个花盆。伊莎贝尔看着它们，却发现里面只有黑土。

Carlos then took Isabel's hand and led her to one of the courtyards of the Alhambra. There, in a corner, were several flowerpots. Isabel looked at them, but saw that they contained nothing but dark earth.

它们很快就会发芽。

—They will sprout soon.

-你是什么意思？

—What do you mean?

——我从波斯带了一些花来，以示对您的敬意。我知道，这只是平息您怒火的拙劣伎俩。

—Some flowers I had brought from Persia in your honor. A poor trick to appease your anger, I know.

伊莎贝尔强忍着泪水。那一簇花盆里蕴藏着美好的希望，在她看来，这是最好的礼物。

Isabel had to hold back her tears. That clump of flowerpots, which held within it the promise of something beautiful, seemed to her the best of gifts.

—我恳求您，大人，永远不要改变您本来的样子。

—I beg you, my lord, never stop being the man you are.

她激动得嘴唇颤抖，皇帝的吻如同抚慰的良药般让她感到舒畅。

Her lips, trembling with emotion, received the emperor's kiss like a balm.

 

 

 

 

事实上，弗朗西斯的背叛确实粉碎了查理的幸福，但格拉纳达远离任何战场或外交场所，而阿尔罕布拉宫的宁静氛围使人得以相对化任何冲突的重要性。战前的紧张气氛主要集中在法国宫廷，但渐渐地也蔓延到了教廷。教皇克莱门特在法国大使的劝说下，加入了一个旨在惩罚查理的联盟，理由是“他先是残害了弗朗西斯，然后又残害了他的孩子们”。这些孩子仍然处于皇帝的监护之下，却被法国人无耻地利用来煽动潜在盟友的情绪，而事实上，他们的父亲并没有因为无视《马德里条约》而危及子女的安全。毫无疑问，弗朗西斯正是料到查理看起来不会做出任何伤害他人的事：如果他都对自己仁慈，又怎能对无辜的孩子如此残忍呢？但对于罗马和伦敦，他却始终保持着平静，就像一位父亲害怕皇帝会对“他的孩子们”造成什么伤害一样。

The truth was that Francis's betrayal had shattered Charles's happiness, but Granada was too far removed from any battlefield or diplomatic hall, and the Alhambra possessed a soothing quality that led one to relativize the significance of any conflict. The pre-war nervousness was concentrated entirely in the French court, but little by little it spread to the Holy See as well, where Pope Clement allowed himself to be persuaded by the French ambassadors to join a league that would punish Charles for "the intolerable cruelty shown first to Francis, and then to his children." The children, who remained under the emperor's guardianship, were shamelessly used by the French to inflame the passions of their potential allies, when in fact their father had done nothing to endanger his offspring by disregarding the Treaty of Madrid. Undoubtedly, Francis counted on Charles seeming incapable of causing any harm: if he had shown mercy to him, how could he act otherwise toward innocent children? But he certainly kept that tranquility to himself when it came to Rome and London, which he addressed like a father terrified of what the emperor might inflict on "his little ones".

总之，无论是法国君主子女的未来，还是围绕《马德里条约》的种种争论，实际上都不过是梵蒂冈、英国，当然还有法国，为他们急于做的事情——攻击皇帝并削弱其在欧洲的权威——寻找借口罢了。然而，这种一致行动却被英国国王的一时兴起所阻碍：他想借此机会实现他毕生的使命——与妻子凯瑟琳离婚。亨利自信满满地命令沃尔西与教皇谈判此事，并将离婚作为英国加入反查理联盟的必要条件。而教皇，一如既往地热衷于那些道德可疑的条约，只要他能自由设定例外条款，并且从不强迫自己，因此拒绝了这一提议。沃尔西不遗余力地试图改变亨利的想法，因为近来亨利不再像以前那样把他当作先知，甚至在某些问题上完全无视他的意见，完全依靠自己的意志做出决定。这位毕生致力于操控人心、对人性波动极其敏感的红衣主教，并没有将亨利这种新出现的独立性解读为必然的成熟，而是将其视为一种更为可怕的预兆：暴君的萌芽。亨利变得难以捉摸，他的言辞夸张浮夸，自由奔放，毫无道德可言。沃尔西不禁思忖，这种转变究竟有多少是他一手促成的；或许正是多年来对国王意志的执着掌控，最终迫使亨利彻底摆脱了束缚。事实上，这位大法官现在感到了威胁。他知道，年轻的博林在某种程度上是亨利的新顾问，或者至少是除了自己之外，国王唯一会听取意见的人。这位交际花——容貌姣好却毫不起眼，尽管自信满满——十分机敏地挫败了国王的性骚扰，使他始终对她依附。国王不善于辨别情感，却自以为是地认为自己感受到的是爱。再加上出于政治和家族原因，他想与凯瑟琳保持距离，离婚对他来说比以往任何时候都更加合情合理。此外，从博林那里——或者，如果这段爱情破裂，从其他任何人那里——他都能得到他所需要的继承人。

In any case, both the future of the French sovereign's children and all the back-and-forth regarding the Treaty of Madrid were, in reality, nothing more than pretexts to justify what the Vatican, England, and of course France were eager to do: attack the emperor and diminish his authority in Europe. However, such unanimity was hampered by a whim of the English king: to seize the opportunity to achieve the objective that had suddenly become his life's mission, which was none other than divorcing his wife, Catherine. Confident, Henry ordered Wolsey to negotiate the matter with the Pope, elevating it to the status of a necessary condition for his kingdom to join the coalition against Charles. And the Pontiff, who, as was customary for his office, was fond of pacts of dubious morality as long as he freely established the exceptions and never coerced himself, refused. Wolsey worked tirelessly to change Henry's mind, because lately Henry no longer listened to him as if he were an oracle, and even completely disregarded his views on certain matters, relying solely on his own will to make decisions. The cardinal, who was sensitive to the shifts in the vibrations of the human soul, having dedicated his life to manipulating them, did not interpret this newfound independence as inevitable maturity, but as something far more frightening: the genesis of a tyrant. Henry had become unpredictable, and his speech was bombastic and far too free to be moral. Wolsey wondered to what extent he had been the one to provoke this change; perhaps having so tenaciously dominated the king's will for years had finally forced Henry to emancipate himself in a radical way. The truth was, the chancellor now felt threatened. He knew that the young Boleyn was, in a way, Henry's new advisor, or at least the only person the monarch listened to other than himself. The courtesan—an attractive but unremarkable figure, though brimming with self-confidence—had been astute enough to thwart the monarch's sexual advances, thus keeping him in a perpetual state of dependence on her. The king, not adept at classifying emotions, had convinced himself that what he felt was love. This, coupled with his desire to distance himself from Catherine for political and familial reasons, had made divorce seem more logical to him than ever before. Besides, from Boleyn—or, if that love were to crumble, from any other—he would obtain the heir he needed.

在教皇克莱门特面前，沃尔西不得不像亨利本人一样假装相信他的论点，哪怕是最荒谬的——“陛下相信自己被全能的上帝判处不育，这无疑是对他与凯瑟琳结婚的惩罚。别忘了，她是他的兄弟的遗孀；他们的结合无异于乱伦！”——这种伪装毫无用处。罗马宁愿让英格兰落入对抗查理的联盟手中，也不愿屈服于这种明目张胆的操纵。

Before Pope Clement, Wolsey had to feign belief in Henry's arguments as much as Henry himself, even the most outlandish ones—"My lord believes himself condemned by the Almighty to infertility, undoubtedly as punishment for his marriage to Catherine. Remember that she is his brother's widow; their union is nothing short of incest!"—The charade was useless. Rome preferred to lose England to the league against Charles than to yield to such blatant manipulation.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在昂布瓦兹宫廷，亨利的诡计激怒了弗朗西斯。在他母亲看来，这愤怒远超其应得的程度。

Meanwhile, at the court of Amboise, Henry's trickery was met with fury by Francis. In his mother's eyes, with more fury than it deserved.

“一个不冷不热的盟友是完全没有必要的，”萨伏依的路易丝宣称，“我们有罗马，他们有威尼斯和佛罗伦萨。我们可以结成强大的联盟来对抗皇帝。”

"A lukewarm ally is never necessary," declared Louise of Savoy. "We have Rome, and they have Venice and Florence. A powerful alliance against the emperor."

“这是一个强大的联盟，但并非不可战胜，”法国国王回答道。

"A strong league, but not invincible," replied the French king.

——到底是哪一个？别再耽搁了，下令进攻！

—Which one is it? Don't delay any longer. Give the order to attack!

国王困惑地盯着母亲看了一会儿。虽然这些年来他们争吵过无数次，但这却是他第一次感到如此不被理解。从马德里回来的那个男人已经和以前不一样了，而她似乎并没有察觉，或者即使察觉了，也并不在意。

The monarch stared at his mother for a moment, puzzled. Although they had argued many times over the years, this was the first time he had felt so misunderstood. The man who had returned from Madrid was not the same as before, and she didn't seem to notice, or if she did, she didn't attach much importance to it.

“如果我这次做出了明智的决定，请原谅我，”他试图总结道。

"Forgive me if for once I decide sensibly," he tried to conclude.

“是感性……还是恐惧？”路易莎问他。

"Sensibility... or fear?" Luisa asked him.

弗朗西斯愤怒地回应。

Francis reacted angrily.

——害怕失败？害怕再次蒙羞？老天作证，当然！我宁愿死也不愿再经历一次同样的事。

—Afraid of defeat? Of being humiliated again? By God, yes! I'd rather die than go through the same thing again.

“你们必须让他为自己的罪行付出代价，不是通过外交手段，而是在战场上。如果这是你们最害怕的，那么它也将赋予你们勇气去执行这项任务。你们会收复失地，没错，但最重要的是，你们会重拾自我。”

"You must make him pay for his offense, not with diplomacy, but on the battlefield. If that is what you fear most, it will also be what fills you with courage to carry it out. You will recapture territories, yes, but above all, you will reclaim yourselves."

“你以为我在想别的事吗？”他回答道；他并没有撒谎，因为他知道，要想从他尚未挣脱的精神牢笼中逃脱出来，唯一的办法就是战胜他的狱卒。

"Do you think I'm thinking about anything else?" he replied; and he wasn't lying, for he was aware that the only way to escape from the spiritual prison from which he had not yet emerged was to defeat his jailer.

“那就快下定决心吧！”路易莎坚持道，“查理现在颜面尽失。欧洲人认为他天真地放走了你们，又卑鄙地囚禁了我的孙辈。没有人能阻止你们复仇！”

"Make up your minds, then!" Luisa insisted. "Charles is now a humiliated man. Europe considers him naive for letting you go free, and vile for keeping my grandchildren imprisoned. No one will stand in the way of your revenge!"

然而，弗朗西斯犹豫了，这反而加深了他的自我失望。他一想到自己身处战场，就感到窒息，并非因为长矛可能危及生命，也并非因为致命的火药会将尸体撕成碎片，而是因为又一次失败的可能性。眼前这位冷酷无情的女人，培养他就是为了让他取得胜利，也仅仅是为了她。失败，哪怕只有一次，对这位君主而言，都意味着对自身的否定。

However, Francis hesitated, and this only deepened his self-disappointment. He felt breathless when he imagined himself on the battlefield, not because of the lances that might endanger his life, or the lethal gunpowder that tore bodies to pieces, but because of the possibility of yet another defeat. This implacable woman before him had raised him for victory, and for her alone. Failure, even a single one, represented for the sovereign a denial of himself.

你别无选择。你已经违背了协议。如果你不反击，他迟早会反击，让你为这次冒犯付出代价。

—You have no choice. You have broken the agreement. If you don't attack, he will attack you sooner or later to make you pay for this offense.

君主一时之间思忖，如果他任由痛苦驱使自己去做——什么都不做——会发生什么。或许他应该容忍皇帝的毁灭；一旦一切都失去了，他就再也没有什么可畏惧的了。

For a moment the monarch wondered what would happen if he allowed himself to do what his anguish urged him to do: nothing. Perhaps he should tolerate the emperor's destruction; once everything was lost, he would have nothing left to fear.

他确实变成了一个懦夫。他为此感到无比厌恶自己。

He had certainly become a coward. And he despised himself for it.

 

 

 

 

一个月后，加蒂纳拉正从巴利亚多利德前往格拉纳达。马匹行进速度很快，因为命令要求他们尽快抵达目的地。他和查理就像一对明智的夫妻，决定暂时分开一段时间，因为在法国国王被俘期间，他们的争吵已经严重损害了彼此的关系。然而，法国和教皇的军队入侵意大利帝国据点的消息——弗朗西斯从中获得了力量——不仅为他们重聚提供了借口，更成为了他们再次并肩作战的充分理由。皇帝一见到加蒂纳拉，便急忙谦卑而迫切地请求他的原谅。

A month later, Gattinara was traveling the distance between Valladolid and Granada. The horses moved at a good pace, as orders dictated reaching their destination as quickly as possible. He and Charles, like a sensible couple, had decided to separate for a time, since their arguments during the French king's captivity had excessively strained their relationship. However, the news that both French and papal troops had invaded imperial positions in Italy—Francis finding strength in its use—was not only an excuse to reunite, but more than enough reason to work side by side again. The moment he saw him at the Alhambra, the emperor hastened to ask his forgiveness, with humility and urgency.

——你对弗朗西斯的看法是对的。请原谅我没有听从你的指导。

—You were right about Francis. Forgive me for not letting myself be guided by you.

这位意大利人并不乐意凌驾于他的君主之上；考虑到他们的地位，这种感觉显得不合情理，因此也显得有些粗暴。如果他曾因君主对法国人的天真而感到愤怒，那并非因为他的意见被忽视，而是因为他担心最终会发生的事情会发生：查理一世会在欧洲人面前受人嘲笑，被描绘成远不如他实际那样精明。

The Italian was not pleased to feel superior to his lord; it seemed unnatural given their rank and, therefore, violent. If he had been enraged by the monarch's naiveté toward the Frenchman, it was not because his opinion had been disregarded, but because he had feared that what ultimately happened would come to pass: that Charles would be ridiculed before Europe and portrayed as less astute than he truly was.

“我们不要浪费时间纠缠于过去。”说完，加蒂纳拉就化解了他们的分歧。“我们必须尽快对意大利发生的事情做出反应。”

"Let's not waste time dwelling on the past." And with that, Gattinara settled their differences. "We must react as soon as possible to what has happened in Italy."

皇帝眯起了眼睛。战争，又是战争。说实话，他之所以相信能与法国媾和，是因为他渴望这场冲突能彻底结束。他厌恶人们用野蛮的方式解决冲突，结果只会让冲突更加深重。战争不仅夺走士兵的生命，而且由于其代价高昂，交战国的民众也因赋税和动乱而饱受煎熬。作为统治者，他感到必须寻求任何解决办法，而不是继续这种局面。但显而易见，这取决于其他君主的意愿，而弗朗西斯对战争的嗜好仿佛已融入他的本性，他无法长久地背叛这种本性。他的领地又一次无法发展繁荣，反而浪费时间流逝在毫无意义的战争中，因为不久之后，他们就会意识到这场冲突的徒劳，于是签订一份永远不会遵守的条约来解决问题。很快，这个循环就会再次上演。

The emperor narrowed his eyes. War, war again. Truthfully, what had motivated him to believe in peace with France was his desire for the conflict to end once and for all. He was disgusted by the barbaric way men thought they could resolve conflicts, only to deepen them. War not only killed soldiers, but, given its cost, it stifled the populations of the warring kingdoms with taxes and unrest. As a ruler, he felt compelled to pursue any solution rather than this one, but, as seemed evident, this depended on the will of the other monarchs, and Francis's inclination toward battle was as if it were his very essence, something he could not betray for long. Once again, his domains, instead of developing and achieving prosperity, would waste time shedding young blood, something utterly pointless, for soon after, aware of the futility of the conflict, they would settle it with a pact that would never be honored. Soon, the cycle would repeat itself.

法国人的攻击激怒了他，但并不令他意外。令他难以置信的是，教皇竟然与他结盟。查理怀疑教皇是否真的相信了方济各攻击他的借口。相反，他担心——而且他的担心不无道理——这位主教是借此机会暴露了他对皇权的不满，这预示着一个危险的未来。

The Frenchman's attack infuriated him, though it didn't surprise him. What was inconceivable to him was that the Pope had allied himself with him. Charles doubted that the Pope had given credence to Francis's excuses for attacking him. Rather, he feared, and rightly so, that the prelate had taken advantage of the situation to reveal his disaffection with imperial authority, which foreshadowed a dangerous future.

“我的国库根本无力支付军队的薪饷，”查理焦急地补充道，“我每天都收到波旁公爵的来信，提醒我士兵们正嚷嚷着要领薪饷！我已经下令在卡斯蒂利亚筹集资金，但我不知道这些士兵的毅力还能坚持多久。如果他们放弃战斗，罗马和法国很快就会瓜分我的意大利领土，而且他们还会很快入侵其他地区。”

“And my coffers are incapable of paying the troops,” Charles added anxiously. “I receive a letter a day from the Duke of Bourbon reminding me that the troops are clamoring to be paid! I have ordered that the funds be raised in Castile, but I don’t know how long I can count on the stamina of these men. If they were to abandon the fight, Rome and France would soon divide my Italian territories between them, and they would soon invade others as well.”

“陛下，我毫不怀疑您的军队会忠于您。这场战争会让您的部下专注于保全性命。当您积蓄了足够的兵力后，请慷慨地奖赏他们。这件事您不必为此夜不能寐。”

"I have no doubt that your troops will be loyal to you, Your Majesty. The conflict will keep your servants focused on saving their own lives. When you have amassed enough, reward them generously. That matter should not keep you awake at night."

事实上，近来他忧心忡忡。他原本以为，得益于与法国的协议，自己会迎来一段悠闲的时光，然而现实却远非平静。尽管如此，他仍然尽力每天抽出尽可能多的时间陪伴妻子，尤其是在医生确认她怀上第一胎之后。他甚至与一些部下发生了冲突，他们恳求他将宫廷从格拉纳达迁回巴利亚多利德，因为在战火重燃之际，从那里管理资源和组织通讯会更加便捷。皇帝拒绝了这一提议，因为至少在最初几个月里，妻子的孕期并不顺利。而且，他必须悉心呵护这份他梦寐以求的母子情谊。这是查理的第三个孩子，然而，孩子的降生带给他的喜悦远胜于前两个孩子。这是合法的后代；或许，但愿是个男性继承人；而且，这也是他与伊莎贝拉结合的第一个结晶，是他一生中最幸福的结合。

In truth, everything had been worrying him lately. What he had assumed would be a period of leisure—thanks to the agreement with France—was far from tranquil. Despite this, he managed to dedicate as many hours a day as he could to his wife, even more so now that the physicians had confirmed her first pregnancy. He had even clashed with some of his own men, who begged him to return the court from Granada to Valladolid, from where it would be easier to manage resources and organize communications now that the war had once again taken hold. The emperor had refused such a move because the pregnancy, at least in its first months, was proving complicated. And he had to nurture this bond he had so longed to possess. This was Charles's third child, and yet the emotion of its arrival far surpassed that of the previous ones. It was legitimate offspring; perhaps, hopefully, a male heir, and it also represented the first fruit of his union with Isabella, the most blissful encounter of his life.

波斯的花朵很快盛开，安达卢西亚迎来了第一批康乃馨，这朵花最终会成为安达卢西亚人民无比钟爱的花朵。每天早晨，皇帝都会在妻子床边放一朵康乃馨，这样当她醒来时，看到的不是空荡荡的枕头，而是一朵花，提醒她，尽管他身处战火纷飞之中，但他对她的爱却始终如一。伊莎贝拉每次醒来，第一眼看到的都是那朵异域风情的花朵，鲜红欲滴，花瓣簇拥，宛如最精致的蕾丝；如此娇弱的花朵，却让她感到自己备受尊崇，仿佛刀枪不入。

The Persian flowers soon bloomed, and Andalusia saw its first carnations, which it would eventually embrace with such fervor. Every morning, the emperor placed one on the bed beside his wife, so that when she awoke she would not find an empty pillow, but rather a reminder that, though war occupied him, he loved her unconditionally. Isabella could not help but be moved each time she awoke and the first thing her eyes beheld was that exotic flower, so red, with its cluster of petals arranged like the most delicate lace; a fragile object that, nevertheless, made her feel revered and, therefore, invulnerable.

不久之后，当查理从帝国方面得知这令人震惊的消息时，他不禁疑惑命运究竟用了什么奇特的机制来弥补他之前过度沉溺的幸福。他与伊莎贝拉坠入爱河的喜悦，已被与法国的新冲突冲淡。如今，正当他为继承人的希望而欢欣鼓舞时，在他不在期间代行德意志统治的弟弟斐迪南却告知他，奥斯曼帝国的军队已兵临维也纳城下，随时准备在合适的时机发动进攻，开始征服欧洲的征程。如果说有什么噩梦能够将欧洲人团结在一起，那就是苏莱曼大帝——这位奥斯曼版的查理，以其好战和征服的野心而著称——的军队入侵的威胁。对于西方人而言，从北方大陆到地中海沿岸，奥斯曼帝国都代表着对他们信仰根基的威胁：基督教信仰。如果说一个人的价值在于其信仰的坚定程度，那么异教徒就如同行尸走肉，甚至更糟，拥有被毒害的、亵渎神灵的灵魂。土耳其人是基督徒的死敌，是他们的异端对应者，因此被认为拥有魔鬼般的邪恶。当欧洲人想象被穆斯林入侵的后果时，他们脑海中浮现出一幅末日景象：绑架、强奸和斩首——仿佛基督徒在战争中从未犯下过此类罪行。因此，当得知这两个文明距离与苏莱曼大帝的冲突仅一步之遥时，作为这个岌岌可危帝国的统治者，查理不仅惊慌失措，而且每个欧洲人都虔诚祈祷，恳求拯救他们的世界和他们自身。

Shortly afterward, when Charles learned the terrifying news from the Empire, he wondered what strange mechanism fate employed to compensate for his excesses of bliss. The joy of his falling in love with Isabella had been tempered by the new conflict with France. Now, as he celebrated the hope of an heir, his brother Ferdinand, who governed Germany in his absence, informed him that the armies of the Ottoman Empire had positioned themselves at the gates of Vienna, ready to attack at the opportune moment and begin their conquest of Europe. If any nightmare united Europeans, it was the threat of an invasion by the armies of Suleiman the Magnificent—that Ottoman version of Charles, distinguished by his bellicose and conquering drive. For Westerners, from those inhabiting the northern lands to those along the Mediterranean coast, the Ottomans represented a threat to what they considered their very essence: the Christian faith. If a man was defined by the firmness of his faith, an infidel was a soulless body or, even worse, one with a poisoned and sacrilegious soul. The Turk was the Christian's nemesis, his heretical counterpart, and was presumed, accordingly, to possess diabolical evil. When Europeans imagined the consequences of being invaded by the Muslims, they conjured up an apocalyptic landscape of abductions, rapes, and beheadings—as if Christians, in their wars, did not commit such crimes. Therefore, upon learning that the two civilizations were just one order away from clashing with Suleiman, not only did Charles, as ruler of the threatened empire, panic seize him, but every European offered fervent prayers begging for the salvation of their world and themselves.

对于哈布斯堡家族而言，这场战役并非一帆风顺。苏莱曼大帝之所以能够抵达维也纳多瑙河畔，是因为布达佩斯率先陷落。在那场战役——莫哈奇战役中，查理和斐迪南的妹妹玛丽亚成了寡妇，她的丈夫，匈牙利国王，为了阻止异教徒的推进而牺牲。这场战役对皇帝打击巨大，不仅是军事和政治上的重大挫败，也因为他与家族关系密切。事实上，妹妹伊莎贝拉的死让他深感愧疚。他知道当时自己本可以为她做更多，但他却因为自己的焦虑而拖延了援助。因此，尽管他不能将北方领土的命运听天由命，但他仍然希望玛丽亚和斐迪南都能得到他的支持。

The event was not without its share of drama for the Habsburg family. Suleiman the Magnificent had only reached the Viennese Danube because Budapest had fallen first. In that battle, the Battle of Mohács, Maria, a sister of Charles and Ferdinand, had been widowed, her husband, the King of Hungary, having perished trying to halt the infidel's advance. The event deeply affected the Emperor, as it was a major military and political setback, and also the close family member he was. In truth, the death of his sister Isabella had filled him with a profound sense of guilt. He knew he could have done more for her at the time, but he had done nothing but postpone her aid, consumed by his own anxieties. Therefore, even though he could not leave the fate of the northern territories to chance, he wanted both Maria and Ferdinand to have his support.

“我们别无选择，只管保卫维也纳。这不是一场掠夺之战，而是对我们身份和我们所信仰的神的威胁。”

"There will be no other undertaking than the defense of Vienna. This is not a war for plunder. It is a threat to who we are and to the God we pray to."

“你的决定无疑是虔诚的，”加蒂纳拉点头表示同意，“但我必须提醒你，这可能会带来后果。如果没有资金，我们在意大利的军队将拒绝作战。”

"Your decision is undeniably devout," Gattinara said with a nod of agreement, "but I must remind you of the consequences it may bring. Without funds, our troops in Italy will refuse to fight."

皇帝对他的警告感到困惑不解。

The emperor reacted with bewilderment to his warning.

“难道我们要在土耳其人进军维也纳之际，继续内讧吗？我会请求法国和罗马停战，他们不敢违抗我的命令。”

"Are we going to continue fighting amongst ourselves while the Turk advances on Vienna? I will ask France and Rome for a truce, and they will not dare to defy me."

-和…

-AND…

“我们会离开格拉纳达，”查理猜测道，“没有什么比与妻子分离更让我痛苦，但王位的重担必须大于联盟的重担。”

—We will leave Granada—Charles guessed. Nothing pains me more than parting from my wife, but the weight of the crown must be greater than that of the alliance.

几个小时后，伊莎贝尔下令准备她的行李：如果凯撒因不得不离开她而感到不安，那么她甚至没有考虑过在帝国如此危急的时刻离开他。

A few hours later, Isabel ordered that her luggage be prepared: if the Caesar was troubled by having to leave her in her condition, she did not even consider the possibility of leaving him at such a delicate moment for her Empire.

——没有我，你们就无法保卫维也纳。

—You will not work for the defense of Vienna without me.

“你们疯了吗？”卡洛斯回答道，他的目光落在了女孩隆起的肚子上，这是她身体的一个特殊之处，但她似乎对此毫不在意。

"Have you lost your minds?" replied Carlos, and his gaze fell upon the girl's bulging belly, an exceptional feature with which she seemed to live without alarm.

—我将乘坐上下铺旅行，如果需要休息，我将在沿途的村庄过夜。

—I will travel by bunk bed, and if I need to rest, I will spend the night in the villages along the way.

皇帝还没来得及回答，伊莎贝尔就用一个短暂的吻封住了他的嘴唇，但这足以让他心神不宁，打断他的思路。

Before the emperor could reply, Isabel sealed his lips with a very brief kiss, but it was enough to disconcert him and throw him off his train of thought.

我是国王的女儿和孙女。我深知这种严峻困境带来的痛苦。你们需要我。危在旦夕的不是你们的帝国，而是我们的帝国。

—I am the daughter and granddaughter of kings. I know the suffering that such grave difficulties bring. You will need me. It is not your Empire that is in danger: it is ours.

妻子的态度让卡洛斯既钦佩又担忧。他自然而然地想要保护她和她腹中的孩子，如同保护一个棉笼；但与此同时，他也深深地被爱人的品格所吸引，她慷慨大方，而且无可挑剔。他确信未来他们之间会有许多分歧，但他绝不会放过任何一个。

His wife's attitude stirred in Carlos equal parts admiration and concern. He naturally felt compelled to protect her and the child she carried, as if in a cotton cage, if possible; but at the same time, he was captivated by his beloved's character, so generous and, at once, impossible to contradict. He was certain the future held many disagreements for them, but he had no intention of forgoing a single one.

——女性既能养育孩子又能工作。难道我还需要提醒你你祖母的例子吗？

—Women can raise children and work. Do I need to remind you of your grandmother?

—你经常这样做，不仅仅是因为你姓他。

—You do it often, and not just because you bear his name.

他们相视一笑。

They smiled at each other.

——鲜花也会和我一起去。

—And the flowers will come with me.

 

 

 

 

然而，正如命运似乎总是让喜悦与逆境交织，伊莎贝拉的忠诚与奉献也并非没有与之相反的一面，而这恰恰体现在两个人身上：一个是法国人，另一个是罗马人。查理请求暂停战争，直到土耳其人被击败或阻止进军维也纳，但弗朗西斯和教皇克莱门特二世都置之不理。皇帝对此感到无比震惊。这位所谓的“最虔诚的君主”和教会领袖，怎能将争夺意大利领土的斗争置于阻止奥斯曼帝国的扩张之上？他们的行为如同最不敬神之人，完全不配身居要职。他们如此轻蔑，迫使查理独自一人去抵御苏莱曼的进攻。敌人的冷漠——他们似乎忘记了，一旦帝国落入土耳其人之手，他自己的领土也将很快遭受同样的命运——令他感到震惊、愤怒和忧郁。但他最终得出结论：上帝赋予他的使命是成为他信仰的唯一救世主。他决心接受这一挑战，即便这意味着失去意大利；即便这意味着毁掉一切，因为他仍然拥有基督徒的骄傲，而这种骄傲在方济各和教皇的灵魂深处正经历着一段微妙的时期。

However, just as fate seemed to balance joys with adversities, Isabella's loyalty and devotion were not without their opposite, in this case embodied in two figures: one French and the other Roman. Charles's request that the conflict be suspended until the Turk had been defeated or deterred from advancing on Vienna was ignored by both Francis and Pope Clement. The emperor was utterly astonished. How could the so-called Most Christian King and the leader of the Church prioritize the struggle for Italian lands over halting the Ottoman advance? They behaved like the most impious of men, both proving themselves unworthy of the positions they held. And, with their disdain, they forced him to undertake the feat of repelling Suleiman alone. The lack of solidarity from his enemies—who seemed to forget that, should the Empire fall into Turkish hands, his own territories would soon suffer the same fate—filled him with astonishment, anger, and melancholy, but he ultimately concluded that God had reserved for him the mission of being the sole savior of his faith. He would rise to that challenge, even if he lost Italy along the way; even if he ruined everything, because he would still have his Christian pride, that pride which was going through a delicate period in the souls of Francis and the Pope.

苏莱曼将他们置于进退两难的境地。当这位法国人请求土耳其援助以对抗查理时——这是一项秘密联盟，因为一旦泄露，法国人在基督教世界的威望将永远崩塌——他做梦也没想到后者竟敢入侵欧洲。如今，他无法应对这场入侵，否则他将背弃与奥斯曼帝国的协议，更重要的是，他还有可能被奥斯曼帝国揭露。这位“最虔诚的基督徒”国王竟然为了区区几块意大利土地而将自己卖给了土耳其人！如果消息传开，他恐怕连臣民的尊重都难以保全。即便如此，弗朗西斯的灵魂也并非完全麻木于自身的罪孽。自从得知此事后，他白天的冥想常常被悔恨的煎熬所打断，夜晚，他则反复梦见一个异教徒横行的欧洲，以及自己因纵容这种疏忽而遭受地狱之火的灵魂。然而，罪孽带来的痛苦似乎比他从西班牙归来时所感受到的那种失败主义情绪更容易忍受。他更希望英格兰而非土耳其人能与他并肩作战，但亨利八世（他一直否认与教皇凯瑟琳离婚）已置身事外。令他惊讶的是，苏莱曼一世除了要求若他攻占任何欧洲要塞不得被击退外，没有提出任何其他条件。弗朗西斯接受这一要求时，并不知道这个要塞竟是匈牙利王国，也不知道一旦得手，苏莱曼的意图便是继续西进。

Suleiman had placed them in a compromising situation. When the Frenchman requested Turkish aid to confront Charles—a clandestine alliance, since, if revealed, the Frenchman's prestige would crumble forever among Christendom—he never imagined that the latter would dare to advance into Europe. Now he could not respond to this invasion, or he would betray his agreement with the Ottoman and, more importantly, risk being exposed by him. The Most Christian King sold to the Turk for some Italian lands! He would be lucky if, should the news break, he could even retain the respect of his own subjects. Even so, Francis's soul was not entirely insensitive to his own unworthiness. Since learning of the situation, his daytime meditations were often interrupted by pangs of remorse, and at night he would relive the nightmare of an infidel Europe, and of his soul burning in hell for facilitating such negligence. However, the suffering that sin brought him seemed more bearable than the defeatism with which he had returned from Spain. He would much have preferred to have England on his side for this campaign rather than the Turks, but Henry, whose divorce from Catherine the Pope continued to deny, had distanced himself from the conflict. To his surprise, Suleiman had stipulated no condition other than that he not be repelled if he captured any European stronghold. When Francis accepted this requirement, he had no idea that this stronghold would be the Kingdom of Hungary and that, once secured, his intention was to continue advancing westward.

当然，教皇所承受的罪恶感远比那位法国人更加难以承受。如果他接受了土耳其人的帮助，哪怕是暗中协助，以巩固他与法国人结成的联盟，那不仅是因为他对查理的敌意，还因为一度有传言称，沃尔西枢机主教意图撼动教皇宝座，直至将克莱门特赶下台。亨利八世得出的结论是正确的：只有让他的顾问掌管教会，才能确保他梦寐以求的“离婚”得以实现。英国的阴谋很快便渗透到了梵蒂冈。教皇深知，只有军事行动的胜利才能确保他稳坐王位，因此他甚至愿意接受魔鬼作为盟友，所以并没有对苏莱曼不屑一顾。最终，英国人的意图也仅限于此——因为教会的阴谋远比暴风雨中织就的千张蜘蛛网还要复杂。但事实是，教宗已无法在联盟问题上退让。当他得知奥斯曼帝国征服匈牙利和围攻维也纳的消息后，他恳求法国人至少同意皇帝提出的停战请求。弗朗西斯的唯一回应是威胁要揭露克莱门特与苏莱曼的勾结。经过一番深思熟虑的沉默后，此事再也没有被提起。

Naturally, the guilt gnawing at the Holy Father was far more mortifying than that of the Frenchman. If he had accepted the Turk's assistance, even covertly, to the league he had formed with the Frenchman, it was not only because of his animosity toward Charles, but also because, for a moment, rumors arose that Cardinal Wolsey intended to shake the papal throne until he ousted Clement. Henry had reached the correct conclusion that only with his advisor at the head of the Church could the longed-for divorce be guaranteed, and English intrigues soon wound their way to the Vatican. Aware that only the success of his military campaign would secure his hold on the throne, the Pope would have accepted the devil himself as an ally, and thus did not turn his nose up at Suleiman. Ultimately, the British intention went no further than that—for an ecclesiastical conspiracy proved more complex to weave than a thousand spiderwebs in a storm. But the truth was that the Holy Father could no longer back down from his alliance. When he learned of the Ottoman conquest of Hungary and the siege of Vienna, he begged the Frenchman to at least grant the emperor's request for a truce. Francis's only response was to threaten to reveal Clement's collusion with Suleiman. After a thoughtful silence, the matter was never discussed again.

 

 

 

 

—我告诉过你我会忍受这段旅程。

—I told you I would endure the journey.

查理急忙拥抱妻子。他做梦也没想到，他的到来竟让巴利亚多利德宫廷瞬间变得温馨宜人，不再仅仅是军事要塞。皇帝殷勤地吩咐人送来一张软椅。伊莎贝拉坐下，抚摸着隆起的腹部——从肚子的大小来看，似乎不太可能再长大了——同时注意到丈夫疲惫的面容。

Charles rushed to embrace his wife. He would never have imagined that, with his mere arrival, the court of Valladolid would suddenly become habitable and warm, something more than just a center of military operations. The emperor, attentive, ordered that a soft seat be brought to him. Isabella sat down and, caressing her belly, which judging by its size seemed unlikely to grow any larger, noticed her husband's tired face.

“我日夜都在忙着筹款，”他坦言。

"Fundraising occupies me day and night," he admitted.

——你可以相信我为你争取到的一切。

—You can count on what I've obtained for you.

卡洛斯看着妻子，一脸茫然。

Carlos looked at his wife, not quite understanding.

“在我休憩的每一栋别墅里，我都为维也纳的事业筹集了资金，”她热情地说。

"In every villa where I've stayed to rest, I've raised funds for the Vienna cause," she said enthusiastically.

“而不是休息！” 这句责备再亲切不过了。

"Instead of resting!" Never was a more affectionate reproach uttered.

他不再生气了；那个女人只需一个微笑就能化解他的怒火。

He gave up on getting angry; that woman dissolved his outbursts with just a smile.

——所以西班牙已经了解了你的固执和魅力。

—So Spain already knows about your stubbornness and your charm.

伊莎贝尔微微一笑，眯起眼睛，再也掩饰不住疲惫。皇帝对她这突如其来的困倦感到不安，但他选择不去惊慌，只是轻轻吻了吻她的手。

Isabel smiled and squinted, unable to hide her exhaustion any longer. The emperor was unsettled by this sudden drowsiness, but he chose not to be alarmed. He simply kissed her hands.

安息吧，我的爱人。

—Rest, my love.

 

 

尊敬的神圣天主教皇帝陛下：恳请您以我所期望的严肃态度阅读我的信件。不要畏惧这场战争；胜利已在我们手中。但这并不能支付您的士兵的薪水。他们长期的困苦已化作愤怒。在佛罗伦萨，他们肆意掠夺财富，如今许多人扬言要进军罗马，夺取您扣留的财物。他们怒不可遏，我担心他们会像秃鹫一样攻击圣城。我也同样担心自己的性命，因为只有我才能阻止他们实现他们的目标。因此，陛下，我恳求您，在您的士兵变成野兽之前，支付他们的薪水。

Your Sacred Catholic Imperial Majesty: I beg you to read my letters with the gravity I intend them to have. Do not fear the battle; victory is with us. But this does not pay your troops. Their prolonged hardship has turned to rage. In Florence, they seized wealth without measure, and now many say they wish to advance on Rome and take from it the riches you withhold. They are incensed, and I fear they will attack the holy city like vultures. And I fear equally for my life, for I alone stand between them and their purpose. Therefore, I beg you, Your Majesty, to pay your men before they become beasts.

 

 

波旁王朝的查理公爵

CHARLES OF BOURBON , DUKE

 

 

加蒂纳拉和法德里克·德·阿尔巴原本以为皇帝会仔细考虑如何应对那位率领帝国军队在意大利作战的法国贵族。然而，令两位顾问惊讶的是，皇帝立即做出了决定。

Gattinara and Fadrique de Alba had assumed that the emperor would take his time deciding how to respond to the French nobleman, who was leading the imperial armies in the ongoing struggle in Italy. To the advisors' surprise, the imperial decision was immediate.

—我将命令部队保持克制。

—I will order the troops to exercise restraint.

“就这些吗？”加蒂纳拉惊讶地问道。

"Nothing more?" Gattinara asked, astonished.

“我该提防那些拒绝援助维也纳的人吗？”查理毫不犹豫地回答道，“教皇为停战做了什么？或者派兵支援我的兄弟了吗？”

"Should I look out for those who refuse to come to Vienna's aid?" Charles replied without hesitation. "Has the Pope done anything for a truce? Or offered troops to serve my brother?"

皇帝的高贵品格，以及他对他人高贵品格的期望，在他记仇的能力中显露出了另一面。如果他过分信任他人，那么他保护自己的唯一方法就是从错误中吸取教训；而记仇不正是如此吗？

The emperor's nobility, and the nobility he expected from others, revealed its other side in his capacity for holding grudges. If he trusted others more than he should, his only way to defend himself was by learning from his mistakes; and wasn't that precisely what grudges were?

“如果我必须独自保卫维也纳，我会把我的金币留作此用。即使这会激怒我在意大利的军队。这是罗马的旨意。”

"If I must defend Vienna alone, I will save my ducats for that purpose. Even if it inflames my troops in Italy. That is Rome's will."

卡洛斯的语气不容置疑。

Carlos's tone left no room for opposition.

“陛下，幸好西班牙人民以极大的慷慨支持了这项事业。如果奥斯曼帝国能够被阻止，很大程度上要归功于这个王国对信仰的坚定不移。”

"Fortunately, Your Majesty, the Spanish have embraced the cause with overwhelming generosity. If the Ottomans are stopped, it will be largely due to this kingdom's commitment to its faith."

皇帝深深地感动着，点了点头。他与伊莎贝拉的恋情发展得如此迅速，以至于他几乎没注意到自己也爱上了西班牙。在他们的婚礼和蜜月期间，王国仅仅是他爱情的平静背景。卡斯蒂利亚王国曾是令皇帝忧心忡忡的土地，如今，那些日子仿佛已是遥远的记忆。现在，没有任何领地能比这里更让他感到满足；以至于几天前在格拉纳达，清晨的阳光下，他一边享用早餐，一边短暂地感受到，自己仿佛回到了家。

The emperor nodded, deeply moved. The development of his relationship with Isabella had barely allowed him to notice that he was also falling in love with Spain. During their wedding and honeymoon, the kingdom had served merely as a calm backdrop to his love. How distant those times seemed when Castile, with its revolts, had been the land that so troubled the emperor. Now, no domain brought him more satisfaction than this one; so much so that, days earlier in Granada, during a fleeting moment, while savoring breakfast in the early morning light, he had felt as if he were truly home.

 

 

 

 

1527 年 5 月 21 日，宫廷在几个小时内忘记了苏莱曼和弗朗西斯，忘记了各种预防措施、邪恶的教皇和惊恐的帝国；除了皇帝第一个孩子的出生之外，没有人关注其他任何事情。

On May 21, 1527, the court forgot for a few hours about Suleiman and Francis, about precautions, wicked pontiffs and frightened empires; nobody paid attention to anything other than the birth of the emperors' first offspring.

分娩过程漫长而艰辛。伊莎贝尔在分娩过程中的表现令在场的所有人都感到惊讶。她即使在那时也想保持她一贯的沉着冷静，克制自己不去抱怨或呼喊。她的坚忍达到了极致，以至于产程停滞不前，因为她为了不表达痛苦，也未能使出必要的力气来分娩。医生们焦急万分，担心孩子会因此夭折，恳求她放下所有伪装，大声呼救。

The birth was long. And Isabel's demeanor during it was surprising to those attending her. She wished to maintain her celebrated composure even then, and forbade herself from complaining or shouting. Her stoicism reached such a point that the labor stalled, because, seeking not to express suffering, she also failed to exert the necessary effort to give birth. The physicians, desperate and fearing that the baby would be lost in the process, begged her to forget all pretense and help herself with cries.

“我会死，但我不会喊叫。”伊莎贝尔一遍又一遍地回答，她的脸上满是汗水，但她的表情却镇定自若。

— I will die, but I will not shout — Isabel replied again and again, her face soaked in sweat but her expression imperturbable.

这位饱经风霜、威严高贵的女子生下了一个光彩夺目的孩子，皇帝为了纪念他的父亲，同意给他取名为菲利普。

And it was from this long-suffering and majestic woman that a lustrous child was born, whom the emperor, in memory of his father, agreed to call Philip.

 

 

 

 

洗礼在巴利亚多利德的圣巴勃罗教堂举行。战争的忧虑再次被暂时搁置，因为此刻的场合值得人们放下一切：西班牙、佛兰德斯、帝国、印度，以及所有抵抗敌人侵略的意大利领土，终于迎来了继承人。如今，未来化身为这个拥有白皙双眸、肌肤如牛奶般柔嫩的孩子，他享受着宁静，尤其享受着母亲的拥抱。查理感到一股前所未有的力量，决心捍卫属于他的一切。菲利普日后将继承的遗产，取决于他统治的成败。凝视着儿子，皇帝对时间和历史的感悟更加深刻。

The baptism took place in the Church of San Pablo in Valladolid. Once again, the anxieties of war were suspended, for the occasion warranted it: Spain, Flanders, the Empire, the Indies, and all those Italian territories that resisted the enemy's onslaught finally had an heir. Now that the future was personified in this fair-eyed, milky-skinned child who enjoyed the silence and, above all, his mother's embrace, Charles felt an unknown vigor in defending what was his. The legacy that Philip would one day receive depended on the triumph of his reign. Gazing at his son, the emperor became even more aware of time and of History.

孩子的头发，橙黄柔软，如同成熟果实，以成人般的庄严接受着洗礼之水。伊莎贝尔和她的丈夫默默地凝视着彼此。某种程度上，这一幕正在重演：托莱多大主教主持着仪式，他庄重的拉丁语礼仪再次让两位皇帝心神宁静。他们如同以往一样，感到与周围的众人格格不入，因为这一刻完全属于他们，他们无法与他人分享。查理深情地看着妻子，她脸上依然带着明显的疲惫。她的康复过程缓慢，起初病情十分危重，以至于宫廷上下都担心她会离世。皇帝对那些日子只剩下模糊的记忆：他害怕上帝会带走伊莎贝尔，这种恐惧甚至扰乱了他的感官，在她康复之前，他眼中的现实如同噩梦一般。他无数次向上帝祈求妻子的生命，以至于双膝因摩擦石板地面而疼痛难忍。他记得自己双手紧紧交握，胸口因害怕失去她而隐隐作痛，痛哭流涕。

The child's hair, orange and soft like that of a ripe fruit, received the baptismal water with adult solemnity. Isabel and her husband gazed at each other in silence. In a way, the scene was repeating itself: the Archbishop of Toledo was officiating, his grave diction of the Latin ritual lulling the emperors once more. They, as before, felt apart from the many who surrounded them, because this moment belonged to them so completely that they could not share it with others. Charles smiled affectionately at his wife, in whom weariness was still evident. Her recovery had been slow and, in the beginning, so delicate that the court had feared losing her. The emperor retained only a vague memory of those days: his fear that God would take Isabel disturbed even his senses, which, until she recovered, perceived reality with the texture of a nightmare. He begged the Lord so many times for his wife's life that his knees were sore from rubbing against the stone floor. He remembers himself with his hands clasped tightly together, his chest aching with fear of losing her, weeping.

—Per Christum Dominum Nostrum，阿门。

—Per Christum Dominum Nostrum, Amen .

洗礼仪式上的宾客们纷纷划十字。菲利普神情镇定，双手紧紧攥着母亲的长袍。皇帝们迈着庄严的步伐，抬着他们的继承人，走出教堂。在到达大门前，一个身影在宾客中穿梭，迂回而过。查理注意到了。他惊讶地发现，那并非某个举止粗鲁的贵族，而是阿尔瓦公爵。他仔细端详着公爵的脸。他想不起来曾见过公爵脸上如此忧虑的神情。皇帝惊恐万分，停下脚步，从他的顾问那里听取消息。他预感到，无论消息是什么，都将是致命的。公爵的叙述以一桩死亡事件开篇：波旁王朝的查理战死沙场，被他的部下疏忽大意，在他身负重伤时，士兵们没有伸出援手；但故事并未就此结束，而是继续讲述了一个愚蠢的决定：那些帝国军队群龙无首，毫无理智和约束地决定攻入罗马。影片以一百幅恐怖的画面结尾：被摧毁的永恒之城，惨遭凌辱的妇女，无数被洗劫一空的教堂，成千上万的无辜者惨遭屠戮，鲜血浸透了古老的鹅卵石街道。士兵们以皇帝的名义，夷平了基督教的心脏。敌人被称作苏莱曼和路德，但真相是，几个世纪以来，没有人如此残暴地蹂躏过罗马；而令他自己也感到震惊的是，这场屠杀的罪魁祸首正是他自己：查理。

The guests at the christening crossed themselves. Philip remained calm, his fists clutching his mother's robes. With solemn steps, the emperors, carrying their successor, made their way outside the church. Before reaching the gate, a figure zigzagged through the guests, weaving through them. Charles noticed. He was surprised that it wasn't some ill-mannered aristocrat, but the Duke of Alba. He studied the Duke's face. He couldn't recall ever seeing such a troubled expression on his face. Alarmed, the emperor stopped to receive the news from his advisor, which, whatever it was, he sensed would be fatal. The Duke's account began with a death, that of Charles of Bourbon, who had perished in battle, neglected by his men, who failed to aid him when the enemy seriously wounded him; but it didn't end there, for it continued with a senseless decision: that of those imperial troops who, leaderless, without reason or restraint, had decided to enter Rome; It ended with a hundred images of horror: the devastated Eternal City, its violated women, its countless churches desecrated by looting, the thousands of innocents slaughtered, their blood soaked into the ancient cobblestones. In the emperor's name, the soldiers had razed the heart of Christendom. The enemy was said to be Suleiman, and Luther as well, but the truth was that for centuries no one had so viciously ravaged Rome; and to his own horror, the one responsible for such a massacre was himself: Charles.

自他上次踏足卡斯蒂利亚以来，已经过去了二十四年。1528年5月，当埃尔南·科尔特斯在帕洛斯港下船时，他感觉自己像个异乡人。人们常说出身塑造性格，或许这句话也适用于这位征服者。因为那个十九岁就离开故土的少年，本质上和那时并无二致：冲动、果断、迷人、精明、骄傲、雄心勃勃，且无所畏惧。然而，他在印度度过的这二十五年，让他的眼睛习惯了西班牙没有的绿色和蓝色；也让他尝到了其他滋味；他的欲望转向了拥有古铜色肌肤和猫一般眼神的女子，她们说西班牙语时带着一种令他心动的沙哑口音。在韦尔瓦港，科尔特斯环顾四周，一切都令他感到陌生：大多数人苍白的肤色，城市的轮廓，甚至空气中的气味。那么，他究竟是谁？他的身份或许已随着岁月的流逝而模糊不清，因为他显然不再是卡斯蒂利亚人了。尽管在新西班牙——他担任总督的地方——印第安人仍然视他为外国人。然而，他的心已完全归属阿兹特克，这份爱是他所能拥有的最接近归属感的东西。

It had been twenty-four years since he had set foot in Castile, and when he disembarked at the port of Palos in May 1528, Hernán Cortés felt like a foreigner. They say that origins shape character, and perhaps that saying could be applied to the conquistador, for that nineteen-year-old boy who had left that land so long ago was, in essence, the same as he had been then: impetuous, decisive, captivating, astute, proud, brimming with ambition, and disdainful of fear. But the quarter-century he had spent in the Indies had accustomed his eyes to shades of green and blue that had no place in Spain; it had opened his palate to other flavors, and his desires had turned to women with tanned skin and feline eyes, women who, when they spoke Spanish, did so with a sibilant accent that disarmed him. In the port of Huelva, Cortés glanced around and everything seemed strange to him: the pale skin that made up the majority of the people, the silhouette of the city, and even the scent of the air. Who was he, then? His identity must have probably faded over the years, for he was certainly no longer Castilian, although in New Spain, where he held the position of governor, the Indians still regarded him as a foreigner. His heart, however, had surrendered to the Aztec lands, and that love was the closest thing he possessed to belonging.

因此，驱使他回到故乡的并非他几乎不曾体验过的怀旧之情，而是义愤填膺。自从开始征服伊斯帕尼奥拉岛以北的土地以来，科尔特斯与卡斯蒂利亚的权威——同样也是帝国式的权威——之间的距离感日益加深。他仅凭寥寥数人便夺取了数百万人口居住的领土。一个取得如此壮举的人，怎会甘愿为了权威这种抽象的概念而屈从于他人？皇帝及其顾问对这些新土地一无所知，出于虚荣或无知，他们强加给他的法律在他看来荒谬至极，根本不利于殖民地的正常运转。他与部下已经征服了蒙特祖玛的帝国，尽管科尔特斯接受了查理五世的附庸地位，但他并不认为自己有义务对皇帝的决定表示效忠，只要他认为这些决定是错误的或滥用权力的。对皇帝而言，西印度群岛与欧洲其他地区一样：是传播福音的土地，但更重要的是，它是一座金银宝石的宝库，可以用来补充他因战争、偶尔的作物歉收和挥霍无度而日渐枯竭的国库。债台高筑的皇帝作为西印度群岛财富的受益者，不断索取更多，而征服者科尔特斯则对新西班牙不得不供养一个管理不善的王国感到愤怒。但这并非他们之间唯一的分歧。皇室与科尔特斯之间的另一个主要冲突源于对征服土地的分配。埃斯特雷马杜拉国王主张实行委任制——将大片土地分配给那些发动入侵的人——但国王不喜欢这种权力分配方式，因为它脱离了他的管辖。恩科米诺领主们，是科尔特斯而不是卡洛斯做出的决定，他们以自己的方式成为了新一代的领主，他们因勇敢和对王室的贡献而令人钦佩，但他们也因自己的英勇和与自己应该服从的人——整个海洋——之间的距离而感到自负。

Therefore, it wasn't nostalgia, which he barely knew, that had brought him back to his birthplace, but indignation. Since beginning the conquest of those lands north of Hispaniola, Cortés had been developing a growing detachment from Castilian authority, which was also imperial. With a handful of men, he had seized territories inhabited by millions. How could someone who had accomplished such a feat feel that he should submit to others for something as abstract as authority? The emperor and his advisors knew nothing of these new lands, and, out of vanity or ignorance, they dictated laws that he considered absurd for the proper functioning of the colonies. Together with his men, he had already subdued an empire, that of Moctezuma, and although Cortés accepted his vassalage to Charles, he did not believe himself obligated to pay homage to the emperor's decisions if he believed them to be erroneous or abusive. For the emperor, the Indies were what they were for the rest of Europe: a land for evangelization, but above all, a mine of gold, silver, and precious stones with which to replenish his coffers, depleted by wars, occasional crop failures, and extravagance. Drowning in debt, the emperor had been increasing his demands as the beneficiary of the Indies' treasures, and the conquistador was furious that New Spain had to support a poorly administered kingdom. But this was not the only source of their disagreements. The other major conflict between the Crown and Cortés stemmed from the allocation of the conquered lands. While the Extremaduran advocated for the encomienda system—the distribution of large estates among those who had undertaken the invasion—the king disliked such empowerment because it was independent of his authority. The encomenderos, by decision of Cortés and not of Carlos, became, in their own way, a new breed of lords, admirable for their bravery and for their service to the Crown, but also vain about their own prowess and about the distance that separated them from the one to whom they owed obedience: an entire ocean.

事实上，皇帝和所有人一样，都钦佩这位来自麦德林的男子。这无可厚非。科尔特斯宛如传奇人物，他以意志改变世界，视风险为动力，视不可能为突破口。然而，查理五世也深知，终有一天他必须面对这位征服者，因为多年来他已得到一些消息，而这些消息也并非毫无预兆：这种敢于冒险、绘制新版图的人物，几乎无法容忍屈服，即便臣服于凯撒也不例外。尽管科尔特斯征服的土地似乎足以弥补他的桀骜不驯，但事实是，允许他独立，除了会触怒王室之外，还会为印度与王国之间的关系开创一个极其恶劣的先例。因此，当伊斯帕尼奥拉岛总督、科尔特斯昔日的支持者迭戈·贝拉斯克斯，因嫉妒科尔特斯的荣耀而向国王告发他时，查理五世抓住机会，试图控制这位征服者，并发起审判，以确定他是否犯有藐视王室罪。得知判决结果后，这位来自埃斯特雷马杜拉的征服者并未等待审判，而是集结了一艘船，返回西班牙，捍卫自己的权利，并与皇帝对峙。

In reality, the emperor, like everyone else, admired the man from Medellín. It was impossible not to. Cortés was cut from the cloth of legends, one of those beings who transform the world with their will and who see in risk a goad and in the impossible, a crack. However, Charles was fully aware that one day he would have to confront the conquistador, because over the years he had received news of what, on the other hand, was to be expected: that the audacious character so necessary for drawing new maps barely tolerated submission, not even to a Caesar. And although what Cortés had conquered seemed valuable enough to compensate for his defiance, the truth was that allowing his independence, aside from offending the Crown, would set a poisonous precedent for the relationship between the Indies and the kingdom. Therefore, when Diego Velázquez, governor of Hispaniola and Cortés's former supporter, consumed by envy of Cortés's glory, denounced him to the king, Charles seized the opportunity to bring the conquistador to heel, initiating a trial to determine whether he had committed contempt of the Crown. Upon learning of the verdict, the Extremaduran did not wait for the trial; he assembled a ship and returned to Spain to defend his rights and face the emperor.

 

 

 

 

说实话，在那段时间里，皇帝比平时更常低头看向地面，羞愧难当。罗马之劫是旧大陆历史上最残暴的事件之一。他急于否认下令进行如此劫掠，反而更加凸显了他的责任，因为正是他的军队，而非其他人，对基督教的中心发动了暴行。难道他的士兵不该违抗他的命令吗？难道他们不该因为他无法给予他们应有的补偿而决定攻打罗马吗？欧洲震惊不已，当得知帝国军队不仅对罗马城及其居民犯下了罪行，甚至还胆敢劫持教皇本人为人质时，更是震惊万分。出于基督教的理智和怜悯，皇帝最终下令释放了教皇。但经过深思熟虑，他决定是时候从自己的错误中吸取教训了，其中最大的错误莫过于因理想主义的骑士精神而浪费了弗朗西斯被俘的机会。他无疑对罗马发生的事情感到愤慨，也无意对教皇施以任何残忍之举；然而，这一次，他想以其人之道还治其人之身，以牙还牙，与敌人的权谋诡计一较高下。

To tell the truth, around that time, the emperor tended to look at the ground more often than usual, for shame pierced him. The sack of Rome had been a landmark of cruelty in the history of the old continent. His haste to deny that the order to carry out such pillage had come from his mouth only served to point to his responsibility, for it was his troops, and no others, who had unleashed their violence against the seat of Christendom. Was he not to blame for his men having acted outside his commands? Or for their having resolved to assault Rome because he had been unable to compensate them as he should have? Europe was scandalized, and even more so when it learned that the imperial forces had not only acted criminally against the city and its inhabitants, but had also had the audacity to take the Holy Father himself hostage. Christian sanity and compassion compelled the emperor to order his release. But, after careful consideration, he decided that the time had come to learn from his mistakes, the greatest of which had been squandering Francis's captivity because of his idealistic sense of chivalry.
