He was undoubtedly outraged by what had happened in Rome and had no intention of inflicting any cruelty on the Pope; however, for once, he wanted to balance the Machiavellianism of his enemies with a dose of his own.

 

 

 

 

只要你同意他的条件，陛下就会恢复你的自由。

—His Majesty will restore your freedom as soon as you agree to his conditions.

教皇视帝国使节如同视他为不可思议之物，因为他所传达的信息荒谬至极。自帝国军队攻入罗马城以来，克莱门特七世便一直躲藏在圣天使堡，如今却被同一批军队囚禁于城内。他面容憔悴，几乎不吃东西，皮肤苍白如纸。他心中充满愤怒。他做梦也想不到自己竟会落到这般境地。他可是教皇啊！查理二世怎能如此冒犯他？先是蹂躏他的城市，后又将他囚禁？皇帝已向欧洲各地发出道歉信，为劫掠罗马城道歉，但对教皇而言，这些道歉不过是空洞的宣传。因为他此刻正被帝国士兵严密看守，稍有动静，他们便会用枪指着他。

The Pope regarded the imperial envoy as if he were an inconceivable object, such was the absurdity of his message. Having taken refuge in Castel Sant'Angelo since the imperial troops stormed into the city, and now a prisoner within its walls by those same forces, Clement VII looked ill. He barely ate, and his skin was parchment-like. The affliction he suffered was fury. He would never have believed it possible to find himself in such a situation. He was the Holy Father! How could Charles offend him so, first by ravaging his city and then by holding him captive? The emperor had plastered Europe with messages of apology for the sack, but for the Pope, they were nothing but empty propaganda, for there he was, guarded by soldiers of the Empire who pointed their weapons at him at the slightest movement.

“如果冲突尚未结束，你又想让我让步什么？”他得意洋洋地问使者，“我毫不怀疑我的盟友会毫不留情地向皇帝发起猛攻，以报复这一冒犯；因为如今，他们除了拥有武器之外，还承受着神的愤怒。”

"What are you asking me to concede, if the conflict is not over?" he replied smugly to the envoy. "I have no doubt that my allies will avenge this offense by charging mercilessly against the emperor; for now, in addition to their weapons, they have divine wrath."

然而，弗朗西斯对教皇被囚禁的同情却显得苍白无力。在自己的王国和其他国家面前，这位君主似乎对劫掠事件义愤填膺，信仰受到重创（因为除了他的办公室和梵蒂冈之外，外界对他与土耳其人的协议一无所知）。但事实是，他并没有立即派兵营救他的盟友。或许，他认为最好是拖延一段时间，让欧洲人对查理的愤怒积聚到一定程度，以便为弗朗西斯想要对他发动的全面进攻找到借口。

However, Francis's compassion for the Pope's imprisonment proved unconvincing. Before his own kingdom and others, the monarch appeared outraged by the sack , wounded as a believer (since nothing was known of his agreements with the Turk outside his office and the Vatican). But the truth was that he did not react to the news by sending his troops to free his ally. Perhaps, he thought, it was best to delay the situation for a while, and let the indignation of Europeans against Charles grow enough to justify the indiscriminate attack that Francis wished to launch against him.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在不列颠群岛，一种与上述类似的虚伪现象正在上演。教皇被俘削弱了他的力量，因此，任何救出他的人都将获得丰厚的报酬，甚至可能包括离婚。命运站在了亨利一边，而他，如同他那个时代的所有人一样，全心全意地相信天意：上帝正在表明祂支持他摆脱凯瑟琳的愿望。有人怀疑这位英国君主的信念是真诚的，还是仅仅掩盖着一个相当平庸的目的——娶另一个女人，让她为他生下一个男性继承人，因为王后似乎无法生育。亨利本人也一度怀疑自己的目的。但这种自我怀疑让他心神不宁，他意识到自己不能再带着这种对信念的怀疑生活下去；他必须解决这个问题。最终，凯瑟琳的良心认定，离婚的理由完全合理，因为那段婚姻本质上就是一场罪恶。之所以如此认定，是因为凯瑟琳违背了她所宣称的，与亨利的弟弟亚瑟圆房，因此，如今的国王和王后是非法结合。所以，即使上帝以残酷的方式彰显祂的旨意，祂也公正地没有赐予他们继承人。

Meanwhile, in the British Isles, a hypocrisy similar to that described above was being practiced. The Pope's capture weakened him enough that whoever rescued him would be generously compensated, perhaps even with a divorce. Fate had sided with Henry, and he, like every man of his time, believed wholeheartedly in Providence: God was declaring himself in favor of his desire to be rid of Catherine. There were those who wondered if the English sovereign's conviction was sincere or merely a disguise for a rather prosaic intention—to marry another woman so that she would provide him with a male heir, the one the queen seemed incapable of conceiving. Henry himself doubted the nature of his aims for a time. But this self-doubt robbed him of peace, and he realized he could not live harboring this doubt about his convictions; he had to resolve it. What her conscience decided was that the excuse for divorce was entirely sound, since that marriage, at its core, was nothing more than a sin. The reason for this conviction lay in the fact that Catherine, contrary to what she proclaimed, had consummated her marriage with Arthur, Henry's brother, and that therefore the now-king and queen had been united illicitly. Hence, the Lord, just even when He manifested Himself with cruelty, did not grant them an heir.

在劫掠事件和教皇随后被拘禁的消息传出前不久，沃尔西枢机主教的焦虑与日俱增。在他看来，英国宫廷​​的围墙——这曾是他权威的舞台——如今却成了隐藏猜忌的屏障。他担心，在石墙背后，有人正窃窃私语，指责他未能完成亨利委托给他的使命。他的光芒黯淡了，有时他甚至感觉它微弱地闪烁着，仿佛注定要消逝。英国君主如同太阳，照亮着周围的人，而那些缺乏王者风范的人，则如同灰烬般的瓦砾。沃尔西几十年来一直享有这种好运，在宫廷中光芒四射——人们在他面前比在亨利面前更战栗，因为只有用恩惠或诡计才能收买这位红衣主教，而他在这两方面都比任何人都更擅长——如今却变得令人畏惧，失去了恐吓臣民的能力，更重要的是，失去了赢得君主尊重的能力。

Shortly before news broke of the looting and the Pope's subsequent detention, Cardinal Wolsey was in a state of growing anxiety. The walls of the English court, which had so long been the stage for his authority, had become, in his view, walls that concealed suspicion. He feared that behind the stone, whispers were being made against him for having failed in the mission Henry had entrusted to him. The light of his star had dimmed, and at times he even felt it flickering faintly, like something destined to fade. The English sovereign was the sun that chose to illuminate those around him, mere gray rubble when they lacked royal grace. Wolsey, who for decades had enjoyed that luck and had come to shine at court in a blinding way—men trembled before him more than before Henry, because the cardinal could only be won over with favors or cunning, and he spent both like no other person—was now petrifying, losing his ability to intimidate subjects and, above all, to make himself respected by the sovereign.

因此，当沃尔西得知罗马发生的事情时，他认出了砸在他身上的石板上的那条血管。

Therefore, when news of what had happened in Rome reached him, Wolsey recognized the vein in the slab that had fallen on him.

殿下，请立即加入对抗皇帝的行列，并展现出绝对的忠诚。陛下比以往任何时候都更需要您的帮助，我相信他一定会重赏那些为他复仇的人。

—Join the cause against the Emperor without delay and with absolute dedication, Your Highness. His Holiness is in greater need than ever before, and I have no doubt that he will richly reward those who strive to avenge him.

尽管亨利精力充沛，但他对战争却毫无兴趣。他并不把战争视为展现自身伟大成就的机会，而仅仅视之为财富的消耗，一种愚蠢的、毫无回报的自我毁灭的方式。战争往往只是为了满足交战双方扩张领土的欲望。他缺乏这种渴望。他并不否认自己乐于收复某些欧洲大陆领土，但这并非他夜不能寐的念头。他真正渴望的是怀抱一个儿子，一个他能从中看到自己影子的儿子，一个能够延续都铎王朝统治英格兰王位的儿子。

Despite his manly vigor, Henry found wars utterly unmotivating. He perceived them not as opportunities to demonstrate his greatness, but simply as drains of wealth, a foolish way to impoverish himself without any guarantee of reward. More often than not, battle served only the desires of both sides to expand their borders. He lacked that hunger. He didn't deny that he would be pleased to recover certain continental territories, but it wasn't something that kept him awake at night. What he truly desired was to cradle in his arms a son in whom he could see himself reflected, a son who would perpetuate the Tudor dynasty on the English throne.

恩里克沉思着。他真的如此渴望离婚，以至于愿意为此坠入战争的深渊吗？他用那种他已经用了很久的眼神看着红衣主教，那眼神里充满了不信任，甚至有些厌恶，就像对待一个自己已经厌倦的爱人一样。

Enrique pondered it. Did he really crave that divorce so much that he would descend into the abyss of war to get it? He regarded the cardinal with that look he had been using for some time now, a look that exuded distrust and even a certain repulsion, like the one reserved for a lover one has grown tired of.

难道仅仅因为你谈判能力不足，我的王国就要在战争中被榨干吗？

—Must my kingdom be bled dry in war because of your incompetence as a negotiator?

“如果我不能带领你们达成目标，那就是我的失职。”尽管沃尔西的地位有所下降，但他的语气并不顺从；他认为，维持权威的唯一方法就是假装自己仍然拥有权威。“大人，究竟是走在官场还是战场上，这完全取决于事情的复杂性。”

"I would be incompetent if I did not lead you to the achievement of your objective." Despite his decline, Wolsey's tone was not submissive; the only way to maintain his authority, he thought, was to pretend he still possessed it. "Whether the path lies in the offices or on the battlefield, my lord, is simply due to the complexity of the matter."

——所以你保证，只要我派遣军队支持教皇，就能实现我的愿望？

—So you guarantee that by launching my troops in support of the Pope I will achieve what I desire?

“保证”二字对红衣主教来说犹如一把双刃剑。听到这个动词，他几乎能感觉到一股寒意袭遍全身。毫无疑问，国王是在威胁他。如果沃尔西无法促成离婚，他就会被指控欺骗国王，危及王室的国库，甚至危及那些将要参加选拔的人的生命。这位大法官不愿去想象国王一旦失望将会带来的后果。

The word "guarantee" struck the cardinal as a double-edged sword. The shiver that ran through him upon hearing the verb was almost palpable. There was no doubt the king was threatening him. If he didn't obtain the divorce, Wolsey could be accused of having deceived him, jeopardizing the crown's coffers and the lives of those who would compete in the contest. The chancellor preferred not to imagine what might follow from the king's potential disappointment.

我保证。

—I guarantee it.

亨利离开办公室——正赶往与博林的另一次会面；世界正处于水深火热之中，而那个荡妇竟然还掌控着君主！——红衣主教感到一股久违的情绪涌上心头，他努力辨认着这是什么。他已经很多年没有感受到这种电流般的感觉了。那是恐惧。

As Henry left the office—on his way to another meeting with Boleyn; the world burning and that harlot still holding sway over the monarch!—the cardinal felt an old emotion stir within him, one he struggled to recognize. It had been years since he'd felt that electricity coursing through his veins. It was fear.

 

 

 

 

尽管亨利对宰相的建议表面上持怀疑态度，但他最终还是同意了。他认为，教皇克莱门特急于寻求盟友以解救自己，一旦被法英联军救出，就会忘记他之前不愿宣布亨利与凯瑟琳的婚姻无效。这样一来，王国的一个王位就会空缺，不久之后，一位拥有纯洁子宫的年轻女子将登上这个宝座。

Despite his apparent skepticism at his chancellor's suggestion, Henry agreed that, eager for allies to free him, Pope Clement, once rescued by the French and English, would forget his reluctance to grant an annulment of his marriage to Catherine. This would leave one of the kingdom's thrones vacant, soon to be occupied by a young woman whose innocent womb would be generous.

但当教皇克莱门特得知亨利的计划后，他的满意程度并不高。诚然，他乐见英军与他并肩作战，但他深知自己是英国胁迫的受害者。没有什么比教皇的权力并非完全独立更令他恼火的了。

But when Pope Clement learned of Henry's plans, his satisfaction was lukewarm. It was true that he welcomed the prospect of the English army fighting alongside him, but he knew himself to be a victim of British coercion. And nothing displeased a pontiff more than the evidence that his power was not entirely independent.

—我目前不会做出任何决定。

—I will not make any decision at the moment.

他一边说着，一边望着圣天使教堂窗外的景色，将话音刚落便告诉了一位秘书。整个城市尽收眼底。罗马城看似平静，但他的镇定却像个受害者，在经历了暴力之后，疲惫不堪，恐惧万分。

With those words, he informed one of his secretaries as he gazed out of one of the windows of Sant'Angelo. The view encompassed the entire city. Rome seemed calm, but his composure resembled that of a victim, exhausted and fearful after the violence.

我会静观其变，看看这场战争会带来什么结果。如果我能很快从囚禁中获释，我就没有理由屈从于英国人的任性。他作为一位基督教国王，职责是守护我，不求任何回报。

—I will wait to see what this war brings. If I were quickly released from this captivity, I would have no reason to yield to the Englishman's whims. His duty as a Christian king is to watch over me, without any expectation of reward.

这时，教皇注意到台伯河——这条河将圣天使堡与圣城隔开——河面上漂浮着什么东西。那是两具尸体，已经发青肿胀。看来劫掠的痕迹永远不会消失。教皇感到不安，别过脸去。

Then the Pope noticed something floating in the Tiber, the river that separated Sant'Angelo from the city. It was two bodies, by then blue and bloated. It seemed the traces of the looting would never disappear. The Pontiff, uneasy, looked away.

“那个根特人不过是装模作样地扮演领导者，”他继续说道，“他似乎很享受强加自己意志的把戏，但他的本性既不严谨也不大胆。想想那个法国人的事：查理对他就像母亲一样慈爱。如果他连除掉自己最大的对手的勇气都没有，又怎么可能和我走到最后呢？”

“The man from Ghent is merely masquerading as a leader,” he continued. “He seems to enjoy playing at imposing his will, but he possesses neither rigor nor audacity in his nature. Remember what happened with the Frenchman: Charles was as compassionate to him as a mother. If he lacked the courage to finish off his worst rival, how could he possibly see this situation through to the end with me?”

教皇的观点与他同时代的大多数人一致。皇帝被认为是一种野兽般的生物，攻击之后会露出一张没有牙齿的嘴：虽然他的攻击力很强，但却无法彻底杀死受害者。

The Pope's belief was shared by most of his contemporaries. The emperor was considered to be an animal-like being who, after attacking, revealed a toothless mouth: although his blows were felt, he was not capable of finishing off his victims.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在法国宫廷，得知英国支持联盟对抗查理后，这位君主欣喜若狂，近乎孩童般的兴奋。帕维亚之战的屈辱，以及在马德里被囚禁的漫长岁月，如今看来已是遥远的记忆。那段时期之后，他一直深陷于深深的忧郁之中，这种忧郁一度几乎融入了他的灵魂，但在罗马之劫后，它已然消散殆尽。如今，在整个欧洲的眼中，这位皇帝似乎成了被放逐者，一个在经历了这一切之后不再配得上基督徒身份的人。仿佛两位国王始终处于天平的平衡点上，一方的不幸意味着另一方的崛起，这位法国人如今成为了维护欧洲大陆秩序的道德和军事救星。弗朗西斯一直渴望凌驾于查理之上，如今他终于如愿以偿，他的野心也随之释放。进攻帝国军队以解救教皇是他的职责，但如果最终仅仅止步于此，他岂不是错失了这千载难逢的机会？毫无疑问，执行这项任务将为他赢得教皇的永恒感激，并带来未来的政治利益。然而，对于这位法国国王来说，成为教皇的救世主所带来的荣耀，与其他选择相比就显得微不足道了——其他选择或许不够虔诚，但无疑更能满足他对荣耀的渴望。

Meanwhile, at the French court, after learning of English support for the league against Charles, the monarch was in a state of almost childlike enthusiasm. How distant the humiliation suffered at Pavia, prolonged by his imprisonment in Madrid, seemed now. The deep melancholy that had followed that period, and which for a time had threatened to become part of his very being, had evaporated after the Sack of Rome: now the emperor appeared, in the eyes of all Europe, to be an outcast, a Christian who no longer deserved to be considered as such after what had happened. And as if the two kings were always balanced on a scale where the misfortune of one meant the rise of the other, the Frenchman now stood as the moral and military salvation of proper order on the continent. Francis had so longed to look down on Charles that, now that he could, his ambition was unleashed. Attacking the imperial troops to free the Holy Father was his duty, but wouldn't he be squandering a unique opportunity if that were all it came down to? Undoubtedly, carrying it out would earn him the pontiff's eternal gratitude, which would bring future political benefits. However, for the French king, the pride he might gain from becoming the Pope's savior paled in comparison to other options—less pious, but certainly far more worthy of his hunger for glory.

那不勒斯。

-Naples.

萨伏依的路易莎静静地听着儿子的话，陷入沉思。她凝视着弗朗西斯科，他的眼神中闪烁着昔日的热情，尽管他的脸上已是饱经沧桑的岁月，岁月的痕迹是任何一个自满的肖像画家都无法捕捉的。她欣慰地看到儿子重拾了在马德里失去的希望，但有时她也察觉到，儿子的计划中似乎隐藏着危险的愚蠢，必须在它彻底失控之前加以遏制。

Luisa of Savoy responded to her son's words with a meditative silence. She gazed at Francisco, whose eyes shone with a bygone enthusiasm, though his face was now that of a mature man and bore marks that a complacent portraitist would never capture. She was moved to see that her offspring had recovered the hope he had lost in Madrid, but at times she perceived in his plans glimpses of a dangerous folly that should be checked before it spiraled out of control.

—您是否有足够的资源在不给法国造成债务的情况下开展这个项目？

—Do you have sufficient resources to undertake this project without indebting France?

国王听了这番话，就像炼金术士发现了贤者之石，却因徒劳无功而受到责备一样。然而，他的顾问蒙莫朗西却丝毫没有察觉到任何魔法石的存在。

The king received his words like an alchemist who had discovered the philosopher's stone and was reprimanded for the effort he had expended. His advisor, Montmorency, however, didn't perceive any magic stone at all.

——母亲，想想看，如果我征服了半个意大利，控制了整个地中海，我将获得多么丰厚的利润啊！

—Mother, just think of the profit I'll make from winning half of Italy and bringing the Mediterranean under my control!

“无论目标多么诱人，都不能忽视实现目标所需的勇气和力量。”路易莎干脆利落地总结道。

—However appealing a goal may be, one cannot ignore the strength required to embark on the journey towards it—Luisa concluded sharply.

蒙莫朗西插话道：“你有没有想过，如果你把入侵那不勒斯放在解放那不勒斯之前，教宗会作何反应？”

—Have you considered how the Holy Father might take it if you put the invasion of Naples before its liberation? —Montmorency interjected.

“一旦征服完成，我们一定会救他出来，”君主回答道，对如此多的反对感到恼火。“这个策略会是一个很好的借口。我们会让他相信，他的自由只能从南方赢得。”

"We will undoubtedly rescue him once the conquest is complete," replied the monarch, annoyed by so much opposition. "The strategy will serve as a good excuse. We will convince him that his freedom could only have been won from the south."

如同任何一个被白日梦蒙蔽双眼的人一样，弗朗西斯也擅长撒谎。他对自己的策略十分满意，拒绝接受任何反对意见。他下令开战，然后退下休息。然而，躺到床上后，他却辗转难眠。失败的景象不断袭来，从他自满的无形裂缝中渗出。他用一个每天都萦绕心头的痛苦念头来掩盖这些景象：他的儿子们被囚禁在西班牙。尽管他曾利用他们与皇帝谈判以换取自己的自由，但弗朗西斯绝非一个冷漠的父亲，他几乎无法忍受他们的缺席。白天，各种招待会和会议的喧嚣让他暂时忘记了这件事；但当寂静降临，他几乎能感受到儿子们的无助——他们被孤立在卡斯蒂利亚，觉得自己被抛弃，心中涌起一种与他们年龄不符的深沉忧郁。这位法国君主紧紧抓住靠垫，试图释放想要拥抱他们的渴望。

Like any man blinded by a pipe dream, Francis had a talent for lying. Satisfied with his strategy, he refused to accept any further objections. He ordered the campaign to begin and retired to rest. However, once in bed, he struggled to fall asleep. Images of defeat assailed him, seeping through invisible cracks in his complacency. He effectively masked them with a painful thought that visited him every day: his sons, captive in Spain. Although he had used them to negotiate his release with the emperor, Francis was far from an unloving father, and he could barely bear their absence. During the day, the noise of receptions and meetings allowed him to forget the matter; but when silence reigned, he could almost sense his sons' helplessness, isolated in Castile, believing themselves abandoned and developing a profound melancholy uncharacteristic of their age. The French monarch then clung to his cushions to release his desire to hug them.

 

 

 

 

——陛下今日政务在身，恕我冒昧。

—The emperor has too many matters to attend to today. I'm sorry.

这已经是科尔特斯第五次得到同样的答复了。这位来自埃斯特雷马杜拉的男子不知自己究竟是从哪里汲取了多少耐心，才能在面对查理如此轻蔑的态度时，依然保持沉默。不过说实话，他从来就不是一个冲动的人。他意志坚定，不亚于任何人；但他同时也精于算计，富有战略眼光，正是凭借这些，他才得以征服特诺奇蒂特兰。冲动是他的动力，而战略则是他成功的关键。他难道能仅凭武力征服阿兹特克帝国吗？他手下几十名英勇却茫然无措的士兵，面对的是数百万的敌人。唯有坚持不懈和足智多谋，才使他最终战胜了蒙特祖玛。蒙特祖玛最终相信，是上帝选择了这些面色苍白、蓄着胡须的男人作为他帝国的新统治者。科尔特斯利用土著居民之间的内部斗争进行征服，但他的耐心以及他对待阿兹特克首领的方式，也体现了他那种除了胜利别无选择的沉着冷静。

This was the fifth time Cortés had received the same answer. The man from Extremadura didn't know where in his soul he found the patience to keep his sword sheathed in the face of such disdain from Charles. Although, truth be told, he had never been an impulsive man. Determined, as any; but also calculating and strategic, thanks to which he had been able to conquer Tenochtitlán. Impetuosity was his driving force; strategy, the key to his success. Could he have subdued the Aztec Empire by sheer force—his dozens of men, valiant but bewildered, against millions? Nothing but perseverance and cunning had given him victory over Moctezuma, who finally became convinced that Providence had chosen these pale, bearded men as the new rulers of his empire. Cortés had used the internal struggles among the indigenous populations for his conquest, but also his patience and his way of dealing with the Aztec leader, with the serenity of someone who sees no other option than victory.

如果他真有此等功绩，他绝不会退缩，他要说服查理五世，让他相信自己不该受审判，他的功绩如此之多，足以掩盖他与王室的冲突。他为西班牙赢得了宝贵的土地；公平地说，无论他与皇帝有多少分歧，这位来自埃斯特雷马杜拉的男子理应得到认可、敬佩和信任。

If he had been capable of such a feat, he wasn't going to back down from the challenge of convincing Charles that he didn't deserve to be judged, and that his merits were so numerous that they dwarfed the significance of his conflicts with the Crown. He had won formidable and valuable lands for Spain; in justice, and however many his disagreements with the emperor, the man from Extremadura should only receive recognition, admiration, and trust in return.

当科尔特斯意识到查理正试图巩固自己的权力，无视他的存在时，他决定改变策略。一天下午，这位征服者驻守在巴利亚多利德宫外，偶遇了皇后伊莎贝拉。当时伊莎贝拉怀着第二个孩子，当她注意到科尔特斯的目光时，便停下了脚步。她认出了他；宫廷里所有人都知道他的存在，但为了与皇帝的行事作风保持一致，他们都刻意对她视而不见。皇后不幸与科尔特斯的目光相遇；他如同美杜莎一般，任何与他对视的人都会被他的眼睛所震慑。据说，无数女子因他的目光而屈服于他的欲望，而更多的男子则被他的目光所点燃，抛却一切恐惧，追随他到天涯海角。

Once he understood that Charles was entrenching himself in his power to ignore him, Cortés decided to change his strategy. One afternoon, stationed outside the Valladolid palace, the conquistador encountered the Empress. Isabella, pregnant with her second child, stopped when she noticed the accused man's attention upon her. She knew who he was; everyone at court was aware of his presence, although, to be consistent with the emperor's behavior, they deliberately ignored her. The Empress had the misfortune of meeting the conquistador's gaze; he, like Medusa, paralyzed anyone who looked into his eyes. It was said that countless women had succumbed to his desires because of that gaze, and even more men, inflamed by those eyes, had cast aside all fear to follow him to the ends of the earth.

于是伊莎贝尔停下了脚步。科尔特斯迈着沉稳的步伐向她走来，他确信自己的猎物对他感兴趣。皇后对这次会面毫无准备。她已辗转反侧数日。第二次怀孕已进入后期，令她身体虚弱，除了身体上的不适，还夹杂着一件棘手的事。自从她踏上卡斯蒂利亚的土地，宫廷里一位年轻的侍童便成了她忠实的仆人。他名叫弗朗西斯科·德·博尔哈，对皇后的忠诚无可挑剔。但他的奴性，正如一个臣属应有的那样，却演变成了一种别样的奉献。尽管他对伊莎贝尔的无限敬重使他无法坦诚相待，但她却能分辨出钦佩和渴望之间的区别。弗朗西斯科·德·博尔哈渴望着她，尽管这种渴望带着浪漫的色彩，一种超凡脱俗、升华的激情。几天前，这位年轻人背负着沉重的罪恶感，向她吐露了自己的心意。他羞愧地低声忏悔，只预料到自己会因爱错人而受到应有的惩罚。第二天他离开了宫廷，伊莎贝拉注意到他的缺席。说实话，她对他只有淡淡的友谊，但他的陪伴让她感到愉悦，尤其是在如今像他这样真正善良的仆人难得一见的情况下。她犹豫着是否应该召他回宫。但答案似乎难以轻易确定。皇后心想，有些事情太过复杂，难以明辨是非，难以确定该如何抉择；任何决定似乎都是错误的。

So Isabel stopped. Cortés approached her with a serene gait, so certain was he of his prey's interest in him. The empress did not feel prepared for this encounter. She had been restless for days. Her second pregnancy, in its advanced stages, had left her vulnerable, and to the physical discomfort had been added a delicate matter. Since she had set foot in Castile, a young page of the court had become her faithful servant. His name was Francisco de Borja, and his loyalty to the empress was unimpeachable. But his servility, as expected of a vassal, had become a different kind of devotion. Although his infinite respect for Isabel had prevented him from being sincere, she knew how to distinguish between admiration and longing. Francisco de Borja desired her, albeit in a romantic way, with an ethereal, sublimated passion. Days before, the young man, burdened with guilt, had revealed his feelings to her. From his confession, which he murmured with shame, he expected nothing more than the punishment he deserved for daring to love the wrong person. The next day he left the court, and Isabella noticed his absence. To tell the truth, she felt nothing more for him than tender friendship, but his company pleased her, especially considering how difficult it was to find servants like him, genuinely kind. She wondered whether she should summon him back to court. But the answer didn't seem to come easily. Some matters, the empress thought, were too complex to discern clearly, to know for sure what position to take; any decision seemed wrong.

甚至在科尔特斯开口说话之前，伊莎贝尔几乎能猜到他的措辞，她就知道这位来自埃斯特雷马杜拉的男人会让她面临一个同样复杂的难题。

Even before Cortés spoke to her, Isabel, who could almost guess his speech, knew that the man from Extremadura would place her before an equally complex dilemma to resolve.

——陛下。——来自麦德林的男子吻了吻皇后的手——。能遇见您，我真是太幸运了，因为我相信您一定会愿意倾听我的心声。

—Your Majesty. —The man from Medellín kissed the empress's hand—. My luck is boundless in meeting you, for I have no doubt that you will be able to lend me an ear.

她仔细地打量着他。他举止文雅，谈吐文雅，一副博学之士的模样，这让她感到惊讶。征服印度的工程浩大而艰辛，以至于皇后认为只有那些在很大程度上未开化的人才能完成。但科尔特斯却拥有绅士的风度和文士的笔法。很难想象一个人竟能同时具备博学的优雅——因为这种气质并非与生俱来，而是源于阅读和思考——以及征服帝国所需的残暴本性。

She studied him closely. She was surprised by his refined manner and speech, the way a learned man spoke. The conquest of the Indies was so overwhelming and rigorous that the Empress had imagined it could only be carried out by individuals who were, to a large extent, uncivilized. But Cortés had the bearing of a gentleman and the hands of a scribe. It was difficult to conceive that a single man could combine the refinement of erudition—for that tone could not come from any innate nature, but only from reading and reflection—with the capacity for brutality needed to subdue an empire.

“我不能违背凯撒的意愿，我也找不到任何理由这样做。”伊莎贝尔坚定地说。

"I cannot go against the will of Caesar. Nor do I find any reason to do so," Isabel stated firmly.

—如果我被剥夺了听证机会，我该如何为自己辩护，反驳对我的指控？

—How can I defend myself against the accusations made against me if I am denied a hearing?

—如果你相信自己是清白的，那么这场诉讼就无需让你担忧。每个人都应该相信正义会审判自己。

—If you trust in your innocence, the lawsuit shouldn't worry you. Every man must entrust himself to justice.

陛下，恕我直言，我并非普通人。

—Your Majesty, allow me to be blunt, but I am not just any man.

皇后确信这些话的真实性。这些话放在别人听来或许是自夸，但放在科尔特斯身上，却与他的传奇经历和性格相符——那种从他的一举一动、一言一行都能感受到的性格。随后，这位来自埃斯特雷马杜拉的男子向她展示了他一直珍藏的木制十字架。十字架上，受难的基督正为全人类牺牲自己。

The empress was certain of the truth of those words, which in others would have sounded boastful, but in Cortés, they were in keeping with his legend and his character, the kind that could be perceived in every gesture, in every inflection of his voice. Then the man from Extremadura showed her a wooden crucifix he had kept with him. On it, a suffering Christ was sacrificing himself for humankind.

我以祂的名义向你们发誓，我所做的一切都是为了我的君王。如果说谁配得上怜悯，那就是我，我曾多次徘徊在生命边缘，只为荣耀我曾经离开的国度。

—I swear to you by Him that everything I did, I did for my king. If anyone deserves mercy, it is he who has so often been on the verge of losing his life to glorify the kingdom he once left.

女人凝视着那饱经风霜的十字架；它的磨损痕迹让人觉得，这件物件很可能曾陪伴科尔特斯横渡大洋，征服新大陆，而这位征服者也像虔诚的基督徒一样紧紧依偎着它。据说，这位来自埃斯特雷马杜拉的征服者并不愿意在新西班牙建立宗教裁判所，而是倾向于以更为温和的方式向王室的新臣民传播福音。有人由此推断，科尔特斯对信仰的虔诚程度或许不及他应有的，但这十字架似乎属于一位虔诚的信徒。

The woman gazed at the weathered wood of the crucifix; its wear made it seem plausible that this object had accompanied Cortés on his ocean crossing and in the conquest of new lands, and that the conquistador had clung to it like a devout Christian. It was said that the man from Extremadura was reluctant to establish the Inquisition in New Spain, preferring a gentler evangelization of the Crown's new subjects. Some concluded from this that Cortés wasn't as faithful to his faith as he should have been, but this cross seemed to belong to a devout believer.

皇后沉默地回应了他的请求，点头告别后便离开了。来自麦德林的男子不想再坚持，他知道沉默是投降的第一步。

The empress responded to the request with silence, and left after a nod of farewell. The man from Medellín didn't want to insist; he knew that silence was the first step toward surrender.

 

 

 

 

几天后，蒙莫朗西抵达卡斯蒂利亚宫廷。皇帝对他抱有怀疑，就像自弗朗西斯背叛以来他对待所有法国人一样。

A few days later, Montmorency arrived at the Castilian court. The emperor received him with suspicion, as he had done with everything French since Francis's betrayal.

—陛下，我大人还有最后一个提议。

—My lord has one last offer for you, Your Majesty.

查理坐在王座上，只是冷冷地看着这位法国顾问，仿佛他不配得到答复。

Charles, seated on the throne, merely gazed at the French advisor, as if he did not deserve a reply.

法国将支付一笔巨款以换取其国王儿子的释放。只有这样，停战才有可能实现。

—France will pay a generous sum for the release of its king's sons. Only then would a truce be possible.

“我很惊讶，你的主人自己都未能遵守约定，却还对我提出要求。”卡洛斯厉声回答道。

—I am surprised that your lord makes demands of me when he himself fails to uphold what was agreed upon—Carlos replied sharply.

自从你签署那份协议以来，发生了很多事情。

—A lot has happened since you signed that agreement.

首先，是他的背叛。

—His betrayal, first and foremost.

——还有你对教宗犯下的可怕冒犯。我提醒你，我的君主拥有“最虔诚的基督徒国王”的称号，而这份荣誉赋予了他捍卫教宗的义务。

—And the terrible offense you have caused the Holy Father. I remind you that my lord holds the title of Most Christian King, and that this honor obliges him to defend His Holiness.

“你是在威胁我吗？”恼怒的凯撒厉声问道。

"Are you threatening me?" the offended Caesar snapped.

皇帝和蒙莫朗西交换了一个充满挑战的眼神。

The emperor and Montmorency exchanged a challenging glance.

“我给你一个解决冲突的机会，”法国人回答道。

—I'm giving you the opportunity to settle the conflict —replied the Frenchman.

—你竟然认为我会天真地再次信任一个嘲笑我好意的人，这简直是在侮辱我。

—You insult me ​​by thinking I'm naive enough to trust again someone who mocked my good intentions.

这位顾问带着圆满完成使命的平静心情离开了卡斯蒂利亚宫廷。法国入侵那不勒斯需要一个外交借口，而查理拒绝接受他们的停战条件恰好提供了这个借口。蒙莫朗西唯一担心的是，作为新战争的宣告者，他是否会因此无法完成弗朗西斯委托给他的另一项任务，但他选择奥地利的埃莉诺来调解此事是正确的。

The advisor left the Castilian court with the placid feeling of one who has fulfilled his mission completely. The French invasion of Naples required a diplomatic pretext, and Charles's refusal to accept their terms for a truce served that purpose. Montmorency's only concern was whether, having been the bearer of the announcement of a new war, he would be prevented from fulfilling the other task Francis had entrusted to him, but he was right to choose Eleanor of Austria to mediate the matter.

第二天，议员来到佩德拉萨城堡，弗朗西斯科的儿子们在那里遭受囚禁，他们的囚禁时间已经比他们的父亲曾经遭受的还要长。

The next day, the councilor arrived at the castle of Pedraza, where Francisco's sons were suffering a captivity that was already longer than the one their father had once endured.

蒙莫朗西走进埃莉诺带他来的牢房时，不禁打了个寒颤。他一直看到的亨利和弗朗西斯都沉浸在他们原本的生活环境中：法国宫廷的奢华，两位王子应有的特权，骑士们的游戏，与王国中最杰出的头脑一起学习的清晨；那种特权阶层所生活的仁慈而充满希望的氛围。在蒙莫朗西眼中，他们身处这牢笼简直是一种亵渎。房间简陋，或许只是个普通工匠或养猪人的住所。石墙毫无装饰，陈设也仅够勉强维持生存：两张床，两把凳子，一间简易的祈祷室，一个破旧的箱子，里面露出几片不起眼的衣物碎片，如同死寂的舌头。但最令他痛心的是，弗朗西斯和亨利，这两个离开法国时心灵未受任何创伤的人，如今却连笑容都找不到。

When Montmorency entered the cell to which Eleanor had escorted him, he shuddered. He had always seen Henry and Francis surrounded by their natural element: the luxury of the French court, the privileges befitting two royal princes, the games of knights, the mornings spent studying with the kingdom's brightest minds; that benevolent and hopeful atmosphere in which the privileged live. Their appearance in that prison was an abomination in Montmorency's eyes. The room was humble, it could have served as the dwelling of a simple craftsman, or a swineherd. The stone walls bore no adornment, and the furnishings were the bare essentials for survival: two cots, two seats, a simple oratory, a worn chest from which scraps of unremarkable clothing protruded like dead tongues. But what was most painful was to see that both Francis and Henry, who had left France without any wounds in their souls, now did not know how to smile.

“你不用担心他们的健康，”莱昂诺尔说。“我会亲自确保他们有足够的保暖衣物，并且一旦出现任何疾病迹象，都会立即安排医生诊治。”

"You don't need to worry about their health," Leonor said. "I personally see to it that they have plenty of warm clothing and that doctors attend to them at the slightest sign of illness."

蒙莫朗西亲眼目睹亨利紧紧抓住皇帝妹妹的裙摆，知道她没有撒谎，但她难以理解，自己曾是弗朗西斯的主要受害者之一，为何妹妹却如此慷慨。埃莉诺察觉到她的困惑，但没有解释，照顾那些孩子多少减少了她女儿鬼魂的来访次数。

Montmorency witnessed Henry clinging to the emperor's sister's skirts and knew she wasn't lying, though she struggled to understand why she was so generous when she herself had been one of Francis's main victims. Eleanor sensed her bewilderment but refrained from explaining that caring for those children had somewhat reduced the visits from her daughter's ghost.

 

 

 

 

当查理得知法国进攻他在意大利的阵地时，他并不感到十分意外。正如已故的波旁公爵曾告诫他的那样，他对法国人的所作所为早已预料到最糟糕的情况。真正令他感到不安的是，法国竟然选择进攻那不勒斯而非罗马。他对弗朗西斯的愚蠢和大胆感到震惊，弗朗西斯盲目的野心有时使他沦为平庸的战略家。

When Charles learned that France had attacked his positions in Italy, he wasn't overly surprised. From the French, as the late Duke of Bourbon had once advised him, he expected nothing but the worst. What disconcerted him was that France had decided to advance on Naples instead of Rome. He was astonished by Francis's foolish audacity, whose blind ambition, at times, made him a mediocre strategist.

“我将是释放教宗的人，”他一进入与合作者的每日例会就宣布道。

"I will be the one to free the Holy Father," he announced as soon as he entered the daily meeting with his collaborators.

“你？”加蒂纳拉惊呼道，惊讶不已，和陪同他的阿尔巴一家一样茫然不知所措。

"You?" Gattinara exclaimed, surprised, as disoriented as the Albas who were accompanying him.

顾问们看着皇帝，要求他解释这项决定需要哪些方面的解释。

The advisors looked at the emperor demanding the many explanations that this decision required to be understood.

——这样做，我将揭露弗朗西斯在意大利的自私伎俩。我只需一个举动，就能在罗马洗清我的罪名。

—By doing so, I will expose the selfishness of Francis's maneuver in Italy. With a single gesture, I can clear my name in Rome.

——但是教皇仍然是你们的对手。他还没有放弃与法国对抗你们的联盟。

—But the Pope remains your rival in the battle. He has not renounced the alliance with France against you.

他无疑必须接受一些条件才能获得自由。首先，他必须将自己的命运与弗朗西斯科的命运分开。其次，他必须宣誓效忠于我。

—He will undoubtedly have to accept conditions to gain his freedom. Separating his fate from that of Francisco will be the first. Swearing his future loyalty to me, the next.

顾问们的眉毛齐刷刷地扬了起来，表示赞赏。皇帝说得没错：出人意料地释放教皇，其益处不亚于一场伟大的胜利。只有加蒂纳拉似乎还有话要说；他若有所思地低声说道，查理察觉到了，仿佛听到了意大利人的心声，而非低沉的咕哝。

The advisors' eyebrows arched in unison in a gesture of admiration. The emperor was right: an unexpected release of the Pope could be as profitable as the greatest of victories. Only Gattinara seemed to have something to add; he let it be known by uttering a thoughtful murmur, which Charles perceived and to which he responded as if, instead of a guttural noise, he could hear the Italian's thoughts.

当然，如果你不承诺在罗马为我加冕为皇帝，我们就不可能达成协议。

—Of course, there will be no agreement without your commitment to crown me emperor in Rome.

加蒂娜拉笑了。有时她觉得自己没什么可以教给凯撒的。

Gattinara smiled. Sometimes she felt she had very little to teach Caesar.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在英格兰，沃尔西不得不克制自己，不去日夜守候在宫廷里等待来自欧洲大陆的信使。他的地位取决于他收到的消息，鉴于亨利近来的态度，或许甚至关乎他的性命。这位君主对离婚问题的执念与日俱增，最终成为宫廷乃至整个英格兰唯一的谈资。各种会议都围绕着离婚问题展开，任何其他事情都只会激起国王的漠不关心或恼怒，仿佛讨论财政、贸易和基础设施是对在他看来困扰王国的唯一严重问题的轻视。这种执念几乎让他发疯。有时，在会议或晚宴进行到一半时，亨利会突然将目光转向某个随机的物体——一块吃了一半的水果或桌布上的褶皱——长时间凝视着它；他无疑是在思考。每当沃尔西目睹亨利沉思的时刻，他都会食欲全无，默默祈祷。过了一会儿，君主便恢复了镇定，重新参与到谈话中，仿佛他从未缺席过。正是他这种精神状态的反复无常最令大臣感到恐惧；毕竟，疯子也有他自己的内在逻辑，而要控制他，只需理解它即可。问题在于，亨利仿佛变成了两个人，而沃尔西发现自己根本无法驾驭他们。

Meanwhile, in England, Wolsey had to restrain himself from waiting day and night around the court for messengers from the continent. His position depended on the news he received, and given Henry's recent tone, perhaps even his very life. The monarch's obsession with the divorce issue grew daily, until it became the sole topic of conversation, first at court and then throughout England. Councils revolved around it, and any other matter aroused in the king as much indifference as annoyance, as if discussing finance, trade, and infrastructure were a slight against the only serious problem, in his view, afflicting the kingdom. This obsession had driven him mad. Sometimes, in the middle of meetings or dinners, Henry would turn his gaze to some random object—a half-eaten piece of fruit or a fold in the tablecloth—and stare at it for a long time; he was undoubtedly thinking. When Wolsey witnessed these moments of introspection, he would lose his appetite and pray quietly. After a while, the sovereign would regain his composure and participate in the conversations as if he had never been absent. It was this inconsistency in his sanity that most frightened the chancellor; after all, a madman has his own internal logic, and one only needs to understand it to control it. The problem was that Henry had become two men, and Wolsey found himself incapable of manipulating both.

 

 

 

 

“我的侄子释放了教皇……”英国国王脱口而出，仿佛是红衣主教亲手打开了教皇的牢房。“你知道这意味着什么吗？！”

"My nephew has freed the Pope…" The English king blurted out to the cardinal as if it were the cardinal's own hands that had opened the Pontiff's cell. "Do you know what that means?!"

沃尔西心知肚明。如果无法以释放教皇为要挟，就再无其他办法迫使罗马同意英国君主离婚。外交手段失败了，其他不那么巧妙的策略也同样无效。这位红衣主教第一次努力克制住自己，不让自己的声音哽咽。

Wolsey knew it; perfectly well. Without the possibility of blackmailing the Pope with his release, there was no recourse left to force Rome to grant the British monarchs' divorce. Diplomacy had failed; less subtle tactics, too. For the first time, the cardinal struggled to keep his voice from breaking.

“我今天将启程前往法国，以便国王能够向我解释为什么他自己没有承担这项任务……”

"I will leave for France today so that the king can explain to me why he hasn't taken on that task himself..."

“休想！你必须听我的！”亨利的吼声如同失望的父亲、叛逆的儿子、乞讨食物的孩子，原始而可怕。“让教皇派个使节来，”亨利继续说道，语气中带着超乎常人的坚定。

"None of that. You will do as I command!" Henry's cry was that of a disappointed father, a rebellious son, a child begging for food; primal and terrible. "Get the Pope to send you a nuncio," Henry continued, speaking with superhuman determination.

“为了什么目的？”红衣主教问道。

"For what purpose?" asked the cardinal.

—她将主持我即将对卡塔琳娜提起的诉讼。

—She will preside over the trial I am going to open against Catalina.

说实话，沃尔西觉得这个想法很荒谬，但同时，这似乎让他免于垮台；虽然内心也有些痛苦，但他还是松了一口气，从那一刻起，他便全身心地投入到组织诉讼中，就像囚犯在看守突然移开视线时所展现出的那种勇气一样。

To tell the truth, Wolsey found the idea ridiculous, but at the same time it seemed to him like a reprieve from his own downfall; although not without some agony, he breathed a sigh of relief and from that moment on devoted himself to organizing the lawsuit, with the nerve that a prisoner uses when his captor, suddenly, looks the other way.

几周后，坎佩乔枢机主教从梵蒂冈抵达，沃尔西热情接待了他，如同迎接一位老朋友。这位百岁高龄的教廷大使，举止文雅，学识渊博，接受人们的款待，但每当被问及对即将到来的审判有何看法时，他都保持沉默。当教宗将这项任务委托给他时，他丝毫没有动摇，尽管这项任务无疑吃力不讨好：如果他支持亨利，他和罗马都将招致皇帝和凯瑟琳叔叔的愤怒；另一方面，如果他拒绝安抚这位英国人，后者很可能会将不满转化为与教宗的永世仇恨，而谁也不知道这位枢机主教能否离开这座岛屿，还是会在英国的土地上长眠。

A few weeks later, Cardinal Campeggio arrived from the Vatican, and Wolsey received him as if he were an old friend. The nuncio, with his centenarian scholarly air and his mind brimming with legal knowledge, allowed himself to be feted, but remained silent each time he was invited to express his opinion about the upcoming trial. When the Holy Father entrusted him with the mission, not a fiber of his being wavered, even though the task would undoubtedly be thankless: if he ruled in favor of Henry, both he and Rome would incur the wrath of the emperor and Catherine's uncle; if, on the other hand, he refused to appease the Englishman, the latter could well turn his frustration into eternal enmity with the Holy Father, and who knew whether the cardinal would be allowed to leave the island or would pay with a tombstone on British soil.

 

 

 

 

卡塔琳娜走进法庭，目光直视前方，丈夫像个陌生人一样坐在那里。得知即将开庭的消息后，她意识到自己可能遭受的羞辱远比最初预想的要严重得多，甚至可能无边无际。尽管近来她的生活如同噩梦一般，她依然保持着镇定，直到合适的时机才开口。

Catalina entered the courtroom, her gaze fixed straight ahead, where her husband sat as a stranger. When she learned of the hearing, she realized the potential humiliation was far greater than she had initially feared; perhaps even boundless. Despite her life having become a nightmare in recent times, she maintained her composure and the ability to remain silent until the right moment to speak out.

——英格兰女王凯瑟琳，请到法庭来。

—Catherine, Queen of England, appear before this court.

沃尔西生硬的声音在房间里回荡。西班牙王后甚至都没看红衣主教一眼。几天前，她曾当面质问过他，厌倦了这位大法官自从亨利炮制出那场法律闹剧以来就一直挂在脸上的得意洋洋的表情。“我的不幸就是你的不幸，”王后厉声说道。虽然沃尔西没有回应她的警告，但凯瑟琳知道他是在指责她，因为她太聪明了，不会被蒙蔽。

Wolsey's wooden voice echoed through the chamber. The Spanish queen didn't even glance at the cardinal. Days earlier, she had confronted him, tired of the triumphant expression the chancellor had worn ever since Henry had conjured up that legal charade. "My misfortune will be yours," the queen had snapped. Although Wolsey didn't reply to the warning, Catherine knew he had accused her, because she was too intelligent to be deceived.

那位西班牙女子继续前行，经过宫廷和为她预留的座位。她径直走到亨利国王的座位前，目光紧紧锁定他，然后俯身跪拜。国王神情自信，但目光却微微避开了妻子的目光。

The Spanish woman continued on her way, passing by the court and the seat reserved for her. She advanced to the exact spot where Henry sat and fixed her gaze upon him before prostrating herself before him. The king wore a confident expression, but he slightly averted his eyes from his wife's.

“陛下，我前来觐见，因为您是这王国的正义化身，”凯瑟琳说道。“二十年来，我一直是陛下忠贞的妻子。我爱您所爱的一切，无论我是否有理由。我并不自夸；我只是遵守了在上帝面前许下的诺言，与您相伴终生，唯有死亡才能将我们分开。”

“My lord, I come before you, for you are Justice in this kingdom,” said Catherine. “For twenty years I have been a loyal wife to Your Majesty. I have loved all that you have loved, whether I had reason or not. I do not boast of it; I have only obeyed my promise before God to be one with you until death, and death alone, do us part.”

—站起来，听从法庭的指示。

—Stand up and follow the court's instructions.

恩里克心神不宁，仿佛坐在燃烧的余烬上。

Enrique was agitated, as if he were sitting on a cushion of embers.

难道我们共同拥有的一切都不重要吗？就连我为这个王国所做的一切也不重要吗？这个王国爱我，就像我爱它一样，正如你多次宣称的那样？

—Does nothing we have shared matter? Not even my service to this kingdom, which loves me as much as I love it, as you have proclaimed so many times?

——众所周知，我是一个话多的人。

—As everyone already knows, I'm a man who talks too much.

人群中传来低低的笑声。君主也面带微笑，但他的手指却不停地互相敲击着。

There were muffled laughs. The sovereign smiled too, but his fingers drummed on each other incessantly.

我以神的名义作证，你第一次生我的时候，我还是个处女。至于我说的是不是真话，就让你的良心来判断吧。

—I call God to witness that when you first had me, I was a virgin. Let your conscience decide whether I am telling the truth or not.

亨利的额头上突然渗出一层汗珠。沃尔西赶紧上前帮忙。

Henry's forehead glistened with a sudden sheen of sweat. Wolsey rushed to his aid.

殿下，请您坐下，等待召唤。

—Your Highness, I beg you to take a seat and wait to be asked.

凯瑟琳怒视着红衣主教。

Catherine glared at the cardinal.

我不承认这个法庭的权威。只有上帝才能审判我。

—I do not recognize the authority of this court. Only God will judge me.

随后，女王转身离去。在沃尔西的严厉警告和坎佩乔红衣主教的注视下，她离开了房间。坎佩乔红衣主教自抵达英国以来，一直设法掩盖着自己的真实意图。

The queen then turned her back on them. She left the room amidst Wolsey's stern warnings and under the watchful eye of Cardinal Campeggio, who, as he had done since his arrival in England, managed to conceal his true intentions.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，意大利的战事仍在继续。帝国军队与其敌军之间的力量对比对双方而言都岌岌可危。一方一旦取得进展，另一方便会以同样的力量予以反击。兵力损耗日益明显，双方的国库都因维持战争而捉襟见肘。双方都无法预见决定性的打击，哪怕是足以令对方胆寒的打击。参与战争的君主们的财政顾问们已经数周彻夜难眠，疯狂地寻找资金来源以维持如此庞大的军费开支。毫无疑问，他们都得出了相同的结论：如果想要延长这场战争，就必须牺牲臣民的福祉。但弗朗西斯和查理都不愿提及“停战”二字；他们的骄傲不允许他们这样做。

Meanwhile, the war in Italy raged on. The balance of power between the imperial army and its enemies was proving desperate for both sides. As soon as one gained ground, the other would retaliate with equal force. Troop attrition was becoming increasingly evident, and the coffers of both sides were being drained to sustain the fight. Neither could foresee a decisive blow, not even one significant enough to make the other tremble. The financial advisors of the monarchs involved had been sleepless for weeks, frantically searching for sources of income to fuel such massive military expenditures. Undoubtedly, they all shared the same conclusion: sacrificing the well-being of their subjects was imperative if the battle was to be prolonged. But neither Francis nor Charles would utter the word "truce"; their pride forbade it.

然而，皇帝的失明逐渐好转。伊莎贝尔在生下第二个孩子玛丽亚后，虽然体力所剩无几，却依然扮演着皇帝愧疚良心的代言人，毫不妥协。她似乎在为即将到来的摄政做准备。随着时间的推移，这位皇后越来越像一位政治家。

The emperor's blindness, however, gradually faded. Isabel, even with the meager strength left to her after childbirth with her second child, Maria, acted as the voice of her husband's guilty conscience, an unyielding voice. She seemed to be training for the regency she knew would soon await her. With each passing day, the empress was becoming more and more of a stateswoman.

“你的固执会给这个王国带来苦难，并削弱你其余的领土。继续打这场似乎注定无法结束的战争有什么意义呢？”

"Your stubbornness will cause suffering to this kingdom and weaken the rest of your possessions. What is the point of persisting in a war that seems destined to remain unresolved?"

“说我固执？”他反驳道，“我只是在回应那些攻击我的人。我很乐意结束这场争端，避免卷入任何未来的争端。但如果我不回应这些攻击，我就失职了！”

“My stubbornness?” he retorted. “I am merely responding to those who attack me. I would gladly end this dispute and avoid taking part in any future ones. But if I do not answer these attacks, I would be failing in my primary duty!”

尽管他的回答听起来像是套话，但内疚却啃噬着查理的心。如果他为了维护尊严而拒绝停战，最终却会给他本应保护的人——他的子民——带来苦难，那该怎么办？责任感真的是他固执的真正原因吗？还是仅仅是伪装？然而，请求停战的想法甚至让他感到生理上的不适，就像一块石头卡在他的胃里，怎么也咽不下去。实际上，他无法忍受的是向那个无耻背叛他的人让步。他心中充满怨恨，渴望对方的失败，以便给予对方应有的惩罚。查理的怨恨源于他深知自己的脆弱。“一个轻信他人的人，”他有时会自言自语道，“怨恨是他未来唯一的保障。只有永远拒绝那些伤害过他的人，他才能避免再次受骗。”但是，这条准则是否足以成为将无辜的被统治人民拖入毁灭深渊的理由呢？尽管另一方面，找到一种既能解决这种冒犯又不使斗争持续下去的方法似乎是不可能的。

Despite his answer, which sounded formulaic to him, guilt gnawed at Charles. What if safeguarding his pride by refusing a truce would lead him to inflict suffering on those he was meant to protect: his subjects? Was responsibility the true reason for his obstinacy, or merely a disguise? Yet the idea of ​​requesting a ceasefire caused him even physical discomfort; it lodged in his stomach like a stone that could never be swallowed. In reality, what he couldn't bear was the idea of ​​yielding ground to the one who had betrayed him so shamelessly. He harbored a deep resentment and longed for his defeat so he could inflict a dose of poetic justice. Charles's resentment stemmed from knowing himself to be vulnerable. "A trusting man," he sometimes thought aloud, "has in resentment his only protection for the future. Only by forever rejecting those who have wounded him can he avoid being deceived again." But did that maxim justify dragging the innocent people it governed into ruin? Although, on the other hand, finding a way to resolve the affront without perpetuating the struggle seemed impossible.

直到这位来自根特的男子将他的想象力带到了他想要居住的那个田园诗般的高贵世界，就像一个在梦中找到烦恼答案的人一样，他在那里找到了解决办法。

Until the man from Ghent took his imagination to that idyllically noble world in which he would have liked to live and, like someone who finds the answer to his troubles in a dream, found the solution there.

 

 

 

 

“巴蒂罗斯要和法国国王决斗？！”伊莎贝尔惊呼道。

—"Batiros in a duel with the King of France?!" exclaimed Isabel.

“你说得对。我必须保护我的王国免受这场私人恩怨的波及。这场决斗将捍卫我的荣誉，并终结这场血腥的杀戮和财富的损失。”

"You were right. I must shield my kingdoms from the consequences of this personal grudge. The duel will safeguard my honor and put an end to the bloodshed of men and riches."

你们疯了吗？

—You have lost your minds.

皇后双腿一软，只好坐了下来。她丈夫的遗嘱已经写好、盖章，正在送往法国的路上。

The Empress's legs gave way; she had to sit down. Her husband's will was already written, sealed, and on its way to France.

—我的寡居难道比不上我的荣誉，以及你们孩子失去父亲的痛苦吗？

—Is my widowhood worth my honor, and the fatherlessness of your children?

我以为我的价值观会让你感到骄傲。

—I thought my values ​​made you proud.

——当他们兼具高尚品格和常识时。但如果他们是骑士的妄想，那就另当别论了。

—When they combine nobility and common sense. Not if they are the delusions of a knight.

查理正要反驳这番侮辱，伊莎贝拉一个细微的动作——痛苦和恐惧让她闭上了双眼——让他瞬间明白了妻子的感受。他能感受到她对这场悲剧的忧虑，仿佛看到她在葬礼上嘴唇颤抖，以及未来多年独自抚养孩子、饱受思念的煎熬。他看到她在孩子们面前强忍泪水，直到泪水夺眶而出，不得不接受在觊觎皇位的觊觎者中艰难求生的命运，这些人不会尊重继承权，因为菲利普太年轻，阴谋诡计层出不穷。

Charles was about to respond to the insult when, with a slight gesture from Isabella—a closing of her eyes in pain and fear—he suddenly understood his wife's emotions. He could feel her apprehension of the tragedy and imagine her with trembling lips during the funeral, and a future of years of longing and raising children alone. He saw her holding back tears in front of her children until they tore from within, and having to accept a turbulent destiny among pretenders to the imperial inheritance, who would not respect the succession because Philip was so young and there was so much room for conspiracy.

也许最大的荣耀莫过于不伤害自己所爱的人。

Perhaps there was no greater honor than not hurting the one you loved.

 

 

 

 

对伊莎贝拉来说幸运的是，弗朗西斯对骑士精神并不感冒。他一得知挑战，便煞费苦心地遵循礼仪，以体面的方式拒绝了挑战。和查理一样，这位法国人也不断受到身边人的劝告，希望他结束战争。但对查理而言，停战不过是懦弱的失败。然而，他深知破产迫在眉睫。尽管他或许更愿意继续沉浸在君主的幻想世界里，但事实上，他开始意识到自己已成为法国繁荣的绊脚石。他赖以在地中海作战的安德烈亚·多利亚舰队的债务不断累积，但放弃这支舰队就意味着放弃那片至关重要的海域。弗朗西斯内心深处渴望和平，因为和平意味着可以摆脱债务和伤亡的困扰，摆脱每次得知战况时那种如坐针毡的紧张感。他怀念起查理对他而言仅仅是个名字，几乎不会引起他注意的时光，那时他沉溺于肉欲和艺术的享乐之中。如今，他的生活重心却围绕着如何征服皇帝。他依然与情人厮混，却不再像从前那样沉醉其中；他依然欣赏音乐、文学和绘画，但他的目光却变得遥远。以至于任何与他和皇帝的竞争无关的事物，在他眼中都显得毫无意义。他从马德里返回后，弗朗西斯卡·德·福瓦便从宫廷消失了，她是萨伏依的路易丝阴谋的牺牲品。路易丝无法容忍国王情妇对国王的影响力，而国王非但没有反抗，反而带着一种既顺从又冷漠的情绪接受了她的离去。在内心深处，那时他唯一在乎的，只有与查理的关系。他随后将此归因于被囚禁在他精神上留下的印记，但事实是，时间流逝，他焦虑的中心却丝毫没有离开凯撒。

Fortunately for Isabella, Francis had little regard for chivalric ideals, and as soon as he learned of the challenge, he took pains to follow the proper protocol for declining it without dishonor. The Frenchman, like Charles, received constant advice from those around him to end the war, but, as for Charles, a truce was nothing more than a cowardly defeat. However, he was well aware that bankruptcy was looming, and although he might have preferred to remain in the lofty realm of royal whims, the truth was that he was beginning to see himself as an obstacle to France's prosperity. The debts to Andrea Doria's fleet, which he relied on for the battles in the Mediterranean, continued to mount, but relinquishing it meant surrendering that sea where everything was at stake. Deep down, Francis longed for peace, because it meant forgetting about payments and death tolls, about the tension that accompanied him every time he was to be informed of the war's progress. He recalled with nostalgia the times when Charles was merely a name that barely troubled him, while he was devoted to the pleasures of the flesh and art. Now his existence revolved around the idea of ​​subduing the emperor. He gave himself to his lovers, but he didn't lose himself in them as before, and he still appreciated music, literature, and painting, but his gaze had grown distant. So much so, that anything that lacked relevance to his rivalry with the emperor seemed entirely dispensable. Upon his return from Madrid, Francisca de Foix had disappeared from court, a victim of the machinations of Louise of Savoy, who could not tolerate the influence the king's mistress wielded over him, and the monarch, instead of rebelling, had accepted her absence with a mixture of resignation and indifference. Deep down, his relationship with Charles was the only one that mattered to him at that point. He then attributed it to the mark that captivity had left on his spirit, but the truth was that time passed and the center of his anxieties had not moved an iota from Caesar.

 

 

 

 

对于围绕在两位君主身边的人来说，最令人绝望的是，两人之间的攻防战已经陷入了一种似乎无法停止的惯性状态，就像是从山顶发射的炮弹，连脚都看不见。

What was desperate for those surrounding both monarchs was that the dance of attacks and responses between the two had entered an inertia that seemed impossible to stop, as if it were a projectile launched from a summit from which not even the foot could be seen.

决斗失败后，意识到无法从他们那里获得和平的钥匙，两位足智多谋的女性挺身而出。萨伏依的路易丝提出了这个提议，奥地利的玛格丽特接受了。她们将负责斡旋，结束帝国派系和弗朗茨领导的派系之间的敌对状态。谈判注定艰辛，但她们会沉着冷静地进行。无论是皇帝还是那位法国人，都无法放下各自的执念和敌意，去满足臣民和顾问们的呼声。他们顽固的男性虚荣心终将一事无成；就让他们各自待在自己的角落里吧，就像两个泪痕未干却依然怒气冲冲的固执孩子，而让两位女性为欧洲带来和平。

It was after the failed duel that, realizing they wouldn't obtain the key to peace from them, two figures, both women and brimming with cunning, stepped forward. The proposal came from Louise of Savoy, and Margaret of Austria accepted it. They would be the ones to negotiate an end to hostilities between the imperial faction and the one led by Francis. The negotiation was expected to be arduous, but it would be approached with composure. Neither the emperor nor the Frenchman was capable of setting aside their obsessions and their animosity to achieve what their subjects and advisors were clamoring for. Nothing would come of their stubborn male vanity; let them each remain in their own corner, like stubborn children with dried tears but still scowls, while the women restored peace to Europe.

 

 

 

 

会面在康布雷举行。所幸1529年的夏天气候温和，但路易丝和玛格丽特之间的每次会面都难免充满紧张气氛。从她们第一次坐下来谈判起，就显而易见：尽管结束战争的愿望将她们联系在一起，但两人都不愿轻易让步。她们所代表的阵营之间尖锐的竞争，以一种优雅、辩证且相互猜忌的方式，在她们身上得到了体现。

The meeting took place in Cambrai. Fortunately, the summer of 1529 was mild, but meetings between Louise and Margaret never ended without a certain tension. From the first time they sat down to negotiate, it was clear that while their desire to end the war had brought them together, neither was going to easily concede on the terms. The sharp rivalry between those they represented was reflected in them in an elegant, dialectical, and mutually suspicious manner.

然而，法国小镇并非唯一描绘这场冲突未来走向的舞台。路易丝和玛格丽特寻求达成协议的同时，查理和弗朗索瓦也在忙于各自巩固阵地，以期影响两位女士的谈判。两人都觊觎着同一样东西：安德烈亚·多利亚的舰队。法国君主急需资金来维持舰队的运转，查理抵押了自己所剩无几的财产，以博取这位海军上将的好感。只有在与多利亚的谈判告一段落后，和平条约才开始起草，而条约的条款却对皇帝有利：意大利人厌倦了等待弗朗索瓦的付款，决定倒戈。一旦落入皇帝之手，法国赢得战争的希望便如同奇迹一般渺茫，而教皇眼见己方势力日渐衰弱，也并未为法国人祈求上帝赐予他这样的奇迹。弗朗索瓦在皇家会议上彻底崩溃：教皇和海军上将都抛弃了他，让他陷入困境。维系他们的联盟毫无价值；当命运对他们不利时，那些曾经自诩为盟友中最忠诚的人也随之倒戈。

However, the French town was not the only canvas where the future of the conflict was being painted. While Louise and Margaret sought an agreement, Charles and Francis were busy gaining ground on their own so that the ladies' negotiations would be influenced by this advantage. And both coveted the same thing: Andrea Doria's fleet. The French sovereign was desperate to find funds to maintain the fleet at his service, and Charles mortgaged what little he had left to curry favor with the admiral. Only when the courting of Doria was resolved did the peace treaty begin to be written, and it was written in favor of the emperor: the Italian, tired of waiting for Francis's payments, decided to change sides. Once under the emperor's command, the chances of France winning the war were reduced to a miracle, and the Pope, seeing his side weakening, did not intercede for God to grant such a prodigy to the Frenchman. Francis left his knuckles on the royal council table: the Pope and the admiral had abandoned him in his misfortune. The alliances that bound them were worthless; when fortune turned against them, it took with it those who had once declared themselves the most loyal among allies.

 

 

 

 

和平条约于八月初签署。玛格丽特毫不犹豫地签下了这份协议。她的侄子必须放弃对勃艮第的继承权，但作为交换，他将被重新确认为意大利和佛兰德斯大部分地区以及阿图瓦城的统治者。法国诸侯回归王国的提议被接受，弗朗索瓦二世与埃莉诺的婚约也得到确认。当路易丝拿起笔签署条约时，她不禁反思自己是否已竭尽全力避免这样的失败。她从昂布瓦兹宫廷得到了国王对这些条件的认可，尽管国王的语气简短，流露出些许失望。事实上，多利亚倒戈投靠皇室以及教皇克莱门特的态度，使得一切都已无回旋余地。而英国方面，一如既往地对法国的困境置之不理；除了这桩婚事，它再也无法假装关心其他任何事情了。因此，法国意识到自己孤立无援，也正因如此，被迫自贬身价。

Peace was signed at the beginning of August. It was easy for Margaret to sign the agreement. Her nephew would have to renounce his claim to Burgundy, but in return, he would be reaffirmed as ruler of a large part of Italy and Flanders, as well as the town of Artois. The return of the French princes to their kingdom was accepted, and the marriage between Francis and Eleanor was confirmed. When she took up her pen to sign the treaty, Louise wondered if she had done everything possible to avoid such a failure. From the court of Amboise, she had received the king's approval of the conditions, albeit with terse expressions that revealed a certain disappointment. The truth was that Doria's defection to the imperial side and the attitude of Pope Clement had left no room for anything more. England, for its part, and as was its custom, ended up washing its hands of the French plight; it could no longer pretend to care about anything other than the marriage. Therefore, France knew itself to be alone, and as such, forced to debase itself.

为了尽快结束这场磨难，路易莎迅速签署了协议。随着《女士和平条约》的签订，这片大陆终于迎来了喘息之机。

With a swift stroke, so the ordeal would be over as quickly as possible, Luisa signed the agreement. With the Ladies' Peace, the continent found respite.

 

 

 

 

停战协定签署之际，一只美洲豹走进了卡斯蒂利亚宫廷的皇家大厅。查理一见到它，不禁心头一紧，尽管这动物被关在笼子里。抬着它的人身材矮小，皮肤黝黑如木，头发乌黑。皇帝此前鲜少见到土著臣民，如今这些人匍匐在他面前，近在咫尺，令他既敬畏又忐忑不安，这种不安感是面对未知事物时才会有的。一只羽毛华丽、色彩斑斓的鸟儿，用如同昆虫般明亮的双眼凝视着君主。查理的目光被这极致的奢华所震撼，随后落在了镶嵌着宝石的华服上，这些华服与精雕细琢、栩栩如生的金银饰品并排摆放。

As the armistice was being signed, a jaguar entered the royal hall of the Castilian court. Charles recoiled at the sight, even though the animal was caged. The men carrying it were short in stature, with skin the color of wood and jet-black hair. The emperor had rarely seen indigenous subjects before, and the proximity of those who now prostrated themselves before him filled him with awe and the unease one feels before the unknown. A bird with majestic plumage and impossible colors gazed at the monarch with eyes as vibrant as insects. Charles's gaze, overwhelmed by such extravagance, then rested upon garments encrusted with precious stones, which lay alongside gold and silver ornaments carved with superhuman delicacy.

-威严。

-Majesty.

埃尔南·科尔特斯跪在石板地上。当他抬起头时，皇帝和这位征服者第一次目光交汇。查理五世预料到这位来自埃斯特雷马杜拉的男子会是一位性情急躁的人，然而他却被科尔特斯身上散发出的力量所震撼。他立刻明白了科尔特斯是如何在几乎没有任何资源的情况下征服一个帝国的，因为他拥有卓越的劝说才能和必胜的气场。

Hernán Cortés knelt on the stone floor. As he raised his head, the emperor and the conqueror locked eyes for the first time. Charles had anticipated that the man from Extremadura would be one of those men of impetuous spirit, and yet he was impressed by the power he exuded. He understood instantly how Cortés could have conquered an empire with virtually no resources, for he possessed the gift of persuasion and the aura of victory.

—请接受来自新西班牙的这些微薄礼物。

—Accept these humble gifts from New Spain.

科尔特斯先生，在你之前很多人都认为黄金可以买到违法的权利。

—Mr. Cortés, many before you thought that gold buys the right to break the laws.

来自麦德林的男子露出一丝勉强的微笑。在他看来，皇帝似乎很脆弱，但这只是表面现象。他能洞察每个人内心深处的潜在威胁，因此丝毫不敢低估他。科尔特斯挺直身子，拔出长剑。目睹这一切的人惊恐地倒吸一口凉气，但当征服者将剑丢在地上时，这惊恐的声响戛然而止。

The man from Medellín offered a half-smile. The emperor seemed fragile to him, but only superficially. He, who could read the potential threat within each man, felt far from underestimating him. Cortés straightened and drew his sword. The witnesses to the encounter gasped in terror, a gasp that was stifled when the conquistador dropped the blade to the ground.

—如果你认为我是叛徒，那就砍下我的头吧。但请你自己主持公道。因为我的命运，无论是好是坏，都只归功于你。

—If you consider me a traitor, cut off my head. But administer justice yourself. For I owe my fortune or my misfortune only to you.

卡洛斯冷静地观察着新西班牙的总督。

Carlos calmly observed the governor of New Spain.

—首先，我赋予你们自卫的权利。

—First, I grant you the right to defend yourselves.

另一个人像基督一样举起双臂，画了一幅画：画中他自己被他带来的奇珍异宝环绕。

The other raised his arms, like a Christ, to draw a picture: one that framed himself surrounded by the wonders he had brought with him.

那里的生活与你想象的截然不同。

—Life there is very different from how you imagine it.

服从没有国界。你就是法律。我的法律！而你却违抗我的命令，与王室为敌。

—Obedience knows no borders. You were the law. My law! And you have acted against the Crown by disobeying my commands.

——为了那些土地的福祉，那些土地也是你的土地。你难道从未做过违背自己意愿的决定吗？

—For the good of those lands, which is also your own. Have you never made decisions contrary to what you desired?

卡洛斯想出了几十个主意，但他似乎并没有认真考虑这个问题。

Carlos came up with dozens of ideas, but he didn't seem to think about the matter.

我曾面对贪婪、最残酷的暴力，以及让两个世界共存的艰辛。而且，我已经尽我所能做到了！

—I have faced greed, the most savage violence, and the ordeal of making two worlds coexist in one. And I have done it to the best of my ability!

从来没有人像科尔特斯那样在皇帝面前大声说话。皇帝不喜欢他的态度，但同时又觉得这让他感到安心：终于有人以绝对的真诚与他交谈，不计后果地坚持自己所信奉的真理。查理五世早已厌倦了弗朗西斯科等人的狡诈伎俩和空头支票，因此，这位埃斯特雷马杜拉人的坦率直言令他钦佩不已。

No one had ever raised their voice before the emperor the way Cortés was doing. The emperor disliked his manner, but at the same time found it reassuring: at last, a man was addressing him with absolute sincerity, not caring whether he would leave that room alive, driven by what he believed to be his truth. Fed up as Charles was with cunning maneuvers and empty promises like those of Francisco, the Extremaduran's stark honesty struck him as admirable.

“我无法定你的罪，因为我不了解你罪行的严重程度。但请放心，从今以后我会密切关注你。隔开我们的大海也无法掩盖你的罪行。”

"I cannot condemn you, for I do not know the extent of your guilt. But rest assured that I will keep a close watch on you from now on. The vast sea that separates us will not be able to conceal your transgressions."

科尔特斯低头表示感谢。这位埃斯特雷马杜拉人的举止在优雅、高贵和强悍之间摇摆不定，前者无疑是一位开明人士的体现，后者则展现出一位肆无忌惮的殖民者的强硬。

Cortés bowed his head in gratitude. The Extremaduran's mannerisms oscillated between the refinement of the enlightened man he undoubtedly was and the forcefulness one might expect from an unbridled colonizer.

——你将继续担任总司令一职。你将被授予瓦哈卡山谷的第一侯爵领地，作为对你补偿。

—You will retain the position of captain general. And you will be granted the first marquisate of those lands, that of the valley of Oaxaca. Let it serve as compensation for you.

“你们要罢免我的总督职务吗？”科尔特斯语气中充满了难以置信。

—Are you deposing me as governor? —Cortés's tone was one of disbelief.

我劝你不要再冒险了。

—I advise you not to tempt fate any further.

皇帝随即结束了觐见。他被美洲虎和珍奇鸟类环绕着，离开了房间。科尔特斯呆立原地，目光紧紧盯着空荡荡的王座。他的表情仿佛是第一次直面一种无法撼动的强大力量。

The emperor immediately ended the audience. Surrounded by jaguars and exotic birds, he left the chamber. Cortés remained rooted to the spot, his gaze fixed on the now-empty throne. His expression was that of someone who, for the first time, had come face to face with a power that could not be undone.

 

 

 

 

不久之后，弗朗西斯的子女们跟随埃莉诺离开了西班牙。查理的妹妹，在他们被囚禁期间唯一对他们表示同情的人，正前往法国成为他们的继母。最小的太子亨利感到庆幸。他对母亲的记忆如今已如同幽灵般模糊。但这份幸运中夹杂着苦涩，因为他知道，那份让他们重获自由的协议条款对他的父亲和他统治的王国来说是一种耻辱。他只找到一个方法来缓解内心的不安。

Shortly afterward, Francis's children left Spain with Eleanor. Charles's sister, the only person who had shown them compassion during their captivity, was traveling to France to become their stepmother. The youngest of the Dauphins, Henry, felt fortunate. His memory of his mother was now little more than a ghost. But this sense of good fortune was tinged with bitterness, for he knew that the terms of the agreement that had freed them were humiliating for his father and the kingdom he ruled. He found only one way to ease his unease.

“总有一天我会成为你的噩梦，”当他前来送别前往高卢的随从时，他对皇帝说道。

"One day I will be your nightmare," he told the emperor when he came to see off the entourage that was leaving for Gaul.

在场的人都被男孩的话逗乐了。只有卡洛斯感到一阵寒意，他想象着自己将来变成老人，回想起那一刻，那时威胁已经变成了现实。

Those present were amused by the boy's remark. Except for Carlos, who felt a slight chill, imagining himself in the future, as an old man, recalling that moment, when the threat had already been fulfilled.

 

 

 

 

但他在那短暂的幻象中瞥见的黯淡未来还很遥远。眼下似乎一片祥和，值得好好享受：战争结束，《康布雷和约》的外交胜利，以及教皇的臣服。教皇一得知法国战败的消息，便立即寻求皇帝的友谊，因为他能否结束隐居生活，能否重返梵蒂冈，完全取决于此。查理五世趁虚而入，充分利用了教皇的脆弱。首先，他要求罗马无视英格兰国王亨利的要求。他绝不容忍姑姑凯瑟琳继续遭受如此屈辱的折磨。她绝不会成为叛徒，教会必须明确地将这一点告知英国国王。皇帝的命令立即产生了后果：坎佩乔枢机主教立即离开英国，留下了关于王室离婚的悬而未决的案件。亨利感到自己受到了嘲弄，而沃尔西则茫然地凝视着深渊。任何合理的解决冲突的方案都因此被排除在外。在绝望之下，这位红衣主教重拾了之前被忽略的旧论点，试图说服他的君主放弃他的计划。然而，这位君主已被罗马的决定彻底激怒，认为解雇他的顾问更为明智。

But that grim future he had glimpsed in that fleeting vision was still far off. The present seemed auspicious and should be savored: the end of the war, the diplomatic triumph of the Peace of Cambrai, and also the Pope's submission. As soon as he learned of France's defeat, the Pontiff sought the Emperor's friendship, for the end of his seclusion and the restoration of his position in the Vatican depended solely on it. His vulnerability was such that Charles took full advantage of it. First, he demanded that Rome disregard the demands of Henry of England. He would not tolerate his aunt Catherine continuing to suffer the humiliating anguish to which she was being subjected. She would never become a renegade, and the Church had to be unequivocal in informing the British king of this. The Emperor's imperative had an immediate consequence: Cardinal Campeggio left England at once, leaving the case concerning the royal divorce unresolved. Henry felt mocked, and Wolsey, staring into an abyss. Any reasonable solution to the conflict was thus ruled out. In a desperate attempt, the cardinal resurrected arguments from the past, previously ignored, to try to convince his lord to abandon his endeavor. The monarch, whose blood had been completely poisoned by Rome's decision, deemed it more prudent to dismiss his advisor.

 

 

 

 

说实话，教皇克莱门特二世原本以为自己已经与皇帝达成了和平协议，但皇帝却为赦免和释放教皇提出了新的条件。得知具体内容后，教皇几乎想要放弃与皇帝的联盟。然而，面对英国的威胁，又与法国决裂，他已无力随心所欲地行事。

To tell the truth, Pope Clement believed he had already made peace with the emperor when the latter added a new requirement for the Pontiff's pardon and freedom. As soon as he learned what it was, the Holy Father almost spurned the alliance with the emperor. But, facing England and having broken his alliance with France, he was in no position to act with all the vanity his heart desired.

 

 

 

 

1529年11月5日，博洛尼亚的圣彼得罗尼奥广场人山人海，挤满了观众和士兵，士兵们身着盛装，那是他们只有在重要场合才会穿的。竞技场内装饰一新，号手们悄悄地排练着乐曲，等待着这一刻的到来。当皇帝步入竞技场时，铜管乐器奏响了庄严的旋律。查理四世步履蹒跚，身体因这激动人心的时刻而略显僵硬，他回想起自己在塞维利亚的觐见，那时他已受到伊莎贝拉的庇护。前往意大利的旅程迫使他第一次与她分离。他离去的理由是喜悦，但这并不能消除离别的不安和彼此的悲伤，因为皇后和他都意识到，这很可能只是众多离别中的第一次。在此之前，他们一直设法避免离别，但天真地以为，统治着众多遥远领土的凯撒，其重任不会让他经常远离家人。然而，查理接受了这种艰辛，因为这正是他一直渴望的：一种如此强烈的爱，足以将离别化作深深的悲伤。

On November 5, 1529, Bologna's San Petronio square was overflowing with spectators and soldiers, the latter dressed in their finest attire reserved for grand occasions. The arena was adorned with decorations everywhere, and trumpeters discreetly rehearsed their melodies, awaiting the event. When the emperor entered the arena, the brass instruments began their solemn melody. As he advanced, his body stiff with the weight of the moment, Charles recalled his presentation in Seville, already under the patronage of Isabella. The journey to Italy had forced him to part from her for the first time. The reason for his departure was joy, but that did not prevent the unease at the parting, a mutual sorrow, because both the empress and he were aware that this would likely be the first of many farewells. Until then, they had managed to avoid them, but it was naive to expect that the responsibilities of a Caesar who ruled so many distant domains wouldn't frequently keep him away from his family. Nevertheless, Charles accepted this hardship, for it was what he had always longed to feel: a love so powerful that it transformed farewells into moments of profound sadness.

号角声吸引了他的注意。近八百年前，帝中之王查理曼也曾经历过类似的荣耀：即将由教皇加冕。尽管这位与他同名的人十年前已在亚琛被册封为凯撒，但第二次加冕对于他而言仍然至关重要，唯有如此，他才能真正成为一位名副其实的皇帝。他的祖父马克西米利安未能取得如此成就。因此，他既没有获得选择帝国继承人的权力——因为只有教皇的册封才能赋予他这项权利——也没有享受到他孙子即将拥有的那种象征性的荣耀。无论他多么渴望，他都从未从当时的教皇手中接过等待着查理在博洛尼亚大教堂的两顶王冠：伦巴第铁冠和帝国皇冠。教皇的手将放在他的头上，使他理所当然地成为天主教信仰和教会本身的捍卫者和保护者。荣誉意味着责任，在土耳其人和路德教徒威胁的时代，这很冒险，但查理知道，当他感受到头冠冰冷的触感时，任何捍卫自己信仰的挑战都会显得自然而然、势在必行，而且更具历史意义而非人性。

The trumpets demanded his attention. Almost eight hundred years earlier, the emperor of emperors, Charlemagne, had experienced similar glory: that of his imminent coronation by the Pope. Although the one who bore his name had been named Caesar in Aachen a decade earlier, this second coronation was still needed for him to be as much of an emperor as one could be. His grandfather Maximilian had not achieved such a feat. Consequently, he had neither earned the power to choose a successor to the Empire—since only being invested by the Pope granted that right—nor had he enjoyed the symbolic grandeur with which his grandson would be clothed. However much he aspired to it, he never received from the hands of the pontiff of the day the two crowns that awaited Charles in the cathedral of Bologna: the Iron Crown of Lombardy and the imperial crown itself. The hands of the Holy Father would rest upon his head, thus making him, by right, defender and protector of the Catholic faith and of the Church itself. Honor entailed duties, risky in that era of Turkish and Lutheran threats, but Charles knew that when he felt the cold touch of the tiaras on his skull, any challenge to defend his creed would seem natural, necessary, more historical than human.

 

 

 

 

教皇克莱门特在教堂的祭坛前等候着他。尽管他表面上保持着应有的镇定，但内心却怒火中烧。他即将授予那个几个月前还蹂躏他的城市、剥夺其自由意志的人——那个权倾一时的欧洲之主，以及意大利大部分地区的统治者，那个夺走他意大利的人——至高无上的荣誉。当查理走过教堂的走道，站在教皇面前时，他凝视着教皇，那眼神仿佛是一个即将被驱逐、即将战败，却不仅毫发无损，反而受到敌人赞扬的人。

Pope Clement awaited him at the altar of the cathedral. Although he maintained the composure befitting the occasion, a sea of ​​rage seethed within him. He was about to bestow the highest honor upon the man who, only months before, had ravaged his city and robbed it of its free will; the all-powerful lord of Europe and a good part of Italy, of his Italy. When Charles, after walking down the aisle of the cathedral, stood before him, he gave him a long look; the look of one who had been on the verge of being thrown out and then defeated, and yet had emerged not only unscathed, but lauded by his enemy.

然而，在这样的境况下，这种竞争对皇帝而言显得微不足道。他更愿意仰望苍穹。他想象着查理曼大帝正从英雄的天堂注视着他。与平庸的统治者相提并论并不能使他臻于完美，唯有仰望伟人才能。在仪式开始前，查理与第一位皇帝进行了一场精神上的对话，发誓要每日精进自己的品德，以便在这光辉灿烂的当下被年轻的亨利预言的阴影所取代时——而根特皇帝也确信这阴影终将到来——他能够做好充分的准备。

However, such rivalry was a petty emotion for the emperor in such circumstances. He preferred to look upwards. He imagined that Charlemagne, from the paradise of heroes, was watching him. Comparing himself to mediocre rulers would not perfect him, but looking to great men would. Before the ceremony began, Charles, in spiritual dialogue with the first emperor, vowed to refine his virtues every day, so that when this radiant present gave way to the shadows that the young Henry had prophesied, and which the emperor of Ghent was certain would come, he would be ready.

11

11

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

马车轻快地驶入一条绿树成荫的小路。树影婆娑，车厢内一片昏暗，车内的查理昏昏欲睡。他沉浸在这平静的梦境中，濒临昏睡，仿佛置身于一个记忆的世界，那里没有想象，只有回忆；而他回忆起的一切，都指向意大利，指向他的加冕典礼。那些画面依然鲜活而丰富：教皇将拔出的宝剑递给他，象征着皇帝对教会的忠诚；伴随加冕典礼的格里高利圣咏；他的誓词：“我，查理，罗马之王，主的辅佐，未来的皇帝，我承诺……”；外面的礼炮齐鸣；他和教皇一同走出大教堂，在金色华盖的遮蔽下；随后数百名侍从护送着他；聚集在圣殿前的人群，成千上万的头颅寻找着他，口中发出阵阵欢呼，这群模糊的人群从中汲取着力量，而加蒂娜拉的目光中充满了感动和深深的自豪。查理不想忘记在博洛尼亚的那一天的任何一刻。他害怕有一天自己的记忆会衰退，那些辉煌的景象会消失，因为他觉得他需要时不时地回忆起这些，才能感到自己配得上，才能胜任未来的任务。第二次加冕礼是皇帝与命运的最终契约：无论在任何情况下都要捍卫基督教世界。而上帝似乎有意让他在教会面临前所未有的重重威胁之时，享受这份荣耀：苏莱曼大帝率领的土耳其军队的进犯；改革者的知识分子和社会反抗；以及英格兰国王亨利的嚣张气焰，他似乎准备在自己的要求得不到满足时挑起教会分裂。

The carriage, moving briskly, entered a path shaded by the canopies of colossal trees. The shadows they cast darkened the interior of the vehicle and lulled Charles, who was traveling inside, into a drowsy state. He was absorbed in this placid state, on the verge of unconsciousness, in a realm where not yet imagination reigned, but memories; and all those he recalled led back to Italy, to his coronation. The images were still vivid and numerous: the Pope handing him the drawn sword, symbol of the emperor's defensive commitment to the Church; the Gregorian chants that accompanied the ceremony; his oath: "Ego Carolus, Rex Romanorum, adjuvante Domino, futurus imperator, promitto…" ; the cannon salutes outside; the Pontiff and he leaving the cathedral together, under a canopy of gold fabric; the retinue of hundreds of men who then escorted him; The crowd that had gathered before the temple, thousands of heads searching for him, mouths cheering him, an indistinct mass from which he drew encouragement, and Gattinara's gaze, moved, filled with profound pride. Charles didn't want to forget a single moment of that day in Bologna. He was terrified that his memory might one day fail him and that those images of grandeur would vanish, because he felt he would need to recall them from time to time to feel worthy and capable of undertaking the task ahead. The second coronation had been the emperor's definitive contract with his destiny: the safeguarding of Christendom under any circumstances. And God had willed that he enjoy this honor precisely when the Church was besieged by more threats than ever before: the Turkish advance led by Suleiman the Magnificent; the intellectual and social revolt of the reformers; and the bravado of Henry of England, who seemed prepared to provoke his own schism if his demands were not met.

马车停在一座灯火通明的宫殿前。透过窗户，可以看到聚集在此向皇帝致敬的大批人群。他走下马车，抬头望向繁星点点的夜空。那一刻，他仿佛感到所有的星星都向他倾泻而下，将他压得喘不过气来，同时也赋予了他一种使命感。

The carriage stopped before a palatial building whose interior was illuminated. Through the windows, one could glimpse the large crowd gathered to pay homage to the emperor. He stepped out of the carriage and looked up at the sky, which had already displayed its stars. For a moment, he seemed to feel them all falling upon him, crushing him with a sense of purpose.

 

 

 

 

迎接这位双冠君主的仪式隆重而盛大。大厅装饰华丽，数十位显赫人物聚集于此，按照既定的臣服礼仪，向皇帝低头致敬。在众多对他而言无关紧要的面孔中，查理终于找到了家人，他们上前迎接他。奥地利的玛格丽特和玛丽亚的拥抱让他感到放松。他认出了她们身上甜美而令人陶醉的香气。不远处，斐迪南德则显得更为矜持。

The reception for the doubly crowned man was conducted with the most solemn pomp. The hall had been adorned with splendor, and the dozens of illustrious figures gathered there bowed their heads before the emperor, following a choreography of vassalage. Among so many faces unimportant to him, Charles finally found those of his family, who came forward to welcome him. The embraces of Margaret of Austria and Maria relaxed him. He recognized their perfumes, sweet and evocative. A short distance away, more reserved, stood Ferdinand.

“你这小丫头怎么了？”凯撒看到他姑妈拄着拐杖，便问她。

"What's wrong, you little brat ?" Caesar asked his aunt when he saw her using a walking stick.

——这是一起荒唐到令人尴尬的意外。我踩到了一块玻璃。

—An accident so ridiculous it's embarrassing to even mention. I stepped on a piece of glass.

卡洛斯给了他一个慈父般的眼神。

Carlos gave him a paternal look.

“你偶尔也应该把注意力从治理弗兰德斯的事务上转移到世俗之事上。保重，求你了！”皇帝这时注意到了玛丽亚。“姐姐。”

"You should occasionally turn your attention from the affairs of governing Flanders to earthly matters. Take care, I beg you!" The emperor then noticed Maria. "Sister."

年轻女子与皇帝握住了彼此的手。他们不约而同地回想起自上次见面以来发生的一切，心中充满悲伤：玛丽亚在莫哈奇战役中失去了丈夫，苏莱曼征服匈牙利，兵临帝国城下。不幸降临在查理的妹妹身上。她还不到三十岁，却已显露出即将退休的神态。然而，尽管她面容忧伤，眼神却依旧明亮如初。那双眼睛里闪烁着智慧的光芒，也正是当年令查理头疼的那份聪慧：玛丽亚总能妙语连珠，在智力游戏中轻松取胜。毫无疑问，她是兄弟姐妹中最聪慧的。在再次见到她之前，皇帝曾担心忧郁会让她失去智慧，但事实是，她依然保持着那双睿智而如猫头鹰般的眼睛。

The young woman and the emperor took each other's hands. Instantly and in unison, they both reflected on everything that had happened since their last meeting, and they were saddened: in that time, Maria had lost her husband at the Battle of Mohács, where Suleiman had conquered Hungary and stood at the gates of the Empire. Misfortune had taken its toll on Charles's sister. She was less than thirty, yet she still had the air of someone on the verge of retirement. However, although her countenance exuded sadness, her eyes remained as lively as ever. They reflected the intelligence that had driven Charles to despair when they were children: Maria always delivered the most brilliant retort and won effortlessly in games of wit. Without a doubt, she was the most astute of all the siblings. Before meeting her again, the emperor had feared that melancholy might have dulled her wit, but the truth was that she retained her wise, owl-like gaze.

“我们很荣幸您能加入我们，”她说着，手始终没有松开他的手。

—We are honored to have you among us —she said without letting go of his hands.

他们严肃的问候掩饰不住重逢时的激动之情。与此同时，费尔南多静静地等待着。他身着的正式礼服与卡洛斯的精致程度不相上下；毫无疑问，两人都是聚会上的焦点。最后，他们拥抱在一起，脸上带着微笑，但四肢略显僵硬。

The seriousness of their greeting did not conceal the emotion they both felt at seeing each other again. Meanwhile, Fernando waited his turn. The formal attire he wore rivaled Carlos's in exquisiteness; both were, without a doubt, the center of attention at the gathering. Finally, they embraced, smiling but with stiff limbs.

—兄弟，祝贺你在博洛尼亚峰会上取得的成就。

—I congratulate you on the summit you reached in Bologna, brother.

荣耀与责任相伴而生。

—Glory is matched by the responsibility it entails.

费尔南多对凯撒的繁文缛节感到恼火。凯撒似乎无法像对待亲人一样与他交谈。

Fernando was irritated by the Caesar's formalities when addressing him. He seemed incapable of speaking to him as what he truly was: his own flesh and blood.

—当土耳其军队兵临维也纳城下时，你们从西班牙派兵援助，做出了巨大的贡献。

—You did a great service by sending help from Spain when the Turk positioned himself before Vienna.

“你不必感谢我如此悉心照顾我的孩子，”卡洛斯回答道。

—You don't have to thank me for taking such good care of my children —Carlos replied.

尽管那番话语气友善，费迪南却感到受到了冒犯。多年来，由于皇帝长期不在位，他一直代行帝国的统治。尽管他尽职尽责，也享受着随之而来的恩惠，但他始终觉得自己就像一座宏伟宅邸的看守人，主人不在时，他可以享受宅邸的奢华，却时不时地被提醒，这地方并不属于他。这种情况会改变吗？得知查理在博洛尼亚加冕，并因此获得了指定皇位继承人的权力后，费迪南心中便涌起一股渴望，希望自己也能被选中。毕竟，他比任何人都更了解这片错综复杂的领土网络是如何运作的，他的臣民也珍视他温和平和的统治方式。这项任务并不轻松。日益激化的路德教冲突需要他采取精准的策略。但除此之外，过往的伤痛始终萦绕在凯撒之弟的心头。无论时光流逝多久，他依然觉得自己像个没有王位的国王。他每日在官邸中践行祖父的教诲，但内心深处，这远远不够，因为他在阿拉贡学到的最重要的一课便是如何运用权力，而如今他不过是个傀儡皇帝，一个名存实亡的替身。但这并未削弱他治理国家的决心，因为他无法忍受懈怠自己的职责。玛格丽特自与他相识之初便对他倾慕不已，并承诺会支持他继承王位。但鉴于查理的态度，费迪南明白，他恐怕又要被迫退位了。事实上，他对弟弟已几乎毫无感情，更谈不上任何无条件的忠诚。

Although the tone of the comment was friendly, Ferdinand felt offended. He had been governing the Empire for years, as the emperor's absence there was prolonged, and although he performed his duties with dedication and enjoyed the favors that came with it, he saw himself as the caretaker of a magnificent mansion who, when the owner was absent, could enjoy its luxuries, but was reminded every so often that the place did not belong to him. Would that ever change? Upon learning of the coronation in Bologna, with which Charles had won the right to designate an imperial successor, Ferdinand had not been able to suppress the ambition that he himself should be chosen. After all, he knew better than anyone how that complex network of territories functioned, and his subjects valued his conciliatory and serene way of ruling them. The task had not been easy. The Lutheran conflict, which had only intensified, had required a surgical approach. But beyond that logic, the past stung the Caesar's brother. No matter how much time had passed, he still felt like a king without a throne. He applied his grandfather's teachings daily in his office, but deep down, that wasn't enough, because the most important of those lessons he'd learned in Aragon was the exercise of power, and now he was nothing more than a figurehead emperor, a mere substitute. That didn't diminish his determination to govern, because he couldn't bear to neglect his duties. Margaret, who had admired him since she met him, had promised to support him as successor. But given the attitude with which Charles had presented himself, Ferdinand understood that, once again, he would be forced to resign himself. The fact was, he had hardly any reserves of affection left for his brother, nor any unconditional loyalty.

 

 

 

 

正式的招待会结束后，皇帝终于可以好好休息了。尽管他享受到了与其身份相符的奢华待遇，但他仍然想念西班牙。当他躺下时，没有伊莎贝拉的温暖陪伴，床铺显得冷清无比。他为自己曾如此热烈地爱上她而感到骄傲，但同时也承受着失去她的痛苦。他渴望她的吻，她的缺席让他浑身隐隐作痛。

The official reception was followed by the rest the emperor so desperately needed. Despite the lavish attention he received, befitting his rank, he missed Spain, and as he lay down, the bed felt unwelcoming without Isabella's warmth beside him. He was proud to have fallen in love with her, and so passionately, but he suffered the consequences. He felt a fierce hunger for her kisses, and his skin ached from her absence.

他不知道是不是和伊莎贝拉在那里度过的美好时光让他对西班牙产生了怀旧之情。在此之前，他一直认为一个人除了出生地之外别无归处，但现在他却觉得，他与那些王国之间有着千丝万缕的联系，正如它们也属于他一样。西班牙人身上那种沉稳理智的气质与他自身颇为契合，他也能理解他们那种坚定不移、恪守正统、纯粹的宗教信仰，那种超越一切私利的信仰。他甚至可以说，他与西班牙人的冲突正是源于他们共同的特质：和他一样，他们也曾抱持着不信任的态度，直到找到改变的理由。他就是这样理解他们的。

He didn't know if it was the happiness he had experienced there with Isabella that made him feel nostalgic for Spain. Until then, he had believed that a man could have no home other than the one where he was born, but the truth was that now he felt he belonged to those kingdoms as much as they belonged to him. There was something in the sober and sensible character of the Spanish that harmonized with his own, and he also identified with their unwavering, orthodox, and pure religiosity, detached from any other self-interest. He could even think that his conflict with them had stemmed from their shared traits: like him, they had acted with distrust until they found reasons to change their attitude. How he understood them.

 

 

 

 

第二天早上，查尔斯、加蒂娜拉和玛格丽特一起吃了早餐，玛格丽特因为受伤，脚被抬了起来。处理完这些轻松的事情后，荷兰摄政王抓住了这个机会。

The following morning, Charles, Gattinara, and Margaret had breakfast together, she with her foot elevated due to her injury. Once the lighter matters had been reviewed, the Regent of the Netherlands seized the opportunity.

你哥哥会是一位杰出的继承人。

—Your brother would make a magnificent successor.

皇帝突然感觉到了胃里的食物。

The emperor suddenly felt the food in his stomach.

——你是在剥夺我儿子费利佩的这项能力吗？

—Are you denying my son Felipe that ability?

“他开始走路了吗？”她回答道。

"Has he even started walking?" she replied.

——迈着坚定的步伐。

—And with a firm step.

玛格丽塔和卡洛斯相视一笑。即使在争吵中，他们也从未真正无法理解对方。

Margarita and Carlos exchanged a smile. Even in their arguments, they never failed to understand each other.

费尔南多的工作非常出色，德国人对此表示赞赏。

—Fernando's work has been magnificent, and the Germans appreciate it.

“就像当年西班牙人那样，”凯撒咬牙切齿地说，他想起当年他的兄弟是如何赢得卡斯蒂利亚人和阿拉贡人爱戴的。“我不想分割我的遗产。”

—Just like the Spaniards did in their day—said the Caesar through gritted teeth, recalling those times when his brother stole the affection of the Castilians and Aragonese. —I do not wish to divide my inheritance.

此前一直旁观的加蒂纳拉擦了擦嘴唇，然后介入了此事。

Gattinara, until then a mere spectator, wiped his lips before intervening.

—普世君主制的构想要求它由一人统治。这一人必须拥有共同的良知，品德高尚，慈父情怀，能够将所有人团结在信仰和博爱的共同价值观之下。

—The project of Universal Monarchy requires that it be ruled by a single man. A single conscience, virtuous and paternal, that unites all men under the same values ​​of faith and fraternity.

“我亲爱的梅尔库里诺，”那女人说，“你的理想固然值得称赞，但说实话，你认为这能实现吗？一个男人统治法国、英国，甚至非洲？”

"My dear Mercurino," said the woman, "your ideal is laudable, but honestly, do you think it can be achieved? A single man ruling France, England, even Africa?"

——当然，现在还没到你侄子统治的地步。但这才是最理想的归宿，每一个决定都应该朝着这个方向努力。

—Not yet under your nephew's rule, certainly. But it's the perfect destiny, and every decision should be directed toward it.

“你竟然责怪我不关注世俗之事？”她转向查尔斯问道，语气骤然变得阴沉起来。“帝国正处于动荡之中，它需要的是一位名正言顺的统治者，而不是一个摄政王。你的幻想很可能会害了你。”

"And you reproach me for not focusing on worldly matters?" she asked, turning to Charles. Her tone suddenly took on a dark hue. "The Empire is in turmoil; it needs a rightful ruler, not a mere regent. Your chimera could very well lead to your loss."

玛格丽塔的秘书前来宣布，费尔南多已经在议事厅等候她们了。加蒂娜拉和那位女士动身离开。凯撒过了好一会儿才反应过来，他沉浸在姑妈临终遗言带来的思绪中。

Margarita's secretary appeared to announce that Fernando was already waiting for them in the council chamber. Gattinara and the woman set off. It took the Caesar a little longer to react, lost in a thousand thoughts after his aunt's last words.

 

 

 

 

尽管已是清晨，议会厅里的光线却很昏暗。卡洛斯觉得很奇怪：房间里的所有物体都泛着灰蒙蒙的光泽，而不是西班牙阳光通常呈现出的千变万化的色彩。

The light in the council chamber was dim, even though morning was in full swing. Carlos found it strange: every object in the room reflected a grayish tint, not the thousand shades of color that Spanish light usually reveals.

皇帝的弟弟在会议开始时概述了帝国面临的紧迫困难。他的叙述细致入微，不愧为一位专家，因为他的确是这方面的专家。当他多次提及土耳其的威胁时，他的语气变得激动起来，暗示这实际上是唯一真正的问题。查理认真地听着，等他讲完后才插话。

The emperor's brother opened the meeting by outlining the pressing difficulties facing the Empire.
