His account was meticulous, befitting an expert on the matter, for he was one, and when referring to the Turkish threat—which he did on several occasions—he became impassioned, implying that this was, in fact, the only real problem. Charles listened attentively and waited for him to finish speaking before intervening.

他说：“我们必须立即解决宗教问题。”

"We must address the religious question without delay," he said.

“我所做的只是捍卫我们的信仰，”他的兄弟回答说。

"I have done nothing but mention the defense of our faith," replied his brother.

——你知道我指的是路德的追随者。我向教宗承诺，会优先处理这场斗争。

—You know I'm referring to Luther's followers. I made a commitment to the Holy Father to give priority to that battle.

“那么，你误判了最大的危险是什么。如果你骚扰改革者，帝国将会更加动荡不安。而这种冲突将会削弱帝国。苏莱曼一定会毫不犹豫地利用这一点！”

"You miscalculated, then, what the greatest danger is. If you harass the reformers, the Empire will become even more agitated. And that conflict will weaken it. Suleiman will not hesitate to take advantage of that!"

查理勃然大怒。费迪南德则用一种自以为是的语气反驳他，似乎在印证皇帝在西班牙待了这么久，已经失去了对帝国发表意见的资格。

Charles was furious. Ferdinand countered him with a self-important tone that seemed to confirm that the emperor, with his long stay in Spain, had lost the right to have an opinion about the Empire.

“我无意分裂德国人，”来自根特的男子说，“而是要让他们重新团结起来。”

"I do not intend to divide the Germans," said the man from Ghent, "but to unite them again."

——以何种方式？你不会打算使用武力吧？

—In what way? You don't intend to use force, do you?

我将向教皇提议召开一次宗教会议。我毫不怀疑我们之间的分歧能够找到共同点。

—I will propose to the Pope the holding of a council. I have no doubt that the differences between us can find common ground.

费尔南多露出了讽刺的笑容。

Fernando smiled ironically.

教皇绝不会同意你的请求！他绝不会听信那些指责他是罪恶根源的人。

—The Pope will never agree to your request! He will never listen to those who point to him as the cause of the evils.

皇帝寻求玛格丽特的支持，但他只从她的脸上看到了不自在的神情，她目睹了本应和睦相处的人之间又一次发生争执。

The emperor looked for Margarita's support, but he only perceived on her face the discomfort of witnessing yet another disagreement between those who should be getting along.

“先别管路德教徒了，把兵力都投向土耳其人吧，”费尔南多继续说道，“异端邪说比异教徒的入侵要好得多！”

"Forget about the Lutherans for a while and throw your troops at the Turk," Fernando continued. "Heresy is a lesser evil compared to the invasion of the infidel!"

查理凝视着他的弟弟，后者虽年仅二十七岁，却散发着成熟男人的沉稳气质，仿佛早已领悟了人生的真谛。两人的人生轨迹颇为相似，都刚刚结婚生子——小马克西米利安在菲利普出生几个月后便已降生。然而，皇帝认为他的弟弟没有资格与他平起平坐，这不仅是因为他们头衔不同，更因为他们肩负的责任截然不同。统治一个帝国无疑是一项艰巨的任务，但查理统领着半个欧洲和印度的领土，如此强大的权力需要远见卓识，而这只有他和加蒂娜拉才能做到。其他人的目光都局限于他们所处的领地。

Charles gazed at his brother, who, though barely twenty-seven, exuded the grave demeanor of a mature man who had already learned life's important lessons. Their personal paths ran parallel, as both had recently married and had fathered sons—little Maximilian had been born just a few months after Philip. However, the emperor believed his brother had no right to speak to him as an equal, not only because of the difference in their titles, but also because their responsibilities were entirely disparate. Ruling an empire was undoubtedly a daunting task, but Charles commanded half of Europe and the Indian territories, and such formidable power demanded a broad vision that only he and Gattinara were capable of grasping. The others saw no further than the domain they stood upon.

“聆听不同的意见总是有益的，即使这些意见是错误的。我希望得到你们的帮助，确保改革派能够参与到委员会的工作中来。”

"It's always enriching to hear opposing opinions, even if they're misguided. I'm counting on your help to ensure that the reformers take part in the council."

费尔南多一言不发地离开了办公室。皇帝这才看向他的姑姑，姑姑明白，在那一刻，在她侄子的心中，除了菲利普，别无他人可以继承皇位。

Fernando simply left the office without a word. The emperor then looked at his aunt, who understood that, at that moment, in her nephew's mind there was no other successor but Philip.

会议休会，延期至下午继续；大家都无暇顾及其他。玛格丽塔和卡洛斯正要离开房间时，身后传来一声沉重的闷响。他们转过身，看到加蒂纳拉倒在地上，昏迷不醒。

The council meeting was adjourned and postponed until the afternoon; there was no energy for anything else. As Margarita and Carlos were leaving the room, they heard a heavy, sharp thud behind them. Turning around, they saw that Gattinara had collapsed to the floor, where he lay unconscious.

当晚他恢复意识时，议员注意到卡洛斯守在他身边，一脸担忧。加蒂纳拉用尽最后的力气，对他露出一丝微笑。

When he regained consciousness that night, the councilor noticed that Carlos was at his side, looking worried. Gattinara used what little strength he had left to smile at him.

“从意大利来的路途十分疲惫，”凯撒说，“我本该让你之后好好休息。在你恢复体力之前，不许下床。”

"The journey from Italy has been exhausting," said the Caesar. "I should have forced you to rest afterward. You will not leave your bed until you have regained your strength."

陛下，我不会离开我的床。

—I will not leave my bed, Your Majesty.

卡洛斯顿时感到一阵寒意。

Carlos's blood ran cold.

—别这么说！

—Don't say such a thing!

然而，皇帝随即想起这位顾问近来表现出的诸多衰弱迹象：谈话时无故停顿，步履蹒跚，食欲减退，以及长时间午睡醒来后仍感到疲惫不堪。他握住了顾问的手。

However, the emperor then recalled the many signs of decline the advisor had shown recently: unnecessary pauses in conversation, a shuffling gait, a diminishing appetite, and long naps from which he returned still feeling fatigued. He took his hand.

我需要你的指导。

—I need your lessons.

我还有时间再给你一个……

—I still have time to give you one more…

卡洛斯动容了。突然间，离别的确定性在他们之间显现，而似乎只有这位意大利人做好了面对离别的准备。

Carlos was moved. Suddenly, the certainty of the farewell materialized between them, and only the Italian seemed prepared to face it.

——质疑我教给你的东西。你的疑虑是健康的，我一直强调这一点。即使是伟大的想法，也仅仅是想法而已。

—Doubt what I've taught you. Your uncertainties are healthy, I've always emphasized that. Even great ideas are just that, ideas.

—你打算抛弃我，而且让我失去信念吗？

—Do you intend to abandon me and, moreover, leave me without convictions?

不，留着它们。但如果出现更合适的、更有益的替代者，也不要拒绝。陛下，或许您姑妈是对的。

—No. Keep them. But don't close yourselves off to other, better ones replacing them if they serve a greater good. Perhaps your aunt is right, Your Majesty.

凯撒知道加蒂纳拉指的是斐迪南。

Caesar knew that Gattinara was referring to Ferdinand.

—求求你，留下来。

—I beg you, stay.

顾问的视线似乎开始模糊。生命正一分一秒地从他身边流逝。然而，他脸上还是露出了最后一个微笑，那是卡洛斯见过的最满足的笑容。

The advisor's vision seemed to blur. Life was slipping away from him by the moment. And yet, he managed one last smile, the most contented Carlos had ever seen on his face.

——博洛尼亚是我的宿命，让我亲眼见证你接受教宗的加冕。当一个人达到人生目标时，他所能做的最好的事情就是彻底退休。

—Bologna was my destiny, to see you crowned by the Holy Father. When a man reaches his goal, the best thing he can do is retire, completely.

显然，这位意大利人的满意并非毫无根据，因为第二天他去世时，面容平静安详，毫无遗憾。卡洛斯在昏暗的房间里为他哭泣，悲伤中夹杂着一丝喜悦，因为他知道自己何其有幸，曾受这位将他从迷茫中拉出来、赋予他人生意义的人的影响。

Apparently, the Italian's satisfaction was well-founded, because when he died the next day, he did so with the serene face of a man with no regrets. Carlos wept for him in the dim light of his room, though his sadness was tinged with joy, for he knew himself privileged to have enjoyed the influence of the man who had pulled him out of his doubts and given him a purpose in life.

 

 

 

 

加蒂纳拉在世间的位置被一个出生在卡斯蒂利亚的男孩取代了。他的母亲，葡萄牙的伊莎贝拉，欣喜若狂地迎接他的到来，因为他不仅是一个新生的儿子，也让她从丈夫离世的痛苦孤独中解脱出来。她给他取名为费迪南德。小男孩哭闹不止，也不肯好好吃饭，但从他那双朦胧的小眼睛映照出她自己的那一刻起，皇后就深深地爱上了他。她需要将无法给予查理的爱倾注到另一个生命中，尽管她深爱着她的长子菲利普，但这个新生儿却让她感到无比满足。离开小男孩的那一刻，离别的忧伤和对何时才能结束的期盼再次袭来，而且愈发强烈。事实上，她还没有真正把西班牙当作自己的家。有时，她会怀念葡萄牙，怀念与身边人共同拥有的过去。然而，法德里克·德·阿尔巴和被任命为她御马总管的弗朗西斯科·德·博尔哈都尽心尽力地安抚她的悲伤。后者虽然依然深爱着她，却将这份感情转化为服从和侍奉。公爵在政务上发挥了不可或缺的作用，但近年来，伊莎贝拉解除了他的一些职务，因为这位贵族年事已高，需要更平静的生活。

Gattinara's place in the world was taken by a boy born in Castile. His mother, Isabella of Portugal, welcomed him with great joy, for he was not only a new son, but also a relief from the agonizing loneliness she suffered from her husband's absence. She named him Ferdinand. The little boy cried excessively and refused to eat properly, but the Empress adored him from the moment his small, cloudy eyes reflected hers. She needed to channel the love she could not give to Charles into another being, and although she devotedly loved her firstborn, Philip, the new son completely fulfilled her. The moment she left the little boy, the melancholy of separation and the question of when it would end returned with a vengeance. The truth was, she had not yet made Spain her home. Sometimes she felt nostalgic for Portugal, for sharing a past with those around her. However, both Fadrique de Alba and Francisco de Borja—who had been appointed her Master of the Horse—worked diligently to alleviate her grief. The latter, though still loving her, channeled his feelings into obedience and service. The duke proved invaluable in matters of governance, although in recent times Isabella relieved him of some duties, as the aristocrat's advanced age demanded a more tranquil life.

伊莎贝尔产后恢复后，比预期更早地重返工作岗位。她本想日夜依偎在怀里，与新生儿相伴，但她厌恶无所事事。产后她参加的第一次议会会议，就不得不搁置原定议程，因为传来消息：巴巴罗萨袭击了西班牙地中海沿岸。这并非第一次。尽管巴利阿里群岛此前已多次遭受这位奥斯曼海盗的劫掠，但这一次的袭击更为凶猛，这本身就足以证明他的实力，同时也预示着劫掠将会再次发生。许多人已经接受了这样的命运，但伊莎贝尔却不愿就此罢休。

When she recovered from the birth of her son, Isabel returned to her duties sooner than advised. She wouldn't have minded spending day and night with the newborn nestled against her breast, but she detested feeling idle. At the first council meeting she attended after the delivery, the scheduled business had to be set aside, as news arrived that Barbarossa had attacked the Spanish Mediterranean coast. It wasn't the first time. Although the Balearic Islands had already been raided several times by the Ottoman pirate, this time the ferocity had been greater, which in itself was a sign of his power, as well as a warning that the raids would be repeated. Many had come to accept this fate. Not Isabel.

她问道：“骚扰我们的土耳其船只从哪个港口出发？”

"From which port do the Turkish ships that are harassing us sail?" she inquired.

“夫人，我来自阿尔及尔。”阿尔巴公爵回答道。

—From Algiers, my lady —replied the Duke of Alba.

皇后抬起头，目光与那位贵族的目光相遇。

The empress raised her gaze; her eyes met those of the nobleman.

“攻击他？”他明白了。

"Attack him?" he understood.

——我们还有什么其他办法来阻止他们的袭击？

—What other way would we have to prevent their attacks?

公爵大吃一惊。他原以为要辅佐的是一位缺乏判断力和魄力的摄政王，一位总是不知所措的女士，但伊莎贝尔却截然相反：她对所有政务都充满热情，并且以坚定的语气发号施令。即便如今她身体仍因产后虚弱，也展现出一位经验老道的将军般的果断。

The duke was astonished. He had expected to guide a regent lacking judgment and drive, a lady constantly bewildered, but Isabel proved to be quite the opposite: she was interested in all matters of governance and commanded with a firm voice. Even now, her body still frail from childbirth, she displayed the decisiveness of a seasoned general.

我将请求皇帝批准我的决定。

—I will ask the emperor to approve my decision.

“如果我同意你的观点，”法德里克补充道，“很遗憾地提醒你，英国王室没有足够的资金在最佳条件下发动进攻。我们还有时间从与法国的战争中恢复过来。”

“In the event that I agree with you,” Fadrique added, “I regret to remind you that the Crown does not have the funds to carry out an assault under optimal conditions. We still have time to recover from the wars with France.”

“这些王国曾竭尽全力支持维也纳的保卫，”她说道，“如今事关自身安危，你难道怀疑他们会回应我们的请求吗？”

"These kingdoms went out of their way to support the protection of Vienna," she said. "Do you doubt that they will respond to our request, now that the cause is their own defense?"

那封寄往帝国的信件几个小时后离开了宫廷。之后，伊莎贝拉回房休息，陪伴着小费迪南德。小费迪南德又开始烦躁不安，神经兮兮的。他似乎感觉到，就在此时，一艘由巴巴罗萨指挥的战舰正从阿尔及尔驶往西班牙。由于其秘密资助者——法国国王的慷慨解囊，这艘战舰的武器装备比上次入侵时有所提升。

The letter destined for the Empire left the court a few hours later, after which Isabella retired to rest with little Ferdinand, who was once again fussy and restless, a bundle of nerves. He seemed to sense that, at that very moment, a ship under Barbarossa's command was sailing from Algiers bound for Spain. Its armament had been improved since the last incursion, thanks to the contribution of its secret benefactor: the King of France.

 

 

 

 

埃莉诺喜爱昂布瓦兹的花园。自从来到法国宫廷，她几乎每天都待在那里。另一种选择是把自己关在房间里，但她不想像母亲那样，习惯了孤独，变得悲伤，与世隔绝。几个星期以来，她都拒绝与新家庭有任何进一步的联系。萨伏依的路易丝对她彬彬有礼，却又冷若冰霜，仿佛她只是个只会做三种动作的机器人。国王在他们圆房之后，便从她的寝宫消失了，再也没有回来。他也对她彬彬有礼，所以埃莉诺找不到什么具体的过错可以抱怨。她不能要求被爱，更不能要求她的婚姻是出于自愿，而不仅仅是为了与查理达成和平。也许这就是许多女王的生活，而她之所以如此冷漠，是因为她多愁善感，觉得自己可有可无，而且太过孤独，以至于有时，死亡的念头反而能安慰她。

Eleanor loved the gardens at Amboise. Since arriving at the French court, she had spent most of her daylight hours there. The alternative would have been to shut herself away in her chamber, and she didn't want to end up like her mother, too accustomed to isolation, sad and lost to the outside world. For weeks she had ruled out any further involvement with her new family. Louise of Savoy treated her with impeccable but icy respect, as if she were an automaton with a repertoire of three gestures and no more. The king, after the consummation of their marriage, had disappeared from her bedchamber, never to return. He, too, extended courtesies to her, so that Eleanor found no specific offense to complain about. She couldn't demand to be loved, much less that her union had been desired and not merely a means to achieve peace with Charles. Perhaps this was the life of many queens, and that she felt indifference on such a scale was due to her sentimental tendency, to feeling dispensable and too alone, so much so that, at times, the idea of ​​death came to console her.

然而，在花园里，她却能自由呼吸。幸运的是，太子亨利多次陪她散步。这个十二岁的男孩是宫廷里唯一对她亲切的人，就像当年在马德里，只有埃莉诺在他被囚禁期间照顾他一样。那一刻，她忘记了自己有多么渴望被众人爱着，也忘记了在遥远的葡萄牙，一个小女孩正在长大，心中怀着对她的怨恨。

In the gardens, however, she could breathe. Fortunately, on numerous occasions, the Dauphin Henry joined her for walks. The twelve-year-old boy was the only one at court who showed her affection, just as only Eleanor had cared for him in Madrid during his captivity. For a moment, she forgot how much she missed feeling loved by so many, and also that, far away in Portugal, a little girl was growing up harboring resentment towards her.

弗朗西斯对妻子的痛苦漠不关心；他根本不在乎，懒得费心揣摩她的感受。事实上，他对她和对待已故的克劳迪娅并无二致。在他看来，婚姻是国家大事；爱情和欲望应该远离婚姻。然而，他对埃莉诺的冷漠另有原因，最主要的是，每当他见到妻子，脑海中就挥之不去他哥哥的身影。康布雷和约对他的王国极为不利，他对皇帝的敌意丝毫未减。尽管如此，屡战屡败让他打消了发动新攻势的念头。他不愿冒着再次失败的风险，因为那样会削弱他的权力。暗中支持巴巴罗萨对西班牙海岸的劫掠被证明是一个完美的解决方案：投入极少，声誉完好无损，却能对皇帝的财产造成严重损失。的确，他无法公开承认这场胜利，在所有人眼中，他永远都是欧洲统治者的二把手；但就目前而言，满足他永不停歇地惩罚自己憎恨之人的愿望就足够了。

Francis paid no attention to his wife's distress; he cared too little for it to bother deciphering her feelings. In truth, he treated her no differently than he had treated the late Claudia. Marriage seemed to him a matter of state; love and desire were to be kept far from it. However, his indifference toward Eleanor stemmed from other causes, above all from the fact that, whenever he saw his wife, he couldn't get the thought of his brother out of his mind. The peace signed at Cambrai had proven so unkind to his kingdom that his animosity toward the emperor hadn't diminished in the slightest. Nevertheless, repeated failures had dissuaded him from launching new attacks. He wouldn't risk further defeats, as his power would consequently wane. Secretly supporting Barbarossa in his raids on the Spanish coast had proven a perfect solution: minimal investment, untarnished reputation, and serious damage to the emperor's possessions. It was true that he could not publicly acknowledge the victory, and that in everyone's eyes he remained the eternal second-in-command to European rulers; but for the moment it was enough for him to satisfy his desire to never stop punishing the one he hated.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在皇宫里，玛丽和身在法国的姐姐埃莉诺一样，都以散步来寻求慰藉。她因长时间照料姨妈玛格丽特而精疲力竭，玛格丽特的伤口感染，高烧不退。查理的妹妹很珍惜这些每日的散步，让她得以反思自丈夫去世以来一直萦绕在心头的悲痛。

Meanwhile, at the imperial court, Mary, like her sister Eleanor in France, sought solace in walks. She was exhausted from the long hours she spent caring for her aunt Margaret, whose wound had become infected and was causing her to run high fevers. Charles's sister appreciated these daily walks, during which she could reflect on her own grief, which she had carried since her husband's death.

一天下午，她注意到一辆马车停在她常走的那条小路旁。一个男人走了出来，玛丽亚一眼就认出了他：是萨克森的腓特烈大帝。她纳闷他来这里做什么，但当她走到他跟前，这位贵族向她鞠躬致意时，她就知道他是在等她。

One afternoon she noticed a carriage parked beside the path she always walked. A man stepped out, and Maria recognized him instantly: it was Frederick of Saxony. She wondered what he was doing there, but when she reached him and the nobleman greeted her with a bow, she knew he had been expecting her.

—请允许我陪您一会儿好吗？

—Would you allow me to keep you company for a while?

他们沿着小路一起走，小路通向一片空地。玛丽亚注意到他手里拿着一份卷起来的文件。

They walked together along the path, which led to a clearing. Maria noticed that he was carrying a rolled-up document.

—我明白你想传达一些信息给我哥哥。

—I understand that you want to convey something to my brother.

—女士，您弄错了，您才是收件人。

—You are mistaken, ma'am, you are the intended recipient.

“我？”她问道，公爵将文件递给了她。

"Me?" she asked as the duke offered her the document.

我假设你熟悉路德的思想。你对他的思想有何看法？

—I assume you are familiar with Luther's ideas. What is your opinion of them?

玛丽亚用全新的目光审视着这份文件，语气中带着一丝犹豫。她沉默了片刻才回复。

Maria looked at the document with fresh eyes, showing some reserve. She took a while to reply.

我并不否认他的一些提议带有暗示性。令人欣慰的是，有些人研读圣经是为了追求纯洁。

—I don't deny that some of his proposals are suggestive. It's appreciated that there are those who read the Scriptures seeking purity.

卡洛斯的妹妹并非假装感兴趣。改革思想很符合她严谨的性格，在哀悼期间，她惊讶地发现自己从其中一些思想中找到了慰藉。

Carlos's sister wasn't feigning interest. Reformist ideas suited her austere personality, and during the mourning period she had surprised herself by finding solace in some of them.

——这是我的得意门生的新书。他希望你能读一读，如果你愿意，他还想把这本书题献给你。

—This is my protégé's new book. He would like you to read it and, if you wish, to have it dedicated to you.

小路在他们面前消失，无路可走了。前方是一片广袤无垠、嶙峋怪石遍布的空地。每当玛丽亚走到那里，她都会想起丈夫牺牲的战场，觉得这里多么像啊。

The path faded before them; there was no more way to go. Ahead lay the clearing, immense and dotted with crags. Whenever Maria reached it, she thought how much it resembled the battlefield where her husband had died.

我只保证我会读。

—I only promise that I will read it.

弗雷德里克点了点头。他懒得叮嘱她保密，因为一旦消息泄露，受苦的只会是她一个人。在他看来，玛丽亚是个好女人，利用她挑拨哈布斯堡家族内部矛盾让他感到有些痛苦。但他的决心早已让他顾虑尽失。

Frederick nodded. He didn't bother asking her to be discreet, because if it got out, she would be the only one who would suffer. Maria seemed like a good woman to him, and it pained him somewhat to use her to sow the seeds of discord among the Habsburgs. But his determination had long since diminished his scruples.

 

 

 

 

公爵提出带玛丽亚回宫廷，让她觐见皇帝。他还将递交一份文件，但目的却截然不同：这是一份改革者请愿书的摘要，皇帝希望将其呈递给罗马，以敦促教皇召开宗教会议。正如皇帝所要求的，这份文件措辞平静而深思熟虑，字里行间没有任何对教皇的冒犯之意。

The duke offered to take Maria back to court. She was to meet with the emperor. He would also deliver a text to him, but with a very different purpose: it was a summary of the reformers' petitions that the emperor wished to present in Rome, in order to encourage the Pope to convene the council. As the emperor had requested, the document was written in a calm and thoughtful tone, and none of its lines could be interpreted as containing any insult to the Holy Father.

进入觐见厅后，腓特烈翻阅着报纸打发时间，等待查理的到来。尽管他是世上与路德宗创始人关系最密切的人，但他却并未受到路德宗思想的影响。然而，他仍然热情地捍卫路德宗，呼吁人们享有良心自由，并谴责梵蒂冈无可辩驳的罪行。他最不希望看到的就是召开宗教会议：如果改革者与教皇媾和，他如此渴望的德国独立又将何去何从？这样的谅解只会延长教皇在帝国的统治，即便教皇的行使方式更加顺从。这位萨克森王子最渴望的是他的子民能够自治；或者更确切地说，他希望他的子民——他自己也身在其中——能够不受罗马干预地进行统治，因为罗马的干预也给国库带来了沉重的负担。

Once in the audience hall, Frederick glanced through the papers to pass the time while he waited for Charles. He remained untouched by Lutheran ideas, despite being the closest person in the world to their originator. Nevertheless, he defended them passionately, appealing to freedom of conscience and the undeniable transgressions of the Vatican. The last thing he wanted was a council: what would become of the independence of Germany, which he so desperately desired, if the reformers were to make peace with the Pope? Such an understanding would only prolong the Pontiff's authority in the Empire, even if he exercised it in a more amenable manner. And what the Saxon prince wanted above all else was for his people to govern themselves; or, rather, for his princes, among whom he counted himself, to rule without Roman interference, which was also so costly for the treasury.

查理匆匆而来，仿佛急匆匆。王子甚至来不及做任何礼节性的举动，只是敷衍地鞠了一躬。突然，皇帝站在他面前，要求他交出文本。

Charles made his entrance unceremoniously, as if he were in a hurry. The prince didn't even have time to do more than make a half-hearted bow. Suddenly, the emperor stood before him, demanding the text.

——请允许我。

—Allow me.

皇帝审阅了那份文件，同时察觉到那位贵族的举止有些不安。皇帝心中因曾庇护路德而产生的怨恨，使他无法以不同的态度对待这位贵族；他竭力克制自己，没有为此斥责路德，这一切都是为了避免加深他与宗教改革者之间的裂痕。

The emperor reviewed the document, and as he did so, he perceived that the nobleman was disconcerted by his manner. The resentment the emperor harbored for having protected Luther prevented him from treating him otherwise; he had enough to restrain himself from reprimanding him for it, all to avoid widening the rift between himself and the reformers.

——我们非常高兴您回来。您离开的时间……确实很长。但我必须说，费迪南德殿下表现得像一位伟大的政治家。

—We are delighted to have you back. Your absence has been… prolonged. But I must say that His Highness Ferdinand is performing like a great statesman.

卡洛斯被这番话惹恼了，抬起头来，停止了写作。

Carlos, annoyed by the comment, looked up from his writing.

“须知，我对和平的渴望远胜于教皇的意愿，”他说道，“如果这场冲突最终能以和解​​告终，我想我们都希望如此，那将归功于我的努力。召开大公会议是避免灾难的唯一途径。”皇帝目光锁定在贵族身上。“甚至有些人应该为我的宽容而感到庆幸，因为我没有惩罚那些其他人永远不会原谅的事情。”

“Know that my desire for peace exceeds what the Pope would wish,” he said. “If this conflict ends in reconciliation, as I suppose we all hope, it will be thanks to my efforts. The council is the only way to avert disaster.” The emperor fixed his gaze on the nobleman’s. “There are even those who should congratulate themselves on my generosity, which does not punish what others would never forgive.”

来自萨克森的男子笑了。

The man from Saxony smiled.

——我的凯撒大人，我向您保证，我每天都感谢上帝让我成为您的臣属。但愿这份喜悦是相互的，因为您在其他王国所遭受的叛乱，在这里不过是教堂里的布道而已。

—I assure you, my Caesar, that I thank God every day for being your vassal. But let the joy be mutual, for the uprisings you had to endure in other kingdoms are barely more than church sermons here.

弗雷德里克的话语在查尔斯的脑海中回荡了一整天。显然，其中暗藏着威胁，几乎难以掩饰。但事实是，这份文件表达了对和平的渴望，这位贵族桀骜不驯的性格也无法掩盖这一好消息。

Frederick's words echoed in Charles's mind for the rest of the day. It was clear that a threat was hidden within them, barely concealed. But the truth was that the document conveyed a yearning for peace, and the aristocrat's defiant nature was unable to overshadow that good news.

 

 

 

 

夜幕降临，皇帝晚饭后与妹妹私下会面。玛丽亚看到他进屋，便匆忙收起了路德的著作。

Night was falling when the emperor, after dinner, met privately with his sister. Upon seeing him enter the room, Maria hurriedly put away Luther's text.

“我有个好消息要告诉你，”他宣布道。

"I have good news for you," he announced.

—姑姑的病情好转了吗？

—Has our aunt improved?

“明亮而友善的眼睛，”卡洛斯心想。

"Bright and kind eyes," Carlos thought.

你将成为苏格兰女王。

—You will be queen of Scotland.

玛丽亚将目光转向温暖房间的炉火。她站在那里沉思了很久，直到想出了正确的答案。

Maria turned her gaze toward the fire that warmed the room. She stood contemplating it for a long time, until she came up with the right answer.

-因为？

-Because?

英格兰正在摆脱罗马的影响。那个恶棍亨利似乎毫不犹豫地继续他的疯狂行径。我们必须与岛屿建立牢固而持久的联系，以保障我们在那里的信仰健康发展。而詹姆斯国王是世上最正统的君主。

—England is escaping the influence of Rome. That wretch Henry seems to have no qualms about continuing his madness. We must establish firm and lasting ties with the islands, guaranteeing the health of our faith there. And King James is the most orthodox among men.

她太年轻了……

—She's too young…

——她单身这一点才是最重要的。机会千载难逢。

—Her single status is the only thing that matters. The opportunity is magnificent.

她感到窒息。她唯一能排解丧夫之痛的方式，就是享受平静，与亲人相伴。她想象着自己身处苏格兰，被陌生人包围，被迫强颜欢笑，违背内心的渴望，不得不将自己每时每刻都渴望丈夫的身体交付给陌生人。对卡洛斯的思念让她注定要过着虚伪孤独的生活。

The woman felt like she was suffocating. The only way she had found to cope with the pain of her widowhood was through peace and the company of her loved ones. She imagined herself in Scotland, surrounded by strangers, forced to appear charming despite what her heart desired, and having to surrender to a stranger the body that still yearned for her husband every moment. The thought of Carlos condemned her to a life of pretense and solitude.

“我不会嫁给他，”玛丽亚断然说道。“你可以说我自私，但外交上的优势并不能弥补这样的牺牲。”

"I will not marry him," Maria declared. "Call me selfish, but a diplomatic advantage does not compensate for such a sacrifice."

凯撒简直不敢相信自己刚才听到的。

Caesar could not believe what he had just heard.

——我还以为你比我们的姐姐埃莉诺更有责任心呢！

—I thought you were more responsible than our sister Eleanor!

—我愿意为你做任何你需要的事，但不是以这种方式。

—I am willing to serve you in whatever you need, but not in that way.

她昂首离开前，两人互相打量了一番。皇帝感到自己注定要一次又一次地重蹈覆辙：正是这种境况让他成为一个专横残暴的家族首领。但他知道自己不能屈服。欧洲的宗教动荡要求天主教徒团结起来。这将使他们在宗教会议上更有力量。上帝赋予他们成为君王的命运，他们的使命超越了感伤。这就是为什么他身处帝国，而不是在他渴望的地方：西班牙，与他的妻子和孩子们在一起，其中一个孩子他甚至还没见过。但查理需要其他人来履行他的职责。如果玛丽亚像之前的费迪南一样质疑他，反抗他的决定，他又如何统治如此广袤的领土呢？似乎没有人理解坚定权威的重要性。或许他们认为皇帝从专制中获得了某种快感，而事实恰恰相反。

They sized each other up with a glance before she left, head held high. The emperor felt condemned to relive the same situation over and over: the one that made him a tyrannical and ruthless head of the family. But he knew he couldn't give in. The religious turmoil in Europe demanded that Catholics unite. That would strengthen them for the council. God had marked them with a destiny of kings, and their mission transcended sentimentality. That was why he was in the Empire and not where he longed to be: in Spain, with his wife and children, one of whom he hadn't even met yet. But Charles needed the others to carry out his duties. How could he rule such vast domains if Maria, like Ferdinand before her, questioned him and rebelled against his decisions? No one seemed to understand the importance of firm authority. Perhaps they believed the emperor found a certain pleasure in despotism, when the opposite was true.

“你将为我们的信仰做出巨大贡献。我将永远感激你。”说完，他的妹妹便走进了房间。

"You will be doing a great service to our faith. I will be eternally grateful," he concluded before his sister crossed the threshold of the room.

当晚，皇帝的妹妹擦了擦额头的汗，向姑姑吐露心声。她这辈子都不打算嫁给詹姆斯，也不打算嫁给任何其他男人。玛格丽特虽然裹着厚厚的衣服，却像风中的落叶一样瑟瑟发抖，听了这话，她皱起了眉头。

That night, as she wiped the sweat from her brow, the emperor's sister confided in her aunt. She had no intention of marrying James, or any other man, for the rest of her life. Margaret, shivering like a leaf in the wind despite being bundled up in thick layers of clothing, reacted with a scowl.

“如果你仍然为丧夫之痛而难过，那是因为你还没有再婚。但这只是次要问题：卡洛斯说得对，这无疑是一段合适的婚姻。他结婚也只是出于责任。”

"If your widowhood still pains you, it's because you haven't remarried. But that's a secondary matter: Carlos is right, it's undoubtedly a suitable marriage. He, too, married for no other reason than duty."

玛丽亚感到被抛弃了。似乎没有人支持她渴望独处的愿望。她幻想退休后住进修道院，在那里度过余生，享受宁静祥和的氛围和简单的快乐，严格的作息安排让她的生活不受打扰。

Maria felt abandoned. No one seemed to support her desire for solitude. She fantasized about retiring to a convent, where she could live out her days enjoying peace and quiet and simple pleasures, under a strict routine where no one could disrupt her life.

 

 

 

 

仿佛令一位挚爱之人失望还不够，查理二世断然拒绝了妻子伊莎贝拉提出的进攻阿尔及尔基地的提议，且未作过多解释。进攻土耳其人将违背他对教皇的承诺，即优先解决路德教问题。事实上，他素来不喜主动挑起争端；这位爱好和平的皇帝更倾向于自卫而非主动出击。在他写给伊莎贝拉的信中，所有这些原因都被他以资源匮乏为由掩盖了。国库根本无力承担如此大规模的军事行动。不过，皇帝承诺一旦返回西班牙，便会着手解决这个问题。

As if disappointing just one of his loved ones weren't enough, Charles rejected, without offering much explanation, his wife's idea of ​​attacking the Algiers base. An assault against the Turk would contradict his commitment to the Pope to resolve the Lutheran question before anything else. Truthfully, it wasn't his custom to take the initiative in conflict; the pacifist emperor preferred defending himself to inflicting blows. In the letter he sent to Isabella, all these reasons were masked by the excuse of a lack of resources. The treasury simply wasn't in place to undertake such a large-scale operation. The emperor did promise, however, to address the problem as soon as he returned to Spain.

尽管伊莎贝拉理解丈夫的论点，但她第一次感觉到两人之间的和谐出现了裂痕。他们之间的距离导致了彼此的不理解。身处帝国的查理无法预见西班牙海岸正面临的威胁。此外，在她看来，这位皇帝的视野就像一个即将失明的人：他只能辨认出大致的轮廓，而无法欣赏细节，因为他需要的是一种特殊的视角，因此其他人无法理解。皇后也对丈夫略带居高临下的语气感到不满。他试图掩饰，但似乎并没有认真考虑过她的提议。难道他不信任她的判断吗？无论如何，她并非对丈夫的态度感到恼火，而是担心如果继续放任海盗逍遥法外，西班牙将会面临怎样的命运。

Although she understood her husband's arguments, Isabella sensed for the first time a breakdown in their harmony. The physical distance between them translated into incomprehension. Charles, in the Empire, was incapable of foreseeing the threat looming over the Spanish coast. Moreover, the emperor's vision seemed to her like that of a man on the verge of blindness: he could only distinguish large figures, without appreciating the details, for what was demanded of him was a privileged perspective, and therefore incomprehensible to everyone else. The empress was also offended by the slightly patronizing tone with which her husband answered her. He tried to hide it, but he didn't seem to have given her proposal much thought. Did he perhaps not trust her judgment? In any case, she wasn't so much bothered by her husband's manner as she was worried about what might become of Spain if the pirate continued to be allowed to act with impunity.

他只能祈祷。

All he could do was pray.

 

 

 

 

伊莎贝尔正在祈祷时，突然听到宫里传来一声尖叫。毫无疑问，是个女人的尖叫；她想，或许是个仆人。之后一段时间，宫里没有其他异样的声音，她便继续祈祷。不久之后，她感到有人敲门——后来，她一遍又一遍地回想起得知悲剧发生前的那段时光，羡慕自己当时的无忧无虑。出现在她面前的是弗朗西斯科·德·博尔哈。很明显，她的首席侍从一直在哭泣，并且努力克制着不哭出来。她还注意到他微微颤抖，像个病人。伊莎贝尔看到他的嘴唇动了动，但她不太明白他在说什么。他正在谈论一个孩子，一个死去的孩子；而且他用的是过去式，仿佛要将所有的希望都扼杀掉。伊莎贝尔不知不觉地来到了这里，过了一会儿，她发现自己站在一张婴儿床前，床上躺着一具僵硬的小身体，让她想起了年幼的费尔南多。但这不可能是他。她的儿子总是动来动去，而且，他总是盯着她看，非常专注。他会抓着他的衣服，用他那薄如纸片的指甲抓挠他的脸；然后他会发出咕哝声，或者哭，或者笑，仿佛他懂得的远超一个几个月大的婴儿所能理解的。躺在摇篮里的东西却什么都不会，因为它只是一个物体，没有生命，也没有颜色。伊莎贝拉无法相信这个静止的生命会是费迪南德，事实上，她花了几天时间才接受这个事实，尽管有证据表明她的儿子已经去世：宫廷里笼罩的哀悼，小男孩的缺席，她哥哥菲利普的眼泪，以及皇后内心感受到的那种如同被砍断般的痛苦。当她不得不写信告诉丈夫发生了什么事时，文字帮助她理解了这场悲剧的残酷现实。她在写信时哭泣，接下来的两天，从早到晚，她也一直在哭泣。她太想念卡洛斯的安慰了，以至于明知自己的情绪毫无道理，却还是对他发起了明显的怒火。在人前，她努力保持镇定，但事实上，那一刻，生平第一次，她不在乎示弱，因为她内心深处就是如此：心如刀绞，震惊于世间竟有如此巨大的痛苦，也为自己身为一个女人，无力改变生死的法则而感到无比沮丧。

It was during one of her prayers that Isabel heard a scream in the palace. Undoubtedly a woman's; perhaps a servant, she thought. Nothing else unusual was heard for a while, so she continued with her prayers. Shortly afterward, she felt a knock at her door—later she would recall those moments before learning of the tragedy again and again, and envy the carefree attitude she had then. The one who appeared before her was Francisco de Borja. It was clear that her chief equerry had been crying and was trying hard not to. She also noticed that he was trembling slightly, like someone ill. Isabel saw his lips move, but she didn't quite understand what he was saying. He was speaking of a child, a dead child; and he spoke of it in the past tense, extinguishing all hope. Without quite knowing how she had arrived there, Isabel found herself after a while before a child's cot, on which lay a petrified little body that reminded her of her young Fernando. But it couldn't be him. Her son was always moving, and besides, he was looking at her, very much so. It would also cling to his clothes and scratch his face with its papery nails; and then it would gurgle, or cry, or laugh as if it knew more than a baby of only a few months could possibly know. The thing lying in the cradle did none of that, because it was just an object, lifeless and colorless. Isabella couldn't conceive that this inert being could be Ferdinand, and in fact, it took her days to understand, even though there was evidence that her son had died: the mourning imposed on the court, the absence of the little boy, the tears of her brother Philip, the feeling of amputation that the empress suffered in her soul. When she had to write to her husband to tell him what had happened, the words helped her grasp the reality of the tragedy. She wept while writing that letter and also for the next two days, from dawn till dusk. She missed Carlos's comfort so much that she was visibly angry with him, even though she knew her emotion was unjustified. In front of others, she tried to maintain her composure, but the truth was that for a time, and for the first time in her life, she didn't care about showing weakness, because that's how she felt: devastated, astonished that there could be a pain greater than the person experiencing it, and frustrated at being just a woman and unable to change the rules of life and death.

伊莎贝拉收到皇帝回信的当天，便决定重新参加朝廷会议。说实话，查理的信并未给她带来多少安慰。皇帝异常平静地劝她尽快走出悲痛。伊莎贝拉接受了他的挑战，心中却充满愤怒。在最初的几次朝廷会议上，她努力集中注意力，试图做出决定，但在一次会议上，她宣布要为阿尔及尔战役筹集资金，尽管她的丈夫尚未确定开战日期。皇后从给自己设定一个使命中找到了慰藉，并很快全身心地投入其中。就这样，她的生活再次有了些许意义。她无法使家人免遭命运的捉弄，但她会竭尽全力保护她的其他孩子：西班牙人民。

The very day she received the emperor's reply to her letter, Isabella decided to resume participating in the councils. Truthfully, she found little comfort in Charles's letter. The emperor, with excessive serenity, advised her to overcome her grief as quickly as possible. Isabella accepted his challenge, not without anger. In the first government meetings, she struggled to pay attention and make decisions, but during one of them, she declared her intention to raise funds for the Algiers campaign, even though her husband had not yet set a date for such an undertaking. The empress found relief in setting herself a mission and soon dedicated herself to it wholeheartedly. In this way, her life once again possessed something resembling meaning. She could not save her family from the whims of providence, but she would do everything in her power to protect her other children: the Spanish.

 

 

 

 

——召开会议？讨论这一连串的异端邪说？焚烧圣火岂不更合适！

—A council? To discuss this string of heresies? A holy bonfire would be far more fitting!

教皇脸上露出厌恶的表情，又瞥了一眼那份列有新教徒要求的文书。他把文书重重地摔在桌子上，再也没看过一眼。与他会面的蒙莫朗西则靠回座位，准备欣赏这场好戏。

The Pope, with a grimace of disgust, glanced once more at the document listing the Protestants' demands. He slammed it down on his desk and never looked at it again. Montmorency, with whom he was meeting, settled back in his seat and prepared to enjoy the spectacle.

“皇帝的要求当然合情合理，”高卢人说道，“但是，法国可能不会支持。”

"The emperor's request certainly makes sense," said the Gaul. "However, France might refuse to support it."

教皇目光灼灼地注视着他的对话者。他之所以对这次会议感到恐惧，不仅是因为正如他所论证的，这将意味着为异端分子提供发声的平台，还因为会议可能会被用来评判他的教皇任期，而他的教皇任期很容易被发现存在缺陷。

The Pope regarded his interlocutor with eager eyes. The council terrified him not only because, as he argued, it would mean giving a platform to heretics, but also because it could be used to judge his papacy, which would easily be found to have flaws.

“你和我一样对此漠不关心，”他回答说。“如果帝国实现和平，皇帝的权力就会得到加强。我怀疑这不会让你高兴。”

"It interests you as little as it interests me," he replied. "If the Empire were pacified, the emperor would see his power strengthened. I doubt that would please you."

法国顾问一动不动。

The French advisor didn't move a muscle.

“我请求你们的支持，”克莱门特压低声音继续说道，“我想我也必须给予你们一些回报。”

—I ask for your support —Clemente continued, lowering his voice—. And I assume I must give you something in return.

此时，高卢人和教皇本应反目成仇。他们上次的合作以双方皆败的结局告终，他们当然有很多理由互相指责。但心怀怨恨只会对查理有利，因为失去强大的盟友，他的权力会更加膨胀。为了削弱皇帝的势力，忽略彼此间的不满是完全值得的。

By this point, the Gauls and the Holy Father should have been at odds. Their last collaboration had ended in disaster for both, and they certainly had much to reproach each other for. But harboring resentment would only benefit Charles, who, without a powerful front, would be able to grow even more powerful. It was well worth ignoring their mutual grievances in order to clip the emperor's wings.

“你有什么建议？”顾问问道。

"What do you suggest?" the advisor asked.

教皇假装认真思考，尽管他其实已经考虑这个想法一段时间了。

The Pope pretended to ponder it, even though he had been considering the idea for some time.

—建立在美满婚姻基础上的联盟：我的侄女凯瑟琳与亨利王子的婚姻。

—An alliance built on a good marriage: that of my niece, Catherine, with Prince Henry.

蒙莫朗西满意地点了点头。与罗马保持和谐关系，将为法国的未来描绘出一片光明。

Montmorency nodded with satisfaction. Securing harmony with Rome painted France's future in bright colors.

—至少在我看来，这是一项有益的联盟，但是……你如何才能证明不支持皇帝的意图是合理的呢？

—A beneficial union, at least in my eyes, but… How will you justify not supporting the emperor's intentions?

教宗示意秘书去拿新教徒的文本。然后他微笑着看向那位法国人。

The Holy Father gestured for his secretary to take the Protestants' text. Then he smiled at the Frenchman.

—你姐姐给了我们一个完美的借口。

—Your sister has given us the perfect excuse.

 

 

 

 

教皇的拒绝很快传遍了帝国，令查理五世倍感沉重。这位皇帝已连续数日沉浸在极度的悲痛之中。这是他第一次失去儿子，而公务使他无法前往卡斯蒂利亚悼念，也无法安慰妻子。他从妻子的来信中得知，妻子悲痛欲绝。尽管他努力在妻子和世人面前保持镇定，但事实上，这不过是一副并不合身的面具。

The Pope's refusal quickly reached the Empire and weighed heavily on Charles. The emperor had been in a state of deep distress for days. For the first time, he had lost a son, and his duties had prevented him from going to Castile to mourn him and comfort his wife, whom he knew, from the letter she had sent him, to be devastated. Although he had tried to appear composed, both to her and to the world, the truth was that this demeanor was nothing more than a mask that didn't fit him well.

雪上加霜的是，卡洛斯的指路明灯——玛格丽塔的健康状况每况愈下。她脚上的伤口感染迅速扩散，即使是最好的医生也束手无策，最终发展成坏疽。一度，卡洛斯的姑姑唯一的生路似乎只有截肢。仅仅是想到这一点就让所有人感到恐惧，但在她面前，他们都尽量淡化此事。玛格丽塔远远地听着他们的谈话，被持续数周的剧痛折磨着。她感觉自己的肢体仿佛被燃烧的利齿啃噬。只有鸦片酊能暂时缓解她的痛苦，但她必须小心，不能过量服用，否则这种短暂的解脱可能会变成永无止境的折磨。

As if that weren't enough, the health of Margarita, his guiding light, was only deteriorating. The infection in the cut on her foot had spread relentlessly, and not even the treatments suggested by the best physicians could reverse the process, which ultimately led to gangrene. At one point, the only way for Carlos's aunt to escape death was the amputation of her poisoned leg. The mere thought horrified everyone, but in her presence, they downplayed the matter. Margarita listened to them from afar, behind the bell of sharp pain that had enveloped her for weeks. She felt as if her limb were being gnawed by fiery teeth. Only laudanum offered any relief from her torment, but she had to be careful not to overuse it, or the respite it provided could become eternal.

玛格丽塔拒绝接受残害。她仍然抱有一线希望，希望能保住自己的腿，但她也清楚自己面临的风险。她没有告诉家人她已经做出了最终决定，而是请求家人给她一些时间考虑。尽管她心中仍存有一丝获救的希望，但她感觉自己正滑入一个黑暗的虚无之地，一个存在却正在消逝的地方。她不确定这是否只是一个暂时的停留，因此，她叫来了她的侄子卡洛斯。

Margarita refused to be mutilated. She clung to the possibility of healing while keeping her leg, but she was aware of the risk she faced. She didn't tell her family that her decision had been made and was final, and she concealed it by asking for time to decide. Although she maintained some hope of being saved, she felt herself slipping into a dark limbo, a place where one still exists, but is already fading away. She wasn't certain that this place was only a temporary stop, and for that reason, she summoned her nephew, Carlos.

凯撒跪在床边。他握住姑妈的手，发现冰冷刺骨，不禁打了个寒颤。她因病痛和疲惫，双眼泛着紫红。

Caesar knelt beside the bed. He shuddered as he took his aunt's hand and found it icy cold. Her eyes were rimmed with purple from illness and exhaustion.

“你为什么不肯立你的弟弟为帝国继承人？”她虚弱地低声问道。

"Why are you resisting naming your brother heir to the Empire?" she murmured weakly.

——这些对我来说都不重要了，我只祈祷你早日康复……

—That matter little to me now, I only pray for your recovery…

“忘了我吧，”她哀求道。“如果你真的想让我好，就请给予我的家人应有的尊重。”

"Forget about me," she pleaded. "If you want what's best for me, give my family the value it deserves."

皇帝感到心神不宁。他因与一位患病的女子争吵而心烦意乱，更何况是与他深爱的女子争吵。

The emperor felt uneasy. He was distressed by arguing with a sick woman, and even more so with one he loved so much.

你这个蠢货，你一心想奖赏费迪南德，却害了我的儿子。他不也是哈布斯堡家族的人吗？竟敢毁掉我的遗产……

— You fool , your desire to reward Ferdinand punishes my son. Isn't he a Habsburg too? To tear apart my inheritance…

——这就是你的盲点：你以为把帝国传给你的兄弟就会失去它。他是你的亲兄弟！而且无论发生什么，他都一直对你忠心耿耿。

—That is your blindness: believing that by bequeathing the Empire to your brother you are losing it. He is your blood! And he has been loyal to you despite everything.

卡洛斯微微点头，丝毫没有相信。

Carlos gave a slight nod, not at all convinced.

“你还是不信任他？”玛格丽塔感到困惑。

"You still don't trust him?" Margarita was perplexed.

皇帝沉默不语。他知道自己没有任何理由来证明他对弟弟依然怀有的不信任。这种感觉甚至让他感到恼火。他们的关系似乎永远被他们在西班牙的最初几周所烙印。那时，费迪南德还只是个孩子，却允许查理的对手们接近他——事后想想，任何一个从小就被培养成王位继承人的少年都会这么做。多年过去了，皇帝的怀疑却并未完全消散。或许他根本不知道该如何看待自己的弟弟。而怨恨，如同在其他方面一样，让他感到安全。

The emperor remained silent. He knew he had no argument to justify the mistrust he still harbored toward his brother. It even irritated him to feel it. It seemed their relationship had been forever marked by those first weeks together in Spain, when Ferdinand, little more than a boy, had allowed himself to be courted by Charles's opponents—something any teenager raised for the throne would have done, upon reflection. Years had passed since then, but the emperor's suspicion hadn't entirely faded. Perhaps he didn't know any other way to look at his brother. And resentment, as in other matters, made him feel secure.

 

 

 

 

教皇拒绝召开宗教会议的提议，这更加深了皇帝的担忧：全世界都在与他为敌，背叛他的不仅仅是外国人。皇帝手里拿着梵蒂冈的信，四处寻找玛丽亚。他在宫殿外找到了她，她正准备开始每日的散步。查理追上了她。

The news that the Pope had rejected the proposal to hold a council only reinforced the emperor's belief that the world was turning against him, and that it wasn't only foreigners who betrayed him. Still holding the Vatican letter, the emperor sought out Maria. He found her outside the palace, about to begin her daily walk. Charles caught up with her.

—你竟然让路德把一篇经文献给你？！

—You let Luther dedicate a text to you?!

她转过身，几乎掩饰不住内心的满足。

She turned around. She could barely hide her satisfaction.

苏格兰国王拒绝娶我这样的异教徒，对吧？

—The King of Scotland refuses to marry a heretic like me, doesn't he?

皇帝明白了妹妹的诡计，他其实早已有所怀疑，他的心跳开始加速。

The emperor understood his sister's trick, which he had already suspected, and his heart began to race.

“是教皇拒绝召开宗教会议！而你只是个借口。”卡洛斯念道：“未能将异端邪说从自己家族中根除的人，无权强加自己的解决方案。”

"It's the Pope who refuses to convene the council! And you're the excuse." Carlos read the text: "He who has not banished heresy from his own family has no authority to impose his solutions."

玛丽亚震惊得说不出话来。她从未预料到会造成这样的后果。这时，她听到身后传来一个男人的声音。

Maria fell silent, stunned. She had never foreseen such a consequence. Then a male voice could be heard behind her.

—发生了什么事？

—What's happening?

听到愤怒的叫喊声，费尔南多离开了宫殿，加入到他们中间。在花园里，他感受到了一种令人难以忍受的气氛。

Alerted by the angry shouts, Fernando had left the palace to join them. In the gardens, he encountered an unbearable atmosphere.

“我的妹妹强迫我用武力解决基督教的分裂！”凯撒抱怨道，他紧张地预感到这件事会给他带来怎样的未来。

"Our sister is forcing me to resolve the Christian schism by force!" complained Caesar, nervous as he glimpsed the future that this held for him.

“我不知道你在指控他什么，”另一个人回答说，“但我怀疑他做出你建议的决定没有任何借口。”

—I don't know what you're accusing him of —replied the other—, but I doubt there's any excuse for taking the decision you're suggesting.

皇帝跨越了与哥哥之间的距离，直截了当地将教皇的信递给了他。

The emperor bridged the distance that separated him from his brother and brusquely handed him the Pope's letter.

——不召开任何议会！除了镇压，我还能有什么其他办法？

—There will be no council! What other solution is in my hands but repression?

听到最后一个字，费尔南多感到一阵寒意袭遍全身。

Upon hearing that last word, Fernando felt a chill run through him.

—如果教皇对此事不采取任何行动，你也没有义务履行你向他作出的解决问题的承诺。

—If the Pope does nothing about the matter, you are not obliged to keep the promise you made to him to resolve it.

—我发誓不仅在他面前，也在上帝面前守护我们的信仰！

—I pledged to watch over our faith not only before him, but before God!

卡洛斯的兄弟很生气，因为他生活在一个与世隔绝的、充满无形价​​值的世界里，而不是生活在一个充满人、政治以及两者之间复杂关系的世界里。

Carlos's brother was incensed by the fact that he lived isolated in the world of intangible values, not in the world of men, politics, and the complex relationship between the two.

——我亲爱的兄弟，冷静一下。你这是在挑起德国的战争！难道你没意识到苏莱曼会利用这场冲突的机会进攻帝国吗？

—My dear brother, come down to earth for a moment. You're talking about provoking a war in Germany! Don't you realize that Suleiman will use the conflict as an opportunity to attack the Empire?

从凯撒的表情来看，人们会认为他觉得这个想法很荒谬。

Judging by Caesar's grimace, one would have said that he found the idea absurd.

“没有任何迹象表明他打算这样做。他肯定还在为围攻维也纳失败而恢复元气。现在正是扼杀异端邪说的良机！”

"There's no indication he intends to do such a thing. He must still be recovering from the failure of his siege of Vienna. Now is the time to nip heresy in the bud!"

—别把我算在内，我不会参与这场战斗。

—Don't count me in that fight.

玛丽亚经常听玛格丽塔讲述她兄弟俩关系紧张的故事。但她一直以为那种男性之间的竞争冲突早已成为过去。如今亲眼目睹他们的对峙，她感觉自己仿佛在观看历史的重演，一场她自己当初用那个让她如今无比后悔的伎俩挑起的幼稚闹剧。

Maria had often heard Margarita tell the story of her brothers' difficult relationship. But she had considered those clashes of male competitiveness a thing of the past. Now that she was witnessing their confrontation, she felt as though she were watching a reenactment of the past, a display of immaturity that she herself had instigated with that trick she now so deeply regretted.

“我乐意放弃你，”查理回答说，“为了对抗异端，并立你为帝国继承人。”

—I will gladly renounce you —replied Charles—. To fight against the heretic, and to name you successor to the Empire.

 

 

 

 

夜幕降临时，费尔南多离开了法庭，法庭里一片令人不安的沉默，大家都失去了食欲，早早地回到了各自的公寓。

By nightfall, Fernando had left the court, where an uncomfortable silence settled in, appetite was lost, and everyone retired early to their apartments.

当宫廷沉睡时，玛格丽塔再次感到灼热的利齿在她腿上肆虐，那感觉异常强烈。仿佛岩浆喷洒在皮肤上，又像是无数把匕首刺穿了她的血肉。泪水涌上她的唇边，她强忍着疼痛，不让自己的呻吟声吵醒任何人。即便有人照料，又有什么用呢？侍女和亲戚们投来的怜悯目光，尤其是玛丽亚那充满悲伤的眼神，令她倍感痛苦。她伸手去拿放在床边家具上的鸦片酊。她将滴管放在舌头上，滴入了常规剂量。她想着这药要多久才能起效，而且对于她正在遭受的这种折磨，它又能起到多大的作用呢？然后，她举起瓶子，一口气喝光了。

When the court was asleep, Margarita again felt the fiery teeth ravaging her leg with unusual fury. It felt like lava sprayed on her skin and a thousand daggers piercing her flesh. Tears sprang to her lips, and she stifled her cries of pain so as not to wake anyone. What good would it do to be attended to? The pitying looks she received from her ladies and relatives, and even more so from Maria's, so profoundly sad, were painful. She reached for the laudanum, which lay on a piece of furniture near the bed. She placed the dropper on her tongue and dispensed the routine dose. She thought about how long it would take to take effect, and how little relief it would offer against an attack like the one she was suffering. Then she raised the bottle to her lips and drank until it was empty.

他安然离世，却无药可医。

And he rested, without remedy.

 

 

 

 

玛格丽特的葬礼对查理来说几乎像是一场梦。回想起来，他意识到最近他曾守候过两位对他至关重要的人的遗体——希耶夫尔和加蒂纳拉。虽然两次他都目睹了他们如同雕像般僵硬的模样，但他却从未预料到自己走向姑姑灵柩时的感受。除了她，他别无其他母亲，对此他心怀感激。他对其他人没有任何记忆，唯一痛苦的记忆是最后几个小时的景象，是玛丽发现她冰冷的遗体和紧握鸦片酊瓶的手时发出的尖叫声。查理否定了她死于意外的可能性。像她这样虔诚的信徒，没有最后一次领受圣餐就离世是不合适的。毫无疑问，悲痛蒙蔽了她的双眼。她将与上帝重聚，并成为他的顾问。想到这里，皇帝露出了微笑，并品味着从眼中流出的苦涩泪水。上帝第一次取走了他的一部分灵魂。

Margaret's funeral had an almost unreal quality for Charles. If he thought back, he realized that in recent times he had kept vigil over the bodies of two people important to him, Chièvres and Gattinara. Although on both occasions he had been struck by the sight of a man reduced to a statue, he had not been prepared for what he felt as he approached his aunt's bier. He had had no other mother but her, and he was grateful for that. He had no other memory of anyone else, and the only painful ones were those of the last few hours, those that had followed Marie's scream when she found the lifeless body and the hand clutching the laudanum bottle. Charles dismissed the possibility that her death had been accidental. It was not fitting for a believer like her to depart without having received communion one last time. Undoubtedly, grief had blinded her. She would be reunited with God, and she would become his advisor. That thought made the emperor smile and savor the bitter tears that flowed from his eyes. For the first time, God was taking a part of his soul.

 

 

 

 

费尔南多前来吊唁姑妈，站在灵堂旁时，也忍不住落泪。兄妹俩对视一眼，却一言不发。玛丽亚在悲痛的迷雾中察觉到了这一点，心中愤慨。这场悲剧怎能丝毫不伤及他们的骄傲？这时，她想起姑妈临终前对她说的话：“做维系他们关系的纽带。”玛格丽塔深知她所言非虚；正是她与萨伏依的路易莎的斡旋，才结束了与法国的战争。铭记这一里程碑，激励着她听从玛格丽塔的劝告。凡是男人拆散的，女人终将让他们重聚。

When Fernando arrived to pay his respects to his aunt and stood beside the chapel of rest, he too wept. The siblings glanced at each other, but exchanged no words. Through the haze of grief, María noticed this and was indignant. How could this tragedy not diminish their pride in the slightest? Then she recalled the last words she had heard from her aunt: "Be the thread that binds them together." Margarita knew what she was talking about; only her intervention, along with that of Luisa of Savoy, had brought an end to the wars with France. Remembering this milestone encouraged her to follow Margarita's advice. What men had separated, a woman would once again reunite.

 

 

 

 

几天后，玛丽亚写信给她的妹妹埃莉诺，就此事征求意见。当时的法国王后埃莉诺比玛丽亚更了解她的兄弟们，因为她与他们相识多年。这封信送到了昂布瓦兹宫廷，但和所有寄给王后的信件一样，它首先经由萨伏依的路易丝之手。路易丝读完信后，在《康布雷和约》中为写信人的灵魂祈祷，然后匆匆告知弗朗西斯，帝国内部正在发生一场分裂，这场分裂甚至可能比宗教分裂更有利可图。当时，弗朗西斯正与他的儿子们进行着严格的剑术训练，他津津有味地品味着哈布斯堡家族的危机，仿佛那是一道美味佳肴。

Days later, Maria wrote to her sister Eleanor for advice on the matter. The then Queen of France knew her brothers far better than Maria did, having known them for many years. The letter reached the court at Amboise, but, like all those intended for the consort, it first passed through the hands of Louise of Savoy. Once she had read it, the king's mother prayed for the soul of her correspondent in the Peace of Cambrai and then hastened to tell Francis that a schism was taking place within the Empire, one that could be even more profitable than the religious one. The monarch, who was enjoying a rigorous sword training session with his sons, savored the Habsburg crisis as if it were a delicacy.

 

 

 

 

路易莎和弗朗西斯科都不知道莱昂诺尔的精明，因为他们与她相处的时间不多，所以没有注意到她的能力。他们只知道她很聪明，但认为她幼稚。否则，卡洛斯的妹妹为何会在发现丈夫有情妇出轨后如此愤怒？难道她没有预料到这种皇室习俗吗？他们没有意识到，他们眼中的莱昂诺尔的幼稚仅仅是多愁善感，因此他们没有预料到，当她发现丈夫的背叛后，她会做出同样的反应。

Neither Luisa nor Francisco were aware of Leonor's shrewdness, for having spent little time with her, they hadn't noticed her abilities. They knew only that she was intelligent, yes, but they considered her childish. Why else would Carlos's sister have been outraged upon discovering that her husband had a habit of cheating on her with a mistress? Had she not expected such a regal custom? They didn't realize that what they considered childish in Leonor was merely sentimental, and therefore they didn't anticipate that upon discovering her betrayal, she would react in kind.

当太子亨利以远比表面看起来更天真的语气告诉查理的妹妹，法国国王已经察觉到皇帝与斐迪南之间的裂痕，并且打算唆使路德教徒利用这一点时，王后立即将此事告知帝国。她请求这位年轻的王子出面干预，确保信件能够送达目的地：她早就注意到收到的信件封口存在问题。亨利犹豫了：如果他帮助王后，就等于帮了皇帝一个忙，他对皇帝怀恨在心，因为他曾被囚禁在马德里。但此刻，他觉得自己更应该感谢继母，而不是折磨他的父亲——他的父亲总是用军事训练折磨他。太子答应了，尽管他认为自己此举已经偿还了对埃莉诺的恩情。从此以后，他将只效忠法国，并会兴高采烈地庆祝西班牙的失败。

When the Dauphin Henry told Charles's sister, with less innocence than he appeared, that the French king was aware of the rift between the emperor and Ferdinand, and that he intended to encourage the Lutherans to exploit it, the queen hastened to inform the Empire. She asked the young prince to intervene so that the letter would reach its destination: she had long noticed irregularities in the sealing of the letters that arrived. Henry hesitated: if he helped her, he would be doing the emperor a favor, for whom he harbored an endless grudge for the captivity he had suffered in Madrid. But at that moment, he felt more indebted to his stepmother than to his father, who tormented him with military exercises. The Dauphin agreed, though with this gesture he considered his debt to Eleanor settled. From then on, he would serve only France, and he would celebrate Spain's failures with enthusiasm.

 

 

 

 

莱昂诺尔的信函顺利送达，信中既有关于如何处理查理和费迪南之间冲突的建议，也有关于法国战略的警告。信中，玛丽女王亲手将信送到了玛丽手中。她无力阻止巴巴罗萨的舰队再次进攻西班牙海岸，这次的目标是加的斯，而这支舰队得到了法国的资助。弗朗西斯甚至没有将这一计划告知他的儿子。家族危机以及皇帝不在西班牙领地，促使法国君主继续削弱他。时机绝佳；此外，他深知整个帝国的命运都系于西班牙的安危。如果他能破坏西班牙的稳定，这场他并不被视为敌人的战争，将成为他最伟大的胜利。

Leonor's letter, which included advice on how to handle the conflict between Charles and Ferdinand and a warning about French strategy, reached its destination without hindrance: Mary's hands. She could not prevent Barbarossa's fleet, duly supported with French funds, from attacking the Spanish coast again, this time Cádiz. Francis had not even informed his son of this plan. The family crisis and the emperor's absence from his Spanish domains had spurred the French monarch to continue weakening him. The opportunity was perfect; moreover, he knew that the entire Empire depended on the health of Spain. If he disrupted it, this war, in which he was not seen as an enemy, could become his greatest victory.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在德国，斐迪南勉强适应了远离宫廷的生活。他原以为远离宫廷就能重获自由的乐趣，但事实是，回归闲散的生活令他难以忍受。他习惯于干预政事，而现在一切都由他人替他做主。每当他偶然得知国家出现问题，出于习惯，他的大脑便会立即做出反应，寻找解决办法；然而，这种努力在那时已变得毫无意义。日子如同他乘坐的马车般飞驰而过，眼前的景色虽然近在眼前，他却无法触及，它不停地变化着，对他的目光漠不关心。这令他感到绝望。

Meanwhile, in Germany, Ferdinand was barely coping with life away from court. He had believed that by distancing himself from it he would experience the pleasure of regained freedom, but the truth was that the return to idleness was unbearable. He was accustomed to intervening in matters of government, and now everything was decided behind his back. When he happened to learn of a state problem, his mind, out of habit, reacted immediately, searching for solutions; an exercise that, by then, had become pointless. The days slipped by as if he were in a carriage speeding along, before which a landscape paraded by that, even though it was right in front of him, he could not reach, and which moved ceaselessly, indifferent to his gaze. It drove him to despair.

玛丽亚经常来看望他。费尔南多很高兴见到她，但他们的谈话总是以他妹妹催促他回法庭而告终。因此，他最终只能编造一些最牵强的借口来躲避她，不得不再次重申他永远不会回到那个让他感觉像个闯入者的地方。

Maria visited him frequently. Fernando enjoyed seeing her, but their conversations always ended with his sister urging him to return to court. Therefore, he ended up inventing the most mundane excuses to avoid receiving her and having to say again that he would never return to a place where he felt like an intruder.

几周后，他收到了萨克森的腓特烈的来信。信的内容不多：腓特烈对奥地利的玛格丽特去世表示哀悼，并对斐迪南目前的处境表示慰问。信的最后，他邀请斐迪南见面。查理的兄弟因遭受排斥而感到窒息，便准备好了马匹。

A few weeks later, he received a message from Frederick of Saxony. It didn't say much: he expressed his condolences for the death of Margaret of Austria and the situation in which Ferdinand now found himself. In the last line, he invited him to meet. Suffocated as he was by the ostracism he suffered, Charles's brother prepared his horse.

这次遭遇发生在茂密的森林里，没有小路，对行人来说毫无吸引力。那里是狼和其他对人类怀有敌意的害兽的领地。

The encounter took place in a dense forest, without paths, unappealing to walkers. It was territory of wolves and other vermin hostile to humans.

“我能为您做些什么？”费尔南多问这位贵族。“我警告您，我不希望您的门徒将任何书籍献给我。”

"What can I do for you?" Fernando asked the nobleman. "I warn you that I do not wish your protégé to dedicate any book to me."

费德里科面带微笑，心情并未受到影响。

Federico smiled, without his mood being disturbed.

——你会知道教皇已经否决了这次会议。

—You will know that the Pope has rejected the council.

-是的。

-Yeah.

但我怀疑这并不意味着他轻视路德教问题。如果谈判解决方案不能让他满意，那是因为他更倾向于其他流血冲突的方案。

—But I doubt that means he disdains the Lutheran problem. If a negotiated solution doesn't please him, it's because other solutions, involving bloodshed, do.

费尔南多试图找到答案。最终，一切都归于沉默，这反而印证了那位萨克森人的判断。

Fernando tried to find an answer. In the end, everything remained in silence, which only served to prove the man from Saxony right.

——你要知道，我们会对你兄弟的每一次攻击都予以回击。必要时，我们甚至会脱离帝国。除非帝国的统治方式截然不同……就像你经常吹嘘的那样。

—Know that we will respond to every attack from your brother. We will even secede from the Empire if necessary. Unless it were ruled in a very different way… the way you so often boast of.

费尔南多被狼嚎声吓了一跳。在卡斯蒂利亚，他曾被迫逃离过一头这样的野兽。他记得那场惊心动魄的追逐，记得那犬吠声在他身后急促的喘息；也记得之后回到宫廷时，虽然浑身颤抖，但总算安全了，心中涌起的平静。无论他在帝国待了多少年，一切都让他想起西班牙。在那里，他曾无数次听到腓特烈的邀请。

Fernando jumped at the sound of a wolf howling. Once, in Castile, he had had to flee from one of those beasts. He remembered the desperate chase and the canine's panting at his back; and the peace he felt afterward, upon reaching the court, still trembling but safe. However many years he had spent in the Empire, everything reminded him of Spain. He had heard Frederick's offer there a hundred times.

—你凭什么认为我会背叛我的哥哥？

—What makes you think I would be willing to betray my brother?

“他对待你的方式或许会激怒你，因为在所有人眼中这都是不公正的。但这并非促使你接受成为我们君主的原因，而是让你意识到，在查理手中，帝国正走向战争和分裂。当你意识到自己本可以阻止这一切时，你的良心能否承受这样的重负？”

"The way he treats you might incite you, since it is unjust in everyone's eyes. But that will not be what leads you to accept becoming our sovereign, but rather the knowledge that in Charles's hands, the Empire is headed for war and schism. Will your conscience bear that burden, knowing that you could have prevented it?"

这种论调与那些希望他登上王位的西班牙人所使用的论调几乎如出一辙。“只有你才能拯救西班牙！”

The argument was hardly different from the one used by the Spaniards who had wanted to see him on the throne. "Only you can save Spain!"

费尔南多心想，上帝是不是给了他第二次机会，让他改正过去的错误。

Fernando wondered if God was giving him a second chance to correct his past decisions.

 

 

 

 

那是大公与腓特烈之间多次会面中的第一次。查理的弟弟经过深思熟虑，制定了一个计划。

That was the first of several meetings between the archduke and Frederick. Charles's brother, after careful consideration, had devised a plan.

尽管他们的会面极其隐秘，皇帝的密探最终还是发现了。皇帝察觉到他的兄弟正受到路德教徒的诱惑，便下令跟踪他。得知他与撒克逊人会面后，皇帝高度警惕；因为如果说在卡斯蒂利亚时期，他曾担心兄弟的忠诚度会受到影响，毕竟当时支持他的不过是一群桀骜不驯的贵族，那么这一次，他的兄弟完全可以指望得到半个德国的支持。

Although their meetings were conducted with the utmost secrecy, the emperor's spies eventually discovered them. Alerted that his brother was being tempted by the Lutherans, the emperor had ordered him to be followed. Learning of his meetings with the Saxon put him on high alert; for if in Castile he had feared for his loyalty, when those who supported him were little more than a band of unruly aristocrats, this time his brother could well count on the backing of half of Germany.

无论如何，卡洛斯的焦虑远不及他的忧郁。他多么希望自己错了，多么希望能够彻底信任他的哥哥，多么希望能够听从他可怜的姑妈的建议，立他为继承人，即使他永远也无法摆脱对背叛挥之不去的恐惧。

Carlos's anxiety, in any case, was less than his melancholy. He would have liked to be wrong, to trust his brother once and for all, to follow his poor aunt's advice and make him his successor, even though he would never be free of a lingering fear of betrayal.

在叛乱完成之前，他派了一支帝国卫队前往斐迪南的住所，逮捕了他，而大公没有表现出任何抵抗。

Before the sedition was consummated, he sent an imperial squad to Ferdinand's residence, who arrested him without the archduke showing any resistance.

 

 

 

 

—我想查明阴谋者是谁，以及他们掌握了哪些力量。

—I wanted to find out who the conspirators were and what forces they had at their disposal.

凯撒目不转睛地盯着他的兄弟。费迪南德看起来衣衫褴褛——头发蓬乱，衣衫褴褛——就像一个毫无预警被捕的罪犯。

The Caesar stared at his brother without blinking. Ferdinand looked disheveled—his hair unkempt, his clothes scruffy—like a criminal arrested without warning.

“你以为我会天真到相信这种借口吗？”卡洛斯反驳道，“你原本计划起来反抗我！”

"Do you think I'm naive enough to believe that excuse?" Carlos retorted. "You were planning to rise up against me!"

那句指责在客厅的墙壁间回荡。目睹这一切的玛丽亚感到一阵眩晕。

The accusation echoed off the walls of the living room. Maria, who was watching the scene, felt a jolt.

“我绝不会那样做，”费尔南多宣称。

"I will never do it," Fernando declared.

—我知道你的愿望！

—I know your desires!

——还有我对你的忠诚！我并非事事都支持你，但这仅仅说明问题。如果时机成熟，我定会与你并肩作战，你难道不怀疑吗？我们拥有相同的信仰……

—And my loyalty too! The fact that I don't support you in every decision means nothing more than that. If the time came, I would have fought by your side, do you doubt it? We share the same faith…

“还有血，”玛丽亚插嘴道。

—And blood —María interjected.

兄弟俩被她的插手惹恼了，转过身来看着她，但他们察觉到她受到了他们冲突的影响，于是便开始关注她。

The brothers turned to her, annoyed by her intervention, but they perceived that she was so affected by their confrontation that they paid attention to her.

“我们面临着巨大的危险，”年轻女子继续说道，“改革者的阴谋诡计就证明了这一点。如果我们不团结起来，又怎能阻止他们轻而易举地毁灭我们？不要让我们的先辈白白牺牲。让我们吸取他们的教训！”

“Grave dangers lie in wait for us,” the young woman continued. “The intrigues of the reformers prove it. If we do not stand together, how can we prevent them from destroying us with little effort? Let the lives of our ancestors not have been in vain. Let us learn their lessons!”

玛格丽塔的灵魂随后在房间里游荡，虽然她没能给卡洛斯或费尔南多带来她所希望的平静，但她至少成功地结束了这场争吵。

Margarita's spirit then wandered through the room, and although she did not manage to instill all the peace she would have liked in either Carlos or Fernando, she at least succeeded in putting an end to the argument.

 

 

 

 

起初，远处传来一阵隆隆声。若非紧接着是地震，人们或许会以为是狂风呼啸。帝国的哨兵们急忙派信使返回帝国。他们的哨所距离所守卫的匈牙利边境很远，但只有迅速发出警告，才能阻止地平线上出现的军队越过边境。信使策马扬鞭而去，守卫们面面相觑，难以置信。仅仅三年前，他们才经历过同样的境况。帝国收复匈牙利，驱逐入侵的土耳其人后，他们曾坚信噩梦不会重演，至少不会持续太久。事实上，长期生活在威胁之下简直是一种折磨。但哨兵们敏锐的目光没有错：苏莱曼大帝的军队卷土重来。

First, a distant rumble was heard. It would have passed for a noisy wind had it not been followed by an earthquake. The imperial sentinels hastened to send messengers back to the Empire. Their posts were a great distance from the Hungarian border they guarded, but only by sending a swift warning could they prevent it from being violated by the armies that appeared on the horizon. As the messengers galloped off, the guards looked at each other in disbelief. It had been only three years since they had lived through the same situation. When the Empire recovered Hungary, driving out the Turks who had invaded it, they had convinced themselves that the nightmare would not be repeated, at least not for long. The truth was that living constantly under the threat would have been torture. But the sentinels' keen eyesight did not deceive: the army of Suleiman the Magnificent was back.

 

 

 

 

奥斯曼帝国即将进攻的消息对德国人来说犹如一剂良药，抚慰了他们的创伤，或者至少有效地缓解了他们的痛苦，以至于在一段时间内，这些创伤都被人忽略了。皇帝甚至无需开口，他的兄弟就欣然同意与他并肩作战，组织防御，日复一日，直至黎明。在共同对抗外部威胁时，他们之间的分歧显得微不足道。查理为自己低估了斐迪南的警告而感到羞愧，他曾说过苏莱曼随时可能发动进攻。毫无疑问，他的兄弟比他更了解帝国的自然规律。他也明白了为什么在斐迪南大公确保改革派为抵御奥斯曼帝国的进攻出力时，自己拒绝与他们直接对抗：他们不能与改革派为敌；尤其是在苏莱曼随时可能来袭的情况下。皇帝承诺将寻求和平解决德国宗教冲突的方案。他将完成阻止信仰分裂的使命，但不会采取激进的、弥赛亚式的措施来加深分裂。

The news of the imminent Ottoman attack acted as a miraculous balm for the Germans, healing their wounds or, at least, alleviating them effectively enough that, for a time, they went unnoticed. The emperor didn't have to say a word for his brother to readily agree to work shoulder to shoulder with him in organizing the defense, every day until dawn. Working together against the external threat, their differences seemed ridiculous. Charles felt ashamed for having underestimated Ferdinand's warning that Suleiman could attack them at any moment. Undoubtedly, his brother knew the laws of nature of the Empire better than he did. He also understood why he had refused a direct confrontation with the reformers when the archduke secured their contribution to the defense against the Ottomans: they couldn't afford to make them their enemies; not then, with Suleiman knocking at their doors every so often. The emperor pledged to seek peaceful solutions to the German religious discord. He would fulfill his mission of preventing the schism of his faith, but without radical and messianic measures deepening it.

 

 

 

 

驻扎在匈牙利的帝国军队人数众多，土耳其人甚至没有抵抗就撤退了。当查理和斐迪南得知土耳其人撤退的消息时，他们交换了一个眼神，那是玛格丽特一直渴望看到的。

The imperial forces stationed in Hungary were so numerous that the Turks withdrew without even putting up a fight. When they learned of their retreat, Charles and Ferdinand exchanged the look that Margaret had always longed for.

 

 

 

 

苏莱曼大帝之前的胜利喜悦席卷了德国，也无疑席卷了宫廷。然而，来自西班牙的消息却给所有人的心情蒙上了一层不和谐的色彩：阿尔瓦公爵法德里克·阿尔瓦雷斯·德·托莱多驾崩，他的孙子费迪南德继承了爵位。皇帝毫不怀疑，这位年轻人拥有近乎魔幻般的魅力和惊人的智慧，足以胜任这份荣耀。但他心中却涌起一丝不安，因为他亲眼目睹了整整一代人的逝去，而这一代人此前一直是他统治世界的支柱。加蒂娜拉、玛格丽特，如今又是法德里克；上帝似乎想让他束手无策。然而，他明白，自古以来，死亡都会在每个人心中激起同样的恐惧，夺走前人的性命。新的时代终将到来，即便起初步履蹒跚。生活本身，自有其无情的法则，需要勇气。

The joy of victory before Suleiman swept through Germany, and undoubtedly the court, though news from Spain cast a discordant note over everyone's mood: the Duke of Alba, Fadrique Álvarez de Toledo, had died, making his grandson Ferdinand the new bearer of the title. The emperor had no doubt that this young man, with his almost magical charisma and dazzling intelligence, would be worthy of the honor. But he felt a sense of unease at having witnessed, in such a short time, the disappearance of an entire generation, which until then had served as a pillar of the world he ruled. Gattinara, Margaret, and now Fadrique; God wanted him to be helpless. However, he understood that, since the beginning of time, death had provoked this same fear in every man with the sweeping away of his predecessors, and that the new had to prevail, even if it did so hesitantly at first. Life itself, with its implacable rules, demanded courage.

皇帝任命玛丽为尼德兰摄政王的决定令众人欣喜。或许最不高兴的要数玛丽本人了，她原本更希望安享晚年。但当她的哥哥承诺不再为她安排婚事时，她接受了这一职位。如果这能让她永远哀悼亡夫，那么一切责任都是值得的。

The emperor's decision to appoint Mary regent of the Netherlands pleased everyone. Perhaps the least pleased was Mary herself, who would have preferred to remain in the tranquility of her life until the end of her days. But when her brother promised in return never to offer her in marriage again, she accepted the position. The responsibilities were worth it if they allowed her to mourn her husband eternally.

 

 

 

 

你将继承帝国。

—You will inherit the Empire.

听到哥哥的判决，费尔南多的眼眶瞬间盈满了泪水。但他强忍着泪水，神情严肃，就像一个士兵获得梦寐以求却又理应获得的勋章一样。

Fernando's eyes welled up with tears when he heard the sentence from his brother. He refused to break down, remaining serious, with the expression of a soldier receiving a medal he longs for but knows he deserves.

卡洛斯补充道：“我只请求，在你去世的时候，这份荣誉能从你传给我的儿子菲利普。”

—I only ask that the honor, when your day comes, pass from you to my son Philip —Carlos added.

那就这样吧。

—So be it.

大公对凯撒的让步感到十分意外，以至于无法完全理解接受这一条件的后果。那一刻如同走过一条崎岖坎坷、障碍重重的道路，终于抵达终点，而他们两人都曾险些迷失方向。除此之外，他们几乎没有再说任何话。那些未说出口的话，他们彼此心照不宣，也觉得最好还是藏在心底：他们终于觉得自己配得上彼此。

The archduke was too surprised by the Caesar's concession to fully grasp the consequences of accepting such a condition. The moment possessed the magic of the end of a rocky and obstacle-strewn road, one on which both had nearly strayed. They exchanged hardly any words beyond these. What they left unsaid, they both knew, and it seemed fitting to keep it to themselves: that at last they felt worthy of one another.

 

 

 

 

几周后，卡斯蒂利亚宫廷陷入一片忙碌之中。伊莎贝拉亲自监督着迎接丈夫归来的仪式的每一个细节。皇后显得异常紧张，如同孩童一般。在查理长期不在的这段时间里，她每天都在期盼着这一刻的到来。事实上，过去的几个月对她来说尤其难熬。当她得知奥斯曼帝国再次向帝国发起进攻，皇帝也致信请求她的援助时，她被迫交出了为阿尔及尔战役筹集的资金。这样做，她违背了对西班牙人民的承诺：他们为抵御巴巴罗萨入侵而捐献的资金将无法再用于保卫海岸。因此，海岸线注定要遭受土耳其海盗的进一步袭击。尽管伊莎贝拉明白她不能拒绝保护帝国领土免受异教徒的入侵，但她痛心的是，她统治的王国总是屈从于其他利益，而非她的利益。尽管事态发展令她失望，但小费迪南的死带给她的悲痛却显而易见。她知道这种未竟之感永远不会消失，她必须每天想办法将它埋葬。

A few weeks later, the Castilian court was engulfed in frenetic activity. Isabella herself oversaw every detail of the ceremony with which her husband was to be welcomed back. The Empress was visibly nervous, like a child. She had dreamed of this moment every day during Charles's long absence, and the truth was that the last few months had been especially difficult for her. When she learned that the Ottomans had once again positioned themselves before the Empire and the Emperor wrote to her requesting her assistance, she was forced to hand over the funds raised for the Algiers campaign. In doing so, she betrayed her word to the Spanish people: the money they had contributed to defend their coasts against Barbarossa would no longer serve that purpose. Consequently, the coastline was condemned to suffer further attacks from the Turkish pirate. Although Isabella understood that she could not refuse to protect the imperial domains from an invasion by the infidel, it pained her that the kingdoms she ruled always submitted to other interests, and never to her own. Disappointed as she was by events, her grief over the death of young Ferdinand became evident. She knew that this feeling of incompleteness would never leave her, and that she would have to find a way to bury it each day.

我亲爱的。

—My beloved.

查尔斯在侍童、贵族和随从的簇拥下入场，但皇后的目光却只落在他身上。她记得他风度翩翩，却又不及当年那般英俊潇洒；他曾让她心生悸动，却又并非此刻这般炽热的激情。

Charles made his entrance surrounded by a swarm of pages, nobles, and attendants, but the Empress had eyes only for him. She remembered him as gallant, but not quite so; and capable of provoking in her a devastating sensation, though not the passion that suddenly coursed through her.

我亲爱的。

—My beloved.

当他们拥抱在一起时，伊莎贝尔才意识到自己这些年来是多么需要他，意识到自己内心早已崩溃，却还要强颜欢笑，是多么厌倦。她依偎在他的胸膛上，避开旁人的视线，为那个到来的人哭泣，也为那个永远不会回来的人哭泣。

When they embraced, Isabel realized how much she had needed him all this time, how tired she was of appearing whole even though she was crumbling inside. Sheltered against his chest, out of sight of those who witnessed the encounter, she wept for the one who had arrived and for the one who would never return.

12

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

那天下午，巴利亚多利德的天空飘着皇帝从未见过的浓郁橙色云彩。他勒住马，凝视着它们，陷入沉思。西班牙的色彩和宜人的气候抚慰着他的心灵。他在帝国的动荡岁月已经过去，事实上，他并不怀念。他所需要的一切，以及他最爱的人，都笼罩在卡斯蒂利亚那片果香四溢的云朵之下。

That afternoon, the clouds in the Valladolid sky were tinged with the most intense orange the emperor had ever seen. He halted his horse and gazed at them, lost in thought. Spain soothed his soul with its colors and its ever-pleasing climate. His turbulent time in the Empire was behind him, and the truth was, he didn't miss it. Everything he needed, and those he loved most, lay beneath the fruity clouds of Castile.

伊莎贝尔也骑着马，来到他身边。卡洛斯凝视着她，渴望亲吻她。夕阳的余晖为她苍白疲惫的脸庞增添了几分神采。她的美貌依旧不减，毋庸置疑，但当阳光不再照耀她时，人们便能看出，那个从葡萄牙而来、无忧无虑的公主已所剩无几，她如今已成为一位尽职尽责的摄政王，一位内心饱受创伤的母亲。这对夫妇静静地欣赏着天空的美景。他们都喜欢彼此静静地待在一起；仅仅是感受到对方的存在，就足以让他们感到满足。

Isabel, also on horseback, drew alongside him. Carlos gazed at her and longed to kiss her. The light of the setting sun brought life to the pale, weary face she had worn lately. Her beauty remained undiminished, undoubtedly, but when the sun did not illuminate her, one could see that little remained of the carefree princess who had arrived from Portugal, for she had become a regent devoted to her duties and a mother with wounds in her soul. The couple silently enjoyed the spectacle of the sky. They both liked to be silent together; simply feeling each other's presence was enough to satisfy them.

不久之后，皇帝启程了。他的妻子没有跟随他，而是回头望去。小菲利普在弗朗西斯·博尔吉亚的照看下，独自寻找鸟儿玩耍。

Shortly afterward, the emperor set off. His wife, instead of following him, looked back. Little Philip amused himself by searching for birds, watched over by Francis Borgia.

“你稍微走远一点，他不会有事的。让他去打猎吧。”来自根特的男人说道。

"Nothing will happen to him if you go a little ways away. Let him hunt," said the man from Ghent.

他不猎鸟，他收集鸟类。他喜欢研究它们。

—He doesn't hunt birds: he collects them. He enjoys studying them.

皇帝不悦地皱起了眉头。他回家时原本很开心，但他很快意识到，在他离开的这段时间里，伊莎贝拉变成了一个过度保护的母亲，而菲利普则太过天真，无法承受等待着他的命运。

The emperor grimaced in displeasure. His return home had been happy, but he had soon realized that, in his absence, Isabella had become an overprotective mother and Philip, far too tender a child for the destiny that awaited him.

皇后转过身，看到了丈夫脸上的责备之色。

The empress turned around and perceived the reproach in her husband's face.

“那些遭受过损失的人害怕再次遭受损失，”她这样安慰自己，然后决定出发去追随卡洛斯。

"Those who have suffered a loss fear that another will come," she justified herself, as she decided to set off to follow Carlos.

——不要让不幸雪上加霜，还要生活在恐惧之中，担心不幸再次发生。

—Do not add to the misfortune the punishment of living in fear that it will happen again.

“你不应该白发人送黑发人，”伊莎贝尔语气尖锐而充满感情地回答道。

"You shouldn't have had to bury a son," Isabel replied in a sharp and visceral tone.

他似乎很生气。

He seemed offended.

—你以为我没有受苦吗？

—Do you think I didn't suffer?

我并非指责你们冷酷无情。距离使伤害无法波及我们。无论是我们儿子所受的伤害，还是这些王国所遭受的伤害，都无法阻挡我们。

—I do not accuse you of being inhumane. Distance prevents harm from reaching us. Neither the harm done to our son, nor the harm suffered by these kingdoms.

——阿尔及尔……——卡洛斯明白了。

—Algiers… —Carlos understood.

“你们必须铲除那群异教徒的马蜂窝，否则我们的海岸迟早会落入他们手中。为什么西班牙总是要为帝国牺牲自己？”

"You must raze that hornet's nest of infidels, or our coasts will be theirs sooner or later. Why must Spain always sacrifice itself for the Empire?"

“夫人，您的目光太短浅了。”她被这话激怒了，正要反驳，凯撒却先开了口：“这是统治一个领地之人的目光。我统治着无数的领地。凯撒不可能像凡人那样判断每一种困境！”

"Your vision is short-sighted, my lady." Inflamed by the comment, she was about to reply when the Caesar spoke first: "The vision of one who rules a single domain. I govern countless ones. A Caesar cannot judge every predicament as a man would!"

皇帝想起了查理曼大帝。自从他在博洛尼亚加冕以来，他每天都想着查理曼，每当犹豫不决时，他常常会想，如果查理曼站在他的位置上，他会怎么做。他仰望查理曼，因为在当今时代，他找不到可以效仿的榜样，因为没有人能像查理曼那样拥有如此强大的权力。作为信仰的捍卫者，他感到无比孤独，这促使他寻求在传奇时代寻求慰藉，因为只有超人的精神才能让他对抗宗教改革者、向他发动战争的教皇、不敬的英国人以及可怕的奥斯曼帝国。这样的责任一直折磨着他，直到苏莱曼最近退位，他才确信上帝正在给他一个机会，让他自己也成为传奇。这就是上帝让他身处如此困境并剥夺他盟友的原因。天意推动他走向伟大，而事实是，只有相信自己是第一位皇帝精神的继承人，他才感到有足够的力量去面对成千上万个困扰他的问题，其中任何一个问题都足以让一个普通人发疯。

The emperor thought of Charlemagne. Ever since his coronation in Bologna, he had him in mind daily, and when he hesitated, he would often wonder what the Great would have done in his place. He looked to him because in the present he found no examples to guide him, for there was no man who enjoyed the power he wielded. The loneliness he felt as defender of the faith contributed to his seeking refuge in legendary times, since only a superhuman spirit would allow him to confront reformers, popes who waged war against him, irreverent Englishmen, and the fearsome Ottoman Empire. Such a responsibility had tormented him until, with Suleiman's recent abdication, he became certain that God was offering him the chance to become a legend himself. That was why He placed him in such dire straits and deprived him of allies. Providence was pushing him towards greatness, and the truth was that only by believing that he was the heir in spirit of the first emperor did he feel strong enough to face the thousands of problems that assailed him, just one of which would have driven an ordinary man to delirium.

此外，通过与查理曼大帝的比较，他也意识到了自己的不足。当他阅读查理曼大帝的生平时，为自己从未亲临战场而感到羞愧。在瓦朗谢讷战役中，面对法军，他却一直待在后卫位置，一旦意识到法军的猛攻威胁到自己，便立即撤退——他竟然逃跑了！查理曼大帝几乎从未回避过战斗；他的佩剑“欢乐号”（Joyeuse）早已磨损不堪，无数次击败敌人。他的传奇正是在血染的土地上铸就的。如果他仅仅像个法官一样，坐在官邸里治理国家，又怎能震慑众多敌人呢？他的权力要求他即便在世时，也要创造一个神话，以此震慑对手，鼓舞士气。此前他那温和仁慈、爱好和平的统治者形象，显然不符合上帝赋予他的使命。

Furthermore, by comparing himself to Charlemagne, he also became aware of his own shortcomings. When he read the account of Charlemagne's life, he felt somewhat ashamed for never having gone down to the battlefield. At Valenciennes, facing the French troops, he had remained in the rearguard, and upon realizing he was threatened by the French onslaught, he had immediately retreated: he had fled! Charlemagne had hardly ever avoided combat; his sword Joyeuse was worn down defeating enemies. This was how his legend had been forged, treading on bloodstained earth. How could he appear imposing to his many enemies if he limited himself to administering his domains from an office, like a mere jurist? His power demanded that he create, even in his lifetime, a myth that would intimidate his rivals and embolden his troops. The good-natured and peaceful ruler he had been until then did not fit the requirement that God had assigned him.

——后人会评判我的，伊莎贝尔。

—Posterity will judge me, Isabel.

“现在的情况也是如此，”她斩钉截铁地说。

"So will the present," she said categorically.

与丈夫重聚后，皇后暂时忘却了丈夫不在期间的种种忧虑，但笼罩着他们的阴霾渐渐消散，坦诚也开始占据上风。她怀疑，如果将抱怨藏在心底，是否能让她成为更好的妻子或摄政。顺从既不符合她的本性，也无济于事。

Having been reunited with her husband, the Empress had forgotten for a few days the anxieties she had suffered while he was away, but the cloud that had enveloped them during those first few days gradually dissipated, and honesty began to prevail. She doubted that keeping her complaints to herself would make her a better wife or regent. Compliance was neither in her nature nor useful.

皇帝催马疾驰。伊莎贝拉勒住马，转身望向儿子所在的地方；他们已经走得很远了，菲利普如今在地平线上只剩下一个小点。

The emperor urged his horse on. Isabella stopped hers and turned towards where her son was; they had gone so far away that Philip was now barely a dot on the horizon.

我们回去吧。

—Let's go back.

但凯撒不仅继续前进，而且还加快了速度。

But Caesar not only kept going, he gained speed.

——还没到时候。让我摆脱这些指责吧。

—Not yet. Let me escape from so much reproach.

皇后没有跟上去。她站在原地，看着他越骑越快，直到速度快得惊人。这景象让她感到一阵莫名的不安，于是她决定转身离开，回到儿子身边。渐渐地，菲利普的身影在远处越来越近。伊莎贝尔听到身后传来一阵嘈杂的声音：马嘶声夹杂着一声喊叫，随后又是一阵巨响，最后归于沉寂。她转过身，看到查理的马空无一物地骑着，而她的丈夫则毫无生气地躺在地上。

The Empress did not follow him. She stood watching as he rode faster and faster, until he reached a frenetic pace. The sight filled her with a strange unease, so she decided to turn her back on him and return to her son. Little by little, the distant figure of Philip grew larger. Isabel then heard a confused sound behind her: the neighing of a horse mingled with a shout, followed by a sudden noise and then a heavy silence. Turning around, she saw Charles's horse, now riding unburdened, her husband lying lifeless on the ground.

 

 

 

 

当地最优秀的医生们立即响应王室的召唤：国王病危。他们携带着各种仪器，在仆人的陪伴下，与国王一同待在寝宫中，以免被打扰。于是，宫廷里充满了泪水和祈祷，人们被迫对病情一无所知，直到医生们宣布诊断结果。就在人们祈祷奇迹出现的同时，新任阿尔瓦公爵费迪南德命令卫兵保护继承人。如果查理驾崩，年仅八岁的菲利普将成为无数争夺王位阴谋的目标，而这些阴谋是可以预见的。

The finest physicians in the region responded immediately to the Crown's summons: the king was dying. Equipped with their instruments and attended by servants, they secluded themselves with him in a bedchamber to avoid being disturbed. Thus, the court was filled with tears and prayers, forced as it was to remain ignorant until the physicians pronounced their diagnosis. While a miracle was being prayed for, Ferdinand, the newly appointed Duke of Alba, ordered the guard to secure the heir. Should Charles die, Philip, who was barely eight years old, would become the target of the countless conspiracies vying for the throne that were to be expected.

西班牙的未来是安全的，但其其他领土的未来则未必如此。

—The future of Spain is safe. Not so that of the rest of its territories.

塔韦拉枢机主教疲惫地点头回应公爵的话。他是托莱多大主教，近年来在卡斯蒂利亚政坛的影响力与日俱增，但事实上，他仍然没有充分意识到像皇帝这样巨大的权力其实非常脆弱。

Cardinal Tavera nodded wearily at the duke's words. He was the Archbishop of Toledo, whose role in Castilian politics had steadily grown in importance in recent years, but the truth was that he was still not fully aware of the fragility of such immense power as that of the emperor.

他问道：“你认为这位继承人在帝国和其他领土上不会受到应有的尊重吗？”

"Do you think the heir would not be respected as such in the Empire and the other territories?" he asked.

“帝国？”公爵答道，“费迪南德将继承他的王位，而且他还有一个儿子。你真认为他会宁愿把帝国传给菲利普，一个如此没有野心的孩子……？”

"The Empire?" replied the duke. "Ferdinand would succeed him, and he has a son. Do you really think he would prefer to give it to Philip, a child with so little ambition...?"

“闭嘴！”伊莎贝尔打断了他们，她出现在他们身后，眼睛哭得红肿。

"Shut up!" interrupted Isabel, who appeared behind them with eyes swollen from crying so much.

阿尔巴公爵低下了头。他很后悔在如此戏剧性的时刻冒犯了皇后，但他对继承人的看法和对自己的看法一样坚定，所有认识菲利普的人都和他一样，认为菲利普是个体弱多病的孩子，比起剑，他更喜欢弹奏鲁特琴，而且自从哥哥去世后，他就一直依偎在母亲的裙摆旁。

The Duke of Alba lowered his head. He regretted having offended the Empress at such a dramatic moment, but his opinion of the heir was as firm as any of his own, and it was shared by all those who had known Philip, a delicate child, more inclined to pick up a lute than a sword, and who, since his brother's death, had clung to his mother's skirts.

“祈祷吧。他还活着。”伊莎贝尔说道。

—And pray. He is still alive —Isabel declared.

 

 

 

 

皇帝睁开双眼，一头雾水。一群物理学家在他周围漫无目的地走来走去。皇帝不记得自己是怎么到这儿来的。但他却记得刚才醒来时做的那个梦，梦里他看到自己变成了石头。

When the emperor opened his eyes, he understood nothing. A swarm of physicists moved around him without any clear purpose. The emperor didn't remember how he had gotten there. However, he did retain a memory of the dream from which he had just awakened, in which he had seen himself turned to stone.

尽管他几乎没有力气，但他还是发出了一声喉音，引起了在场一人的注意，那人跑去通知了其他物理学家，随后又立即通知了皇后。

Although he barely had any strength, he managed to emit a guttural sound that caught the attention of one of those present, who ran to inform the rest of the physicists and, immediately afterwards, the empress.

伊莎贝尔曾向自己保证，绝不在丈夫面前哭泣，但当她走进房间，与他对视——那双湛蓝的眼睛，仿佛又焕发出了生机——她再也无法抑制住泪水。她走向床边，却不知该如何触碰他，甚至不知道这样做是否合适。她震惊不已。尽管她曾向法庭祈求祈祷和希望，但事实上，她自己也已经相信他已去世。她曾短暂体验过寡居的滋味，那段日子令她茫然不知所措。她承受着难以忍受的痛苦，但最让她感到的，是无尽的虚无；仿佛丈夫的离去抹去了世间所有的快乐，甚至连事物的名称也消失了。她所经历的那种难以承受的现实，在她心中留下了深深的烙印。得知他平安无事，她感到无比欣慰，但内心依然颤抖不已。

Isabel had promised herself she wouldn't cry in front of her husband, but upon entering the room and meeting his eyes—so blue, so alive again—she was unable to hold back her tears. She approached the bed, though she didn't know how to touch him, or even if it was appropriate. She was stunned. Despite having asked the court for prayers and hope, the truth was that she herself had come to believe him dead. The time she had spent glimpsing widowhood had been bewildering. She had suffered unbearable pain, but above all, a sense of meaninglessness; as if her husband, by disappearing, had erased pleasures from the world, even the names of things. That impossible reality she had glimpsed had left its mark on her. She felt immense joy at knowing he was safe, but she still trembled.

物理学家们允许他们牵手。两位皇帝彼此凝视，一言不发；任何言语都显得多余。

The physicists allowed them to hold hands. The emperors gazed at each other without saying a word; any words would have been superfluous.

“陛下，”他们身后传来一个声音。

"Your Majesty," came a voice from behind them.

阿尔瓦公爵、塔韦拉枢机主教和弗朗西斯科·德·博尔哈向房间里张望。凯撒看起来很疲惫，但他还是让他们进去了。医生们离开去给他们腾出地方，但他们仍然在门后警戒，保持警惕。

The Duke of Alba, Cardinal Tavera, and Francisco de Borja peered into the room. The Caesar looked tired, but he let them in. The physicians left to make room for them, though they remained on guard behind the door, alert.

“得知你正在康复，真是太好了，”红衣主教说道。和其他人一样，他看着查尔斯，仍然不太相信他真的躲过了这场悲剧。

"What a joy to know that you are recovering," said the cardinal, who, like the rest, looked at Charles without quite believing that he had managed to avoid tragedy.

博尔哈补充道：“法庭上下都热泪盈眶地庆祝这一喜讯。”

"The court celebrates this joy with tears," Borja added.
