物理学家们向受伤的男子解释了他身上发生了什么。听着他们的解释，他能感受到自己给别人带来的痛苦。他后悔自己的意外让所有人失望了。

The physicists had explained to the injured man what had happened to him. Listening to them, he had imagined the anguish he had caused. He regretted having disappointed everyone with his accident.

——帮帮我，我要让他们看到我。让他们确信无疑，世上确实有皇帝和国王。

—Assist me, I want them to see me. Let them not doubt that there is an emperor and a king.

他相对轻松地坐了起来，但正要下床时，却发出一声痛苦的嚎叫，震得在场的人脊背发凉。卡洛斯掀开被子，看了看他的腿。腿上满是淤青和伤口，但似乎都不算严重。凯撒再次尝试动弹，但很快又发出了一声痛苦的呻吟。

He sat up with relative ease, but as he prepared to get out of bed, he let out a howl of pain that sent shivers down the spines of those present. Carlos threw back the sheets and looked at his legs. They displayed a catalog of bruises and wounds, but none appeared particularly serious. The Caesar tried to move again, but the groan of pain was soon repeated.

“大人，您该休息了……”伊莎贝尔劝道。

"My lord, you must rest..." Isabel urged him.

—我搬不动它们！

—I can't move them!

他说着，目光呆滞地盯着自己的双腿，仿佛它们不属于自己。顾问们和博尔哈沉默地交换着眼神。他们努力掩饰内心的不安，但又觉得不该加重卡洛斯的忧虑；他脸色苍白，呼吸急促而紊乱，惊恐万分。

As he said this, he stared at his legs as if they belonged to someone else. The advisors and Borja, silent, exchanged glances. They struggled to hide their unease, but felt compelled not to add to Carlos's worry; he had paled and was breathing in short, ragged breaths, gripped by panic.

 

 

 

 

第二天，皇帝召见阿尔巴和塔韦拉到寝宫。他特意要求伊莎贝尔不要陪同她们一同前往。

The next day, the emperor summoned Alba and Tavera to his bedchamber. He expressly requested that Isabel not accompany them on this visit.

帮帮我。

—Assist me.

凯撒向他的顾问们伸出双臂，他们不知所措地站在那里。他以威严的姿态坚持，强迫他们每人抓住他的肩膀，把他扶了起来。查理哼了一声表示不满，但他没有退缩。

The Caesar stretched out his arms toward his advisors, who stood at a loss for what to do. He insisted with an imperious gesture, managing to get each of them to take hold of one of his shoulders and help him to his feet. Charles grunted in complaint, but he did not back down.

“继续，”他命令道。

—Go on —he ordered.

阿尔巴和塔韦拉虽然谨慎，但还是遵照他的命令行事，只是动作非常缓慢。皇帝试图双脚着地行走。尽管十分艰难，他最终还是做到了。

Alba and Tavera, though cautious, followed his orders, albeit very slowly. The emperor tried to put his feet on the ground and walk. Although with great difficulty, he managed to do so.

——我可以自己做。

—I can do it alone.

“陛下，您确定吗？”阿尔巴公爵半信半疑地问道，“或许您应该再休息几天，恢复体力后再尝试。”

"Are you sure, Your Majesty?" the Duke of Alba asked skeptically. "Perhaps you should rest for a few more days before attempting it... to regain your strength."

“我有这个力量，你这个傻瓜！”卡洛斯在情绪爆发中没有意识到自己，但他的内心却燃起了熊熊怒火。

"I have the strength, you fool!" Carlos didn't recognize himself in his outburst, but his spirit was ablaze.

其他人渐渐放开了他。皇帝抓住附近的一件家具，试图自己行走。他迈出了四步，这让他胆子大了些；走到第五步时，支撑腿突然剧痛，让他失去了平衡。

Little by little, the others let go of him. Then the emperor grabbed hold of a nearby piece of furniture and tried to walk on his own. He managed four steps, which emboldened him; on the fifth, a sharp pain in his supporting leg caused him to lose his balance.

-威严！

-Majesty!

阿尔巴公爵冲上前去，救了他一命，使他免于摔倒。这位康复中的病人垂头丧气，任由别人抬回床上，他捶打床垫，发泄心中的怒火。大臣们不知该如何安慰他，他们从未见过他如此狼狈的模样。

The Duke of Alba rushed to him and saved him from a certain fall. Defeated, the convalescent allowed himself to be carried back to his bed, where he released his rage by punching the mattress. The advisors were at a loss for words to console him. They had never seen him in such a state.

“你挺过了一场严峻的考验，”阿尔巴终于鼓起勇气说道，“好好庆祝一下，别急着恢复。”

"You have survived a serious ordeal," Alba finally dared to say. "Celebrate it and don't rush to recover."

——发生的一切让我明白，将我与生命联系起来的那根线是多么脆弱。

—What happened has made me see how fragile the thread that connects me to life is.

“陛下，这与其他任何人的做法一样，毫不逊色。”塔韦拉喃喃自语道。

"It is no less consistent than that of any other man, Your Majesty," Tavera mused aloud.

——但只有我会在死亡面前暴露。我至今为止做过什么值得被铭记的事？我又能带着怎样的骄傲进入来世？

—But only I would be exposed by death. What have I done until now that could be remembered? What pride would I take with me to the next life?

“你是世界上最有权势的人！”红衣主教说道。

"You are the most powerful man in the world!" said the cardinal.

凯撒失望地哼了一声：那番话对他毫无意义。他所拥有的头衔都是继承来的。任何一个平庸之辈，如果生于此地，都能像他一样炫耀这些头衔。但他除了利用这些荣誉来抵御敌人之外，又做了什么呢？

The Caesar snorted in disappointment: that statement meant nothing to him. The titles he possessed were inherited. Any mediocre person could have flaunted them in his place had they been born there. But what had he done with those honors, other than defend himself against his enemies from his office?

“我以为我有足够的时间来弥补我的错误。”卡洛斯说完这句话，瞬间老了好几岁。

"I thought I had plenty of time to make amends for my mistakes." Carlos aged instantly as he said this.

“你一定能做到，”来自阿尔巴的男人鼓励他。

"You'll have it," the man from Alba encouraged him.

皇帝很想相信他，但四肢传来一阵难以忍受的灼热刺痛感，让他想起姑母的遭遇，更加怜悯她，这让他不敢抱太大希望。他紧紧抓住公爵的前臂，眼神炽热地望着他，仿佛即将说出最后的遗愿。

The emperor wanted to believe him, but the sensation in his limbs—an unbearable, hot tingling that made him think of his aunt's ordeal and pity her even more than before—prevented him from getting his hopes up. He clung to the duke's forearm and looked at him with the intensity of someone about to utter their last wish.

——我恳求你，好好管教费利佩。让他变得坚强，对他毫不留情。如果我遭遇不幸，愿它不要波及我的领地。

—I beg you, educate Felipe. Toughen him up, and spare no severity. If misfortune should ever befall me, may it not also invade my domains.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在法国宫廷里，奇迹无处容身。萨伏依的路易丝长期以来一直默默忍受着胆囊疾病的折磨。一次旅途中，她的病情加重，被迫中途停留，而那次停留仿佛漫长得如同永无止境。临终前，尽管知道自己时日无多，弗朗索瓦的母亲仍担忧着儿子将如何面对她的离去。她的担忧并非毫无根据，也并非妄自揣测。人人都知道，君主与母亲之间有着一种非同寻常的爱，他们绝不会将这份爱给予任何人。没有人能够想象没有母亲的他会是什么样子，但他们都确信，他一定会变得不一样。

Meanwhile, at the French court, there was no room for miracles. Louise of Savoy had long endured a gallbladder ailment with stoicism. During a journey, her illness worsened, forcing her to make a stop that proved to be an eternity. Before dying, but knowing her end was near, Francis's mother worried about how her son would cope with her absence. Her concern was neither unfounded nor presumptuous. Everyone knew that the monarch and his mother shared a love unlike any they would ever bestow upon another. No one could imagine what he would be like without her, but they had no doubt he would be different.

路易莎庆幸自己没能在儿子临终时陪伴在他身边。“我和他都无法承受这样的痛苦，”她在临终前向女儿玛格丽塔坦白道。然而，对弗朗西斯科来说，没能陪伴母亲走完人生最后一程却是毁灭性的打击。当母亲的遗体运回宫廷后，国王寸步不离地守候在她身边，却丝毫没有从中获得慰藉：失去母亲的痛苦非但没有随着时间流逝而减轻，反而愈发真切，也更加难以承受。

Luisa was relieved not to be with her son when he died. "Neither he nor I could have borne it," she confessed to her daughter Margarita before passing away. For Francisco, however, not having been with his mother in her final moments was devastating. When the woman's body arrived at court, the king never left her side, but he found no solace in it: the sense of loss, instead of diminishing with time, became more tangible and, therefore, more unbearable.

整个贵族阶层都涌向昂布瓦兹，向路易丝致以哀悼。弗朗西斯接受了他们的慰问，但他沉浸在悲痛之中，根本无法分辨来往的人。他只认出了一张脸，以及那纤细白皙的脖颈：那是弗朗索瓦丝·德·福瓦伯爵夫人，夏多布里昂伯爵夫人，他昔日的情人。路易丝的遗体就在几步之遥，这对昔日的恋人敷衍地寒暄了几句，间或交换着匆匆的眼神。随后，弗朗索瓦丝走上前去，向这位曾经趁国王不在将她逐出宫廷的女人告别。在深色薄纱下，路易丝的表情僵硬，仿佛成了一段痛苦的回忆。伯爵夫人对她没有丝毫怜悯，她知道，这种感觉——或者更确切地说，是缺乏怜悯——在王国里比比皆是。她觉得这很不公平，后人会记住她促成了康布雷冲突的结束，而她的一生却一直在与所有非她子女的人作战。

The entire aristocracy flocked to Amboise to pay their respects to Louise. Francis received their condolences, but he was so absorbed by grief that he couldn't truly distinguish one from another. He recognized only one face, and with it the slender, white neck that adorned it: that of Countess Françoise de Foix, Countess of Chateaubriand, his former lover. With Louise's body just a few feet away, the once-lovers exchanged a perfunctory exchange, punctuated by fleeting glances. Françoise then approached to bid farewell to the deceased, the very woman who had once cast her aside from court, taking advantage of the king's absence. Beneath the dark tulle, her expression frozen, Louise seemed like a painful memory. The Countess felt no pity for her, and she knew that her sentiment—or rather, the lack thereof—was shared by many in the kingdom. How unfair it seemed to her that posterity would remember her for having obtained the cessation of a conflict in Cambrai, when her existence had consisted of waging war against all those who were not her children.

伯爵夫人在众人的注视下离开了，他们都熟知她的过去。莱昂诺尔也听说了这件事，她很高兴摆脱了这个女人。她握住丈夫的手想安慰他，但国王甩开她的手，追随他的前情人而去。

The countess left under the watchful eyes of all those present, who knew her past well. Leonor, too, had heard of the affair and was grateful to be rid of the lady. She took her husband's hand to comfort him in his grief, but the king shook it off to follow his former lover.

 

 

 

 

在法国，没有比我更孤儿的人了。

—There is no greater orphan in France than me.

弗朗西斯科和伯爵夫人待在皇家寝宫里，与其他人隔绝开来。国王走近她时，曾投入她的怀抱痛哭，此刻他神情恍惚，仿佛被下了药。

Francisco and the countess were in the royal bedchamber, sheltered from the rest of the group. The king, who had sought refuge in her arms to weep upon approaching her, was dazed, as if drugged.

“成为孤儿是一种不幸，但也是一种教训，”弗朗西斯卡说。“它关乎生活，告诉我们能够自力更生。每个人心中都蕴藏着伟大。但只有当我们无依无靠时，才能发现它。”

“Being orphaned is a misfortune, but also a lesson,” Francisca said. “It’s about life, which tells us that we can fend for ourselves. Greatness lies within each of us. But we only discover it when there’s no one left to cling to.”

“我永远也无法让她满意！”他哀叹道。“她在我最辉煌的时候离开了。她想让我成为凯撒，而现在我只是个平庸的国王……”

"I could never please her!" he lamented. "She left when my glory was at its lowest. She wanted to make me Caesar, and now I'm just a lackluster king..."

伯爵夫人知道弗朗西斯科的愧疚是真诚的。尽管她怨恨他如此轻易地接受了分居，但她也承认自己对他怀有深厚的感情。说到底，这位君主不过是个迷失方向的孩子，被他的母亲培养成了一个永远格格不入的异类。

The countess knew that Francisco's guilt was genuine. And although she resented him for having so readily accepted their separation, she recognized the affection she felt for him. Deep down, the monarch was nothing more than a disoriented child whom his mother had turned into a perpetual misfit.

“你母亲的时间已经不多了，”弗朗西斯卡回答说，“但你的时间还很长。如果你不采取行动，而是继续哀叹自己没有做的事情，你就会失败。”

"Time has run out for your mother," Francisca replied, "but not for you. You will only fail if, instead of acting, you remain lamenting what you haven't done."

多亏了伯爵夫人的话语，国王自母亲去世以来第一次感受到一丝愉悦。如果说他会怀念路易莎的什么，那就是她的智慧，那种他所缺乏的分析能力。弗朗西斯卡的智慧让他感到慰藉。或许他正需要这样的慰藉。国王靠在伯爵夫人的肩上，吻了吻她的脖颈。伯爵夫人站了起来。

Thanks to the countess's words, for the first time since his mother's death, the king felt a pleasant emotion. If there was anything he was going to miss about Luisa, it was her intelligence, that gift for analysis that he lacked. Francisca's wisdom was comforting to him. Perhaps he needed it. The monarch leaned against the countess's shoulder and kissed her neck. The woman stood up.

大人，死物无法复活。

—My lord, what is dead cannot be revived.

她等待着答案，却始终没有等到。她离开了卧室，而房间里，只剩下一个茫然无措的男人。

She waited for an answer that never came. She left the bedroom, and in it, a man adrift.

 

 

 

 

尽管他曾遭受拒绝，但与昔日爱人的重逢却对他大有裨益。伯爵夫人无疑是对的：在他母亲在世时未能登顶固然是一种失败，但放弃努力才是更大的遗憾。真正令君主痛苦的是，路易莎的存在似乎毫无意义；她为确保他战胜所有人所做的一切努力，最终都付诸东流。

Despite the rejection he had suffered, the encounter with his former lover proved most advantageous. The countess was undoubtedly right: his failure to reach the pinnacle while his mother was alive might have been a failure, but giving up trying would have been an even greater one. What truly tormented the monarch was that Luisa's existence had vanished in vain; that all her efforts to ensure his triumph over everyone else had been nothing but a useless expenditure.

国王召见蒙莫朗西紧急会面。这位顾问感到惊讶，因为他原本以为国王的哀悼会持续数周。更令他震惊的是，弗朗西斯看起来精神矍铄。

The king summoned Montmorency for an urgent meeting. The advisor was surprised, as he had expected his lord's mourning to last for weeks. He was even more astonished to see Francis appear full of energy.

“只有以胜利来荣耀她，我才能获得和平，”君主宣称。

"Only by honoring her with triumphs will I achieve peace," the sovereign declared.

蒙莫朗西被视为扫兴者。他提醒国王，以免他忘记，王室已无力资助任何事业，因为在与皇帝的连番战争中追求“胜利”已耗尽国库——已故路易丝的贪婪在国库中挖了个大洞，这位顾问宁愿将此事留到哀悼期结束后再处理。至多只能计划一次特殊的筹款活动，但这无论如何都需要时间，而且会涉及一些不太光彩的手段，例如要求那些曾经从君主的荣光中获利的人——朋友、情人以及信徒——归还他们曾经的馈赠。弗朗西斯接受了这些解决方案，但纯粹的行政措施或掠夺性手段都无助于提振他的士气。就在这时，他想起自己拥有两枚价值连城的硬币，而且最近有人打听过其中一枚。

Montmorency was cast as the spoilsport. He reminded the king, lest he have forgotten, that the Crown had no funds to finance any undertaking, since the pursuit of "victories" in the successive wars with the emperor had become a drain on the coffers—the late Louise's avarice had created its own hole in the treasury, a fact the advisor preferred to save for when the mourning period ended. At most, an exceptional fundraising effort could be planned, which in any case would take time and involve less than honorable gestures, such as requesting those who had once profited from the monarch's splendor—friends, lovers, and men of faith—to return what they had given. Francis accepted these solutions as valid, but purely administrative or predatory measures did little to lift his spirits. It was then that he remembered he possessed two coins of incalculable value, and that someone had recently inquired about one of them.

 

 

 

 

—我们接受您向我们提出的提议：法国希望正式缔结您侄女凯瑟琳与亨利王子的婚约。

—We accept the proposal you made to us: France wishes to formalize the engagement between your niece Catherine and Prince Henry.

克莱门特七世惊讶地看着蒙莫朗西，手里拿着弗朗西斯的儿子的画像，这是他的访客抵达梵蒂冈办公室时交给他的。

Clement VII gave Montmorency a look of astonishment, while holding in his hands the portrait of Francis' son that his visitor had handed him upon arriving at the Vatican office.

——这么快？有什么理由如此急迫？

—Already? What reasons are there for such urgency?

顾问辩称：“当没有理由推迟一件好事时，仓促行事只会造成浪费。”

—When there are no reasons to postpone something good, haste makes waste—the advisor argued.

“他们几乎还是孩子……”教皇反驳道。

"They are almost children..." objected the Pope.

——这样他们就有充足的时间去学习如何相爱。

—That way they will have a long life to learn to love each other.

教皇认为正式会谈已经结束。他无奈地叹了口气；权势人物之间的会谈结构总是千篇一律：先是一些形式上的寒暄，然后才是袒露他们真实利益的环节。

The Pope considered the official chapter of the conversation over. He sighed with resignation; the structure of talks between powerful figures was always the same: a segment of formalities followed by the revelation of their raw interests.

——你的主人要求什么回报？

—What does your lord ask in return?

米兰公爵将无嗣而终。届时，法国国王将争夺这一爵位。

—The Duke of Milan is going to die without heirs. When that happens, the King of France will fight for that position.

教宗花了一些时间思考此事。

The Holy Father took some time to reflect on it.

—如果我们的协议被公之于众，我就违背了我对皇帝保持中立的承诺。

—If our agreement is made public, I will have broken my promise of neutrality to the emperor.

你的说法有误，我们要求的只是漠然。我们只要求你不要选边站队。让命运和武器来决定吧。

—You speak wrongly, for it is indifference that we ask of you. We only ask that you not take sides. Let fate and weapons decide.

这个提议看似合理，但教皇仍然犹豫不决。他艰难地起身；罗马陷落及其后的一切仍然给他的健康带来后遗症。他缺乏精力，因此也缺乏勇气去冒险发动另一场战争。几步疲惫的步伐让他来到办公室的窗前，从那里他眺望城市，只见一场可怕的风暴正肆虐着。隆隆的雷声令他心生畏惧；这让他想起不久前帝国军队的火药爆炸。这位法国人开始变得不耐烦起来。

The offer seemed reasonable, but the Pope remained hesitant. He rose with difficulty; his health still bore the consequences of the sack of Rome and all that followed. He lacked the vigor and, consequently, the courage to risk another war. Several weary steps brought him to the window of his office, from where he surveyed the city, over which a formidable storm was raging. The rumble of thunder intimidated him; it reminded him of the gunpowder explosions of the imperial troops not so long ago. The Frenchman began to grow impatient.

你想取悦那个攻陷罗马、把你俘虏的人吗？

—Do you want to please the one who sacked Rome and made you his captive?

教皇勃然大怒。

The Pope became irate.

——胆敢冒犯我，我对皇帝的怨恨永无止境！

—Do not dare offend me. My resentment towards the emperor is infinite!

——那就签署我们的协议吧。你将与法国王室结盟，全世界都会知道，没有任何暴君能够征服教皇。

—Then sign our agreement. You will be linked to the Crown of France, and the world will know that no tyrant can subdue the Holy Father.

克莱门特再次凝视着罗马的天空。他似乎从那片乌云中看到了某种预兆：他即将死去。或许，这是他最后一次机会，以极其优雅的方式，为根特的查理所受的侮辱复仇。

Clement gazed once more at the Roman sky. He seemed to discern a sign in those dark clouds: he would soon die. Perhaps he had before him his last chance to avenge himself, albeit with excessive elegance, for the affronts of Charles of Ghent.

 

 

 

 

当欧洲各国领导人仍在沉湎于过去的恩怨时，英国宫廷​​却一心着眼于未来。每天早晨，亨利国王都需要瞥一眼身旁，才能确信自己并非在做梦。看到安妮·博林那纤细的侧脸——如今已是王后——便确信自己长久以来的夙愿终于实现了。然而，当他走进枢密院时，却发现沃尔西那威严的红袍身影不在那里，这让他感到十分惊讶。取而代之的是托马斯·克伦威尔，这位出身卑微、默默无闻的人物，曾被这位失势的红衣主教雇佣多年，如今正等待着与他商讨国事。这位新任首相从他的导师那里学到了很多，例如，如何不择手段地晋升。正因如此，他才毫不犹豫地背叛了沃尔西，成为了英国君主的得力助手。对亨利而言，克伦威尔简直是个奇迹：他拥有沃尔西的记忆和智慧，却并非沃尔西本人。

While European leaders continued to dwell on past grievances, the English court was solely focused on the future. Every morning, King Henry needed to glance beside him to reassure himself that he wasn't dreaming. The sight of Anne Boleyn's delicate profile, now queen, confirmed that what he had striven for so long had finally come to pass. He was also still surprised to enter the council chamber and not find Wolsey's august, red-robed figure there. Now, Thomas Cromwell, a man of humble and obscure origins whom the disgraced cardinal had employed for years, awaited him to discuss the affairs of the realm. The new prime minister had learned much from his mentor; for example, how to advance his career without excessive scruples. This was why he didn't hesitate to betray him in order to become the English monarch's right-hand man. For Henry, Cromwell was a miracle: he possessed Wolsey's memories and wisdom without being him.

尽管几十年来，红衣主教和国王的权威在众人眼中似乎不相上下，但国王用短短几周时间就将他昔日的宰相贬为无足轻重之人，证明这不过是一种假象。权力始终属于亨利，而这正是其地位稳固的明证。沃尔西这才发现，他一直以来的怀疑并非空穴来风：一个失去财富和显赫头衔的人毫无价值——这便是他终其一生致力于权力扩张的原因，为了避免沦为血肉之躯的脆弱。当他得知自己曾效力之人计划将他送上法庭，并向多年来与他关系密切的法国国王寻求帮助时，却遭到了极度的蔑视。弗朗西斯甚至似乎对他的来访感到恼怒，仿佛一个满身泥泞的劳工竟敢闯入他的宫殿。

Although for decades the cardinal's and the king's authority seemed equal in everyone's eyes, the latter proved that this had been a mere illusion, taking only a few weeks to reduce his former chancellor to a nobody. Power had always belonged to Henry, and this was the proof that sustained it. Wolsey then discovered what he had always suspected: that a man stripped of wealth and important titles was worthless—hence his lifelong dedication to aggrandizement, to avoid the vulnerability of one who is merely flesh and blood. When he learned that the man he had served planned to put him on trial and sought help from the King of France, with whom he had had such a close relationship over the years, he was treated with utter disdain. Francis even seemed offended by his visit, as if a mud-footed laborer had dared to enter his palace.

“我愿倾尽所有知识和谋略为您效力！无需您支付任何报酬！”红衣主教恳求道，这令他颜面尽失。

"I will put all my knowledge and cunning at your service! Without you compensating me for it!" the cardinal had pleaded, mortifying his pride.

—如果接受你才华的人都否定你，那我姑且质疑你的才华吧。

—Let me doubt your talent if the one to whom you have given it condemns you.

沃尔西从法国到英国的旅程就这样变成了走向断头台的漫长旅程。

Wolsey's journey from France to England thus became a long walk to the scaffold.

亨利对待凯瑟琳的慷慨程度仅略高于对待他的顾问。这位西班牙公主深受英国民众爱戴，虐待她显然不合民意。在因拒绝接受婚姻无效的判决而被判刑后，她被剥夺了王位，并被软禁在金博尔顿城堡——一座位于伦敦北部偏远地区、规模庞大却阴暗潮湿的建筑。接待她的仆人称呼她为“夫人”。此时的她已不再是夫人。尽管她仍保留着威尔士太后王妃的头衔——亨利强调，这仅仅是她与哥哥的婚姻——凯瑟琳并没有纠正他们，因为她认为自己唯一有资格享有的荣誉就是英格兰女王。她坚信，在上帝眼中，她依然是女王。无论如何，即使痛苦，她也能忍受自己的衰落，但她无法接受衰落带来的后果：她的女儿玛丽将被视为私生女，从而被剥夺王位继承权。对国王而言，只有他与新王后所生的孩子才是合法的。亨利与博林圆房的那晚，他相信自己感受到了神明在新婚妻子子宫中的祝福，也相信自己终于可以摆脱延续血脉的痛苦担忧。

Henry was only slightly more generous to Catherine than to his advisor. The Spanish princess enjoyed the affection of the English people, and it would not have been popular to treat her cruelly. After being condemned for refusing to accept the annulment of her marriage, she was stripped of her crown and confined to Kimbolton Castle, a large but damp and isolated building far north of London. The servants who received her there addressed her as "Lady." She was nothing else by now. Although she still held the title of Dowager Princess of Wales—with which Henry emphasized that only her brother's marriage to her had taken place—Catherine did not correct them, because the only honor she believed she had a right to claim was that of Queen of England. She was convinced that in God's eyes she still was. In any case, and even with pain, she could bear her decline, but not what it entailed: that her daughter Mary would be considered illegitimate and, as such, removed from the line of succession to the throne. For the king, only the children he expected to have with the new queen would be legitimate. The night he consummated his marriage to Boleyn, Henry had believed he felt divine blessing in his new wife's womb, and with it, the end of his agonizing worry about perpetuating his lineage.

然而，尽管近来厄运连连，凯瑟琳仍然坚信上帝站在她这边。事实上，唯一能让她感到慰藉的，就是想到迟早有一天，像君主所犯下的这种侮辱，会受到全能上帝的严厉惩罚。

Catherine, however, was convinced that Providence was on her side, despite the misfortunes that had befallen her recently. In fact, the only thing that consoled her was the thought that, sooner or later, such an indignity as the one perpetrated by the monarch would be punished, and severely, by the Almighty.

 

 

 

 

 

 

亲爱的兄弟和先生：

Dear brother and sir:

连日来，我一直试图不让您读到这些文字。我竭力克制自己的软弱，但令我羞愧的是，最终还是败下阵来。我恳求您将弗兰德斯的治理权托付他人。那里的诸多困境似乎无解。连日暴雨摧毁了庄稼，丹麦禁止我们进行贸易，王室也无力供养臣民，因为所有资源都已用于帮助您阻止土耳其人的推进。饥荒已经十分严重，但与若不能立即找到解决办法将会到来的灾难相比，这还算轻微——而我深知自己无力找到解决办法。摄政如此重任，怎能托付给我这样脆弱之人？我内心毫无勇气承担这项重任。忧郁和恐惧攫住了我。陛下，我的兄弟，我害怕毁灭我们母亲的邪恶会在我的血液中流淌。

For days I have tried to spare you from reading these lines. I have fought against my weaknesses, but they, to my shame, have overcome me. I beg you to entrust the government of Flanders to another. Its many troubles seem impossible to resolve. The rains have ravaged the crops, Denmark forbids us trade, and the Crown has no funds to feed its subjects, for all its resources have been devoted to helping you halt the Turkish advance. The famines are already terrible, but mild compared to those that will come if a remedy is not found immediately—one that I know myself incapable of finding. Such a high duty as the regency cannot be entrusted to someone as fragile as I. I find no courage in my soul for such a task. Melancholy and fear have taken hold of me. I fear, Your Majesty, my brother, that the evil that destroyed our mother may course through my veins.

 

 

哈布斯堡的玛丽亚

MARIA OF HABSBURG​

 

 

读完妹妹的信后，卡洛斯小心翼翼地把它叠好，锁进书桌里。然后，他回到床上。几个星期以来，他几乎寸步不离。他遵照医嘱，拄着一根他讨厌的拐杖，每天散步两次。他很不情愿，因为他知道自己永远也无法完全康复。拐杖和他的怀疑态度让他看起来比实际年龄老得多。只要有机会，他就会回到房间，摆弄钟表，或者只是打个盹。对他来说，失去意识似乎是缓解他心情的唯一方法：停止存在，也就停止痛苦。尽管他一天中大部分时间都卧床不起，但疲惫感却从未消退，任何行动都需要付出巨大的努力。起初，人们都认为这种忧郁只是事故造成的暂时性后果，可以理解，但如今它已彻底攫住了他，皇帝却找不到任何摆脱它的方法。曾经令他兴奋的事物，如今却令他漠不关心，甚至鄙夷不已。他甚至没有力气去憎恨，除了对他自己的无尽憎恨。得知菲利普逃课，他竟也无动于衷。这又有什么关系呢？最令他羞愧的是玩忽职守，但他却日复一日地徒劳地寻找着参加议会的勇气。即便他真的参加了，也只不过是占据一个位置而已，根本无法对顾问们的建议表示赞同或反对，因为他的意志早已荡然无存。

After reading his sister's letter, Carlos carefully folded it and locked it in his desk. He then returned to his bed. For weeks he had barely left it. He followed the doctors' orders and, aided by a cane he hated, took two walks a day, which he undertook with a certain reluctance because he had no hope of ever fully recovering. The cane and his skepticism made him look much older than he actually was. Whenever he had the chance, he returned to his room, where he would wind and unwind clocks or simply doze. Unconsciousness seemed to him the only relief for his mood: to cease to exist and, therefore, to cease suffering. Although he spent a good part of the day in bed, fatigue never left him, and any action required a tremendous effort. The melancholy, which everyone had considered understandable when it seemed a temporary consequence of the accident, had finally taken hold of him, and the emperor could find no way to rid himself of it. What had once thrilled him now left him indifferent, if not contemptible, and he didn't even have the strength for hatred, except for the boundless hatred he felt for himself. He hadn't even been irritated to learn that Philip had deserted the Duke of Alba's lessons. What did it matter? What shamed him most was neglecting his duties, but day after day he searched in vain for the courage to attend council meetings. Had he participated, he would have been able to do nothing more than occupy a space, and not even agree or disagree with the suggestions of his advisors, since his will had vanished.

卡洛斯没有力气回复妹妹，但他渐渐习惯了随身携带这封信。玛丽亚在信中表达的情感与他自己的如此相似，以至于他只能找到一个解释来说明这种巧合：“是毁灭我们母亲的邪恶力量。”

Carlos couldn't find the strength to reply to his sister, but he grew accustomed to carrying the letter with him. The emotions Maria expressed were so similar to his own that he could only find one explanation for that synchronicity: "The evil that destroyed our mother."

 

 

 

 

提香等了皇帝许久，他终于走进了房间。感受到皇帝的到来，这位意大利画家下意识地鞠了一躬，但当他直起身子时，却大吃一惊。皇帝倚着权杖，像一棵摇摇欲坠的大树，除了长袍之外，几乎看不出什么帝王的风范。提香一眼就看出皇帝苍白的面色，不知该如何才能在肖像中捕捉到他，而不让他看起来像一具尸体。最棘手的并非他羸弱的外表——这可以通过在衣袍上运用醒目的笔触或将他置于宏大的背景中来弥补；真正的挑战在于，如何赋予他那毫无生气的神情以尊严。

Titian had been waiting for the emperor for quite some time when he finally entered the room. Sensing his presence, the Italian painter automatically bowed, but when he straightened up, he was surprised. The emperor, leaning on his staff like a tree about to collapse, had little imperial about him except for his robes. The moment he saw him, the artist wondered how he could capture that pallid complexion in his portrait without making him look like a corpse. And the worst part wasn't his fragile appearance, which could be compensated for with striking brushstrokes on the garments or by framing his figure in an epic setting; the real challenge was to imbue his expression, so devoid of feeling, with dignity.

陛下，您能邀请我，我深感荣幸。

—Your Majesty, I am honored that you have asked me.

—把你带到这里是因为你的才华，而不是我的一时兴起。

—It is your talent that has brought you here, not my whim.

事实上，皇帝对为画家做模特这件事的意愿，和其他任何事一样：毫无兴趣。这是伊莎贝尔的主意，他之所以答应，是因为他想在妻子面前假装自己已经从悲伤中走出来。查理心中唯一残存的甜蜜情感，就是对她的爱。

The truth was that the emperor had as much desire to pose for the artist as to do anything else: nothing. It had been Isabel's idea, and he had agreed because he wanted to pretend to his wife that he was recovering from his sadness. The only sweet emotion left in Charles was his love for her.

“你的工具呢？”凯撒惊讶地问道，一边坐下，一边邀请画家也坐下。

"Where are your tools?" asked the Caesar in surprise, as he took a seat and invited the painter to do the same.

这位意大利人显然没带任何行李，他抚摸着浓密的胡须，胡须浓密得如同智者一般，只是颜色乌黑，更显年轻。提香拥有一张威严的脸庞：高挺的鼻梁、深邃的目光和轮廓分明的颧骨。他无疑值得拥有一幅属于自己的肖像。

The Italian, who certainly carried no belongings, stroked his beard, which was as abundant as a sage's, except that it was jet black, revealing his youth. Titian possessed an august face: a long, straight nose, a deep gaze, and beautifully sculpted cheekbones. He undoubtedly deserved his own portrait.

—如果我不知道我要画的人是谁，我的画笔对我来说就毫无用处。

—My brushes are useless to me if I don't know the person I'm going to paint.

蒂齐亚诺坐在卡洛斯对面。

Tiziano occupied a seat opposite Carlos's.

你是谁？

—Who are you?

这个问题让皇帝百思不得其解。他曾想过坦诚相告，但这岂不是意味着他将直面深渊？

The question baffled the emperor. The thought of being honest crossed his mind, but that would have meant staring himself in the abyss.

—一个不怎么说话的人。

—A man who doesn't talk too much.

或许是因为你的职责迫使你谨慎行事。我认识许多领主、教皇和国王，但从未见过像你这样肩负重任的人。

—Perhaps because your duties compel you to prudence. I have known lords, popes, and kings, but never one who carries as much as you.

—凯瑞，你说得对……—卡洛斯立刻后悔了自己的冲动，尤其当他意识到这样的回应引起了艺术家的好奇心时。

—Carry, you're right… —Carlos instantly regretted his spontaneity, especially when he realized that such a response had aroused the artist's curiosity.

—你的现状是否让你感到压力过大？

—Does what you are overwhelm you?

皇帝知道答案，但却没有勇气说出口。

The emperor had the answer, but not the will to utter it.

“它让你感到不知所措吗？”提香追问道。

"Does it overwhelm you?" Titian insisted.

意大利人从凯撒的表情中看出他终于开始考虑这件事了。他给了凯撒一段长时间的沉默时间，让他好好思考。

The Italian realized from the Caesar's expression that he was finally considering the matter. He granted him a long silence to reflect in peace.

“有时候我觉得，现在的我和我应该成为的我，是两个截然不同的人。”卡洛斯说着，眼神迷离。

"Sometimes I feel that the person I am and the person I should be are two very different men." Carlos spoke with a faraway look in his eyes.

——你应该成为怎样的人？

—What is the person you should be like?

精力充沛。意志坚定，无所畏惧。永不言败。永远凌驾于众人之上，永远如此！——凯撒的语气越来越激烈。——“而且不是那种没有精神的人，”他轻蔑地自言自语道，“那种明明不老却觉得自己老了的人……”

—Energetic. With a spirit that nothing can faze. Relentlessly tenacious. Always superior to the rest, always!—The Caesar's tone was becoming increasingly visceral.—And not someone without spirit—he said to himself with disdain—who feels old when he isn't…

卡洛斯抬头看着意大利人，后者欣喜地看到表面覆盖着一层水润的铜绿。

Carlos looked up at the Italian, who was thrilled to see the watery patina covering it.

—有时候我宁愿默默无闻，过平静的生活。

—Sometimes I'd rather be nobody and live peacefully.

他们对视了片刻。皇帝不知道自己为何要向这个陌生人倾诉那些他不敢告诉任何人的事，甚至连伊莎贝尔都不敢说。但他无法抑制内心的激动：他的灵魂早已被情感彻底淹没。

They held each other's gaze for a few moments. The emperor didn't know what he was doing confessing to this stranger what he didn't dare tell anyone, not even Isabel. But he couldn't contain himself: his soul had overflowed.

陛下，世上没有哪个人身上没有魔鬼居住。

—There is no man in whom demons do not dwell, Your Majesty.

——可是像我这样的人应该知道怎么打败他们才对。可是我不知道……我真的不知道！

—But someone like me should know how to beat them. And I don't… I don't!

那声咆哮吓了艺术家一跳。仿佛从与提香共谋的梦境中惊醒，查尔斯突然恢复了镇定。他做了什么？他抓起拐杖，以最快的速度离开了房间，留下画家惊魂未定。

The roar startled the artist. Suddenly, as if emerging from a dream of complicity with Titian, Charles regained his composure. What had he done? He grabbed his walking stick and, with all the haste he could muster, left the room, leaving the painter shaken.

皇帝随后走出宫殿，朝他猜测儿子会去的鸽舍走去。他恼火地发现自己猜对了；菲利普就在那里，无忧无虑地照料着他的鸽子。

The emperor then made his way outside the palace, towards the dovecote where he guessed his son would be. He was irritated to find he was right; there was Philip, carefree, tending to his birds.

“你为何拒绝接受公爵的教诲？”他父亲厉声问道。

"Why do you reject the duke's lessons?" his father asked him sharply.

性格沉稳的男孩向他展示了自己的手，手上有一道难看的划痕。

The phlegmatic boy showed him his hand, which had an ugly scratch.

他伤害了我。

—He hurt me.

他父亲轻蔑地哼了一声。

His father snorted in contempt.

我没看到伤口，也没看到自尊。

—I see no wound. Nor self-respect.

费利佩将注意力重新转向鸟儿们，卡洛斯紧张的神情让鸟儿们兴奋不已。

Felipe turned his attention back to the birds, which were excited by Carlos's nervous presence.

“父亲，那些都是野蛮人的训练方法。再说，学这些有什么用呢？等我遇到战争，我会像你一样派兵作战。”

"Those are exercises for savages, Father. Besides, what's the point of learning them? When I face a war, I'll send troops, just like you do."

皇帝对自己的后代感到羞愧，就像对自己感到羞愧一样，因为他给后代树立了这样的榜样。

The emperor was as ashamed of his offspring as he was of himself, for having set such an example.

“你以为你迟早不用战斗吗？”他厉声问道，“士兵们会给你胜利。而荣耀就在于成为他们的领袖，必要时与他们同归于尽！”

"Do you think you won't have to fight, sooner or later?" he snapped. "The soldiers will give you victory. The glory will be that of being their leader, dying with them if it must be!"

费利佩沉思片刻，然后神情平静而庄重，如同圣人一般，看向他的父亲。

Felipe pondered it for a moment. Then, serene and grave as a saint, he looked at his father.

—我宁愿安于现状，也不愿追求荣耀。

—I prefer my contentment to glory.

这句话让卡洛斯哑口无言。

The sentence left Carlos speechless.

当晚，仆人们用精美的银盘为皇室成员呈上晚餐时，菲利普惊恐地发现，他亲手烹制的几只鸟竟然躺在其中一个盘子里。他别过脸去，不去看这在他看来是犯罪的行为，激动地瞪着父亲，充满责备。

That night, when the servants served dinner to the imperial family on rich silver platters, Philip discovered with horror that several of his birds, cooked, lay on one of them. The boy averted his eyes from what he perceived as a crime and, agitated, fixed accusing glances on his father.

“上帝创造他们，就是为了让他们死去，成为你们的食物，”凯撒辩解道。“重要的不是你们想要从这世上得到什么，而是这世上想要你们得到什么。明天你们就要离开宫廷了。最好的老师会教导你们，他们会把你们培养成我梦寐以求的继承人。”

"God created them to die and serve as food for you," the Caesar justified. "What matters little is what you want from this life, but what it wants from you. Tomorrow you will leave this court. The best tutors will educate you, and they will make you the heir I long to have."

男孩惊魂未定。他望着母亲，寻求安慰，但母亲只能用她所能展现的全部理解看着他，然后允许他回房间休息。

The boy was shaken. He looked at his mother, searching for salvation, but she could only look at him with all the understanding she could muster and give him permission to retire to his room.

“你在干什么？”伊莎贝尔和丈夫单独相处时，她厉声质问他。

"What are you doing?" Isabel snapped at her husband when they were alone.

——为了确保我领土的未来。你使他软弱。你对他的怜悯，他在敌人那里是找不到的。

—To guarantee the future of my domains. You have raised him to be weak. The mercy you show him he will not find in his enemies.

他还是个孩子！他还有时间变得坚强。

—He's a child! There's time for him to toughen up.

或许未必。

—Maybe not.

伊莎贝尔沉默不语。皇帝的语气不再是愤怒，而是悲伤。

Isabel remained silent. The emperor's tone was now more sorrowful than furious.

——我母亲的病遗传给了我妹妹，或许也遗传给了我。如果我注定要离世，我们必须做好准备。而作为继承人，更是如此。

—My mother's illness resides in my sister, and perhaps in me as well. If I am destined to fade away, we must be prepared. And the heir, more than anyone else.

葡萄牙女人沉默了。她一生中从未感到过如此强烈的恐惧。

The Portuguese woman fell silent. Never in her life had she felt so much fear as at that moment.

 

 

 

 

然而，在法国，这却是一片欢腾。亨利王子与凯瑟琳·德·美第奇的联姻——两人当时都还是十几岁的少年，尽管凯瑟琳拥有百岁老人般的智慧——多少驱散了路易丝·德·萨伏依去世后笼罩的阴霾。但这份喜悦并未持续太久，宴会和舞厅里的舞蹈过后，仅仅几天后，教皇克莱门特就证实了他从罗马上天得到的预感，一些人认为路易丝·德·萨伏依去世后并未升天。随着她的离世，法国国王之子与年轻的凯瑟琳联姻的政治意义也随之消失。如果已故教皇的继任者不是亚历山德罗·法尔内塞，那么这一打击对法国的利益或许不会如此严重。法尔内塞后来成为教皇保罗三世，并且从他登基之日起就展现出对皇帝的绝对支持。这位新教皇拥护正统教义，而这一原则也使查理自然而然地成为了他的合作者。在他看来，罗马之劫正如皇帝所言，是帝国军队的违抗命令之举。这位根特人作为天主教信仰的捍卫者，其功绩之多，足以掩盖那场不幸的事件，尤其是在评判他时，更应如此；尤其与其他基督教君主相比：教宗在从克莱门特继承的文献中发现了弗朗西斯和苏莱曼曾是盟友的证据。因此，这位法国人试图赢得教宗信任的努力注定徒劳；一个将个人野心置于信仰之上的人，不配得到教宗的信任。

In France, however, it was a time of celebration. The marriage between Prince Henry and Catherine de Medici—both teenagers, though she possessed the intelligence of someone who had lived a hundred years—somewhat dispelled the somber atmosphere that had settled in after the death of Louise of Savoy. But the joy lasted little beyond the banquet and the dances in the ballroom, for just a few days later Pope Clement confirmed the premonition he had received from the Roman heavens, to which some believed she had not ascended after her death. With her passing, the political utility of the marriage between the son of the French king and the young Catherine vanished, and this setback would not have been so serious for French interests had the deceased pontiff's successor not been Alessandro Farnese, who would assume the papal throne as Paul III, and who from the first day of his papacy showed himself to be an unconditional supporter of the emperor. The new Pope championed orthodoxy, and this principle made Charles his natural collaborator. From his perspective, the Sack of Rome had been an act of disobedience by the imperial troops, just as the emperor had recounted. The merits of the man from Ghent as a protector of the Catholic faith were far too numerous to overshadow that unfortunate event when judging him; especially when compared to the other monarchs of Christendom: in the documents he inherited from Clement, the Holy Father discovered evidence that Francis and Suleiman had been allies. Therefore, the Frenchman's attempts to win over the Pontiff were futile; he who had placed his ambitions before the faith did not deserve his trust.

英格兰国王也未能逃脱保罗三世的严苛惩罚。为了展现他对教会及其庇护者的纯洁追求，教宗决定遵从克莱门特的意愿，将其逐出教会。亨利与安妮·博林的婚姻违背了教会法，因此是对罗马的公然挑衅和侮辱。教宗相信，这一极端措施会让这位英国君主重新考虑，再次臣服于梵蒂冈的官方指令。显然，教宗保罗三世并不了解这位君主灵魂深处的根本机制——傲慢的权威——而且此时，博林已经怀孕，这位英国人绝不会退缩。在罗马之外所享有的自由对亨利来说如同不可或缺的天堂，他决定以一项史无前例、胆大妄为的决定来维护这份自由，这项决定将永远改变欧洲的命运。

Nor did the King of England escape unscathed from the scrupulousness of Paul III. To demonstrate the purity he desired for the Church and those who sought its protection, the Holy Father resolved to comply with Clement's wishes and excommunicated him. Henry's marriage to Anne Boleyn was outside the bounds of ecclesiastical law, and as such, it was defiant and insulting to Rome. The Pontiff trusted that this extreme measure would make the Briton reconsider and submit him once again to the official dictates of the Vatican. It was evident that Pope Paul was unaware of the fundamental mechanism of the monarch's soul—arrogant authority—and that at this point, once Boleyn had become pregnant, the last thing the Englishman intended to do was back down. The freedom he enjoyed outside the bosom of Rome seemed to Henry an indispensable paradise, and he decided to perpetuate it with an unprecedented decision, colossal in its audacity, one that would forever change the destiny of Europe.

“英格兰将拥有自己的教会，”他带着救世主般的神情对克伦威尔说，“而我将成为它的领袖。”

"England will have its own Church," he told Cromwell with a messianic look. "And I will be its head."

 

 

 

 

弗朗西斯本人既不像那位英国人那样大胆无畏，也不像他那样桀骜不驯，他甚至从未想过要效仿他。但他意识到自己必须做点什么，因为财政拮据，加上罗马和亨利的独立，他根本无法兑现用胜利来荣耀路易丝的承诺。他需要盟友，但他又能去哪里寻找呢？

Francis, for his part, was neither as bold nor as irreverent as the Briton, and he never even considered imitating him, but he was aware that he had to do something, because with his depleted finances and the independence of Rome and Henry, he could never fulfill his promise to honor Louise with victories. He needed allies, but where could he find them?

自从母亲去世后，她一直依靠妹妹玛格丽塔，玛格丽塔给了她一个主意。

Her sister Margarita, on whom she had relied since the death of her mother, gave her an idea.

——我亲爱的兄弟，宗教改革的支持者在德国已经是个问题了。如果我们王国支持他们，帝国可能会分裂，教皇的权力也会削弱。

—My dear brother, the supporters of the Reformation are already a problem in Germany. With the support of our kingdom, the Empire could be divided, and the Pope's power would also diminish.

弗朗西斯知道这番建议并非出于利他主义。玛格丽特长期以来都乐于接受那些质疑罗马教廷的人的观点。她的朋友中就有约翰·加尔文，这位崭露头角的法学家和知识分子似乎注定要在法国掀起一场类似于路德式的神学革命。

Francis knew the advice was not altruistic. Margaret had long been receptive to the arguments of those who questioned Rome. Among her friends was John Calvin, an emerging jurist and intellectual who seemed destined to lead a theological revolution in France similar to Luther's.

但这位高卢君主在宗教事务上非常传统，这个建议并没有引起他的兴趣。

But the Gallic monarch was deeply traditional in religious matters, and the suggestion did not appeal to him.

“你和那个土耳其人一起工作时毫无顾虑，”玛格丽塔提醒他，“那你和像你一样虔诚的基督徒一起工作，会有顾虑吗？”

—You had no qualms about working with the Turk—Margarita reminded him. —Do you have any qualms about working with someone who is as Christian as you?

“奥斯曼人对我来说如此陌生，以至于他的异端邪说并不令我惊讶。我无法理解一个与我地位相当的人会做出如此离经叛道的事情。”国王回答道。

"The Ottoman is so foreign to me that his heresy does not surprise me. I do not understand the deviation of one who is my equal," replied the king.

尽管心存疑虑，弗朗西斯仍然认为他在信仰上无比正直——只有他自己才了解自己的灵魂，而他觉得他的信仰比任何人都更加正统。其余的一切都不过是政治：为了达到目的而不择手段，只要能为他带来荣耀，就对潜在盟友的缺点视而不见。

Despite his reservations, Francis considered him righteous in his faith like no other—only he knew his own soul, and it seemed to him more orthodox than any other. The rest was nothing but politics: means to achieve ends and blindness to the flaws of potential allies as long as they served his glory.

 

 

 

 

如果说法国人只关注未来，那么查理则感到自己无法展望未来，眼前只有一片黑暗的帷幕。然而，当他得知提香尽管与他相遇时发生了不愉快的事情，却仍然带着他的肖像草图回到了宫殿时，他感到无比惊讶，于是鼓起勇气接见了他。画家来访之后，皇帝特意询问了他的生平，试图弄清这位意大利画家为何拥有洞察人心的天赋。虽然他了解到了许多关于这位艺术家的细节，但最令他震惊的是，提香不久前失去了妻子，而且据说他的画风也随之发生了变化。皇帝推断，这表明他也受到了这种变化的影响。毫无疑问，他是一位经历过巨大磨难的人，或许正因如此，查理才觉得在他身边比在那些虽然与他关系更亲近，却试图鼓励他，但眼神中却缺乏理解的人身边更自在，因为他们从未如此近距离地窥见过黑暗。

If the Frenchman thought only of the future, Charles felt incapable of looking ahead and saw nothing but a dark curtain. However, he was so surprised to learn that Titian, despite what had happened during their encounter, had returned to the palace with the sketch of his portrait, that he mustered the strength to receive him. After the painter's visit, the emperor had taken the trouble to inquire about his life, seeking an explanation for the Italian's gift for glimpsing the human soul. Although he discovered numerous details about the artist, what struck him most was that Titian had lost his wife not too long ago and that, he was told, his style had changed since then. This fact, the emperor deduced, reflected that the change had also taken hold of him. He was undoubtedly a man who had gone through a terrible ordeal, and perhaps that was why Carlos had felt more comfortable by his side than with those who, even though they were closer, tried to encourage him but without their gazes reflecting any understanding, because they had never glimpsed the darkness so closely.

如同上次一样，这位艺术家耐心地等待着。他早已习惯了名流们的等待，这些人常常利用等待来彰显自己的地位。他身边放着他带来的画布，上面盖着一块布。查理向提香打过招呼后，请他揭开画布，顿时惊呆了：这位意大利画家的素描确实技艺精湛，但画中的人物却憔悴、卑微、饱经风霜，毫无气度可言；这与他所见过的那种精神典范相去甚远。

The artist, as on the previous occasion, waited patiently. He was accustomed to the waiting of the illustrious, who often used it to distinguish themselves. Near him lay the canvas he had brought with him, covered by a cloth. When Charles, after greeting Titian, asked him to unveil it, he was stunned: the Italian's sketch was indeed masterful, but it depicted someone withered, petty, bent by life, devoid of grandeur; the furthest thing from an example for the spirit he had ever seen.

皇帝勃然大怒，用手杖猛击画布，将其打落一地。他想毁掉这幅素描，连同其中所蕴含的关于他灵魂的所有真相一起销毁。

The emperor flew into a rage and struck the canvas with his cane, knocking it to the ground. He wished to destroy the sketch, and with it all the truth it held about his soul.

查理在回房的路上，心中涌起一股怒火。他坐到书桌前，拿起笔和纸，给妹妹玛丽亚写信：“因为我感同身受你的悲痛，所以我决定在我不在期间，由你继续掌管佛兰德斯的政务。你每克服一个难关，你的精神就会恢复一些。你永远不要觉得自己所向披靡。真正的功德在于超越你自认为的力量，并以此为动力，不断追求卓越。”

On his way to his chamber, Charles felt a surge of anger rising within him. Once seated at his desk, he took pen and paper and wrote to his sister Maria: “Because I share your grief, I have decided that you will remain in charge of the government of Flanders during my absences. Your spirits will return with each obstacle you overcome. You will never feel invincible. Merit lies in living and aspiring beyond your perceived strength, and from that pride, drawing upon it.”

凯撒签了字，然后哭了：他还活着。

Caesar signed the letter and wept: he was alive.

 

 

 

 

当大臣们看到皇帝数周以来第一次走进办公室时，他们什么也没说，但都忍不住交换了欣喜而如释重负的眼神。查理看起来精神焕发，仿佛突然间所有在沉睡中积蓄的力量都回来了。当他得知一批黄金从他们新征服的、位于大洋彼岸的秘鲁运抵时，皇帝的眼睛亮了起来。上帝在奖赏他的复活，祂不希望他无所事事。

The advisors said nothing when they saw the emperor enter the office for the first time in weeks, but they couldn't help but exchange joyful and relieved glances. Charles seemed exuberant, as if he suddenly possessed all the strength he had conserved during his slumber. When he was informed that a shipment of gold had arrived from those newly conquered lands across the ocean they called Peru, the emperor's eyes lit up. God was rewarding him for his resurrection, and He didn't want him to be idle.

 

 

 

 

—我将下令进攻阿尔及尔。

—I am going to give the order to attack Algiers.

如果不是同时发生了一件真正值得关注的事情，伊莎贝尔或许会对这个决定更加震惊：她的丈夫又露出了笑容。看到自己的两个愿望都实现了，她感到无比欣慰。

Isabel would have been more shocked by the decision had it not been accompanied by something truly newsworthy: her husband was smiling again. Seeing both her wishes fulfilled filled her with joy.

——你根本无法想象这些王国会有多么感激。他们终于可以生活在没有恐惧的环境中了！

—You have no idea how grateful these kingdoms will be. They will finally live without fear!

我总是选择我认为最好的做法，而不是听从内心的指引，尽管我确实有内心的声音。

—I always decide what I think is best. Not what my heart tells me to do, even though I have one.

皇后对此毫不怀疑。她用温柔的目光凝视着查尔斯。这时，她注意到他没有拄拐杖。

The Empress had no doubt about it. She gazed at Charles with tender eyes. She then noticed that he had appeared without his cane.

—你不再需要帮助了吗？

—Don't you need support anymore?

—不适感依然存在。但渐渐地，活力正在恢复。

—The discomfort persists. But little by little, vigor returns.

凯撒将她拥入怀中，热情地吻了她。

Caesar took her in his arms and kissed her passionately.

“也许浪费掉它不太明智，”她说，希望他会不同意。

"Perhaps it would be unwise to waste it," she said, hoping he would disagree.

“在你身上？我觉得没有比这更好的开销了。”他一边脱她的衣服一边回答道。

"On you? I don't see a better expense," he replied as he undressed her.

 

 

 

 

法国宫廷对英格兰国王亨利的接待十分隆重，虽然不及多年前在黄金平原上的盛况。这位英国人并不怀念那些奢华的场面；弗朗西斯没有因为他脱离罗马而抛弃他，这在他看来已是莫大的恩惠。

The French court's reception of Henry of England was splendid, though lacking the splendor displayed years before at the Field of Tela de Oro. The Briton did not miss those extravagances; the fact that Francis had not abandoned him for his independence from Rome seemed generosity enough.

——而其他君主给我的只有厌恶。或者更糟：沉默。

—From other sovereigns I only receive revulsion. Or worse: silence.

“你可以按照自己的意愿治理你的王国，”高卢国王在他们入座宴会桌旁时对他说。

"You are free to govern your kingdom as you please," the Gallic monarch told him as they took their seats at the banquet table.

这位英国人似乎欣喜若狂。

The Englishman seemed overjoyed.

我感觉自己像个重见天日的囚犯。没有什么决定能逃脱我的掌控，也没有什么义务能束缚我。

—I feel like a prisoner who finally sees the light of day. There is no decision that escapes me, nor any obligation that submits me.

午餐气氛轻松愉快。他们甚至还开玩笑地谈起了过去那场让他们针锋相对的摔跤比赛。弗朗西斯确信，今天最终会以结盟告终。

Lunch took place in a lighthearted atmosphere. They even joked about the wrestling match that had pitted them against each other in the past. Francis was certain that the day would end in an alliance.

“你应该效仿我，”亨利说。“为什么要直接僭越罗马的权力呢？”

"You should imitate me," said Henry. "Why simply assume the power of Rome?"

法国人认为这是一个提出自己计划的好时机。

The Frenchman saw this as an opportune moment to suggest his plans.

“我愿意，”他撒谎道，“但我认为独立存在缺陷。我们俩都会被排除在外。明智的做法是与他人结盟，以免成为皇帝和教皇的猎物，不幸的是，他们的联合是不可避免的。”

“I would be willing,” he lied. “But I see a flaw in independence. We would both be left out of the equation. It would be wise to join forces with others so as not to become easy prey for the Emperor and the Pope, whose union is, unfortunately, inevitable.”

恩里克抿了一口法国葡萄酒，他始终不习惯这种酒的味道。

Enrique took a sip of French wine, which he never got used to.

他饶有兴趣地问道：“你有什么建议？”

"What do you suggest?" he asked, interested.

—加强与改革支持者的联系。

—Strengthen ties with supporters of reform.

弗朗西斯科本想阐述他的提议，但当他察觉到对方对他的话语的直接反应时，他不知道该如何继续；英国人的表情已经完全失去了对他的同情。

Francisco intended to argue his proposal, but when he perceived the other's immediate reaction to his words, he didn't know how to continue; the Englishman's expression had lost all trace of sympathy towards him.

恩里克把酒杯重重地放在桌子上。

Enrique placed his glass on the table with a sharp thud.

—我已与罗马保持距离，但丝毫没有背离教条！

—I have distanced myself from Rome, but not one iota from dogma!

在场众人陷入沉默。蒙莫朗西感觉自己仿佛又回到了那个噩梦般的夜晚——黄金原野。弗朗西斯科则试图将话题拉回正轨，假装很肯定，尽管他内心深处知道自己正走向灾难。

Those present fell silent. Montmorency felt as if he were reliving that nightmarish evening in the Field of Gold. For his part, Francisco tried to steer the conversation back on track, feigning conviction, though inwardly he saw himself headed for disaster.

“战略没有固定的模式，”法国人回答说，“正如你们自己教导我们的那样。”

"Strategy knows no orthodoxies," replied the Frenchman. "As you yourselves have taught us."

你竟敢称我为异端？

—Do you dare call me a heretic?

 

 

 

 

说实话，弗朗西斯觉得自己就像一个求婚者，选错了花。他选择的“花束”——那些改革派——反而让他与亨利疏远了。如果连英国国王都不接受他们为盟友——甚至准备与任何接纳他们的人断绝关系——那么指望他们就毫无意义。可是，他又能做些什么来彰显自己的威望呢？与英国人的会面失败后，这位君主的焦虑彻底失控。他仿佛能看到母亲失望的目光，无论她身在何处。

To tell the truth, Francis felt like a suitor who had chosen the wrong flowers to woo his beloved. The bouquet he had selected—the reformers—had alienated him from Henry. If even the English king wouldn't accept them as allies—and was even prepared to repudiate anyone who did—there was no point in relying on them. But then, what could he do to aggrandize himself? After the failed meeting with the Briton, the monarch's anxiety spiraled out of control. He thought he could see his mother's disappointed gaze from wherever she might be.

然而，弗朗西斯科很快意识到，从天上审判他的并非路易莎，而是上帝本人。当他站在十八岁少年冰冷的尸体前时，他明白了这一点：那是他唯一的儿子。这场悲剧向他揭示了神的惩罚，不仅因为他儿子年纪尚轻——目睹他那冰冷稚嫩的面容是多么令人毛骨悚然，接受他永远无法长大成人的残酷现实更是令人煎熬——还因为如此猝然的死亡根本无法解释。这只能是天意的安排，它以残酷的方式施行教训：夺走了他的继承人，让国王认识到自己的罪孽。

However, it wasn't long before Francisco realized that it wasn't Luisa judging him from on high, but God himself. He knew this when he stood before the lifeless body of an eighteen-year-old: his firstborn son. The tragedy revealed itself to him as divine punishment, not only because of his son's youth—how grotesque it was to witness those icy, adolescent features, and what torture to accept that they would never mature—but also because no consistent explanation could be found for such a sudden death. This could only be the work of Providence, which had acted with the cruelty it employed when it sought to teach lessons: it had snatched away his heir so that the king would know himself to be in sin.

弗朗西斯利用妹妹的影响力召集了一群法国著名改革家。玛格丽特将此举解读为国王接受新神学的一步。当她发现哥哥派兵迎战，并且这些人无一幸免时，她几乎要疯了。弗朗西斯默默忍受着她的侮辱，​​以及她似乎永无止境的泪水。

Francis used his sister's influence to gather a group of prominent French reformers. Margaret interpreted the request as a step by the king toward accepting the new theology. When she discovered that her brother had sent his troops to meet them and that they had left none of those men alive, she thought she would go mad. Francis stoically endured her insults, and also her tears, which seemed endless.

——你应该感谢我。上帝因​​为我们与异端结盟而惩罚了我们。谁知道祂是不是因为你长期以来对他们的同情而夺走了我们的母亲。

—You should thank me. God had singled us out for allying ourselves with the heretics. Who knows if He hasn't taken our mother from us because of the sympathy you've shown them for so long.

泪水模糊了玛格丽塔的双眼，即便视线清晰，她也认不出自己的哥哥。在她眼前，只有一只怪物。

Tears blurred Margarita's eyes, but even if they had been clear, she still wouldn't have recognized her brother. All she saw before her was a monster.

“你们犯下那场屠杀不是为了让我们与上帝和解，而是为了让我们与英国和罗马和解！”

"You did not commit that massacre to reconcile us with God, but with England, and with Rome!"

—我的决定既符合主的意愿，也符合我自己的意愿，这意味着采取这一措施是必要的。

—That my decision serves the Lord's wishes as much as my own means that the measure was necessary.

她神情恍惚，身体僵硬，后退了几步。

She, dazed and with her body stiff, took several steps back.

“上帝或许会原谅你，但我不会，”他喃喃自语道。

"God may forgive you, but I will not," he murmured.

玛格丽塔立刻转身离去。目送她离去，弗朗西斯科感到内心无比破碎。他原本用来下令屠杀新教徒的冷酷无情，如同盔甲般瞬间化为乌有。短短时间内，他失去了母亲和长子；还有弗朗西斯卡，自从国王要求她归还他曾赠予的珠宝后，她便不再理睬他，这一举动深深伤害了这位昔日的爱人。为了弥补失去的一切，这位君主屈服于野心，试图用这些失去赋予他生命的意义，他紧紧抓住上帝惩罚他的理论不放，以此逃避自己如同最邪恶之人般的罪行。然而，他的内心早已破碎不堪。

Margarita immediately turned her back on him. As he watched her leave, Francisco felt himself breaking inside. The coldness he had needed to order the murder of the Protestants crumbled like armor that had turned to liquid. In a short space of time, he had lost his mother and his firstborn son; and also Francesca, who had stopped speaking to him when the king demanded the return of the jewels he had once given her, a gesture his former lover deeply wounded. The monarch had surrendered to ambition to give his life all the meaning these losses had stolen, and he had clung to his theory that God had punished him to avoid judging his actions as those of the worst of men. But his heart was devastated.

——不是你。——那是一个一无所有的人的声音。——帮帮我，让我重拾活下去的希望。

—Not you. —It was the voice of someone who had nothing left.— Help me want to live.

玛格丽塔只想离开他；然而，她却停下了脚步。

Margarita wanted nothing more than to leave him; and yet, she stopped walking.

 

 

 

 

自命运让查理和弗朗西斯成为宿敌以来，似乎一直如此：命运抛弃一人，便眷顾另一人。当弗朗西斯身处逆境之时，皇帝却精神抖擞。他的健康状况日益好转，攻打阿尔及尔的战争计划也接近完成。此外，他的儿子似乎也很好地适应了新的生活，甚至在他写给母亲——而且只写给她——的信件中，字里行间都流露出他重获的活力。皇帝在养伤和辛勤工作之余，重拾对查理曼大帝的著作，比以往任何时候都更加坚定地要尽可能地效仿他的丰功伟绩。

As had been the custom ever since fate had made Charles and Francis rivals, when fortune abandoned one, it blessed the other. While the Frenchman was going through his worst period, the emperor was in high spirits. His health was improving daily, and the war plans against Algiers were nearing completion. Moreover, his son seemed to have adapted reasonably well to his new life, and even in the strokes of the letters he wrote to his mother—and only to her—one could perceive the newfound strength. The emperor, while recovering and working tirelessly, had returned to his readings about Charlemagne and was more determined than ever to emulate, as far as possible, those feats.

就在那时，消息传来：巴巴罗萨——这位逐渐成为传奇反派的人物——为苏莱曼大帝夺取了突尼斯。这座要塞此前一直由皇帝的附庸贝伊·穆莱·哈桑统治，具有极其重要的战略价值。它位于北非海岸，意大利南部，是控制地中海的关键所在。如果突尼斯继续留在奥斯曼帝国手中，皇帝在意大利的领地将时刻处于危险之中；人人都知道，突尼斯是苏莱曼征服南欧的第一站。

It was then that news arrived that Barbarossa, who was beginning to emerge as a legendary villain, had won Tunis for Suleiman the Magnificent. The stronghold, which until then had been governed by Bey Muley Hassan, a vassal of the emperor, possessed paramount strategic value. Its location, on the North African coast and south of Italy, made it a key point for dominating the Mediterranean. If it remained in Ottoman hands, the emperor's Italian possessions would be exposed to constant danger; everyone knew that Tunis was the first stop on Suleiman's path to conquering southern Europe.

 

 

 

 

“阿尔及尔还得等等。”尽管确信自己的策略已经改变，查理还是为再次让妻子失望而感到羞愧。“我必须保卫那不勒斯和西西里。”

"Algiers will have to wait." Despite being convinced of his change of strategy, Charles felt ashamed to disappoint his wife again. "I must protect Naples and Sicily."

伊莎贝尔默默地接受了这个决定。

Isabel silently accepted the decision.

“教宗要求我这样做，”他继续说道。

"The Holy Father asks me to," he continued.

“我知道他们的要求比我对你的要求更让你感到压力，”葡萄牙女人回答道，语气中带着一丝愤世嫉俗。

—I understand that their demands weigh more heavily on you than the ones I make of you —replied the Portuguese woman, not without cynicism.

——是罗马方面提出的请求！幸好，新教皇向我伸出了援手！您很清楚我在前任教皇统治下遭受了多少苦难，也知道当教会反对我时，我根本无法履行我的职责。

—It is Rome that requests it! The new Pope extends his hand to me, fortunately! You know well what I suffered under his predecessor, and how impossible it is for me to assume my duties when the Church opposes me.

皇后知道查理的讲话不无道理，但她恳求停止对西班牙海岸的进一步袭击，却让她感到失望。她明白目前的局势令皇帝进退两难，但她恼火的是，事情最终还是会像往常一样，通过忽视西班牙来解决。伊莎贝拉竭力想办法，避免这种失望导致两人关系疏远。一想到要对皇帝生气，她就备受煎熬。

The Empress knew that Charles's speech held some truth, but neither did her plea to prevent further attacks on the Spanish coast. She recognized that the situation put the Emperor in a difficult position, but she was irritated that it would be resolved as usual—by neglecting Spain. Isabella sought a way to prevent this disappointment from creating distance between them. The thought of being angry with him tormented her.

“我不能违抗皇帝的命令。但如果你愿意听从我的意愿，我也会欣然服从：在西班牙待上一段时间。从这段近距离观察，你就能意识到这些王国面临的严峻威胁。到那时，我的要求也就显得多余了。”

"I can do nothing to contradict the commands of an emperor. But I would better obey your will if you would heed mine: remain in Spain for an extended period. From this proximity, you will become aware of the grave threats these kingdoms face. Then my demands will be superfluous."

伊莎贝尔没有告诉丈夫的是，虽然那确实是事实，但她同样需要他在身边。她至今仍未从那场意外后她以为失去他时的疏离感中恢复过来。在他康复期间，她强颜欢笑，而他却无精打采、郁郁寡欢地四处游荡。但当胡安娜的疯狂阴影笼罩查理时，皇后再次徘徊在悬崖边。她明白，即使他活着，她也可能失去他的精神，这与彻底失去他并无二致。小费迪南的记忆和与菲利普的分离丝毫没有让她振作起来。摄政是她最不担心的事，她觉得自己完全可以独自处理。如果她不肯让皇帝离开，那是因为她发现自己爱他胜过爱自己。

What Isabel didn't tell her husband was that, while that was true, it was no less true that she needed him close. She hadn't recovered from the feeling of estrangement she felt when she feared she had lost him after the accident. During his convalescence, she pretended to be strong, while he wandered about listlessly and sadly. But when the shadow of Juana's madness fell upon Charles, the empress once again peered over a precipice. She understood that even if he remained alive, she could lose him in spirit, which amounted to the same thing as losing him completely. The memory of little Ferdinand and the separation from Philip did nothing to strengthen her. The regency was the least of her worries, and she felt capable of handling it alone. If she refused to let the emperor leave, it was because she had discovered that she loved that man more than herself.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在金博尔顿城堡，一位牧师正在聆听凯瑟琳的最后忏悔。房间里光线昏暗；这位前王后悄然离世，没有炫耀自己的衰弱，这让她感到些许慰藉。当她得知自己的病情时，她感到无比悲痛和讽刺：她的子宫里长了一个肿瘤，仿佛她多年来因父亲未能给她生个儿子而对他的无数诅咒，最终都应验了，而且是以最糟糕的方式。她唯一的孩子如今悲痛欲绝，泪流满面。玛丽·都铎二十出头，像她父亲一样有着浅金色的头发，由于父亲近来给予她的生活，她变得脆弱不堪。凯瑟琳是她的全世界；她既敬佩她，又憎恨她的父亲和安妮·博林。不公将这对母女紧紧联系在一起，几乎使她们融为一体，而如今，这位西班牙女人的死却将这份纽带撕裂。

Meanwhile, at Kimbolton Castle, a priest was hearing Catherine's last confession. Light barely entered the chamber; the former queen found some solace in departing without flaunting her decline. When she learned of her illness, it struck her as tragically ironic: a tumor had grown in her womb, as if the thousand curses she had hurled at him for years for not giving her a son had finally borne fruit, and in the worst possible way. The only child she had borne was now distraught in tears. Mary Tudor was in her early twenties, a young woman with pale blonde hair like her father, and vulnerable because of the life he had given her in recent times. Catherine had been her world; she admired her as much as she hated her father and Anne Boleyn. Injustice had bound mother and daughter together, almost making them one, a bond that was now being torn apart by the death of the Spanish woman.

仪式结束了。凯瑟琳已准备好与主同在，事实上，她渴望终于可以安息。她几乎耗尽了所有力气，示意女儿靠近些。玛丽亚跪在她身旁，虔诚地亲吻着她的双手，泪水仍在流淌。

The priest concluded the ritual. Catherine was ready to be with the Lord, and the truth was, she longed to finally rest. With barely any strength left, she gestured to her daughter to come closer. Maria knelt beside her and kissed her hands with reverence, still weeping.

“我想和你一起去，”年轻女子呻吟道。

"I want to go with you," the young woman moaned.

来自阿拉贡的女子平静地否认了此事。

The woman from Aragon calmly denied it.

——尽管悲伤，但当你离开这间屋子时，请抬起头，接受你的命运。

—Lament, but when you leave this room, lift your head and accept your destiny.

——流放和孤独，除此之外，别无其他。

—Exile and solitude, it is nothing else.

——感到孤独吗？我把你们留给你们最好的陪伴：那就是主，他已经表明自己与我们同在。

—Loneliness? I leave you in the best company: that of the Lord, who has shown himself to be on our side.

玛丽亚明白她的意思。国王和博林的第一个孩子是个男孩，但却是死胎。

Maria knew what she meant. The king and Boleyn's first child had been a boy, but stillborn.

“他们会骂你是私生子。当他们这么说的时候，”西班牙女人说，“你就看看你的真实身份：你是英国女王的女儿，将来也会是女王的女儿。”

"They will call you a bastard. When they do," said the Spanish woman, "look at them for what you are: the daughter of the Queen of England, and the one who will be in the future."

临终前，凯瑟琳口述了一封信给亨利。信中，她谴责亨利对他们的残忍，并请求他从此好好照顾他们的女儿玛丽。她把真正想说的话留在最后：尽管经历了这一切，她还是原谅了他，而且她依然对他念念不忘。玛丽听后心想，母亲的仁慈大概是她少数几个没有继承到的品质之一。

Before dying, Catherine dictated a letter to Henry. In it, she reproached him for the cruelty with which he had treated them and asked him to take care of their daughter Mary from then on. She reserved the last lines for what she truly wanted to tell him: that, despite everything, she forgave him, and that her eyes still desired him above all else. Upon hearing it, Mary thought that her mother's mercy must be one of the few traits she had not inherited from her.

 

 

 

 

在西班牙宫廷，皇帝下令为他的姑姑举行弥撒。除了失去亲人的悲痛之外，回忆起逝者晚年的遭遇也令他倍感伤痛。查理一想到她晚年所受的屈辱，就感到一阵恶心。他希望将突尼斯战役中战胜巴巴罗萨的胜利献给她，以此弥补她晚年未能获得的荣耀。

At the Spanish court, the emperor ordered a mass for his aunt's soul. To the inherent sadness of a family loss was added the sorrow of recalling the deceased's final years. Charles felt nauseous imagining how humiliating they must have been for her. He hoped to dedicate the victory over Barbarossa in Tunis to her, that the glory she had been denied in her last years would somehow be compensated.

入侵非洲要塞的准备工作仍在紧锣密鼓地进行。巴塞罗那被选为数百艘船只的集结地，这些船只来自西班牙各地和佛兰德斯，将与土耳其人展开决战。在策划此次进攻期间流传的众多文件中，出现了一份署有苏莱曼本人签名的信函，但无人能够证实其真实性。

Preparations for the invasion of the African stronghold continued unabated. Barcelona was chosen as the assembly point for the hundreds of ships, arriving from all over Spain and Flanders, that would confront the Turks. Among the many documents circulating during the planning of the assault, a message appeared bearing the signature of Suleiman himself, though no one could verify its authenticity.

——读——皇帝命令塔韦拉，并表现出了恰到好处的兴趣。

—Read —the emperor ordered Tavera, with just the right amount of interest.

红衣主教面前放着那份文件，他饶有兴致地笑了；他觉得上面的内容很滑稽。

The cardinal, with the paper in front of him, smiled amusedly; he found the text comical.

陛下，这全是胡说八道！他们甚至在战前就开始为战败找借口！而且理由还牵强附会。

—It's a load of nonsense, Your Majesty. They're trying to make excuses for their defeat, even before the battle! And with far-fetched arguments.

“比如什么？”凯撒一边签署文件，一边饶有兴致地问道。

"Like what?" asked Caesar, amused, as he signed documents.

他说他不想像在维也纳那样去前线与士兵作战。“没有指挥官的战斗是不光彩的，不值得打。”多么虚伪的懦弱……

—He says he doesn't want to go to the front to fight against soldiers, as he did in Vienna. "A battle without leaders is dishonorable and not worth fighting." Such convoluted cowardice…

在场的阿尔巴公爵立刻意识到，那位自称苏莱曼的家伙的话对他的君主造成了多么深远的影响。查理陷入了沉思，更重要的是，他感到受到了极大的冒犯。

The Duke of Alba, who was also present, immediately realized how deeply the words of the supposed Suleiman had affected his lord. Charles was left deep in thought and, above all, offended.

“他说的有道理，”凯撒说道。

"He has a point," said Caesar.

“他只是想贬低你的胜利，”红衣主教语气变得严肃起来。

"He's just trying to diminish your triumph," said the cardinal in a less lighthearted tone.

“避免战争是明智之举，”公爵补充道，“你们不能冒生命危险，尤其不能因为异教徒的冒犯而战。继承人还只是个孩子，你们也还在恢复之中。”

“Avoiding battle is wise,” the duke added. “You cannot afford to risk your lives, least of all in response to an offense from the infidel. The heir is just a child, and you are still recovering.”

皇帝不愿谈论此事。他确信无人会理解他的困境。

The emperor preferred not to discuss it. He was certain that no one would understand his dilemma.

那天下午，他几个月来第一次来到田野，身边跟着一匹马。最难的是骑上马：他注意到自己的腿虽然健康，却感觉很僵硬。伸展双腿很痛，但一旦坐上马鞍，过了一会儿，事故的记忆再次涌上心头，他催促马走起来。过了一会儿，焦虑渐渐消散。这促使他加快步伐，直到骑得稳稳当当。他感到风吹拂着脸庞，汗水浸透全身，心脏怦怦直跳，仿佛焕然一新。他想，总有一天，那一天总是比人们预想的来得更快，也总是毫无预兆，他将无法再做他正在做的事情。到那时，只剩下他辉煌的记忆。现在是时候创造未来的记忆了：是时候行动了。

That afternoon he went out into the fields for the first time in months, accompanied by a horse. The hardest part was getting on the animal: he noticed his legs felt stiff, though otherwise healthy. It hurt to stretch them, but once in the saddle, and after a few moments when the memory of the accident overwhelmed him, he urged the horse to walk. After a while, the anxiety had dissipated. This prompted him to increase the pace until he was riding. He felt the wind whipping his face, sweat bathing his entire body, and his heart pounding as if it were brand new. He thought that one day, that day that would always come sooner than desired and without warning, he wouldn't be able to do what he was doing. By then, only the memories of his greatness would remain. It was time to create the material of future memories: it was time to act.

 

 

 

 

几天后，卡洛斯汗流浃背、精力充沛地从乡间又一次策马返回时，伊莎贝尔在宫殿的一条走廊里找到了他。

A few days later, when Carlos, sweaty and full of energy, was returning from another gallop in the countryside, Isabel approached him in one of the palace corridors.

——宫廷里说你正考虑亲自指挥军队。那不是真的。

—They say at court that you are considering taking command of your armies. That won't be true.

卡洛斯用前臂擦了擦额头的汗，装作一副茫然不知所措的样子。

Carlos wiped the sweat from his brow with his forearm and pretended to be disoriented.

“我早就料到了，”他的妻子接着说。“我告诉他们这不可能。你答应过要留在我身边。这世上没有任何野心或骄傲能让你违背诺言。”

“I figured as much,” his wife continued. “I told them it was impossible. That you promised to stay by my side. And that there is no ambition or pride in this world that could lead you to break your word.”

皇后等待着答复。皇帝察觉到她有些异样，显得脆弱不堪。他的沉默本身就是一种罪证。

The empress waited for a reply. The emperor noticed she was strange, fragile. His silence was incriminating.

“这是谎言，”他最后说道。

"It's a lie," he finally said.

他们默默地对视着，一言不发，直到她点了点头，然后神情严肃地继续沿着走廊走去。

They looked at each other without saying a word until she nodded and, serious, continued on her way down the corridor.

 

 

 

 

菲利普的老师们对这位继承人性格的转变感到惊讶。在与宫廷其他人分离的那段时间里，这个男孩既愤怒又多愁善感，每晚都给母亲写信——没完没了的信，常常带着泪痕。然而，他渐渐适应了新的生活。他开始认真学习，学习内容也因需要而变得十分广泛，并逐渐展现出一种学术的气质。他对音乐产生了兴趣，也想了解绘画。至于体育锻炼，考虑到他的年龄，这些锻炼并不多，也比较轻松，但他竟然开始享受其中。他时不时地要求学习剑术，虽然他只是把剑术当作游戏，但他的老师们仍然希望，这位继承人的性格终于觉醒了。

Philip's tutors were astonished by the evolution in the heir's character. In the days following his separation from the rest of the court, the boy had been both angry and sentimental, writing to his mother every night—endless letters, often dampened with tears. However, little by little, he adapted to his new routine. He applied himself to his studies, which were, by necessity, quite varied, and a scholarly tone had emerged. He showed an interest in music and also wanted to learn about painters. As for the physical exercises, which were occasional and light given his age, he had actually come to enjoy them. From time to time, he asked to be trained in swordsmanship, and although he approached it as a game, his tutors wanted to believe that, at last, the heir's character had awakened.

一天下午，当一位老师正在教他击剑的基本要领时，皇帝出现在地平线上。皇帝身边跟着阿尔巴公爵和一队士兵。皇帝留下他的部下，菲利普也留下他的老师。父子二人相遇时，菲利普立刻立正，这让这位来自根特的年轻人既感到骄傲又感到温柔。

One afternoon, while one of his instructors was teaching him the rudiments of fencing, the emperor appeared on the horizon. He was accompanied by the Duke of Alba and a retinue of soldiers. The emperor left his men behind; Philip did the same with his teacher. When father and son met, the latter snapped to attention, which stirred pride and tenderness in the man from Ghent.

—你还得再回法庭一段时间。

—You will return to court, for a while.

听到这话，费利佩不由自主地笑了。

Upon hearing this, Felipe smiled involuntarily.

——别把这当成休息。这是你的职责。国王不在的时候，继承人必须履行职责。

—Don't take this as a break. It's your duty. The heir must be there in the king's absence.

——你要走了吗？——话音刚落，男孩就明白了父亲所在的部队就在附近。

—Are you leaving? —No sooner had he said it than the boy understood the presence of the troop with which his father was traveling.

——战斗迟早会到来。

—The battle comes sooner or later.

小男孩虽然担心，但并没有大吵大闹。

The little boy was worried, but he didn't make a fuss.

“我们俩都能做出牺牲。伟大不在于头衔，而在于能否挺身而出。”说着这番话，查理不禁反思自己是否真的做到了，因为他带着谎言离开了宫廷，没有勇气向伊莎贝拉坦白自己要去巴塞罗那，然后再从那里去突尼斯，从而违背了自己对她的承诺。“照顾好你母亲。”

"We are both capable of sacrifice. Greatness lies not in titles, but in rising to the occasion." And as he said this, Charles wondered if he had, because he had left the court with a lie, lacking the courage to confess to Isabella that he was going to Barcelona and from there to Tunis, thus betraying the word he had given her. "Keep your mother warm."

这时，等候凯撒的骑兵队的马匹发出了一声鼻息。他这才想起，时间紧迫，刻不容缓。

Then there was a snort from the horses of the troop waiting for Caesar. He remembered that there was no time to lose.

“你必须服从，一切都要服从。”卡洛斯对儿子说。

—You will comply, with everything—Carlos told his son.

菲利普胸口涌起一股异样的感觉：既有对父亲信任的感激之情，也有对父亲安危的担忧。他再次行了个军礼，皇帝却突然拥抱了他，打断了他的动作。

Philip felt an unusual sensation in his chest: it was emotion at the trust placed in him, but also fear for his father's life. He repeated his martial salute, which the emperor interrupted by embracing him.

 

 

 

 

伊莎贝尔像在宫廷里见到他时那样拥抱了这个孩子。他的出现让她惊喜万分，她毫不犹豫地询问他来此的目的。

Isabel embraced the child in the same way when she received him at court. The surprise of having him there delighted her so much that she didn't hesitate to question the reason for his presence.

—他不在的时候，我会陪着你。

—I'll keep you company while he's away.

皇后难以接受丈夫背叛了她。她想到自己腹中的孩子，她还没来得及告诉他。震惊过后，愤怒瞬间吞噬了她。她忘记了平日里展现的镇定。查理的谎言深深刺痛了她，更让她时刻提心吊胆，担心他的安危。战争，种种可能性，他恐怕无法平安归来。毫无疑问，皇帝在做出那个决定时只考虑了自己，这让伊莎贝拉不禁怀疑，这个男人是否配得上她所宣扬的爱。

The Empress struggled to accept that her husband had betrayed her. She thought of the child she carried within her, whose presence she hadn't yet had time to tell him about. Then, once the shock subsided, rage consumed her. She forgot the composure she usually displayed. Charles had wounded her to the core by lying to her, and above all, by condemning her to constantly fear for his life. A war; so many possibilities that he wouldn't return safe and sound. Undoubtedly, the Emperor had thought only of himself when making that decision, and this led Isabella to wonder if this man was worthy of the love she professed for him.

令他痛苦的是，他最终得出结论：他并没有。

And, to his torment, he concluded that he did not.

13

13

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

皇后微微睁开双眼。她环顾四周，只见医生和助产士熙熙攘攘。由于尚未听到任何胎动，她想胎儿应该还在腹中；但她也不敢肯定，因为几个小时以来她所承受的痛苦实在太过剧烈，最终让她昏昏睡去。她闻到房间里弥漫着血腥味，即使对于分娩来说也显得过浓。这几乎令人难以忍受的气味唤起了她对葡萄牙的回忆，尽管她想不出原因。伊莎贝尔比以往任何时候都更加疲惫，以至于她很高兴终于耗尽所有力气，沉沉睡去。

The Empress opened her eyes slightly. Around her, she glimpsed the swarming figures of physicians and midwives. Since she hadn't yet heard any baby moving, she thought it must still be inside her womb; but she couldn't be sure, because the torment she had been enduring for hours was so intense that it had finally lulled her to sleep. She perceived the smell of blood that hung in the chamber, and it seemed excessive even for childbirth. That almost unbearable odor stirred memories of Portugal, though she couldn't guess why. Isabel was more tired than ever, so much so that she was glad to finally lose all her strength and fall asleep.

“陛下，用力！”医生催促道，将她唤醒。

"Your Majesty, push!" urged a doctor, waking her up.

皇后神情恍惚，渴望感受痛苦，于是遵从了命令。很快，房间里便充满了孩子的哭声。

Dazed and desperate to feel pain, the empress obeyed. Soon the chamber was filled with the sound of a child crying.

 

 

 

 

在女儿乔安娜出生的同时，查理也沐浴在光环之中，尽管这光环源于他的名望和美貌。突尼斯战役取得了胜利，如今，罗马——这座帝王的诞生地，神话的摇篮，屋大维、图拉真、查理曼大帝加冕，甚至尤利乌斯·凯撒的舞台——首次迎接了他的到来。这座城市的历史不仅被史学家们记录下来，更在它的古迹中得以延续，而这些古迹正是这位来自根特的皇帝在沿着阿庇亚大道凯旋入城后所看到的。这段旅程令他叹为观止。熙熙攘攘的人群赞叹着凯撒的仪态和服饰所展现的尊严，但在这般景象中，他却感到自己渺小如尘，每一寸土地都显得既迷人又虚幻。当他经过斗兽场、古罗马广场，最后来到万神殿时，他不得不努力压抑住内心的激动。此地的美景，再加上它对于拥有皇帝头衔的人来说意义非凡，让他觉得自己已经达到了人生的巅峰。

While his daughter Joanna was being born, Charles was also basking in a halo, albeit one of fame and beauty. The Tunis campaign had been a success, and now Rome—the birthplace of emperors, the cradle of myths, the stage for Octavian, Trajan, Charlemagne's coronation, and even Julius Caesar!—welcomed him for the first time. The city's history was not only preserved in the accounts of chroniclers but lived on in its monuments, the very ones the emperor from Ghent beheld after his triumphal entry along the Appian Way. The journey left him awestruck. The crowds that thronged the streets admired the Caesar's dignity in his bearing and attire, but he felt insignificant in that setting, where every inch seemed both captivating and unreal. He had to suppress his emotion as he passed the Colosseum, the Forum, and then the Pantheon. The beauty of the place, added to the significance it held for the one who held the title of emperor, made him feel that he had reached a peak.

保罗三世在基督教世界的中心——圣彼得广场等候着他。教皇和皇帝热情地互相问候，并一同进入圣彼得大教堂，参加了弥撒。正因为如此，对查理而言，一切都承载着永恒的意义。

Paul III awaited him in St. Peter's Square, the heart of Christendom. Pope and emperor greeted each other warmly and entered the basilica together, where they attended Mass. Because of the context, everything held for Charles the weight of something enduring.

然而，当教皇和他从无声的姿态转变为言语时，永恒的魅力便退居幕后，世界又恢复了往常的样子：琐碎而又符合人类的尺度。

However, when the Pope and he moved from silent gestures to words, the enchantment of the eternal faded into the background, and the world became as it usually was: petty and of human scale.

—我不会偏袒弗朗西斯，也不会偏袒你。

—I will not favor Francis, but neither will I favor you.

皇帝怀疑自己的耳朵。在其他情况下，教皇的中立或许是正义之举，但在此情况下却并非如此：教皇的办公桌上放着几封查理从突尼斯带来的信件。这些信件连同其他文件，都是查理从奥斯曼当局手中缴获的。负责分析缴获文件的官员在阅读了这些信件后，立即向皇帝禀报。皇帝仔细研读了这些信件，震惊不已：信中包含着法国国王与奥斯曼帝国多年来勾结的证据。

The emperor doubted his ears. The Pope's neutrality would have been an act of justice under other circumstances, but not in this one: on the Holy Father's desk lay several letters that Charles had brought him from Tunis. He had seized them, along with other documents, from the Ottoman authorities. Those tasked with analyzing the seized documents, after reading those letters, had rushed to inform the emperor. He studied them, scandalized: they contained evidence of years of collaboration between the King of France and the Turkish Empire.

“您打算同样对待我们吗？”教宗的回答让卡洛斯突然感到自己身处一个毫无逻辑的世界。“对于那些冒着生命危险与异教徒作战的人，以及那些与他结盟的人，您打算如何对待他们？”

"Do you intend to treat us the same?" After the Holy Father's response, Carlos suddenly felt trapped in a world devoid of logic. "To whomever risked his life against the infidel, and to whomever was his ally?"

—最近，弗朗西斯表现出想要打击王国境内异端邪说的迹象……

—Lately, Francis has shown signs of wanting to tackle heresy in his kingdom…

教宗知道，鉴于高卢人的罪行，他的论点听起来很荒谬，但事实是，随着时间的推移，他越来越觉得坚持正统教义是不切实际的。如果他继续坚持正统教义，就只能依靠皇帝，而一旦被皇帝吞并，或许只是一步之遥。梵蒂冈大多数同僚都持同样的观点，而教宗也通过各种会议、晚宴、耳语和信息，逐渐意识到了这一点。

The Pope knew his arguments seemed ridiculous given the Gaul's sins, but the truth was that, with the passage of time, his demand for orthodoxy had struck him as impractical. If he remained faithful to it, he could only count on the emperor, and from there, being absorbed by his empire might be but a short step. The opinion of most of his collaborators in the Vatican reflected this, and the warning had sunk in with the Holy Father through meetings, dinners, whispers, and messages.

“你竟然将四位改革者的处决与我为了捍卫基督信仰而不得不奋斗、并且仍在奋斗的事情相提并论，这让我感到愤慨！”查尔斯宣称。

—You offend me by comparing the execution of four reformers with what I have had to struggle with, and still struggle with, to safeguard the faith of Christ! —Charles declared.

教皇无言以对，只好提出质问。

Having no argument with which to reply, the Pope chose to demand.

为了基督教世界的利益，你必须停止斗争。

—You must desist from your struggle, for the good of Christendom.

——我曾率先出手吗？如今是谁与萨伏伊为敌？又是谁在威胁米兰？

—Has my hand ever struck the first blow? Who has acted against Savoy now? Who threatens Milan again?

教宗早已知晓方济各的最新攻势。即便身处困境，方济各仍再次挑战皇帝，当时皇帝正在突尼斯作战。这位法国人的固执似乎无穷无尽，很难不承认他是个煽动者。但还有什么解决办法呢？或许是进攻法国？在宗教改革和英国自治的双重压力下，基督教世界已岌岌可危，此时再火上浇油，岂不更可一击？

The Holy Father was aware of Francis's latest attacks, who, even in his ruined state, had once again challenged the emperor while the latter was fighting in Tunis. The Frenchman's stubbornness seemed boundless, and it was difficult not to agree that he was quite the agitator. But what solution remained? To attack France, perhaps? To inflame Christendom when it could barely stand given the Reformation and English autonomy?

你们亵渎了这座圣城，但你们已被宽恕。我要求你们二人保持和平！接受你们无法改变我意志的事实吧。

—You violated this holy city, and you have been forgiven. I demand peace from both of you! Accept that you can do nothing to change my will.

尽管查理深知事实，但他的愤慨却让他无法轻易屈服。他连续数日无所作为，在罗马虔诚地度过了圣周，为穷人洗脚，并在最精美的宗教圣像前祈祷。然而，在教皇和枢机主教团齐聚一堂为他送行的那天，皇帝却走上讲台，指责这位法国国王与土耳其人交好，并宣称自己是他信仰中唯一无可指望的纯洁捍卫者，这番话令在场众人不寒而栗。他发表了一番充满真情实感的哀叹，其中饱含着数十年来积攒的失望与愤怒：无论他如何努力和平治理，弗朗西斯都从未允许过。这位法国人鄙视基督教的艰辛；他的一生似乎都只专注于抬高自己的荣耀，贬低查理的名声。这种固执不仅让他感到疲惫，而且还使交战的王国变得贫穷，并使他们偏离了他们应该做的唯一努力：征服苏莱曼的人民。

And although Charles knew this to be true, his indignation wouldn't allow him to simply comply. He did nothing for days, and spent a devout Holy Week in Rome, washing the feet of needy men and praying before the most beautiful religious images. But on the day the Pope and the College of Cardinals gathered to bid him farewell, the emperor took the floor and chilled the blood of those present by accusing the French king of his friendship with the Turk, and proclaiming himself the only unblemished defender his faith, unfortunately, could count on. He delivered a lament filled with sincerity and fueled by the rage accumulated over decades of disillusionment: however much he had tried to govern peacefully, Francis had never allowed it. The Frenchman despised the hardships of Christianity; his entire existence could be summed up as a preoccupation with inflating his own glory and diminishing that of Charles. This stubbornness not only seemed exhausting to him, but it had impoverished the contending kingdoms and diverted them from what should have been their sole endeavor: to subdue Suleiman's people.

凯撒的直言不讳令在场众人震惊，当他直接向教皇喊话，指责教皇对殉道者和罪人、和平主义者和狂热分子一视同仁时，全场鸦雀无声。和谐不能以不公正为代价，而且无论如何，应该向法国人提出这样的要求。查理知道，他的话语或许在大厅里难以引起共鸣，即使只是短暂地给听众带来一丝不适，但他的耐心已经耗尽。至少后人会知道弗朗西斯让他承受了多少痛苦，以及他多年来徒劳地与教皇抗争。

The attendees, stunned by the Caesar's bluntness, fell silent when he addressed the Pope directly, accusing him of being equally accommodating to the martyr and the sinner, the peaceful man and the fanatic. Concord could not be paid for with injustice, and in any case, it was the Frenchman from whom it should be demanded. Charles knew that his words might barely resonate in that hall and produce an uncomfortable effect, even if only for a brief moment, on those who heard them. But his patience had run out. At least posterity would know how much Francis had made him suffer, and how futilely he had forced him to fight for years.

最后，我要再说一遍三遍：我想要和平，我想要和平，我想要和平！

—And with this I end by saying once and three times: I want peace, I want peace, I want peace!

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在西班牙宫廷，伊莎贝拉正忙于从女儿胡安娜的出生中恢复过来。令她欣喜的是，她生下了一个健康活泼的孩子，但这带来的身体疲惫迫使这位皇后不得不休息。她卧病在床，却仍努力履行摄政的职责。这些职责也成了医生们让她独处的借口，因为自从她生产以来，医生们就对她过度关注，而且态度严肃而居高临下。伊莎贝拉心想，她疲惫的唯一原因就是她已经三十三岁了，她已经生过好几个孩子，巴巴罗萨再次入侵西班牙海岸，蹂躏了马翁，以及她对查理的愤怒正在消耗她曾经的精力。甚至在突尼斯挑拨离间之前，丈夫的离去就让她难以忍受，但这位葡萄牙皇后仍然抱有与他重聚的希望。如今，在皇帝撒谎之后，再次见到他似乎成了一种痛苦的经历。她依然爱着他，但她觉得自己这样做很愚蠢。

Meanwhile, at the Spanish court, Isabella was preoccupied with recovering from the birth of Joanna. To her joy, she had brought a healthy and cheerful child into the world, but the physical exhaustion this entailed forced the empress to rest. From her sickbed, she tried to attend to her responsibilities as regent. These duties provided a convenient excuse for the physicians to leave her alone, as they had been paying her excessive attention since the delivery and adopting a serious and condescending tone. The only reason for her weariness, Isabella thought, was that she was now thirty-three years old, that she had given birth several times, that Barbarossa had once again invaded the Spanish coast and ravaged Mahón, and that her anger with Charles was sapping her former energy. Even before Tunis had pitted them against each other, her husband's absences had been difficult to bear, but the Portuguese empress was able to keep alive the hope of their reunion. Now, after the emperor's lie, seeing him again seemed like a painful experience. She still loved him, but she judged herself foolish for it.

 

 

 

 

一天早晨，塔韦拉枢机主教比往常晚些抵达皇后寝宫。皇后责备了他，因为当天待处理的文书需要尽快处理。这位神职人员没有回应皇后的责备，只是凝视着皇后，仿佛他们是初次见面。

One morning, Cardinal Tavera arrived at the Empress's bedchamber somewhat later than usual. She reprimanded him, as the pending dispatches for that day required prompt attention. The clergyman did not respond to her complaint, but merely looked at his lady as if they were meeting for the first time.

我已经和物理学家们谈过了。陛下，您务必避免再次怀孕。

—I've spoken with the physicists. You must avoid becoming pregnant again, Your Majesty.

这位葡萄牙女子将目光从铺在床上的文件上移开。

The Portuguese woman looked away from the papers covering her bed.

他们对我的保护过度了。我会听取他们的建议，但不会奉为圭臬。

—They're being overly protective of me. I heed their advice, but not as dogma.

—如果你不放弃，你将面临太多死于分娩的风险！

—If you don't give up, you'll run too many risks of dying in childbirth!

那声咆哮吓得伊莎贝尔一哆嗦。红衣主教为自己的失态感到羞愧，但并不为造成的后果感到羞愧：那女人突然变得像他希望的那样惊慌失措。

The roar made Isabel flinch. The cardinal was ashamed of his outburst, but not of the effect it had caused: the woman was suddenly as disturbed as he had wanted her to be.

—你的身体太疲惫了，无法完成这项工作。

—Your body is too exhausted for that work.

两人都保持沉默。他们知道，禁止怀孕意味着要与皇帝分居。红衣主教也清楚他所侍奉之人之间的爱恋。他被迫拆散他们，这令他痛苦不堪。

Both remained silent. They knew that the prohibition against pregnancy meant living separately from the emperor. The cardinal was aware of the love between those he served. It pained him that he had been given the task of separating them.

“您希望我回去后与皇帝陛下交谈吗？”牧师温和地问道。

—Do you wish me to speak with the emperor when I return? —the clergyman asked gently.

皇后沉思片刻，然后摇了摇头。几个星期以来，她一直试图对查尔斯心存厌恶；如今医生们强迫她如此冷漠，她却后悔自己没有全心全意地爱他的每一分钟。她愿意付出一切，只求能再和他共度一个夜晚。

The Empress pondered it for a few moments. Then she shook her head. For weeks she had tried to harbor disdain for Charles; now that the doctors were forcing this coldness upon her, she regretted every minute she hadn't spent loving him unreservedly. She would have given anything for one more night by his side.

 

 

 

 

于是，她努力做好接替御医的准备。真​​正令她忧虑的是，她无法通过再生一个儿子来确保王位继承。所幸，菲利普虽然身体时好时坏，但总体上健康成长。然而，那项关于她健康状况的诊断真正让她感到痛苦的是，她再也无法与丈夫同房。从此以后，他们只能像一对老夫老妻那样相处：激情让位于友谊，亲密仅限于睡前在床上轻吻和牵手。有些人赞扬这种关系，认为它比基于欲望的关系更显高贵——精神之爱战胜了本能。然而，皇后预见到了阴影：丈夫的不忠，以及她自身的挫败感。

So she tried to prepare herself to assume the order of the physicians. What truly worried her was not being able to secure the succession by bringing another son into the world. Fortunately, Philip, even with his fluctuating strength, was growing up healthy. The real curse of that pronouncement on her health was that she would never again be able to lie with her husband. From then on, they would have to behave like an elderly couple: passion would have to give way to friendship, to contact limited to chaste kisses and holding hands in bed before falling asleep. There were those who praised this kind of bond, which they considered more dignified than one based on desire—spiritual love as a victory over instincts. However, the empress foresaw shadows: those of the infidelities of an unsatisfied husband, and those of her own frustration.

伊莎贝尔内心深处，理应之事与渴望之事交织成一团，最终吞噬了她的灵魂。未来对她而言失去了光彩。她只满足于与儿子相伴。菲利普和他的母亲彼此深爱，这份情谊牢不可破，仿佛曾经将他们紧紧相连的血脉从未断裂。皇帝的离去反而加深了这份情谊：在那些日子里，他们常常成为彼此唯一的慰藉。这份情谊自幼年斐迪南去世后便已铸就。伊莎贝尔无法让斐迪南复活，但她可以守护留下的儿子，免受厄运。许多人说，她对儿子过度保护。继承人的健康成了她执念，只要菲利普稍有病态，哪怕是轻微的，皇后都会下令悉心照料，如同他即将离世一般。这个男孩性格与他父亲相似——外表冷漠，实则内心敏感，将自己与世间的苦难隔绝开来——最终承担了母亲的忧虑，变得有些疑病症，并且，受伊莎贝尔的影响，也成了一个早熟的虔诚者。归根结底，这个继承人不过是他父亲的翻版：无论是性格，还是即将承担的责任，亦或是他对伊莎贝尔那份超乎常人的爱。
