The conflict between what she should do and what she desired crystallized within Isabel, extinguishing her spirit. The future had lost its luster for her. She was content only with the company of her son. Philip and his mother venerated each other deeply and irrevocably, as if the knot of flesh that had once bound them had never been severed. The emperor's absences had strengthened this bond: during those periods, they often became each other's sole source of daily joy. This bond had been forged since the death of young Ferdinand. Isabel could not bring that son back, but she could shield the one she had left from misfortune. She overprotected him, many said. The heir's health had become an obsession for her, and as soon as Philip showed any sign of ailment, however minor, the empress ordered that he be cared for as if the ailment were about to become fatal. The boy, who possessed a character similar to his father's—that is, he appeared cold, but in reality, he was a sensitive soul who shielded himself from the world's hardships—ended up taking on his mother's worries and became a little hypochondriac, and also, by imitation of Isabel, a precocious devotee. Deep down, the heir was nothing more than a carbon copy of his father: in his character, in the responsibility he was about to assume, and in the superhuman love he felt for Isabel.

 

 

 

 

—我亲爱的！

—My beloved!

皇帝渴望拥抱妻子。在全体朝臣的见证下，经过正式的觐见之后，他终于有机会与她独处。然而，葡萄牙王后的表情却让他止步不前：她那浓烈的不满仿佛在她周围形成了一个不可逾越的屏障。

The emperor sought his wife's embrace. After the formal reception in the presence of the entire court, he had finally managed to be alone with her. But the Portuguese queen's expression stopped him: her displeasure was so profound that it created an inviolable circle around her.

她厉声问道：“你还指望听到甜言蜜语吗？”

"Did you expect sweet words of welcome?" she snapped.

他惊呆了。

He was stunned.

我经历过战争，当然希望得到你的温暖！

—I survived a war. Of course I expected warmth from you!

你欺骗了我。你抛弃了你的家人，就像抛弃了这些王国一样。

—You deceived me. And you abandoned your family as much as these kingdoms.

卡洛斯原本以为时间和思念会赢得妻子的原谅。他每天早晚都想念她，可现在她却对他充满敌意，连教皇保罗的态度都显得友善。凯撒勃然大怒。

Carlos had trusted that time and longing would have won him his wife's forgiveness. He had missed her every morning and every evening, and now she was showing him a hostility that made Pope Paul's attitude seem friendly. The Caesar was furious.

我只是尽职尽责地做了我该做的事！如果机会再次来临，我也会毫不犹豫地采取同样的做法。

—I did nothing but what duty demanded! And I would not hesitate to act in the same way if the opportunity arose.

伊莎贝尔走向门口，留下他哑口无言。

Isabel headed towards the door, leaving him speechless.

我不认识你。

—I don't recognize you.

皇帝说完这些话时，他的妻子即将消失在他的视线中。她多么想转身坦白，并非怨恨，而是对继续爱着他或死亡的恐惧让她不知所措。然而，这些话却哽在喉咙里，像绝望的鸟儿，无法展翅飞翔，只能焦躁地扑腾着，在她体内撕扯着她。

The emperor uttered those words as his wife was about to disappear from his sight. She longed to turn and confess that it wasn't resentment, but the fear of continuing to love him or of dying that had overwhelmed her. However, the words wouldn't reach her tongue; they remained trapped in her chest, like desperate birds that couldn't bring themselves to take flight but fluttered nervously, tearing at her from within.

 

 

 

 

经过数日的紧张和沉默，卡洛斯卸下了虚荣心，出现在伊莎贝尔面前。

After several days of tension and silence, Carlos appeared before Isabel stripped of vanity.

“我一开始的做法是错误的，”他承认道。“我并不否认我对职责的尽责，但我绝不应该用谎言来羞辱你。如果我说我一直为此感到无比懊悔，你或许不会相信。”

“I was wrong in the way I started,” he admitted. “I don’t deny my commitment to my duties, but I should never have disrespected you with a lie. You might not believe me if I say that I’ve despised myself for it all this time.”

皇后相信他，所以她爱他。

The empress believed him; that's why she loved him.

——我好想你，我的女士……

—I have missed you so much, my lady…

皇帝走向他的妻子，双臂环抱住她，嘴唇贴上她的脖颈。皇后感受到渴望之人温暖的呼吸，一股电流瞬间窜过。他将手移到她的腰间，紧紧握住。伊莎贝拉看似漠然，几乎一动不动，但她已完全臣服，双目紧闭，思绪飘向远方，沉浸在一个激情得以实现的梦境中。然后，她抽回了那只曾如此充满力量地握着她的手。皇帝感到一阵刺痛。

The emperor approached his wife, encircled her with his arms, and placed his mouth against her neck. The empress felt a jolt of electricity as she felt the warm breath of the man she desired. He moved his hand to her waist and gripped it tightly. Isabella seemed indifferent, barely moving, but she was completely surrendered, her eyes closed and her imagination elsewhere, in a world where this passion could be fulfilled. Then she took his hand, the one that held her with such virility, and pulled it away. The emperor felt offended.

“你拒绝我吗？”凯撒的声音里带着恼怒，但也夹杂着深深的悲伤。

—Do you reject me? —In Caesar's voice there was annoyance, but also a deep sadness.

看着丈夫无助的眼神，伊莎贝尔心想，他试图逃避死亡，却让自己过着自己不想过的生活。

Looking into her husband's eyes, which showed him as helpless, Isabel thought that by trying to avoid death he was giving himself an existence he did not wish to live.

 

 

 

 

根特公爵唯一能应对伊莎贝拉冷漠态度的办法就是专注于国事。然而，他的不安始终挥之不去，导致他行事冷酷无情。

The only way the Duke of Ghent found to cope with Isabella's coldness was to focus on matters of state. His unease, however, persisted, causing him to behave ruthlessly.

—如果弗朗西斯想要战争，那就让他开战吧。

—If Francis wants war, he will have it.

——陛下——阿尔巴公爵说道，他并非回避暴力手段，而是回避不合逻辑的手段——，没有资源了。

—Your Majesty —said the Duke of Alba, who was not exactly a man who shied away from violent solutions, but rather from illogical ones—, there are no resources.

——钱，永远都是钱！难道金属乐比我更重要吗？

—Money, always money! Does metal rule more than I do?

—你们足够明智，可以自己找到答案。

—You are sensible enough to answer yourselves.

卡洛斯厌恶地转身离​​去。这位贵族是所有顾问中最聪颖的，问题在于他对此心知肚明。他对皇帝的忠诚如同他的祖父法德里克一样坚定不移；皇帝毫不怀疑这位公爵会为他献出生命。但他却无法对公爵提出丝毫批评。

Carlos turned his back on him in disgust. The aristocrat possessed the most brilliant mind among his advisors; the problem was that he was fully aware of it. His loyalty was as unwavering as that of his grandfather Fadrique; the emperor had no doubt that the duke would give his life for him. But he was incapable of withholding a single criticism.

“你们的王国需要和平，”来自阿尔巴的那位坚持道。

"Your kingdoms need peace," insisted the one from Alba.

“还有我的灵魂！我绝不会把它交给你。”皇帝凝视着眼前的欧洲地图，像雄鹰盘旋在乡间寻找猎物一般扫视着，直到他把目光落在自己感兴趣的那块区域上。“让我们入侵普罗旺斯。”

"And my soul! And I will not grant it to you." The emperor gazed at the map of Europe before him and scanned it like an eagle circling the countryside in search of prey, until he settled down to hover over the one that interested him. "Let us invade Provence."

另一个人过了一会儿，点了点头。他的建议被忽视后，他便服从命令，并像命令是自己下达的一样维护它们。然而，他注意到，尽管已经做出了决定，他的主人仍然焦躁不安。事实上，卡洛斯对自己判断的信心不足。失去了妻子的爱——这曾是他唯一确定的事——他开始漫无目的地游荡。

The other, after a few moments, nodded. When his advice was ignored, he obeyed orders and defended them as if they had come from him. He noticed, however, that his master, despite the decision made, remained agitated. The truth was that Carlos distrusted his own judgment. Having lost the love of his wife, which had always seemed to him his only certainty, he wandered aimlessly.

 

 

 

 

一天早晨，菲利普正在上拉丁语课，突然感到一阵眩晕。他的家庭教师十分担心，立即请来医生，但医生检查后并未发现任何异常。然而，两天后，同样的情况再次发生，这一次，这位继承人躺在床上，精疲力竭，浑身湿透，语无伦次地念叨着什么：他发烧了。

One morning, while taking Latin lessons, Philip felt dizzy. His tutor, alarmed, summoned a physician, who found nothing unusual about the boy. However, the scene was repeated two days later, and this time it ended with the heir in bed, exhausted, drenched in sweat, and uttering a rambling speech: he was suffering from a fever.

起初，宫廷内一片平静，因为人人都知道皇后忧心忡忡，他们通常会安抚皇后对继承人健康的担忧。但随着时间流逝，乐观情绪逐渐消散：据医生诊断，王子病情危重。

At first, the court remained calm, as everyone was aware of the empress's alarmism and they usually acted as a counterweight to her fears about the heir's health. But as the hours passed, the optimism turned unwise: according to the physicians, the prince was gravely ill.

 

 

 

 

卡洛斯走进小男孩的房间时，伊莎贝尔已经在那里了。她颤抖着，握着儿子的一只手，低声祈祷，几乎没有喘息。她的脸颊上已经干涸了。

When Carlos entered the little boy's room, Isabel was already there. The woman, trembling, held one of her son's hands in hers and murmured a prayer, barely pausing to catch her breath. Tears had dried on her cheeks.

皇帝在离她不远的一张扶手椅上坐下，望着熟睡的王子。他像一根放在床中央的蜡烛：面色发黄，毫无生气，仿佛被高烧灼烧。查理心想，帝国的未来竟寄托在这脆弱的肩膀上。

The emperor sat down in an armchair a little way from hers and looked at the prince, who was asleep. He resembled a candle placed in the middle of the bed: yellowish, inert, burning with fever. On what fragile shoulders rested the future of the Empire, Charles thought.

很长一段时间，尽管两人都待在寝宫里，却从未说过话。他们之间只有偶尔的、怯懦的眼神交流，除此之外别无其他。直到仆人送来夜宵，皇帝才发现妻子一口也不肯吃。

For a long time, even though neither of them left the bedchamber, the couple didn't speak to each other. There were fleeting, timid glances, and nothing more. Until some servants brought them food for the night, and the emperor saw that his wife refused to eat a thing.

—求求你们，先养活自己吧。

—Feed yourselves, I beg you.

——他有什么胃口？

—With what appetite?

查尔斯拿着一块甜点走近她，递给她。伊莎贝拉看了他一眼，却毫无反应。他握住她的手，将甜点放在她手上，但她纤细的手却抓不住。甜点掉落在地，皇后顿时泪如雨下。皇帝拥抱了她，起初有些怯懦，随后便用力地拥抱起来。

Charles approached her with a sweet and offered it to her. Isabella looked at him, but did not react. He then took her hands and placed the food on them, but they, being fragile, could not grasp it. The sweet fell to the ground, and the Empress burst into tears. The Emperor embraced her, first timidly, and then with vigor.

 

 

 

 

菲利普在黎明的第一缕曙光中醒来。他睁开眼第一眼看到的是他的母亲，她正依偎在皇帝的肩头睡着。

Philip awoke with the first light of dawn. The first thing he saw when he opened his eyes was his mother, who had fallen asleep on the emperor's shoulder.

“儿子！”凯撒惊呼道。

"Son," exclaimed Caesar.

伊莎贝尔立刻醒了过来。孩子的双眼重新焕发出健康的光彩；那双眼睛虽疲惫不堪，却顽强地与生命搏斗着。如果她还有眼泪，她一定会喜极而泣。然而，尽管感到如释重负，皇后却无法摆脱一个念头，这个念头在她看到菲利普病倒的那一刻就已浮现：作为妻子，她的职责莫过于为查理诞下继承人。维系着他们之间的情感，却无法让她忽视自己身处宫廷，甚至出现在皇帝生命中的真正原因。帝国凌驾于他们之上，她的使命是确保帝国的延续，确保她的时代不会削弱这延续了几个世纪的理想。如果菲利普死了，她的使命就无法实现。身为皇后，她享有诸多特权；她怎能辜负自己最重要的职责呢？

Isabel awoke instantly. The child's eyes had regained their healthy sparkle; they were those of someone exhausted but tenaciously clinging to life. His mother would have wept with joy had she had any tears left. However, despite the relief, the Empress couldn't shake a thought that had arisen the moment she saw Philip ill: her duty as wife was none other than to provide Charles with an heir. The feelings that bound them could not make her ignore the true reason for her presence at that court, and even in the life of the Emperor. The Empire was above them both, and her mission was to ensure its perpetuation, to ensure that her era did not diminish that ideal that had lasted for centuries. If Philip had died, her purpose would have failed. Many were the privileges of being Empress; how could she fail to fulfill the most important of her duties?

那天晚上，卡洛斯与她做爱后，伊莎贝尔辗转难眠，感谢上帝，他的牺牲如此甜蜜。

That night, after Carlos made love to her, Isabel, who couldn't sleep, thanked God that his sacrifice was so sweet.

 

 

大土耳其人蹂躏了意大利海岸。他不过是趁着基督教世界深陷内战泥潭、背弃真正敌人之际，肆意妄为。罗马感到威胁，而罪魁祸首正是你，天主教国王，最虔诚的基督徒。上帝和后世都不会原谅你的自私。我命令你缔结和平，愿你们用来互相残杀的精力和兵力，如果还有时间，能拯救我们脱离异教徒的魔爪。

The Grand Turk has ravaged the coasts of Italy. He has merely exploited the vulnerability of Christendom, embroiled in fratricidal wars and thus turning its back on its true enemy. Rome feels threatened, and the guilty ones are none other than you, the Catholic King and the Most Christian. Neither God nor posterity will forgive your selfishness. I command you to make peace, and may the energies and men you dedicate to killing one another save us, if there is still time, from the infidel.

 

 

保罗三世

PAUL III​

 

 

读完教宗的信后，皇帝承认这封信达到了预期的效果：他感到愧疚。尽管他的本能驱使他延长与法国的战争，但奥斯曼帝国对意大利海岸的猛烈进攻却造成了惨重的后果，不仅对基督教世界，也对他在该地区的领土造成了灾难性的打击。上帝似乎惩罚了他和方济各的短视。

After reading the Holy Father's letter, the emperor acknowledged that it had produced the desired effect: he felt guilty. Although his instincts urged him to prolong the fight against France, the Ottoman onslaught against the Italian coast was dramatic, with dire consequences for Christendom and for his own territories in the region. God seemed to have punished the shortsightedness of both himself and Francis.

皇帝环视每一位顾问，征求他们的意见。不出所料，阿尔巴公爵毫不犹豫地回答道：

The emperor looked at each of his advisors and asked for their opinion. As he expected, the Duke of Alba did not hesitate to reply:

——在罗马，你们三次高声呼吁和平。如果你们不回应教皇的呼吁，你们的逻辑何在？

—In Rome you raised your voices three times asking for peace. What logic would you demonstrate if you did not respond to the Pope's call?

卡洛斯随后征求了塔韦拉枢机的意见。

Carlos then sought the opinion of Cardinal Tavera.

我们未能拿下普罗旺斯。即使没有任何理由，停战也是明智之举。

—We failed to win Provence. A truce would be advisable even if there were no excuse for it.

——我理解你的理由，我也认同这些理由，但是……——凯撒觉得他以前也遇到过这种情况；同样的问题，同样的困境——，为什么总是我妥协呢？

—I understand your reasons, and I share them, but… —The Caesar thought he had experienced this situation before; the same problems, the same dilemma—, why must I always be the one who gives in?

—因为，我的大人，弗朗西斯所缺乏的智慧，上帝赐予了您。

—Because, my lord, the wisdom that Francis lacks, God granted to you.

 

 

 

 

在高卢宫廷，教皇的呼吁也引起了同样的共鸣。顾问们如同希腊合唱队一般，试图传达王国的心声，而这心声只有一个：够了！对弗朗西斯和查理来说，他们之间的敌对关系已然成为一种令人沉迷的不幸。两人都将部分精力投入到彼此较量、积攒怨恨、寻找理由来延续彼此的仇恨之中。一段时间以来，这种对怨恨的盘算早已失去了客观性。事实上，弗朗西斯始终未能释怀未能当选皇帝的失望，此后他便像港口里的凶猛猎手一样，孜孜不倦地寻衅滋事。而查理虽然自知是高卢侵略的受害者，却也未能学会将谈判置于战争之上。而战争的旷日持久，恰恰是它迟迟无法结束的原因：他们都不愿让之前为取得胜利所做的一切努力付诸东流。

In the Gallic court, the Pope's plea resonated similarly. The advisors, like a Greek chorus, tried to express the voice of the kingdom, which said nothing but: enough! For Francis, as for Charles, the rivalry between them had become an addictive misfortune. Both devoted a part of their spirit to measuring themselves against each other, to accumulating grievances, to finding reasons to perpetuate their resentment. For some time now, this tallying of grievances had been far from objective. In truth, Francis had never gotten over the disappointment of not being chosen emperor, after which he had relentlessly sought out a fight, like a cutthroat in a harbor. For his part, Charles, although he knew himself to be a victim of the Gaul's aggression, had also not learned to prioritize negotiation over battle. And the fact that the war between them had dragged on was precisely what prevented it from ending: neither wanted all their previous efforts to emerge victorious to have been in vain.

 

 

 

 

但人的虚荣心有时会被不幸所动摇，他们两人的情况正是如此。经历了伊莎贝拉和菲利普的遭遇后，皇帝的内心变得更加虔诚。与法国人的斗争在他心中已不再是首要之事，他心想，既然上帝救了他的儿子，他又有什么资格让他继承战乱的遗产呢？

But men's vanity is sometimes shaken by misfortune, and that happened in both their cases. The emperor's spirit was walking a pious path after what he had experienced with Isabella and Philip. Maintaining the struggle with the Frenchman had fallen in his order of priorities, and he reasoned that, since God had saved his son, who was he to condemn him to inherit a legacy of conflict?

对弗朗西斯而言，是疾病耗尽了他的精力。在他受苦期间，他的妻子埃莉诺寸步不离地守候在他身边。她像一位挚爱的女人般虔诚地守候在他的床边，但这与事实相去甚远。查理的妹妹决定用她那充满爱意的本领来赢得这位法国人的心，从而摆脱她在宫廷和床上的孤立。她再也无法忍受被忽视。弗朗西斯的疾病给了她一个机会，让她可以全身心地投入到他身上——因为在此之前，这位君主一直行踪飘忽，是个在婚外情面前毫无悔意的浪荡子。国王在病痛中被埃莉诺的无私所感动，放弃了自他们结婚以来几乎一直折磨她的轻蔑。在那段康复的日子里，他们都仿佛回到了马德里，那个他们相遇的地方，也是莱昂诺像现在一样照顾他的地方。曾经将他们紧紧联系在一起的纽带再次被点燃。当他虚弱不堪时，他们的关系似乎才有了意义，而她，正是那个给予他力量的人。

In Francis's case, it was illness that sapped his vigor. While he suffered, his wife, Eleanor, never left his side. She kept watch at his bedside with the devotion of a beloved woman, which was far from the truth. Charles's sister had decided to use her capacity for love to win over the Frenchman and thus escape her ostracism at court, and in bed. She could no longer bear being ignored. Francis's illness gave her the opportunity to surrender herself to him—for until then, in full health, the monarch had been elusive, a fleeting man without remorse when it came to adultery. The king, amidst his suffering, was moved by Eleanor's selflessness and abandoned the disdain with which he had tormented her practically since their marriage. During those days of convalescence, they both felt, in a way, back in Madrid, the place where they had met and where Leonor had acted, as she did now, as his caregiver. The bond that had united them then was rekindled. Their relationship seemed to gain meaning when he was a weakened man and she, the one who gave him strength.

他们之间建立起的亲密关系，给意大利的局势带来了不同的感觉。

The closeness that had developed between them gave a different feel to the situation in Italy.

“我已经接受了与你哥哥的休战协议。”有一天，当病情有所好转时，弗朗西斯告诉他。

—I have accepted a truce with your brother —Francis told him one day, when the illness was subsiding.

自从罗马的信寄到后，埃莉诺就一直在想方设法说服丈夫接受教宗的请求。不仅她希望如此，臣民、顾问，甚至亨利王子也都希望如此。哥哥去世后，亨利王子已是王位继承人，他当时已十九岁，很快就意识到自己将面临的未来。他对皇帝的怨恨从未消减——一天也没有，尤其是在长子去世之后，他儿子短暂的一生中有一部分被浪费在了佩德拉萨城堡的牢房里——但他更害怕的是继承一个破产的王国，一个对王室和他的家族都充满不满的王国。他有时间偿还皇帝欠他的债。就目前而言，最明智的做法似乎是结束战争。

Ever since the letter arrived from Rome, Eleanor had sought ways to convince her husband to accept the Holy Father's plea. It wasn't just her who desired it, but also the subjects, the advisors, and even Prince Henry. The heir apparent after his brother's death was already nineteen, and he had quickly become aware of the future that awaited him. He didn't forget his resentment toward the emperor—not for a single day, and certainly not since the death of his firstborn son, part of whose short life had been wasted in that cell in Pedraza Castle—but he feared even more the prospect of inheriting a bankrupt kingdom from his father, a kingdom disaffected with the Crown and with his lineage. He would have time to repay the debt the emperor owed him. For now, the most sensible course seemed to be to end the war.

“既然可以实现持久和平，为何要休战？”莱昂诺尔反驳道，“如果能得到米兰，你难道不会接受吗？”

"Why a truce when you could have lasting peace?" Leonor retorted to her husband. "Wouldn't you accept it if you received Milan?"

“米兰？”弗朗西斯科笑了笑，但笑声渐渐平息，只因他已筋疲力尽。“你哥哥永远不会答应我的。”

"Milan?" Francisco laughed, and only stopped because he lacked the strength. "Your brother will never grant it to me."

你低估了我。你一直都低估我。

—You underestimate me. You always have.

国王对这番话反应很负面：他的笑容消失了。

The king reacted negatively to the comment: his smile vanished.

—你母亲和我姑姑当年设法制止了这场争斗。

—Your mother and my aunt managed to stop the fighting back in the day.

“我为此付出的代价是耻辱。我绝不会重蹈覆辙。”他说。

"The price I paid for it was dishonor. I refuse to repeat it," he said.

—如果你给我报酬，我就会帮你找到你想要的东西。

—I will get you what you are looking for if you reward me for it.

——以什么方式？

—In what way?

莱昂诺尔看着她的丈夫，心想，尽管经历了这一切，为什么她仍然渴望着他。

Leonor looked at her husband and wondered why, despite everything, she still desired him.

—带着孩子。

—With a child.

 

 

 

 

你确定你所说的话是正确的吗？

Are you sure about what you're saying?

—没错，陛下。

—That's right, Your Majesty.

伊莎贝尔脸色苍白，看着物理学家收拾东西。幸好，她设法镇定下来，说道：

Isabel, pale-faced, watched as the physicist gathered his belongings. Fortunately, she found a moment of composure to say:

——别把这件事告诉任何人。我命令你。

—Don't tell anyone about it. I order you.

医生点点头，默默地道别，神情悲伤；他明白自己刚才的诊断可能带来的后果。她独自一人时，用手捂住隆起的腹部，手心已经开始冒汗。

The doctor nodded and said his goodbyes in silence, looking sad; he knew the potential consequences of the diagnosis he had just given. Once alone, she covered her stomach with her hands, which were now sweating.

当皇后告诉塔韦拉枢机主教她再次怀孕时，他脸色骤然变得惨白。出于担忧，他急忙指责她愚蠢。伊莎贝尔听着他的责备，觉得这只是一连串毫无意义的指责，因为自从得知自己怀孕的那一刻起，她就一直在自责。最终，意识到一切都已无法挽回，这位神职人员停止了指责。

Cardinal Tavera's face drained of blood when the Empress told him she was pregnant again. Hastily, and driven by his concern, he accused her of being foolish. Isabel listened to his reproaches as a pointless litany of faults, for she had already blamed herself the moment she learned of her condition. Finally, realizing that nothing could be done to avert the danger, the clergyman ceased his recriminations.

“你必须告诉皇帝，”他最后说道。

"You must tell the emperor," he finished.

但伊莎贝拉不肯。查理必须立即动身前往法国，与他宿敌会面，后者同意坐下来谈判。他们怎能让他背负着妻子可能自取灭亡，而他自己也难辞其咎的重担离开呢？因此，第二天的告别仅限于美好的祝愿，葡萄牙王后多次叮嘱他“早日归来”，以及红衣主教沮丧的表情。他亲眼目睹了这场闹剧：皇帝扮演着一个无忧无虑的丈夫，但代价却是对真相的无知。

But Isabella did not. Charles had to leave immediately for France to meet with his eternal enemy, who had agreed to sit down and negotiate. How could they force him to depart with the burden of knowing that his wife might have condemned herself, and that he had contributed to it? Therefore, their farewell, which took place the following day, was limited to good wishes, many "come back soon" from the Portuguese queen, and the cardinal's frustrated expression. He had witnessed this charade in which the emperor played the role of a carefree husband, yes, but at the cost of remaining ignorant.

 

 

 

 

自埃莉诺和查理上次见面以来，已经过去了七年。这位法国王后要求在其他人之前单独觐见他；这是她凭空想出来的家族特权，弗朗西斯皇帝欣然应允。皇帝注意到她面色略显憔悴，但精神却很好；他并不知道，这种精神上的愉悦，源于她与法国君主之间关系的缓和，而且是近来才出现的，实属难得。他的妹妹宁愿将她在法国宫廷中直至最近才逐渐疏远的经历隐瞒起来。她不愿破坏和平谈判，也不愿重温她认为早已过去的空虚岁月。她相信未来会如何，无论对欧洲还是对她自己而言，而这一切只有在彻底放下过去、不再回头的情况下才能实现。

Seven years had passed since Eleanor and Charles had last met. The French queen requested a private audience with him before anyone else; a family privilege she had pulled out of thin air, which Francis granted. The emperor noticed she looked somewhat unwell but was cheerful; he was unaware that this cheerfulness, due to the rapprochement between her and the French sovereign, was recent and quite a novelty. His sister preferred to keep to herself the story of the isolation her time at the French court had become until very recently. She did not wish to jeopardize the peace negotiations, nor resurrect that period of emptiness she considered to be behind her. She trusted in what the future might hold, both for Europe and for herself, and that was only possible if the past was buried without looking back.

“我恳求你，在和我丈夫坐下来谈话时，请放下悲观和怨恨，”莱昂诺尔对她的哥哥说。“这次会面可能会带来前所未有的结果：一份永无止境的停战协议。”

—I beg you to put aside pessimism and resentment when you sit down to talk with my husband— Leonor told her brother. —From this meeting could come what has never happened before: an endless armistice.

皇帝既感到惊讶又心存怀疑。

The emperor was both surprised and skeptical.

——你很清楚我想要的也正是如此。但他们的要求必须和我的一样合理。

—You know very well that I want nothing different. But their demands must be as just as mine.

“把米兰赐给他吧，”她说。

"Grant him Milan," she said.

卡洛斯发出了一声讽刺的笑声，那是失望的笑声。

Carlos let out a sarcastic laugh, a laugh of disappointment.

——我以为我在跟我姐姐说话；我忘了您也是法国王后……

—I thought I was speaking to my sister; I forgot that you are also the Queen of France…

莱昂诺尔拦住了已经准备离开的凯撒。

Leonor stopped Caesar, who was already slipping away.

“以公国为交换，让他与你并肩作战，对抗异教徒。你难道要放弃履行你作为信仰捍卫者的首要职责的机会吗？如果米兰能确保十字军东征的成功，那么这个代价是合理的。”

"In exchange for the duchy, ask him to fight alongside you against the infidel. Will you scorn the opportunity to fulfill your primary duty as a defender of the faith? Milan is a just price if it guarantees the crusade."

起初，凯撒不愿与弗朗西斯并肩作战对抗苏莱曼；然而，当这个念头浮现在他脑海中时，任何其他可能性都显得更糟。问题依然如故：他能信任这个法国人吗？米兰公国是否足以让他放弃两人之间由来已久的敌对关系？

At first, the Caesar resisted the thought of fighting side-by-side with Francis against Suleiman; however, when that image surfaced in his mind, any other possibility seemed worse. The question was the same as always: could he trust the Frenchman? Would the Duchy of Milan be enough to make him abandon this perpetual rivalry between them?

 

 

 

 

当弗朗西斯热情地拥抱他时，查理一时不知该作何反应。环绕着他的，是那个曾多次攻击他的人的手臂；是那个在马德里信誓旦旦却又欺骗了他的人的手臂；而且，最重要的是，是那个毫不犹豫地与异教徒结盟的人的手臂。尽管如此，皇帝还是回以拥抱；这是礼仪的要求。

When Francis embraced him in welcome, Charles didn't know how to react. The endless arms that encircled him were those of the man who had attacked him time and again; those of the man who, after swearing otherwise, had deceived him in Madrid; and also, and above all, those of the man who had had no qualms about allying himself with the infidel. Despite all this, the emperor reciprocated the gesture; protocol demanded it.

然后，他们彼此凝视，仔细打量着对方。两人都比上次见面时显得苍白许多。尽管他们正值壮年，但上次的经历，对他们两人而言，都比上千人加起来还要激烈。

Then they gazed at each other, studying one another intently. Both resembled a paler version of themselves than in their last encounter. Although they were in the prime of life, it had been, in both cases, more intense than that of a thousand men combined.

“皇帝陛下，我们都老了。”弗朗西斯说道。

"We have grown old, Emperor," said Francis.

——那本应让我们变得更明智。

—That should have made us wiser.

他们开始散步，渐渐远离了同伴。蒙莫朗西和阿尔巴公爵仍留在原地，彼此心照不宣地对视了一眼，感觉自己有点像是主人固执己见的受害者。

They began a stroll that took them away from their companions. Montmorency and the Duke of Alba remained in their places, glancing at each other knowingly, feeling somewhat like victims of their masters' stubbornness.

“更明智？毫无疑问，”高卢人说道，“这就是我邀请你们的原因，也是你们来此的原因。”查理微微点头，应允了他的请求。“我愿和平。你们认为达成协议是否可能？”

"Wiser? Undoubtedly we are," the Gaul declared. "That is why I invited you, and why you are here." Charles granted his request with a slight nod. "My will is peace. Do you see an agreement as possible?"

你认为这有可能实现吗？

—Do you think it's possible to achieve it?

他们彼此露出嘲讽的笑容。他们之间流露出一段破裂婚姻的迹象，但又像是注定要永远生活在一起的婚姻。

They smiled at each other with a mocking grin. There was a hint of a ruined marriage about them, but one condemned to live together for all eternity.

 

 

 

 

如果弗朗西斯的意图要从他所展现的荣耀来判断，查理只能寄希望于此。宴会、舞会和宫廷游戏接踵而至。谁也想不到，就在几周前，这两个人还统领着互相残杀的军队。

If Francis's intentions were to be judged by the display of honors, Charles was obliged to hope. Feasts and banquets, dances and courtly games followed one after another. No one would have guessed that these two men, just a few weeks before, had commanded armies that were massacring each other.

这次峰会也为皇帝提供了一个与法国王位继承人亨利重逢的机会，亨利曾被他囚禁在卡斯蒂利亚。这个男孩已经长成了一个接近二十岁的年轻人。他有一双深邃而忧郁的眼睛，给查理留下了深刻的印象：或许童年被囚禁的记忆仍然深深地刻在他的眼中。这位年轻人将他介绍给了自己的妻子凯瑟琳·德·美第奇，但总体上却沉默寡言。皇帝这才确信，他并没有忘记自己孩提时代离开马德里时发出的威胁；不仅如此，他还一直坚持着这个威胁，甚至可能还在不断强化它。

The summit also served as an opportunity for the emperor to reunite with the heir to the French throne, Henry, whom he had once held captive in Castile. The boy had grown into a young man nearing twenty. He possessed enormous, sad eyes that impressed Charles: perhaps the memory of his childhood imprisonment had remained etched in his gaze. The young man introduced him to his wife, Catherine de' Medici, but was generally laconic. The emperor then became certain that he had not forgotten the threat he had made as a child upon leaving Madrid; and not only that, but he continued to maintain it and perhaps even nurture it.

随着时间推移，根特皇帝逐渐对他的对手渴望和平的愿望有了初步的了解，并开始相信这一点。弗朗西斯依然是个自负且桀骜不驯的人，尤其是在他感到被注视的时候——即便是在游戏或对话中，他也绝不肯让步。但当皇帝与他单独交谈时，那种因共同的荣耀和重担而产生的默契，让这位法国人显得比以往更加谦逊。查理将此归因于母亲和长子的离世。谁在经历如此悲剧之后不会变得更加沉稳冷静呢？他甚至开始怀疑自己是否能够从如此沉重的打击中恢复过来。

As the days passed, the emperor of Ghent formed an opinion about his rival's desire for peace, and began to believe in it. Francis remained, especially when he felt observed, a boastful and defiant man—incapable of yielding even in a game or a dialogue. But when the emperor and he conversed alone, with that complicity born of shared grandeur and burdens, the Frenchman seemed more humble than before. Charles attributed this to the loss of his mother and his firstborn son. Who wouldn't emerge more level-headed from such tragedy? He even began to doubt whether he would be able to recover from such a blow.

“让我们为我们的孩子订婚吧，”皇帝在临行前不久提议道，当时这桩婚事已经成为他们讨论的焦点。“我的小玛丽亚和你的亨利。嫁妆就选米兰吧。”

"Let's betroth our children," the emperor proposed shortly before his departure, when the agreement was already the focus of their discussions. "My little Maria and your Henry. And let the dowry be Milan."

——既不是为了我，也不是为了你？

—Neither for me nor for you?

——总有一天，它会传到你们的后裔手中。但代价是耐心……以及你们必须完全效忠于圣父，永远不再为异教徒效力。你们应该团结一致，共同对抗苏莱曼，这才是你们应有的立场。

—In time, it would pass to your lineage. But the price is patience… and that you place yourselves entirely at the service of the Holy Father, and never again at the service of the infidel. Together, against Suleiman, as it should always have been.

弗朗西斯认真考虑了一下。他本希望无需等待一代人的时间就能获得公爵之位，但如果代价是时间，他也愿意付出，因为这是他仅存的财产。最终，他接受了。

Francis considered it. He would have preferred to gain the duchy without having to wait a generation, but if the price was time, he would pay it, for it was the only possession he had left. Finally, he accepted.

 

 

 

 

不久之后，皇帝受到了隆重的送别。埃莉诺容光焕发地向他告别，这不仅是因为和平协议的达成（无疑她促成了这一协议），也因为前一天晚上，弗朗西斯多年来第一次到她的寝宫探望她。

Shortly afterward, the emperor was given a grand send-off. Eleanor looked radiant as she bid him farewell, due to the peace agreement that had been reached, which she had undoubtedly facilitated, but also because of the previous night, when Francis had visited her in her bedchamber for the first time in years.

在登上返回西班牙的马车之前，查理走向了法国王位继承人。亨利双目如两轮阴郁的月亮，与他握手，礼貌却略显拘谨。皇帝凝视着他。他很想知道，在那张面容宽阔、略带慵懒的脸庞下，究竟隐藏着什么，那脸庞宛如哥特式的基督。

Before boarding the carriage that would take him back to Spain, Charles approached the heir to the French throne. Henry, his eyes like two somber moons, shook his hand, cordial but excessively ceremonious. The emperor stared at him. He would have liked to know what lay hidden beneath that face with its large, languid features, like a Gothic Christ.

“你和我儿子可别像你们父母那样疯啊，”他恳求道。

"Don't you and my son be as crazy as your parents," he begged.

 

 

 

 

查理得知伊莎贝拉怀孕的消息时，欣喜若狂！皇后也与他同乐，因为在丈夫不在的这段时间里，她深信医生们的预言不过是臆测，根本无法预知未来，也无法做出任何决定。没有人——无论是医生、红衣主教，还是她自己——考虑到一个至关重要的因素：她的意志。当这桩婚事看似不可能时，她听从了那些劝她放弃皇帝的人的劝告吗？没有；那时她仿佛失去了理智，将自己封闭起来，不去理会所有人的悲观情绪，强迫自己相信。正是这种看似荒谬的固执，才让她最终嫁给了皇帝。伊莎贝拉告诉自己，她要用同样的勇气拯救自己，确保王位的继承。她要生个孩子，一个儿子，她要再次向世人证明，只有她的坚韧才能铸就她的命运。

How happy Charles was when he learned that Isabella was pregnant! The Empress shared his joy, for during her husband's absence she had become convinced that the physicians' predictions were just that: human assumptions that could foresee little and determine nothing. No one—not the doctors, not the cardinal, not even herself—had taken into account a fundamental element: her will. Did she heed those who urged her to renounce the Emperor when the marriage seemed impossible? No; back then she acted as if her senses didn't exist, she shut herself out of everyone's pessimism and forced herself to believe. Only that seemingly senseless stubbornness allowed her to marry the Emperor. Isabella told herself that she would use that same strength to save herself and to secure the kingdom's succession. She would have a child, a son, and she would once again demonstrate to everyone that only her tenacity forged her destiny.

 

 

 

 

事实上，皇帝返回后立即面临着组织一场新的抗击土耳其人的战役。这场战役将首次得到法国的支持，尽管两国都需要时间才能从战争中恢复过来，有足够的资金来支持它。他对这种合作带来的可能性感到兴奋不已；如果苏莱曼在突尼斯战败，如今敌军人数将是他的两倍，他无疑会放弃君士坦丁堡。自1454年君士坦丁堡沦陷于奥斯曼帝国以来，收复这座基督教要塞一直是他们的目标。无论如何，哈布斯堡王朝最终都无法让这位皇帝觉得自己配得上查理曼的王冠。

The truth was that upon his return, the emperor was immediately faced with organizing a new campaign against the Turks, which for the first time would have the support of France, although it would still take time for both countries to recover sufficiently from the wars to finance it. He was thrilled by the possibilities this collaboration opened up; if Suleiman had succumbed in Tunis, now that the troops against him would be twice as numerous, he would undoubtedly surrender Constantinople, whose recovery for the Christian faith had been an objective since its fall to the Ottomans in 1454. No achievement could make the Habsburg, at last, feel worthy bearer of Charlemagne's crown.

 

 

 

 

然而，当战略最终敲定后，这位法国人却退出了。土耳其人不会轻易放弃他们在欧洲的盟友，也不会允许他们进军旧大陆的企图被昔日对手的联盟所阻挡。分裂的西方符合他们的利益，如果弗朗西斯不认同这一观点，他们就会威胁他，迫使他改变立场。对于这位因病而更加珍惜生命、厌恶风险的法国君主来说，君士坦丁堡之战似乎成了一场不切实际的空想，不值得为此付出生命。如果基督教世界在没有这座堡垒的情况下也能延续近百年，那么它完全可以再延续一百年。

However, when the strategy was already finalized, the Frenchman backed out. The Turks were not about to so easily dispense with their European accomplice, nor would they allow their attempts to advance in the Old Continent to be repelled by the alliance of their former rivals. A divided West was in their interest, and if Francis did not share this view, they threatened him to persuade him. To the French monarch, whose illness had made him value his life more and disdain risks, the Constantinople campaign began to seem like a delusional feat for which it was not worth dying. If Christendom had survived for almost a hundred years without that stronghold, it could endure for another hundred.

 

 

 

 

谁也没料到，无法指望法国的帮助竟会促使查理一世孤身一人，毫不拖延地展开这项事业。这位皇帝生性固执，不到达成目标，或者至少到筋疲力竭，他绝不会轻易放弃。阿尔瓦公爵和塔韦拉红衣主教使尽浑身解数劝阻他，却始终无济于事。红衣主教的劝说尤为激烈：他不仅担心这场战役可能带来的经济灾难，更担心皇帝凯旋归来时会发现自己成了鳏夫。

What no one foresaw was that the disappointment of not being able to count on France would spur Charles to undertake the enterprise alone, and without delay. The emperor was a stubborn man, who rarely gave up on an endeavor until he achieved it, or at least until he was exhausted in the attempt. The Duke of Alba and Cardinal Tavera used countless arguments to try to dissuade him, but they couldn't find a way. The cardinal argued most vehemently: he cared about the potential economic disaster the campaign might entail, but even more so about the possibility that, upon his return, the emperor might find himself a widower.

卡洛斯见同事们全是反对意见，顿时精神振奋，离开了会议室，沿着走廊走去。他听到身后传来塔韦拉的声音。

Carlos, his spirits raised at encountering nothing but opposition from his colleagues, left the council meeting and headed down a corridor. Behind him, he heard Tavera's voice.

-威严。

-Majesty.

但凯撒不想再听到任何反对他计划的声音。

But Caesar did not wish to hear any more objections to his plans.

-我求求你！

—I beg you!

红衣主教抓住他的手臂来制止他；这一举动违反了所有礼仪，鉴于凯撒的愤怒，更是激怒了他。

The cardinal grabbed his arm to restrain him; a gesture that broke all protocols and, given the Caesar's anger, enraged him.

你竟敢这样？

—How dare you?

—有件事你应该知道。这件事与皇后有关。

—There is something you should know. It's about the Empress.

 

 

 

 

卡洛斯等到情绪平静下来才去看望妻子，这花了他几个小时。自从听到塔韦拉的启示后，那番话就一直在他脑海中挥之不去。这信息仿佛来自另一个世界：皇帝不知道该如何将它与自己的认知调和，在他看来，伊莎贝尔注定永生，如同食物和土地一样不可或缺。他请求红衣主教让他一个人待着。

Carlos waited until he had calmed down before going to see his wife, and the task took him hours. Tavera's revelation had echoed ceaselessly in his mind ever since he had heard it. The message seemed otherworldly: the emperor didn't know how to reconcile it with his own, where Isabel was destined to be eternal, as essential to him as food or the ground. He asked the cardinal to leave him alone.

起初有人说这不可能是真的。

At first it was said that it couldn't be true.

后来，她独自一人时，怒火中烧。她明明知道会面临什么风险，却还是傻乎乎地把自己交给了他！她恨自己，恨自己竟然愚蠢到自我毁灭。

Later, still alone, she grew angry. How foolish she had been to give herself to him when she already knew what she was risking! She hated herself for it, for having been foolish enough to condemn herself.

然后他试着想象没有她的生活。

Then he tried to imagine life without her.

伊莎贝尔的无数身影涌上心头，每一幅都如同无数座君士坦丁堡般珍贵。他想，自己还能珍藏关于妻子的回忆，让她的身影充满他的脑海：她指甲的形状，她的声音，她绿色眼眸中流露出的千言万语，她背上的那颗痣，以及她微笑时仿佛无限延伸的嘴唇。他能闻到她的气息，触摸到她柔软的耳廓，听到她责备前那轻柔的咕噜声。他能……

A thousand and one images of Isabel flooded his mind. Each one was as precious as so many Constantinoples. He thought then that he could still treasure memories of his wife, filling his mind with her: the shape of her nails, the sound of her voice, the thousand details expressed by her green eyes, that mole on her back, and the way her lips seemed to stretch endlessly when she smiled. He could smell her, touch the soft edges of her ears, and hear that purr that preceded her reproaches. He could…

于是他跑了起来，他穿过一条又一条走廊和房间，在他看来，这些走廊和房间似乎无穷无尽，因为他想尽快见到她，开始把她深深地印在自己的记忆里，这样就永远不会失去她。

And he ran, he ran through a succession of corridors and rooms, which seemed endless to him, because he wanted to get to her as soon as possible, and start accumulating her in his memory, and thus never lose her.

 

 

 

 

—你为什么不拒绝我？

—Why didn't you reject me?

伊莎贝尔垂下眼帘。在她内心深处，她感谢红衣主教的背叛，因为这场闹剧终于让她无法忍受。

Isabel lowered her gaze. Deep down, she thanked the cardinal for the betrayal, because the charade had finally become unbearable.

我当时吓坏了。

—I was overcome with fear.

——还有比危及生命更大的风险吗？

—Are there any greater risks than putting your life at risk?

皇后用她所能展现出的所有坦率目光打量着她的丈夫。

The empress looked at her husband with all the frankness she was capable of.

—我没能履行确保王国继承的职责……或者失去了你。

—Not having fulfilled my role of ensuring the succession of the kingdom… Or losing you.

卡洛斯则在一旁观察着她，却并不理解。他知道她话里的意思，但这似乎并不像是他们之间的典型情况，而更像是其他婚姻的写照，而这些婚姻都平庸无奇。

Carlos, in turn, observed her without understanding. He knew what she meant, but it didn't seem like something typical of them, but rather of other marriages, all of them mediocre.

没有什么能将我们分开。你很快就会明白的。

—Nothing could separate me from you. You'll soon find out.

葡萄牙女人相信了他的话。她的眼眶里噙满了泪水。

The Portuguese woman believed him. Her eyes welled up with tears.

“一切都会好起来的，”她说；在过去的几周里，她每天每时每刻都在对自己重复这句话，能够大声说出来让她感到宽慰，这样这句话就有了更多的力量。

"Everything will be alright," she said; in the last few weeks she had been repeating those words to herself every day, every hour, and it relieved her to be able to express them out loud, so that they would have more strength.

我绝不允许有其他办法。

—I will not allow it any other way.

他们拥抱在一起，怀着同样的爱和同样的恐惧。

They hugged, with the same love and the same fear.

 

 

 

 

那天晚上，凌晨时分，伊莎贝尔已经入睡，皇帝在房间里，对着一壶啤酒，目光空洞地盯着前方，房间里只有他的影子陪伴着他。

That night, in the early hours of the morning, while Isabel was already resting, the emperor lost his gaze in nothingness before a jug of beer, in a room where only his shadow accompanied him.

“他会死吗？”一个稚嫩的声音问道。

"Is he going to die?" said a voice that was still immature.

卡洛斯抬起头。费利佩站在门口，穿着睡衣，但脸上却一副根本没注意到他的表情。

Carlos looked up. On the threshold stood Felipe, dressed for bed but with the expression of someone who didn't even notice him.

“你知道吗？”他父亲惊讶地喊道。

"Did you know?" his father exclaimed in amazement.

—我听到了不该听到的话，我真希望是我的感官背叛了我。

—I heard what I shouldn't have, and I wanted to believe that my senses had betrayed me.

皇帝明白了。他鼓励查理坐在自己身边。菲利普走近时，查理意识到自己快要哭了。

The emperor understood. He encouraged him to sit beside him. As Philip approached, Charles realized he was about to cry.

—是我的错，对吗？

—It's my fault, isn't it?

你在说什么？

—What are you saying?

—如果我更强大，如果她不为我担心，她就不必冒着风险为你培养另一个继承人了。

—If I were stronger, if she weren't afraid for me, she wouldn't have had to risk it to give you another successor.

卡洛斯总是对他的儿子感到惊讶：他看起来很脆弱，但似乎被一个理智而沉默寡言的成年人所控制。

Carlos was always surprised by his son: he looked fragile, but he seemed possessed by a sensible and taciturn adult.

愿上帝带走我，而不是她，父亲。

—May God take me, and not her, Father.

“如果真有这种魔法，我向你们保证，它不会带走你们中的任何一个人。”

"If such magic existed, it wouldn't take any of you, I assure you."

费利佩极力忍住不哭。

Felipe was making a great effort not to cry.

“让我们相信他的力量吧，”凯撒鼓励他。

"Let's trust in his strength," the Caesar encouraged him.

——但是如果……呢？

—But what if…?

父子俩交换了一个无声的眼神。

Father and son exchanged a silent glance.

——一切交给上帝决定。我只求你，无论发生什么，都帮助我。你是我的继承人。

—Let God decide. I only ask that, whatever happens, you help me. You are my heir.

男孩听过“继承人”这个词无数次，但从未像此刻这般感同身受。他肩负的命运似乎一直都是一项艰巨的挑战，部分原因是许多人并不相信他已经准备好面对。但费利佩像他父亲一样，观察入微、内敛沉稳，他懂得如何洞察他人，即使对方不开口；而他从周围大多数人的言行中读出，作为如此显赫遗产的继承人，他更应该展现出截然不同的性格：更加精力充沛，或许更加睿智，当然，也绝不会像现在这样依恋母亲。但在那阴郁的时刻，在那间弥漫着啤酒味、炉火即将熄灭的房间里，男孩却觉得自己能够承担起这份责任，因为他怀疑，即便将来拥有无垠的疆域，他是否还会面临比眼前这更加可怕的境地。

The boy had heard the word "heir" many times, but it had never resonated with him as it did at that moment. The destiny that had been dealt to him had always seemed a daunting challenge, partly because many didn't believe he was ready to face it. But Felipe, observant and reserved like his father, knew how to read others without them having to speak openly; and what he had read in most of those around him was that it would have been better for the successor to such an illustrious legacy to display a very different character: more energetic, perhaps wiser, certainly less attached to his mother. But in those somber hours, in that room smelling of beer and where the fire was about to go out, the boy felt capable of assuming his duty, because he doubted that, even as the owner of infinite domains, he would ever have to face anything more terrible than what now lay before him.

—是的，父亲，我是您的继承人。

—Yes, father, I am your heir.

他们一起祈祷。

And together they prayed.

 

 

 

 

一天早晨，怀孕三个月的伊莎贝尔感到腹部一阵剧痛。紧接着又是一阵剧痛，剧烈得让她觉得这就是被剑刺中倒下的人所感受到的疼痛。她弯下腰，这时，她看到脚边是血。

One morning, when she was three months pregnant, Isabel felt a sharp pain in her belly. Then came another, so violent that she thought that's what those who fall from a sword wound must feel like. She bent over, and as she did, she saw blood at her feet.

 

 

 

 

医生和助产士再次蜂拥而至……血腥味扑面而来……皇后闭着双眼，轻声祈祷。疼痛尚可忍受，恐惧却难以承受。她感到一只手握住了她的手。她仅凭肌肤的触感便知晓那是他的手。她感到喜悦；那份存在对她而言，如同阳光穿透云层。她睁开了双眼。

Physicians and midwives swarmed again… The smell of blood… The Empress, with her eyes closed, prayed softly. The pain was bearable; the fear, less so. She felt a hand clasp hers. She knew it was his simply by the touch of his skin. She felt joy; that presence seemed to her like a ray of sunlight piercing a cloud. She opened her eyes.

“我失败了，”她说。

"I have failed," she said.

卡洛斯吻了吻她的手。他的妻子感觉到他的嘴唇在颤抖。物理学家们正在为实验做最后的准备。气氛紧张，没有人说话，既不想担心，也不想说谎。

Carlos kissed her hand. His wife felt his lips tremble. The physicists were finalizing the preparations for the procedure. The atmosphere was tense, and no one spoke, neither to worry nor to lie.

—我很害怕。

—I'm very scared.

他看到她像尊雕像一样僵住了，浑身冰冷，恐惧让他动弹不得。他愿意付出一切，只为让她免受这份痛苦。

He saw her frozen like a statue, cold with fear. He would have given anything to spare her that anguish.

“我没打算离开你，”他说道。

"I don't plan on leaving you," he declared.

一位御医拿着一块布走近皇后，那块布是为了防止像她这样身份尊贵的人即使在恍惚状态下也流露出痛苦，以免有失体面。这块布能保证她表面上的镇定，而这正是她一直以来所追求的。

One of the physicians approached the empress with a cloth, the kind used to prevent the dishonor of someone of her rank displaying pain, even during such a trance. It was the guarantee of apparent composure, the very thing she had always championed.

“不，”伊莎贝尔说着，把脸转了过去。“我不想停止见我的丈夫。”

"No," Isabel said, turning her face away. "I don't want to stop seeing my husband."

皇帝对她笑了笑，自己也不知从何而来。皇后也回以微笑，直到她再也无法抗拒寝宫中弥漫的血腥味，才想起为何这股味道在胡安娜分娩时让她想起葡萄牙：这味道也曾弥漫在她母亲玛丽亚的房间里，那天她生下弟弟安东尼奥，也是那天她去世。

The emperor smiled at her, unsure where he found the strength to do so. The empress returned the smile until, unable to resist the scent of blood that lingered in the bedchamber, she remembered why this smell, during Juana's childbirth, had reminded her of Portugal: it was the same scent that filled her mother Maria's room the day she gave birth to her brother Antonio; the day she died.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，寝宫外，仿佛一场幽灵般的聚会正在进行。皇帝的孩子们，在塔韦拉红衣主教、弗朗西斯科·德·博尔哈和阿尔瓦公爵的护卫下，静静地等待着消息，他们僵立在原地，彼此之间甚至不敢对视。等待期间，时间仿佛变得不稳定，时而拉长——每一秒对内情的未知都令人难以忍受——时而又缩短——与可能致命的确定性相比，不确定性似乎更令人向往。

Meanwhile, outside the bedchamber, what seemed like a ghostly gathering was taking place. The emperors' children, guarded by Cardinal Tavera, Francisco de Borja, and the Duke of Alba, waited silently for news, frozen in place and not even looking at one another. During the wait, time seemed like an unstable material, stretched at times—each second without knowing what was happening inside was unbearable—and contracted at the same time—uncertainty seemed a desirable state compared to a certainty that could be fatal.

卧室的门终于开了。里面没有哭声或啜泣声，这让他们松了一口气。他们满怀希望地对视着。然而，当皇帝的身影从门槛下出现时，菲利普读懂了他的表情，不由得倒吸了一口凉气。

Finally, the bedroom door opened. No cries or sobs came from within, and that encouraged them. Now they looked at each other, hopeful. However, when the emperor's figure appeared from under the threshold, Philip read his expression and let out a stifled gasp.

 

 

 

 

伊莎贝尔逐一与孩子们告别。先是玛丽亚，她纤弱的脸上满是恐惧；然后是小胡安娜，她还是个婴儿，人人都羡慕她对即将发生的一切浑然不知。接着，她张开双臂迎接菲利普。男孩缓缓走向她。皇帝片刻未曾离开床边，示意他上前。皇后握住长子的手，骄傲地向他微笑。

Isabel said goodbye to her children one by one. First to Maria, her delicate features contorted with terror, and then to little Juana, still a baby, whom everyone envied for her lack of awareness of what was happening. Then she opened her arms to Philip. The boy approached her slowly. The emperor, who hadn't left the bedside for a moment, gestured for him to move forward. As she took her firstborn's hand, the empress smiled proudly at him.

我把所有的希望都寄托在你身上。你要像做儿子一样，做一个好国王。

—I place all my hopes in you. Be as good a king as you have been a son.

费利佩顺从地低下了头。他觉得自己像个男人了。

Felipe lowered his head obediently. He felt like a man.

——照顾好你的父亲。你给予他的爱，就是给予我的爱。

—Look after your father. The love you give him, you are giving to me.

继承人点了点头，随即感到父亲的手搭在了他的肩上；他必须离开了。他感到无比悲痛；告别太过短暂，就像他母亲短暂的一生一样。

The heir nodded, and at once felt his father's hand on his shoulder; he had to leave. He felt devastated; the goodbye had been too short, just like his mother's life.

儿子，我爱你。

—I love you, son.

菲利普从凯撒手中抽回手，拥抱了他的母亲。他昔日的男子气概瞬间瓦解，痛哭流涕，最后一次感受到了母亲的温暖。

Philip pulled his hand away from Caesar to embrace his mother. The man he once was broke down and wept as he felt her warmth for the last time.

皇帝让孩子们、医生和助产士离开寝宫。当最后一个人关上门离开时，查理接受了自己无法像希望的那样与妻子道别的事实：那些未说出口的话语，那些未表达的爱意，都将永远无法诉说。他心灰意冷地坐在她身旁的床上，看着她渐渐离世。

The emperor asked his children, the doctors, and the midwives to leave the bedchamber. When the last of them closed the door behind him, Charles accepted that he would not be able to say goodbye to his wife as he would have wished: that words would remain unsaid and love unexpressed. Defeated, he sat on the bed beside her, as she faded away by the moment.

—上帝至少让我没有死在离你很远的地方，正如我一直祈求的那样。

—God has at least granted me not to die far from you, as I always asked him.

他吻了吻她的手。他从未如此词穷过。

He kissed her hand. He had never been at a loss for words like that.

你的生命不会随着我的离去而结束。

—Your life does not end with me.

“我再也不娶老婆了！”他反抗道。

"I will never take a wife again!" he rebelled.

然后，卡洛斯把手放在她紧紧抱着的小十字架上。

Carlos then placed his hand on a small crucifix that she was clinging to.

我发誓，我对你的爱不会随着你的离去而消失。

—I swear. The love I have for you will not die with you.

伊莎贝尔的眼皮越来越费力地上下颤动，胸口似乎再也没有空气可呼吸了。

Isabel's eyelids fluttered down and up with increasing effort, and there seemed to be no more room for air in her chest.

-拥抱我。

—Hug me.

他顺从了。他害怕伤害她，害怕更加惩罚那具他即将永远渴望的躯体。但她用尽最后的力气抱着他，他也像个受惊的孩子一样，拼命地紧紧抓住她。她湿漉漉的头发，她柔软的脖颈，她垂死肌肤上苦乐参半的气息。卡洛斯闭上了眼睛。积累关于她的记忆对他有什么用呢？它们都太少了。

He obeyed. He was afraid of hurting her, of punishing even more that body he would soon long for, forever. But she was spending her last bit of strength holding him, and he responded by clinging to her desperately, like a frightened child. Her damp hair, her soft neck, the bittersweet scent of her dying skin. Carlos closed his eyes. What good would it do him to accumulate memories of her? They would all be too few.

“我爱你，”他说，然后等待着永远不会到来的回应。

"I love you," he said, and waited for a reply that never came.

 

 

 

 

凯撒的惨叫声响彻卧室的墙壁，然后响彻宫殿里所有房间的墙壁，所有听到的人都战栗不已，因为他们由此知道皇后已经去世，而且她的丈夫也想和她一起走。

The Caesar's cry of pain pierced the walls of the bedchamber, and then those of all the rooms in the palace, and everyone who heard it shuddered, for in this way they knew that the Empress had died, and also that her husband wished to go with her.

 

 

 

 

葬礼在格拉纳达举行。伊莎贝尔就这样回到了她最幸福的城市，回到了她一生中唯一一次坠入爱河的地方。菲利普陪同母亲的灵柩，尽管悲痛欲绝，但他仍尽到继承人的责任，强忍着悲伤，直到确认下葬者确为皇后为止。这位年轻人实在无法直视母亲残缺的遗容。弗朗西斯·博尔吉亚主动提出为他辨认。伊莎贝尔的马夫揭开了覆盖在死者脸上的面纱，但只露出了眼睛。他从未停止过爱她，正因如此，他才选择将这份爱深藏心底：只为留在她身边，侍奉她，在心中永远敬仰她。然而，当面纱被揭开的那一刻，他所看到的景象令他震惊不已。

The burial took place in Granada. Isabel thus returned to the city where she had been happiest, where she had fallen in love for the first and only time in her life. Philip accompanied his mother's coffin, and although he was devastated by grief, he assumed his role as heir and managed to remain stoic until it had to be confirmed that the one being buried was indeed the Empress. The young man could not find the strength to look upon his disfigured mother. Francis Borgia offered to identify her for him. Isabel's master of the horse lifted the veil that covered the deceased's face, but only for his eyes. The man had never stopped loving her, and for that very reason, he had resigned himself to keeping his feelings hidden: so that he could remain by her side, serving her, venerating her only in his heart. What he revealed when the cloth was removed horrified him.

“我不能发誓这就是皇后，”他嘴唇颤抖地低语道，“但我发誓，我们放在这里的就是她的遗体。”

"I cannot swear that this is the Empress," he murmured with trembling lips, "but I do swear that it is her corpse that we place here."

 

 

 

 

葬礼举行之时，在西斯拉修道院的一间小室里，一个仿佛活着却已死去的人正在被埋葬。这个人曾在突尼斯凯旋，阻止了苏莱曼的入侵；他曾与路德、方济各以及无数教皇对峙；他曾统治过半个已知世界，却无法面对妻子入土为安的现实——他如同其他任何物品一般，被封存在棺椁之中，永远地被排除在她曾照亮的世界之外。没有了她，这个世界对他充满敌意；没有人再愿意假装坚强来欺骗他人。他紧紧抱着她的十字架，想要尽情地哀悼她，直到他觉得一切都足够。责任可以暂时搁置。他想，或许有些丈夫会夸耀自己没有经历过像他们这样的丧妻之痛，能够不受悲剧的侵扰；但对他来说，这种痛苦却是一种骄傲的源泉，因为伊莎贝尔值得拥有这一切，也因为这意味着他实现了他一度认为自己无法做到的事情：去爱。

While the funeral was taking place, in a cell of the Sisla monastery, a man, dead while still alive, was being buried. The man who had triumphed in Tunis and stopped Suleiman; the man who had confronted Luther, Francis, and countless popes; the man who ruled half the known world, had not felt capable of watching his wife being laid to rest—remained like any other object, enclosed in a coffin, forever relegated from the existence she had illuminated. The world without her was hostile to him; no one wanted to deceive anyone by feigning strength anymore. Clinging to her crucifix, he wished to mourn her for as long as he needed. Duty could wait. Perhaps there were husbands, he thought, who boasted of not suffering from a loss like theirs, of remaining undisturbed by tragedy; but for him, this pain was a source of pride, for Isabel deserved it, and because it meant that he had achieved what, for a time, he had felt incapable of: to love.

14

14

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

皇后去世后的三年，查理五世的生活如同旋风般忙碌。在托莱多修道院隐居之后，他重返宫廷，但死妻的回忆如影随形，令他倍感窒息。因此，当他得知家乡根特爆发起义时，便决定亲自前往镇压。这场冲突如同磁铁般吸引着他——尽管风险重重，他还是义无反顾地投身其中。他后悔将孩子们留在西班牙，但渴望坠入困境，被各种问题淹没，从而麻木思考的欲望更加强烈。他的眼神空洞，对生活毫无眷恋。

The three years following the Empress's death were a whirlwind of activity for Charles. After his monastic seclusion in Toledo, he returned to court, but once there, surrounded by the memories of his deceased wife, he lived in a constant state of suffocation. Therefore, as soon as he learned of the uprising in Ghent, his hometown, he decided to go in person to quell it. The conflict attracted him like a magnet to light—that is, inevitably, despite the risk. He regretted leaving his children in Spain, but the longing to fall into a chasm of problems that would overwhelm him, that would prevent him from thinking, was even more powerful. His eyes held no attachment to life.

 

 

 

 

他穿越法国前往荷兰。许多人认为，让自己暴露在宿敌的伏击之下是愚蠢的。但查理置之不理。最坏的情况又能怎样呢？最坏、最可怕的事情，其实已经发生了。

He crossed France on his way to the Netherlands. Many considered it foolish to expose himself to any ambush by his eternal enemy. But Charles ignored them. What was the worst that could happen? The worst, the most horrible thing, had already happened.

 

 

 

 

在根特，他对现实的愤怒找到了宣泄口。他毫不留情地使用武力镇压叛乱——这场叛乱源于难以承受的赋税负担，最终演变成暴力抗议。鉴于叛乱者的凶残和不忠，这种武力镇压似乎是必要的，尽管在其他情况下，查理会寻求对话。但如今，他心如刀绞，对一切希望都嗤之以鼻。他以如此狂热的热情伸张正义，以至于根特民众最终跪倒在他的住所，列队前来乞求他的原谅，而他也宽恕了他们。

In Ghent, his fury with reality found an outlet. He spared no brute force in suppressing the rebellion—which arose from an unbearable tax burden that erupted into violent protest. Such force seemed necessary given the ferocity and disloyalty of the insurgents, although in other circumstances Charles would have sought dialogue. But now, with his heart broken as it was, he scorned all hope. He applied justice with such zeal that the people of Ghent eventually came in procession to his residence, on their knees, to beg his forgiveness, which he granted.

 

 

 

 

怒气消散后，皇帝一心想促成和谈。他巡视帝国各地，怀着美好的愿望，寻求改革派和天主教徒之间的和解。他厌倦了等待教会为此召开秘密会议：他为此呼吁了近二十年，却始终无果。皇帝在雷根斯堡召集了帝国议会，让双方坐在长凳上，让他们发言，倾听他们的意见，并要求他们彼此倾听。就这样，一份共同的文本开始被起草。达成协议似乎指日可待。然而，正统观念和傲慢自大却起了作用，他们只关注彼此的分歧，而忽略了共同之处。议会最终无果而终。查理不仅为失败感到惋惜，也为缺乏解决方案而感到遗憾。他想，如果在他那个时代，他对路德的态度没有那么宽容，情况或许会好得多。想到这里，他意识到自己内心深处的绅士风度正在逐渐消逝。

Empty of anger, the emperor found himself in a conciliar mood. He traveled throughout the Empire and, with the best of intentions, sought concord between reformers and Catholics. He was tired of waiting for the Church to hold a conclave for this purpose: he had been demanding it for almost twenty years without success. The emperor convened a Diet in Regensburg, seated both sides on long benches, gave them a voice, listened to them, and compelled them to listen to one another. In this way, a common text began to be drafted. Agreement seemed within reach. But orthodoxies and pride came into play, focusing on what separated them and disregarding what united them. The Diet adjourned without any agreement. Charles not only lamented the failure but also the lack of solutions. He thought it would have been better if, in his day, he had been less lenient with Luther. And in thinking this, he realized that the gentleman within him was fading away.

 

 

 

 

宗教和解失败后，他一度迷失了方向。事实上，当冲突还不足以让他感到痛苦时，对她的思念便会如影随形。很多时候，当他起草信件或阅读国事文件时，回忆便如温暖的拥抱般涌上心头，皇帝便沉浸其中，无法自拔；他便会完全沉浸在对伊莎贝拉的思念之中。这种对过去的逃避令人感到慰藉，但回到现实，回到妻子永远不会回来的确定之中，却总让他感觉像是坠入深渊。以至于他甚至开始怀念法国的威胁。幸好他与弗朗索瓦达成了和平协议：这正是他最需要战斗的时候。另一方面，他也坚信，如今的他会比以往任何时候都更加出色：无所畏惧，无牵挂，一颗冰冷的灵魂将以胜利为食。

After the failure of religious concord, he remained disoriented for a time. The truth was that when conflicts weren't overwhelming enough, the memory of her became too present. Many times, while drafting a letter or reading a matter of state, memory offered itself to him like a warm embrace, and the emperor took refuge in it; then he would become absorbed in thinking of Isabella. This escape to the past was comforting, but the return to reality, to the certainty that his wife would never return, always felt like a fall into the abyss. So much so that he even came to miss the French threat. It was a good thing he had made peace with Francis: just when he most needed to fight. On the other hand, he was also convinced that now he would be a better general than ever: without fear, without attachments, a frozen soul that would feed on victories.

 

 

 

 

出于对战争的渴望和对伊莎贝拉的爱慕，一个目标浮现在眼前，驱使着这位皇帝跃上战马，手持利剑：阿尔及尔。他要完成皇后的遗愿，攻克这座城市，以此来缅怀她，阻止土耳其舰队从那里继续骚扰西班牙海岸。这样做，他既能体验到渴望的战争快感，又能表达对皇后的爱。他决心为胜利付出一切。

From his thirst for battle and his longing for Isabella arose a horizon that compelled the emperor to mount his horse, sword in hand: Algiers. He would honor the empress's memory by finally fulfilling her desire to capture that city, preventing any more Turkish fleets from sailing from it to harass the Spanish coast. In doing so, he would combine the adrenaline of war he craved with an act of love for the empress. He was determined to give everything for victory.

 

 

 

 

几周后，皇帝从马特富角眺望阿尔及利亚海岸，此时暴雨倾盆，海岸隐约可见。就在几分钟前，他刚刚决定解除对要塞的围困：暴风雨使之成为不可能。在返回西班牙的途中，船只饱受风暴摧残，有的沉入海底，有的则偏离航线，漂泊不定。皇帝花了将近一个月的时间才抵达巴利阿里群岛。在那段时间里，他的日子平淡无奇，因为他早已习惯了动荡不安的海面、缺乏欢乐的生活以及漫无目的的漂泊。

A few weeks later, from Cape Matefú, the emperor gazed at the Algerian coast, barely visible behind the curtain of rain that was pouring down at that moment. Just moments before, he had decided to lift the siege of the fortress: the storms had made it impossible. On the return voyage to Spain, the ships, battered by the storm, ended up either at the bottom of the sea or blown off course, adrift. It took the emperor almost a month to reach the Balearic Islands. During that time, his days were unremarkable, for he was accustomed to the unstable surface, to the lack of joy, and to living without direction.

 

 

 

 

幸运的是，尽管战败，宫廷仍以热烈的掌声迎接皇帝的归来。在他缺席的两年里，宫廷上下都非常想念他。查理与他委托摄政的塔韦拉枢机主教重聚，因为继承人年幼。他还见到了自己的女儿们：六岁的乔安娜，她还不认识自己的父亲；以及十三岁的玛丽亚，她已然举止优雅，宛如一位亭亭玉立的少女。然而，皇帝最渴望见到的那个人却并未前来迎接他。

Fortunately, despite the defeat, the court welcomed the emperor with joy. He had been sorely missed during his two-year absence. Charles was reunited with Cardinal Tavera, to whom he had entrusted the regency given the heir's young age, and also with his daughters: six-year-old Joanna, who did not recognize her father; and Maria, who at thirteen already possessed the bearing of a young lady. But the one whom the emperor most longed to see did not come to greet him.

“费利佩在哪儿？”他显然很生气地问塔韦拉。

"Where is Felipe?" he asked Tavera, clearly upset.

红衣主教犹豫了一下。他们一起走进宫殿，远离了公主们。

The cardinal hesitated. They walked together into the palace, away from the princesses.

陛下，他一定很享受阅读的过程。

—He must have been entertained by his reading, Your Majesty.

“别装了。”卡洛斯变得暴躁易怒，对委婉的说法也深恶痛绝。“我从他导师给我的信里得知，他远称不上是个好学生。”

"Stop pretending." Carlos had become grumpy and allergic to euphemisms. "I know from what his tutors have written to me that he is far from being a good student."

这位牧师想方设法既能同意他的观点，又不冒犯王子。

The clergyman sought a way to agree with him without being offensive to the prince.

殿下健康强壮，聪颖过人。他觉得上课枯燥乏味，或许恰恰是好奇心过强的表现。他对一切都充满兴趣……

—His Highness has grown up healthy, strong, and astute. That he finds lessons boring may be a sign, precisely, of excessive curiosity. Everything seems to interest him…

“所有的一切？”凯撒打断道，“你只需专注于那些能让你成为合格继承人的事情。难道你在任何领域都不出类拔萃吗？”

"Everything?" interrupted the Caesar. "You must attend to only what will make you a worthy successor. Do you not excel in any discipline?"

塔韦拉再次犹豫了。

Tavera hesitated again.

“请畅所欲言！你没有权利对我撒谎。”卡洛斯说道。

"Speak openly! You are not authorized to lie to me," Carlos declared.

“他觉得学习很累，”红衣主教最后坦白道，“他没有语言天赋，不屑骑马，对战争也毫无兴趣……”

“He finds studying tiring,” the cardinal finally confessed. “He has no aptitude for languages. He disdains horsemanship, and matters of war are of no interest to him…”

皇帝尽力接受了这份报告。

The emperor accepted the report as best he could.

—他难道一无是处吗？

—Is he not good… at anything?

“哦，是的，”另一个人回答说，“他真的很有植物方面的天赋。”

"Oh, yes," replied the other. "He has a real talent for plants."

卡洛斯的困惑被一个幻影打断了。

Carlos's bewilderment was interrupted by an apparition.

-父亲。

-Father.

卡洛斯转过身，惊奇地凝视着他的儿子。短短两年，费利佩就长成了一个英俊的青年。十五岁的他个子不算高，但体格健壮，身材匀称，一副成熟的模样；五官精致，只是嘴唇略显丰满；蓝色的眼睛和金色的头发，无不彰显着他哈布斯堡家族的血统。他是一位英俊的年轻人，而且从他的外表来看，想必也颇具魅力。

Carlos turned and stared in amazement at his son. In just two years, Felipe had grown into a young man. At fifteen, he wasn't tall, but he was athletic, with a well-proportioned, adult physique; he had refined features, except for his full lips; and his blue eyes and blond hair were a testament to his Habsburg blood. He was a handsome young man, and judging by his good looks, not lacking in character.

—很抱歉我迟到了。

—I apologize for my lateness.

他们都惊讶于对方的变化之大。在费利佩的记忆中，父亲是一位威严的男人：成熟稳重，目光炯炯有神，充满干劲和决心。然而现实却截然不同。卡洛斯在短短几年间迅速衰老。他的头发已经花白，痛风使他步履蹒跚，举手投足间都透着疲惫，而且总是愁眉苦脸的。

They were both surprised by how much the other had changed. In Felipe's memory, his father was an imposing man: mature and vigorous, with drive and determination in his eyes. Reality seemed quite different. Carlos had aged rapidly in those couple of years. His hair had turned gray, gout made him limp, weariness was evident in his movements, and he generally displayed a sullen air.

但儿子的一切都让皇帝感到困惑；他甚至能从儿子涨红的双颊和过分放松的表情中猜到，儿子肯定有外遇。

But everything about his son baffled the emperor; he could even guess, from the vividly flushed cheeks and the excessively relaxed expression he wore, that he was undoubtedly having an affair.

 

 

 

 

伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥是菲利普十几岁的妹妹玛丽亚的侍女之一，就像她之前侍奉已故皇后一样。她大约二十岁，拥有高贵的容貌。她的贵族血统赋予了她一丝傲慢，但侍奉过地位更高的女性的经历让她明白，尽管她很有价值，但终究是可有可无的。

Isabel Osorio was part of the retinue of ladies-in-waiting to Maria, Philip's teenage sister, as she had previously been to that of the late Empress. She was around twenty years old and possessed a dignified beauty. Her aristocratic lineage lent her a touch of haughtiness, but having served women of higher rank reminded her that, while valuable, she was expendable.

正因如此，她深知自己在社会阶层中的地位，才对菲利普的追求置之不理。这位王位继承人素来以风流成性著称，据说对女人有着永不满足的欲望。这位年轻女子自尊心极强，不愿甘于做情妇，也明白自己别无所求：与王子谈情说爱不会有任何结果；顶多也就是生个私生子，再从王室领到一笔养老金，作为对她“服侍”的酬谢。

That's why, because she knew her place in the social order, she tried to ignore Philip's advances. The heir had a reputation as a womanizer and was said to have a voracious appetite for women. The young woman had enough self-respect not to settle for being a mere mistress, and the good sense to know that she couldn't aspire to anything more than that: nothing would come of a romance with the prince; at most, a bastard child and a pension from the Crown, as a token of gratitude for services rendered.

唯一的问题是，伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥喜欢上了费利佩。这位继承人健谈而大胆，浑身散发着一股调情的活力。他浑身散发着现代人的气息：好奇心强，求知欲旺盛，并且反抗着过去的种种。这不仅仅是因为他年轻；他真正代表着一个新时代。每当伊莎贝尔听到他博学地谈论科学或故事时，她都感觉仿佛置身于一个等待探索的世界；更何况，这个世界还拥有她渴望亲吻的明亮双眸和灿烂笑容。

The only problem was that Isabel Osorio liked Felipe. The heir was talkative and daring, pure energy dedicated to flirtation. He had the air of a modern man: inquisitive, eager to learn, and rebellious against the ways of the past. It wasn't just his youth; he truly represented a new era. When she heard him speak eruditely about science or stories, Isabel felt as if she were in the presence of a world waiting to be discovered; a world that, moreover, possessed beautiful light eyes and a smile she longed to kiss.

一天晚上，在又一次追求之后，继承人出现在了女孩的卧室里。

One night, after another courtship, the heir had appeared in the girl's bedroom.

“你在这里做什么？”年轻女子问他。

"What are you doing here?" the young woman had said to him.

我的嘴唇会回答你。是用言语还是用吻，由你决定。

—My lips will answer you. Whether with words or with kisses, you decide.

——这是鲁莽的行为。

—It's reckless.

我无时无刻不在想你。

—I think about you every single moment.

你做错了！

—You're doing wrong!

我别无选择。

—I have no choice.

费利佩的身体就像一个充满欲望的火药桶。伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥察觉到了这一点，感觉自己几乎就要屈服了。尽管她有很多理由反对这段恋情，但她感觉自己就像被扔进一口井里，而那个继承人就是她注定要坠落的井底。

Felipe's body was like a powder keg of desire. Isabel Osorio noticed this and felt herself on the verge of giving in. Despite her many reasons against this romance, she felt as if she had been thrown into a well and the heir was the bottom into which she was inevitably going to fall.

“为什么是我？”她问道。

"Why me?" she asked.

因为你拥有我童年时被夺走的光芒。

—Because you possess the light that was stolen from me as a child.

费利佩说话或许有些夸张，但他的语气却是真诚的。这位年轻女子让他感受到了一种自母亲去世后便从未在任何人身上体验过的情感。他曾与许多女子交往，但自从皇后最后一次拥抱他之后，他的情感似乎就被压抑了下来。母亲的离世如同重锤般击碎了这位继承人的心。他沉溺于享乐，因为这让他意识到自己还活着，但对他而言，爱情就像一个容器，被母亲的鲜血注满后，最终爆裂开来。

Felipe spoke in hyperbole, but he was sincere. This young woman made him feel something he hadn't allowed himself to feel with anyone since his mother's death. He had been with many women, but it seemed his emotions had been put on hold since the Empress's last embrace. The pain of her death had left the heir's heart crippled. He had become fond of pleasure because it reminded him he was alive, but for him, love was a vessel his mother had filled to overflowing and then burst.

然而，自从遇见伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥之后，费利佩的情感麻木开始动摇。这位女士拥有诸多美德——沉静的智慧、美丽的容貌、面对逆境时的幽默感、真诚的笑容——但如果说费利佩爱上了她，那是因为她施展了某种魔力，也因为他的心早已厌倦了毫无生气的状态。

However, since meeting Isabel Osorio, that emotional lethargy began to waver. The lady possessed many virtues—serene intelligence, beauty, irony in the face of adversity, a sincere smile—but if Felipe fell in love with her, it was because the necessary spell had been cast and because his heart had grown weary of not beating.

 

 

 

 

男人赢得女士信任的唯一方法就是推迟探望，菲利普正是这样做的。这对于这位继承人来说毫不费力；毕竟，他的一生都在懂得等待——等待母亲去世的伤痛愈合，等待自己继承凯撒的遗产。

The only way a man could win a lady's trust was to postpone his bedside visit, and that is what Philip did with his beloved. It required no effort from the heir; after all, his life consisted of knowing how to wait—for the wound of his mother's death to heal, for him to receive Caesar's legacy.

但皇帝的归来扰乱了年轻人的心情，也考验了他的耐心；尤其是当他的父亲很快发现伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥和他的儿子有染后，以法官的姿态出现在他面前时。

But the emperor's return upset the young man's mood and also tested his patience; especially when his father, who soon found out that Isabel Osorio and his son were having an affair, appeared before him with the air of a judge.

“你不能再见那个女孩了，”凯撒宣布道。

"You cannot see that girl anymore," Caesar declared.

“我做的每件事，你当年在我这个年纪也会做，”他的儿子回答说。

"I don't do anything you wouldn't have done at my age," replied his son.

卡洛斯无法相信，一个本应向他致敬的年轻人，竟然会把自己的罪孽公之于众。

Carlos could not believe that a young man whose duty it was to honor him would throw his sins in his face.

你竟敢这样？

—How dare you?

—如果你担心我玩忽职守，那么当多娜·杰尔马娜帮助你在这些王国安顿下来时，你肯定有更多分心的事情。

—If what worries you is that I neglect my duties, you had more distractions when Doña Germana helped you settle in these kingdoms.

皇帝脸色苍白。

The emperor paled.

“都怪你让我学历史，”继承人补充道。

"It's your fault for making me study History," added the heir.

“滚出去！”他父亲吼道。

"Get out!" roared his father.

 

 

 

 

冲突过后，皇帝决定解雇儿子的老师，亲自承担起教育儿子的重任，至少暂时如此。显然，无论这些老师多么德高望重、学识渊博，他们都失职了。菲利普只学习自己想学的东西，而且他的行为举止缺乏纪律，这虽然符合他这个年龄段的典型特征，却与他的身份格格不入。或许这只是年轻人的不羁，但如果并非如此呢？如果注定要继承如此庞大遗产的人，最终却是一个误入歧途的人呢？

Following the clash, the emperor decided to dismiss his son's tutors and assume, at least for a time, the task of educating him himself. It was clear that, however prestigious and wise they possessed, those teachers had failed in their duty. Philip only learned what he wanted to learn, and moreover, he behaved with a lack of discipline typical of his age but unsuitable for his position. Perhaps it was a youthful indiscipline, but what if it wasn't? What if the one destined to inherit such a vast legacy turned out to be a wayward individual?

这场战斗也让卡洛斯意识到时光飞逝。年过四十的他，已然是一个过去远多于未来的人。他深知未来仍会经历胜利与失败，但此刻，他最优先考虑的却是保住自己的遗产。事实上，自从伊莎贝尔去世后，这位凯撒就觉得自己的人生已步入尾声。他确信，真正的幸福再也不会回来了；或许正因如此，自从成为鳏夫后，他的身体才如此迅速地衰弱。当然，多年的奔波、战争以及日积月累的病痛，足以让任何人衰老。但卡洛斯明白，他衰老的根本原因，是他那颗充满怀旧和绝望的心。

The fight also helped Carlos realize how quickly time had passed. At just over forty, he was already a man with more past than future. He had no doubt that moments of triumph and defeat still lay ahead, but suddenly his priority became securing his inheritance. In truth, since Isabel's death, the Caesar felt he was in the epilogue of his life. Complete happiness would never return, he was certain of it; perhaps that was why, since becoming a widower, his body had withered so rapidly. Certainly, the many journeys, the wars, and the headaches that had accumulated over the years would have aged any man. But Carlos knew that the main reason for his decline was his nostalgic, hopeless heart.

 

 

 

 

国王禁止我见你。

—The king has forbidden me to see you.

费利佩出现在伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥的房间里，仍然因为和父亲的争吵而情绪激动。

Felipe appeared in Isabel Osorio's room, still in a state of agitation from the argument with his father.

所以你就服从他？

—And so you obey him?

继承人以一个吻回应。这并非他们唇齿相依的第一次，但这一次的接触却饱含着情欲与急切：一个吻，引领他们走向床笫。伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥没有退缩；几个星期以来，她一直在幻想与王子共度的场景，而这些幻想她绝不会告诉任何人。

The heir responded with a kiss. It wasn't the first time their lips had met, but this time the contact possessed sensuality and urgency: a kiss that led to the bed. Isabel Osorio didn't back down; for weeks she had been fantasizing about scenes with the prince that she wouldn't have confessed to anyone.

过了一会儿，他们赤身裸体地休息着，脸上带着甜蜜的微笑，他们彼此相爱了。

When after a while, naked, they rested with a sweet smile sewn onto their faces, they were both in love.

 

 

 

 

远在法国的蒙莫朗西正准备与他的君主进行每日例行会谈。说实话，这种仪式已经让他感到难以忍受。他厌倦了弗朗西斯一遍又一遍地重复着同样的说辞，也厌倦了年复一年地重复着同样的辩解。这位君主如今成了一个残酷的笑话：他体弱多病，与查理的敌对关系成了他生命中唯一不变的纽带，也是唯一能让人想起他曾经辉煌的迹象。母亲和儿子的去世无疑让他迷失了方向，他生命中唯一的支柱似乎只剩下与皇帝之间那段不健康的亲密关系。

Far away, in France, Montmorency was preparing for his daily council with his lord. To tell the truth, for some time now, this ritual had been unbearable. He was exhausted from hearing Francis deliver the same speech, and from responding with the same retorts meeting after meeting, year after year. The monarch had become a cruel joke: frail and weakened by illness, his rivalry with Charles was the only thing that remained intact, the only reminder of the man he had once been. The deaths of his mother and son had undoubtedly disoriented him, and the only pillar left in his life was his unhealthy relationship with the emperor.

这位顾问越来越不服从他的上级，他的耐心已然耗尽，他宁愿因自己的不敬而受罚，也不愿眼睁睁地看着法国因国王的盲目执念而坠入深渊。有时，他幻想一个明智的弗朗西斯，一个能够安于现状、不再觊觎更多，并最终致力于守护国土的弗朗西斯。蒙莫朗西的确曾与他的主人一样，对皇帝抱有强烈的敌意。他怎能不如此呢？根特皇帝的领土如同刺客扼住猎物喉咙的利爪，将法国紧紧包围：北面、南面，乃至意大利，高卢人所见的一切都带有查理的印记。但随着时间的推移，人们逐渐明白，这位皇帝并非一个好战的统治者，他并不渴望扩张疆域。他甚至没有利用弗朗西斯的俘虏来夺取王位！

The advisor was becoming increasingly defiant of his superior, for his patience was wearing thin, and he preferred to be punished for his irreverence than to let France plunge into the abyss because of his king's blind obsession. At times, he fantasized about a sensible Francis, one who would accept his possessions without aspiring to anything more and who would finally dedicate himself to caring for what remained within his borders. It was true that Montmorency had once shared his master's zeal against the emperor. How could he not? The possessions of the emperor of Ghent hemmed in France like an assassin's hands around his victim's throat: to the north, to the south, and in Italy, everything the Gauls saw bore the mark of Charles. But with time, it became clear that the emperor was not a bellicose ruler who aspired to expand his borders. He had even refrained from using Francis's captivity to seize the kingdom!

然而，当顾问走进办公室时，看到的却是和往常一样的景象：他的君主站在一张因日复一日翻阅而磨损的欧洲地图前，目光焦急地扫视着地图，似乎在寻找什么线索。亨利王子站在他身旁，身姿挺拔，青春洋溢。然而，他父亲的模样却透着一股忧郁：稀疏凌乱的胡须，灰白的皮肤，以及佝偻的身躯，如同一丛阴郁的灌木。

However, when the advisor entered the office, he saw the same thing as every day: his lord before a map of Europe worn from constant handling, his eyes anxiously scanning the document in search of a feat. Beside him stood Prince Henry, whose erect figure radiated youth. His father's appearance, however, evoked nothing but sadness: his sparse, disheveled beard, his grayish skin, and his body hunched like a gloomy bush.

“我们必须利用他们在阿尔及尔的失败，”君主说道。

"We must take advantage of their defeat in Algiers," said the sovereign.

听到这番话，蒙莫朗西不禁思忖，如果当初他没有早点止步于宫廷的晋升之路，自己的人生又会是怎样一番景象。他本可以过上一个平庸贵族的舒适生活，而不是觊觎元帅的头衔——这个头衔让他不得不服从一位被野心蒙蔽双眼的君主。“我宁愿少些权力，多些清晨的狩猎时光，午后陪伴孩子学习，晚间品酒赏乐……”他每天出门赴宫廷之前都会这样对妻子玛德琳说道。

Upon hearing this, Montmorency wondered what his life might have been like had he halted his rise at court sooner. Instead of coveting the title of Constable, which obligated him to obey a monarch blinded by ambition, he could have led the comfortable life of a mediocre aristocrat. "I wish for less power and instead long mornings hunting, afternoons educating my children, evenings of wine and music..." he would tell his wife, Madeleine, each day before departing for the royal office.

“战败后，他们的军队实力削弱了，”国王继续说道。

"Their armies are weakened after the defeat," the monarch continued.

议员沉默不语。弗朗西斯科看着他，猜想蒙莫朗西已经把他当成疯子了。

The councilor remained silent. Francisco looked at him and guessed that Montmorency already considered him a madman.

“我向你保证，这次袭击将彻底终结我对他的仇恨！我也很累了……但现在是最后的机会了！你给我记住这一点。”

"I promise you that with this attack I will end my hatred for him! I am tired too... But it's now or never! Understand this."

“这有什么好理解的？”亨利王子厉声说道，“难道是两个心怀怨恨的老头用拐杖互相殴打致死吗？”

"What's there to understand?" burst Prince Henry. "That you're two spiteful old men beating each other to death with canes?"

国王随后趾高气扬地走向继承人，一把抓住他的胸膛，用力摇晃。继承人却任由他摆布，仿佛这丝毫不会对他构成威胁。

Then the king approached the heir with a boastful air. He grabbed him by the breast and shook him. The heir let him, as if it posed no threat to him whatsoever.

“看到你这样我很难过，”年轻人道歉道。

"It hurts me to see you like this," the young man apologized.

弗朗西斯科回过神来，松开了手。他双手抱头，精疲力竭。在他看来，生活就像一个永无止境、令人烦恼的白昼，似乎永远也走不完，但必须在夜幕降临前结束。恩里克同情他的父亲，但一想到将来有一天自己可能要继承一个因他而破产的王国，他就感到痛苦不堪。

Francisco regained his senses and let go. He put his hands to his head. He was exhausted. Life seemed to him like an endless, troubled day that appeared interminable, but which had to be completed before nightfall. Enrique felt pity for his father, although he was distressed at the prospect of one day inheriting a bankrupt kingdom because of him.

“我只希望法国和你都能过得更好，”年轻人说。

"I just want what's best for France, and for you," said the young man.

“我总有一天会完成我开始做的事情，否则我就不会死去。”国王回答说。

"I cannot die without having finished what I started one day," replied the king.

弗朗西斯唯一遵守的诫命就是不参与战争。他的判断没错：如果他是一头野兽，他们早就给他致命一击了。但他不是野兽，上帝仍然允许他梦想胜利。

The only thing Francis obeyed was refraining from taking part in the war. He wasn't mistaken: if he had been an animal, they would have already given him the coup de grâce. But he wasn't, and God still allowed him to dream of victory.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在卡斯蒂利亚，皇帝每天都惊讶于儿子如此乐于教导他，并从中汲取自己人生的经验教训。他意识到，自己需要从人生中学习，其重要性不亚于，甚至可能超过继承人从中受益的程度。

Meanwhile, in Castile, the emperor was surprised daily by how much his son enjoyed instructing him, drawing lessons from his own past. He realized that he needed to learn from his life as much as, or even more than, his heir could benefit from it.

菲利普得知皇帝打算亲自教导他时，曾以为会遭受漫长的责骂，但得知父亲并非要惩罚他，而是想让他成为一个更好的人，他感到十分欣慰。皇帝讲述的故事颇具英雄史诗的色彩，其中不乏路德、英格兰的亨利以及后来的法国国王等杰出人物。这位王位继承人被这些故事深深吸引，但父亲的存在却让他百感交集：他敬佩父亲，但同时，某种难以言喻的因素又让他感到不安。他曾对皇后怀有深切的爱戴；相比之下，查理在他心中激起的情感却复杂而令人不安。他承认，自己害怕配不上父亲。他意识到自己求学时成绩平平，过于叛逆，而且他的性格与那些刀光剑影、战火纷飞的故事格格不入。他担心将来自己会活在前任的阴影下，让所有人失望，而且前任留下的遗产，无论多么完好地保存下来，都会在他手中崩塌。

Philip, who upon learning of the emperor's intention to educate him had imagined long days of scolding, was pleased to discover that his father did not want to punish him, but rather to make him a better man. The emperor's tales had something of a heroic novel about them, with illustrious protagonists such as Luther, Henry of England, and the inevitable French king. The heir was fascinated by them, although his father's presence stirred mixed feelings: he admired him, but at the same time, something he couldn't quite put his finger on irritated him. He had felt a devoted love for the empress; in contrast, the emotion Charles aroused in him was ambivalent, unsettling. What he did acknowledge was that he was afraid of not being worthy of him. He was aware that as a student he hadn't excelled, that he was too prone to disobedience, and that his inclinations were entirely foreign to the epic of the sword and wars. He feared that in the future he would govern in the shadow of his predecessor and disappoint everyone, and that the legacy, however well preserved by the latter, would crumble in his hands.

尽管内心缺乏安全感，菲利普在那些课程中仍反复公开地质疑查理一生所做的决定。皇帝对此感到受到攻击，便会辩解或断然回避。但事实上，儿子的责备令他印象深刻，他意识到菲利普并非他想象中那样轻浮无知的年轻人。实际上，他聪明、沉稳、深思熟虑，并且拥有他自己一直缺乏的魅力。他的儿子绝不会让自己被一个希耶夫尔（Chièvres）所吞噬：他会用两句犀利的反驳让他哑口无言。皇帝第一次敢于相信，他的遗产掌握在可靠的人手中。

Despite his insecurity, throughout those lessons Philip repeatedly and openly questioned the decisions Charles had made throughout his career. The emperor would then feel attacked and defend himself with arguments or dismiss the matter curtly. But the truth was that his son's reproaches struck him as brilliant, and he realized that Philip was not the scatterbrained and ignorant young man he had imagined. In reality, he was intelligent, serene, and thoughtful, and possessed the charisma that he himself had always lacked. His son would never have allowed himself to be swallowed up by a Chièvres: he would have put him in his place with two sharp retorts. For the first time, the emperor dared to believe that his legacy was in good hands.

 

 

 

 

未来吞噬当下的这种感觉不仅在西班牙，而且在整个帝国都普遍存在。查理忙于培养儿子的能力，他的弟弟费迪南也在培养长子马克西米利安。马克西米利安与继承人同龄，但他的关注点却截然不同：他并非为与父亲的关系而烦恼，而是为家族在皇帝手中遭受的不公而耿耿于怀。这位英俊桀骜不驯的年轻人，正是费迪南所有怨恨的化身，并且毫不掩饰地表达出来。尽管查理的弟弟在讲述家族历史时竭力避免将自己描绘成受害者，但对马克西米利安而言，事实胜于雄辩：从他们在卡斯蒂利亚的初次相遇起，皇帝就无情地利用了他父亲的善良本性。男孩也感到自己受到了极大的愤慨，因为他叔叔提出的皇位继承方案将他排除在指挥权之外：虽然他的父亲会继承那些领地，但继承他皇位的是菲利普，而不是他。

That the future was devouring the present was something felt not only in Spain, but throughout the entire Empire. While Charles was busy honing his son's abilities, his brother Ferdinand was doing the same with his eldest son, Maximilian. Maximilian was the same age as the heir, but his concerns were very different: he wasn't troubled by his relationship with his father, but rather by the perceived injustice his lineage had suffered at the hands of the emperor. The young man, handsome and defiant, was the embodiment of all of Ferdinand's resentments, and he didn't hesitate to express them. However much Charles's brother tried, when recounting the family history, not to portray himself as a victim, for Maximilian the facts spoke for themselves: the emperor had ruthlessly exploited his father's good nature from their very first encounters in Castile. The boy also felt personally outraged, since the imperial succession proposed by his uncle excluded him from command: it was true that his father would inherit those domains, but the one who would succeed him would be Philip and not him.

费尔南多很快察觉到儿子心中的不安。为了安抚他，他描绘了一幅美好的未来图景。他确信，只要儿子忠心耿耿，查理就会赏赐他一些财产。虽然皇帝有时在处理自己人的事情上笨手笨脚，但最终通常还是会慷慨解囊的。马克西米利安想要相信他，于是压抑住对叔叔的怨恨。他愿意给费尔南多一次机会。但他并不打算像父亲那样对查理百依百顺。他的原则绝不会轻易被践踏。如果皇帝不能尽快展现出与其品格相符的姿态，他就不会再有第二次机会了。

Fernando quickly realized the unease brewing in his son. To soothe him, he painted a picture of a bright future. He was certain that if he acted loyally, Charles would reward him with some of his possessions. Although the emperor was sometimes clumsy in dealing with his own, he was usually generous in the end. Maximilian wanted to believe him and tempered his resentment toward his uncle. He would give him a chance. But he didn't intend to behave like the accommodating ally his father had been. His spirit wouldn't be trampled on like that. If the emperor didn't show a gesture befitting his character, and soon, he wouldn't be given a second chance.

 

 

 

 

查理对帝国境内弥漫的怨恨之网浑然不觉，因为种种事件让他无暇顾及这些抽象的问题。一天晚上，痛风发作后，他正歇息休息，却得知法国一夜之间占领了尼斯。皇帝想起弗朗索瓦曾许下的和平承诺，几乎要笑出声来；他知道，即便弗朗索瓦真心实意地想要阻止战火，法国人的性格也绝不会允许任何改变，只会让战争持续下去。

Charles remained oblivious to the web of resentment being woven throughout the Empire, for events left him little time to dwell on such abstract matters. One evening, while resting his feet after a gout attack, he learned that France had seized Nice overnight. The emperor nearly laughed as he recalled Francis's promise of peace; he knew that, even if Francis sincerely tried to halt the fighting between them, the French character would never allow for anything other than perpetuating it.

“我已经命令我的军队准备夺回广场，”阿尔巴公爵向他的领主报告说。

"I have ordered my troops to prepare to retake the square," the Duke of Alba informed his lord.

卡洛斯摇了摇头，表示不赞同。

Carlos nodded his head in disapproval.

尼斯已经陷落了。我们夺回它没有任何意义。我们最好还是准备保卫米兰，因为我毫不怀疑弗朗西斯别无所求。

—Nice has already fallen. We wouldn't gain anything by recapturing it. We'd be better off preparing our defense of Milan, because I have no doubt that Francis wants nothing else.

皇帝毫不犹豫地判了他死刑。他和那个法国人之间那场没完没了的拉锯战唯一的好处就是，皇帝终于学会了其中的门道。查理一世归来后，塔韦拉红衣主教不再统治那些王国，而是专注于他的宗教裁判长一职，但他对这一消息的反应，仿佛他的孩子们受到了威胁。

The emperor sentenced him without a shadow of a doubt. The only good thing about that endless dance he and the Frenchman were having was that the emperor had finally learned the steps. With Charles's return, Cardinal Tavera no longer governed those kingdoms and was dedicated to his post as Inquisitor General, but he reacted to the announcement as if he felt his children were threatened.

陛下，西班牙已经背负了债务。请相信我，我们再也经不起另一场战争了。

—Your Majesty, Spain is mortgaged. Believe me when I say that another war cannot be afforded.

“就让法国人心甘情愿地接管公国吗？”阿尔巴公爵插话道。

—And let the Frenchman happily take over the duchy? —intervened the Duke of Alba.

得知公爵站在自己这边，皇帝更加坚定了自卫的决心。但是，一如既往，资金短缺。

Knowing that the duke was on his side reinforced the emperor's resolve to defend himself. But, as always, money was lacking.

经过几天的思考，查尔斯找到了资助米兰保护的办法，同时也确保了他的儿子正式步入成年：继承人结婚的时机已经到了。

After several days of reflection, Charles found a way to finance Milan's protection, and at the same time, to ensure his son's definitive entry into adulthood: the time had come for the heir to marry.

 

 

 

 

葡萄牙宫廷同意了：年轻的玛丽亚·曼努埃拉将成为菲利普的第一任妻子。皇帝和他的顾问们满意地读完信后，仔细查看葡萄牙方面的信件，寻找一个数字：这位年轻女子带来的嫁妆。最终，他们找到了：三十万杜卡特。这笔交易无可挑剔；它足以使米兰免遭法国的侵占，甚至还能帮助缓解王国的一些长期债务。皇帝唯一担心的是他的儿子会如何看待这桩婚事。

The Portuguese court agreed: the young Maria Manuela would become Philip's first wife. After reading this with satisfaction, the emperor and his advisors scanned the Portuguese letter, searching for a figure: the dowry the young woman would bring with her. Finally, they found it: three hundred thousand ducats. The deal was unbeatable; it would be enough to keep Milan from the French and even help alleviate some of the kingdoms' perpetual debt. The emperor's only concern was how his son would react to the wedding.

然而，最初的震惊和不满过后，菲利普接受了自己的命运。即便爱上了姐姐的侍女，他也没有忘记自己的责任。而且，这桩婚事似乎对他很有吸引力。他对这个年轻女子一无所知，但他的直觉告诉他，她会让他忘记情人。

However, after an initial moment of shock and discontent, Philip accepted his fate. Even in love with his sister's lady-in-waiting, he did not forget his responsibilities. And besides, something about this marriage seemed promising to him. He knew nothing about this young woman, but his intuition told him she would make him forget his lover.

“你们已经有钱打仗了，”塔韦拉无奈地说。

"You already have the money for your war," Tavera said resignedly.

凯撒补充道：“还有英格兰国王亨利的支持。”

—And the support of Henry of England—added the Caesar.

查理一世始终无法原谅那个英国人给他的姑姑凯瑟琳带来的苦难，但事实上，命运早已让他付出了代价：与安妮·博林的婚姻是一场灾难，最终她因叛国罪被审判。这位曾令亨利一见倾心的女子，最终被从断头台上斩首，托马斯·克伦威尔——这位他曾希望借以忘却沃尔西主教的顾问——也同样如此。之后，亨利与简·西摩结婚，两人短暂地享受了一段幸福时光，因为简在生下期盼已久的都铎王朝继承人后不久便去世了。王位继承人是凯瑟琳·霍华德，但她婚后不久便被证实背叛了丈夫，最终也落得与博林同样的下场：被斩首。此时的亨利，已与凯瑟琳·帕尔结婚，变成了一个肥胖而精神失常、饱受诅咒的国王。如果阿拉贡女王想要上帝降下震怒于他，那么上帝显然已经决定应允，而且毫不留情。他的虚荣心被彻底践踏，凯撒感到复仇的快感，因此毫不犹豫地指望他支持自己对抗高卢人。
