Charles had not forgiven the Briton for the ordeal he had put his aunt Catherine through, but the truth was that fate had already made him pay for it: the marriage to Anne Boleyn was a disaster that ended with her being tried for treason against the English Crown. The head that had once captivated Henry ended up sliding from a scaffold, as did that of Thomas Cromwell, the advisor with whom he had hoped to forget Cardinal Wolsey. The monarch then married Jane Seymour, with whom he enjoyed a fleeting happiness, as she died shortly after giving birth to the long-awaited heir of the Tudor dynasty. The successor to the throne was Catherine Howard, but after it was proven that she had cheated on her husband soon after the wedding, she suffered the same fate as Boleyn: beheading. Henry, who was at that time married to Catherine Parr, had become an obese and disturbed king, cursed. If the Aragonese queen had desired the wrath of the Almighty for him, it was clear that He had resolved to grant it, and without mercy. His vanity had been so thoroughly trampled that the Caesar felt avenged, and thus did not hesitate to count on his support against the Gaul.

“没有战争是件值得高兴的事，”塔韦拉回答说。

"No war is a cause for joy," Tavera replied.

“我同意您的请求，殿下，”查尔斯说道，“但我迫不及待地想动身前往米兰。”

—That I grant you, Your Eminence— said Charles. But I can scarcely wait to depart for Milan.

红衣主教惊恐万分，划了个十字。

The cardinal, horrified, crossed himself.

——是你？又一次统领军队？这有什么意义？看来你是在寻死，还是在逃避痛苦……

—You? At the head of your armies again? What's the point? It seems you're seeking death, or fleeing from your pain…

“我无需为我的行为负责，”皇帝打断道，“更不必为我的动机负责！”

"Nothing compels me to account for my actions," interrupted the emperor. "Least of all my motives!"

说实话，卡洛斯很高兴能回到西班牙，与孩子们团聚，好好休息一段时间。但塔韦拉说得对：他需要逃离，而且他想用战斗的方式逃离。他怀念战斗的喧嚣，怀念敌人的利剑袭来，而他自己在最后一刻用剑挡下的感觉。在死里逃生的那一刻，他会庆幸自己还活着——伊莎贝尔失踪后，他几乎无法体会这种感觉，但像所有男人一样，他需要这种感觉。如果必须冒着生命危险才能找到她，他也会毫不犹豫。另一种选择就是慢慢地消逝，最终归于虚无。

To tell the truth, Carlos had found it pleasant to return to Spain, to be reunited with his children, and to rest for a while. But Tavera was right: he needed to escape, and he wanted to do so by fighting. He missed the clamor of combat, the feeling of an enemy sword attacking him and blocking it with his own at the last instant. In that moment when he would narrowly escape death, he would be glad to be alive—an emotion he could barely experience after Isabel's disappearance, but which, like every man, he needed. If he had to find her by putting himself at risk, he would do it. The other option was to slowly wither away into nothingness.

 

 

 

 

一天下午，狩猎结束后，费利佩和他的父亲站在山顶上眺望地平线。万里无云的天空像一幅完美的深蓝色帷幕一样铺展在大地之上。

One afternoon, after a day of hunting, Felipe and his father stood gazing at the horizon from a hilltop. The cloudless sky stretched out over the earth like a perfect, dark blue curtain.

“我要出兵了，”他宣布道。菲利普听了皇帝的话，感到十分困惑，胸口一阵紧缩。“在我不在期间，你将摄政这些王国，”皇帝继续说道，“你将有机会向我证明，我可以信任你。”

“I am going to war,” he announced, and Philip received the emperor’s words with bewilderment. He felt a flutter of nerves in his chest. “You will be the regent of these kingdoms in my absence,” the emperor continued. “You will have the opportunity to prove to me that I can trust you.”

“你又要抛弃我了，”继承人说道。

"You're abandoning me again," said the heir.

卡洛斯转向他，在这个傲慢而精明的年轻人的外表下，他看到了一个孩子。

Carlos turned towards him and beneath the demeanor of the arrogant and shrewd young man, he saw a child.

儿子，我会尽我所能回来。

—I will do everything in my power to return, son.

菲利普看了他一眼，受伤地转过身去。他突然明白了皇帝自他到来以来为何一直令他恼火：两年来，他一直不在家，一心扑在政务上，却忽略了在皇后去世后急需他照顾的孩子们。而现在，他又要离开，完全没有必要，这很可能会让孩子们成为孤儿。他们之间再也没有交流了，而这个年轻人需要他的陪伴。他喜欢看到，当查理分享他的智慧时，他们之间的隔阂正在逐渐消融。

Philip looked at him and, hurt, turned away. He suddenly understood why the emperor had irritated him since his arrival: he had been absent for two years, months and months prioritizing governance over providing for his children who so desperately needed him after the empress's death. And now he was leaving again, without any need to, risking leaving them orphans. There would be no more conversation between them, and the young man needed his company. He liked to see how the wall between them was crumbling as Charles shared his wisdom.

那次遗弃是不是又一次教训？

Was that abandonment yet another lesson?

沿着僻静的小路返回宫廷的路上，男孩心想，或许父亲正在做一位皇帝应该做的事，而做一个普通人和一位统治者，或许是两种无法兼顾的职责。他想起母亲在皇帝不在时所承受的煎熬，想起皇帝在那些日子里所进行的种种壮举——而这些壮举，正是他，菲利普，所着迷地聆听的。

As he walked back to court along lonely paths, the boy thought that perhaps his father was doing what an emperor was supposed to do, and that being a man and a ruler were probably two incompatible tasks. He remembered his mother suffering through the emperor's absences, during which he carried out those enterprises that he, Philip, was fascinated to hear about.

继承人怒不可遏，浑身颤抖；森林里回荡着他口中咒骂的声响，矛头直指那个来自根特的男人，随后是一声凄厉的嚎叫。他渴望父亲，却又痛恨失去父亲的念头。

The heir trembled with rage; the forest heard curses escape his lips, directed at the man from Ghent, followed by a cry. He longed for a father and hated the thought of losing him.

他向自己发誓，时机成熟时，无论肩负多少责任，他都会竭尽全力做一个好父亲、好丈夫。

He vowed to himself that, when the time came, he would do everything in his power to be a father and husband despite his responsibilities.

 

 

 

 

我要结婚了。

—I'm going to get married.

伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥感到胸口一阵剧痛，但她依然保持直立，脸上只有惊讶的神色。夜色已深，房间里光线昏暗。她们俩都喜欢这种昏暗的氛围；这让她们能够装出一副镇定自若的样子。

Isabel Osorio felt a blow to her chest, but she remained upright, her face reflecting nothing but surprise. It was night, and her room was barely lit. They both appreciated the dimness; it allowed them to feign composure.

“我祝贺你。”她回答道。

—I congratulate you —she replied.

——我的未婚妻是葡萄牙公主，我的表弟玛丽亚·曼努埃拉。

—My fiancée is the Infanta of Portugal, my cousin Maria Manuela.

那位女士默默地点了点头。她从未感到如此强烈的想哭的冲动。她后悔自己的软弱，后悔自从初吻后他们一天也没有分开过，后悔浪费了那么多时间沉浸在彼此的爱慕中，后悔他们之间心照不宣的默契，后悔他们之间竟然没有一丝一毫的不快。她不得不承受的打击——他与另一个女人结婚——似乎早已注定在费利佩的命运之中。她无法责怪他。

The lady nodded silently. She had never felt such a strong urge to cry. She regretted her weakness, the fact that they hadn't stopped seeing each other for a single day since their first kiss, the time wasted gazing at each other with rapture, the complicity in their conversations, the fact that there hadn't been even a second of unhappiness between them. The blow she had to bear—his marriage to another woman—had been written in Felipe's destiny since birth. She couldn't blame him.

现在我必须专注于我作为摄政王和丈夫的职责。

—Now I must focus on my duties as regent and husband.

你这是在浪费口舌。没必要解释。咱们各自回到自己的位置上去吧。

—You're wasting words. There's no need to explain. Let's both take our rightful places.

年轻女子为他打开门，让他离开，并向他鞠了一躬。

The young woman opened the door for him to leave. She bowed to him.

晚上好，殿下。

—Good evening, Your Highness.

他点了点头。正当他要跨过门槛时，他转过身面对她。

He nodded. As he was about to cross the threshold, he turned to face her.

你给了我生命中最快乐的时光。

—You have given me the happiest moments of my life.

她不知为何保持了镇定。

Without knowing how, she maintained her composure.

“与你未来的幸福相比，这些都算不了什么，”他临别时说道。

"They will be nothing compared to your future happiness," he said as a farewell.

 

 

 

 

几天后，费利佩一时冲动，明知这有悖常理，还是去了情人的寝宫寻找，却一无所获。他向妹妹玛丽亚询问情人的下落，玛丽亚告诉他，那位女士已经决定离开宫廷。这位继承人试图逃避现实，全身心投入到摄政的职责中；他的父亲已经离去，还有许多事情需要处理。他一度对伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥的决定感到庆幸；这或许是结束这段荒唐恋情的唯一办法。然而，无论他如何努力，都无法集中精力工作。他的思绪总是萦绕着她。

A few days later, Felipe, acting on an impulse he knew defied logic, searched for his lover in her bedchamber, but in vain. When he asked his sister María about her, she informed him that the lady had decided to leave the court. The heir tried to escape by throwing himself into his duties as regent; his father had already departed, and there were many matters to attend to. For a moment, he was grateful for Isabel Osorio's decision; it was the only way this senseless affair would finally end. However, try as he might, he couldn't concentrate on his work. His mind kept dwelling on her.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在法国，蒙莫朗西亲眼目睹了他的君主又一次鲁莽行事。得知皇帝打算亲自率军出征后，这位法国君主也决定效仿。顾问试图劝阻他；很明显，如果弗朗西斯以他现在的状态奔赴战场，死期将至。但一切都无济于事。亨利王子的恳求也未能动摇他父亲的决心。

Meanwhile, in France, Montmorency witnessed yet another act of recklessness from his lord. Having learned that the emperor intended to lead his troops, the French monarch had decided he would do the same. The advisor tried to dissuade him; it was clear that if Francis went down to the battlefield in his condition, death would soon claim him. But it was no use. Nor could Prince Henry's pleas sway his father.

—我宁愿战死沙场，也不愿留下来思考这无休止的葬礼，这便是我现在的人生。

—I'd rather die on horseback than stay and contemplate this endless funeral that is now my existence.

事实上，蒙莫朗西从未想过他的主人会卧床不起直至咽下最后一口气。这种毫无意义的死亡之旅，似乎更符合他的性格。

In truth, Montmorency had never imagined his master languishing in bed until his last breath. This senseless ride towards death seemed more in keeping with his character.

 

 

 

 

不久，顾问便置身于塞里索勒斯的一片平原上。黎明破晓，空气中弥漫着即将到来的战斗的紧张气氛。弗朗西斯从帐篷里出来，与他会合。两人一同环顾四周。君主面容憔悴，但身上的盔甲使他看起来仍然是一位能够统领众人的领袖。

It wasn't long before the advisor found himself on a plain in Cerisoles. Dawn was breaking, and the air crackled with the anticipation of the impending battle. Francis emerged from his tent and joined him. Together they scanned the surroundings. The monarch's face was gaunt, but the armor he wore made him appear a man still capable of commanding others.

——胜利必将属于我们。苏莱曼的支持使我们坚不可摧。

—Victory will be ours. Suleiman's support makes us unbreakable.

蒙莫朗西点了点头；他早就不再问国王，如果他们与异教徒结盟，死后会受到怎样的审判。

Montmorency nodded; he had long since stopped asking the king what judgment awaited them in the afterlife if they allied themselves with the infidel.

“跟我来，”国王继续说道，“和我一起享受胜利的前夜吧。”

—Come with me—the monarch continued.—Enjoy with me the eve of victory.

他们漫步在军队的帐篷之间。士兵们看到他们经过，立刻立正，其中大多数年轻而惊恐。议员感到内疚，因为他知道他们中的一些人会在这场战斗中丧命，而这场战斗的唯一目的似乎只是为了平息君主的怒火。然而，君主似乎并未意识到这份责任。他很久以来第一次挺直了腰杆行走，虽然他体态臃肿，看起来并不健康，但却突然间比往年都精神焕发。“他唯一的精神支柱就是战胜查理的希望，”蒙莫朗西心想。这位警长知道，如果他们无法取得胜利，弗朗西斯恐怕很难再有精力享受这样的时刻了。或许，他正在见证君主生命最后的辉煌。

They strolled among the tents of their troops. The soldiers snapped to attention as they passed, most of them young and frightened. The councilor felt guilty knowing that some of them would lose their lives in a fight whose sole purpose was to sate the sovereign's resentment. However, the sovereign seemed unaware of this responsibility. For the first time in a long time, he walked upright, and although he lacked the weight to appear healthy, he suddenly looked better than he had in years. "His sustenance is the hope of defeating Charles," Montmorency thought. The constable knew that if victory did not fall to them, there was little chance that Francis would have the energy to enjoy another such occasion. Perhaps he was witnessing the last moments of his lord's vitality.

然而，命运似乎并不打算让法国国王凯旋而归。太阳刚升至正午，就有一名信使出现在指挥部前，报告说帝国军队的规模远超预期，因为他们并非孤军奋战：凯撒的军队与英国军队汇合，他们正向法军阵地猛攻。

But fate did not see fit for the French king to depart on a high note. No sooner had the sun reached its zenith than a messenger appeared before the command to report that the imperial forces were far larger than expected, for they were not fighting alone: ​​the Caesar's troops were joined by the English, and all of them were rushing upon the French positions.

顾问急切地看着弗朗西斯。

The advisor looked at Francis with urgency.

除了撤退别无选择！

—There is no other option but retreat!

国王的紧张情绪战胜了他。他拒绝改变自己早已为当天准备好的剧本。

The king's nerves got the better of him. He refused to change the script his mind had already written for that day.

“我绝不会像个吓坏了的老太太一样逃跑！”国王咆哮道，“把我的马牵来！”

"I will never run away like a frightened old woman!" roared the king. "Bring me my horse!"

那就这样吧。但愿它能引导你走向与敌人截然相反的方向！

—So be it. But may it lead you in the opposite direction from the enemy!

—你对我这么不信任吗？

—Do you have so little trust in me?

蒙莫朗西的眼神再也无法欺骗他的君主。弗朗西斯从他的眼神中看到了他的败落。他停顿片刻，沉思片刻，但那一眼已然注定了他的命运。面纱落下，露出了无能为力的君主。

Montmorency's eyes could no longer deceive his lord. Francis saw his downfall in them. He paused for a moment to reflect, but that look had just sealed his fate. The veil had fallen, revealing a powerless monarch.

 

 

 

 

尽管法军撤退，查理一世仍拒绝继续作战。他厌倦了与英格兰国王亨利八世周旋的种种困难，更厌倦了维持战争所需的巨额开支。最终，双方在克雷皮签署了和平条约。这份条约的签署毫无诚意可言：法军和英帝国军队都未能从中获得任何好处，除了恢复到战前状态。如果说这份条约有什么意义的话，那就是它表明了将这场由来已久的仇恨延续到最终的悲剧结局是徒劳的。

Despite the French withdrawal, Charles refused to continue fighting. He was weary of the difficulty of dealing with Henry of England, and above all, of the enormous expense of maintaining the war effort. Peace was signed at Crepy. It was an agreement sealed without enthusiasm: neither the French nor the Imperial forces gained anything from it, beyond a return to the pre-war conditions. If it served any purpose, it was to demonstrate the futility of carrying that long-standing enmity to its bitter end.

 

 

 

 

在西班牙，战争的结束带来了一丝解脱。如今已是摄政王的菲利普，无法忍受王国如此被榨干，只为资助他父亲好战的野心。至少，他的顾问们给予了他些许慰藉：阿尔瓦公爵，他才智过人，意志坚定；塔韦拉枢机主教，他能妥善处理宗教事务；还有格朗维尔，一位与王位继承人年龄相仿、为王室孜孜不倦效力的政治家。尽管需要他们的帮助，菲利普却始终无法摆脱父亲在对法开战前写给他的那句话：“不要相信任何人。”他对皇帝的疑虑并未削弱他建议的权威性。王位继承人当时还只是个初出茅庐的君主，实际上，他真正重视的只有查理的判断。

In Spain, the end of the war was met with relief. Philip, now regent, could not bear to see his kingdoms bled dry in this way to finance his father's warlike whims. At least he found solace in his distress in the support of his advisors: the Duke of Alba, with his intelligence and unwavering resolve; Cardinal Tavera, who competently handled matters of faith; and Granvelle, a statesman closer to the heir in age and who worked tirelessly for the Crown. Despite needing their help, Philip was haunted daily by the words his father had written to him on the way to war against France: "Trust no one." The unease he felt toward the emperor had not diminished the authority of his recommendations. The heir was still a fledgling ruler, and in reality, he only truly valued Charles's judgment.

然而，这一标准在一个问题上并没有起到预期的效果：那就是这位年轻人与葡萄牙的玛丽亚·曼努埃拉的婚姻。

This criterion, however, did not have the desired effect on one issue: the marriage of the young man to Maria Manuela of Portugal.

 

 

 

 

尽管菲利普接受了这桩婚事，也接受了与一位陌生人结合的不确定性，但他仍然抱有与她相伴幸福的希望。他从小就目睹父母的爱情，渴望拥有他们那样的幸福。他无数次听过皇帝们相爱的故事：伊莎贝拉和查理一见面，就知道彼此是命中注定。因此，当他遇到玛丽亚·曼努埃拉时，菲利普深感失望。这位年轻女子温柔迷人，无疑是带着让丈夫幸福的目的而来；但她却未能激起这位王位继承人的激情。

Although Philip had accepted the marriage and with it the uncertainty of uniting with a stranger, he still held out hope of being happy by her side. He had grown up witnessing the love between his parents and longed for the same fortune they had enjoyed. He had heard countless times the tale of the emperors' falling in love: the moment they met, Isabella and Charles knew they were made for each other. For this reason, when he met Maria Manuela, Philip was deeply disappointed. The young woman was kind and charming, and she undoubtedly came with the intention of making her husband happy; but she stirred no passion in the heir.

“这和我预想的完全不一样，”他一看到格兰维拉走进宫殿庭院就向她坦白道。

"It's not what I expected," he confessed to Granvela as soon as he saw her enter the palace courtyard.

——殿下，您还指望什么呢？

—And what did you expect, Your Highness?

摄政王沉思片刻。顾问察觉到年轻人已经找到了答案，却拒绝透露。

The regent pondered it. The advisor sensed that the young man had found the answer but refused to reveal it.

——大人，世上只会有一个像您母亲那样的人。

—There will only ever be one like your mother, my lord.

费利佩对这番话很不高兴，径直走向他的未婚妻。她带着一大群人马簇拥着到来。他走近她时，失望之情愈发强烈。说实话，玛丽亚·曼努埃拉并不畸形，甚至也不丑，但她缺乏魅力。对于一个曾经坠入爱河的人来说，接受一段毫无激情的婚姻简直难以忍受。他暗自咒骂自己，当初就不该遇见伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥，也不该和她一起体验欲望的魔力。

Felipe, displeased by the comment, went ahead to greet his fiancée, who arrived surrounded by an imposing entourage. As he approached her, his disappointment grew. To tell the truth, María Manuela wasn't deformed, nor was she even ugly, but she lacked charm. And for someone who had once been in love, resigning himself to a union devoid of enthusiasm was an unbearable prospect. He cursed himself for having met Isabel Osorio and, with her, the magic of desire.

他对新来的客人打招呼时，语气有些机械。

His greeting to the newcomer had something mechanical about it.

很高兴见到你。

—It's a pleasure to meet you.

然而，他的未婚妻似乎对他的好运感到​​非常高兴。

His fiancée, however, seemed delighted with his luck.

“这段旅程虽然漫长，但绝对值得，”她双眼闪闪发光地说。

"The journey has been long, but it has certainly been worth it," she said with radiant eyes.

费利佩试图以绅士的姿态回应，但失望让他失去了幽默感。他的沉默震耳欲聋。

Felipe tried to respond with a gallant gesture, but the disappointment had dulled his wit. His silence was deafening.

“我让你失望了。”年轻女子指着他，脸上带着一丝悲伤的微笑。

"I have disappointed you." The young woman pointed at him with a sad smile.

摄政王深感愧疚。

The regent was overcome with guilt.

—说实话，我以为你会更高一些。

—To tell you the truth, I imagined you were taller.

这句话让继承人笑了。

The comment made the heir smile.

“但我恐怕我们的意愿并不重要，”她继续说道，“他们已经替我们做了决定。”

—But I'm afraid our wishes don't matter much—she continued. —They've already decided for us.

 

 

 

 

伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥试图将费利佩与葡萄牙公主的婚礼当天过得像往常一样，但徒劳无功。此前，她一直都能平静地忍受着他的缺席。只有在清晨，当她不得不鼓起勇气面对又一个没有他的日子时，忧郁才会袭来。然而，那天，当她看到街道上为婚礼装点一新，听到人们谈论的都是这对新人时，她感到心神不宁，几乎要病倒了。她回到住处，试图不去想婚礼的事，但这并没有消除她的焦虑。她尝试用读书和刺绣来分散注意力，但她的眼睛无法阅读，双手也无法动弹，最终她只能坐在扶手椅上，目光呆滞地望着前方，无奈地接受着这一天只能默默承受痛苦的现实。夜晚，她辗转反侧，难以入眠。这位年轻的女子不禁怀疑，这种不安是否会永远伴随着她，因为它既没有消退，也没有减轻。

Isabel Osorio tried in vain to live the day of Felipe's wedding to the Portuguese Infanta as if it were any other. Until then, she had borne his absence with composure. Melancholy only visited her in the mornings, when she had to find the strength to face another day without him. However, that day, when she saw the streets adorned for the wedding and heard people talking of nothing but the couple, she felt unsettled, almost ill. She returned to her residence to avoid thinking about the wedding, but that did not erase her agitation. She tried to distract herself with reading and embroidery, but neither her eyes could read nor her hands capable of any movement, so she ended up sitting in an armchair, staring straight ahead, resigned to spending the day doing nothing but suffering. The night did not lull her to sleep. The young woman wondered if this unease would be with her forever, because it neither subsided nor diminished.

凌晨时分，她还没睡，就听到了敲门声。她吓了一跳，以为自己疯了。但她又听到了敲门声，于是凭着直觉，跑去开门。

She was still awake in the early hours of the morning when she heard the knocking. She was frightened: she thought she had lost her mind. But she heard it again, and then, seized by a hunch, she ran to open the door.

是他。

It was him.

——就在这里？在你的新婚之夜？

—Here? On your wedding night?

—如果你不收留我，我也能理解。我没有骗你：我已经尽到了对妻子的义务。

—I would understand if you didn't take me in. I'm not deceiving you: I have fulfilled my obligations to my wife.

一片寂静，但他们谁也没有动一下。

There was silence, but none of them moved an inch.

“他们说他爱你，”她说。

"They say he loves you," she said.

费利佩沉默了。他仔细端详着伊莎贝尔的脸，久违的凝视让他仿佛要将她的脸吞噬。感受到他的目光，这位年轻女子察觉到自己的不安已然转化为另一种情绪：一种想要臣服于他的强烈渴望。或许，她原本就从未有过别的感受。

Felipe fell silent. He scanned Isabel's face, devouring it after so long without having gazed upon it. Feeling that gaze, the young woman noticed how her unease transformed into something else: an overwhelming desire to surrender to him. Perhaps it had never been anything else.

“她给你的还不够吗？”她问他。

"Isn't what she has given you enough?" she asked him.

他否认了。

He denied it.

我想要更多。我想要你。

—I want more. I want you.

伊莎贝尔知道，如果她放任不管，这样的场景每晚都会重演。她四处寻找那座堡垒，想要关上大门。但还没等她找到，他就走上前去吻了她，这吻注定了他们两人的命运。

Isabel knew that if she let it go, the scene would repeat itself every night. She searched for the fortress to close the door. But before she could find it, he moved forward and kissed her, condemning them both.

 

 

 

 

与法国缔结和平后，皇帝很快抵达帝国。斐迪南的宫廷竭尽全力欢迎他；查理与他哥哥之间的紧张关系似乎已彻底化解。离开战场后，皇帝奔赴宴会、舞会和畅饮啤酒的场合。欢庆的气氛麻痹了他的忧郁。这并非他在战争中获得的那种活力，而是一种截然不同的精神慰藉，一种来自轻松交谈和微醺的宁静。查理沉浸在持续不断的庆祝活动中。他知道伤口不会因此痊愈，但有时，至少伤口不再像往常那样疼痛，对他来说就足够了。

Soon the emperor arrived in the Empire, having secured peace with France. Ferdinand's court went to great lengths to welcome him; the tensions between Charles and his brother seemed to have been definitively left behind. From the battlefield, the emperor went to banquets, dances, and rivers of beer. The festive atmosphere numbed his melancholy. It was not like the vigor he found in war, but rather a different kind of tranquility for his spirit, the kind that comes from light conversation and intoxication. Charles immersed himself in a cloud of continuous celebrations. He knew his wounds wouldn't heal that way, but sometimes it was enough for him that they didn't hurt as much as usual.

在一次庆典上，喧闹的谈笑声中，皇帝听到一首歌仿佛从天际传来；歌声来自芭芭拉·布隆伯格，一位容貌妩媚、气质自信的年轻女子。早已失去理智的皇帝被她的歌声深深吸引，仿佛置身于一个没有痛苦的世界。自从丧妻以来一直伴随他的悲伤，此刻也随之消散。那一刻，他的人生不再是一条封闭的下坡路，而是一片开阔、未知的平原。

At one of the celebrations, amidst the bustle of conversation and laughter, the emperor heard a song that seemed to rise from a corner of the sky; it came from Barbara Blomberg, a young woman of sensual beauty and confident bearing. The emperor, who had long since lost his sobriety, was mesmerized by her voice. He felt transported to a place where pain had no place. The sadness that had accompanied him since becoming a widower was momentarily suspended. For an instant, his life did not seem like a closed, downward path, but an open, still unexplored plain.

这位女士察觉到自己的歌声对皇帝产生了影响。她举止优雅，表演结束后便上前与皇帝会合。

The lady noticed the impact her singing had had on the emperor. As poised as she was, she approached him after her performance.

陛下，希望我的表现令您满意。

—Your Majesty, I hope I have pleased you.

距离的增加并没有减弱女孩的魅力；她身上散发着一种难以摆脱的魔力。

The proximity did not diminish the girl's appeal; she possessed a magical aura that was difficult to escape.

“我好像看到上帝在听你说话，”他回答说。

—I thought I saw God listening to you —he replied.

芭芭拉·布隆伯格目不转睛地盯着凯撒，仿佛他是一尊雕像，目光专注而毫无保留。凯撒对她如此大胆的举动感到惊喜不已。

Barbara Blomberg gazed at the Caesar as if he were a statue, intently and without restraint. He was pleasantly surprised by such audacity.

“能亲眼见到你而不是在画作或挂毯上见到你，真是令人印象深刻，”她说。

"It's impressive to see you in person and not in paintings or tapestries," she said.

“就我个人而言，我希望画作能永葆青春，”他开玩笑说。

"For myself, I would like the eternal youth of paintings," he joked.

他们彼此凝视了一会儿，就被其他宾客的打扰分散了注意力。卡洛斯随后失去了她的踪影，但她却在他脑海中萦绕了一整晚。很久以来，没有什么能像她一样让他感到如此惊喜。

They held each other's gaze just long enough for other guests to distract them. Carlos lost sight of her then, but she remained in his mind for the rest of the evening. Nothing had surprised him like that woman in a long time.

 

 

 

 

沉浸于酒宴和盛大庆典营造的虚假欢乐之中，皇帝对宫廷内早已暗流涌动的事实浑然不觉。与法国的和平协议确认了皇帝对米兰的继承权，马克西米利安得知此事后，便将米兰公国视为自己应得的奖赏。这虽无法弥补他被排除在皇位继承之外的屈辱，但至少可以抚慰他受伤的自尊。

Numbed by the artificial merriment of drink and pageantry, the emperor remained oblivious to the fact that tempers at court were far from calm. The peace with France had confirmed the emperor's rights to Milan, and as soon as he learned of this, Maximilian considered the duchy his just reward. It wouldn't compensate for the slight of having been excluded from the imperial succession, but it would at least soothe his wounded pride.

“我的儿子将接管米兰公国，”卡洛斯在一次宴会上说道。

—My son will take charge of the Duchy of Milan—Carlos remarked in the middle of one of the many banquets.

他脱口而出，全然不知马克西米利安的野心。马克西米利安相信，当晚余下的时间里，他会被授予某个职位，即便价值稍低。他期待皇帝能对他或他父亲表示感谢。但查理除了授予菲利普公爵爵位之外，没有提及任何其他奖励，无论是当晚还是接下来的几个晚上。费迪南的儿子开始显露出不满：他的举止变得粗鲁，言辞也越来越尖锐。他的父亲察觉到了儿子日益增长的怒火。一天晚上，马克西米利安似乎即将爆发，费迪南找了个借口把他带离了正在用餐的大厅。到了隔壁房间的僻静之处，他向儿子开口说道。

He confessed it spontaneously, unaware of Maximilian's ambitions. Maximilian trusted that, at some point during the remainder of the evening, he would be named the beneficiary of some other post, even if it were of lesser value. He expected a gesture of gratitude from the emperor, either toward him or toward his father. But Charles mentioned no reward other than the dukedom for Philip, neither that night nor during the nights that followed. Ferdinand's son's frustration began to materialize: his gestures became brusque and his comments increasingly sharp. His father sensed this growing anger. One night, when Maximilian seemed on the verge of exploding, Ferdinand invented an excuse to take him away from the hall where dinner was being held. Once in the seclusion of an adjoining room, he addressed his son.

—冷静点！你们这样只会让自己看起来很愚蠢！

—Calm down! You're making yourselves look foolish!

“他是不是瞧不起我们？你是不是只想着别惹他不高兴？”年轻人认为父亲对凯撒的忠诚不过是顺从。“他什么都没给我们！他的一切都属于腓力！你哥哥是个忘恩负义的家伙，不配得到效忠。”

"Does he despise us, and is your only concern not to upset him?" The young man perceived his father's loyalty to Caesar as mere submission. "He hasn't given us a single thing! Everything he owns is and will be for Philip! Your brother is an ungrateful wretch who doesn't deserve loyalty."

费尔南多忧心忡忡地看着儿子。儿子的激烈举动令他感到害怕。

Fernando regarded his son with apprehension. His vehemence frightened him.

——我说的都是您心里想的，神父。我说的这些话，正是您因为所谓的忠诚而一直隐藏起来的，而所谓​​的忠诚，其实不过是懦弱罢了。

—I'm not saying anything you don't already think, Father. My words express what you keep hidden because of what you call fidelity, which is nothing but cowardice.

马克西米利安不等父亲回答便离开了。查理的弟弟独自一人待了一会儿。从大厅里，他能听到宴会上人们的笑声，听起来虚伪而自满。“和谐建立在谎言之上，”他心想。从这个意义上讲，儿子说得没错：他之所以能活到四十岁而没有反抗哥哥，部分原因在于他为了家族和帝国的利益而压抑了自己的不满。查理显然没有给予他们应得的补偿：他居高临下地看待他们，理所当然地认为无论发生什么，他们都会继续为他效力。费迪南知道，正是他自己允许这种情况发生的。每次他扬言要反抗，最终都以退缩告终。但很明显，他多年来积攒的怨恨并没有消失；它只是找到了另一个寄托，一个比他自己更有勇气、更少顾忌的容器：马克西米利安的。

Maximilian left before his father could reply. Charles's brother was left alone for a moment. From the hall, he could hear the laughter of those enjoying the banquet, which sounded artificial and complacent. "Concord is built on lies," he thought. In that sense, his son wasn't wrong: if he had reached forty without rebelling against his brother, it was partly because he had suppressed his discontent for the good of the family and the Empire. Charles had certainly not compensated them as they deserved: he regarded them condescendingly, taking it for granted that, whatever happened, they would remain at his service. Ferdinand knew that he had allowed it to be so. Every time he had threatened to rebel, he had ended up backing down. But it was clear that the bile he had accumulated over the years hadn't evaporated; it had merely sought another vessel in which to lodge itself, one with more courage and fewer scruples than his own: Maximilian's.

 

 

 

 

一切都发生在当晚。芭芭拉·布隆伯格再次出现在宫廷宴会上，查尔斯像往常一样被啤酒迷得神志不清，跟着她四处走动。醉意让他几乎不知道自己在做什么。第二天，他只能依稀记得当晚发生的事情：她的笑声指引着他穿过走廊，她在私人房间里为他唱的歌的片段，以及她年轻身体的温暖让他得以拥抱她。“让我试着抚慰你的悲伤，”她说。

It all happened that same night. Barbara Blomberg reappeared at a palace party, and Charles, as bewildered by beer as usual, followed her wherever she led him. His intoxication barely allowed him to know what he was doing. The next day, he would only recall fleeting glimpses of what had happened: her laughter guiding him through the corridors, fragments of the song she sang to him in a private room, the warmth of that young body that allowed him to embrace her. "Let me try to ease your sadness," she had said.

在皇帝接受安慰之际，马克西米利安在一位德国王子的宫殿一隅，与那些钦佩他决心的人交谈。谈话以握手告终，这握手也促成了一个冒险的决定。斐迪南的儿子第一次感到自己举足轻重，觉得自己参与了一项将改变帝国命运的伟大事业。

While the emperor was being consoled, Maximilian, in a discreet corner of a German prince's palace, conversed with men who admired his resolve. The conversation ended with handshakes that sealed a risky decision. For the first time, Ferdinand's son felt important, part of something that would change the destiny of the Empire.

在那夜一切似乎皆有可能之后的第二天早晨，卡洛斯在一间陈腐的卧室里醒来。他努力理解自己为何赤身裸体地躺在一个陌生人身边。酒精的作用不再像之前那样带来平静的麻木感，而是伴随着身体上的不适，尤其是精神上的不适。他的意识不再迷离，而是再次变得敏锐而刺痛。他默默地穿好衣服，衣服上还残留着啤酒的味道，凯撒哀叹自己不像其他男人。他多么希望拥有他们的冷漠，他们的遗忘能力，他们能够沉溺于千百种享乐而不自欺欺人。然而，他将永远背负着丧妻的重担。这甚至不是他刻意为之；他只是依然深爱着伊莎贝尔，即使她已经死去。离开房间前，他瞥了一眼芭芭拉·布隆伯格。睡梦中的她比清醒时更加美丽；静谧的姿态让她宛如一座饱含细腻情感的雕像。卡洛斯没有吵醒她，只是轻轻吻了吻她的手。回到房间后，凯撒下定决心，以后再也不用酒精和狂欢麻痹自己了。在试图逃避之后，回归真相变得更加艰难。他必须接受自己的现实：一个爱上幽灵的人，也正因如此，他再也无法真正快乐。

The morning after that night when everything seemed possible, Carlos awoke in a stale bedroom. He struggled to understand what he was doing naked beside a stranger. The effects of the alcohol no longer resembled a placid cloud of insensitivity, but were accompanied by physical and, above all, spiritual discomfort. His consciousness was no longer suspended; it was once again sharp and piercing. As he dressed in silence, in clothes that smelled of beer, the Caesar lamented not being like other men. He would have liked to possess their coldness, their capacity to forget, to surrender to a thousand pleasures without feeling they were deceiving themselves. He, however, would always bear the burden of his widowhood. It wasn't even a conscious decision; he was simply still in love with Isabel, even though she was dead. Before leaving the room, he glanced at Barbara Blomberg. Asleep, the girl was even more beautiful than when awake; The stillness made her resemble a statue sculpted with sensitivity. Carlos, without waking her, kissed her hand. As he returned to his chamber, the Caesar resolved never again to numb himself with drink and revelry. The return to truth was all the harder after trying to avoid it. He would accept what he was: a man who loved a ghost and who, because of it, would never again be truly happy.

 

 

 

 

相比之下，菲利普在卡斯蒂利亚的生活则截然不同：只有和伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥在一起时，他才感觉自己像个真正的自己。他和玛丽亚·曼努埃拉的婚姻充其量只是一段愉快的友谊。这位葡萄牙女人并没有自欺欺人：她知道丈夫不爱她，而且与另一个女人有染，她也无奈地接受了这个事实；毕竟，她的处境虽然令人不快，但也并非什么稀奇事。她甚至觉得自己很幸运：尽管菲利普不爱她，但他对她却无可挑剔，这是许多被欺骗的女人都无法做到的。

In contrast, Philip lived a very different reality in Castile: he only felt like himself when he was with Isabel Osorio. His marriage to Maria Manuela was little more than a pleasant friendship. The Portuguese woman didn't deceive herself: she knew her husband didn't love her and was sleeping with another woman, and she had accepted the fact with resignation; after all, her situation seemed unpleasant but nothing extraordinary. She even considered herself fortunate: although Philip didn't love her, he behaved impeccably toward her, something many deceived women couldn't say.

 

 

 

 

不久，她便怀孕了。玛丽亚·曼努埃拉欣喜若狂，不仅因为她将履行为皇帝继承人诞下儿子的职责，更因为她相信，有了这个孩子，她就能获得丈夫从未给予她的真爱。孩子需要她，在她离开时会哭泣。想到自己对某人而言如此重要，这位年轻女子不禁心生感动。

The pregnancy soon followed. María Manuela received the news with joy, not only because she would fulfill her duty of bearing a son for the emperor's heir, but also because with this child she could establish the genuine love her husband denied her. The baby would need her, would cry whenever she left. The young woman was moved thinking how wonderful it would be to feel important to someone.

 

 

 

 

在临产前的几天，眼看就要生产了，费利佩却一直没有去看望伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥。尽管他觉得自己无法放弃情人，但他始终无法彻底摆脱婚外情的罪恶感。他的妻子一直爱着他，而他却无法回应这份爱，这让他痛苦不堪。他觉得玛丽亚·曼努埃拉是个迷人的年轻女子。如果她是朋友或姐妹，他一定会非常爱她。在分娩前夜全心全意地照顾她，让他稍微平静了一些。

In the days leading up to the birth, when it seemed imminent, Felipe refrained from visiting Isabel Osorio. Although he felt incapable of giving up his lover, he had never felt entirely free of guilt for his adultery. His wife had always loved him, and it devastated him to perceive it and not be able to reciprocate. He found María Manuela to be a charming young woman. He would have adored her had she been a friend, or a sister. Devoting himself to her care on the eve of the delivery calmed him somewhat.

 

 

 

 

婴儿终于降生，宫廷里一片欢腾：是个健康的男婴，继承权有了保障。骄傲的父亲毫不犹豫地为儿子取名：卡洛斯。

When the baby finally arrived, the court erupted in jubilation: it was a healthy infant, and a boy at that. The succession was assured. The proud father had no hesitation in choosing his name: his son would be called Carlos.

但喜悦转瞬即逝：物理学家们宣布玛丽亚·曼努埃拉无法在分娩中幸存下来。

But the joy was short-lived: the physicists declared that María Manuela would not survive childbirth.

菲利普被即将到来的悲剧震惊了，他请求陪伴妻子走完人生的最后一程。这位年轻的女子弥留之际，几乎没有力气向他道谢。皇帝的儿子感觉自己陷入了一场可怕的噩梦：在查理曾经居住的地方，他仿佛又一次经历了母亲的死亡。

Philip, stunned by the imminence of the tragedy, asked to be with his wife in her final hours. The young woman, dying, barely had the strength to thank him. The son of the emperor felt trapped in a macabre nightmare: he was reliving, in the place once occupied by Charles, his mother's death.

“我的路到此结束了。”她低声说道。

"My path ends here," she whispered.

丈夫心中充满了愧疚。那个女孩就这样带着遗憾离开了人世，从未感受过爱。

Guilt struck her husband. That girl was going to leave this world without ever having been loved.

——我的职责已经完成，我即将离开。请照顾好我们的儿子，给他我一直没时间给予他的爱。

—I'm leaving with my duty fulfilled. Take care of our son. Give him the love I haven't had time to offer him.

费利佩注意到她已陷入沉思。他凝视着妻子的容貌，仿佛是第一次见到她。他从她唇形和眼线中感受到一丝温柔。然而，在他还没来得及将她的容颜牢牢记住之前，那张脸就会变得如同石头一般。

Felipe noticed that her gaze was already lost in thought. He contemplated his wife's features as if for the first time. He found sweetness in the shape of her lips and the lines of her eyes. That face would turn to stone before he had even memorized it.

“请原谅我，求求您原谅我。”摄政王眼眶含泪。

"Forgive me, I beg you. Forgive me." The regent was on the verge of tears.

玛丽亚·曼努埃拉随后要求见她的儿子，但她还没来得及抱住他便去世了。

María Manuela then asked to see her son, but she died before she could hold him in her arms.

 

 

 

 

死神似乎并不满足于带走这位葡萄牙女子：仅仅几天后，在筹备这位年轻女子的葬礼时，塔韦拉枢机主教也驾崩了。整个宫廷陷入了哀悼和绝望之中。

Death was not content with taking the Portuguese woman: just a few days later, while preparing the young woman's funeral, Cardinal Tavera died. The court went into mourning and was plunged into a spirit of despair.

费利佩随后写信给父亲：他需要父亲陪伴在身边。尽管他表面上在所有人面前表现得坚强，默默承受着接踵而至的悲剧，但事实上，他正在经历着一些他始料未及的全新情感。

Felipe then wrote to his father: he needed him by his side. Although he had managed to appear to everyone that he was bearing the accumulation of tragedies with fortitude, the truth was that he was experiencing new emotions for which he did not feel prepared.

但当他收到信时，皇帝已无暇顾及任何事。突然间，德意志诸侯起兵反抗。斐迪南惊恐万分，因为他担忧帝国的未来，更重要的是，他怀疑挑起叛乱的叛徒正是他的儿子。

But by the time he received his letter, the emperor was in no position to attend to any matters. Suddenly, the German princes had risen up against him. Ferdinand received the uprising with panic, because he feared for the future of the Empire and, above all, because he suspected that the traitor who had provoked it was none other than his son.

15

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

法国国王弗朗索瓦一世迁居朗布依埃，是为了逃避死亡的预感。在此之前，宫廷曾辗转于贡比涅、圣日耳曼昂莱、利默尔和罗什福尔等皇家要塞，但国王始终未能找到他所寻求的安宁。他感到威胁的并非敌人或阴谋，而是自己的命运。正如他从未向查理屈服一样，他也无意向天命低头。他的身形已远不如从前，甚至不再祈求恢复往日的活力——那活力随着岁月和种种挫折逐渐消逝，直至彻底消失。尽管如此，弗朗索瓦一世仍不愿面对死亡。“有些人天生就不该死，”他躺在床上，日渐难以离开，心中如此想着。然而，他明白，这些想法与现实并不相符；死亡带走一切，无论显赫还是平庸，无论才华横溢还是默默无闻。这令他怒不可遏。“卓越理应抵御虚无！”他对自己说。他无法理解，为何达芬奇当年幸免于难，几个月前，英格兰的亨利八世也未能幸免。伟大并非盔甲，它只会让不可避免的死亡更加充满悖论。

Francis I of France moved to Rambouillet fleeing a premonition of death. Before settling there, the court had wandered through, among other royal sites, Compiègne, Saint-Germain-en-Laye, Limeurs, and Rochefort, but in none of them had the monarch found the security he sought. He felt threatened not by enemies or intrigues, but by his destiny, and just as he had never surrendered to Charles, neither did he intend to surrender to Providence. His figure was a frail version of what it had once been, and he no longer even prayed for the return of his former vigor, which he had gradually lost with the years and disappointments until it had completely faded. Despite everything, Francis was not prepared to contemplate his end. "There are men for whom death has no place," he thought in that bed which each day he found harder to leave. He knew, however, that these thoughts of his did not correspond to reality; That death takes away illustrious and mediocre alike, brilliant men and those whose existence has left no trace on the world. That infuriated him. "Excellence should protect against nothingness!" he told himself. He couldn't understand how life had spared Leonardo in his day or, a few months earlier, Henry of England. Greatness didn't serve as armor; it only made the inevitable more paradoxical.

在《克雷皮和约》签订后的几年里，这位法国君主比以往任何时候都更加沉迷于世俗享乐，这绝非夸张。他已无力继续征战，但他的心境却变得仁慈起来：他喜欢回忆自己统治时期的辉煌——他曾是法国文艺复兴的缔造者：他建造了雄伟的城堡，创建了图书馆，并赞助了伟大的艺术家。然而，有时，当他在宴会上翩翩起舞或与情人缠绵时，弗朗西斯会突然感到一阵空虚：这种空虚源于他意识到自己既没有实现梦寐以求的荣耀，也没有战胜敌人。

In the years following the signing of the Peace of Crepy, the French sovereign had devoted himself to worldly pleasures with even greater fervor than before, which is saying something. He no longer had the strength to continue fighting, but his mind had become benevolent: he liked to bring to mind the positive aspects of his reign—he had been the French Renaissance: he had built imposing castles, created libraries, and patronized great artists. However, sometimes, when he danced at parties or lay with a lover, Francis was momentarily overcome by a feeling of emptiness: the emptiness that came from remembering that he had neither achieved the glory he had dreamed of nor vanquished his enemy.

 

 

 

 

尽管害怕君主得知他病情后的反应，医生们最终还是放弃了希望。弗朗西斯科试图反抗判决，但他连反抗的力气都没有了。这时，他想起了母亲，想起了她死后会如何迎接他。无论在天堂还是地狱，他知道他们终会相遇，因为他们就像一对形影不离的双胞胎。他想象着母亲幽灵般高贵，在天堂里榨取着邻居们的钱财。当他们相遇时，路易莎会斥责他的失败，然后立刻将他拥入怀中，直到永远。

Although fearful of the monarch's reaction to his admission, the doctors ultimately gave him no hope. Francisco tried to rebel against the verdict, but he didn't even have the strength for that. He thought then of his mother, and how she would receive him in the afterlife. Whether in heaven or hell, he knew they would meet, for they were like two peas in a pod. He imagined her spectral yet imposing, fleecing her neighbors in paradise. When they met, Luisa would be able to scold him for his failures and then, immediately afterward, cradle him in her arms for all eternity.

但在与她相见之前，他必须先与留下的家人告别。他尽力梳理好头发后，吩咐他们到他面前来。几个小时后，他从一场高烧的午睡中醒来，发现埃莉诺、蒙莫朗西、玛格丽特和亨利围在他的床边，组成了一群悲伤的雕像。弗朗西斯被这在他房间里逐渐成形的陵墓景象深深震撼。

But before meeting her, he had to bid farewell to the family he was leaving behind. Once he had smoothed his hair as best he could, he ordered them to appear before him. Hours later, upon waking from a feverish nap, he noticed that Eleanor, Montmorency, Margaret, and Henry surrounded his bed. They formed a group of sorrowful statues. Francis was shaken by this sketch of a mausoleum that had taken shape in his chamber.

“请原谅我，”国王对莱昂诺尔说。

"Forgive me," the king said to Leonor.

卡洛斯的妹妹神情严肃，而非懊悔，她点了点头。

Carlos's sister, more serious than contrite, nodded.

“我很久以前就做过了，”女王回答说，“你可以安息了。”

—I did it a long time ago—replied the queen. You may rest in peace.

弗朗西斯筋疲力尽，眼皮耷拉着，向他道了谢。这时他才注意到蒙莫朗西，那人看起来就像是被活埋了一样。

Exhausted, Francis thanked him with a droop of his eyelids. He then noticed Montmorency, who already looked like he was being buried alive.

—我已尽我所能为您效劳，大人。

—I served you as well as I could, my lord.

国王怜悯他。他不否认自己曾痴心妄想，但也清楚自己的固执让这位警官多么疲惫不堪。这位顾问年纪虽不及他，却显得健康强壮。国王对他既羡慕又怜惜。

The monarch took pity on him. He didn't deny having chased pipe dreams, but he was aware of how much his stubbornness had worn down the constable's nerves. The advisor, who was no younger than he, nevertheless looked healthy and robust. The king envied him affectionately.

——求你继续效忠王室。或许……或许我应该多听听你的话。

—Continue serving the Crown, I beg you. Perhaps… perhaps I should have listened to you more.

蒙莫朗西和弗朗西斯科再也找不到合适的词语继续交谈。事实上，他们之间的一切早已在多年前说尽。他们日复一日地互相尊重、互相包容，将不满深藏心底，因为他们觉得那样做配不上彼此深厚的感情。

Montmorency and Francisco found no more words to continue their conversation. In truth, everything had already been said between them, years ago. They had respected and tolerated each other daily, keeping their grievances to themselves because they would have been unworthy of the affection they held for one another.

“我很高兴你一直是我的朋友。”君主低声说道。

—I am glad you have been my friend —murmured the monarch.

蒙莫朗西点了点头，动了动，目光转向窗外，透过窗户，他看到清晨的阳光刺眼得过分。他走过去，把窗帘完全拉上，想要掩盖住心中那份令人窒息的感觉。

Montmorency nodded and, moved, turned his gaze toward the window, through which he glimpsed an excessively bright morning. He went over to draw the curtains completely to hide his suffocating feeling.

国王随后向继承人求婚。亨利握了握他的手，然后在他身边坐下；那天他二十七岁。

The king then sought the hand of the heir. Henry shook it and sat down beside him; he was twenty-seven years old that day.

—我的儿子，王位将传给你。

—I give you the throne, my son.

年轻人强忍着泪水。的确，几个月来，他一直察觉到父亲的病情恶化，也一直在为这一刻做准备，但这似乎并没有什么用。那个对他来说意义非凡的人，正在他眼前一点点消逝。即使在争吵中，他也始终敬重着父亲。没有了父亲，未来似乎一片黯淡，充满未知。

The young man held back his tears. It was true that for months, aware of his father's decline, he had prepared himself for this moment, but it hadn't done him much good. The man who had meant everything to him was fading away before his eyes. Even in their clashes, he had revered him. Without him, the future seemed bleak and uncertain.

父亲，我向您保证，我所做的一切，至少也要成为您的影子。

—Father, I promise you that my endeavor will be nothing other than to be, at least, a shadow of you.

弗朗西斯科抚摸着恩里克的脸，他的脸庞如此年轻，却又如此憔悴。

Francisco caressed Enrique's face, so youthful and yet so afflicted.

“你就是我的胜利。你也要以此为荣。”儿子点点头，注意到父亲握紧了他的手，力道越来越大。“你休想停止削弱皇帝的权力。”

"You have been my victory. And as such you will act." The son nodded, and noticed how his father squeezed his hand with increasing firmness. "You will not cease in diminishing the emperor's power."

埃莉诺关切地听着丈夫的请求，却一言不发。蒙莫朗西却露出一丝怅然的微笑：如果他的主人在临终之际背叛了他，他会非常失望的。

Eleanor listened with concern to her husband's request, but said nothing. Montmorency, however, smiled wistfully: he would have been disappointed if his lord had betrayed himself in his final hour.

“除非你发誓，否则我不会安然离去。”国王问他的孩子。

"I will only leave in peace if you swear to it," the king asked his offspring.

然后，他用一种与其身份极不相称的坚定目光打量着继承人。

He then looked at the heir with a determination unbecoming of his station.

——我向您发誓，父亲。

—I swear to you, father.

弥留之际，君主亲吻了他的手。他似乎比以往任何时候都更加以亨利为荣。亨利注意到这一点，意识到自己一直以来多么渴望取悦父亲，以及自己多么觉得自己做得不够好。

As he lay dying, the monarch kissed his hand. He seemed prouder of Henry than he had ever been. The young man, noticing this, realized how much he had always needed to please his father and how little he believed he had succeeded.

 

 

 

 

弗朗西斯双目睁着，死时仍对自己的命运感到难以置信。法国顿时感到一阵异样。不久之后，这位国王，这位神话般的人物，这位虚荣的化身，这位野心勃勃的巨人，将被安葬在一座无疑宏伟壮丽的陵墓中，但那里却只有一片寂静。人们会哀悼他，缅怀他——战争与条约的日期，他的功绩，他的失误，他的爱情——但人们会逐渐遗忘他真正的为人，直至它最终凝固成永恒。

Francis died with his eyes open, incredulous at his fate. France suddenly felt strange. Soon the king, the myth, vanity personified, the towering figure of unbridled ambition, would be enclosed in a tomb undoubtedly magnificent, but one where nothing but silence would be heard. He would be mourned and remembered—dates of wars and treaties, feats, missteps, loves—but the memory of what he had truly been would gradually fade until it was petrified.

生活最终战胜了这个人，就像它一直以来所做的那样。

Life had won against the man, as it always did.

 

 

 

 

当王印从弗朗西斯手中取下时，他的手冰冷刺骨。王印被戴在他的手指上时，亨利感到一阵死亡的寒意。随后，他被披上了绣有鸢尾花图案的斗篷。立刻，朝臣们跪倒在他周围，臣服于他新获得的权力。这位年轻人以慈父般的目光注视着他们；大多数朝臣都比他年长，但他们是他的封臣，因此也是他的孩子，为了他们自身的利益和王室的利益，他必须征服他们。接着，卑微的男男女女走进了王宫。房间里挤满了畸形无力的手臂、皮肤肿胀的脸庞、失明者、坏疽患者，甚至还有神志不清、语无伦次的疯子。他们排成一列，队伍的尽头是亨利。这位新国王带着他厌恶之情中仅存的怜悯之心接纳了他们。他一个接一个地将带有王印的手放在他们身上：“我是国王；我治愈你们。”

Francis's hands were ice-cold when the royal seal was removed from him. As it was placed on his finger, Henry felt the chill of death. He was then dressed in the mantle embroidered with fleur-de-lis. Immediately, the court knelt around him, succumbing to his newfound power. The young man looked at them with a paternal air; most of the courtiers were older than him, but they were his vassals and, therefore, his children, whom he would have to subdue for their own good and that of the Crown. Then, humble men and women entered the royal hall. The room filled with deformed and useless arms, faces with swollen skin, blindness, gangrene, even the demented who babbled incoherently. They formed a line that ended with Henry. The new king received them with all the pity his revulsion allowed. One by one he laid his hand upon them, adorned with the seal: "I am the king; I heal you."

年轻人心想，从显赫的视角来看，一切都显得多么不同。他随即把目光转向埃莉诺，她正悄悄地观察着救济穷人的情景。在他看来，她也与以往不同。弗朗西斯去世后，这位前王后主动请缨，成为亨利的政务助手。但如果君主能够治病救人，难道他就不能背对皇帝，独自一人统治吗？

How different everything seemed from the perspective of grandeur, the young man thought. He then turned his gaze to Eleanor, who was discreetly observing the reception of the destitute. She, too, seemed different to him. Once Francis had died, the former queen had offered herself to Henry as an assistant in matters of government. But if the monarch could heal the sick, wouldn't he be capable of reigning alone, with his back turned to the emperor?

法国不再需要那个女人了，即便它曾经需要过。

France no longer needed that woman, if it ever had.

 

 

 

 

与此同时，在皇宫里，查理一动不动地站着，厌倦了这种死寂。

Meanwhile, at the Imperial court, Charles stood motionless and tired of the stillness.

“求求你们，饶了我吧。”他恳求道。

"Please, give me a break," he pleaded.

——难道是我在册封凯撒吗？

—Am I the one granting a Caesar?

皇帝和提香相视一笑。皇帝匆匆落座，提香则继续在纸上素描了一会儿，直到灵感枯竭。

The emperor and Titian smiled at each other. The former hurried to take his seat. The latter remained for a few more moments sketching on his papers, until his inspiration ran out.

比起你们的性格，我更感兴趣的是你们是如何经历这场战斗的。来自根特的男人邀请他坐到自己旁边，意大利人接受了邀请。“这一切是怎么发生的？”

"More than your personalities, I'm interested in how you experienced the battle." The man from Ghent invited him to sit beside him, which the Italian accepted. "How did it all happen?"

卡洛斯沉思了一会儿。痛风让他双脚火辣辣地疼，过了好一会儿他才有心情回忆往事。

Carlos pondered it. His feet burned from gout, and it took him a while to feel like reminiscing.

易北河将我们与新教诸侯的军队隔开。他们精心摧毁了连接两岸的桥梁。湍急的河水构成了一道难以逾越的障碍。对岸的敌人肆无忌惮地向我们叫嚣，扬言随时准备进攻。他们觉得我们之间仅存的这片水域足以让他们免受伤害。夜幕降临米尔贝格。敌人的叫喊声渐渐平息，我的训话清晰地传到了士兵们的耳中。我警告他们德国的命运岌岌可危。我还向他们讲述了上帝、帝国和命运。我看到他们眼中怒火中烧。他们紧紧握住武器。过了一会儿，一群勇敢的战士涉水进入河中。他们口衔长剑，河水没过了胸口。到达对岸后，他们从敌人手中夺取了浮桥，横跨易北河，以便我们发起进攻。亲爱的提香，即使没有捷径，勇气依然存在。

The Elbe River separated us from the forces of the Protestant princes. They had taken care to destroy the bridges that connected the two banks. The current presented an insurmountable obstacle. From the opposite bank, they shouted at us brazenly, threatening to attack sooner rather than later. They felt protected by the gap of water that remained between them and us. Then night fell on Mühlberg. The enemy's shouts subsided, and my harangue was heard clearly among my troops. I warned them of what was at stake for Germany. I also spoke to them of God, the Empire, and destiny. I saw their blood boil in their eyes. They gripped their weapons. After a while, a group of brave men waded into the river. They held their swords in their mouths, and the water rose above their chests. Once on the other side, they stole pontoons from the enemy and laid them across the Elbe so that we could begin the attack. Where there are no catwalks, courage remains, dear Tiziano.

听完故事，意大利人凝视着凯撒，凯撒仿佛在讲述的过程中焕发了生机。事实上，米尔贝格战役中对改革派诸侯的压倒性胜利，给查理带来了无比的喜悦。生活不再像是一成不变的衰落：他仍然有机会成就伟业，改变历史的进程。凯撒的身体依然虚弱，对伊莎贝拉的思念也始终萦绕心头；但这场胜利让他充满了希望和自豪。

After hearing the tale, the Italian gazed at the Caesar, who seemed to come alive as he recounted it. The truth was that the overwhelming victory over the reformist princes at Mühlberg had brought Charles a surge of joy. Life no longer seemed like a continuous decline: there was still room for epic deeds, for changing the course of history. The Caesar's body was still frail, and longing for Isabella was ever-present; but the triumph had filled him with hope and pride.

看到皇帝这般模样，提香深受触动：他年老体弱，妻子已逝，却依然散发着英雄气概。这位艺术家陷入沉思，闭上了双眼。

Titian was deeply moved to see the emperor in such a state: he was aged, ill, and widowed, yet he exuded heroism. The artist, lost in thought, closed his eyes.

——我将只描绘你一人。战场在背景中。胜利的所有辉煌都凝聚在你身上。

—I will paint you alone. The battle in the background. All the grandeur of the victory summed up in you.

查理听到意大利人的想法后，想到了他的方阵，想到了敢于游过易北河的克里斯托瓦尔·德·蒙德拉贡；也想到了与他并肩作战的阿尔瓦公爵和他的兄弟。但或许这位大师说得对：他，凯撒，代表了他们所有人，也体现了帝国的伟大。

When he heard the Italian's idea, Charles thought of his tercios, and of Cristóbal de Mondragón, who had dared to swim across the Elbe; also of the Duke of Alba and his brother, who had led the battle alongside him. But perhaps the master was right: he, the Caesar, represented them all and embodied the greatness of the Empire.

 

 

 

 

几天后，费尔南多走进画家的房间，看到了那幅画的草稿。他惊讶地发现卡洛斯独自一人站在那里，凝视着提香笔下自信流畅的线条。他心中涌起一阵莫名的情绪。

Days later, Fernando went into the artist's room and saw the sketch of the painting. He was surprised to see Carlos alone. He stood contemplating the confident lines drawn by Titian. He felt a pang in his mood.

不久之后，皇帝出现在房间里。他看着那幅画，猜到了他哥哥在想什么。

Shortly after, the emperor appeared in the room. He guessed what his brother was thinking as he looked at the painting.

——这不过是一幅肖像画。你知道我有多么珍惜你与我并肩作战。

—It's nothing more than a portrait. You know how much I value you fighting by my side.

费尔南多转过身。然后他又看了看那幅素描肖像，坦白道：

Fernando turned around. Then he looked again at the sketched portrait and confessed:

“有时候，光有感激之情是不够的。我这么说可不是在说我自己。”查尔斯的弟弟注意到查尔斯没明白他的意思。“我儿子认为米兰公国配得上他。你不让他证明这一点，他很不高兴。”

“Sometimes gratitude isn’t enough. And I’m not saying that for myself.” Charles’s brother noticed that Charles didn’t understand what he meant. “My son believes the Duchy of Milan is worthy of him. He was displeased that you wouldn’t let him prove it.”

凯撒很惊讶。马克西米利安……事实上，他平时根本不注意这个人。他几乎不认识他，而且有时觉得他精力过剩。

The Caesar was surprised. Maximilian… The truth was, he didn't usually pay him any attention. He barely knew him, and sometimes he seemed too energetic.

费尔南多继续说道：“我不是以父亲的身份说的，但我说他是一个才华横溢的年轻人，而且，在我身边长大，他学会了如何管理，即使在最不利的情况下也是如此。”

—I'm not speaking as a father —Fernando continued— when I say that he is a brilliant young man and that, having grown up by my side, he has learned to govern, even in the most adverse circumstances.

他没有提及的是，他的儿子曾怂恿新教诸侯叛乱，背叛了皇帝。他竭力保守这个秘密，并相信如果皇帝能彻底赏赐马克西米利安一些荣誉，马克西米利安就不会再重蹈覆辙。

What he refrained from mentioning was that his son had betrayed the emperor by encouraging the rebellion of the Protestant princes. He had taken great care to keep this transgression secret, and he trusted that Maximilian would not repeat anything similar if, once and for all, the emperor granted him some honor.

“他们长得那么像吗？”来自根特的男子问道。

"Do they look that much alike?" inquired the man from Ghent.

他哥哥笑了。

His brother smiled.

难道我没有竭尽全力为您服务吗？您对我的信任已得到最忠诚的回报。

—And have I not served you with zeal? Your trust in me has been rewarded with the greatest loyalty.

——你的意思是说，只有我奖励马克西米利安，才能得到他的忠诚吗？

—Are you suggesting that I will only have Maximilian's loyalty if I reward him?

凯撒的兄弟迅速做出反应，阻止卡洛斯的说法成真。

Caesar's brother reacted quickly to prevent Carlos from being right.

——我坚信，谁先放弃谁就赢了。

—I simply believe that whoever gives up first wins.

皇帝曾从热尔曼·德·福瓦口中听过这句话。费迪南肯定也从她那里听过。皇帝突然想起她曾教给他的关于权力中慷慨的教诲。他的前情人已于不久前在瓦伦西亚去世，安详而有尊严，正如她一直渴望的那样。皇帝生命中的主人公们一个个离世。无论好坏，他都接受了这个事实。但当那封来自法国、包装精美的信封送到他手中时，死亡对他而言有了新的意义。

The emperor had heard that phrase before, from the lips of Germaine de Foix. Surely Ferdinand must have heard it from her as well. The emperor suddenly recalled the lessons she had taught him about generosity in power. His former lover had died some time ago in Valencia, peaceful and dignified, as she had always wished to die. Little by little, the protagonists of the emperor's life had departed for the afterlife. He, for better or worse, had come to accept this fact. But when that beautifully sealed envelope, originating in France, reached his hands, death took on a new meaning for him.

 

 

 

 

“弗朗西斯科，”他一边读着纸条，一边一遍遍地低语。卡洛斯惊讶于自己竟会因为这个法国人的死而如此悲伤。他的一生中，这个敌人一直让他提心吊胆，迫使他时刻保持警惕，保护自己。弗朗西斯科的离世，让他感到精疲力竭。在他的人生故事里，弗朗西斯科始终是他的对手，是他不断的挑战，是他的诅咒。这就是为什么戏剧中的反派会在最后一幕死去，因为没有了他们，英雄们的生命就失去了吸引力，剩下的只有帷幕落下。

“Francisco,” he murmured again and again as he read the note. Carlos was surprised to feel so saddened by the Frenchman’s death. Throughout his life, his enemy had kept him on his toes, forcing him to remain vigilant for his own protection. With his passing, he felt himself losing energy. In the story of his existence, Francisco had acted as the adversary, the constant challenge, the curse. That is why in dramas the villains die in the final act, for without them, the lives of the heroes lose their appeal, and all that remains is for the curtain to fall.

法国人的去世只是众多逝者中的又一例。近几个月来，路德和亨利也相继离世。埃尔南·科尔特斯在故乡卡斯蒂利亚被认为年老无用，而曾是西班牙祸害的海盗巴巴罗萨也已在伊斯坦布尔下葬一年。查理感到这个世界不再属于他，仿佛在他被委派出演的那出戏里，所有演员都被替换了，只剩下他一个原班人马。他不排除再活几年的可能性，但很明显，尽管他身处当下，却已然成为过去的一部分。

The Frenchman's death was just one more in a long list of losses. In recent months, the earth had also claimed Luther and Henry. Hernán Cortés was said to be old and useless in his native Castile, and the pirate Barbarossa, once the scourge of Spain, had been buried in Istanbul for a year. Charles felt that the world was no longer his, as if in the play he had been assigned to perform, all the actors had been replaced and he was now the only one left from the original cast. He didn't rule out living a few more years, but it was clear that, although he inhabited the present, he was already part of the past.

 

 

 

 

就这样，他这一代人的命运已然注定，皇帝开始忧心忡忡地思考下一代。米尔贝格战役的胜利重燃了他对帝国使命的信念。在那场胜利之前，他经历了一段黑暗时期。他的领土如同一个难以驾驭的巨人，总是以各种方式最终让他败下阵来：不是卡斯蒂利亚，就是佛兰德斯、德国或意大利。战火永不停歇，如果他试图扑灭其他地方的战火，就会有人起来反抗他，法国会因此胆大妄为地入侵，或者土耳其人会出现在他的边境。无法掌控自身事务的挫败感让他焦虑不已，健康状况每况愈下，难以享受生活。他会强迫菲利普重蹈覆辙吗？在那段悲观时期，他绝不允许这种情况发生。因此，他将皇帝的指挥权授予了费迪南：他的儿子已经有足够的精力去处理佛兰德斯、西班牙、印度和意大利领土上的事务了。指望一个男人能处理这么多事情，事实证明是不可能的。

Thus, his generation's fate sealed, the emperor began to obsess over the next. The triumph at Mühlberg had restored his belief in the Empire's mission. Before that victory, he had endured a dark period. His domains seemed an unmanageable giant that always, in one way or another, ended up defeating him: when it wasn't Castile, it was Flanders, or Germany, or Italy. There was constantly a fire burning, and if he tried to extinguish it elsewhere, someone would rise up against him, France would be emboldened to invade, or the Turks would appear at his borders. The frustration of being unable to keep his own affairs under control had caused him constant anxiety, which had deteriorated his health and made it difficult for him to enjoy life. Would he force Philip to go through the same thing? During that pessimistic period, he refused to allow it. For that reason, he had granted Ferdinand the imperial command: his son would have enough to deal with in Flanders, Spain, the Indies, and the Italian territories. Trusting that a single man could handle so much had proven impossible.

 

 

 

 

直到米尔贝格向他证明，骄傲和信仰可以战胜一切。查理重拾乐观，也重拾梦想。他为何要放弃建立普世君主制的理想？仅仅因为这不可能吗？或许如此；但乌托邦不正是激励人们不断进步的动力吗？即便他们最终未能完全实现。他设想的世界是一个信仰统一、兄弟情谊深厚的世界，正义平等地惠及所有人，没有嫉妒，因此也没有暴力。基督教可以仅仅用于祈祷和忏悔，也可以像他一样，成为统治者的真正指引。在这个他难以割舍的梦想中，没有空间去拆毁他的遗产。恰恰相反：无论谁继承他的事业，都应该以普世性为目标，扩张帝国版图。领土越多，就越接近这个目标。

Until Mühlberg proved to him that pride and faith could conquer all. Charles regained his optimism and with it his dreams. Why renounce his ideal of a universal monarchy? Because it was impossible? Perhaps; but weren't utopias what spurred men to improve, even if they never fully achieved them? He envisioned a world under a single faith, united in brotherhood, where Justice was served equally to all, devoid of envy and therefore of violence. Christianity could remain for prayers and guilt, or it could constitute the true guide of the ruler, as it was for him. And in that dream he found so difficult to relinquish, there was no room for dismantling his legacy. On the contrary: whoever succeeded him should expand the Empire, with universality as the goal. The greater the number of possessions, the closer they would come to that end.

如今，卡洛斯重拾希望，但也深知时日无多，他日夜思念着费利佩。痛风折磨着他的四肢，卡洛斯却越来越坚信儿子能够战胜一切：他天生就拥有伟大的气质。而且，无论如何，只有被赋予超越他人能力的重任，才能变得坚不可摧。

Now that he had regained hope but knew his time was running out, he could think of Felipe day and night. As the gout stung his limbs, Carlos became increasingly convinced that his son could overcome anything: he possessed an innate aura of greatness. And, in any case, only someone who is asked to do more than others can give grows to become unbreakable.

事实上，如果他们之中有人辜负了对方，那也是他，这位皇帝，尤其是他的父亲。他的种种努力一次又一次地让他与儿子疏远。他几乎没给儿子传授过什么，不过是些零碎的教诲。他多年不在卡斯蒂利亚，即便偶尔回来，也总是对儿子十分苛刻。当儿子的妻子玛丽亚·曼努埃拉去世时，他也没有陪伴在儿子身边安慰他。难道现在他又要惩罚儿子，剥夺他真正渴望的、为帝国和他自己创造的未来吗？

In truth, if either of them had failed the other, it was he, the emperor, and above all, the father. His endeavors had repeatedly distanced him from his offspring. He had barely imparted more than a few fragmented lessons. He had been absent from Castile for years and, generally, during his visits had treated him harshly. Nor had he been there to comfort him when his wife, Maria Manuela, died. Was he going to punish him now as well, depriving him of the future he truly desired for the Empire and for himself?

 

 

 

 

几周后，哈布斯堡的马克西米利安从船上瞥见了新的地平线。西班牙海岸静静地伫立在那里，却也冷漠无情。费迪南德之子的心情如同他的船只一般：它向前驶去，却毫无热情。这位年轻人对未来在那片土地上的生活一无所知。他很不情愿地接受了皇帝的命令，要他娶自己的表妹玛丽亚，也就是皇帝的女儿。

After a few weeks, Maximilian of Habsburg glimpsed a new horizon from his ship. The coast of Spain awaited him, placid and indifferent. The mood of Ferdinand's son mirrored that of his vessel: it moved forward, but without enthusiasm. The young man did not know what to expect from the future that awaited him in those lands. He had received with displeasure the emperor's order to marry his daughter, his cousin Maria.

“他把我当公主一样宠爱。而我可是个政治家！”他曾向父亲抱怨道。

"He treats me like a princess. And I'm a statesman!" he had complained to his father.

——你在抱怨吗？你应该感谢我竭尽全力确保你的背叛不被察觉！我必须向王子们发誓保护你。

—Are you complaining? Be thankful that I did everything in my power to ensure your betrayal went unnoticed! I had to pledge my word to the princes to protect you.

父亲，您知道我有多感激您，但是……

—You know how grateful I am, Father, but…

“这桩婚事对你来说是天赐良机，”费尔南多打断道，“我相信，这只是你叔叔众多恩惠的开端。你将成为西班牙的摄政王——想想你昨天的处境！抓住这个机会，我的儿子。你除了有机会证明自己之外，没有什么可以羡慕费利佩的。”

“This engagement is a blessing for you,” Fernando interrupted. “The first of many gestures from your uncle, I’m sure. You will be regent of Spain—think of what your prospects were yesterday! Seize this opportunity, my son. You have nothing to envy Felipe for except the chances to prove it.”

 

 

 

 

马克西米利安考虑过这个问题。他不想像他父亲那样安于现状，但与做一个默默无闻的贵族相比，掌控那些显赫的王国无疑是一种进步。

Maximilian considered it. He didn't want to be complacent like his father, but compared to being an aristocratic nobody, taking command of those prestigious kingdoms was undoubtedly an improvement.

至于玛丽亚，这个年轻人对她一无所知。但这对他来说却是最不重要的事。对费尔南多的儿子来说，爱情不过是无关紧要的小事，是妓女们才会做的事。政治野心才是他夜不能寐的唯一原因。

As for Maria, the young man knew nothing about her. But that was the least of his problems. For Fernando's son, love was nothing more than a trivial preoccupation, the business of courtesans. Political ambition was the only thing that kept him awake at night.

 

 

 

 

卡斯蒂利亚宫廷对马克西米利安的接待恭敬而不张扬。他对此并不十分在意；众所周知，西班牙的习俗倾向于节俭。他对当时遇到的菲利普的态度不太满意。这位皇帝的儿子对他彬彬有礼，但似乎心存疏离。这种态度让马克西米利安暗自窃喜：毫无疑问，他的堂兄一定对皇帝夺走他的摄政之位并交给自己感到恼火。

The reception that the Castilian court extended to Maximilian was respectful but not ostentatious. He didn't attach much importance to it; it was common knowledge that Spanish customs tended toward austerity. He was less pleased with the attitude of Philip, whom he met then. The emperor's son behaved politely toward him, but seemed distant. This attitude made Maximilian smile inwardly: undoubtedly, his cousin had been annoyed that the emperor had taken the regent's office from him and given it to him.

接下来的相遇也让他很满意。他的未婚妻玛丽亚是一位漂亮聪慧的年轻女子，见到他时甚至脸红了，为自己的好运感到​​高兴。

The next encounter also pleased him. Maria, his fiancée, turned out to be an attractive and bright young woman, who even blushed upon seeing him, celebrating her good fortune.

费尔南多的儿子对他的新生活非常满意。

Fernando's son felt more than satisfied with his new life.

 

 

 

 

直到第二天，当他和费利佩单独共进晚餐时，他才发现这种完美不过是一种幻觉。

Until, the next day, while Felipe and he were having dinner alone, he discovered that such perfection could be nothing other than an illusion.

“我恭敬地等待您能就这些王国的摄政问题向我传授一些经验。”马克西米利安说道。

—I humbly await the lessons you may be pleased to offer me concerning the regency of these kingdoms—said Maximilian.

他的表弟沉默不语，又吩咐人端来一盘野味。过了一会儿，他才开口说道：

His cousin remained silent and ordered another platter of game to be served. Only then did he reply:

“冷静下来。你们无需做任何决定。”费利佩平静地切着一块鹿肉，过了片刻。“议会将为你们做出一切决定。如有必要，议会将向陛下请示。”

"Calm yourselves. You will not have to make any decisions." Felipe calmly spent a few moments carving a piece of venison. "The Council will decide everything for you. If necessary, it will ask His Majesty for instructions."

奥地利人希望这只是个玩笑。

The Austrian wanted to believe it was a joke.

—你误解了我来到这里的意义：责任对我来说不是负担，因为这是我所追求的。

—You have misunderstood my presence here: responsibility will not be a burden for me, for it is what I aspire to.

菲利普仿佛没听见他的话，继续说道：

Philip, as if he hadn't heard him, continued speaking:

我建议你信任格兰维拉。他知识渊博，服从性也恰到好处。

—I recommend you trust Granvela. He possesses just the right amount of knowledge and obedience.

但这些建议对马克西米利亚诺来说还远远不够。他情绪激动，根本无暇顾及。

But those recommendations weren't even enough for Maximiliano. He was too agitated to consider them at all.

“你不是也像我一样以摄政王的身份治理国家吗？”费尔南多的儿子强忍着怒火回答道。

—Haven't you governed as regent, just as I will? —replied Fernando's son with barely contained rage.

他的表弟低声应了一声，把肉送到嘴边。他慢慢地咀嚼着，这让对方越来越不耐烦。

His cousin responded with a murmur of assent and brought the meat to his mouth. He chewed it slowly, arousing the other's impatience.

费利佩回答说：“我所拥有的那些经验，将使我能够从现在开始统治荷兰。”

—That experience that I do have —replied Felipe— is what will allow me to rule the Netherlands from now on.

“你要取代我们的姑妈吗？”马克西米利亚诺的怒火不可避免地越来越大。

"Are you going to replace our aunt?" Maximiliano's anger was inevitably increasing.

——这是我父亲的遗愿，他的遗愿必须得到服从。每个人都必须服从。我们每个人都会在各自的时间和地点尽自己的一份力。接受这个事实吧。

—That's what my father wanted, and his will must be obeyed. By everyone. Each one of us will do our part in our time and place. Get used to the idea.

费尔南多的儿子沉默不语，面容僵硬。他刚刚得知的消息迫使他重新审视过去几周的经历，他对每一件事的理解都发生了剧烈的转变。他没有得到皇帝的任何奖赏；相反，他被流放到一个遥远的王国，沦为傀儡，从而彻底粉碎了他觊觎帝国的野心。

Fernando's son fell silent, his features frozen. What he had just learned forced him to reread the account of his last few weeks, and his understanding of each event shifted abruptly. He had received no reward from the emperor; on the contrary, he had been exiled to a distant kingdom where he would be relegated to a mere figurehead, thus thwarting his aspirations to the Empire.

晚餐在沉默中结束。菲利普察觉到表弟的失望，但他理解父亲的理由，即便这些理由对他个人有利。“不要相信任何人，”皇帝曾告诫他。他怎能对一个即使在平静时刻也眼神中流露出如此沮丧的年轻人违背这条格言呢？

Dinner ended in silence. Philip was aware of his cousin's disappointment, but he understood his father's reasons, even if they benefited him personally. "Trust no one," the emperor had told him. How could he disregard that maxim with a young man whose gaze, even in moments of calm, betrayed such frustration?

 

 

 

 

皇帝命令菲利普离开西班牙前往尼德兰指挥军队，这让他内心充满矛盾。一方面，他被这项新的挑战所激励，这也标志着他最终接受了父亲的遗志。但他从未离开过故土，他知道自己会想念那里，尤其是他挚爱的妻子。

Philip felt conflicted when the emperor ordered him to leave Spain and assume command in the Netherlands. On the one hand, he was motivated by this new challenge, which also represented a first step in the eventual acceptance of his father's legacy. But he had never left his homeland, and he knew he would miss it; especially his beloved.

他与伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥的恋情丝毫未减。在她怀里，妻子去世的痛苦和愧疚感都烟消云散。他永远都无法满足于她：每次分开，他都已经开始期待下一次约会了。他对她的迷恋从未消退，这让他确信，这位女士很可能就是他此生的挚爱。从父母的婚姻中，他明白真爱一生只有一次。因此，他决定带她一起去往新的目的地。

His romance with Isabel Osorio had continued unabated. In her arms, the pain and guilt he felt for his wife's death had melted away. He could never get enough of her: as soon as they parted, he was already thinking about their next date. The fact that his infatuation never waned led him to believe that this lady was, in all likelihood, the woman of his life. From his parents' marriage, he had learned that true love only comes once. For that reason, he decided to take her with him to his new destination.

 

 

 

 

年轻女子惊讶地接受了邀请。自从得知菲利普即将前往弗兰德斯后，她的心情便一直低落。她再次感到自己很可笑，竟然执着于这段注定要以她爱人的身份早晚戛然而止的恋情。当他邀请她同行时，伊莎贝拉欣喜若狂：这个男人需要她，正如她需要他一样，而且他愿意不顾一切阻碍和世俗礼仪，只为将她留在身边。她心中燃起了希望，开始想象他们在那个优雅的北方宫廷中共同生活会是什么样子。最初的幻想中只有热情和快乐，但有一天，她的想象力却变得现实起来，浮现出一个令人沮丧的场景：她被指认为摄政王的情妇，而摄政王的名声也因此蒙尘。

The young woman accepted the offer with astonishment. Ever since she learned that Philip was to depart for Flanders, her spirits had darkened. She again felt ridiculous for having prolonged a romance that, given her lover's status, was doomed to end abruptly sooner or later. When he invited her to accompany him, Isabella was thrilled: this man needed her as much as she needed him, and he was willing to disregard obstacles and conventions to keep her by his side. She felt hopeful and began to imagine what their life together would be like in that elegant northern court. In her first fantasies, there was only room for enthusiasm and enjoyment, but one day her imagination saw fit to be realistic and conjured up a disheartening scene: one in which she was singled out as the regent's mistress, and his reputation was tarnished as a result.

在伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥出发的前一天，费利佩去拜访她，为她做最后的准备工作。伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥却出乎意料地告诉他，她还没有准备好旅行的嫁妆。

When, the day before her departure, Felipe visited her to finalize the preparations, Isabel Osorio surprised him by telling him that she had not arranged her trousseau for the trip.

——你们即将向半个欧洲展示自己。暴露自己的弱点对你们没有任何好处。

—You're going to be presenting yourselves to half of Europe. It's not in your best interest to show your weaknesses.

他困惑地看着她，假装不明白。

He looked at her, puzzled, pretending not to understand.

“我不会陪你去，”她说道。

"I will not accompany you," she declared.

—你比我更在意别人的看法吗？

—Do you care more about what others think than I do?

—如果他们窃窃私语说我是国王的娼妓，也许吧。

—If they whispered that I was the king's whore, maybe.

他们沉默不语。现实如同污浊的雨水般倾泻而下，玷污了一切。

They remained silent. Reality fell upon them like a dirty rain, staining everything.

“谁敢说这种话，我就把他的舌头割下来！”他龇牙咧嘴地说。

"I'll rip out the tongue of anyone who dares to say such a thing!" he said, baring his teeth.

伊莎贝尔抚摸着他的脸颊。想到第二天自己就不能再这样做了，她心如刀绞。

Isabel stroked his cheek. It broke her heart to know that she wouldn't be able to do it the next day.

——亲爱的，可悲的是，有些侮辱中也包含着一丝真理。我的位置不在你身边，我们彼此都明白这一点。

—The sad thing, my beloved, is that some insults contain a grain of truth. My place is not by your side, and we both know it.

费利佩瞥了一眼面前的窗户，但窗户无情地映照出她的身影，一个他似乎无法逃离的影像。他真想亲吻玻璃上的那个倒影。

Felipe glanced toward the window before them, but it mercilessly reflected her image back at him, an image from which escape seemed impossible. He would have kissed that reflection in the glass.

我的思绪每时每刻都在寻找你。当我回来时，我也会这样做。你会等我吗？

—My mind will search for you every moment. And when I return, I will do the same. Will you wait for me?

那位女士沉默不语，然后开始解开裙子。

The lady remained silent. Then she began to loosen her dress.

“你会等我吗？”他坚持问道。

"Will you wait for me?" he insisted.

衣服散落在她脚边，她点了点头。

As the clothes fell at her feet, she nodded.

 

 

 

 

奉皇帝之命，弗兰德斯被装点成一片盛大的庆典，迎接菲利普的到来。旅程本身已是一场盛大的庆典：皇帝之子乘坐安德烈亚·多利亚的船只，由卡斯蒂利亚最显赫的贵族成员陪同；毕竟，随从的尊贵程度反映了其所护送之人的尊贵程度。

By order of the emperor, Flanders was transformed into a festival to welcome Philip. The journey itself had already been a display of magnificence: the son of the emperor sailed on the ships of Andrea Doria, accompanied by the most illustrious members of the Castilian aristocracy; after all, the nobility of a retinue reflected that of the one it escorted.

菲利普对大海的险恶感到震惊，但他的航行给整个欧洲带来的震撼远胜于此。事实上，当人们得知这位年轻人离开西班牙时，整个欧洲大陆都感到不安。他的伟大如此令人瞩目，以至于许多人担心他离开西班牙王国的唯一目的就是发动一场征服战争。凯撒之子的威望如此之高，以至于他的存在本身就是一种威胁。

Philip was struck by the harshness of the sea, but less so than his voyage impressed all of Europe. In truth, the continent felt genuine unease when it learned that the young man had left Spain behind. His greatness was such that many feared his departure from that kingdom had no other motive than to begin some conquest. The dignity of the son of Caesar was so considerable that his mere presence made him a threat.

 

 

 

 

弗拉芒宫廷为迎接菲利普盛装打扮，如同迎接皇帝一般：皇家大厅容纳不下前来祝贺的众多宾客。人人都听说过这位即将统治他们的年轻人，而且当那一天到来时，他将以自己的名义治理国家。查理的儿子不负众望，以庄严的姿态迎接菲利普：他克服了在陌生人面前的羞涩，展现出偶像般的风范。他的举止给每个人都留下了深刻的印象；然而，在场的某位人士却认为这种傲慢无礼令人难以接受。当然，这个人就是费迪南。

The Flemish court dressed up for Philip just as it did when receiving the emperor: its royal hall was too small for the many who came to fete him. Everyone had heard of this young man who would soon rule them and, when the day came, govern them in his own right. Charles's son rose to the occasion, befitting the solemnity of the welcome: he overcame his shyness before strangers by presenting himself with the airs of an idol. His bearing impressed everyone; but to one of those present, this display of haughtiness was outrageous. Of course, it was Ferdinand.

尽管在欢迎侄子的庆典上，皇帝表面上表现得十分镇定，但他心里清楚，他的弟弟已经与他反目成仇。几天前，他们曾发生过争吵。斐迪南带着马克西米利安的一封信前来，信很长，字迹略显紧张。

Although he maintained a composed demeanor during the festivities welcoming his nephew, the emperor was well aware that his brother had turned against him. Days earlier, they had had an argument. Ferdinand had arrived with a letter from Maximilian in his hands, a long text written in a nervous hand.

“你欺骗了他！也欺骗了我！”他咆哮道。

"You've deceived him! And me along with him!" he roared.

——我不会在他准备就绪时剥夺他在西班牙摄政时期的影响力。兄弟，通过解除他的职责，我是为了防止你的儿子犯错。

—I will not deny him influence in the regency of Spain when he is ready. By relieving him of responsibilities, brother, I prevent your son from making mistakes.

你们听听自己说的话！你们竟然认为它无效！你们根本不知道这种想法有多么冒犯我。

—Do you hear yourselves? You're assuming it's null and void! You don't realize how much such a thing offends me.

费尔南多的脾气不允许争吵继续下去。卡洛斯相信随着时间的推移，他的怒气会消散。的确，在随后的几次会面中，他的兄弟没有抱怨，但这仅仅是因为他一句话也没说：他已经切断了与皇帝的一切联系。

Fernando's temper did not allow the dispute to continue. Carlos trusted that his anger would lessen with time. It was true that in their subsequent meetings his brother uttered no complaints, but only because not a single syllable escaped his lips: he had cut off all communication with the emperor.

查理对此感到悲伤，随后又感到恼怒。西班牙的权杖是他的，他的弟弟凭什么这样评判他的决定？马克西米利安还有很多需要证明的地方，委任他权力时谨慎一些难道不合情理吗？即便他没有对费迪南采取任何行动，事实是费迪南根本不听话。想到这一点，查理对未来深感忧虑。难道这就是他儿子继承王位后要依靠的帮凶吗？一个自认为有权违抗命令的人？查理预想到，未来将是家族两大派系之间的斗争，一场兄弟相残的争斗，将再次分裂他一手统一的土地。

That reaction provoked sadness in Charles, and then irritation. The scepter of Spain was his; who did his brother think he was to judge his decisions in that way? Maximilian still had everything to prove; wasn't it understandable to be cautious when assigning him power? Even if he didn't take any action against him, the truth was that Ferdinand was not at all obedient. And that fact, projected into the future, greatly worried the emperor. Was this the collaborator his son would have to rely on when he received his inheritance? One who granted himself the right to rebel against the commands he was supposed to obey? Charles then envisioned the future as a battle between the two factions of the family, a fratricidal struggle that would once again divide the lands he had united.

我绝不会容忍这种事。

I wasn't going to tolerate it.

 

 

 

 

“我已经决定册封腓力为罗马国王。我死后，帝国将传给他。”凯撒宣布道。

—I have decided to name Philip King of the Romans. Upon my death, the Empire will pass to him —the Caesar declared.

在费迪南德、玛丽亚、菲利普和皇帝聚集的房间里，连地板吱呀作响的声音都听不见，因为在场的所有人都一动不动。震惊使时间仿佛凝固了。

In the room where Ferdinand, Maria, Philip, and the Emperor were gathered, not even the creaking of the floorboards could be heard, for none of those present moved. Astonishment had frozen time.

玛丽亚注意到了费迪南德。这位昔日的皇位继承人已变得怒火中烧，如同冰冷的岩石。突然间，她曾经为查理做出的所有牺牲、所有的忍耐、所有的忠诚，都在她心中彻底爆发，永远地摧毁了她对他的感情。

Maria noticed Ferdinand. The former imperial successor had become a frozen rock of anger. Suddenly and definitively, all the sacrifices, all the endurance, and every gesture of generous loyalty she had shown to Charles exploded within her and destroyed her feelings for him forever.

他的妹妹担心费尔南多恢复血统后会做出什么事来，便看着卡洛斯说：

His sister, fearing what Fernando might do when the blood returned to him, looked at Carlos and said:

陛下，您犯了两个错误。第一个错误是把过重的负担压在了年纪尚轻的人身上。

—You are making two mistakes, Your Majesty. The first is placing an excessive burden on shoulders that are too young.

费利佩搅拌了一下。

Felipe stirred.

—你认为我能力不足吗？

—Do you consider me incapable?

玛丽亚选择无视侄子的劝阻，继续说道：

Maria chose to ignore her nephew's intervention and continued:

第二个错误是让你的继任者认为忠诚和牺牲毫无价值。

—The second mistake is teaching your successor that loyalty and sacrifice are worthless.

皇帝看着他的兄弟们。他从未见过比他们面前更令人失望的表情。

The emperor looked at his brothers. He had never witnessed a greater disappointment than the one they displayed.

“我们的世界正在走向灭亡，兄弟。”卡洛斯寻求其他人的理解。“让我们为那些注定要在这个新时代出现的人让路吧。”

"Our world is dying, brother." Carlos sought the others' understanding. "Let's make way for those who are meant to be in this new era."

她将与菲利普重逢后一直萦绕心头的想法藏在心底：她的儿子，那个曾经桀骜不驯、不太可靠的儿子，如今已经成熟了。或许是早年丧夫的打击，或许是西班牙摄政的责任。总之，他的性格变得沉稳而坚韧，正是她遗产的合适继承人。

She kept to herself what she had been thinking since her reunion with Philip: that her son, the same one who had once been undisciplined and not entirely reliable, had matured. Perhaps it was the shock of early widowhood, or the responsibility of the Spanish regency. The fact was that his character had become sober and resilient, the right one for the heir to her legacy.

“我将珍视您关于治理帝国的教诲。”菲利普对他的叔叔说道。

—I will treasure your teachings on governing the Empire—Philip told his uncle.

费尔南多怒气冲冲地跳了起来，椅子在他身后翻倒，发出了一声巨响，吓了所有人一跳。他焦躁的目光在卡洛斯和费利佩之间来回扫视。

Fernando jumped to his feet in such anger that his chair fell behind him, causing a loud crash that startled everyone. His agitated gaze darted from Carlos to Felipe.

“我绝不容忍这种以利益为幌子的暴行。我的儿子没有得到任何奖赏，反而被流放，就像我当年被逐出卡斯蒂利亚一样！你们用兄弟情谊的美好外衣掩盖一切。你们把我当傻瓜，而我一直以来都比你们强……！”

"I will not tolerate this outrage being disguised as an advantage. My son received no reward; he was exiled, just as I was from Castile in my day! You cloak everything in the beautiful trappings of brotherhood. You take me for a fool, when I have only ever been a better man than you…!"

皇帝重重地拍了一下桌子，打断了那番话。费迪南德离开了房间。查理注意到他疲惫的脚步，那脚步声仿佛出自一个饱经风霜、早已失去所有希望的人；查理惊讶地发现，自己竟感到一阵莫名的悲伤。

The emperor silenced the speech with a bang on the table. Ferdinand left the room. Charles noticed his weary steps, the steps of a man who had lived a full life and no longer held any hope; and he was surprised to feel an immense sadness.

 

 

 

 

在兄弟俩大打出手之后的几天里，玛丽亚常常想起她的姑姑玛格丽塔。她庆幸姑姑不必亲眼目睹卡洛斯和费尔南多兄弟相残的惨剧，也记得姑姑曾答应她要维系家庭的团结。但事实上，这个承诺似乎越来越难以实现。两兄弟之间积压多年的怨恨和不信任终于爆发了。新一代并没有起到任何缓和气氛的作用；恰恰相反，马克西米利亚诺和费利佩继承了父母的矛盾，再加上他们年轻气盛的劲头：他们就像两朵即将碰撞、爆发成风暴的乌云。

In the days following the fight between her brothers, Maria often thought of her aunt Margarita. She was grateful that the woman hadn't had to witness the fratricidal display of Carlos and Fernando, and she remembered her promise to her to keep the family together. The truth was, that task seemed increasingly utopian. The resentments and mistrust between the two men, simmering for years, had finally erupted. The new generation did nothing to help bring peace; quite the opposite, in fact, for Maximiliano and Felipe had inherited their parents' tensions combined with the energy of their youth: they were two troubled clouds destined to collide and erupt into a storm.

玛丽亚连续数周每天都去探望皇帝。起初，他拒绝谈及斐迪南。这个话题令他精疲力竭，痛风本身就已让他痛苦不堪，他实在不愿再承受精神上的创伤。他的妹妹玛丽亚很有耐心；既然菲利普已经摄政尼德兰，她也无事可做。渐渐地，查理的伪装开始瓦解，直到有一天，玛丽亚提起斐迪南，皇帝没有回避这个话题。沉默良久之后，他终于坦白道：

Maria visited the emperor every day for weeks. At first, he refused to speak of Ferdinand. The subject exhausted him, and his gout was painful enough without him having his soul wounded as well. His sister was patient; now that Philip had assumed the regency of the Netherlands, she had no other task. Little by little, Charles's armor began to crumble, until one day Maria brought up Ferdinand, and the emperor didn't change the subject. After a long silence, he confessed:

我害怕他会背叛我。

—I fear his betrayal.

就像多年前你在托尔德西利亚斯害怕母亲去世一样。

—Just like you feared your mother's death years ago, in Tordesillas.

皇帝的思绪突然回到了过去。他回想起三十年前卡斯蒂利亚起义、胡安娜几乎改写历史时，自己所感受到的恐惧。

The emperor's mind was suddenly thrown back in time. He recalled the fear he had felt no less than thirty years before, when Castile rose up and Joanna almost changed history.

“如果你不信任她会做什么，那是因为你把她当成敌人。就像你现在对待你的兄弟和他的儿子一样。”

"If you distrusted what she might do, it was because you treated her like an enemy. Just as you now treat your brother and his son."

他一言不发，陷入沉思。这么多年过去了，他似乎什么也没学到。然而，一种发自内心的情感驱使他希望一切都为了费利佩。

He pondered without saying a word. He seemed to have learned nothing in all those years. And yet, a visceral emotion made him want everything to be for Felipe.

“为什么没有人明白，我的职责只在于我的继承人，而不是其他人？权力是从父母传给子女的。现在却要我把权力分给所有与我血脉相连的人！”

"Why does no one understand that my duty is to my successor and no one else? Power is passed down from parents to children. I am being asked to divide it among as many as share my blood!"

“只有你能决定。成败也与你无关。但如果你真的关心费利佩，就不要让他去与自己的人民作战。”

"No one but you will decide. The successes and failures will belong to no one else. But if you truly care for Felipe, do not condemn him to fight against his own people."

“你知道些什么？”卡洛斯担忧起来。

"What do you know?" Carlos became worried.

玛丽亚犹豫着不敢如实回答。她当时正试图扑灭一场火灾，而不是在此过程中引发新的火灾。

Maria hesitated to answer truthfully. She was trying to put out a fire, not start others in the process.

一个身负重伤、一无所有的人比任何人都危险。

—A wounded man who has nothing to lose is more dangerous than any other.

这位女子没有透露，最近几周她拜访费尔南多的次数和拜访皇帝的次数一样多，而且她从费尔南多的语气中感觉到他可能会背叛她。

The woman kept quiet about the fact that in recent weeks she had visited Fernando as often as the emperor, and that she had sensed from his tone that betrayal was possible.

凯撒的房间里很冷。他们身上盖着的皮毛和面前的火堆都无法让他们停止瑟瑟发抖。对查理来说，这个世界似乎充满敌意；他在米尔贝格战役胜利后所怀有的希望都到哪里去了？

It was cold in the Caesar's chamber. The furs that covered them and the fire before which they sat did nothing to keep them from shivering. To Charles, the world seemed hostile; where had the hopes he had felt after the victory at Mühlberg gone?

你从来没有爱过他，费尔南多。

—You never loved him. Fernando.

皇帝侧目看了一眼他的妹妹。

The emperor glanced sideways at his sister.

“你们都不懂我的感受。我只是个凡人，并非没有感情。如果你们觉得我没有感情，那是因为我的使命迫使我背叛自己。”

"You're all ignorant of my feelings. I'm just a man. I'm not devoid of emotions. If it seems otherwise, it's because my mission forces me to betray myself."

玛丽亚相信他的话，但如果这导致哈布斯堡王朝分裂，那么她的苦难就毫无意义了。

Maria believed his words, but her tribulation was useless if it led to the Habsburg schism.

想想你将留下什么，想想在你见到上帝之前，你脑海中最后一个念头是什么。你的灵魂不会因为维护了权力而获得更多安宁，而是会因为知道自己行为高尚而获得安宁。

—Think of what you will leave behind, the last thought that will cross your mind before you meet God. Your soul will not find more rest from having maintained authority, but from knowing that you have behaved nobly.

 

 

 

 

几周后，议会大厅召开了一场无人愿去的会议。马克西米利安是最后一个到的。从西班牙来的旅途让他疲惫不堪，但他仍然精力充沛地大步走进房间。查理起身迎接他。费迪南、菲利普和玛丽也纷纷起身。气氛紧张得像一群无赖的聚会，彼此互不信任：偷偷地交换眼神，手指敲击着椅子的扶手，呼吸急促，脖子酸痛得几乎喘不过气来。

A few weeks later, the council chamber hosted a meeting no one wanted to attend. Maximilian was the last to arrive. The journey from Spain had tired him, but he still had enough energy to stride into the room. Charles rose to greet him. Ferdinand, Philip, and Mary did the same. The atmosphere was tense, like that of a gathering of scoundrels where no one trusted anyone: furtive glances, fingers tapping on the arms of chairs, ragged breathing, necks straining because everyone was already suffocating.

待众人落座后，皇帝逐一审视他们。只有费迪南的目光始终避开他——玛丽亚费了好大劲才说服他前来参加这次会议。她不由自主地想起姑妈玛格丽特，因为她知道这总能给他带来神奇的效应。

Once everyone was settled, the emperor looked at them one by one. Only Ferdinand's eyes avoided his—it had been difficult for Maria to convince him to come to the meeting. She felt compelled to summon the memory of her aunt Margaret, knowing that it always had a magical effect on him.

——感谢你们接听我的电话。首先，我必须要求你们在这里说的话，就留在这里。这是关乎家庭和国家的事情。

—I thank you for responding to my call. First of all, I must ask that what is said here, stay here. This is a matter of family and state.

菲利普、马克西米利安以及马克西米利安的父亲都毫无反应。他们与世隔绝，沉浸在各自内心的不满之中。凯撒随后看向他的兄弟。

Neither Philip, Maximilian, nor Maximilian's father reacted. They were isolated from the rest of the world in their own private cries of discontent. The Caesar then looked at his brother.

我必须请求你的原谅。我对你不公平。你依然是罗马人的国王。

—I must ask for your forgiveness. I was not fair to you. You will still be the King of the Romans.

费尔南多听到这话很惊讶，更让他惊讶的是，他听完这些话后竟然毫无感觉。相反，费利佩却勃然大怒。

Fernando was surprised to hear that, and even more so to feel nothing after those words. On the contrary, Felipe bristled.

-父亲…！

-Father…!

卡洛斯用一个尖锐的手势回避了他的回答，目光继续紧盯着他的兄弟。

Carlos avoided his reply with a sharp gesture and continued with his eyes fixed on his brother.

——正如我们之前约定的，我的儿子将继承这份荣誉。但马克西米利安不会孤立无援。——费迪南德的长子抬头看着他的叔叔，叔叔对他说：你将继承菲利普的王位。

—As we agreed, my son will inherit the honor. But Maximilian will not be left without support. —Ferdinand's eldest son looked up at his uncle, who then addressed him—: You will succeed Philip.

年轻人立刻跳了起来。

The young man jumped immediately.

“你在开玩笑吗？”他怒道，“你觉得我能比你儿子活多久？我们俩同岁！”

"Are you joking?" he said angrily. "How long do you think I'll outlive your son? We're both the same age!"

“毋庸置疑，我希望费利佩能够长寿，但只有上帝才能决定这种事……”

"Needless to say, I wish Felipe to reach old age, but only God can decide such a thing..."

“我接受，”费尔南多打断了他的话，站起身来，不让喝酒的场面继续下去；他看着他的兄弟，做出评判——：“但是从今天起，我们的道路就此分道扬镳。”
