—I accept —Fernando interrupted, and stood up so that the drinking would not last any longer; he looked at his brother to pronounce judgment—: But from today onwards, our paths are separate.

他悄然离开了房间，四周一片寂静。马克西米利安还没能冷静下来，对刚才听到的话做出反应。抱怨像毒矛一样在他喉咙里乱窜，数量太多，却始终无法击中任何人。然而，他意识到自己并不想把这些抱怨发泄到皇帝身上。他跟着父亲走了出去。玛丽亚、菲利普和查理沉默了一会儿。

He left the room amidst the general silence. Maximilian had not yet found the composure to react to what he had heard. Complaints crowded in his throat chaotically, like poisoned spears that, too numerous, never quite managed to strike anywhere. However, he realized that it was not the emperor he wished to hurl them at. He followed his father out. Maria, Philip, and Charles remained silent for a moment.

“你没让任何人满意，”年轻人最后说道。

"You haven't pleased anyone," the young man finally said.

-沉默！

—Silence!

皇帝命令他们离开房间。独自一人时，他双手抱头，头骨疼痛难忍，仿佛有人在用锤子敲打他的头骨。提香的画像浮现在他的脑海中，画中他那庄严而又凄凉的身影。

The emperor ordered them to leave the room. Once alone, he buried his head in his hands. It ached as if his skull were being hammered. Titian's portrait came to mind, and his figure in it, so dignified and yet so forlorn.

 

 

 

 

“害虫保护幼崽都比你保护你儿子强！”马克西米利亚诺在走廊里追上父亲时斥责道。

"Vermin protect their young more than you protect your son!" Maximiliano rebuked his father when he caught up with him in the hallway.

费尔南多转过身，脸涨得通红：他简直不知所措。

Fernando turned around and showed a flushed face: he was beside himself.

我还能怎么办？！把家庭一分为二吗？！

—What other option did I have?! Divide the family in two?!

费尔南多从儿子的眼神中察觉到了轻蔑。

Fernando perceived contempt in his offspring's gaze.

—你的同意毁了我的未来！

—By consenting, you have ruined my future!

不，是我把你从深渊中救了出来。为此，我不得不屈辱自己。

—No; I have saved you from the abyss. And I had to humiliate myself to do so.

—我绝不会接受如此不配的遗产！

—Never, never will I accept such an unworthy inheritance!

说完这番话，马克西米利亚诺像幽灵一样消失在走廊尽头：迅捷、难以捉摸，心中只有复仇的渴望。

After saying this, Maximiliano disappeared down the corridor like a specter: swift, elusive, and possessing nothing but the desire for revenge.

 

 

 

 

仅仅几天后，在一片参天大树如方尖碑般耸立、苔藓遍布的森林里，一场会议召开了。与会者蹑手蹑脚、疑神疑鬼地到来，不时回头张望，搜寻间谍。他们装扮成乌鸦，用尽可能低沉的声音互相问候。他们也低声谈论着德国的未来。他们一遍又一遍地重复着：“一个外国人将统治我们。”想到这里，他们怒火中烧，几乎要喊出来。愤慨之情很快被策略所取代。绝望的人低声说，米尔贝格让他们损失了兵力和资源。热情高涨的人迅速回应道：“结盟。”不时有夜鸟的鸣叫声惊扰了他们；他们花了些时间才鼓起勇气再次谈论阴谋，但最终，他们还是这么做了。最后，一个“乌鸦人”问道：“然后呢……怎么办？”回答来自一个在整个会议过程中都保持沉默的人。

Just a few days later, in a forest of trees as tall as obelisks and mossy ground, a meeting took place. The participants arrived stealthily and suspiciously, peering behind them, searching for spies. Dressed as crows, they greeted each other in the lowest tones they could muster. They also spoke in murmurs about the future of Germany. A thousand times they repeated: "A foreigner will rule us," and it was hard not to shout it, so infuriated were they by the thought. Indignation gave way to strategy. The despairing whispered that Mühlberg had left them depleted in troops and resources. The ardent ones were quick to reply: "Alliances." From time to time, the hooting of nocturnal birds startled them; it took them a while to feel confident enough to speak of conspiracies again, but in the end, they did. Finally, one of the crow-men asked, "And then... what?", and the answer came from one who had remained silent throughout the assembly.

——皇帝孤身一人。我向你保证，他的兄弟不会与他作战。

—The emperor is alone. I promise you his brother will not fight with him.

那是马克西米利安的声音。

It was Maximilian's voice.

你负责招募士兵，我负责选拔未来永远的领袖。

—You take care of recruiting men. I'll take care of the one who will lead them all, now and forever.

 

 

 

 

法国国王亨利仔细观察着他的谈话对象，但更重要的是，他观察着对方是如何审视他的。自从登基以来，这位法国君主一直很在意自己给人的印象。他的父亲无论在体魄还是精神上都如此威严，以至于他担心自己的继承人可能无法被他人完全认真对待。这位年轻人经常对着镜子练习庄重的手势和严肃的表情。那天下午，他把这些表情也用在了正在急切讲话的客人——一位新教王子身上。

Henry of France studied his interlocutor, but above all, he observed how the other was studying him. Since ascending the throne, the French monarch had been concerned about the effect he had on others. His father's figure had been so magnificent, in both body and spirit, that he feared his heir might not be taken entirely seriously. The young man often practiced grave gestures and stern looks in front of the mirror. That afternoon, he bestowed a few upon his guest, a Protestant prince who was speaking urgently.

“殿下，请帮助我们摆脱凯撒！”改革者恳求道。

"Help us rid ourselves of Caesar, Your Highness!" pleaded the reformer.

亨利一听到皇帝的名字，便在王座上挺直了身子。看到君主的这一本能举动，王子胆子也大了。

When he heard the emperor mentioned, Henry straightened up on the throne. Witnessing the monarch's instinctive gesture, the prince was emboldened.

—为此我们需要男性，因为我们能执行这项任务的人手不足。

—For this we ask for men, since we have few available for such a mission.

“男人？”蒙莫朗西插话道，疑惑地打量着他的君主。“基督教国王的旗帜与新教徒联合起来了？”

"Men?" Montmorency interjected, and scrutinized his lord doubtfully. "The banners of the Most Christian King united with the Protestants?"

——这项事业是崇高的：你将成为德国人民的解放者。如此一来，你将赢得他们永远的支持。

—The cause is worthy: you will become the liberator of the German people. In doing so, you will gain their eternal support.

顾问的语气带着责备。他知道，华丽的辞藻往往是为了掩盖糟糕的交易。然而，令他惊讶的是，恩里克竟然表现出了兴趣：

The advisor reacted with a censured tone. He knew that grandiloquence often served to disguise bad deals. However, to his surprise, Enrique showed interest:

——我能从中获得什么好处？“捍卫德国自由意志”这个头衔在我看来远远不够……

—What would I gain in return? The title of safeguard of German free will doesn't seem sufficient to me…

“我们将协助你征服位于洛林的帝国教会中心：梅斯、凡尔登和图勒。”这位王子显然不是空手而来。

"We will facilitate your conquest of the ecclesiastical seats of the Empire located in Lorraine: Metz, Verdun, and Toul." The prince had certainly not traveled to France empty-handed.

亨利没有过多拘束，反而以一种略显浮夸的方式，冷淡地礼貌地打发了那位德国王子，让他等着自己的答复。王子离开后，国王开始在御座厅里踱步，心神不宁。蒙莫朗西叫住了他，走上前去：

Without much ceremony, and displaying one of his grand gestures, Henry dismissed the German with cold politeness and told him to await his reply. Once the prince had left, the king began pacing the throne room, driven by unease. Montmorency stopped him in his tracks and approached him:

“这些立场并非无关紧要，但我劝你仔细考虑一下。与分裂分子打交道，你会危及与罗马的关系！”

"These are not insignificant positions, but I would encourage you to think it through carefully. You would be risking your relationship with Rome by dealing with schismatics!"

这位君主显得紧张不安，做出了防御性的回应：

The sovereign, nervous, responded defensively:

我曾向父亲发誓，我要与皇帝作战！

—I swore to my father that I would fight against the emperor!

看来凯撒的领土终将导致他的垮台。我劝您好好欣赏这一幕，大人。

—It seems Caesar's domains will see to his downfall. I advise you to enjoy being a witness, my lord.

亨利认真考虑过这个问题。德国局势的确极不稳定，皇帝也因家族分裂而处于低谷。或许蒙莫朗西是对的，查理的战败迟早会到来，而法国无需为此付出一分钱。

Henry considered it. It was true that the situation in Germany seemed extremely unstable, and that the emperor was at a low ebb because of the schism within his family. Perhaps Montmorency was right, and Charles's defeat would come sooner or later, without France having to contribute a single coin to it.

但这位君主的心智却无法完全忍受这种冷静，他的思绪很快滑向了更为本能的场景。亨利心想，自己究竟要做出多少惊天动地的举动才能赢得世人的尊重。他的父亲在登基不久便征服了米兰，从此在世人心中声名鹊起。也正是在那时，人们才以亨利所期盼的方式看待他：带着敬仰和敬畏，如同看待一位法国国王应有的姿态。

But the monarch's mind could not quite tolerate such level-headedness, and it slipped into more visceral scenarios. Henry wondered how many grandiose gestures he would have to make to earn the world's respect. His father had risen to prominence in the imagination of men when he conquered Milan shortly after ascending the throne. He was then, and only then, regarded in the way Henry wished to be regarded: with admiration and awe, as one should regard a king of France.

“我在临终前向他发誓，”他坚持说，但同时又没有透露，他要与新教徒并肩作战的真正原因是，他终于觉得自己配得上王位。

"I swore it to him on my deathbed," he insisted, while keeping to himself that the real reason he was going to fight alongside the Protestants was to finally feel worthy of his crown.

 

 

 

 

数周后，一份小册子送达德意志宫廷，它是印刷机的产物，也是反抗皇帝情绪的激昂之作。内容简短，它想要在帝国境内传播的思想无需长篇大论。它鼓励人们起来反抗那个不久将篡夺他们身份的人；反抗“外国人”，也就是腓力二世。

Weeks later, a pamphlet arrived at the German court, a product of the printing press and a spirit inflamed against the emperor. The text was brief; the idea it sought to spread throughout the Empire needed no lengthy lines. It encouraged them to rise up against the one who, before too long, would usurp their identity; against "the foreigner," that is, Philip.

卡洛斯刚读完那份诽谤信，便不屑地将其揉成一团。寄信给他的阿尔巴公爵则冷冷地看着他的主人。

No sooner had he read it than Carlos crumpled the libel in contempt. The Duke of Alba, who had sent it to him, looked grimly at his master.

—无论谁写下它，他都了解关于你继承权的约定。

—Whoever wrote it knows the pact regarding your succession.

皇帝勃然大怒。这的确是事实，而且令人毛骨悚然。

The emperor turned livid. It was true, and terrifying.

——费尔南多或马克西米利亚诺背叛了我。——他立刻纠正自己——：一定是我的侄子。

—Fernando or Maximiliano betrayed me. —He immediately corrected himself—: It must have been my nephew.

你为什么如此肯定你哥哥对你忠诚？他甚至都不再跟你说话了。

—Why are you so sure that your brother is loyal to you? He has even stopped speaking to you.

—我不需要听到他的声音就知道他无法说出什么话。

—I don't need to hear his voice to know what he is incapable of saying.

皇帝从公爵的表情中意识到，他并不像自己那样确信。查理心事重重，疑虑重重，于是坐下来给哥哥写信。

The emperor realized, from the duke's expression, that he did not share his certainty. With his soul troubled by doubt, Charles sat down to write to his brother.

 

 

 

 

费尔南多很快就做出了回应：

Fernando's response was not long in coming:

 

 

陛下，您的处境令我深感痛惜。但这完全是您咎由自取。如果您重视我的意见，就应该与敌人谈判。在这样的事情上，我将全力支持您。但我很遗憾，我必须拒绝与您为敌。

Your Majesty, your situation grieves me greatly. But you alone are responsible for it. If you value my opinion at all, negotiate with the enemy. In such a cause you will have my support. But I regret that I must refuse to fight against you.

 

 

——费尔南多的话是出于怨恨，而不是背叛——当卡洛斯怒火中烧地把信给玛丽亚看时，玛丽亚插话道。

—Fernando's words are born of resentment, not betrayal—María interjected when Carlos, consumed by anger, showed her the letter.

那女人看上去筋疲力尽。曾经令她痛苦不堪的弗兰德斯政权，与她现在所做的事情相比，简直是小巫见大巫。调解兄弟之间的纷争，就像身处战场中央，士兵们非但没有疲惫，反而随着时间的推移愈发强大；而鉴于最近发生的事情，这种比喻似乎很有可能成为现实。

The woman looked exhausted. The government of Flanders, which had once caused her so much anguish, seemed like a simple task compared to what she was now doing. Arbitrating between her brothers was proving to be like standing in the middle of a battle where the soldiers, with the passage of time, grew stronger instead of weary; and given recent events, that metaphor seemed likely to become a reality.

“他拒绝为我辩护！”卡洛斯反驳道。

"He refuses to defend me!" Carlos retorted.

——你倒不如拔剑对付他的儿子！如果你是他，你会怎么做？

—Raise your sword against his son, rather! What would you do in his place?

卡洛斯想了想。

Carlos thought about it.

大家都理解他，可是告诉我！我该怎么办？难道要让我的女儿成为寡妇，让我的兄弟没有孩子吗？

—Everyone understands him, but tell me! What am I to do? Leave my daughter a widow, and my brother without a child?

 

 

 

 

更糟糕的是，就在皇帝觉得情况不可能更复杂的时候，阿尔瓦公爵前来报告说，法军已经入侵洛林。查理作为统治者，经验丰富，他不会相信巧合；毫无疑问，法国和德国叛军是一伙的。

To make matters worse, just when the emperor couldn't imagine a more complicated situation, the Duke of Alba arrived to report that French troops had invaded Lorraine. Charles had enough experience as a ruler behind him not to believe in coincidences; without a doubt, France and the German rebels were acting together.

 

 

 

 

—加入我们。

—Join us.

费尔南多茫然地望着他的儿子。

Fernando, disoriented, gazed at his son.

你想要什么？

—What do you want?

—你将领导这场起义，最终获得你应得的、凯撒一直剥夺你的权力：权力。

—That you take the lead in this revolt and finally obtain what you deserve and what Caesar has always denied you: power.

他的父亲瘫坐在皇宫会客厅的扶手椅里。命运之轮再次转动，让他回到了他习以为常的境地：徘徊在阴谋的边缘，身处进退两难的困境之中。

His father sank into an armchair in the imperial palace's drawing room. The wheel turned again, leaving him in the same place he was accustomed to: on the verge of conspiracy, in the uncertain terrain of dilemma.

—如果你觉得自己没有能力做出决定，别担心：王子们会替你做决定。

—If you don't feel capable of making the decision, don't worry: the princes will do it for you.

“你这话是什么意思？”但马克西米利安沉默不语。“你不会愿意杀了查尔斯吧？”

"What do you mean?" But Maximilian remained silent. "You wouldn't be willing to kill Charles, would you?"

年轻人语气平静地回答道，他确信自己站在正义的一边：

The young man replied phlegmatically, so sure was he that he was on the side of justice:

除了他，还有谁在这片土地上制造紧张局势？除了他，还有谁一次又一次地羞辱我们，对我们的牺牲毫无感激之情？他不把你当兄弟，就不要把他当兄弟。让德国拥有它应有的未来，让你们重获本应拥有的荣耀。

—Who but him is causing tension in these lands? Who humiliates us time and again, showing no appreciation for our sacrifice? Do not treat him like a brother when he does not treat you like one. Give Germany the future it deserves, and you the glory you should always have possessed.

 

 

 

 

于是，马克西米利安率领叛军出征。他留下父亲独自承受着巨大的精神压力，几乎无法呼吸。他知道，无论父亲做出怎样的决定，都将失去一位亲人。

So Maximilian marched off to lead the rebels. He left his father in a state of turmoil, barely able to breathe. He knew that whatever decision he made, he would lose one of his own.

 

 

 

 

积雪覆盖着查理骑马穿过的德国森林，两侧是士兵，雪还在下。他们身着白色盔甲，宛如战争雕像。皇帝紧紧握住缰绳，向前走去，却不露丝毫恐惧，因为他知道自己无能为力。尽管他拥有军队，但天主教诸侯们却刻意与皇帝和改革派之间即将到来的冲突保持距离，他们深知，与改革派对抗只会在各自的领地内引发冲突。此外，他们对皇帝的忠诚度也在逐渐下降。查理曾犹豫是否要将帝国传给儿子，但很少有人相信他不会再次改变主意，而受制于一个卡斯蒂利亚人的统治似乎荒谬至极，他们一定会毫不犹豫地反抗。尽管费迪南德出生于西班牙，但如今已无人视他为外国人。多年生活在那片土地上，使他理所当然地成为了最地道的德国人。

The snow had carpeted the German forest through which Charles rode, flanked by soldiers, and it continued to fall. Their white armor gave them the appearance of war statues. The emperor clung to the reins of his horse and advanced without betraying the fear he felt, for he knew himself to be helpless. Although he had troops at his disposal, the Catholic princes had distanced themselves from the imminent confrontation between the emperor and the reformers, knowing that taking a stand against them would bring conflicts within their own domains. Besides, loyalty to the emperor had been steadily waning. While Charles had hesitated to transfer the Empire to his son, few believed he wouldn't change his mind again, and the prospect of being under the rule of a Castilian seemed grotesque, an imposition they would not hesitate to rebel against. Although Ferdinand had been born in Spain, no one considered him a foreigner anymore. So many years in those lands had rightfully made him the most authentic of the Germans.

 

 

 

 

一行人穿过寂静的雪原前行。突然，他们听到马蹄声如雷鸣般朝他们奔来。士兵们举起了武器。直到凯撒转过身，看清来人是谁，才下令收起武器：是他的兄弟。费迪南德喘着粗气才开口说话。他刚才那场艰苦的骑行让他精疲力竭。

The group advanced through the silence of the snowy landscape. Suddenly, they heard the thunder of horses galloping toward them. The soldiers raised their weapons. Only when the Caesar turned and saw who was approaching did he order them to sheath their arms: it was his brother. Ferdinand had to catch his breath before he could speak. His agonizing ride had left him exhausted.

王子们切断了通往因斯布鲁克的道路。你们必须逃走！

—The princes have cut off the road to Innsbruck. You must flee!

查尔斯盯着他。他哥哥的表情难以辨认，嘴唇冻得发紫。他的肌肉因寒冷而麻木，让人无法分辨他脸上是同谋还是敌对的神色。皇帝警惕地一动不动。

Charles stared at him. His brother's expression was barely discernible, his lips blue with cold. His muscles were paralyzed by the temperature; it was impossible to tell if his face was one of complicity or that of a rival. The emperor, wary, didn't move.

“你再这样下去，必死无疑！”费尔南多厉声说道。

"If you continue, you're headed for certain death!" Fernando insisted.

“我为什么要相信你？我求你帮忙，你却选择抛弃我，任由我自生自灭。现在你还来守护我有什么意义？”

"Why should I trust you? I begged you for help and you chose to abandon me to my fate. What would be the point of you watching over me now?"

雪下个不停。兄弟俩面对面站着，在皑皑白雪的掩映下，仿佛渐渐变成了幽灵。

The snow fell relentlessly. Standing facing each other, the brothers, beneath the white blanket, seemed to be turning into ghosts.

——即便我们走上了不同的道路，我也绝不会让他们杀害你。你永远都是我的兄弟。

—Because even though our paths have diverged, I would never let them kill you. You are still my brother.

卡洛斯仍然无法参透费尔南多的意图。他必须决定是否服从费尔南多，而这完全取决于他对费尔南多话语的信任，取决于他对那份家庭情谊的信念——尽管此刻，这种信念对他来说已难以相信。

Carlos still couldn't decipher Fernando's intentions. He would have to decide whether to obey him or not based solely on his faith in those words, on that feeling of family that, at this point, was difficult to believe.

作为交换，饶我儿子一命。你饶他一命。

—In return, spare my son's life. Yours for his.

 

 

 

 

皇帝的少数士兵背弃因斯布鲁克，仓皇逃窜。天气恶劣：凛冽的寒风一路肆虐，他们翻越山口时，马匹经常在湿滑的地面上滑倒，生命危在旦夕。

The emperor's few troops turned their backs on Innsbruck and fled. The weather was merciless: the icy wind lashed them throughout their escape, endangering their lives as they crossed the mountain passes, where the horses frequently lost their footing on the wet ground.

查理拒绝回头。被迫逃离自己的领地所带来的屈辱，反而让他感到无比欣慰。他做梦也想不到，这位基督教世界最有权势的人，竟然要为了保命而仓皇逃亡，而他的性命竟受到了他视为封臣之人的威胁。

Charles refused to look back. The humiliation of being forced to flee his own lands was enough to make him revel in it. He would never have imagined that the most powerful man in Christendom would have to slip away to save his life, which had been threatened by those he considered his vassals.

突然，地平线上出现了一道缝隙。暴风雪停了，太阳穿透云层，洒了下来。对皇帝来说，这日出的味道从未如此像日落。

At one point, a break appeared on the horizon. The snowstorm was ending, and the sun was breaking through. Never before had a sunrise tasted so much like sunset to the emperor.

16

16

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

那天早晨，杜罗河水奔腾而过托尔德西利亚斯宫。前几天一直下着瓢泼大雨。胡安娜听着河水的潺潺声，心想这和她奔涌的血液多么不同。她的血液已经缓慢而粘稠地在她血管里流淌了一段时间，四肢也开始坏疽。女王知道，这是她几十年来久坐不动的生活习惯的必然结果。她的身体勉强维持了生命，在她看来，实在是太久了。

That morning, the Duero River flowed powerfully past the palace of Tordesillas. The rains had been heavy in the preceding days. Juana heard the murmur of the river and thought how little it resembled the torrent of her blood, which for some time now had flowed sluggishly, thickly through her arteries, gangrenous in her limbs. The queen knew that this would be the outcome of the sedentary routine she had followed for decades. Her body had endured long enough to stay alive; in her opinion, far too long.

她双腿疼痛难忍，却默默忍受着。如果说她有什么过人之处，那就是能坦然接受伤痛，仿佛它无关紧要。真正折磨她的是，这种不适让她无法集中精力回忆往事，而今天，这种不适丝毫没有减轻她的痛苦。

The pain in her ailing legs was unbearable, but she endured it stoically. If there was one thing she was adept at, it was accepting the damage as if it were inert. What tormented her was that the discomfort prevented her from concentrating on her memories, and that day it was giving her no respite.

女王听见脚步声，微微抬起头，离开了靠垫。很快，门口出现了一个黑影。那人影让她想起了他。

The queen heard footsteps and lifted her head slightly from her cushion. Soon, a shadowy figure appeared in the doorway. It reminded her of him.

我是费利佩。

—I am Felipe.

是他！他终于要把她带到他身边了！她的身体重新充满了血液，喜悦的泪水涌上了眼眶。

It was him! He was taking her to his side, at last! The blood flowed through her body again and tears of happiness welled up in her eyes.

那人影向前走了几步，就足以粉碎他们的幻想。

The figure advanced inwards just a couple of steps; enough to shatter their illusions.

——你的孙子。

—Your grandson.

胡安娜凝视着他。然后她自嘲地笑了笑，任由为丈夫涌出的泪水顺着脸颊滑落。擦干眼泪后，她挣扎着坐了起来。

Juana stared at him. Then she laughed at herself and let the tears that had sprung up for her husband slide down her cheeks. After wiping them away, she struggled to sit up in bed.

——以他的名字命名的那座。

—The one that bears his name.

她示意他过来坐下。费利佩在附近的扶手椅上坐了下来。他用一种虚伪的眼神凝视着祖母，仿佛面对死亡却不愿示人。

She gestured for him to join her. Felipe took a seat in a nearby armchair. He gazed at his grandmother with the deceitful eyes of someone who faces death but refuses to show it to others.

你在这里做什么？

—What are you doing here?

他的孙子没有告诉他真相：这次探访不过是弗朗西斯·博尔吉亚强加给他的惩罚。这位曾是葡萄牙女王伊莎贝拉的御马大臣，女王去世后被迫遁入空门的男子，认为菲利普必须亲眼目睹女王的不幸，才能让他不再感到与自己的命运格格不入。一段时间以来，这位继承人对自己生活的方方面面都感到不满。他憧憬着自己的晚年生活，希望能够娶一位像父亲爱他母亲那样，让他全心全意爱着的妻子。然而现实是，他已经三十多岁了，是个鳏夫，而且只对情妇有过类似的感觉。此外，帝国是他政治生涯的巅峰，但它却将永远掌握在他叔叔的手中，更糟糕的是，他的父亲还在蓄意削减他的继承权。几周前，皇帝在梅斯战役中战败。法国在争夺帝国教会要塞的战争中取得了决定性的胜利，这三个重要的主教辖区失守不仅是一次挫折，更是一个不祥之兆。据说查理一世身患痛风，行动不便，却依然出现在战场上；他的双手甚至无法握住宝剑，而且不顾顾问们的劝阻，坚持延长战争。因此，皇帝的病情不仅是生理上的，也是判断力的问题：他做出了明显荒谬的决定。菲利普继承的一切——无论是皇位本身，还是外交冲突和宗教困境——都掌握在一个已经不堪重负的人手中。

His grandson refrained from telling him the truth: that this visit was nothing more than a penance imposed by Francis Borgia. The man who had been Master of the Horse to Isabella of Portugal, and whom her death had driven to become a monk, had deemed it necessary for Philip to witness the queen's misfortune, so that he might cease feeling alienated from his own fate. For some time now, the heir had been dissatisfied with every aspect of his existence. When he imagined himself in his later years, he pictured himself married to a woman to whom he could feel devoted, as his father had been to his mother, but the reality was that, at over thirty, he was a widower and had only ever felt anything similar for a mistress. Moreover, the Empire was his political horizon, but it was going to remain indefinitely in the hands of his uncle, and, to make matters worse, his father was deliberately diminishing his inheritance. Weeks earlier, the emperor had been defeated at Metz. France had decisively won the war for the imperial ecclesiastical strongholds, three important bishoprics whose loss was not only a setback but, above all, a bad omen. It was said that Charles had appeared on the battlefield despite being crippled by gout; that his hands hadn't even been able to grasp his sword and that he had insisted on prolonging the war against the advice of his counselors. The emperor's illness, therefore, was not only physical but also a matter of judgment: he made decisions that were clearly absurd. Whatever Philip inherited—the legacy itself, but also the diplomatic conflicts and religious dilemmas—was in the hands of a man for whom the title was already too much.

但对皇帝如此严厉的评判令他的儿子倍感煎熬。他对父亲的敬爱促使他宽恕父亲的一切过错；然而，他内心深处的政治家却幻想着尽快夺取政权。他精力充沛，头脑清醒！万一皇帝再活二十年呢？菲利普的黄金岁月岂不将被浪费在摄政和包办婚姻上？“如果你为未来担忧，就帮助你的父亲，”博尔哈曾劝告他，“在他软弱时给予他力量，在他犯错时给予他指引。”继承人觉得这个建议合情合理，但却难以平息他的不安。如同以往许多次一样，查理在儿子心中激起了一种复杂的情感，一种爱与反叛交织的复杂情绪。

But judging the emperor so harshly tormented his son. The devotion he felt for him urged him to forgive all his faults; yet the statesman within him fantasized about seizing power as soon as possible. He was so brimming with energy and lucidity! What if the emperor lived, say, for another twenty years? Philip's prime would have been wasted on regencies and arranged marriages. "If you are worried about the future, help your father," Borja had advised him, "giving him strength if you see him weak and counsel when he errs." The heir found the suggestion sensible, but it did little to quell his unease. As on so many occasions, Charles stirred in his son an ambiguous emotion, a mixture of love and rebellion.

“夫人，您这是什么意思？我是来看看您的，”孙子回答胡安娜说，“您感觉怎么样？”

"What do you mean, my lady? I came to check on you," the grandson replied to Juana. "How are you feeling?"

伊莎贝尔和费尔南多的女儿疲惫地过了一会儿才回答：

Isabel and Fernando's daughter, tired, replied after a while:

我的双腿已经失去了知觉。它们花了四十年才明白，在这里它们对我毫无用处。

—My legs no longer respond. It's taken them forty years to understand that they're of no use to me here.

“四十年了，”费利佩心想。在年轻人的心中，如同在所有人心中一样，胡安娜女王与其说是个人，不如说是传说。她的囚禁无人质疑，也无人探究她过去是怎样的人，在托尔德西利亚斯宫的高墙之内，她的人生究竟是如何消逝的，更无人质疑囚禁她的决定是否公正：无视她，便成了逃避这种虐待行为带来的罪恶感的一种方式。

Forty years, Felipe thought. In the young man's mind, as in everyone else's, Queen Juana was more legend than human being. Her confinement was not debated, and no one questioned what she had been like in the past, what life had slipped away from her within the walls of the Tordesillas palace, or whether the decision to imprison her had been just: ignoring her was a way of avoiding the guilt of such sadism.

但站在她面前，明知她已被判死刑，继承人第一次想象她年轻时的样子，那时她也和他一样充满抱负和渴望。他凝视着那张七十岁的老脸，凭借想象力，抹去皱纹和病痛的痕迹，展现出表象之下真实的自我。他看着祖母的眼睛：尽管她举止庄重，但她的眼神却透露出她并非对自己的衰老漠不关心，她渴望活力，也渴望得到他人的爱。她接受了别人灌输给她的观念：她已不再是无用之物。然而，她的灵魂渴望像孩子一样被爱，直到生命的最后一刻。这一切都让菲利普感到难以承受的悲伤。

But standing before her, aware of her death sentence, the heir imagined her young for the first time, with ambitions and desires like his own. He gazed at that seventy-year-old face and, with his imagination, stripped it of wrinkles and signs of ill health, revealing the person behind the appearance. He looked into his grandmother's eyes: though the woman's bearing was hieratic, her gaze betrayed that she was not at all indifferent to her decline, and that she longed for vitality as well as for the affection of others. She had accepted what she had been led to believe: that she was a useless object. And yet her soul yearned to be loved like a child, and would do so until her last breath. All of this filled Philip with unbearable sadness.

不，他不想让同样的事情发生在他父亲身上。诚然，他是皇帝，是未来将要统治的疆域的君主；但归根结底，他是一个正在走向衰落的人，眼睁睁地看着生命流逝却无能为力，无可挽回，无力回天，无力阻止 ...

No, he didn't want the same thing to happen to his father. It was true that he was the emperor, the ruler of the lands he would one day govern; but above all, he was a man facing his decline, undoubtedly suffering as he watched life slip away without being able to do anything to stop it, as he erred unintentionally and lost the respect of those who had always admired him.

那一刻，费利佩全心全意地爱着他。

At that moment, Felipe loved him with all his heart.

 

 

 

 

格兰维尔红衣主教走进皇帝的寝宫，发现他斜倚在书桌前，目光呆滞地盯着一台拆卸下来的钟表零件。他清了清嗓子，想把他从沉思中唤醒。

Cardinal Granvelle entered the emperor's bedchamber and found him reclining at his desk, his gaze fixed on the pieces of a disassembled clock. He cleared his throat to rouse him from his reverie.

“进来坐下吧，亲爱的格兰维拉。”凯撒头也不抬地说道。

—Come in and sit down, dear Granvela —said the Caesar without taking his eyes off his task.

顾问遵命行事。这间房间仿佛与宫廷其他地方隔绝开来。在那里，时间如同浓稠的液体般凝固，寂静无声，让人觉得生命仿佛被拒之门外，永不开启。

The advisor obeyed. The room seemed a world apart from the rest of the court. There, time had the consistency of a thick liquid, and the silence made one think that life remained at the door, never to enter.

“一座圣杰罗姆修道院，”格兰维拉说道。

"A Hieronymite monastery," Granvela said.

卡洛斯突然来了兴趣，看向了他。

Suddenly interested, Carlos looked at him.

“他在哪里？”他问道。

"Where is he?" he inquired.

—在卡斯蒂利亚。在拉维拉地区。

—In Castile. In the region of La Vera.

皇帝点了点头。他的眼神闪烁不定：他开始想象那一幕了。

The emperor nodded. His eyes moved playfully: he was beginning to imagine it.

“这符合我的意愿吗？”他问道。

"Does this fit with my wishes?" he asked.

—如果你真像你跟我说的那样渴望宁静，那当然可以。你也知道，这片地区阳光充足，修道院周围环境优美，有树林和小溪。

—If you seek peace as much as you told me, then certainly. The region, as you know, is very sunny, and the surroundings of the abbey are beautiful, with groves and streams.

凯撒闭上双眼，踏上了前往彼岸的旅程。他心满意足地笑了。

Caesar closed his eyes to travel there. He smiled contentedly.

“安排好一切，”他说道。

"Arrange everything," he declared.

顾问没有点头，他看起来很担忧。

The advisor did not nod; he seemed worried.

陛下，您坚持您的想法吗？

—Do you insist on that idea of ​​yours, Your Majesty?

“你说我一时兴起？退休是我很久以来做过的最明智的决定。”他注意到格兰维拉对他的回答有些不安。“别用那种告别的眼神看着我。你比我更清楚，在我母亲去世之前，我无法安息。只有她去世后，我才能卸下在卡斯蒂利亚的指挥权，但那之后，一切才会真正结束。”

"A whim, you say? Retiring is the best idea I've had in a long time." He noticed Granvela's uneasy reaction to the reply. "Don't look at me with such farewell eyes. You know better than I that I won't be able to rest until my mother does. Only when she passes away will I be able to relinquish command in Castile, but that will be followed by the rest."

只有上帝才能罢免君主。

—Only God should remove sovereigns.

虚荣心驱使那些明知自己无用之人继续执掌王位。恋栈权位只会给我的领地带来惩罚。即便查理曼大帝退位，我效仿他也不会有损我的荣誉。

—Vanity keeps on the throne those who know they are useless. Clinging to power would be a punishment for my domains. If Charlemagne abdicated, I do not diminish my honor by following his example.

自从在梅斯战役中被法军击败后，皇帝便认为自己的统治生涯已经结束。那场导致数百名士兵丧生的惨败，让他明白，恋栈权位比放弃权力更加不负责任。痛风使他身体僵硬疼痛，已无法再征战沙场，而他的决策也屡屡失策。战败之后，他便隐居在自己幽暗的寝宫之中。宫廷里的人都以为他又陷入了忧郁期，但事实上，他一如既往地需要时间和独处来反思，寻找解决之道。在那些反思的日子里，有时他的妹妹玛丽亚会陪伴左右，他意识到，作为一名政治家，他是一个失败者：他未能阻止基督教内部的分裂，而与法国频繁的战争更是使他的封地，尤其是卡斯蒂利亚，陷入了贫困。他曾竭尽全力遏制改革的推进，但始终以失败告终。罗马的确对解决这个问题毫无贡献，因为当它决定着手处理时，异端邪说已经像最致命的瘟疫一样蔓延开来。但他无法撇清自己的责任：他登基之初曾誓言捍卫自己的信仰，却彻底失败了。他仍然抱有希望，认为基督教的分裂是可以弥合的，但这必须由其他更强大、更开明的人来承担。而且越快越好。

Since his defeat at Metz by the French armies, the emperor considered himself finished as a ruler. That defeat, which resulted in the deaths of hundreds of soldiers, had made him understand that clinging to power was more irresponsible than renouncing it. His body, stiff and aching from gout, was no longer fit for battle, and his decisions were not proving wise. After that failure, he had retreated to the gloom of his bedchamber. Everyone at court believed he was going through one of his melancholic periods, but the truth was that, as always, he needed time and solitude to reflect and find a solution. During those days of reflection, sometimes accompanied by his sister Maria, he realized that, as a politician, he had been a failure: he had not stemmed the schism within Christianity, and the constant wars, too frequent against France, had impoverished his fiefdoms, especially Castile. He had tried everything to contain the advance of reform, but he had always failed. It was true that Rome had not contributed at all to solving the problem, for by the time it decided to address it, heterodoxy had already spread like the most virulent plague. But he could not absolve himself of blame: upon becoming emperor, he had pledged to defend his faith, and he had utterly failed. He still held out hope that the schism among Christians could be repaired, but it would have to be others, stronger and more enlightened, who took on the task. And the sooner, the better.

随后，凯撒的妹妹玛丽面带灿烂的笑容出现在房间里。

Mary, Caesar's sister, then appeared in the room with a radiant smile.

——你的儿子！

—Your son!

 

 

 

 

在格兰维尔、玛丽和继承人随从们欣喜的注视下，菲利普和查理拥抱了许久。皇帝随后凝视着他的孩子，仿佛仍然不敢相信自己刚刚踏足了弗兰德斯。

Philip and Charles embraced for a long time under the pleased gaze of Granvelle, Marie, and the heir's entourage. The emperor then gazed at his offspring, as if he still couldn't quite believe his visit to Flanders.

你在这里做什么？

—What are you doing here?

“我带来资金，是为了弥补您最近的开支。”卡洛斯显得有些慌乱，他的儿子注意到了。“父亲，我不会责怪您。我非常清楚，如果说有人后悔发生的一切，那一定是您。我相信我的到来也能抚慰您的心灵。”

“I bring you funds to replenish your coffers after… your recent ventures.” Carlos looked flustered, which his son noticed. “I don’t blame you for anything, Father. I know full well that if anyone regrets what has happened, it is you. I trust that my presence here will also serve as a balm for your spirits.”

凯撒动了。

Caesar was moved.

没有什么比这更让我高兴的了。

—Nothing could make me happier.

他们挽着胳膊，走开了。菲利普感到父亲的重量，紧紧抓住他以免摔倒：皇帝走路很吃力。查理注意到人们对他关切的目光。

They linked arms and walked away from the others. Philip felt his father's weight, clinging to him to keep from falling: the emperor was walking with difficulty. Charles noticed the concern with which he was being regarded.

——痛风。还有，像我这样的老人偶尔需要额外付出一些努力。

—Gout. And the occasional extra effort for an old man like me.

他的儿子突然变得激动起来，尽管他之前一直表现得有所保留：

His son suddenly became agitated, although he gave the impression that he had been holding back what he said for some time:

—就像因为你的兄弟拒绝与你并肩作战，你不得不逃离因斯布鲁克以保全性命一样！

—Like having to flee Innsbruck to save your life because your brother refused to fight with you!

凯撒被迫逃亡的经历在腓力心中扎根。当时，腓力试图阻止凯撒逃亡，给他提供金钱和资源以求自保，但如果没有他叔叔的帮助，所有这些援助都无济于事。

The escape that Caesar had been forced to make had taken root in Philip. At the time, he tried to prevent it by providing him with money and resources to defend himself, but all the help proved insufficient without that of his uncle.

—你对他的怨恨比我更深。

—You harbor more resentment towards him than I do.

——你怎么能为他辩护？如果他曾经帮助过你……！

—How can you defend him? If he had helped you…!

“是他干的！”卡洛斯打断道，“他警告过我即将发生的事情。多亏了他，我才能及时逃脱，并做好准备迎战法军……尽管收效甚微。”

"He did it!" Carlos interrupted. "He warned me of what was coming. Thanks to him, I was able to escape in time, and then prepare my armies to face the French... Although with little success."

费利佩对这个消息非常不满意。

The information did not please Felipe at all.

—我叔叔因为之前抛弃你而深感愧疚。但一个悔改的罪犯仍然要放在第一位！

—My uncle was consumed by guilt for having abandoned you before. But a repentant criminal still comes first!

皇帝停下脚步，仔细端详着他的儿子。他从儿子的眼神中看到了他一直祈祷不要看到的东西：对血亲的深深怨恨和仇恨。自从决定放弃王位以来，查理就一直饱受家族分裂的折磨，而他将把这种分裂留给菲利普。他发誓在退位前尽一切可能弥合裂痕。他确信这会很困难——斐迪南甚至没有回复他的信件——但他准备坚持不懈，并在必要时做出妥协，以免他儿子的未来被一场兄弟相残的斗争所玷污，而这场斗争在某种程度上正是他自己挑起的。他近期的失败让他变得谦逊：既然他自己都无法治理如此庞大的帝国，那么相信一个人有能力治理如此庞大的帝国似乎毫无意义。菲利普得到的支持越多，他成功的机会就越大。此外，新教问题悬而未决，基督教世界的未来取决于此，这在他看来，在帝国境内，甚至在居住于此的家族内部制造敌人，反而会确保改革者的胜利：他们会像往常一样，利用分歧来巩固自身地位。如果说查理一世最想清除的污点，那就是教会的分裂。要净化教会，就必须团结一致，并对过去的罪行予以谴责。

The emperor paused to scrutinize his son. He detected in his eyes precisely what he had prayed not to see: deep resentment and hatred for his own blood. Ever since he had decided to relinquish the throne, Charles had been tormented by the family schism he would bequeath to Philip. He had vowed to do everything possible to mend it before abdicating. He was certain it would be difficult—Ferdinand didn't even respond to his letters—but he was prepared to persist and compromise as needed so that his offspring's future would not be marked by a fratricidal struggle that, in one way or another, he himself had instigated. His recent failures had instilled humility in him: it seemed pointless to believe in the capacity of a single man to govern such a vast empire when he himself had been unable to do so. The more support Philip received, the greater his chances of success. Adding to this the fact that the Protestant question remained unresolved and that the future of Christendom depended on how it was settled, creating enemies within the Empire, within the very family that resided there, seemed to him a guarantee of victory for the reformers: as was their custom, they would exploit their differences to gain ground. And if there was one stain that Charles wanted to see removed, it was the division of the Church. To cleanse it, unity and disdain for past offenses would be necessary.

“你叔叔和我之间的故事比你想象的要复杂得多，”凯撒说道，“或许，仔细审视一番，如果我们把我们的罪行一一列举出来，我才是那个罪魁祸首……”

"The story between your uncle and me is more complex than you think," said the Caesar. "Perhaps, upon closer examination, if we list the offenses, I have been the villain..."

——可是父亲……！

—But Father…!

孩子，敌人是其他人。

—The enemies are others, my son.

费利佩没有回答，但他的表情表明，他根本没想过要原谅别人。

Felipe did not reply, but his expression suggested that forgiveness was far from his mind.

 

 

 

 

与皇帝重逢后，菲利普在宫中寻找姑姑埃莉诺。他发现她独自一人在房间里读书，她看起来很吃力，视力已经开始衰退。菲利普热情地问候了她，并送给她一件物品。那是一幅小画像，画中是一位年轻女子，五官精致，目光聪慧。埃莉诺被画中的含义所吸引，试图解读它。

After his reunion with the emperor, his son searched the palace for his aunt Eleanor. He found her reading in a solitary room; she was struggling, her eyesight beginning to fail. After greeting her warmly, Philip presented her with an object. It was a small portrait, depicting a young lady with delicate features and an intelligent gaze. Intrigued, Eleanor tried to decipher its meaning.

——你是谁？你在找新老婆吗？

—Who is it? Are you looking for a new wife?

—而我在你女儿身上找到了它。

—And I have found it in your daughter.

那幅画像从莱昂诺尔手中滑落，她顿时失去了镇定。费利佩在画像落地前接住了它，递给了他的姑姑。姑姑双手颤抖着接过画像。这位年轻人和其他人一样了解这段故事，他让莱昂诺尔静默片刻，让她自生下玛丽亚后第一次凝视着这位葡萄牙女王的画像。卡洛斯的妹妹震惊不已。她一遍又一遍地凝视着这位年轻女子的容貌，心中却只有一股难以言喻的感动。

The portrait slipped from Leonor's hands, her composure suddenly gone. Felipe caught it before it hit the floor and handed it to his aunt, who, with trembling hands, took it again. The young man, who knew the story as well as everyone else, granted Leonor a few moments of silence so she could contemplate Maria of Portugal for the first time since giving birth to her. Carlos's sister was stunned. She studied the young woman's features again and again, but felt little more than a profound emotion.

她给女儿写了一百封信。她从法国开始写信，因为在那里，在她独自度过的漫长时光里，女儿的身影始终萦绕在她心头，成为她唯一的陪伴。她曾考虑请求弗朗西斯允许她去葡萄牙：她想见见女儿。但这个念头既让她心动，又让她恐惧。她反复做噩梦，梦见玛丽亚轻蔑地斥责她，指责她犯了事实：她不是她的母亲。于是，她决定给女儿写信。如果只是没有收到回复，或许还能忍受些，而事实也的确如此。她的信一封也没有收到回复，但埃莉诺仍然坚持写信，她始终抱有希望，相信总有一天，玛丽亚会看到母亲的关心，也会厌倦怨恨，最终原谅她。如今，从弗兰德斯寄往葡萄牙的信件依然不断。在信中，凯撒的妹妹讲述了宫廷里的种种轶事，并请求原谅。这些信件的语气仿佛笃定自己一定会得到回复。莱昂诺从未流露出怨恨或悲伤。她只是想满足自己想要爱他的愿望，而她也确实做到了。

She had written her a hundred letters. She began in France, for there, in the many hours she spent alone, the memory of her daughter had been constant, her only company. She considered asking Francis to let her travel to Portugal: she wanted to meet her. But the prospect both attracted and terrified her. She had recurring nightmares in which Maria scorned her, accusing her of what was true: that she had not been her mother. She then decided to write to her. The rejection would be more bearable if it consisted of receiving no reply, as indeed happened. None of her letters received an answer, but Eleanor continued sending them, without losing hope that, one day, seeing her mother's concern and tired of holding a grudge, Maria would forgive her. Now, letters continued to be sent from Flanders to Portugal. In them, the Caesar's sister recounted anecdotes from the court and asked for forgiveness. The tone of these messages was that of someone who takes it for granted that they will be answered. Leonor never showed offense or sadness. She only wanted to satisfy her desire to give him love, and that's what she did.

你要娶她吗？

—Are you going to marry her?

——如果我父亲允许的话。

—If my father allows it.

“我不会允许他做出其他决定，”他的姑姑说。

"I won't allow him to decide otherwise," said his aunt.

他们相视一笑。女人从震惊中回过神来，情绪瞬间崩溃，哭了起来。她的侄子帮她擦去眼泪。

They smiled at each other. The woman recovered from her shock and her emotions overflowed. She cried. Her nephew wiped away her tears.

为什么是她？

—Why her?

他们说她既漂亮又聪明。他们说她和我一样热爱读书，而且……

—They say she's as beautiful as she is clever. That she loves reading, just like I do, and…

莱昂诺尔用眼神问他。费利佩不知该如何继续。事实上，他对这个年轻女子的感觉毫无缘由，这种感觉不断告诉他，他会在她身上找到真爱；他们会像卡洛斯和伊莎贝尔一样幸福地生活在一起，却又饱受分离之苦——而这种分离，这位继承人几乎无法想象自己会承受。

Leonor asked him with her eyes. Felipe didn't know how to continue. In truth, there was no reason for the feeling he had about this young woman, the feeling that kept telling him that with her he would find true love; that they would be the spitting image of Carlos and Isabel, happy together, tormented by those absences that the heir could scarcely imagine allowing himself.

费利佩盯着那幅画像，他的姑姑正拼命地紧紧抱着它。

Felipe stared at the portrait, which his aunt was desperately clutching.

那就这样吧。

—So be it for you.

女人带着激动的笑容道别。再次独自一人时，她突然泪如雨下。这是她第一次因为想起女儿而喜极而泣。她像个被啜泣声哄睡的婴儿，紧紧抱着照片，在扶手椅上睡着了。一个小时后，她惊醒过来：费利佩可能与玛丽亚订婚的消息并没有驱散她的噩梦。他的确能治好她女儿的病，但她女儿会愿意治她吗？

The woman said goodbye with an excited smile. When she was alone again, she burst into tears. For the first time, thinking of her daughter made her cry tears of joy. Like a baby lulled by her sobs, she fell asleep in her armchair, clutching the picture. She woke an hour later, startled: the news of Felipe's possible engagement to María hadn't banished her nightmares. It was true he could treat her daughter, but would her daughter want to treat her?

 

 

 

 

幸运的是，查理同意了儿子与葡萄牙公主的婚事。这桩婚事或许能抚慰埃莉诺多年来的苦难，这更增添了查理支持这门婚事的理由。这位皇帝一直背负着愧疚，因为他从未做出过任何能让妹妹过上哪怕是稍微幸福的生活的决定。即便他试图让她感到满足，让她登上法国王位，最终也只是让她过上了孤独寂寞的生活。虽然自重逢以来，埃莉诺从未向查理透露过她在法国宫廷的经历，但查理依然能感受到那段时期对她而言是多么煎熬。如今，妹妹已过了适婚年龄——这对她来说是一种真正的解脱——或许，多亏了与女儿的重逢，她才能在晚年获得她一直以来都渴望却始终无法企及的幸福。

Fortunately, Charles approved of the engagement between his son and the Portuguese infanta. The fact that this union could heal Eleanor's years of suffering added another argument in his favor. The emperor carried the guilt of never having made a decision that would have given his sister even a reasonably happy existence. Even when he tried to bring her contentment and placed her on the throne of France, all he had managed to do was condemn her to a life of companionable solitude. Although since their reunion Eleanor had never given him any details of her time at the French court, Charles had been able to sense the ordeal that period must have been for her. Now that his sister was no longer of marriageable age—a true liberation for her—perhaps, thanks to her reunion with her daughter, she could finally achieve in her later years the happiness that had always eluded her.

 

 

 

 

当得知皇帝已祝福玛丽亚和菲利普的婚事后，一直饱受噩梦困扰的埃莉诺登上了一艘前往卡斯蒂利亚的船。她没有过多解释此行的原因，因为真正的缘由太过私密，不便透露。她只向妹妹玛丽亚吐露了自己离开的真正动机：渴望与母亲胡安娜团聚。

When she learned that the emperor had blessed the marriage between Maria and Philip, Eleanor, who had been plagued by nightmares, boarded a ship bound for Castile. She didn't elaborate much on the reasons for her journey. The true reasons were too private to discuss. Only to her sister Maria did she confess what motivated her to leave: the desire to be reunited with her mother, Joanna.

 

 

 

 

女王感到有人握住了她的手。由于服药的缘故，她已昏昏欲睡，迷迷糊糊地转过身。过了好一会儿，她才认出那是自己的女儿。当她意识到这一点时，惊讶之情远胜于喜悦。

The queen felt someone take her hand. Her mind clouded by the sleep she was already experiencing due to the physicians' remedies, she turned around. It took her a while to recognize her daughter. When it dawned on her, the surprise was greater than the joy.

“痛苦让我重获名声，”他喃喃自语道。

"Agony has brought me back to fame," he murmured.

-母亲…

-Mother…

莱昂诺尔抚摸着胡安娜的手指，她的手指骨瘦如柴，皮肤苍白无力。

Leonor stroked Juana's fingers, which were bones covered with sad skin.

“我不想打扰您的休息，但我需要休息。”女王有些不知所措，只好让她继续说下去。“您冷落了我们，查尔斯、玛丽，还有我……”

“I don’t wish to disturb your rest. But I need to gain mine.” The queen, bewildered, let her speak. “You neglected us; Charles, Mary, me…”

凯撒的妹妹在旅途中反复练习这些话，直到她能将其中的情感剥离殆尽，才能勉强说出口。但母亲的出现让她的话语重新焕发了意义，埃莉诺努力克制住泪水，继续说道。

Caesar's sister had rehearsed those words a thousand times throughout the journey, until she had stripped them of enough emotion to be able to utter them. But her mother's presence restored meaning to her speech, and Eleanor struggled to hold back her tears and continue speaking.

——你忘记了我们，似乎并不后悔，就好像我们从未从你的子宫里出来过一样。你有了孩子，但你从未做过母亲。

—You forgot about us without seeming to regret it, as if we had never come from your womb. You had children, but you were never mothers.

—如果你不是想扰乱我的安宁，为什么还要提醒我所有的罪过？

—If you are not trying to disturb my peace, why do you remind me of all my sins?

母亲，您为他们付出了沉重的代价。而我们，您的子女，也犯下了不小的罪过。我们让您被囚禁在这里近半个世纪。我对您的思念，正如您对我的思念一样少之又少。

—Mother, you have paid dearly for them. And we, your children, have sinned no less. We have allowed you to remain locked up here for almost half a century. I have thought of you as little as you have of me.

胡安娜看到两滴眼泪顺着莱昂诺尔的脸颊滑落。

Juana saw two tears run down Leonor's cheeks.

“别自责了。你们怎么能像女儿一样对待一个没有给你们生母的人呢？”她坦然面对真相，没有丝毫责备。“我对丈夫的爱让我容不下其他任何东西。如果事情可以不一样，我会后悔的，但事已至此。”

"Don't blame yourselves. Why would you behave like a daughter to someone who hasn't borne you a mother?" she said without reproach, facing the truth head-on. "My love for my husband left no room for anything else. I would regret it if things could have been different, but they weren't."

她的女儿感到手上微微一紧。女王虽然反应很微妙，但这是她对女儿爱意的回应。莱昂诺尔擦了擦眼泪。

Her daughter felt a slight pressure on her hand. The queen was responding, albeit subtly, to her affection. Leonor wiped away her tears.

—让我们互相原谅吧。我们俩都原谅对方。让我们做回真正的母女，就这一次。

—Let's forgive each other. Both of us. Let's be mother and daughter, just for once.

-因为？

-Because?

—因为我和我女儿犯了和你一样的罪，我需要相信任何距离都可以被跨越，即使为时已晚。

—Because with my daughter I have committed the same sin as you, and I need to believe that any distance can be bridged, even if it is late.

胡安娜觉得她那时还记得感受到爱的滋味，尽管那种甜蜜而又令人妥协的情感对她来说似乎很奇怪，而且无论如何，她生活在将她与世界隔开的钟楼后面，她再也无法离开那里了。

Juana thought she remembered then what it was like to feel affection, although that sweet and compromising emotion seemed strange to her, and in any case, she lived behind the bell that separated her from the world and from which she could no longer leave.

—如果那样能让你感到平静，那就这样吧。

—If that brings you peace, so be it.

莱昂诺尔露出了喜悦的笑容，但笑容很快又被泪水所掩盖。随后，两人陷入了沉默。对她们两人来说，这比假装亲密要自在得多。但女王还是努力尝试着与人亲近。

Leonor let out a joyful smile that was soon mingled with tears. Then there was silence. It was more comfortable for both of them than feigning familiarity. But the queen made an effort.

——你的兄弟们怎么样了？卡洛斯怎么样了？

—How are your brothers? How is Carlos?

——精疲力竭，心灰意冷。

—Exhausted. And withdrawn.

胡安娜笑了。

Juana smiled.

她跟我一样，已经厌倦了这些噪音。

—She's like me. She's already tired of the noise.

 

 

 

 

从见到母亲的那一刻起，莱昂诺尔就感到内心平静下来。然而，历史再次违背了她的意愿。

From the moment she met her mother, Leonor felt her soul ease. But, once again, history chose to turn against her wishes.

“你们不能辜负命运赐予我们的这个机会。玛丽·都铎已经登上英格兰王位，而且她是未婚的。”

"You cannot afford to reject this opportunity that fate has given us. Mary Tudor has ascended the throne of England, and she has done so unmarried."

菲利普惊讶地盯着他的父亲。皇帝趁他沉默不语，开始列举这桩婚姻的种种好处。

Philip stared at his father in astonishment. Taking advantage of his silence, the emperor launched into a list of the advantages of the marriage.

“有很多改革派觊觎王位，如果她无嗣而终，他们就会夺取王位。让她结婚，给她立个继承人，天主教就能在英国延续下去！而且，它在欧洲的影响力也会增强。德国将会发现自己是唯一一个身处异端邪说之中的人。”

"There are many reformist aspirants to that throne, which they would seize if she were to die without issue. Marry her, give her a successor, and Catholicism would be perpetuated in England! Moreover, it would be strengthened in Europe. Germany would find itself alone in heresy."

查理一言不发，等待儿子的答复，但儿子仍未开口。菲利普惊恐万分，难以接受命运的捉弄。皇帝察觉到了他的茫然。

Charles remained silent to allow his son's reply, which still hadn't come. Philip was petrified, coming to terms with the twist of fate. The emperor noticed his bewilderment.

儿子，我们本应携手为基督徒的合一而努力。我曾担心自己在这方面失败了，但毫无疑问，上帝想给我们机会来弥补我的失败。

—Son, you and I would work together for the unity of Christians. I feared I had failed in that endeavor, but without a doubt God has wanted to give us the opportunity to redeem my defeat.

——你是想让我远离帝国吗？你打算用这种方式与你的兄弟和解吗？

—Are you trying to distance me from the Empire? Is this how you plan to reconcile with your brother?

“我想让你当英格兰国王！”查理回答道，他开始对儿子缺乏热情感到厌倦。“你将以一个宏伟的封地扩张帝国。”

"I want to make you King of England!" replied Charles, who was beginning to tire of his son's lack of enthusiasm. "You will expand the Empire with a magnificent fiefdom."

凯撒像父亲一样把手放在他的肩膀上。但对方却畏缩了一下。

Caesar placed his hand on his shoulder, paternally. But the other man recoiled.

——那并非我的计划。我的意愿难道不被考虑吗？

—Those were not my plans. Are my wishes not taken into account?

—你的愿望就是我告诉你的！

—Your wishes are those I dictate to you!

费利佩胸口剧烈起伏，怒火几乎难以抑制。他想起了那个他永远无法娶到的妻子，那个他曾感觉能找到幸福真谛的女人。他永远也无法知道了。在葡萄牙，解除婚约会被视为一种罪过，断送了两人重归于好的可能。这时，伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥的身影浮现在他的脑海。在前往弗兰德斯之前，费利佩以与这位葡萄牙女子的婚约为借口，结束了与她的恋情。当她告诉他他们不能再见面时，他的心仿佛停止了跳动。他仍然能感受到爱人深邃的眼神刺痛着他的记忆，痛苦的记忆如同刻骨铭心的利刃。但他渴望拥有父母婚姻所象征的理想：娶自己所爱之人，爱自己所娶之人。

Felipe's chest heaved rapidly. His anger could barely be contained. He thought of the wife he would not take, the one with whom he had sensed he would find the key to his happiness. He would never know. Breaking off the engagement would be seen in Portugal as an offense that would preclude any second chances. Then Isabel Osorio came to mind. Before leaving for Flanders, and using his engagement to the Portuguese woman as an excuse, Felipe had ended their romance. His heart had stopped dead when she told him they could no longer see each other. He still felt the dark eyes of his lover piercing his memory, a stark reminder of the pain. But he aspired to the ideal of which his parents' marriage was the model: to marry whom he loved, to love whom he wed.

既然他的命运注定要去英国，而他的妻子除了清教徒和相貌丑陋的名声之外，他对她一无所知，那么牺牲伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥在他看来似乎是一个残酷而无用的步骤。

Now that his destiny was to be England, and his wife a woman about whom he knew nothing except her reputation as a puritan and unattractive, sacrificing Isabel Osorio seemed to him a cruel and useless step.

尽管如此，菲利普还是低头服从。他的责任感根深蒂固，以至于他甘愿忍受痛苦，或许直到生命的尽头。

Despite all this, Philip bowed his head in obedience. His sense of duty was so deeply ingrained that he accepted being unhappy, perhaps until the end of his days.

他最后的希望寄托在那个英国女人不同意这门婚事上，但她很快就从岛上发来了同意书，甚至还表现出了热情。

He placed his last hopes on the British woman not agreeing to the marriage, but her acceptance soon arrived from the islands, and even displayed an enthusiastic tone.

父子二人告别时都感到尴尬。父亲犹豫着是否要将只有他和格朗维尔知道的事情告诉继承人：他打算尽快退位。他想，或许如果菲利普意识到继承王位的时刻即将到来，那么接受与英国女王联姻的苦果就会更容易下咽。但他最终还是决定保持沉默；这是一件敏感的事情，一旦说出口，恐怕只会带来更多的失望而非希望。他只希望儿子能与英国女王幸福地生活在一起。他自己与伊丽莎白的婚姻最初也是出于权宜之计，但正是这段婚姻孕育了无与伦比的爱情。

The farewell was awkward for both father and son. The father hesitated to share with his heir what only he and Granvelle knew: his intention to abdicate as soon as possible. He thought that perhaps if Philip saw the moment of receiving his inheritance approaching, the bitter pill of the English marriage would go down more easily. But he decided to keep quiet; it was a delicate matter that, if revealed, could breed more frustration than hope. He contented himself with wishing his son hope that he would find happiness with the English queen. His own marriage to Elizabeth, too, had been one of convenience at first, and from it had sprung an incomparable love.

费利佩很想相信她，但当他见到未婚妻的那一刻，他就知道自己会想念他的爱人。

Felipe wanted to believe her, but as soon as he met his fiancée, he knew he would miss his lover.

 

 

 

 

玛丽·都铎从阿拉贡的凯瑟琳那里继承的不仅是虔诚的宗教信仰，还有坠入爱河的能力。当提香为菲利普所作的画像——皇帝特意送来的——抵达宫廷时，她才真正体会到爱情的真谛。当她看到画中这位年轻英俊的男子时，她立刻感到自己需要他。皇帝的使节对菲利普的描述——他举止优雅、温柔体贴、忠于职守——最终促使她下定了决心。在此之前，男人对她来说是一种威胁，她不愿靠近。父亲的记忆让她认为男性是自私自利的化身，是伤害他人的源泉。由于她从未确信自己能够继承王位——爱德华六世国王和他的继任者简·格雷夫人必须在她登基之前去世——她一直对婚姻避之不及。她从未体验过肉体之爱，想象中它充满了阳刚之气、嘲弄和无情，因此她一点也不怀念。她的贞洁是她的独立，也是她永远不会像母亲那样遭受奴役的保证。

Mary Tudor had inherited from Catherine of Aragon not only religious devotion but also the capacity to fall in love. When a Titian painting of Philip—which the emperor had taken the trouble to send—arrived at her court, she discovered what love truly was. The moment she saw this man, rendered in brushstrokes, so young and handsome, she felt she needed him. What the emperor's ambassador told her about him—that he was elegant in his manner, sensitive, and committed to duty—sealed her decision. Until then, men had represented a threat she didn't want near her. The memory of her father had led her to judge masculinity as the epitome of selfishness and the gift for causing harm. Since she had never had any certainty of ascending the throne—King Edward VI and his successor, Lady Jane Grey, had to die before she could reign—she had turned her back on the idea of ​​marriage. Physical love, which she was unfamiliar with, she imagined as everything virile, mocking, and merciless, and therefore she didn't miss it at all. Her virginity was her independence, and the guarantee that she would never suffer a slavery like her mother's.

但提香的画像仿佛一件魔物，令她着迷，使她放弃了长久以来坚守的信念。突然间，她渴望亲吻画中那双鲜红的嘴唇，拥抱那身着盔甲、显得庄严雄伟的身躯；她梦见嗅闻他的气息，梦见爱上他。以至于他抵达英国宫廷的这段时间，对玛丽亚来说仿佛漫长得如同永恒。

But Titian's portrait, as if it were a magic object, bewitched her, making her renounce the convictions she had held for so long. Suddenly, she longed to kiss those red lips she saw painted, and embrace the robust body that appeared dignifiedly clad in armor; she dreamed of smelling him and of falling in love with him. So much so that the time it took for him to arrive at the English court seemed to Maria an eternity.

 

 

 

 

菲利普在威风凛凛的随从簇拥下出现在未婚妻面前，令王后惊愕的是，他比提香画作中的形象还要英俊。玛丽亚见到他时紧张不已，尽管她强装镇定。由于她不了解恋爱中的男人会如何表现，她并没有将菲利普礼貌却冷淡的态度解读为轻蔑，她仍然希望这段婚姻能够开花结果。

Philip appeared before his betrothed escorted by an imposing retinue and, to the queen's dismay, even more handsome than depicted in Titian's painting. Maria was overcome with nerves when she saw him, though she feigned composure. Since she didn't know how a man in love behaved, she didn't interpret Philip's polite but cold demeanor as disdain, and she wanted to believe that love would blossom in this union.

玛丽亚的迷恋人尽皆知，唯有她的未婚夫感到痛苦。皇帝的儿子回想起已故的玛丽亚·曼努埃拉初次与他相遇时带给他的感觉：毫无感觉。为了避免在不可避免的现实面前活在否认之中，他将注意力集中在政治上：登上英格兰的王位或许值得他做出这样的牺牲。但未婚妻对他的爱让他想起了自己与第一任妻子的经历。那些单相思的女人，就像她们一样，眼神中流露出的悲伤深深地刺痛了他。没有什么比一个知道自己被爱的女人更美的了；伊莎贝尔·奥索里奥的眼神就让他明白了这一点。

Maria's infatuation was obvious to everyone, though painful only for her fiancé. The son of the emperor recalled the feeling the late Maria Manuela had evoked in him during their first encounter: none. To avoid living in denial in the face of the inevitable, he focused his attention on the political matter: sitting on the throne of England might well be worth that sacrifice. But his fiancée's love for him reminded him of his own experiences with his first wife. The sad gazes of unrequited women, like those women, wounded him deeply. Nothing was more beautiful than a lady who knew she was loved; Isabel Osorio's eyes had shown him this.

然而，菲利普最终承认，玛丽亚对他的感情对他来说……很有用。英国议会对他们的君主与这位卡斯蒂利亚女子的婚约充满疑虑。在他们看来，这位皇帝的儿子权力过大，他们担心他的王国最终会被他日后继承的帝国吞并。玛丽亚要想获得议会的同意，唯一的办法就是限制菲利普的权力：他永远只能是她的配偶。当菲利普得知自己的身份后，他勃然大怒。如果他不爱这个女人，那他娶她又有什么意义呢？他唯一的目的就是统治英格兰。由于这项条款必须在婚礼前签署，菲利普威胁说，如果他不被承认为拥有司法权和在欧洲大陆运用英国军队的权力的君主，他将解除婚约。然而，议会拒绝了他的请求。卡斯蒂利亚国王绝望了，若非玛丽亚恳求的眼神让他看到了未来命运的转机，他或许早已启程前往弗兰德斯。王后害怕菲利普会抛弃她，便承诺会尽快扩大他的权力。从她绝望的语气中，她的未婚夫明白她说的都是真话：她会不惜一切代价留住他。

However, Philip eventually admitted that Maria's feelings for him were… useful to him. The English Parliament viewed their sovereign's engagement to the Castilian with suspicion. The son of the emperor seemed excessively powerful to them, and they feared that his kingdom would eventually be swallowed up by the Empire he would one day inherit. The only way Maria could gain their consent to the union was by agreeing to limit Philip's authority: he would never be more than a mere consort. When he learned of his intended status, he erupted. If he didn't love this woman, what was the point of marrying her, when his only motivation was to rule over the English? Since the clause had to be signed before the wedding, Philip threatened to break off the engagement if he wasn't recognized as monarch with the power to administer justice and to use the British armies for his interests on the continent. However, Parliament refused to grant him this favor. The Castilian king despaired, and would have been capable of embarking for Flanders had he not found, in Maria's pleading eyes, the promise that his situation would change in the future. The queen, terrified at the possibility of Philip abandoning her, promised to expand his powers as soon as possible. And in the desperate voice with which she spoke, her betrothed understood that she was telling the truth: she would be capable of anything to keep him by her side.

婚礼终于举行，菲利普加冕为英格兰国王。

The wedding finally took place, and Philip was crowned King of the English.

 

 

 

 

皇帝之子登上英国王位的消息在欧洲引起了广泛关注。如果说查理一世相对于世界其他国家而言已经展现出令人畏惧的强大实力，那么他的儿子则正在成为更大的威胁。不出所料，最大的恐惧降临在了法兰西王国。

The emperor's son ascending the British throne did not go unnoticed in Europe. If Charles had already proven insultingly powerful compared to the rest of the world, his son was on his way to becoming an even greater threat. And, as could be expected, the greatest fear was unleashed in the kingdom of France.

亨利在梅斯击败皇帝后，他渴望荣耀的愿望终于实现。在他与凯撒的首次交锋中，他不仅取得了胜利，还彻底摧毁了敌人的声誉，使他看起来像个垂垂老矣的老人。对于这位高卢君主而言，梅斯之战标志着一个神话的终结和另一个神话的诞生：他自己的神话。

With his victory over the emperor at Metz, Henry's aspiration for glory had been fulfilled. In his first battle against the Caesar, he had not only emerged victorious but had also tarnished his enemy's reputation, leaving him looking like a decaying old man. For the Gallic monarch, Metz had marked the end of one myth and the birth of another: himself.

然而，胜利带来的短暂平静很快就被皇帝篡夺权力、将儿子扶上英格兰王位的举动打破。这一举动预示着法国将面临可怕的未来，法国从此彻底被哈布斯堡王朝吞并。亨利八世凝视着欧洲大陆的地图，感到一阵窒息。

But the tranquility that followed that triumph, though lasting, was shattered by the emperor's power grab of placing his son on the throne of England. That maneuver foreshadowed a terrible future for France, which was now definitively absorbed by Habsburg power. When Henry studied the map of the continent, he felt breathless.

尽管他的国库和蒙莫朗西都不建议发动任何进攻，但这位君主开始在心中构思，如何在这令人窒息的景象中开辟出一条呼吸的通道。

And although neither his coffers nor Montmorency advised any attack, the sovereign, in his mind, began to conceive of a way to open, in that suffocating panorama, a hole through which to breathe.

 

 

 

 

陛下：来自卡斯蒂利亚的紧急来信。

—Your Majesty: urgent letter from Castile.

查理从格兰维尔手中接过信件；信件已被庄严地封缄。当他展开信件时，皇帝的目光仿佛出于本能地被标题中的一句话所吸引，这句话用优美的字体写着：公元1555年4月12日，在托尔德西拉斯宫，最杰出的胡安娜王后逝世了。

Charles took the epistle from Granvelle's hands; it had been solemnly sealed. When he unfolded the sheet, the emperor's eyes were drawn, as if by instinct, to a phrase in the heading, which stated, in beautifully drawn letters, that in the palace of Tordesillas, on the 12th day of April in the year of our Lord 1555, the most excellent Queen Juana had died.

 

 

 

 

为纪念皇帝母亲而举行的葬礼大厅，墙壁上挂满了黑色帷幔，与消息传来后整个宫廷的着装一致。外面的光线透过帷幔洒进来。在这片漆黑之中，只有皇后的纹章格外醒目。

The walls of the hall where the funeral rites in honor of the emperor's mother were held were draped in black cloths, matching the attire of the entire court since the news arrived. The light from outside was filtered through the curtains. The queen's coat of arms was the only exception amidst so much darkness.

在为逝者举行葬礼弥撒时，卡洛斯从他优越的地位出发，想到自己是个孤儿，已经没有上一代人可以保护他免于死亡。如果自然规律主宰一切，下一个死去的便是他。然而，这并没有让他感到痛苦。自从伊莎贝尔去世后，他便坦然接受了死亡：无论他能活多久，美好的事物都不会再回来了。

While the funeral mass was being held for the deceased, Carlos, from his privileged position, reflected that, as an orphan, there was no longer a generation to protect him from death. If the logic of nature prevailed, he would be the next to die. However, this did not torment him. Since Isabel's passing, he accepted mortality without sorrow: however long he lived, the best of things would never return.

然后——当主持仪式的神父用拉丁语将他轻轻托起时——他想起了母亲。他回忆起他们初次相遇的情景：胡安娜隐于阴影中，他畏缩在母亲神秘的身影前，她的手搭在他的肩上，那种焦虑，以及尽管触碰彼此却依然遥不可及的距离。卡洛斯从小就是个孤儿，尽管他的姑姑玛格丽塔竭力想让他忘记这一点。但随着岁月的流逝，他对他人——那个无助孩子的——的顾虑渐渐减少，他无疑爱着！他的兄弟姐妹，他的孩子，以及对妻子的思念。至于他的母亲，他多么希望自己也能有同样的感觉。这些年来，他偶尔会去看望她，在圣诞节，有时只是为了愧疚。在那些探望中，他们很少说话，却彼此心意相通，有时卡洛斯渴望拥抱她，渴望感受到自己不再像个皇帝，而像个儿子。但胡安娜从不允许这种情感流露；她生活在一个独立的世界里，比任何人想象的都更通情达理，却又不可侵犯。她怎么能为此受责备呢？自我封闭是他母亲忍受这个世界的唯一方式。而现在，他也要效仿她，让自己承受她所遭受的禁锢。

Then—as the priest officiating the ceremony cradled him in Latin—he thought of his mother. He recalled their first meeting: Juana in the shadows, him cowering before the mystery of his mother, her hand on his shoulder, the anxiety, the infinite distance between them despite their touch. Carlos had never been anything but an orphan, though his aunt Margarita had tried hard to make him forget it. But, as the years passed, his scruples toward others, those of a helpless child, had diminished, and he loved, undoubtedly! His siblings, his children, the memory of his wife. As for his mother, he would have liked to feel the same. He had visited her from time to time over the years, at Christmas, and other times for no other reason than guilt. During those visits they spoke little but understood each other, and at times Carlos longed to embrace her and feel less like an emperor than a son. But Juana never allowed for such affection; she existed in a separate reality, more sensible than anyone thought, but inviolable. How could she be blamed for that? Self-absorption had been the only way his mother had found to endure the world. And now he was going to imitate her, imposing upon himself the confinement she had suffered.

 

 

奉我之命，于公元10月25日，在布鲁塞尔法院召集你们。你们不得拒绝或推迟执行此遗嘱，此乃命令。届时，我期望你们所有人，务必准时到场……

It is my command to summon you on the 25th of October in this year of our Lord, at the court of Brussels, giving you no option to refuse or postpone compliance with this will, which is an order. On that date, I expect you all, without fail, here at my side…

 

 

那天，在布鲁塞尔皇宫的大厅里，一把略微抬离地面的椅子空着。皇帝召见的众人侧目望着椅子，开始入座。许多人不得不站着；荷兰的显赫人物无一缺席。不久，皇室成员也加入了他们：玛丽和埃莉诺手挽手走进来，随后菲利普也出现了。所有人的目光都转向了他：许多人认为这位卡斯蒂利亚人将成为当天的焦点。这位皇位继承人感到百目瞩目，这种感觉令他十分愉悦。他在贵宾席中落座，靠近为查理准备的椅子。

That day, in the royal hall of the Brussels palace, a chair, slightly raised off the floor, awaited empty. Opposite it, glancing at it sideways, those summoned by the emperor began to take their seats. Many had to remain standing; no illustrious figure from the Netherlands was absent. Soon the imperial family joined them: Mary and Eleanor entered arm in arm, and shortly afterward, Philip appeared. All eyes turned to him: many believed the Castilian would be the star of the day. The still-heir felt a hundred eyes upon him, and the sensation pleased him. He took his place among the seats of honor, near the chair awaiting Charles.

过了一会儿，马克西米利安走了进来。菲利普一见到他，就立刻警觉起来。由于周围都是人群，而且他的表兄马克西米利安还挽着妹妹玛丽亚的胳膊一起来了，凯撒的儿子才没有对他发起攻击。他等到马克西米利安在自己附近坐下后，才咬牙切齿地用尽全力开口。

After a while, Maximilian entered. Upon seeing him, Philip went on his guard. The fact that the crowd surrounded them and that his cousin arrived arm in arm with his sister Maria prevented the Caesar's son from attacking him. He waited until the other man settled into a seat near his own before addressing him through gritted teeth, but with all the force he could muster.

你们竟敢出现在这里？我可以以叛国罪逮捕你们。

—How dare you show yourselves here? I could have you arrested as traitors.

马克西米利亚诺显得很冷静。

Maximiliano appeared phlegmatic.

“违抗皇帝的命令就是叛国罪，”他回答道，同时向他的表弟展示了一封与菲利普收到的信件一模一样的信。

"It would be treasonous to disobey the emperor's orders," he replied, showing his cousin a letter identical to the one Philip had received.

皇帝的儿子先是愣了一下，但随即明白了。他父亲无疑是在试图抚平家族的创伤。

The emperor's son was taken aback, though he understood immediately. His father was undoubtedly trying to lick the family's wounds.

众人入座后，谈话声渐渐安静下来。大家都在翘首期盼皇帝驾临，并想知道此次会面的目的。在场的每个人都提出了自己的猜测。

Once everyone had taken their places in the room, the conversations quieted down. There was anticipation to see the emperor and to learn the reason for the meeting. Each person in the room had come up with their own hypothesis.

 

 

 

 

缓慢而断断续续的脚步声从大厅附近传来，​​在场众人心跳加速，纷纷转过身去。只见皇帝站在门槛下，倚靠在奥兰治的威廉的肩上——这位年轻的弗拉芒国务委员会成员，多年后将因建立荷兰王国而名垂青史。查理在众人屏息凝神、翘首以盼的寂静中，缓缓走向高高的座椅。最终，在奥兰治的威廉的搀扶下，他落座。他环视众人片刻，心中难过。他曾写过一封比其他人更长、更真挚的信邀请斐迪南前来，如今斐迪南却缺席了。

Slow, irregular footsteps echoed from the vicinity of the hall. The palpitations of those present reached their peak. They turned. The emperor stood beneath the threshold of the entrance, leaning on the shoulder of William of Orange—a young member of the Flemish Council of State who, years later, would leave his mark on history by founding the Dutch nation. Charles leisurely covered the distance to the elevated chair, amid the expectant silence of the audience. Finally, assisted by William of Orange, he took his seat. He gazed at the gathering for a moment. The absence of Ferdinand, whom he had invited with a longer and more heartfelt letter than those sent to the others, saddened him.

我想用我自己的话告诉你们几件事。我的母亲，在离这里不远的地方生下了我，最近在卡斯蒂利亚去世了。她的慷慨让我十七岁就统治了那个王国。后来，我年轻时就被授予了帝国的荣耀。最终，我统治了阿拉贡、弗兰德斯、那不勒斯、西西里以及海外领土。

—I want to tell you a few things in my own words. My mother, who brought me into the world not far from here, recently passed away in Castile. Her generosity led me to govern that kingdom in the seventeenth year of my life. Then, while still a young man, I was granted the honor of the Empire. In time, I was to rule Aragon, Flanders, Naples, Sicily, and the overseas territories.

皇帝停顿了一下，喘了口气，仿佛仅仅是列举自己的财产就让他精疲力竭。大殿里，此刻的寂静比以往任何时候都更加令人窒息。

The emperor paused to catch his breath, as if the mere enumeration of his possessions exhausted him. In the hall, the silence was then more resounding than ever.

我的一生就像一连串的旅程，这些旅程不仅耗尽了我的身体，而且常常让我与我最爱的伙伴们分离：我的孩子们……还有我的妻子，我本想把我的所有时光都献给她们。

—My life has been a string of journeys, which have not only consumed this body of mine, but have frequently torn me away from my most beloved companions: my children… and my wife, to whom I would have liked to give all my days.

查理回忆起伊莎贝拉时，声音哽咽了。在皇帝身边，菲利普像往常一样缅怀母亲，也像往常一样，感动得热泪盈眶。

Charles's voice broke as he remembered Isabella. At the emperor's side, Philip evoked his mother as he did every day, and as every day, he was moved to tears.

——召唤我的不仅仅是职责。战争也给我和我的领地带来了痛苦。我总是出于义务而战，为了捍卫自己免受他人的野心侵害：土耳其人，我视他为我唯一的敌人；还有那个诅咒般的国王，弗朗西斯，对我来说就是如此。

—It wasn't just duty that called me. To my torment and that of my domains, so did wars. I always fought out of obligation, to defend myself against the ambition of others: the Turk, whom I considered my only enemy; and that curse made king that was Francis for me.

当他想起自己永远的对手时，凯撒脸上浮现出一丝疲惫而又怀旧的微笑。

As he remembered his eternal rival, a slight smile, weary but also nostalgic, appeared on the Caesar's face.

“我还得应对帝国境内的异端邪说。我没能像我希望的那样彻底平息这场危机。”他脸上浮现出一丝羞愧。“但所有这些劳作，都比不上我现在离开你时所感受到的痛苦和悲伤。”

"I also had to combat the outbreak of heresy within the Empire itself. A danger I haven't been able to quell as I would have liked." Shame crept across his face. "But none of those labors was more painful or grieved me as much as the one I feel now in leaving you."

虽然无人开口，但旁观者中弥漫着震惊之情。离开他们？皇帝要退位吗？他难道不应该像所有君主一样，脚先着地离开吗？以他的地位，这样的辞职简直是难以置信的谦卑之举。

Although no one spoke, astonishment was palpable among those who listened. Leave them? Was the emperor abdicating? Wouldn't he leave his post feet first, like all sovereigns? The resignation seemed an act of inconceivable humility in someone of his rank.

“我已无力治理上帝赐予我的诸州，我所剩无几的精力也将很快耗尽。我如此疲惫，无法像我的继承人那样为你们效力。”

"I no longer have the strength to govern the states God granted me, and what little strength I have left will soon be gone. Being so weary, I can render you no service, as those who receive my legacy will."

客人们的惊讶很快转为钦佩，他们惊叹于这位来自根特的男士的谦逊。随后，他将目光锁定在菲利普身上，菲利普似乎被即将发生的事情所震撼，挺直身躯站在他面前。

The guests' surprise turned to admiration at the modesty of the man from Ghent. He then fixed his eyes on Philip, who, shaken by what was to come, stood tall before him.

我的儿子菲利普将继承西班牙、佛兰德斯、意大利和印度的土地。至于帝国……帝国将继续由我的兄弟费迪南德的后裔统治，我本希望能够亲眼看着他，将这份荣耀授予他的后裔。

—My son Philip will receive Spain, Flanders, the Italian lands, and those of the Indies. And the Empire… the Empire will remain in the hands of the lineage of my brother Ferdinand, whom I would have wished to look in the eye as I bestowed such an honor upon his lineage.

听到这个决定，菲利普脸色苍白。他笔直地站在众人面前，被剥夺了基督教世界仅次于教皇的最重要头衔，而剥夺他这一头衔的，竟然是他自己的父亲，而且是出于自愿。他坐了下来。尽管他竭力掩饰自己的失望，但查理还是看在眼里，马克西米利安也同样动容。马克西米利安生平第一次，用感激的目光望向皇帝。皇帝注视着他的侄子，眼神中既有宽恕，也有责任。这位有责任感的年轻人点了点头。来自根特的皇帝回到了房间里。

Philip paled upon hearing the decision. There he stood, erect before everyone, stripped of the most important title in Christendom alongside the papacy, and the one denying it to him, of his own free will, was his own father. He sat down. Although he tried hard not to show his disappointment, it did not escape Charles's notice, nor did it escape Maximilian's emotion, who, for the first time in his life, looked at the emperor with gratitude. As he gazed at his nephew, the emperor's eyes held absolution, but also a sense of obligation. The responsible young man nodded. The emperor from Ghent returned to the room:

我知道我的兄弟会以他一贯的卓越才能治理国家，并且会因我的儿子成为他最忠诚的盟友而感到欣慰，他也会回报我儿子的忠诚。尽管敌人众多，但唯有我们团结的力量，才能战胜他们。

—I know my brother will govern with the same brilliance he has shown, and with the joy of having my son as his most loyal ally, whom he will reciprocate. Though there are many enemies, the strength of that union, and only that, can defeat them.

菲利普点了点头，但他远不满意。查理的目光紧紧盯着宾客们，逐一打量着他们。他们不过是一群男男女女，但在皇帝眼中，他们代表着他所有的臣民，代表着他四十年来孜孜不倦奉献的子民。

Philip nodded, though he was far from satisfied. Charles's gaze was fixed on the guests. He looked at them one by one. They were just a group of men and women, but to the emperor they represented all his subjects, those to whom he had devoted himself relentlessly for forty years.

——现在，我要离开了。我感激你们的付出，也相信你们会原谅我所有的过错。我即将前往西班牙，永不回头。孩子们，再见了，我会永远把你们放在心上。

—And now, I leave you. I am grateful for your service as much as I trust you will forgive all my failings. I will soon depart for Spain, never to return. Farewell, my children, for I carry you in my heart.

一片寂静。奥兰治的威廉扶起皇帝，再次向他搭上肩膀，送他走向门口。此时，门口已是宾客云集，气氛沉重。他走过时，人们纷纷行礼，落泪。查理走到大厅门口时，也忍不住流下了眼泪。

Silence fell. William of Orange helped the emperor to his feet and offered him his shoulder again on the way to the door, which by then resembled a corridor of emotional guests. As he passed, gestures of respect and tears were repeated. When he reached the threshold of the hall, Charles shed a tear.

 

 

 

 

夜幕降临布鲁塞尔，菲利普走进父亲的卧室，站在门口。

Night had fallen on Brussels when Philip entered his father's bedroom and stood by the door.

“过来，”等着他的凯撒说道。

—Come closer —said Caesar, who was waiting for him.

他的儿子一动不动地站在原地。

His son did not move from the spot.

——父亲，我心情有些烦躁，不太想见他。

—My mood is somewhat agitated for this meeting, Father.

这就是我给你打电话的原因。

—That's why I called you.

菲利普沉思片刻后，上前走到父亲面前。皇帝正站着，倚靠着一根雕工精美的权杖。

After pondering for a few moments, Philip advanced until he stood before his father. The emperor was standing, leaning on a finely carved staff.

“你骗了我，”年轻人指责道，“据我所知，英国一直把我流放，目的是剥夺我的帝国。”

"You lied to me," the young man accused. "As I knew, England has been an exile to strip me of the Empire."

“总有一天，而且不会太久，你会感谢我让你失去他。你不会想承受我哥哥和他的儿子将来要背负的重担。”

"One day, and not too far off, you will thank me for depriving you of him. You wouldn't want the burden my brother and his son will have to bear for yourselves."

——我想要它！这是基督教最伟大的成就！

—I want it! It's the greatest achievement of Christendom!

卡洛斯冷哼了一声，带着讽刺意味。

Carlos let out an ironic snort.

——这是惩罚！开销、异端邪说、背叛……战争！而且他们的未来看起来更加黯淡。

—It's a punishment! Expenses, heresy, betrayals… Wars! And their future looks even bleaker.

费利佩无法否认这是事实，但他仍然感到失望。

Felipe could not deny that it was true, but he remained disappointed.

你是我的长子！

—You are my firstborn!

年轻人抬起头，看到父亲眼中噙满了泪水。

The young man looked up and saw his father's eyes, wet with emotion.

“世上没有什么比你更重要，我的儿子……”凯撒心碎地将手放在菲利普的肩上。“我希望你能明白。你将继承我王冠上的瑰宝：忠诚的西班牙，宝藏般的印度，我的意大利王国，以及我出生的富饶土地……”

“Nothing in the world matters more to me than you, my son…” The Caesar, heartbroken, placed his hand on Philip’s shoulder. “I wish you could understand. You receive the jewels of my crown: loyal Spain, the treasure that is the Indies, my kingdoms of Italy, and the rich lands where I was born…”

这位已是欧洲最有权势的人注意到父亲颤抖的手，凝视着他疲惫的双眼。查理的表情仿佛渴望被理解。菲利普想起自己曾说过的话：“不要相信任何人。”他自己也确实做到了。但如果说这条忠告对他来说总有一个例外，那就是皇帝。尽管他们之间冲突不断，但他从未动摇过对皇帝判断的信任。渐渐地，他的内心平静下来：他要信任他。

The man who was already the most powerful in Europe noticed the trembling in his father's hand and gazed into his weary eyes. Charles's expression was that of a man desperate to be understood. Philip then recalled his words: "Trust no one." That was what he had done. But if that advice had always had one exception for him, it was the emperor. Although their clashes had been numerous, he had never lost faith in his judgment. Little by little, his soul calmed: he would trust him.

——请原谅我。请原谅我，父亲。

—Forgive me. Forgive me, Father.

凯撒感激地抚摸着儿子的脸颊。

The Caesar, grateful, stroked his son's cheek.

我不想只留给你们物质财富，也想传授你们人生经验。对家庭的忠诚是你们将获得的最宝贵的财富。

—I don't want to bequeath you just possessions, but also lessons. Loyalty to family is the greatest asset you will gain.

费利佩点了点头。尽管他需要克服内心的不安才能遵守这条原则，但他愿意这样做。

Felipe nodded. Despite the misgivings he would have to overcome to obey that principle, he was willing to do so.

——没有人能像你一样完成我和命运托付给你的使命。你可是将异端邪说从英格兰彻底根除的人啊！

—No one will fulfill what destiny and I have entrusted to you as you have. The man who has eradicated heresy from England!

查理还没有机会祝贺他的儿子在登上英国王位后不久取得的成就：卡斯蒂利亚和玛丽·都铎签署了王国回归罗马的条约。

Charles had not yet had the opportunity to congratulate his son on the achievement he had obtained shortly after ascending the British throne: the Castilian and Mary Tudor had signed the return of the kingdom to obedience to Rome.

“她已经开始为自己的未来做准备了，因为她怀了个孩子，是个继承人。”费利佩笑着说，他之前一直把这个消息藏在心里。“我妻子在我来这里之前就告诉我了。”

—And she's already taking care of her future thanks to the heir she's expecting— smiled Felipe, who had kept the news to himself until then. —My wife told me about it before I left for here.

“你果然没让我失望！”凯撒满意地说道，脸上洋溢着笑容。

"You are incapable of disappointing me!" exclaimed the Caesar, beaming with satisfaction.

他们深情地对视着，彼此间的紧张气氛完全消散了。

They looked at each other tenderly. The tension between them had completely dissipated.

“我会尽快去你的静修处拜访你，”儿子肯定地说。

"I will visit you at your retreat as soon as I can," the son affirmed.

皇帝否认了此事。

The emperor denied it.

“我以亲身经历知道你将要面对的挑战。你没时间在修道院里浪费。”费利佩吃了一惊。“别担心，我会没事的。而且，我终于可以安宁了。”

"I know from experience the work that awaits you. You won't have time to waste in a monastery." Felipe was taken aback. "Don't worry, I'll be fine. And at peace, finally."

—不……我现在还不能跟你说再见！

—No… I can’t say goodbye to you yet!

年轻人心中涌起一阵刺痛，这种感觉他以前无数次经历过，每次父亲离家参战或履行职责时都会如此。但这一次的悲伤却截然不同，因为是费利佩的职责将父子俩分离；而且，这或许是永别。

The young man felt a pang within him, like the one he had felt so many times before, when his father had left him to go off to war or to fulfill his duties. But this time his grief was different, because it would be Felipe's duty that would separate them; and because the farewell, possibly, would be forever.

他们的目光交汇，都显得茫然失措。他们百感交集，说不出话来。只有卡洛斯勉强开口说道：

Their eyes met, glazed over. They felt too much to speak. Only Carlos managed to say:

你是我的骄傲。

—You are my pride.

菲利普痛苦地紧紧抓住皇帝。他想起了母亲，想起了孩提时代触摸母亲遗体时那种难以承受的痛苦，因为他知道那是最后一次了。而这位欧洲最有权势的人，明知自己只能接受这样的失去，却还是伏在父亲的肩头痛哭。

Philip clung to the emperor in agony. He thought of his mother, of how unbearable it had been as a child to feel her body, knowing it was for the last time. And the most powerful man in Europe, knowing he could only accept this loss, wept on his father's shoulder.

 

 

 

 

查理前往尤斯特安享晚年的旅程漫长而平静。他抵达西班牙后，由于痛风的折磨，不得不卧床休息，这位前皇帝开始了最后的旅程。沿途，许多人都想向他致敬。尽管他每次都表达了感激之情，却都婉拒了这些荣誉。他既不想要庆祝活动，也不想要赞扬，更不想要敬仰，甚至连礼物也不想要。他之所以留在卡斯蒂利亚，正是因为他渴望做一个默默无闻的人。

Charles's journey to his retirement at Yuste was long and peaceful. Once he had disembarked in Spain, and after climbing into a litter due to the debilitating effects of gout, the former emperor embarked on his final voyage. Along the way, many wished to pay him homage. On every occasion, though expressing gratitude, he refused the honors. He wanted neither celebrations nor praise, no reverence, nor even gifts. The very reason he was in Castile was his desire to be nobody.

旅途中，查理有时间思考费迪南德的事。他的弟弟不仅没有出席退位仪式，还无视了之后在退休前与他见面道别的请求。因此，他心中充满了未能抚平对方伤痛的懊恼。尽管费迪南德的态度在所有人看来都显得固执己见——甚至连他的儿子马克西米利安也这么认为——但查理并不想怀恨在心。他想，人生本就不完美，无论多么渴望圆满落幕，现实往往并非如此。从某种意义上说，弟弟造成的隔阂，对这位来自根特的查理来说，是他应得的教训，因为他曾多次伤害过自己的亲人，所以这教训是值得的。只有上帝才能宽恕一切。

During the journey, Charles had time to think about Ferdinand. His brother had not only failed to attend the abdication ceremony, but he had also ignored the subsequent request to meet before his departure for retirement, to say their final goodbyes. He carried with him, therefore, the frustration of not having healed the other's wounds. Although Ferdinand's attitude seemed recalcitrant to everyone—even to his son Maximilian—Charles did not wish to hold a grudge. Life, he thought, was an imperfect story, and however much one might yearn to conclude it without leaving loose ends, the truth was that it rarely happened that way. The distance his brother had created was, in a way, a lesson for the man from Ghent that he deserved to learn, because it was worth it for the many times he had hurt his own. Only God could forgive everything.

 

 

 

 

最终，在1557年2月3日，皇帝在少数随从的陪伴下，第一次看到了他未来的安息之地。尤斯特修道院正如他想象的那样：一座美丽而庄严的建筑，静静地融入拉维拉的自然风光之中。他吩咐随从将他的灵柩放在柔软的草地上，然后凝视着他选定的陵墓。一种前所未有的巨大平静涌上心头。多年统治的忧虑渐渐消散。他也欣然告别了怨恨、愤怒和贪婪。卡洛斯拥有比任何人都多的头衔，他明白幸福并非来自野心，无论是否实现，而是来自无所求的自由，来自能够享受生命所赐予的一切，无论是雨后的清新气息、动人的旋律，还是又一个清晨的生命。

Finally, on February 3, 1557, with a small entourage, the emperor glimpsed for the first time what would be his final resting place. The monastery of Yuste appeared to him exactly as he had imagined it: a beautifully austere structure that gently interrupted the natural landscape of La Vera. He asked those accompanying him to place his litter on the soft grass and remained contemplating the place he had chosen as his tomb. An immense peace, unlike anything he had ever felt, washed over him. The worries of his years of rule gently evaporated. He also gladly bid farewell to resentment, anger, and greed. Having held more titles than any other man, Carlos had understood that happiness was not provided by ambitions, whether achieved or not, but by the freedom of needing nothing, of being able to enjoy whatever existence was pleased to give him, be it the scent of rain, a melody, or one more morning of life.

随后，他去参观了那座修道院。这座修道院始建于一个半世纪前，拥有美丽的哥特式和文艺复兴式回廊，风格始终保持着简朴，与修道院的整体氛围相得益彰。他即将入住的房间是专门为他建造的，在他看来堪称完美。修道士们对此感到惊讶：他们认为，一个习惯了宫殿奢华生活的人，即使表达了想要追求简朴的愿望，也会对住在只有两层楼、几间房的房子里感到失望。然而，查理并非装腔作势：他的房间可以俯瞰教堂内部，无论身体状况如何，他都能参加弥撒；而房间的简朴也让他感到平静。或许很少有人明白，对一个人来说，没有什么比放下身段、庆祝生命更令人愉悦的了。

He then went to see the monastery, whose construction had begun a century and a half earlier, and which housed beautiful Gothic and Renaissance cloisters, always simple, in keeping with the feeling the place evoked. The quarters he would occupy, which had been built to accommodate him, seemed perfect to him. The monks were surprised: they thought that a man accustomed to the magnificence of palaces would be disappointed to have to stay in a house of barely two floors and a few rooms, however much he had expressed his desire to embrace simplicity. However, Charles was not pretending: his chamber overlooked the interior of the church, which would allow him to hear Mass whatever his state of health, and the bareness of the rooms soothed him. Perhaps few understood that nothing pleases a man more than to diminish himself in dignity and celebrate it.

 

 

 

 

但是，逃避责任的人会迫使别人承担责任，而在英国，他的儿子菲利普远未体验到修道院的平静。

But he who relieves himself of duties forces another to take them on, and in England, his son Philip was far from experiencing monastic peace.

从布鲁塞尔回来后，他收到了一条令人不安的消息：玛丽·都铎声称怀有身孕的儿子根本不存在。这难道是一场骗局？还是他的妻子出现了幻觉？的确，有些女人会误以为自己怀孕了，但在如此显赫的圈子里，这种错觉显得十分可疑。然而，他并不想过多纠缠于此事。王后如此深爱着他，他的愤怒只会让她蒙羞，而且菲利普还需要从她那里夺回婚约中被剥夺的权力。

Upon his return from Brussels, he had received disconcerting news: the son Mary Tudor had claimed to be carrying had never existed. Had it been a deception? Or was his wife suffering from delusions? It was true that some women believed they were pregnant when they weren't, but in such high circles, such an illusion seemed suspicious. However, he didn't want to dwell on the matter. The queen was so in love with him that his anger would have mortified her, and Philip still needed to secure from her the power that had been denied him in the marriage contract.

这一失望带来的不安情绪，仅仅持续到另一则消息传到英国宫廷为止。国王得知此事后，所有的注意力都转向了意大利：法国国王亨利决定入侵那不勒斯王国，以承认菲利普新获得的权威。仿佛命运不愿打破旧习，哈布斯堡家族长期以来遭受法国蹂躏的诅咒，如今又在他们的儿子身上重演，菲利普也因此面临他的第一场战争。

The unease caused by this disappointment lasted only as long as it took for another piece of news to reach the English court. When he learned of it, all the king's concern turned to Italy: Henry of France had decided to recognize Philip's newfound authority by invading the Kingdom of Naples. As if fate were reluctant to break with old habits, the perennial curse suffered by the Habsburgs at the hands of the French was being replicated in their son, who thus faced his first war.

这场冲突的严重性人尽皆知。菲利普日夜研究如何应对这场袭击，而此后一直效力于他的阿尔巴公爵则亲眼见证了菲利普的君主虽然或许过于谨慎，但在军事方面无疑极具天赋。

The gravity of the conflict was not lost on anyone. Philip spent day and night studying how to respond to the attack, and the Duke of Alba, from then on always at his service, was a witness that his lord possessed a mind perhaps excessively cautious but undoubtedly talented in matters of war.

“往南我们得翻越比利牛斯山脉……从米兰出发，我们会遇到萨伏伊，我们必须先夺回它……”国王双眼因无数个不眠之夜而黯淡无光，面前摊开着几张地图。“那一定是座重要的城市。一座能让我们一举夺取所需威望的城市。”

"To the south we would have to cross the Pyrenees... And from Milan we would encounter Savoy, which we would have to recapture first..." The king, his eyes dark after countless sleepless nights, had several maps spread out before him. "It must be an important city. One that allows us to gain the prestige we need with a single blow."

公爵听得十分惊讶。桌上堆满了文件。他的新主人似乎不愿留下任何后顾之忧。

The duke listened in astonishment. The table was overflowing with documents. His new master didn't seem inclined to leave any loose ends.

——也许是佩罗纳……或者圣康坦。

—Perhaps Péronne… or Saint-Quentin.

菲利普瞥了那位贵族一眼，想听听他的意见。或许，出于对父亲的服从，他永远不会完全信任他，但这位士兵的确非同凡响。

Philip glanced at the nobleman, seeking his opinion. Perhaps, obeying his father, he would never fully trust him, but this soldier was unparalleled.

圣昆廷监狱会迫使我们转移到其他地方来维持它的防御……但是殿下，它的防御更加脆弱。

—San Quintín will force us to take other places to maintain it… But its defenses are more vulnerable, Your Highness.

国王再次仔细查看了地图。沉思片刻后，他点了点头。

The king scrutinized the map again. After considering it, he nodded.

“大人，您知道您的夫人是否会来帮助我们吗？”公爵问道。

"Do you know yet if your wife will come to our aid, my lord?" inquired the duke.

 

 

 

 

当她的丈夫提起此事时——他以一种略带戏剧性的方式，虽然略显矫揉造作，但显然是出于与法国冲突给他带来的真切痛苦——英国王后却陷入了沉思。她很清楚，菲利普只是在利用她达到自己的目的。她的婚姻就像一杯毒酒：一方面，她觉得自己是世上最幸运的女人，嫁给了一个在她眼中胜过任何人的男人；但与此同时，她也知道他并不爱她。卡斯蒂利亚国王摆脱了父亲的残暴，对她温柔体贴，但至少亨利在他们婚姻的最初几年里，还爱着他的母亲。她一天也没有享受过这种恩惠，她也不再指望菲利普的感情会改变。他把她当成妹妹，尽管他与她同寝只是为了履行职责，想要一个永远不会到来的继承人。她怀着一个不孕的子宫，甚至比她母亲的子宫还要无用，而她的母亲至少生下了她。

When her husband raised the issue—and he did so with dramatic flair, only slightly more theatrical, but clearly driven by the genuine anguish the conflict with France caused him—the English queen remained pensive. It was clear to her that Philip was using her for his own purposes. Her marriage seemed like a poisoned chalice: on the one hand, she considered herself the luckiest woman alive to be married to a man who, in her eyes, was better than any other; but, at the same time, she knew he did not love her.
